and similarly in that incident he imagined she was permitted as a concubine (pilegesh), wherefore the fence of Ezra's immersion assisted him!
פִּסְקָא ג׳ — תּוֹרָה בַּלֵּב מַכְנִיעָה אֶת הַיֵּצֶר — Paragraph 3: Torah in the Heart Vanquishing the Yetzer

The theme: The Torah residing within the heart versus external knowledge, Doeg’s hypocrisy, and the engraving upon the heart. Scholars might assume that through their Torah the yetzer is confused and powerless, for Midrash Tehillim (119:11) states on "Your word have I laid up in my heart": whoever possesses Torah in his heart, the yetzer hara has no dominion over him. But the Midrash emphasizes in the heart—meaning those whose hearts are paved with the highways of Torah (Vayikra Rabbah 17:1 on Tehillim 84:6). Doeg’s Torah was merely from his lips outward (Sanhedrin 106b), lacking fear of Heaven ("the Holy One desires the heart"). The Rabbis in Chagigah (15b) had unholy dross (tina) in their hearts due to a lack of awe ("wherefore is there a price in the hand of a fool to get wisdom, seeing he has no heart to it?", Mishlei 17:16; Yoma 72b). There are ascending levels until the law is engraved upon the tablets of the heart ("upon their heart will I write it", Yirmiyah 31:32), where the heart of stone is removed and the yetzer is eradicated—a level attained in this world only by Avraham, Yitzchak, Yaakov, and King David. Yet certain great sages achieved a measure of this level: Rav Giddel in Kesubos (17a) compared women to white geese, and Rabbi Yochanan in Niddah (13a) declared "he is not of woman born," wherefore they did not require the ordinary fences of men (as Ulla kissed his sisters, Shabbat 13a; Rashba on Yevamos 37a; Rambam, Issurei Biah 11:10).
וְהָכִי נַמֵּי הָנֵי תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים שֶׁחוֹשְׁבִים: עַל יְדֵי תּוֹרָתוֹ נִתְבַּלְבֵּל הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע וְעַד שֶׁאֵין שׁוֹלֵט בָּהֶם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁהוּא בֶּאֱמֶת כֹּחַ הַתּוֹרָה;
And so too regarding those scholars who assume that through their Torah the yetzer hara is confounded so as to have no dominion over them, as indeed is the authentic power of Torah;

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּשׁוֹחֵר טוֹב מִזְמוֹר קי״ט עַל פָּסוּק ״בְּלִבִּי צָפַנְתִּי [אִמְרָתֶךָ לְמַעַן לֹא אֶחֱטָא לָךְ]״ (תְּהִלִּים קי״ט:י״א): ״מִי שֶׁהַתּוֹרָה בְּלִבּוֹ — אֵין יֵצֶר הָרָע שׁוֹלֵט בּוֹ וְלֹא נוֹגֵעַ בּוֹ״;

and as written in Midrash Tehillim (§119) on "Your word have I laid up in my heart, that I might not sin against You" (Tehillim 119:11): "Whoever possesses Torah in his heart, the yetzer hara has no dominion over him nor touches him";

אֲבָל דָּיֵיק: ״לְמִי שֶׁהַתּוֹרָה בְּלִבּוֹ״, וְהַיְינוּ אִילֵּין דִּשְׁבִילִין דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא כְּבִישָׁן בְּלִבְּהוֹן, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּוַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה רֵישׁ פָּרָשָׁה י״ז [צ״ל כ״ה:א׳] עַל פָּסוּק: ״מְסִלּוֹת בִּלְבָבָם״ (תְּהִלִּים פ״ד:ו׳);
but notice the precise phrasing: "unto him who has Torah in his heart," meaning those in whose hearts the paths of Torah are paved, as stated on "highways in their hearts" (Tehillim 84:6);
וְתוֹרָתוֹ שֶׁל דּוֹאֵג הָיָה כּוּלּוֹ רַק מִשָּׂפָה וְלַחוּץ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (ק״ו עַמּוּד ב׳), עַיֵּין שָׁם בְּרַשִׁ״י (דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל: ״עַל פִּיךָ״) דְּלֹא בַּלֵּב;
whereas the Torah of Doeg was merely from his lips outward, as stated in Sanhedrin (106b), see Rashi (s.v. Al picha) that it did not touch his heart;
וְכִדְמַסִּיק שָׁם: ״אֶלָּא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא — לִבָּא בָּעֵי״ (שָׁם).
concluding there: "for the Holy One desires the heart" (ibid.).
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּחֲגִיגָה (ט״ו סוֹף עַמּוּד ב׳): ״טִינָא הָיְתָה בְּלִבָּם״, וְהַיְינוּ עַל יְדֵי שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה בָּהֶם יִרְאַת שָׁמָיִם;
And as stated in Chagigah (15b): "unholy dross (tina) was in their hearts," namely because they lacked fear of Heaven;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּיוֹמָא (ע״ב עַמּוּד ב׳) עַל פָּסוּק: ״לָמָּה זֶּה מְחִיר [בְּיַד כְּסִיל לִקְנוֹת חָכְמָה] — וְלֶב אָיִן״ (מִשְׁלֵי י״ז:ט״ז).
and as expounded in Yoma (72b) on: "Wherefore is there a price in the hand of a fool to get wisdom, seeing he has no heart to it?" (Mishlei 17:16).
וּבְעִנְיַן הַכְּנִיסָה בַּלֵּב שֶׁהוּא לְתַלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים בַּעֲלֵי יִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם, יֵשׁ מַדְרֵיגוֹת מַדְרֵיגוֹת עַד הַחֲקִיקָה הַגְּמוּרָה בַּלֵּב;
And regarding the Torah entering the heart of God-fearing scholars, there are ascending rungs unto absolute engraving upon the heart;
עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ לֶעָתִיד: ״[וְ]עַל לִבָּם אֶכְתֲּבֶנָּה״ (יִרְמְיָה ל״א:ל״ב), שֶׁהוּא בַּהֲסָרַת לֵב הָאֶבֶן וּבִיטּוּל הַיֵּצֶר לְגַמְרֵי לֶעָתִיד;
after the manner spoken of the Future: "and will write it in their hearts" (Yirmiyah 31:32), which is the removal of the stony heart and the total eradication of the yetzer hara;
שֶׁזָּכוּ לָהּ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה רַק אֲבוֹת הָעוֹלָם: אַבְרָהָם, יִצְחָק, וְיַעֲקֹב, וְדָוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם.
which in this world was attained only by the Patriarchs: Avraham, Yitzchak, Yaakov, and King David, peace be upon him.
אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם גַּם קְצָת גְּדוֹלֵי חֲכָמִים זוּלָתָם זָכוּ לִקְצָת מֵאוֹתָהּ הַמַּדְרֵיגָה;
But nevertheless some great sages aside from them merited a measure of that exalted rung;
כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּכְתוּבּוֹת (י״ז עַמּוּד א׳): ״אִי דָּמְיָא עֲלַיְיכִי כְּכַשׁוּרֵי״;
after the manner stated in Kesubos (17a): "if women resemble unto you like wooden beams";
וּבְנִדָּה (י״ג סוֹף עַמּוּד א׳): ״אֵין זֶה יְלִיד אִשָּׁה״;
and in Niddah (13a): "this master is not like one born of a woman";
וּמִפְּנֵי כֵן לֹא הוּצְרְכוּ לְהַגְדָּרוֹת כָּל כָּךְ שֶׁגָּדְרוּ בִּשְׁאָר בְּנֵי אָדָם כִּדְאִיתָא הָתָם;
wherefore they did not require the stringent fences enacted for ordinary men;
וְכַיּוֹצֵא בוֹ: ״עוּלָא דִּמְנַשֵּׁק לַאֲחָתֵיהּ״ בְּשַׁבָּת (י״ג סוֹף עַמּוּד א׳), עַיֵּין שָׁם בְּתוֹסָפוֹת (דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל: ״וּפְלִיגֵי״);
and like Ulla who kissed his sisters (Shabbat 13a; Tosafos s.v. U-pligi);
וְכַיּוֹצֵא בוֹ בְּחִדּוּשֵׁי הָרַשְׁבָּ״א (יְבָמוֹת ל״ז רֵישׁ עַמּוּד ב׳): ״דְּרַבָּנַן זְהִירֵי״;
and as the Rashba wrote in his Chiddushim (Yevamos 37b): "the Rabbis are watchful";
וְעַיֵּין שָׁם דְּהָרַמְבַּ״ם כָּתַב זֶה בִּסְתָם תַּלְמִיד חָכָם, וְעַיֵּין בְּהָרַב הַמַּגִּיד פֶּרֶק י״א מֵהִלְכוֹת אִיסּוּרֵי בִּיאָה הֲלָכָה י׳:
and see Rambam who ruled this for any scholar, and the Maggid Mishneh (Hilchos Issurei Biah 11:10)!
פִּסְקָא ד׳ — אֵין תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים בּוֹטְחִים בְּיִצְרָם — Paragraph 4: Scholars Must Not Overconfidently Trust Their Yetzer

The theme: The Ritva on self-knowledge, the modesty of Rav Amram Chassida, and the danger of presuming personal immunity. The Ritva at the end of Kiddushin (82a) qualifies these leniencies: everything depends upon how well a person knows himself. If a man knows with certainty that his yetzer is utterly subdued and harbors no lustful dross, he may look casually or speak with an ervah—which explains Rabbi Yochanan sitting at the gates of the immersion pool (Berachos 20a), Rabbi Abbahu surrounded by Roman maidens (Kesubos 17a), Rabbis conversing with noblewomen in private rooms (Shabbat 127b), and Rav Acha carrying a bride on his shoulders (Kesubos 17a). Yet no one may rely upon this except a great chassid who has thoroughly tested his yetzer. Most scholars must never trust their yetzer; Rav Amram Chassida was crowned with the unique title "Chassida" among the Amoraim precisely because he subjected himself to public shame in order to conquer his yetzer (Kiddushin 81a). Indeed, "whoever is greater than his fellow, his yetzer is greater than his" (Sukkah 52a). The Maggid Mishneh notes that genuine scholars (tzurba me-rabbanan) are not found in our times; when a scholar imagines he is immune from bodily temptation, the yetzer deceives him into indulging like a rooster without holiness!
וּבֶאֱמֶת אֵין רְאָיָה מֵרַב וְרַב נַחְמָן דְּרַב גּוּבְרַיְיהוּ לְכָל תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים;
And in truth there is no proof from Rav and Rav Nachman, whose spiritual stature was immense, unto all Torah scholars;
וְעַיֵּין בְּרִיטְבָ״א סוֹף קִדּוּשִׁין (פ״ב עַמּוּד א׳): דְּהַכֹּל כְּפִי מַה שֶּׁאָדָם מַכִּיר בְּעַצְמוֹ, אִם רָאוּי לוֹ לַעֲשׂוֹת הַרְחָקָה לְיִצְרוֹ וְכוּלֵיהּ;
and see the Ritva at the end of Kiddushin (82a): everything is evaluated according to how a man knows himself, whether he must distance his yetzer;
וְאִם מַכִּיר בְּעַצְמוֹ שֶׁיִּצְרוֹ נִכְנָע וְכָפִיף לוֹ וְאֵין מַעֲלֶה טִינָא כְּלָל
and if he knows that his yetzer is conquered and subdued, raising no unholy dross;
מוּתָּר לוֹ לְהִסְתַּכֵּל וּלְדַבֵּר עִם הָעֶרְוָה וְלִשְׁאוֹל בִּשְׁלוֹם אֵשֶׁת אִישׁ;
he is permitted to look casually, converse with an ervah, and greet a married woman;
וְהַיְינוּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן יָתֵיב אַשַּׁעֲרֵי טְבִילָה (בְּרָכוֹת כ׳ עַמּוּד א׳);
and this explains why Rabbi Yochanan sat at the gates of the immersion pool (Berachos 20a);
וְרַבִּי אַבָּהוּ דְּנָפְקֵי אַמְהָתָא דְּבֵי קֵיסָר (כְּתוּבּוֹת י״ז עַמּוּד א׳);
and Rabbi Abbahu whom the maidservants of Caesar's palace greeted (Kesubos 17a);
וְכַמָּה מֵרַבָּנַן דְּמִשְׁתָּעוּ עִם מַטְרוֹנִיתָא בְּחֶדֶר סָגוּר דְּעָבְרֵי אַיִּחוּד, כְּהַהוּא דְּשַׁבָּת (קכ״ז עַמּוּד ב׳);
and several Rabbis who conversed with noblewomen in private quarters as recounted in Shabbat (127b);
וְרַב אַחָא דִּנְקֵיט כַּלָּה אַכַּתְפֵיהּ (שָׁם בִּכְתוּבּוֹת י״ז עַמּוּד א׳);
and Rav Acha who carried a bride upon his shoulders (Kesubos 17a);
אֶלָּא שֶׁאֵין רָאוּי לְהָקֵל בָּזֶה אֶלָּא לְחָסִיד גָּדוֹל שֶׁמַּכִּיר בְּיִצְרוֹ, וְלֹא כָּל תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים בּוֹטְחִין בְּיִצְרֵיהֶן כִּדְחָזֵינַן בִּשְׁמַעְתִּין.
but it is unfitting to be lenient in this save for a great chassid who has tested his yetzer, for not all scholars can trust their yetzer.
וּבַגְּמָרָא שָׁם (קִדּוּשִׁין פ״א עַמּוּד א׳) אִיתָא בְּרַב עַמְרָם חֲסִידָא: נִקְרָא ״חָסִיד״ בְּשֵׁם מְיוּחָד כָּךְ בֵּין הָאָמוֹרָאִים עַל יְדֵי הִתְגַּבְּרוּתוֹ עַל הַיֵּצֶר;
And in the Gemara (Kiddushin 81a) regarding Rav Amram Chassida: he was crowned with the unique title "Chassida" among the Amoraim through conquering his yetzer;
רַק עַל יְדֵי הַכְּסִיפָה שֶׁבָּחַר לְעַצְמוֹ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה כְּדֵי לִינָּצֵל מִמֶּנּוּ, וּבָזֶה זָכָה אַחַר כָּךְ דִּנְפַק מִינֵּיהּ לְגַמְרֵי.
choosing humiliating public shame in this world to save himself, through which he merited that the yetzer departed from him entirely like a column of fire!
אֲבָל עִיקַּר שְׁלִיטָתוֹ אַדְּרַבָּא בְּתַלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים יוֹתֵר, וְכָל הַגָּדוֹל — עוֹד יוֹתֵר, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּסֻכָּה (נ״ב סוֹף עַמּוּד א׳);
For the assault of the yetzer is directed preeminently against scholars, and whoever is greater, his yetzer is greater (Sukkah 52a);
אֶלָּא שֶׁמִּכָּל מָקוֹם גַּם בִּכְלַל תַּלְמִיד חָכָם בְּעִנְיַן הַקִּידּוּשׁ בַּמֻּתָּר עֲדִיפֵי מֵעַמֵּי הָאֲרָצוֹת;
nevertheless, scholars in sanctifying the permitted remain elevated above the unlearned masses;
וְיֵשׁ דְּאֵין צָרִיךְ הַגְדָּרָה כָּל כָּךְ, כְּהַהוּא דְּשַׁבָּת (פ״ו סוֹף עַמּוּד א׳): ״יִשְׂרָאֵל קְדוֹשִׁים וְכוּלֵיהּ, תַּלְמִיד חָכָם וְכוּלֵיהּ״, עַיֵּין שָׁם בְּרַשִׁ״י;
and some do not require such rigid fences, as in Shabbat (86b): "Israel are holy... a Torah scholar, etc.," see Rashi there;
וּקְדֻשַּׁת תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים מִצַּד הַתּוֹרָה לִהְיוֹת קְדוֹשִׁים, אַף שֶׁאֵין עוֹשִׂים כִּשְׁאָר יִשְׂרָאֵל קְדוֹשִׁים, וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם הֵם זְהִירֵי וּקְדוֹשֵׁי;
the sanctity of scholars stemming from the Torah to be holy, so that even when they do not adopt outward stringencies they remain watchful and holy;
וְכַיּוֹצֵא בוֹ מָצִינוּ בִּשְׁאָר עִנְיְנֵי גְּזֵירוֹת שָׁם (שַׁבָּת קל״ט עַמּוּד ב׳): ״צוּרְבָא מֵרַבָּנַן — לָא אָתֵי לְמֶעְבַּד לְכַתְּחִלָּה״;
and like the rule in Shabbat (139b): "a young scholar will not come to do it deliberately";

וּבַיְרוּשַׁלְמִי פֶּרֶק א׳ דְּשַׁבָּת (הֲלָכָה ב׳): ״מַתְנִיתִין — בְּעַמֵּי הָאָרֶץ; מַה דִּתְנֵי רַבִּי חִיָּיא — בַּחֲבֵירָיו״, עַיֵּין שָׁם בְּ״קָרְבַּן הָעֵדָה״: דְּעַם הָאָרֶץ צָרִיךְ הַרְחָקָה יְתֵירָה;
and in Yerushalmi Shabbat (1:2): "our Mishnah applies to the unlearned; Rabbi Chiyya taught regarding his scholarly companions," the unlearned requiring a greater distance;

וּבְרֵישׁ פֶּרֶק ד׳ דְּתַעֲנִית (דַּף כ״ד עַמּוּד א׳) אָמַר רַבִּי חַגַּי: ״כְּלוּם אָמְרוּ וְכוּלֵיהּ? אֲנָא מִסְתַּכַּלְנָא וְכוּלֵיהּ״, וְהוּבָא בְּתוֹסָפוֹת חֲגִיגָה (ט״ז עַמּוּד א׳ דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל: ״בַּכֹּהֲנִים״);
and in Yerushalmi Ta'anit (4:1) Rabbi Chaggai stated: "Did they decree thus? I gaze upon the kohanim without fear!" (Tosafos, Chagigah 16a);
וְזֶה עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמַר שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם: ״אֲנִי אַרְבֶּה וְלֹא אָסוּר״ (סַנְהֶדְרִין כ״א עַמּוּד ב׳);
this resembling King Solomon who declared: "I will multiply and not turn aside" (Sanhedrin 21b);
אֶלָּא דְּהַהִיא אַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה שֶׁהוּא כּוֹלֶלֶת כָּל הַנְּפָשׁוֹת, וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְבַטֵּל אוֹת אַחַת מִדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה;
except that Solomon spoke against biblical laws which embrace all souls and cannot be modified;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בִּגְזֵירַת חֲכָמֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה: עַל זֶה שֶׁיּוֹדֵעַ בְּעַצְמוֹ — לֹא גָזְרוּ.
whereas regarding rabbinic decrees, upon one who is completely master of himself the Sages did not decree.
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם הַיְינוּ רַק רַבִּי חַגַּי דְּרַב גּוּבְרֵיהּ;
Nevertheless this applied strictly to Rabbi Chaggai whose spiritual stature was immense;

וְאַף בְּמַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב סְתָם ״צוּרְבָא מֵרַבָּנַן לָא גָזַר״, כָּתַב בְּהָרַב הַמַּגִּיד פֶּרֶק ד׳ מִשַּׁבָּת הֲלָכָה ג׳: דְּהָרַמְבַּ״ם לֹא כָּתַב זֶה מִשּׁוּם דְּאֵין צוּרְבָא מֵרַבָּנַן מָצוּי הָאִידְנָא;
and even where the Talmud exempts a young scholar, the Maggid Mishneh (Hilchos Shabbat 4:3) explains that Rambam omitted it because true scholars of that stature are not found today;

וְצָרִיךְ עִיּוּן מִזֶּה עַל דִּבְרֵי הָרַמְבַּ״ם וְהָרַב הַמַּגִּיד בְּהִלְכוֹת אִיסּוּרֵי בִּיאָה הַנִּזְכָּר, דְּכָתַב הַדִּין לְתַלְמִיד חָכָם אַף בְּמַה דְּאָמְרוּ בַּגְּמָרָא רַק אַרַב וְרַב נַחְמָן וְלֹא לִסְתָם צוּרְבָא מֵרַבָּנַן.
and this requires analysis regarding the Rambam in Hilchos Issurei Biah, who applied the leniency of Rav and Rav Nachman to any scholar.
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם, הוֹאִיל וְכָל תַּלְמִיד חָכָם מַרְגִּישׁ בְּעַצְמוֹ קְצָת קְדוּשָׁה יְתֵירָה מִיהַת עַל יְדֵי הַתּוֹרָה, שֶׁאֵינוֹ כְּעַם הָאָרֶץ לְעִנְיַן הַקִּידּוּשׁ בַּמֻּתָּר;
Nevertheless, since every Torah scholar feels within himself a degree of elevated holiness through the Torah, not being like an unlearned man regarding sanctifying the permitted;
עַל יְדֵי זֶה יוּכַל הַיֵּצֶר לְהַתְעוֹתוֹ שֶׁכְּבָר הִגִּיעַ לַגֶּדֶר שֶׁאֵין צָרִיךְ כָּל כָּךְ פְּרִישׁוּת מֵהַמֻּתָּר, וַאֲפִילּוּ לֹא יִפְרוֹשׁ אֵינוֹ ״נָבָל״;

through this the yetzer can deceive him into imagining he has reached the level where he no longer needs defensive abstinence from the permitted, and that even without self-restraint he is not a "scoundrel"!

וְעַל כֵּן נֶאֱמַר בִּלְשׁוֹן נְקִיָּה: ״כְּתַרְנְגוֹלִים״ (בְּרָכוֹת כ״ב עַמּוּד א׳), שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּעֵירוּבִין (ק׳ סוֹף עַמּוּד ב׳): ״לָמַדְנוּ דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ מִתַּרְנְגוֹל״, שֶׁהוּא נוֹהֵג בְּמִדַּת דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ;
Wherefore the Gemara employed the elevated euphemism: "like roosters" (Berachos 22a), the Sages stating in Eruvin (100b): "We learn proper conduct (derech eretz) from the rooster";
וְעִיקַּר הַזִּיוּוּג נִקְרָא ״דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ״ בְּסוֹף נְדָרִים (צ״א עַמּוּד ב׳): ״צִעַרְתָּן בְּדֶרֶךְ אֶרֶץ״;
marital intimacy being explicitly termed derech eretz in Nedarim (91b);
וּבְגִיטִּין (ע׳ עַמּוּד א׳): ״שְׁמוֹנָה רֻבָּן קָשֶׁה... דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ״;
and in Gittin (70a): "Eight things in excess are harmful... derech eretz";
וְכֵן אִיתָא בְּקִדּוּשִׁין (ב׳ עַמּוּד ב׳): ״בִּיאָה אִיקְּרֵי ׳דֶּרֶךְ׳״;
and in Kiddushin (2b): "cohabitation is called 'the way'";
וְגַם בְּנִדָּה (ט״ז עַמּוּד ב׳) דָּרְשׁוּ מִקְּרָא דְּ״בוֹזֶה דְרָכָיו [יָמוּת]״ (מִשְׁלֵי י״ט:ט״ז), עַיֵּין שָׁם בְּרַשִׁ״י;
and in Niddah (16b) expounding "he that despises his ways shall die" (Mishlei 19:16), see Rashi;

וְכֵן בִּבְרָכוֹת (י״א עַמּוּד א׳) מְמַעֵט מֵהַאי טַעְמָא מִ״בְּלֶכְתְּךָ בַדֶּרֶךְ״ (דְּבָרִים ו:ז) — חָתָן, דְּ״דֶּרֶךְ״ הַיְינוּ דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּתַנָּא דְּבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ רַבָּה (רֵישׁ פֶּרֶק א׳):
and in Berachos (11a) exempting a groom from the Shema because derech denotes derech eretz (Tanna D'vei Eliyahu Rabbah, ch. 1)!
פִּסְקָא ה׳ — דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ שֶׁקָּדְמָה לַתּוֹרָה וִיסוֹד קְדֻשַּׁת יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא — Paragraph 5: Derech Eretz Preceding Torah and the Sanctity of Rabbi Chiyya's Sons

The theme: The definition of Derech Eretz, natural Jewish morality, and the angelic sanctity of Yehudah the son of Rabbi Chiyya. Derech eretz denotes all conduct required for settling the earth ("He created it not a waste, He formed it to be inhabited", Yeshayah 45:18). Submerging oneself in lust beyond worldly need is the antithesis of derech eretz; therefore Avraham chose the Land of Israel when he saw its inhabitants weeding and planting, rather than eating, drinking, and acting recklessly (Bereishis Rabbah 39:8), perceiving that they possessed the derech eretz that precedes Torah (Avos 3:17). In Tractate Kallah, Rabbi Eliezer taught that wherever Torah does not pass through the mouth, true derech eretz cannot endure, for innate shame and moral decency (the three inborn traits of Israel, Yevamos 79a) are fortified solely through Torah. When a scholar convinces himself that his frequent intimacy is for the sake of Heaven, he behaves like a rooster—acting in the way of ordinary man without true holiness. Unlike such self-delusion stands authentic holiness: King David never neglected his marital obligation (Sanhedrin 107a), and Yehudah the son of Rabbi Chiyya was constantly with his wife (Kesubos 62b). In Bava Batra (75a), the two angels Michael and Gabriel correspond to the Amoraim Yehudah and Chizkiyah. Rabbi Chiyya and his sons were compared to the Patriarchs (Bava Metzia 85b); Rabbi Chiyya embodied Yaakov Avinu (Truth/Torah, ensuring Torah is never forgotten, Berachos 18b), while Yehudah stood on his right like the angel Michael, rooted in the lovingkindness of Avraham where physical desires are completely transformed into holiness (ta'avat adam chasdo). Yehudah acted solely for the mitzvah of onah, infusing divine holiness into his heart. The true hallmark of holiness is when a mitzvah awakens additional sanctity before and after its execution (Makkot 5b; Shabbat 130a), whereas the yetzer’s delusion leaves man in carnal emptiness.
וְ״דֶרֶךְ אֶרֶץ״ נִקְרָא מַה שֶּׁהוּא צָרִיךְ לְיִשּׁוּב הָאָרֶץ וְהָעוֹלָם, דְּ״לֹא תֹהוּ בְרָאָהּ [לָשֶׁבֶת יְצָרָהּ]״ (יְשַׁעְיָה מ״ה:י״ח);
And derech eretz denotes all that is required for the settlement of the earth and the cosmos: "He created it not a waste, He formed it to be inhabited" (Yeshayah 45:18);
וְלִהְיוֹת בֵּיתוֹ ״מִיתְבָא יָתֵיב״ עַל יְדֵי זֶה, דְּזֶהוּ כָּל עִנְיַן דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ בְּכָל מָקוֹם הָעוֹסֵק בְּיִשּׁוּב הָעוֹלָם;
and to ensure that his household is established and settled, this being the theme of derech eretz in every passage treating the settlement of the world;
כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרָכוֹת (ל״ה עַמּוּד ב׳): ״הַנּוֹהֵג בָּהֶן מִנְהַג דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ״;
as stated in Berachos (35b): "one who conducts himself with the way of the world";
וּבְקִדּוּשִׁין (מ׳ עַמּוּד ב׳): ״מִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ... בְּדֶרֶךְ אֶרֶץ — אֵינוֹ מִן הַיִּשּׁוּב״.
and in Kiddushin (40b): "Whoever possesses no derech eretz is not part of civilized society".
וְהַהִשְׁתַּקְּעוּת בַּתַּאֲווֹת מַה שֶּׁאֵין צָרִיךְ לְיִשּׁוּב הָעוֹלָם — הוּא הֵיפֶךְ מִדַּת דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ.
And submerging oneself in carnal lusts beyond what is necessary for settling the world is the antithesis of derech eretz.

וְעַל כֵּן בָּחַר אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל: שֶׁרָאָן עוֹסְקִין בְּנִיכּוּשׁ וְכוּלֵיהּ, וְלֹא כְּאוֹתָן הָאוֹכְלִין וְשׁוֹתִין וּפוֹחֲזִין, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה ל״ט:ח׳);
Wherefore Avraham Avinu chose the Land of Israel: seeing its inhabitants toiling in weeding and planting, unlike the heathen who eat, drink, and act with reckless vanity (Bereishis Rabbah 39:8);
שֶׁרָאָה שֶׁהֵן בְּ״דֶרֶךְ אֶרֶץ הַקּוֹדֶמֶת לַתּוֹרָה״ (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה ט:ג);
seeing that they practiced the derech eretz that precedes the Torah (Vayikra Rabbah 9:3);
וְהֵבִין מִזֶּה דְּאוֹתָהּ הָאָרֶץ הִיא הַמּוּכֶנֶת לַתּוֹרָה, כִּי: ״אִם אֵין דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ — אֵין תּוֹרָה״, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ פֶּרֶק ג׳ דְּאָבוֹת (מִשְׁנָה י״ז);
understanding that this Land is prepared for the Torah, for "if there is no derech eretz, there is no Torah" (Avos 3:17).
וּבְמַסֶּכֶת כַּלָּה אִיתָא: שָׁאֲלוּ אֶת רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר... וַהֲלֹא כָּל בְּנוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל יֵשׁ לָהֶם דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ? (עַיֵּין שָׁם בְּהַגָּהוֹת הַגְּרָ״א);
And in Tractate Kallah it is taught: they asked Rabbi Eliezer: do not all daughters of Israel possess derech eretz? (see the glosses of the Gra);
אָמַר לָהֶם: חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, כָּל מִי שֶׁאֵין הַתּוֹרָה עוֹבֶרֶת עַל פִּיו אֵין בּוֹ דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ;
he replied unto them: God forbid! whoever does not have the Torah passing through his mouth possesses no authentic derech eretz;
וְרָצָה לוֹמַר: דְּעַל יְדֵי מִדַּת דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ גַּם כֵּן אֵין מִתְכַּוֵּון לִפְרִיצוּת וּמְרוּחָק מֵהִרְהוּרִים, וְאֵין צָרִיךְ לְהַגְדָּרוֹת כָּל כָּךְ בַּמֻּתָּר;
meaning: through natural derech eretz one does not intend promiscuity, avoiding lustful thoughts, and does not require rigid defensive fences;
וֶהֱשִׁיב: כָּל מִי שֶׁאֵין וְכוּלֵיהּ, דְּ״אִם אֵין תּוֹרָה — אֵין דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ״ גַּם כֵּן.
and he replied: "if there is no Torah, there is no derech eretz" either.
וַאֲפִילּוּ מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ... אֲבָל כֵּן הָאֱמֶת דְּכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל וַאֲפִילּוּ הָרֵיקִין הֵם בְּדֶרֶךְ אֶרֶץ שֶׁקָּדְמָה לַתּוֹרָה;
But such is the truth: that all Israel, even the empty ones, possess the derech eretz that preceded the Torah;
שֶׁכֵּן עֲתִידִין לִזְכּוֹת לֶעָתִיד מִיהַת לַתּוֹרָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: ״כִּי כוּלָּם יֵדְעוּ אוֹתִי [לְמִקְּטַנָּם וְעַד גְּדוֹלָם]״ (יִרְמְיָה ל״א:ל״ג);
for they are destined in the Future to merit Torah: "for they shall all know Me, from the least of them unto the greatest" (Yirmiyah 31:33);

אֶלָּא שֶׁמִּכָּל מָקוֹם, כָּל זְמַן שֶׁלֹּא נִכְנַס עַדַיִין דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה בְּלִבּוֹ, גַּם הַדֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ שֶׁלּוֹ אֵינוֹ דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ גָּמוּר הַמַּצֶּלֶת מִן הַשְּׁקִיעוּת בְּהִפּוּךְ תֹּקֶף הַסָּתַת הַיֵּצֶר;
yet so long as words of Torah have not entered his heart, his derech eretz is not consummate enough to shield him from the fierce seductions of the yetzer;
דְּדָבָר זֶה אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא עַל יְדֵי הַתּוֹרָה.
for complete protection is achieved solely through the Torah.
וּמִי שֶׁהַתּוֹרָה עוֹבֶרֶת תּוֹךְ פִּיו מִיהַת, אַף שֶׁלֹּא נִקְבַּע עַדַיִין בַּלֵּב, הוּא בְּדֶרֶךְ אֶרֶץ מִיהַת;
And one in whose mouth Torah resides, even if not yet deeply engraved in his heart, possesses derech eretz;
וְיָכוֹל לְהַצִּיל עַצְמוֹ גַּם מִתֹּקֶף הַיֵּצֶר עַל יְדֵי מִדַּת דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ, כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמַר רַב עַמְרָם חֲסִידָא עַל יְדֵי הַבּוּשָׁה (קִדּוּשִׁין פ״א עַמּוּד א׳);
empowered to save himself through derech eretz, as Rav Amram Chassida saved himself through shame (Kiddushin 81a);
שֶׁהוּא גַּם כֵּן מִמִּדַּת דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ שֶׁלֹּא לַעֲשׂוֹת כֵּן בִּפְנֵי בְּנֵי אָדָם עַל כָּל פָּנִים;
shame being an aspect of derech eretz, refusing to act licentiously before people;
דְּעַל כֵּן אָמְרוּ (נְדָרִים כ׳ עַמּוּד א׳): ״כָּל הַמִּתְבַּיֵּישׁ — לֹא בִּמְהֵרָה הוּא חוֹטֵא, וְשֶׁאֵין לוֹ בּוּשָׁה — בְּיָדוּעַ שֶׁלֹּא עָמְדוּ אֲבוֹתָיו עַל הַר סִינַי״;
wherefore the Talmud states in Nedarim (20a): "Whoever possesses shame will not readily sin, and whoever lacks shame, his ancestors did not stand at Sinai";
דְּשֶׁאֵין בּוֹ דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ סִימָן שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ רֵיחַ תּוֹרָה גַּם כֵּן מוֹרָשָׁה מֵאֲבוֹתָיו;
for one devoid of derech eretz lacks the fragrance of Torah inherited from his ancestors;
דְּאָז הָיָה בוֹ מוּשְׁרָשׁ עַל כָּל פָּנִים מִדַּת דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ קוֹדֶמֶת לַתּוֹרָה בְּלִבְּבוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל;
which otherwise roots natural derech eretz in the hearts of Israel;
שֶׁזֶּהוּ מִג׳ סִימָנִים דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּיבָמוֹת (ע״ט עַמּוּד א׳): ״רַחֲמָנִין, בַּיְישָׁנִין, וְגוֹמְלֵי חֲסָדִים״
this being the three inborn traits of Israel (Yevamos 79a): merciful, bashful, and doers of kindness;
שֶׁהֵם ג׳ עִיקָּרֵי מִדּוֹת דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ הַקְּבוּעִים בְּכָל לִבְּבוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּטֶבַע תּוֹלַדְתָּם, דְּעַל יְדֵי זֶה הֵם כְּלִי לְקַבֵּל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה.
which serve as the vessels to receive the words of Torah.
אֶלָּא דְּהַדֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ שֶׁבַּטֶּבַע אֵינוֹ מְסַלֵּק הַבְּחִירָה, וְרַק ״לֹא בִּמְהֵרָה חוֹטֵא״;
But innate derech eretz does not eliminate free will, merely ensuring that one does not sin readily;
אֲבָל אִם יִתְקְפֶנּוּ יִצְרוֹ — יוֹצִיאוֹ מִן הָעוֹלָם חַס וְשָׁלוֹם;
but if his yetzer overpowers him, it can cast him from the world, God forbid;
רַק עַל יְדֵי הַתּוֹרָה יִקָּבַע בּוֹ הַדֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ עַל כָּל פָּנִים;
whereas through the Torah derech eretz becomes permanently rooted within him;
שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ אֵין כֹּחוֹ יָפֶה פְּעָמִים לְכָבְשׁוֹ עַל פִּי הַתּוֹרָה, כִּי בְּהַכְנָסַת הִרְהוּרִין בַּלֵּב הוּא מְבַטְּלוֹ מִדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה;
so that even if he cannot conquer it through Torah reflection (unholy thoughts disturbing his study);
מִכָּל מָקוֹם נִשְׁאָר הַדֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ הַקּוֹדֵם לַתּוֹרָה לְכָבְשׁוֹ עַל פִּי הַמִּדַּת דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ.
the preceding derech eretz remains to subdue it through natural moral decency.
וְכֵן אַף כְּשֶׁמַּתְעֵהוּ הַיֵּצֶר שֶׁכַּוָּונָתוֹ לִקְדוּשָׁה וּלְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם לְבַטֵּל הִרְהוּרִין וְכַיּוֹצֵא בְּעִנְיַן הַפְּרִיצוּת בַּמֻּתָּר;
And so even when the yetzer deceives him into thinking his frequent intimacy is for the sake of Heaven to dispel stray thoughts;
הֲרֵי כְּפִי מַחֲשַׁבְתּוֹ מִיהַת הוּא בְּדֶרֶךְ אֶרֶץ, וְעַל כֵּן נִקְרָא ״כְּתַרְנְגוֹלִין״ לְעִנְיַן הַמִּדַּת דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ;
according to his perspective he acts within derech eretz, wherefore it is called "like roosters" regarding natural conduct;
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם הוּא לִגְנַאי גַּם כֵּן, שֶׁאֵינוֹ אֶלָּא כְּדֶרֶךְ גֶּבֶר בְּעָלְמָא בְּלִי שׁוּם קְדוּשָׁה.
yet it is derogatory, being merely the way of physical man without holiness!
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן הַקָּדוֹשׁ בֶּאֱמֶת, שֶׁכַּוָּונָתוֹ בֶּאֱמֶת לַאֲמִיתּוֹ לַמִּצְוָה לְבַד;
Unlike one who is authentically holy, whose intention is purely for the mitzvah alone;
כְּדָוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁלֹּא בִּטֵּל עוֹנָתוֹ (סַנְהֶדְרִין ק״ז עַמּוּד א׳);
like King David who never neglected his onah (Sanhedrin 107a);
וּכִיהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא (כְּתוּבּוֹת ס״ב עַמּוּד ב׳), דְּגַם כֵּן הִגִּיעַ לְמַדְרֵיגָה גְּדוֹלָה מֵהַקְּדוּשָׁה;
and like Yehudah the son of Rabbi Chiyya (Kesubos 62b), who likewise attained an immense rung of holiness;
כִּי מָצִינוּ בְּבָבָא בַּתְרָא (ע״ה עַמּוּד א׳): ״פְּלִיגֵי תְּרֵי מַלְאֲכֵי בִּרְקִיעָא... וְאָמְרֵי לַהּ תְּרֵי אָמוֹרָאֵי: יְהוּדָה וְחִזְקִיָּה״
for in Bava Batra (75a) the two disputing angels Michael and Gabriel correspond to the Amoraim Yehudah and Chizkiyah;
כִּי הֵן דּוּגְמַת אוֹתָן הַמַּלְאָכִים, וְכִמְדוּמֶּה דְּרָאִיתִי כֵּן בְּאֵיזֶה סֵפֶר בְּשֵׁם הָאֲרִיזַ״ל;
they mirroring those supernal angels, as cited in the writings of the Arizal;
וּבְבָבָא מְצִיעָא (פ״ה עַמּוּד ב׳): ״דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא וּבָנָיו — כָּאָבוֹת״.
and in Bava Metzia (85b): "Rabbi Chiyya and his sons are like the Patriarchs".
וְנִרְאֶה לִי דְּהוּא נֶגֶד יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, מִדַּת הָאֱמֶת, ״זוֹ תּוֹרָה״;
And it appears to me that Rabbi Chiyya corresponds to Yaakov Avinu, the attribute of Truth, which is Torah;
דְּעָבֵיד דְּלָא תִּשְׁתַּכַּח מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל, כְּמִדַּת ״שְׂפַת אֱמֶת תִּכּוֹן לָעַד״ (מִשְׁלֵי י״ב:י״ט);
who labored so that Torah would never be forgotten from Israel (Bava Metzia 85b), embodying "the lip of truth shall be established forever" (Mishlei 12:19);
וְעַל כֵּן כִּי אַיְקַר תַּלְמוּדַיְיהוּ וּבָעוּ לְאַדְכּוֹרֵיהּ, אָמְרוּ בִּבְרָכוֹת (י״ח עַמּוּד ב׳): ״יָדַע אֲבוּן בְּהַאי צַעֲרָא״;
wherefore when their study became difficult, his sons said (Berachos 18b): "Our father knows of this sorrow";
דְּזֶה הָיָה כָּל עִסְקוֹ וְכֹחוֹ שֶׁלֹּא תִּשְׁתַּכַּח תּוֹרָה;
for this was his entire essence: that Torah never be forgotten;
וְעַל יְדֵי שֶׁהִזְכִּירוּ מְעַט מִידִיעַת אֲבִיהֶם, חָשְׁבוּ לְעוֹרֵר מַדְרֵיגָתוֹ דְּעַל יְדֵי זֶה יוּכְלוּ לִזְכּוֹר;
invoking their father's knowledge to awaken his soul-level so that they might remember;
וְזֶהוּ מַדְרֵיגַת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם דְּ״לֹא מֵת״ (תַּעֲנִית ה׳ עַמּוּד ב׳), דְּמִדַּת הָאֲמִיתּוּת הוּא שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה לוֹ בִּיטּוּל כְּלָל לְעוֹלָם.
this being the rung of Yaakov who never died (Ta'anit 5b), for truth has no cessation forever.
וּבָנָיו הֵם ״תְּרֵין דְּרוֹעִין״: יְהוּדָה דּוּגְמַת מִיכָאֵל מִיָּמִין;
And his sons are the two arms: Yehudah mirroring the angel Michael on the right;
וְכֵן אִיתָא בְּמוֹעֵד קָטָן (כ״ה סוֹף עַמּוּד א׳): דִּגְנֵי יְהוּדָה מִימִינֵיהּ וְחִזְקִיָּה מִשְּׂמֹאלֵיהּ;
as stated in Moed Katan (25b): Yehudah was buried to his right and Chizkiyah to his left;
וְזֶה אֲחִיזָתוֹ בְּמִדַּת ״חֶסֶד לְאַבְרָהָם״ (מִיכָה ז:כ), שֶׁהוּא שְׁלֵימוּת כָּל תַּאֲווֹתָיו בִּקְדוּשָׁה לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם;
this being his grasp in the lovingkindness of Avraham, which is the elevation of all physical desires into holiness for the sake of Heaven;
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ: ״תַּאֲוַת אָדָם — חַסְדּוֹ״ (מִשְׁלֵי י״ט:כ״ב), כַּנּוֹדָע.
as the Sages expounded on "the desire of a man is his lovingkindness" (Mishlei 19:22) as is known.
וְעַל כֵּן אָמְרוּ עָלָיו גַּם כֵּן: ״לֹא בִּטֵּל עוֹנָתוֹ״ (כְּתוּבּוֹת ס״ב עַמּוּד ב׳);
Wherefore they stated regarding Yehudah likewise: "he never neglected his onah" (Kesubos 62b);
כִּי לֹא הָיָה לוֹ שׁוּם כַּוָּונָה אַחֶרֶת רַק לְמִצְוַת עוֹנָה;
possessing no ulterior motive save the sacred mitzvah of onah;
וְאָז הֲרֵי הוּא כְּכָל הַמִּצְוֹת שֶׁהֵם הַנּוֹתְנוֹת קְדוּשָׁה בְּלֵב בְּנֵי אָדָם, וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה אַדְּרַבָּא הָיְתָה נִתּוֹסֶפֶת קְדוּשָׁה בְּלִבָּם.
acting like all mitzvos which infuse divine holiness into the heart of man, adding holiness to his soul.
וְזֶהוּ הַסִּימָן לָאָדָם שֶׁהִגִּיעַ לְמַדְרֵיגָה בִּקְדוּשָׁה: שֶׁלֹּא יָכוֹל יִצְרוֹ לְהַתְעוֹתוֹ בְּאֵיזֶה תַּאֲוָה שֶׁאֵין כַּוָּונָתוֹ לְגַרְמֵיהּ רַק לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם;
And this is the true sign that a person has attained a genuine rung of holiness: that his yetzer cannot deceive him with false holy pretenses;
כַּאֲשֶׁר הוּא מַרְגִּישׁ עַל יְדֵי זֶה רוּחַ קְדוּשָׁה מִתְעוֹרֵר בְּקִרְבּוֹ;
when he feels a spirit of holiness reawakening within his interior heart;
כִּי הַמִּצְוֹת מַכְנִיסוֹת קְדוּשָׁה בְּלֵב הָאָדָם לִפְנֵיהֶם וּלְאַחֲרֵיהֶם;
for genuine mitzvos infuse holiness into man's heart before their execution and after their execution;
שֶׁגַּם קוֹדֶם הָעֲשִׂיָּה כְּשֶׁמֵּכִין עַצְמוֹ, מַכְשִׁירֵי מִצְוָה מִכְּלַל הַמִּצְוָה;
for even prior to the deed, preparatory accessories of a mitzvah partake of the mitzvah itself;
שֶׁהֲרֵי לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר (שַׁבָּת ק״ל עַמּוּד א׳): אֲפִילּוּ דּוֹחוֹת שַׁבָּת כְּשֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לַעֲשׂוֹתָם מֵעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת;
wherefore according to Rabbi Eliezer (Shabbat 130a) accessories of circumcision override Shabbat if they could not be prepared beforehand.
וּמִשֶּׁהִגִּיעַ זְמַן הַמִּצְוָה וְחִיּוּב עֲשִׂיָּתָהּ, מַשְׁמַע קְצָת מִדִּבְרֵי הָרַ״ן בְּחִדּוּשָׁיו לְבָבָא מְצִיעָא (ל׳ סוֹף עַמּוּד א׳)
And once the appointed hour of a mitzvah arrives, the Ran (Chiddushim, Bava Metzia 30a) implies;

וְהוּבָא גַּם כֵּן בְּ״נִימּוּקֵי יוֹסֵף״ שָׁם (פֶּרֶק ב׳ דַּף י״ז עַמּוּד ב׳ מִדַּפֵּי הָרִי״ף): דַּהֲלִיכָתוֹ לַעֲשׂוֹתָהּ וְכַיּוֹצֵא מִכְּלַל גּוּף הַמִּצְוָה נֶחְשָׁב לְגַמְרֵי לְדִבְרֵי הַכֹּל לִדְחוֹת לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה;
as cited in the Nimukei Yosef: walking to perform a mitzvah is accounted as the body of the mitzvah, overriding a negative prohibition;

וְעַל כָּל פָּנִים לְדִבְרֵי הַכֹּל, גַּם מַכְשִׁירִין גְּמוּרִים אַף שֶׁאֵינָן מִגּוּף הַמִּצְוָה לִדְחוֹת לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה — מִכָּל מָקוֹם שֵׁם מִצְוָה מִיהַת עֲלֵיהֶן כֵּיוָן דְּהֵם הֲכָנָה לַמִּצְוָה;
and at the very least, preparatory accessories bear the title of mitzvah since they prepare the commandment;
וַהֲרֵי אֲפִילּוּ: ״הַנִּטְפָּל לְעוֹשֵׂי מִצְוָה — כְּעוֹשֵׂי מִצְוָה״, כִּדִתְנַן בְּמַכּוֹת (ה׳ סוֹף עַמּוּד ב׳);
for even one who accompanies those who perform a mitzvah is accounted like the performer (Makkot 5b);
וְהָכִי נַמֵּי דָּבָר הַנִּטְפָּל לְמַעֲשֵׂה הַמִּצְוָה הוּא כְּמִצְוָה לְהַכְנִיס קְדוּשָׁה בְּלִבּוֹ;
and so too an act preparatory to a mitzvah operates like a mitzvah to infuse holiness into his heart;
שֶׁזֶּהוּ הַקִּבּוּל שָׂכָר דְּ״שְׂכַר מִצְוָה — מִצְוָה״ (אָבוֹת ד:ב);
this being the reward of "the reward of a mitzvah is another mitzvah" (Avos 4:2);
דְּעַל יְדֵי הִתְעוֹרְרוּת הַקְּדוּשָׁה בַּלֵּב מִתְעוֹרֵר לְהוֹסִיף מִצְוֹת.
for through the awakening of holiness in the heart one is stirred to perform further commandments.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן כְּשֶׁרוּחַ עִוְעִים הִתְעָהוּ, שֶׁהוּא הִיפּוּךְ הַקְּדוּשָׁה שֶׁאֵינָהּ אֶלָּא עַל יְדֵי הַגְדָּרָה וְרִיחוּק מִתַּאֲווֹת, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנִּתְבָּאֵר:
Unlike when a spirit of delusion has misled him, which is the antithesis of holiness that is attained solely through rigorous fences and distancing from bodily lusts, exactly as explained!

5.h: יִשְׂרָאֵל קְדוֹשִׁים — פֶּרֶק ה׳
אוֹת א׳ — מַעֲלַת רַבֵּינוּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ וְהִלֵּל הַזָּקֵן: כָּל מַעֲשָׂיו לְשֵׁם שָׁמָיִם — Section 1: The Level of Rabbeinu HaKadosh and Hillel: All Deeds for Heaven

The theme: Consummate holiness through elevating worldly pleasure, Rabbeinu HaKadosh tasting no bodily delight, and Hillel feeding the soul. The zenith of authentic holiness is achieved when a person reaches that sublime rung where he can engage in all physical pleasures in holiness, completely devoid of self-interest (le-garmeih) or bodily indulgence. Rabbeinu HaKadosh (Rabbi Yehudah HaNasi) testified upon his passing: "I did not derive pleasure from this world even with my little finger" (Kesubos 104a). Tosafos explains that no delicacies entered his physical frame; yet in Avodah Zarah (11a) the Gemara states that radish and lettuce never ceased from his table winter and summer, Tosafos noting that radishes were consumed to open the intestines to take in additional delicacies. Commentators struggled to reconcile these statements. In absolute truth, Rebbe's table was laden with every worldly delicacy, yet he personally derived zero corporeal enjoyment from them. He ate in supreme holiness, his title "holy" denoting that all his actions were dedicated purely to Heaven, feeling no bodily gratification. This mirrors Hillel the Elder in Vayikra Rabbah (34:3), who described eating as "bestowing kindness upon this poor guest in the body". The soul suffers great humiliation by being clothed in a coarse physical frame of dust, unable to receive spiritual vitality except through the garment of physical eating and drinking. Hillel ate on weekdays with the holiness and spiritual focus of Shabbat (Beitzah 16a), his weekday activities being sanctified so that no distinction existed between secular and holy. This is the mystery in the Zohar (Korach 179b): "the Shechinah never departs from Israel, even on secular workdays", resting upon the heart of one who makes his weekdays like Shabbat. In Raya Mehemna (Tzav 29b), scholars are called Sabbaths and festivals; all Israel possesses holiness and a portion in the World to Come (Sanhedrin 90a), which is the soul's capacity to transcend physical appetites (Berachos 17a).

p: וְעִיקַּר הַקְּדוּשָׁה הַגְּמוּרָה הוּא כְּשֶׁהִגִּיעַ לְמַדְרֵיגָה זוֹ הַגְּדוֹלָה
And the primary essence of consummate holiness is when one reaches this exalted spiritual rung;
שֶׁיּוּכַל לְהִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ בְּכָל הֲנָאוֹתָיו בִּקְדוּשָׁה בְּלֹא כַּוָּונָה לְגַרְמֵיהּ וַהֲנָאַת גּוּפוֹ
that he is empowered to utilize all his pleasures in holiness, without any intent for self-gratification or the pleasure of his body;
וְרַבֵּינוּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ אָמַר עַל עַצְמוֹ (כְּתוּבּוֹת ק״ד עַמּוּד א׳): ״שֶׁלֹּא נֶהֱנָה בְּאֶצְבַּע קְטַנָּה״
and our holy Master [Rabbi Yehudah HaNasi] testified concerning himself (Kesubos 104a): "that he derived no pleasure from this world even with his little finger";
עַיֵּין שָׁם בְּתוֹסָפוֹת: ״שֶׁלֹּא נִכְנְסוּ מַעֲדַנִּים לְגוּפוֹ״
see Tosafos there: "that delicacies never entered his physical frame".
וּבַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה (י״א עַמּוּד א׳): ״דְּלֹא פָסַק מֵעַל שֻׁלְחָנוֹ לֹא [צְנוֹן וְלֹא חַזֶּרֶת] וְכוּלֵיהּ״
And yet in Avodah Zarah (11a) the Gemara states: "neither radish nor lettuce ever ceased from his table, etc.";
עַיֵּין שָׁם בְּתוֹסָפוֹת (דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל: ״שֶׁלֹּא״), שֶׁהוּא לְהַרְחִיב בְּנֵי מֵעַיִם לְרִיבּוּי הַמַּעֲדַנִּים
see Tosafos there (s.v. Shelo): that radishes were eaten to open the intestines for consuming abundant delicacies;
וּבְדִבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל ״צְנוֹן״ נִתְקַשּׁוּ מֵהַהוּא דִּכְתוּבּוֹת
and in the heading beginning with Tzenon, the Tosafists were challenged by that statement in Kesubos;
וְתֵירֵץ בְּדוֹחַק: שֶׁלְּשׁוֹן ״שֻׁלְחָנָם״ מַשְׁמַע דְּגַם הוּא אָכַל כֵּן
and answered with difficulty: that the phrasing "their table" implies that Rebbe himself ate thus;
וְגַם לָמָּה יַרְבֶּה מַעֲדַנִּים כָּל כָּךְ לִבְנֵי בֵיתוֹ אִם הוּא לֹא חָפֵץ וְשֶׁאֵין רָאוּי, וְגַם דִּמְדַמֶּה לְאַנְטוֹנִינוּס
and furthermore, why would he provide so many delicacies for his household if he did not desire them and deemed it unfitting, and especially since he was compared to the Roman emperor Antoninus?
אֲבָל הָאֱמֶת כְּמוֹ שֶׁקִּבַּלְתִּי, וְכֵן רָאִיתִי אַחַר כָּךְ בְּאֵיזֶה סֵפֶר, דְּהַפֵּירוּשׁ כִּפְשָׁטוֹ
But the truth is as I received by tradition, and likewise saw later in a certain sacred book, that the matter is according to its literal sense;
וְאַף שֶׁהָיָה שֻׁלְחָנוֹ מָלֵא כָּל מַעֲדַנֵּי עוֹלָם, מִכָּל מָקוֹם הוּא לֹא נֶהֱנָה מִזֶּה כְּלָל
and though his royal table was laden with all the delicacies of the world, he derived no bodily pleasure from them whatsoever;
דְּהַיְינוּ דְּכָל אֲכִילָתוֹ הָיָה בִּקְדוּשָׁה יְתֵירָה כְּמִדָּתוֹ דְּנִקְרָא ״קָדוֹשׁ״
meaning that his entire eating was in supreme holiness according to his spiritual trait, being designated "holy";
שֶׁהוּא שְׁלֵימוּת הַקְּדוּשָׁה: לִהְיוֹת כָּל מַעֲשָׂיו וַהֲנָאוֹתָיו לְשֵׁם שָׁמָיִם, וְלֹא הִרְגִּישׁ הֲנָאַת עַצְמוֹ כְּלָל
which is the perfection of holiness: that all his deeds and pleasures are for the sake of Heaven, experiencing no self-gratification at all;
רַק עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּוַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ל״ד (סִימָן ג׳) בְּהִלֵּל: ״לִגְמוֹל חֶסֶד עִם הָדֵין אַכְסְנַאי וְכוּלֵיהּ״
but only after the manner stated in Vayikra Rabbah (34:3) regarding Hillel: "I go to perform kindness with this guest in the body, etc.";
וְקָאֵי עַל אֲכִילָתוֹ שֶׁהוּא לְהַחֲיוֹת הַנֶּפֶשׁ
which refers to his eating, whose purpose is to sustain the soul.
וּמִתְיַיחֵס אֶל הַנֶּפֶשׁ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּמְנִיעַת הָאֲכִילָה: ״וְעִנִּיתֶם אֶת נַפְשֹׁתֵיכֶם״ (וַיִּקְרָא כ״ג:כ״ז)
And nourishment relates directly to the soul, as stated regarding the withholding of food on Yom Kippur: "and you shall afflict your souls" (Vayikra 23:27);
אַךְ הִלֵּל לֹא הִרְגִּישׁ הֲנָאַת הַגּוּף, אֶלָּא ״מוֹצָא פִי ה׳״ (דְּבָרִים ח:ג) הַמְחַיֶּה הָדֵין נַפְשָׁא עֲלוּבְתָא
but Hillel did not feel the corporeal pleasure of the body, but rather the word that issues from the mouth of Hashem which vitalizes this impoverished soul;

(שֶׁזֶּה עֶלְבּוֹן גָּדוֹל לָהּ מַה שֶּׁהִיא מִתְלַבֶּשֶׁת בַּגּוּף הֶעָכוּר וְהַגַּשְׁמִי ״עָפָר מִן הָאֲדָמָה״, עַד שֶׁלֹּא תַּשִּׂיג הָרוּחָנִיּוּת לְהַחֲיוֹת אֶלָּא דֶּרֶךְ לְבוּשׁ הַגַּשְׁמִי שֶׁל אֲכִילָה וּשְׁתִיָּה דְּבָרִים גַּשְׁמִיִּים)

(it being a profound humiliation for the heavenly soul to be clothed within a murky, physical body fashioned from the dust of the earth, unable to draw spiritual life except through the physical garments of material food and drink);
הָאַכְסְנָאוּת גּוֹ גּוּפָא, עַל כֵּן נִקְרָא ״גּוֹמֵל נַפְשׁוֹ״
which soul is a temporary sojourning guest within the physical frame, wherefore Hillel called this "bestowing kindness upon his soul" (Mishlei 11:17).
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ גַּם כֵּן בְּבֵיצָה (ט״ז עַמּוּד א׳): ״אֲבָל הִלֵּל הַזָּקֵן — מִדָּה אַחֶרֶת הָיְתָה לוֹ, שֶׁכָּל מַעֲשָׂיו לְשֵׁם שָׁמָיִם״
And this is what the Sages stated in Beitzah (16a): "but Hillel the Elder had a different attribute, for all his deeds were for the sake of Heaven";
רָצָה לוֹמַר: שֶׁלֹּא הִנִּיחַ הֲנָאָה לְשַׁבָּת כְּשַׁמַּאי
meaning: he did not reserve food exclusively for the delight of Shabbat like Shammai;
כִּי הוּא הָיָה אוֹכֵל גַּם בִּימוֹת הַחוֹל עַל טָהֳרַת קֹדֶשׁ, לִהְיוֹת כָּל מַאֲכָלוֹ בִּקְדוּשָׁה וְרוּחָנִיּוּת הַמַּאֲכָל כִּבְשַׁבָּת
for he ate even during secular weekdays in consecrated purity, his food imbued with the holiness and spirituality of the Sabbath;
וְזֶה נִקְרָא ״כָּל מַעֲשָׂיו לְשֵׁם שָׁמָיִם״, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְעֵיל שֶׁמִּי שֶׁהוּא כֵן אֵין צָרִיךְ פְּרִישׁוּת, כִּי גַּם כָּל הֲנָאוֹתָיו לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם וְלֹא לְגַרְמֵיהּ

and this is termed "all his deeds are for the sake of Heaven," as I wrote above that one who attains this level does not require ascetic abstinence, his pleasures being for Heaven and not for self-indulgence.
וְזֶהוּ ״כָּל מַעֲשָׂיו״: גַּם מַה שֶּׁנִּרְאֶה כְּמַעֲשֶׂה לַהֲנָאָתוֹ הָיָה בֶּאֱמֶת לְשֵׁם שָׁמָיִם
And this is the depth of "all his deeds": even that which appears outwardly as self-gratification was in truth purely for Heaven;
וּמִי שֶׁהוּא כָּךְ, גַּם כָּל דִּבְרֵי הָרְשׁוּת שֶׁלּוֹ הַכֹּל קָדוֹשׁ, וְאֵין אֶצְלוֹ חִילּוּק בֵּין חוֹל לְשַׁבָּת
and one who abides in this state, all his optional, mundane activities are entirely holy, recognizing no division between the secular and the Sabbath.
וְנִרְאֶה דְּעַל זֶה רָמְזוּ בַּזֹּוהַר (חֵלֶק ג׳ קע״ט עַמּוּד ב׳) סוֹף פָּרָשַׁת קֹרַח: ״לָא זָזָה שְׁכִינְתָּא מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל, וַאֲפִילּוּ בְּשַׁבְּתוֹת דְּחוֹל״
And it appears that this is what the Zohar hinted at (III, 179b) at the end of Parashat Korach: "the Shechinah never departs from Israel, even on secular Sabbaths";
(וְעַיֵּין בְּ״פָּרָשַׁת דְּרָכִים״ דַּף כ״ג, עַיֵּין שָׁם, וּבְסוֹף סֵפֶר ״מִדְרַשׁ אֵלִיָּהוּ״)
(and see Parashat Derachim, leaf 23, and at the end of the book Midrash Eliyahu);
רָצָה לוֹמַר: מִי שֶׁעוֹשֶׂה חוֹלוֹ כְּשַׁבָּת לִהְיוֹת כּוּלּוֹ לַה׳, תָּמִיד שׁוֹבֵת מִכָּל מְלָאכוֹת יְמֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה וְעוּבְדִין דְּחוֹל
meaning: one who transforms his secular weekdays into Shabbat to be entirely dedicated to Hashem, resting continually from mundane labors and secular affairs;
וְכָל עִסְקוֹ רַק בַּתּוֹרָה וַעֲבוֹדַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם, אֵין הַשְּׁכִינָה זָזָה מִכָּתְלֵי לְבָבוֹ
his entire occupation being Torah and divine service for the sake of Heaven, the Shechinah never departs from the walls of his heart;
לְקַדְּשׁוֹ עַל יְדֵי זֶה מִלְּמַעְלָה בִּקְדוּשָׁה הַיְתֵירָה עַל יְדֵי הַשְׁרָאַת שְׁכִינָה בְּקֶרֶב לִבּוֹ
sanctifying him from Above with supreme holiness through the resting of the Shechinah within his heart;
שֶׁיִּרְאֶה בְּכָל עִנְיְנֵי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה אֵיךְ כִּבְיָכוֹל שְׁכִינָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּתוֹכָם וְהוּא הַמְחַיֶּה כוּלָּם
perceiving in all matters of this world how the Shechinah resides within them and vitalizes them all.
וְהוּא מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ בְּ״רַעְיָא מְהֵימְנָא״ פָּרָשַׁת צַו (כ״ט עַמּוּד ב׳): ״דְּתַלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים — כְּיוֹם שַׁבָּת וְכוּלֵיהּ״
And this is what the Sages stated in the Raya Mehemna (Tzav 29b): "Torah scholars are likened unto the Sabbath day, etc.";
״וְנֶפֶשׁ דְּתַלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים אִתְקְרִיאַת ׳שַׁבָּת מַלְכְּתָא׳, נֶפֶשׁ יְתֵירָה דְּשַׁבָּת וְכוּלֵיהּ״
"and the soul of Torah scholars is designated 'Shabbat the Queen', the additional soul of Shabbat, etc.";
״וְהָכִי תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים בְּנוֹי דְּמַלְכָּא וּמַטְרוֹנִיתָא, אִתְקְרִיאוּ שַׁבָּתוֹת וְיָמִים טוֹבִים וְכוּלֵיהּ״
"and so Torah scholars, the children of the King and the Matronita, are called Sabbaths and festivals, etc.";
״כָּל מַה דְּעָבַד בַּר נָשׁ לְשַׁבָּתוֹת וְיָמִים טוֹבִים אִית לְמֶעְבַּד לוֹן וְכוּלֵיהּ״
"all that a man performs to honor Sabbaths and festivals he is obligated to perform for them, etc.";
וְסִיֵּים שָׁם: ״וּכְגַוְונָא דְּכָל מָאנֵי בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ אִתְקְרִיאוּ ׳קֹדֶשׁ׳, הָכִי כָּל אִינּוּן דִּמְשַׁמְּשֵׁי תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים אִתְקְרִיאוּ ׳קֹדֶשׁ׳״
and concludes there: "and just as all vessels of the Holy Temple are called 'holy', so all who attend unto Torah scholars are called 'holy'";
״וְתַלְמוּדִין דְּרַב דְּאִינּוּן לָקֳבֵל אֵיבָרִין דְּגוּפֵיהּ אִתְקְרִיאוּ ׳קֹדֶשׁ קָדָשִׁים׳ וְכוּלֵיהּ״, עַיֵּין שָׁם
"and the disciples of a master, corresponding to the limbs of his body, are designated 'Holy of Holies, etc.,'" see there.
הַיְינוּ דְּבֶאֱמֶת כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל יֵשׁ בָּהֶם קְדוּשָׁה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״קֹדֶשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל [לַה׳] וְגוֹמֵר״ (יִרְמְיָה ב:ג)
Meaning that in truth all Israel possess inherent holiness, as it is said: "Israel is holy unto Hashem, etc." (Yirmiyah 2:3);
וּלְכוּלָּם נֶאֱמַר: ״וְהִתְקַדִּשְׁתֶּם וִהְיִיתֶם קְדֹשִׁים״ (וַיִּקְרָא י״א:מ״ד), ״קְדֹשִׁים תִּהְיוּ״ (שָׁם י״ט:ב׳), וְכָל סִדְרֵי קְדוּשָׁה
and unto all of them it was declared: "and you shall sanctify yourselves and be holy" (Vayikra 11:44), "You shall be holy" (ibid. 19:2), and all orders of holiness;
שֶׁהֲרֵי: ״כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל יֵשׁ לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא״, כִּדִתְנַן רֵישׁ פֶּרֶק חֵלֶק (סַנְהֶדְרִין צ׳ עַמּוּד א׳)
for "all Israel have a portion in the World to Come," as taught at the beginning of Perek Chelek (Sanhedrin 90a);
וְחֵלֶק זֶה הוּא חֵלֶק הַקְּדוּשָׁה שֶׁבְּקִרְבּוֹ שֶׁאֵין לוֹ שׁוּם הֲנָאָה מֵעִינּוּגֵי וְחֶמְדוֹת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה
and this portion is the core of holiness within the Jew that derives no pleasure from the physical lusts of this world;
שֶׁזֶּהוּ הַחֵלֶק שֶׁל עוֹלָם הַבָּא, שֶׁהוּא עוֹלָם שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ אֲכִילָה וְלֹא שְׁתִיָּה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרָכוֹת (י״ז עַמּוּד א׳)
which constitutes the reality of the World to Come, being a world devoid of eating and drinking, as stated in Berachos (17a);
שֶׁאֵין שָׁם שׁוּם הֲנָאָה גּוּפָנִית דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה כְּלָל:
wherein no corporeal physical pleasure of this world exists at all!
אוֹת ב׳ — ״יִשְׂרָאֵל קְדוֹשִׁים הֵם״ וְהַנְהָגַת רַבִּי פִּנְחָס בֶּן יָאִיר — Section 2: "Israel Are Holy" and the Piety of Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair

The theme: The definition of Israel's holiness in Chullin (7b), and the heavenly guardianship over the donkey of Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair. The Gemara in Chullin (7b) states: "Israel are holy: there is one who desires to give but lacks means, and there is one who possesses means but does not desire to give". Tosafos struggled to explain why a miserly person who possesses means but refuses to give is designated "holy". Furthermore, regarding one who desires but lacks means, generosity is not synonymous with holiness, which denotes abstinence from carnal desires. Additionally, Rashi explains that because Israel are holy, one is permitted to partake of their food; why should holiness be required for this, rather than merely avoiding unrepentant sinners who amass wealth unjustly? The Talmud introduces this principle regarding Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair and his donkey, which refused to eat untithed grain (tevel) even under extreme hunger (Chullin 7a; Shabbat 112b). Midrash Bereishis Rabbah (60:8) notes that Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair was uniquely preeminent among the Tannaim in meticulous scrupulousness regarding food, to the extent that even his animal was protected by Heaven from eating prohibited matter!
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּחֻלִּין (ז׳ עַמּוּד ב׳): ״יִשְׂרָאֵל קְדוֹשִׁים הֵם: יֵשׁ שֶׁרוֹצֶה וְאֵין לוֹ, וְיֵשׁ שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ וְאֵינוֹ רוֹצֶה וְכוּלֵיהּ״
And this explains what the Sages stated in Chullin (7b): "Israel are holy: there is one who desires to give but has not, and there is one who has but does not desire to give, etc.";
דְּכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל כּוּלָּם נִקְרָאִים ״קְדוֹשִׁים״
that all Israel without exception are designated "holy";
וְעַיֵּין שָׁם בְּתוֹסָפוֹת שֶׁנִּדְחֲקוּ: אַמַּאי נִקְרָא ״קָדוֹשׁ״ זֶה שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ וְאֵינוֹ רוֹצֶה?
and see Tosafos there who struggled: why is one who possesses means but refuses to give called "holy"?
וּבֶאֱמֶת גַּם עַל זֶה שֶׁרוֹצֶה וְאֵין לוֹ יֵשׁ לְדַקְדֵּק: לָמָּה קְרָאוֹ ״קָדוֹשׁ״ בַּעֲבוּר זֶה?
And in truth regarding one who desires to give but lacks means one must likewise analyze: why is he termed "holy" on this account?
וְאֵין הַנְּדִיבוּת מִגִּדְרֵי הַקְּדוּשָׁה, אֶלָּא הַפְּרִישׁוּת מִתַּאֲווֹת
for generosity does not belong to the definitions of holiness, holiness denoting abstinence from carnal lusts.
גַּם עִיקַּר הַשֵּׁם ״קְדוֹשִׁים״ דְּעַל יְדֵי זֶה רְאוּיִים לֵיהָנוֹת כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב רַשִׁ״י שָׁם (דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל: ״מִיַּמַּי״), צָרִיךְ בֵּיאוּר: מַה צֹּרֶךְ קְדוּשָׁה לָזֶה?
Furthermore, the designation "holy" which renders them worthy that one partake of their food, as Rashi wrote there, requires explanation: why is holiness required for this?
וְלָמָּה לֹא יוּכַל לֵיהָנוֹת גַּם מִמִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ קָדוֹשׁ, וְדַי אִם לֹא יִרְצֶה לֵיהָנוֹת מֵרִשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הָעוֹשִׂים עֹשֶׁר וְלֹא בְּמִשְׁפָּט וְכַיּוֹצֵא?
And why should a pious man not partake of the food of an ordinary Jew who is not "holy," it being sufficient to decline eating only from the wicked who amass wealth unjustly?
אֲבָל עִנְיַן רַבִּי פִּנְחָס בֶּן יָאִיר דְּמַיְיתֵי לֵיהּ שָׁם לְעִנְיַן בְּהֶמְתָּן שֶׁל צַדִּיקִים מֵחֲמוֹרוֹ
But the episode of Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair, cited there regarding the animals of the righteous through the conduct of his donkey;
וְלָקוּחַ מִזֶּה מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ בְּשַׁבָּת (קי״ב עַמּוּד ב׳): ״אָנוּ כַּחֲמוֹרִים, וְלֹא כַּחֲמוֹרוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי פִּנְחָס בֶּן יָאִיר״, עַיֵּין שָׁם בְּרַשִׁ״י
whence the Sages derived the aphorism in Shabbat (112b): "we are like donkeys, and not even like the donkey of Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair," see Rashi there;
וּבְתוֹסָפוֹת שָׁם (דַּף י״ב עַמּוּד ב׳ דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל: ״רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל״) זֶה בְּשֵׁם הַבְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה ס׳:ח׳)
and in Tosafos (Shabbat 12b) citing Bereishis Rabbah (60:8);
דְּמַשְׁמַע שֶׁהוּא הָיָה הַמְיוּחָד בָּזֶה בְּכָל הַתַּנָּאִים בְּתֹקֶף הַזְּהִירוּת בְּמִידֵי דַּאֲכִילָה, עַד שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ חֲמוֹרוֹ הָיָה שָׁמוּר בָּזֶה מִן הַשָּׁמָיִם:
implying that he was uniquely preeminent among all the Tannaim in meticulous vigilance concerning food, such that even his donkey was preserved from on High!

5.h: אוֹת ג׳ — שְׁבִיתַת בְּהֶמְתּוֹ וְהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת הַקְּדוּשָׁה אֶל הַקִּנְיָנִים הַחָמְרִיִּים — Section 3: The Rest of One's Animal and the Expansion of Holiness unto Possessions

The theme: Divine protection extending to physical possessions, the Sabbath rest of animals, and the World to Come. When a tzaddik consecrates himself below to the utmost of his capacity, Heaven sanctifies him from Above, shielding him in areas where he cannot guard himself. This divine protection expands so comprehensively that it envelops even his material possessions and livestock, fulfilling "I Hashem do sanctify them" (Vayikra 21:8). This mirrors the sanctity of Shabbat, concerning which it is written: "that your ox and your ass may rest" (Shemos 23:12), commanding the rest of one's domestic animals because the holiness of Shabbat expands into them. Mortal man cannot independently infuse holiness into beasts; this occurs only through the sanctity of Shabbat consecrated directly by Hashem. Shabbat is a foretaste of the World to Come—a world that is entirely Shabbat—wherein evil and impurity are eradicated, making it manifest to all that everything derives from His holiness.

p: וְזֶהוּ עַל יְדֵי הַהִתְקַדְּשׁוּת מִלְּמַעְלָה לְשָׁמְרוֹ בַּמַּה שֶּׁהוּא עַצְמוֹ לֹא יָכוֹל לְהִשָּׁמֵר
And this occurs through the supernal sanctification from Above, guarding him in matters where he cannot protect himself through his own power;
וּבְהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת כָּל כָּךְ עַד שֶׁהִגִּיעָה גַּם לִקְנְיָנָיו הַחָמְרִיִּים
expanding so extensively that it reaches even his material possessions;
שֶׁזֶּהוּ תַּכְלִית הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת הַקְּדוּשָׁה שֶׁמִּלְּמַעְלָה: ״[כִּי] אֲנִי ה׳ מְקַדִּשְׁכֶם״ (וַיִּקְרָא כ:ח)
this being the ultimate perimeter of supernal holiness from Above: "that I am Hashem Who sanctifies you";
כְּעִנְיַן קְדֻשַּׁת שַׁבָּת דִּכְתִיב בֵּיהּ: ״לְמַעַן יָנוּחַ שׁוֹרְךָ וַחֲמֹרֶךָ [וְיִנָּפֵשׁ בֶּן אֲמָתְךָ וְהַגֵּר]״ (שְׁמוֹת כ״ג:י״ב)
like the sanctity of Shabbat regarding which it is written: "that your ox and your ass may rest, etc." (Shemos 23:12);
וּמְצֻוֶּוה עַל שְׁבִיתַת בְּהֶמְתּוֹ, שֶׁהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת הַקְּדוּשָׁה הוּא גַּם בָּהֶם
man being commanded regarding the resting of his animal, the expansion of Sabbath sanctity encompassing them as well.
דְּדָבָר זֶה אִי אֶפְשָׁר לָאָדָם לְקַדְּשׁוֹ וּלְהַכְנִיס קְדוּשָׁה בְּבַעֲלֵי חַיִּים כְּלָל
For this is impossible for mortal man to consecrate, being unable to infuse holiness into animals on his own;
רַק בִּקְדֻשַּׁת הַשַּׁבָּת ״קֹדֶשׁ לַה׳״ שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מְקַדְּשׁוֹ
but occurring solely through the sanctity of Shabbat, "holy unto Hashem," which the Blessed Name consecrates;
דְּהוּא ״מֵעֵין עוֹלָם הַבָּא״ (בְּרָכוֹת נ״ז עַמּוּד א׳), ״עוֹלָם שֶׁכּוּלּוֹ שַׁבָּת״ (תָּמִיד פֶּרֶק ז׳ מִשְׁנָה ד׳) שֶׁהוּא כּוּלּוֹ קֹדֶשׁ
being a foretaste of the World to Come, "the day that is entirely Shabbat" which is completely holy;
דְּנִתְבַּטֵּל הָרָע וְהַטּוּמְאָה מִן הָעוֹלָם, וְיִהְיֶה נִיכָּר לַכֹּל אֵיךְ הַכֹּל נִמְשָׁךְ מִקְּדֻשָּׁתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ:
wherein evil and defilement are eradicated from the universe, making it evident unto all how everything is drawn from His holiness!

5.h: אוֹת ד׳ — סוֹד הַהַבְדָּלָה, קְדֻשַּׁת אַהֲרֹן כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל, וְקוֹמַת הָאֵבָרִים דִּכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל — Section 4: The Mystery of Havdalah, Aharon's Sanctity, and the Corporate Body of Israel

The theme: The Havdalah between holy and secular, the etymology of Kedushah, and collective Israel as one corporate stature. Shabbat is the "good gift" given to Israel as a sign ("that you may know that I am Hashem that sanctifies you", Shemos 31:13). A righteous man like Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair, who is granted a foretaste of his reward in this world (Kiddushin 39b), merits this perpetual flow because he sanctified his eating below, engaging in ransoming captives. The fundamental distinction between Israel and the nations is holiness, for the nations embody the antithesis of holiness. This is expressed in Havdalah: "Who separates between holy and secular... between Israel and the nations". Holiness (kedushah) denotes absolute separation, like consecrated property (hekdesh) from which all are distanced (Pesachim 6a), and betrothal (kiddushin) which prohibits a woman unto the world (Kiddushin 2b). In Parashat Kedoshim it states: "And you shall be holy unto Me, and I have separated you from the nations" (Vayikra 20:26); Torat Kohanim and Rashi comment: "If you are separated from them, you are Mine; if not, you belong to Nebuchadnezzar and his companions". Although Hashem separates us, man must initiate this separation below through effort. When Israel sanctifies itself, no foreign nation can dominate them, for dominion occurs only where a commonality with evil exists. When Aharon died and the Clouds of Glory departed, the king of Arad attacked and took captives (Rosh Hashanah 3a), because Aharon was consecrated as Holy of Holies (I Divrei HaYamim 23:13), entering the Holy of Holies where no mortal or angel may enter (Vayikra 16:17; Yerushalmi Yoma 1:5). All Israel forms a single organic corporate body (koma sheleimah): the heart is the source of life; the brain and lungs are vital organs upon which life depends; the liver sustains life even when perforated; the kidneys cause suffering when afflicted without terminating life; external wounds cause temporary pain; while nails and hair feel no pain, being superfluities. Yet even the fingernail is called the nail of a human, receiving its life-force from the heart!

p: וְזֶהוּ ״הַמַּתָּנָה טוֹבָה״ דְּשַׁבָּת שֶׁנָּתַן הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְיִשְׂרָאֵל: ״אוֹת הִוא בֵּינִי וּבֵינֵיכֶם... כִּי אֲנִי ה׳ מְקַדִּשְׁכֶם״ (שְׁמוֹת ל״א:י״ג), ״[וְ]לֹא עָשָׂה כֵן לְכָל גּוֹי״ (תְּהִלִּים קמ״ז:כ׳)

And this is the "good gift" of Shabbat that the Holy One bestowed upon Israel: "it is a sign between Me and you... that you may know that I am Hashem that sanctifies you" (Shemos 31:13), "He has not dealt so with any nation" (Tehillim 147:20);
וּלְאָדָם שֶׁטּוֹב כְּרַבִּי פִּנְחָס בֶּן יָאִיר שֶׁמַּטְעִימִין לוֹ מִפְּרִי מַעֲשָׂיו דְּעוֹלָם הַבָּא בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה (קִדּוּשִׁין מ׳ עַמּוּד ב׳)
and unto a good man like Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair who is given a foretaste of the fruits of his deeds of the World to Come in this world (Kiddushin 40b);
זוֹכֶה לְשֶׁפַע קְדוּשָׁה זוֹ תָּמִיד, עַל יְדֵי שֶׁכְּבָר הִתְקַדֵּשׁ עַצְמוֹ מִלְּמַטָּה בְּכָל יְכוֹלְתּוֹ, שֶׁיִּהְיוּ כָּל אֲכִילוֹתָיו וַהֲנָאוֹתָיו קֹדֶשׁ לַה׳
he merits this flow of holiness continually, having sanctified himself below to the utmost of his power, so that all his eating and physical pleasures are holy unto Hashem;
וְזֶה הָיָה עִסְקוֹ בְּפִדְיוֹן שְׁבוּיִם
and this was his holy occupation in ransoming captives.
כִּי עִיקַּר הַהַבְדָּלָה בֵּין יִשְׂרָאֵל לָעַמִּים הוּא עַל יְדֵי הַקְּדוּשָׁה, שֶׁהֵם הִיפּוּךְ הַקְּדוּשָׁה
For the essential separation between Israel and the nations is through holiness, the nations being the antithesis of holiness;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאוֹמְרִים בְּסֵדֶר הַבְדָּלוֹת: ״הַמַּבְדִּיל בֵּין קֹדֶשׁ לְחוֹל... וּבֵין יִשְׂרָאֵל לָעַמִּים״
and as we recite in the Havdalah: "Who separates between holy and secular... and between Israel and the nations";
וְהוּא עַצְמוֹ הַהַבְדָּלָה דְּבֵין יוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי לְשֵׁשֶׁת יְמֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה וּבֵין אוֹר לְחֹשֶׁךְ
which is identical with the separation between the seventh day and the six workdays, and between light and darkness;
וְהַתְחָלַת הַכֹּל וְעִיקָּרָם הוּא הַהַבְדָּלָה דְּבֵין קֹדֶשׁ לְחוֹל
the inception and foundation of all being the separation between holy and secular;
שֶׁזֶּהוּ עִיקַּר כָּל הַהֶבְדֵּלִים: שֶׁזֶּה מִסִּטְרָא דִּקְדוּשָׁה וְשַׁיָּיךְ לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, דְּ״קָדוֹשׁ אֲנִי ה׳״ (וַיִּקְרָא כ:כו) וְדָבֵק בּוֹ, וְזֶה מִסִּטְרָא דִּמְסָאֲבָא
for this is the root of all divisions: this side deriving from holiness and belonging to Hashem ("for I Hashem am holy") cleaved unto Him, while that side derives from defilement.
וְזֶה כָּל עִיקַּר לְשׁוֹן ״קְדוּשָׁה״, כְּ״הֶקְדֵּשׁ״ דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא בְּדִילֵי מִינֵּיהּ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּפְסָחִים (ו׳ עַמּוּד א׳)
And this is the primary meaning of "holiness" (kedushah), like consecrated property (hekdesh) from which the entire world is separated, as stated in Pesachim (6a);
וְכֵן ״קִדּוּשֵׁי אִשָּׁה״ דַּאֲסַר לַהּ אַכּוּלֵי עָלְמָא כְּהֶקְדֵּשׁ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּקִדּוּשִׁין (ב׳ עַמּוּד ב׳)
and so "betrothal of a woman" (kiddushin), which prohibits her unto the entire world like consecrated property, as stated in Kiddushin (2b);
וּבְתוֹסָפוֹת שָׁם: דִּפְשָׁטֵיהּ לְשׁוֹן הַזְמָנָה וְיִחוּד לוֹ
and in Tosafos there: its plain meaning is an expression of designating and setting aside uniquely for him;
וְהָא בְּהָא תַּלְיָא, דְּעַל יְדֵי זֶה שֶׁמְּיוּחֶדֶת לוֹ הִיא מוּבְדֶּלֶת מֵאֲחֵרִים
and the two concepts are interdependent, for by being uniquely designated unto him she is set apart from others;
וְכֵן הֶקְדֵּשׁ הַמְיוּחָד לַשָּׁמַיִם וּבָדִיל מִכּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא, וְכֵן יִשְׂרָאֵל ״קֹדֶשׁ לַה׳״ וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה בְּדוּלִים מִכָּל הָעַמִּים
and so consecrated property is designated unto Heaven and separated from all mortals, and so Israel is "holy unto Hashem" and thereby separated from all the nations.
וּמִקְרָא מְפוֹרָשׁ הוּא בְּסוֹף פָּרָשַׁת קְדוֹשִׁים: ״וִהְיִיתֶם לִי קְדֹשִׁים... וָאַבְדִּל אֶתְכֶם מִן הָעַמִּים [לִהְיוֹת לִי]״ (וַיִּקְרָא כ:כו), דְּעַל יְדֵי זֶה הוּא הַהַבְדָּלָה

And it is an explicit verse at the end of Parashat Kedoshim: "And you shall be holy unto Me... and I have separated you from the peoples, that you should be Mine" (Vayikra 20:26), for through holiness comes separation;
וּבְתוֹרַת כֹּהֲנִים שָׁם, וּמְבִיאוֹ רַשִׁ״י שָׁם: ״אִם מוּבְדָּלִים אַתֶּם [הֲרֵי אַתֶּם שֶׁלִּי, וְאִם לָאו] — הֲרֵי אַתֶּם שֶׁל נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּר וַחֲבֵירָיו וְכוּלֵיהּ״
and in Torat Kohanim, cited by Rashi there: "If you are separated from the nations, you are Mine; but if not, behold you belong to Nebuchadnezzar and his companions";
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלְּשׁוֹן הַכָּתוּב ״וָאַבְדִּל״, שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הוּא הַמַּבְדִּיל, וְלֹא אָמַר בִּלְשׁוֹן צִיוּוּי ״שֶׁתַּבְדִּילוּ עַצְמֵיכֶם״
and although Scripture states "and I have separated you," where Hashem is the One Who separates, rather than commanding "separate yourselves";
וְכֵן רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה דָּיְיקוּ לִישָׁנָא: ״אִם מוּבְדָּלִים״ — מַשְׁמַע מֵעַצְמוֹ
and our Sages precisely phrased it: "if you are separated"—implying an existing state;
מִכָּל מָקוֹם שַׁיָּיךְ עַל זֶה עֹונֶשׁ ״אִם לָאו״, כִּי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מוּכָן תָּמִיד לְהַבְדִּילָם לִהְיוֹת לוֹ
nevertheless punishment applies "if not," because the Blessed Name is always prepared to separate them unto Himself;
כִּי ״יַעֲקֹב בָּחַר לוֹ [יָהּ, יִשְׂרָאֵל לִסְגֻלָּתוֹ]״ (תְּהִלִּים קל״ה:ד׳)
for "Hashem has chosen Jacob unto Himself, and Israel for His own treasure" (Tehillim 135:4);
וְאֵין לְהַקְשׁוֹת: ״וְאַתֶּם תִּהְיוּ לִי [מַמְלֶכֶת כֹּהֲנִים] וְגוֹי קָדוֹשׁ״ (שְׁמוֹת י״ט:ו׳), וְנֶאֱמַר: ״כִּי לִי בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל [עֲבָדִים]״ (וַיִּקְרָא כ״ה:נ״ה)
and one cannot raise an objection from: "and you shall be unto Me a kingdom of priests, and a holy nation" (Shemos 19:6), and: "for unto Me the children of Israel are servants" (Vayikra 25:55);
וְכָל מָקוֹם שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״לִי״ — אֵינוֹ זָז בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה וּבָעוֹלָם הַבָּא, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּוַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ב׳ (סִימָן ב׳)
for wherever the word "unto Me" (li) is stated, it never ceases in this world or in the World to Come (Vayikra Rabbah 2:2).
אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁהוּא עוֹלַם הַמַּעֲשֶׂה וּזְמַן הַטּוֹרַח דְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת לְהָכִין לְשַׁבָּת, שֶׁנִּמְסַר בְּחִירַת הַהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת לָאָדָם
But nevertheless in this world, which is the world of action and the preparation on the eve of Shabbat to prepare for Shabbat, where the choice of human effort is entrusted unto man;
צָרִיךְ הַתְחָלַת הַהִתְקַדְּשׁוּת מִלְּמַטָּה דִּ״וִהְיִיתֶם לִי קְדֹשִׁים״, שֶׁפֵּירֵשׁ בְּתוֹרַת כֹּהֲנִים שָׁם: ״מָה אֲנִי קָדוֹשׁ וְכוּלֵיהּ״
there must be an initial sanctification from below: "and you shall be holy unto Me," which Torat Kohanim expounds: "just as I am holy, etc.";
שֶׁהוּא הַהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת לְהַגִּיעַ לְתַכְלִית שְׁלֵימוּת הַקְּדוּשָׁה עַד הַהִתְדַּמּוּת לִקְדֻשָּׁתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ כִּבְיָכוֹל כְּפִי הָאֶפְשָׁר בְּכֹחַ אֱנוֹשִׁי
which is the human striving to attain consummate holiness, emulating His holiness as far as humanly possible;
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מְקַדֵּשׁ מִלְּמַעְלָה וּמַבְדִּיל מִכָּל מִינֵי טוּמְאָה וְרָע שֶׁאֵין לוֹ שַׁיָּיכוּת וְשׁוּם נְגִיעָה לָהֶם כְּלָל
and through this the Blessed Name sanctifies from Above, separating from all impurity and evil so that they have no affinity with them;
וּמִמֵּילָא אֵין כָּל אוּמָּה וְלָשׁוֹן יְכוֹלִים לִשְׁלוֹט בָּהֶם
and consequently no nation or empire can dominate them;
שֶׁאֵין הַשְּׁלִיטָה אֶלָּא עַל דָּבָר שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ שַׁיָּיכוּת עִמּוֹ, וְלֹא עַל דָּבָר הַנִּבְדָּל מִמֶּנּוּ
for dominion exists only over an entity that shares commonality, and not over that which is entirely separated from it;
וְכָל שְׁלִיטַת הָעַמִּים הוּא עַל יְדֵי הִסְתַּלְּקוּת הַכָּרַת הַקְּדוּשָׁה דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל בִּפְרָט
and all imperial dominion of the nations over Israel occurs solely through the withdrawal of Israel's manifest holiness.

וְעַל כֵּן עַל יְדֵי שֶׁמֵּת אַהֲרֹן וְנִסְתַּלְּקוּ עַנְנֵי כָּבוֹד, בָּא מֶלֶךְ עֲרָד ״וַיִּשְׁבְּ מִמֶּנּוּ שֶׁבִי״ (בַּמִּדְבָּר כ״א:א׳), כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה (ג׳ רֵישׁ עַמּוּד א׳)
Wherefore when Aharon died and the Clouds of Glory departed, the king of Arad attacked and took captives (Rosh Hashanah 3a);
כִּי אַהֲרֹן עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הוּא הָיָה הַנִּבְדָּל מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל: ״לְהַקְדִּישׁוֹ קֹדֶשׁ קָדָשִׁים״ (דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים א כ״ג:י״ג)
for Aharon, peace be upon him, was separated from Israel "to sanctify him as most holy" (I Divrei HaYamim 23:13);
שֶׁבּוֹ הָיָה תֹּקֶף הִתְגַּלּוּת תַּכְלִית הַקְּדוּשָׁה וְהַהַבְדָּלָה שֶׁאֶפְשָׁר לְהִתְגַּלּוֹת בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
within whom resided the ultimate manifestation of holiness and separation achievable in this world;
דְּעַל כֵּן הוּא הָיָה הַנִּכְנָס לְבֵית קֹדֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁים, מָקוֹם שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְכָל אָדָם לֹא יִהְיֶה [בְּאֹהֶל מוֹעֵד בְּבֹאוֹ לְכַפֵּר בַּקֹּדֶשׁ]״ (וַיִּקְרָא ט״ז:י״ז)
wherefore he alone entered the Holy of Holies, the place concerning which it is written: "And there shall be no man in the tent of meeting when he goes in to make atonement" (Vayikra 16:17);
שֶׁדָּרְשׁוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בַּיְרוּשַׁלְמִי דְּיוֹמָא (פֶּרֶק א׳ הֲלָכָה ה׳): ״אֲפִילּוּ אוֹתָן שֶׁדְּמוּת פְּנֵיהֶם פְּנֵי אָדָם״
which the Sages expounded in the Jerusalem Talmud (Yoma 1:5): "even the angels whose faces have the likeness of a man";
כִּי יֵשׁ קְדוּשָׁה שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה מִקְּדֻשַּׁת הַמַּלְאָכִים שֶׁהֵם אֵין יְכוֹלִים לְהַגִּיעַ שָׁם, רַק הַצַּדִּיקִים שֶׁמְּחִיצָתָן לִפְנִים מִמַּלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת
for there exists a holiness transcending the angels which they cannot reach, reserved for the righteous whose partition is set inside the ministering angels.
וְיִשְׂרָאֵל הֵם ״גּוֹי אֶחָד״ (שְׁמוּאֵל ב ז:כג), כּוּלָּם קוֹמָה שְׁלֵימָה
And Israel is "one nation in the earth" (II Shmuel 7:23), all forming a single complete corporate stature;
אֶלָּא שֶׁכְּמוֹ שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּקוֹמַת אָדָם אֵיבָרִים רָאשִׁיִּים שֶׁבָּהֶם תֹּקֶף חַיּוּת יוֹתֵר, כַּלֵּב שֶׁהוּא מְקוֹר הַחַיּוּת
except that just as within the human body there are primary vital organs containing greater life-force, like the heart which is the wellspring of vitality;
וְכֵן שְׁאָר אֵיבָרִים הֵם מַדְרֵיגוֹת מַדְרֵיגוֹת: דְּיֵשׁ אֵיבָרִים שֶׁעִיקַּר חַיּוּת תָּלוּי בָּהֶם, כְּמוֹחַ וְרֵיאָה וְכַדּוֹמֶה
and so other organs exist in descending rungs: organs upon which life directly depends, like the brain and lungs;

וְיֵשׁ שֶׁמְּעַט חַיּוּת תָּלוּי בָּהֶם, כַּכָּבֵד שֶׁכָּשֵׁר בִּנְקִיבָה וְאֵין מַטְרִיף וּמְסַלֵּק חַיּוּת אֶלָּא בִּנְטִילָה עַד שֶׁלֹּא יִשָּׁאֵר כְּזַיִת בִּמְקוֹם מָרָה וְחַיּוּתָא (חֻלִּין מ״ו עַמּוּד א׳)

and organs upon which less vitality depends, like the liver which is kosher if perforated and does not render treifah save if removed entirely leaving less than an olive's volume at the gallbladder (Chullin 46a);
וְיֵשׁ שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ בִּנְטִילָתָם וְחֶסְרוֹנָם לְגַמְרֵי אֵין מַזִּיק לַחַיּוּת, רַק בְּלַקּוּת כִּכְלָיוֹת (שָׁם נ״ד עַמּוּד א׳)
and organs whose total removal does not extinguish life, only causing illness, like the kidneys (Chullin 54a);
וְיֵשׁ שֶׁאֵין נוֹגֵעַ לַחַיּוּת כְּלָל, רַק מִכָּל מָקוֹם מַכְאִיב הַרְבֵּה לַגּוּף וּמוֹלִיד חֳלָיִים רָעִים
and parts that do not touch vitality at all, yet their injury causes severe bodily pain and illness;
וְיֵשׁ שֶׁאֵין מַכְאִיב גַּם כֵּן אֶלָּא מְעַט וּזְמַן מוּעָט, כְּמַכּוֹת בְּחִיצוֹנִיּוּת הַגּוּף וּבְאֵיבָרִים חִיצוֹנִים
and parts where injury causes only minor and brief pain, like bruises on the external surface of the body;
וְיֵשׁ שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ כְּאֵב גָּמוּר אֵין מַרְגִּישׁ בָּהֶם, הֵם כְּעֵין מוֹתָרוֹת כְּצִפָּרְנַיִם וּשְׂעָרוֹת וְכַדּוֹמֶה, כַּמָּה מִינֵי מַדְרֵיגוֹת
and parts that feel no pain whatsoever, being like superfluities, such as fingernails and hair, possessing various descending rungs;
וְהַכֹּל מִכְּלַל הַקּוֹמָה, שֶׁגַּם הַצִּפּוֹרֶן נִקְרֵאת ״צִפּוֹרֶן אָדָם״, וְהוּא חֵלֶק מִגּוּף וְעֶצֶם הָאָדָם
yet all are an integral part of the complete stature, the fingernail being called a human fingernail, part of the person's body;
וְהַכֹּל מְקַבֵּל חַיּוּת מֵהַלֵּב שֶׁמִּמֶּנּוּ תּוֹצְאוֹת הַחַיִּים (מִשְׁלֵי ד:כג)
all receiving vitality from the heart, whence flow the issues of life (Mishlei 4:23);
וּכְפִי הַחַיּוּת הַנִּשְׁפָּע מֵהַלֵּב, כָּךְ חַיּוּת כָּל הָאֵיבָרִים וּכְלַל הַקּוֹמָה:
and according to the vitality channeled from the heart, so is the life of all organs and the collective stature!

5.h: יִשְׂרָאֵל קְדוֹשִׁים — פֶּרֶק ה׳, אוֹת ה׳–ח׳

אוֹת ה׳ — קוֹמַת דּוֹר הַמִּדְבָּר, שִׁשִּׁים רִבּוֹא רָאשִׁים, וּמַעֲלַת מֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן — Section 5: The Stature of the Generation of the Wilderness, 600,000 Leaders, and the Roles of Moshe and Aharon

The theme: The wilderness generation as the corporate heart of all history, the reincarnation of its souls as heads of subsequent eras, and the complementary roles of Moshe (Chokhmah) and Aharon (Kedushah). The generation of the wilderness was the "generation of knowledge" (dor de'ah), attaining the apex of earthly perfection unequaled until King Mashiach, dwelling in complete holiness and separation from impurity. Korach claimed: "all the congregation are holy, every one of them, and Hashem is among them" (Bamidbar 16:3)—for the Shechinah resides exclusively in a place of holiness, parallel to the Holy Temple and the officiating Kohanim (Ezra 8:28). Just as holiness is delineated across Space (the Land of Israel, Jerusalem, the Sanctuary, and the Holy of Holies) and Time (Shabbat, Yom Tov, and Mikra'ei Kodesh), so is it structured across human Souls. In every generation there is a central soul corresponding to the Heart and the Holy of Holies—the High Priest of that generation (Zohar, Shelach 161b)—followed by the Kohanim, the Israelites entering the courtyard, down to the lowliest transgressor, all forming one complete stature (koma sheleimah) possessing an inalienable root in the sanctity of the Land of Israel (Kelim 1:6–9; Keritot 5b). The wilderness generation is the Heart and Holy of Holies of all world history. On the verse "And he was king in Jeshurun, when the heads of the people were gathered" (Devarim 33:5), the tradition teaches that the wilderness generation represents the heads of all generations: even the lowliest individual among them reincarnates as a leader or head in a subsequent generation, while Moshe Rabbeinu serves as their supreme monarch. This is the mystery of the 600,000 root souls radiating through all generations (Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 69, 110a). Moshe’s soul spreads through them in Wisdom (Chokhmah / the Brain), serving as the "attendant of the King" (shoshvina d'Malka) through the Torah; while Aharon’s soul illuminates them in Sanctity (Kedushah / the Heart), serving as the "attendant of the Queen" (shoshvina d'Matronita), anchoring the dwelling place of the Shechinah for all generations.

p: וְכָךְ בִּכְלַל אוּמָּה הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִית: וּבְדוֹר הַמִּדְבָּר שֶׁהָיוּ ״דּוֹר דֵּעָה״ (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה ט:א) בְּתַכְלִית הַשְּׁלֵימוּת שֶׁל עוֹלָם הַזֶּה, שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה דוֹר כְּמוֹהוּ עַד דּוֹרוֹ שֶׁל מָשִׁיחַ

And so it is within the collective Israelite nation: in the generation of the wilderness who were the "generation of knowledge" in the absolute zenith of worldly perfection, unrivaled by any generation until the generation of Mashiach;
הָיוּ בְּתַכְלִית שְׁלֵימוּת הַקְּדוּשָׁה וְהַהַבְדָּלָה
they existed in the absolute perfection of holiness and separation from impurity.
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״כִּי כָל הָעֵדָה כֻּלָּם קְדֹשִׁים וּבְתוֹכָם ה׳״ (בַּמִּדְבָּר ט״ז:ג׳)
As it is said: "Seeing all the congregation are holy, every one of them, and Hashem is among them" (Bamidbar 16:3);
שֶׁזֶּהוּ שְׁלֵימוּת הַקְּדוּשָׁה: כַּאֲשֶׁר ״בְּתוֹכָם ה׳״ שֶׁשּׁוֹכֵן בְּקֶרֶב לְבָבָם
this being the perfection of holiness: when "Hashem is among them," dwelling within the interior of their hearts;
וְאֵין שְׁכִינָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ אֶלָּא בִּמְקוֹם קְדוּשָׁה
for the Shechinah of the Blessed One abides exclusively in a place of sanctity;
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנִּתְיַיחֵד לָזֶה בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ שֶׁהוּא מְקוֹם הַקְּדוּשָׁה, וְכֵן הַכֹּהֲנִים הָעוֹבְדִים
just as the Holy Temple was set apart for this as the sanctuary of holiness, and likewise the serving Kohanim;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״אַתֶּם קֹדֶשׁ לַה׳ וְהַכֵּלִים קֹדֶשׁ וְגוֹמֵר״ (עֶזְרָא ח:כח)
and as it is said: "You are holy unto Hashem; the vessels are holy also, etc." (Ezra 8:28).
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁיֵּשׁ חֲלוּקַּת קְדוּשָׁה בַּמָּקוֹם שֶׁהוּא ״עוֹלָם״, וְכֵן בְּ״שָׁנָה״ בַּחֲלוּקַּת הַזְּמַנִּים דְּשַׁבָּת וְיוֹם טוֹב וּמִקְרָאֵי קֹדֶשׁ
And just as there is a division of sanctity in Space (Olam), and so in Time (Shanah) in the division of seasons into Shabbat, Yom Tov, and holy convocations;
כָּךְ יֵשׁ חֲלוּקוֹת בְּ״נֶפֶשׁ״:
so are there divisions in Soul (Nefesh):
וּבְכָל דּוֹר וָדוֹר יֵשׁ נֶפֶשׁ אַחַת דּוּגְמַת הַלֵּב שֶׁהוּא נֶגֶד בֵּית קֹדֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁים, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּזֹּוהַר (שְׁלַח קס״א עַמּוּד ב׳)
And in every single generation there is one soul mirroring the Heart which corresponds to the Holy of Holies, as stated in the Zohar (Shelach 161b);
וְהוּא הַכֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל שֶׁבַּדּוֹר הַנִּבְדָּל לְקֹדֶשׁ קָדָשִׁים
he being the High Priest of that generation who is set apart for the Holy of Holies;
וְאַחֲרָיו שְׁאָר נְפָשׁוֹת הַמְקוּדָּשׁוֹת דּוּגְמַת הַכֹּהֲנִים
and after him the other consecrated souls mirroring the Kohanim;
וְאַחֲרָיו שְׁאָר יִשְׂרָאֵל קְדוֹשִׁים הַנִּכְנָסִים לְעֶזְרַת יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁהוּא גַּם כֵּן מְקוּדֶּשֶׁת מִכְּלַל הַמִּקְדָּשׁ עַצְמוֹ
and after him the rest of holy Israel who enter the Courtyard of the Israelites, which is likewise sanctified within the precinct of the Temple itself;
וְעַד הָאַחֲרוֹן שֶׁבְּיִשְׂרָאֵל הַכָּלוּל בִּכְלַל הַקּוֹמָה, שֶׁכּוּלָּם ״גּוֹי אֶחָד״ (שְׁמוֹת ב ז:כג) וַאֲגֻדָּה אַחַת, אֲפִילּוּ פּוֹשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
down to the very last Jew included within the collective stature, all forming "one nation" and one unified band, even the transgressors of Israel.
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּכְרֵיתוֹת (ה׳ עַמּוּד ב׳): דְּעֶשֶׂר קְדוּשּׁוֹת הֵן שֶׁנִּשְׁנוּ בְּפֶרֶק קַמָּא דְּכֵלִים (מִשְׁנָה ו׳)
As stated in Keritot (5b): there are ten gradations of sanctity enumerated in Kelim (1:6);
וּקְדוּשָׁה רִאשׁוֹנָה הִיא קְדֻשַּׁת אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁגַּם הִיא יֵשׁ בָּהּ קְדוּשָׁה דִּמְקוּדֶּשֶׁת מִכָּל הָאֲרָצוֹת
and the first gradation is the sanctity of the Land of Israel, which is consecrated above all lands;
וַאֲפִילּוּ הַפָּחוּת וְהַיּוֹתֵר גָּרוּעַ שֶׁבְּיִשְׂרָאֵל כָּל שֶׁהוּא מִזֶּרַע יַעֲקֹב, יֵשׁ לוֹ חֵלֶק בָּאָרֶץ שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ מִקְּדֻשַּׁת הָאָרֶץ
and even the lowliest and most degraded person in Israel, so long as he is of Jacob's seed, possesses a portion in the Land absorbing its sanctity;
שֶׁבָּזֶה נִבְדָּל מִכָּל הָעַמִּים וְאַרְצוֹת הָעַמִּים שֶׁאֵין בָּהֶם שׁוּם קְדוּשָׁה כְּלָל, וְזֶהוּ קוֹמַת כָּל דּוֹר בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ
through which he is separated from all nations and gentile lands which possess no sanctity at all, this being the stature of each generation independently.
וּכְלַל הַדּוֹרוֹת כּוּלָּם הֵם גַּם כֵּן יַחַד קוֹמָה שְׁלֵימָה
And the sum of all generations together likewise forms one complete corporate stature;
שֶׁהוּא כְּלַל קוֹמַת כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל הַחֲלוּק גַּם כֵּן כְּפִי מַדְרֵיגַת הַדּוֹרוֹת שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
which is the stature of Knesset Israel, divided according to the spiritual rungs of the generations in this world;
וְדוֹר הֶחָבִיב מִכָּל הַדּוֹרוֹת כְּדוֹר הַמִּדְבָּר, הוּא הַלֵּב וְקֹדֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁים שֶׁבִּכְלַל הַקּוֹמָה כוּלָּהּ
and the most cherished generation of all—the generation of the wilderness—is the Heart and the Holy of Holies within the entire collective stature.
וְכֵן קִבַּלְתִּי בְּפֵירוּשׁ פָּסוּק: ״וַיְהִי בִישֻׁרוּן מֶלֶךְ, בְּהִתְאַסֵּף רָאשֵׁי עָם [יַחַד שִׁבְטֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל]״ (דְּבָרִים ל״ג:ה׳)
And so have I received by tradition in expounding the verse: "And he was king in Jeshurun, when the heads of the people were gathered, all the tribes of Israel together" (Devarim 33:5);
כִּי דוֹר הַמִּדְבָּר הֵם ״רָאשִׁים״ שֶׁבְּכָל הַדּוֹרוֹת
for the generation of the wilderness are the heads of all generations;
וְנֶפֶשׁ הַיּוֹתֵר פָּחוּת שֶׁבְּדוֹר הַמִּדְבָּר, הוּא אַחַר כָּךְ מִתְגַּלְגֵּל וּבָא לִהְיוֹת רֹאשׁ בְּאֵיזֶה דּוֹר
and the lowliest soul in the wilderness generation reincarnates in a later generation to serve as a head and leader;
וּבְהִתְאַסֵּף רָאשֵׁי עָם שֶׁל כָּל הַדּוֹרוֹת, יִהְיֶה מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הָרֹאשׁ שֶׁל דּוֹר הַמִּדְבָּר — מֶלֶךְ וְרֹאשׁ עֲלֵיהֶם
and when the heads of the people of all generations gather, Moshe Rabbeinu, the head of the wilderness generation, will be king and supreme head over them!
וְזֶהוּ מְכֻוָּון לְמַה שֶּׁכָּתַבְתִּי: דְּדוֹר הַמִּדְבָּר הֵם הַלֵּב וּבֵית קֹדֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁים שֶׁל כָּל הַדּוֹרוֹת
And this aligns precisely with what I wrote: that the wilderness generation is the Heart and the Holy of Holies of all generations;
שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ הָאַחֲרוֹן שֶׁבָּהֶם הוּא רֹאשׁ וְלֵב בְּאֵיזֶה דּוֹר
so that even the lowliest among them functions as a head and a heart in some generation.
וְנִרְאֶה לִי דְּעַל זֶה רָמְזוּ בְּתִקּוּנֵי זֹוהַר (תִּקּוּן ס״ט דַּף ק״י עַמּוּד א׳): דְּאִתְפַּשְׁטוּתֵיהּ הוּא בְּכָל דּוֹר וָדוֹר וְכוּלֵיהּ עַד שִׁשִּׁים רִבּוֹא וְכוּלֵיהּ, יְעוּיַּן שָׁם
And it appears to me that concerning this they hinted in Tikkunei Zohar (Tikkun 69, 110a): that Moshe's expansion extends into every generation unto 600,000, see there;
שֶׁכֵּן הֵם שִׁשִּׁים רִבּוֹא בְּכָל הַדּוֹרוֹת
there being 600,000 root souls across all generations.
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לִהְיוֹת שִׁשִּׁים רִבּוֹא דּוֹרוֹת בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, דְּכוּלּוֹ רַק שֵׁשֶׁת אֲלָפִים שָׁנָה
And although it is chronologically impossible for there to be 600,000 generations in this world, which spans only six thousand years;
וּמֵהֶם יְמוֹת הַמָּשִׁיחַ, וּמֵהֶם שְׁנֵי אֲלָפִים אַרְבַּע מֵאוֹת שְׁמוֹנִים וּשְׁמוֹנֶה עַד דּוֹר יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
and of these are the Messianic era, and 2,488 years elapsed from Creation until Joshua;
מִכָּל מָקוֹם גַּם בְּדוֹר אֶחָד יֵשׁ הַרְבֵּה נְפָשׁוֹת הַכְּלוּלִים בַּלֵּב
nevertheless even in a single generation there are multiple souls rooted within the Heart;
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלְּעוֹלָם ״דַּבָּר אֶחָד לַדּוֹר״ (סַנְהֶדְרִין ח׳ עַמּוּד א׳) וְרֹאשׁ אֶחָד
and though "there is only one leader for a generation" (Sanhedrin 8a) and a single supreme head;
מִכָּל מָקוֹם אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁיִּשְׁתַּנֶּה בְּדוֹר אֶחָד גַּם כֵּן מִנֶּפֶשׁ לְנֶפֶשׁ
nevertheless leadership may transition within a single era from soul to soul;
וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְנֵי קִמְחִית שֶׁשִּׁמְּשׁוּ שְׁנֵיהֶם בִּכְהֻנָּה גְּדוֹלָה בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים אֶחָד
as stated regarding the sons of Kimchit who both served in the High Priesthood on a single Yom Kippur (Yoma 47a);
וְהָרִאשׁוֹן חוֹזֵר לַעֲבוֹדָתוֹ וְכָל מִצְוֹת כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל עָלָיו, וַהֲרֵי הָיָה בִּשְׁנֵיהֶם קְדֻשַּׁת קֹדֶשׁ קָדָשִׁים
and the first returned to his service bearing all obligations of a High Priest, both embodying the sanctity of the Holy of Holies.
וְאַחַר הַחֻרְבָּן שֶׁנִּתְפַּשְּׁטוּ וְנִתְפַּזְּרוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל בַּאֲרָצוֹת שׁוֹנוֹת, יֵשׁ לָהֶם הַרְבֵּה רָאשִׁים וּמַנְהִיגִים שֶׁאֵין הָאֶחָד כָּיֵיף לַחֲבֵירוֹ, וְכוּלָּם בְּמַדְרֵגַת הַלֵּב
And following the Destruction, when Israel was dispersed throughout various lands, they have multiple heads and leaders, none subordinate to the other, all possessing the level of the Heart;
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם לְעוֹלָם שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַכֹּל הוּא רַק אֶחָד, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ: ״אָנוּ גּוֹי אֶחָד, וֵאלֹהַי אֶחָד, וְכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל אֶחָד״
yet in ultimate essence the root of all is strictly one: "We are one nation, our God is One, and one High Priest";
אֶלָּא שֶׁפְּעָמִים מֵאִיר שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַחַיּוּת לְתוֹצְאוֹת הַחַיִּים בָּזֶה וְנַעֲשָׂה הוּא רֹאשׁ הַהַנְהָגָה וְלֵב הָעוֹלָם, וּפְעָמִים בָּזֶה
except that at times the root of vitality radiates in this leader making him the heart of the world, and at times in that one;
וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ זֶה הוּא מְצִיאוּת שִׁשִּׁים רִבּוֹא רָאשִׁים בְּכָל הַדּוֹרוֹת כְּמִסְפַּר הַנְּפָשׁוֹת דְּדוֹר הַמִּדְבָּר
and in this manner exist 600,000 leaders throughout all generations corresponding to the number of souls of the wilderness generation;
שֶׁנֶּפֶשׁ מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם מִתְפַּשֶּׁטֶת בְּכוּלָּם מִצַּד הַחָכְמָה, וְנֶפֶשׁ אַהֲרֹן הַכֹּהֵן מְאִירָה לְכוּלָּם מִצַּד הַקְּדוּשָׁה
the soul of Moshe Rabbeinu expanding into all of them from the aspect of Wisdom, and the soul of Aharon the Kohen illuminating all from the aspect of Holiness.
וְזֶה הָיָה טַעֲנַת קֹרַח וַעֲדָתוֹ: ״דְּכָל הָעֵדָה כֻּלָּם קְדֹשִׁים״ (בַּמִּדְבָּר ט״ז:ג׳)
And this was the claim of Korach and his assembly: "Seeing all the congregation are holy" (Bamidbar 16:3);
שֶׁהִרְגִּישׁוּ בִּקְדוּשָׁה זוֹ שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּהַיּוֹתֵר גָּרוּעַ שֶׁבְּדוֹר הַמִּדְבָּר, שֶׁהוּא כִּקְדֻשַּׁת כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל בְּדוֹר אַחֵר
