וְשֶׁאֵין לוֹ — דְּלֹא נָתְנוּ לוֹ מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם, עַל כָּרְחָךְ יָדְעוּ שֶׁאֵינוֹ כְּלִי לְקַבֵּל חֶמְדוֹת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה בִּקְדוּשָׁה.
and one who lacks means was withheld wealth from Heaven because he was not yet a vessel to manage worldly goods in holiness.
וְרַבִּי — הוּא רַבֵּינוּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ שֶׁהָיָה מָלֵא קְדוּשָׁה בְּתַכְלִית דְּלֹא נֶהֱנָה מֵעוֹלָם הַזֶּה כְּלָל — הָיָה לוֹ שְׁנֵיהֶם: ״רוֹצֶה״ וְ״יֵשׁ לוֹ״!
While Rebbe—Rabbeinu HaKadosh who was in consummate holiness, enjoying nothing of this world—possessed both: he desired to give, and he had abundant means!
וּכְפִי הַנִּרְאֶה הָיוּ שְׁנֵיהֶם מִשּׁוֹרֶשׁ אֶחָד: מִשּׁוֹרֶשׁ הַלֵּב וּבֵית קֹדֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁים שֶׁבַּדּוֹר
And apparently both issued from a single soul-root: from the root of the Heart and the Holy of Holies of the generation;
וְשׁוּב מָצָאתִי כֵן בְּ״גִלְגּוּלֵי נְשָׁמוֹת״ לְהָרַב מְנַחֵם עֲזַרְיָה (אוֹת פ׳): ״דְּרַבִּי פִּנְחָס בֶּן יָאִיר וְרַבִּי — מִנִּיצוֹץ אֶחָד״
and subsequently I found this explicit in the Gilgulei Neshamot of Rabbi Menachem Azariah of Fano (letter Pei): "Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair and Rebbe derive from one single spark";
וּכְפִי הַנִּרְאֶה הוּא מֵהָאֲרִיזַ״ל... וְאַהֲנְיַין דְּזָכִיתִי לְכַוֵּון הָאֱמֶת!
and it derives from the holy Arizal, and I rejoice that I merited to align with the truth!
וְרַבִּי פִּנְחָס בֶּן יָאִיר קַשִּׁישׁ מִינֵּיהּ טוּבָא, דַּהֲרֵי הָיָה חוֹתְנוֹ דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בַּר יוֹחָאי רַבֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי
And Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair was far senior to Rebbe, being the father-in-law of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, the master of Rebbe;
וְגַם נִפְטַר מִקַּמֵּי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בַּר יוֹחָאי, כִּמְבוֹאָר בַּזֹּוהַר בְּכַמָּה דּוּכְתֵּי וּבְאִדְּרָא הַאֲזִינוּ
and passed away before Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, as taught in several passages in the Zohar and the Idra of Ha'azinu;
וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בַּר יוֹחָאי נִפְטַר בְּחַיֵּי רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל בְּעוֹד רַבִּי קָטָן וְלָמַד לִפְנֵי חֲכָמִים (בָּבָא מְצִיעָא פ״ד סוֹף עַמּוּד ב׳)
and Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai passed away during the lifetime of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel while Rebbe was still a youth studying before the Sages (Bava Metzia 84b);
וְעַל כָּרְחָךְ דְּהָיָה זֶה גַּם כֵּן בְּיַלְדוּתוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי, וְהָיָה עַדַיִין רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל נָשִׂיא, וְלֹא הָיָה הוּא רֹאשׁ הַדּוֹר עַדַיִין כְּלָל:
and perforce this encounter occurred during Rebbe's youth while Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel was Nasi, and Rebbe was not yet the leader of the generation at all!
יִשְׂרָאֵל קְדוֹשִׁים — פֶּרֶק ה׳, אוֹתִיּוֹת ל״א–ל״ו
אוֹת ל״א — תְּמִיהַת בַּעַל ״סֵפֶר יוּחֲסִין״, שְׁמִיטָה בַּיְרוּשַׁלְמִי, וּמַעֲלַת רַבִּי פִּנְחָס בֶּן יָאִיר כְּרַבּוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי בִּקְדוּשָׁה
Section 31: The Query of Sefer Yuchasin, Shemitah in the Yerushalmi, and Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair as Rebbe's Master in Holiness

The theme: Chronology of the encounter between Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair and Rebbe, the inviolable sanctity of the Land and of Israel, and the ascending levels of holiness. In Sefer Yuchasin, the author wondered how Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair could have visited Rebbe's house during Rebbe's youth, and likewise how Rabbi Meir attended the wedding of Rabbi Shimon the son of Rebbe. There is no difficulty: Rebbe possessed an independent household and vast wealth even during his father's lifetime, marrying off his son before reaching old age. However, in Yerushalmi Demai (1:3) and Ta'anit (3:1), the account reveals that Rebbe sought to permit the sabbatical year (shemitah), proving he had already been appointed Nasi. Thus, Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair and Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai lived past the demise of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, Rebbe being crowned Nasi during the lifetime of his elders by virtue of his patriarchal dynasty, though not yet the recognized head of the generation. The Yerushalmi terms Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair "Rebbe" without qualification, indicating he was Rebbe's master in matters of holiness. Although Rebbe did not study formal halachic jurisprudence before him, he received from him the ruling not to abolish Shemitah, teaching that the holiness of the Land of Israel was never nullified even in deep concealment. This matches what Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair told him in the Bavli: "Israel are holy"—declaring that even the lowest among Israel possess an indelible root of holiness veiled within. Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair was the head of the generation and the Holy of Holies of his era, the master of the celebrated Baraita tracing the rungs unto the Holy Spirit; Rebbe had not yet attained equal stature, wherefore Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair declined to dine with him!
וּבְ״סֵפֶר יוּחֲסִין״ (דְּפוּס אַמְשְׂטֶרְדָּם רכ״ט רֵישׁ עַמּוּד ד׳) תָּמַהּ: אֵיךְ הָיָה רַבִּי פִּנְחָס בֶּן יָאִיר בְּבֵית רַבִּי?
And in Sefer Yuchasin (Amsterdam edition, 229a) the author wondered: how could Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair have been present in the house of Rebbe?
וְכֵן הִקְשָׁה שָׁם (דַּף ל״א עַמּוּד ב׳): אֵיךְ הָיָה רַבִּי מֵאִיר בַּחֲתֻנַּת רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בְּרֵיהּ? עַיֵּין שָׁם.
And likewise he challenged there (31b): how could Rabbi Meir have been present at the wedding of Rabbi Shimon the son of Rebbe? See there.
וְאֵין בָּזֶה תֵּימָהּ אִם הָיָה לְרַבִּי בַּיִת בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ וְעֹשֶׁר גָּדוֹל בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ, וְשֶׁיַּשִּׂיא כְּבָר בֵּן עוֹד בְּחַיֵּי אָבִיו וְהַזְּקֵנִים
And there is no wonder in this if Rebbe possessed an independent household and vast wealth of his own, marrying off a son during the lifetime of his father and the elder sages;
וְאַף דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הָיָה הַצָּעִיר דְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל הַבְּכוֹר, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּכְתוּבּוֹת (ק״ג עַמּוּד ב׳)
and even though Rabbi Shimon was younger, Rabban Gamliel being the firstborn, as stated in Kesubos (103b);
וְהָיָה לוֹ שְׁנֵי בָנִים גְּדוֹלִים וּנְשׂוּאִים, אֵינוֹ תֵּימָהּ כְּלָל, וְיֵשׁ לוֹמַר דְּעַדַיִין לֹא הִגִּיעַ לִימֵי בִינָה.
and Rebbe had two adult, married sons, it is no wonder, and one may say he had not yet arrived at the years of understanding (age forty).
וְאָמְנָם בַּיְרוּשַׁלְמִי פֶּרֶק א׳ דִּדְמַאי (הֲלָכָה ג׳) וְרֵישׁ פֶּרֶק ג׳ דְּתַעֲנִית (הֲלָכָה א׳) אִיתָא גַּם כֵּן עוּבְדָא דְּרַבִּי פִּנְחָס בֶּן יָאִיר וְרַבִּי
However, in the Jerusalem Talmud (Demai 1:3 and Ta'anit 3:1) this narrative of Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair and Rebbe is likewise recorded;
וְאִיתָא: דְּרַבִּי בָּעֵי לְמִשְׁרֵא שְׁמִיטְתָא, וְעַל כָּרְחָךְ דְּהָיָה כְּבָר נָשִׂיא
and it states there: that Rebbe sought to permit the sabbatical year, proving perforce that he was already appointed Nasi!
וְאִם כֵּן צָרִיךְ לוֹמַר דְּרַבִּי פִּנְחָס בֶּן יָאִיר וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בַּר יוֹחָאי הֶאֱרִיכוּ יָמִים אַחַר רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
And if so, one must conclude that Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair and Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai outlived Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel;
וּמַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בְּבָבָא מְצִיעָא שָׁם (פ״ד סוֹף עַמּוּד ב׳): ״שֶׁאֵין לוֹ אָב״ אַרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, לֹא דְּנָח נַפְשֵׁיהּ כְּפֵירוּשׁ רַשִׁ״י
and what the Gemara states in Bava Metzia (84b) that Rabbi Elazar the son of Rabbi Shimon "had no father," did not mean his father had died as Rashi expounds;
רַק שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה שָׁם בַּיְשִׁיבָה עִמָּהֶם
but that Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai was merely absent from the study hall with them;
וְנִתְמַנָּה נָשִׂיא בְּחַיֵּי רַבּוֹתָיו לְפִי שֶׁהָיָה מִשַּׁלְשֶׁלֶת נְשִׂיאִים וּבֵית דִּין וְהִגִּיעַ לוֹ הַיְרוּשָּׁה, וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם לֹא הָיָה גְּדוֹל הַדּוֹר אָז עַדַיִין.
Rebbe being appointed Nasi during the lifetime of his teachers because he descended from the patriarchal dynasty, though not yet the recognized head of the generation.
וְשָׁם בַּיְרוּשַׁלְמִי אִיתָא: ״לְרַבִּי פִּנְחָס בֶּן יָאִיר מִשָּׁנַח רַבִּי וְכוּלֵיהּ״, קְרָאוֹ ״רַבִּי״ סְתָם, מַשְׁמַע דְּהָיָה רַבּוֹ

And there in the Jerusalem Talmud it records regarding Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair: "from when my master rested, etc.," calling him "my master" (Rebbi) without qualification, implying he was Rebbe's teacher;
וְנִרְאֶה דְּהַיְינוּ בְּעִנְיְנֵי קְדוּשָׁה, שֶׁלֹּא מָצִינוּ שֶׁלָּמַד לְפָנָיו הֲלָכוֹת בְּשׁוּם מָקוֹם
and it appears that this was specifically in matters of holiness, for we do not find that Rebbe studied halachot before him anywhere;
וְאֶפְשָׁר שֶׁנַּעֲשָׂה רַבּוֹ בְּאוֹתוֹ עִנְיָן שֶׁקִּבֵּל מִמֶּנּוּ שֶׁלֹּא לְהַתִּיר שְׁמִיטָה, דְּהוֹדִיעוֹ שֶׁקְּדֻשַּׁת הָאָרֶץ לֹא בָּטְלָה
and perhaps he became his master in that very incident when Rebbe accepted his counsel not to permit Shemitah, Rabbi Pinchas informing him that the holiness of the Land was never nullified;
וְדָבָר זֶה הוּא לִימּוּד גָּדוֹל בְּעִנְיְנֵי הַקְּדוּשָׁה: לָדַעַת שֶׁאַף עַכְשָׁיו שֶׁהַקְּדוּשָׁה בְּהֶעְלֵם גָּדוֹל, מִכָּל מָקוֹם לֹא בָּטְלָה.
this being a monumental teaching in holiness: to know that even now when holiness is in profound concealment, it is never abolished.
וְהוּא עַצְמוֹ מַה שֶּׁאָמַר לוֹ בַּבַּבְלִי: ״יִשְׂרָאֵל קְדוֹשִׁים הֵם״ (חֻלִּין ז׳ עַמּוּד ב׳)
And this is identical with what he told him in the Babylonian Talmud: "Israel are holy" (Chullin 7b);
שֶׁהוֹדִיעוֹ דָּבָר זֶה: שֶׁבְּכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל, אַף הַיּוֹתֵר פְּחוּתִים, יֵשׁ קְדוּשָׁה, אֶלָּא שֶׁהוּא בְּהֶעְלֵם גָּדוֹל אֶצְלָם.
informing him of this principle: that in all Israel, even the most degraded, holiness abides, albeit in deep concealment.
וְהָיָה אָז רַבִּי פִּנְחָס בֶּן יָאִיר בְּמַעֲלַת הַקְּדוּשָׁה — רֹאשׁ הַדּוֹר וּבֵית קֹדֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁים שֶׁבַּדּוֹר
And Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair was then in the virtue of holiness the head of the generation and the Holy of Holies of the era;
וְהוּא בַּעַל הַבָּרַיְיתָא דְּסוֹף סוֹטָה (מ״ט עַמּוּד ב׳) וַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה (כ׳ עַמּוּד ב׳) בְּסֵדֶר הַמַּדְרֵיגוֹת עַד תַּכְלִית הַקְּדוּשָׁה וְעַד רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ
he being the author of the Baraita at the end of Sotah (49b) and Avodah Zarah (20b) detailing the rungs unto ultimate holiness and the Holy Spirit;
לְפִי שֶׁהוּא הִשִּׂיג כָּל הַמַּדְרֵיגוֹת הַשְּׁלֵימוֹת, יָדַע לְסַדְּרָן וּלְלַמְּדָן.
because he attained all perfected rungs, he knew how to arrange and transmit them.
וְרַבִּי אַחַר כָּךְ הוּא שֶׁנִּקְרָא ״רַבֵּינוּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ״
And Rebbe was only later crowned "our holy Master";
וְאָז עַדַיִין לֹא הָיָה בִּשְׁלֵימוּת לְגַמְרֵי, דְּעַל כֵּן לֹא עָלְתָה בְּיָדוֹ שֶׁיִּסְעוֹד אֶצְלוֹ רַבִּי פִּנְחָס בֶּן יָאִיר, דְּעַדַיִין לֹא הָיָה שָׁוֶה אֵלָיו בְּמַדְרֵיגַת הַקְּדוּשָׁה:
and at that time he had not yet attained absolute perfection, wherefore it did not succeed in his hand that Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair dine with him, not yet being equal to him in holiness!

5.h: אוֹת ל״ב — עִנְיַן הַפְּרֵידוֹת הַלְּבָנוֹת, עָשְׁרוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי, וְהַבְּרָכָה שֶׁאֵינָהּ עוֹשָׂה פֵּירוֹת — Section 32: The White Mules, Rebbe's Imperial Wealth, and Blessings that Bear No Fruit

The theme: The white mules of the Patriarchal House, the dung of mules surpassing royal gold, and why gentile blessing is barren. In Shabbat (113b), Scripture's phrase "and she had left" is expounded: "in the days of Rebbe, whose stable-master (ahuryarei) was wealthier than King Shapur". Tosafos (Bava Metzia 85a) explains that this wealth derived from the manure of his beasts, matching Bereishis Rabbah (64:7): "the dung of the mules of Isaac, and not the gold and silver of Abimelech". Mules were royal animals possessed exclusively by monarchs like Absalom and Solomon (II Shmuel 13:29, I Melachim 1:33), and in Israel found only in the Patriarchal palace (mula'ot shel beit Rebbi, Shabbat 52a; Yerushalmi Berachos 8:2, Kilayim 8:3). Breeding mules (kilayim) is prohibited to Jews (Vayikra 19:19); they originated from Anah the Horite (Bereishis 36:24). Israel acquires these animals from gentiles as part of the inheritance of the nations ("blessed shall you be above all peoples; there shall not be male or female barren among you, or among your cattle", Devarim 7:14). All worldly abundance is patterned within the Torah; at Sinai the angelic princes of the nations offered tribute unto Israel (Zohar on Devarim 33:2). Because the "other god is castrated and produces no fruit" (Zohar), gentile blessing manifests in barren entities—like the sterile mule that cannot give birth (Bechoros 8b)!

p: וְזֶה עִנְיַן הַפְּרֵידוֹת לְבָנוֹת, דִּבְשַׁבָּת (קי״ג סוֹף עַמּוּד ב׳) אִיתָא: ״׳וַתֹּתַר׳ (רוּת ב:יד) — בִּימֵי רַבִּי, דַּאֲהוֹרְיָירֵיהּ עַתִּיר מִשָּׁבוּר מַלְכָּא״
And this is the mystery of the white mules, for in Shabbat (113b) it is taught: "'and she had left' (Rut 2:14)—in the days of Rebbe, whose stable-master was wealthier than King Shapur";
וּפֵירֵשׁ בְּתוֹסָפוֹת בָּבָא מְצִיעָא (פ״ה עַמּוּד א׳): מִזֶּבֶל בְּהֵמוֹתָיו, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה: ״זֶבֶל בְּהֵמוֹתָיו שֶׁל יִצְחָק, וְלֹא כַּסְפּוֹ וּזְהָבוֹ דַּאֲבִימֶלֶךְ״
and Tosafos expounds in Bava Metzia (85a): from the manure of his beasts, as stated in Bereishis Rabbah: "the manure of Isaac's beasts, and not the gold and silver of Abimelech";
וּמַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב ״בְּהֵמוֹתָיו״ לָאו דַּוְוקָא, וְנָקְטוּ לְשׁוֹן הַגְּמָרָא שָׁם: ״כִּיסְתָא לְחֵיוָתָא״
and the term "his beasts" is not exact, borrowing the Gemara's phrasing: fodder for beasts;
וּבִבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ס״ד (סִימָן ז׳) אִיתָא: ״זֶבֶל פִּרְדוֹתָיו״.
while in Bereishis Rabbah (64:7) the precise text is: "the manure of his mules".
וְנִרְאֶה דְּעִיקַּר הָעֹשֶׁר בַּפְּרֵידוֹת שֶׁהָיוּ חֲשׁוּבוֹת, וְלֹא הָיוּ מְצוּיִים אֶלָּא בְּבָתֵּי הַמְּלָכִים
And it appears that the essence of wealth lay in mules which were highly prized, found exclusively in royal palaces;
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְנֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ גַּבֵּי אַבְשָׁלוֹם (שְׁמוּאֵל ב י״ג:כ״ט), וּבְאַבְשָׁלוֹם (שָׁם י״ח:ט׳), וּבִמְלוּכַת שְׁלֹמֹה (מְלָכִים א א:לג)
as stated regarding the king's sons with Absalom (II Shmuel 13:29), Absalom himself (ibid. 18:9), and the coronation of Solomon (I Melachim 1:33);
וּבְשַׁבָּת (נ״ב עַמּוּד א׳): ״מוּלָאוֹת שֶׁל בֵּית רַבִּי״, מַשְׁמַע דְּלֹא הָיוּ מְצוּיִים אֶלָּא בְּבֵית רַבִּי לְרוֹב עָשְׁרוֹ
and in Shabbat (52a): "the mules of the House of Rebbe," implying they were found only in Rebbe's house due to his immense wealth;
וְכֵן בַּיְרוּשַׁלְמִי פֶּרֶק ח׳ דִּבְרָכוֹת (הֲלָכָה ו׳) וּפֶרֶק ח׳ דְּכִלְאַיִם (הֲלָכָה ד׳): דַּאֲמַר לִדְבֵי נְשִׂיאָה: כִּי זְבַנִיתוּ וְכוּלֵיהּ, עַיֵּין שָׁם
and in Yerushalmi Berachos (8:6) and Kilayim (8:4) where the Sages addressed the Patriarchal House regarding purchasing mules;
מַשְׁמַע דְּלֹא הָיוּ אֲחֵרִים בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל לוֹקְחֵי פְּרֵידוֹת זוּלַת בֵּי נְשִׂיאָה.
implying that no other Jews purchased mules save the Patriarchal House.
וּמָצָאתִי בְּ״סֵפֶר יוּחֲסִין״ (דַּף ל״א סוֹף עַמּוּד ב׳) שֶׁהֵבִיא עוּבְדָא דְּרַבִּי דְּבָבָא מְצִיעָא שָׁם (פ״ה עַמּוּד א׳), כָּתַב: ״וְעָבַר קָלֵיהּ לְקוֹל הַפְּרֵידוֹת״
And I found in Sefer Yuchasin (31b) citing that incident in Bava Metzia (85a), writing: "his voice carried over the sound of the mules";
הִנֵּה כָּתַב בִּמְקוֹם ״חֵיוָתֵיהּ״ דִּגְמָרָא: ״פְּרֵידוֹת״
substituting "mules" for the Gemara's "beasts";
וְרַשִׁ״י שַׁבָּת שָׁם פֵּירֵשׁ ״אֲהוֹרְיָירֵיהּ״: שׁוֹמֵר סוּסִים וּפְרֵידוֹת, וְזֶה עִיקָּר, לֹא כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּבָבָא מְצִיעָא שָׁם סוּסִים לְבַד
and Rashi in Shabbat explains ahuryarei as keeper of horses and mules, which is primary, and not merely horses;
וְהַפְּרֵידוֹת עִיקַּר הָעֹשֶׁר, כִּלְשׁוֹן הַבְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה.
the mules constituting the core of the wealth, as phrased in Bereishis Rabbah.
וְהַיְינוּ כִּי זֶהוּ נַחֲלַת גּוֹיִם, דַּעֲנָה הַפָּסוּל הוּא שֶׁהֵבִיא פְּסוּלִים אֵלּוּ (בְּרֵאשִׁית ל״ו:כ״ד; פְּסָחִים נ״ד עַמּוּד א׳)
Meaning: for this is the inheritance of the gentiles, Anah the illegitimate having bred these crossbreeds (Bereishis 36:24; Pesachim 54a);
וְיִשְׂרָאֵל אָסוּר לְהַרְכִּיב כִּלְאַיִם, וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁיִּוָּולְדוּ בְּבֵית יִשְׂרָאֵל כְּלָל, רַק שֶׁלָּקְחוּ מִמַּה שֶּׁהִרְבִּיעַ גּוֹי
and an Israelite is forbidden to crossbreed animals, making it impossible that they be born in a Jewish house, acquired solely from gentile crossbreeding;
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר בְּרֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת עֵקֶב: ״בָּרוּךְ תִּהְיֶה מִכָּל הָעַמִּים, לֹא יִהְיֶה בְךָ עָקָר וַעֲקָרָה וּבִבְהֶמְתֶּךָ״ (דְּבָרִים ז:יד)
and on this Scripture states in Parashat Eikev: "You shall be blessed above all peoples; there shall not be male or female barren among you, or among your cattle" (Devarim 7:14);
הַיְינוּ שֶׁיִּקַּח גַּם הַבְּרָכָה שֶׁל כָּל הָאוּמּוֹת
meaning that Israel absorbs the blessing of all the nations.
כִּי עַל יְדֵי הַתּוֹרָה זוֹכִין גַּם לְ״נַחֲלַת גּוֹיִם״ (תְּהִלִּים קי״א:ו׳) וַ״עֲמַל לְאֻמִּים״ (שָׁם ק״ה:מ״ד)
For through the Torah Israel merits the heritage of the nations and the labor of peoples;
וְכָל הַבְּרָכוֹת הַשַּׁיָּיכוֹת לָהֶם גַּם כֵּן, שֶׁהַכֹּל כָּלוּל בַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁהוּא דְּפוּס כָּל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ
and all blessings belonging to them, everything being contained within the Torah which is the blueprint of the cosmos;
וּכְמוֹ בִּשְׁעַת מַתַּן תּוֹרָה, דְּגַם שָׂרֵי כָל הָאוּמּוֹת נָתְנוּ לָהֶם נִבְזְבְּזוֹן מִכֹּחָם וּמֵהַשַּׁיָּיךְ לָהֶם
as at Sinai, where the angelic princes of all nations gave tribute unto Israel from their power;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּזֹּוהַר (חֵלֶק ג׳ קצ״ב עַמּוּד ב׳) עַל פָּסוּק ״וְזָרַח מִשֵּׂעִיר לָמוֹ [הוֹפִיעַ מֵהַר פָּארָן] וְגוֹמֵר״ (דְּבָרִים ל״ג:ב׳)
as stated in the Zohar on "and rose from Seir unto them; He shined forth from Mount Paran" (Devarim 33:2).
וּלְפִי דְּ״אֵל אַחֵר אִסְתָּרַס וְלָא עָבֵיד פֵּירִין״ (זֹוהַר חֵלֶק א׳ נ״ה עַמּוּד ב׳)
And because the "other god is castrated and produces no fruit" (Zohar I, 55b);
כָּל בִּרְכַּת הָאוּמּוֹת הוּא בְּדָבָר שֶׁאֵין עוֹשֶׂה פֵּירוֹת, כִּפְרֵידוֹת דְּלָא יָלְדָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְכוֹרוֹת (ח׳ סוֹף עַמּוּד ב׳):
the blessing of the nations resides in entities that bear no fruit, like the sterile mule that cannot give birth (Bechoros 8b)!

5.h: אוֹת ל״ג — תְּשׁוּבַת רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ לְסָבֵי דְּבֵי אַתּוּנָא: בְּרִית מֶלַח עוֹלָם וְזֶבֶל פִּרְדוֹתָיו שֶׁל יִצְחָק — Section 33: Rabbi Yehoshua's Riddle to the Elders of Athens: The Covenant of Salt and Isaac's Mules

The theme: The elders of Athens challenging Israel's chosenness, the covenant of salt, and the dung of mules surpassing royal gold. This illuminates the riddle posed to Rabbi Yehoshua ben Chananya by the elders of Athens: "When salt spoils, wherewith is it salted?" (Bechoros 8b). They challenged the eternal "covenant of salt" (brit melach olam, Bamidbar 18:19) of Israel, claiming Israel had become corrupt and that the nations were now the chosen. Rabbi Yehoshua answered: "Salt it with the afterbirth of a mule (kudneita)". They countered: "Does a mule give birth?!" whereupon he retorted: "And can salt ever spoil?!" He demonstrated that the nations are sterile like the mule, incapable of divine choice, while the covenant of salt with Israel never spoils. Hashem blessed Israel: "there shall not be barren among you"—meaning when gentile blessing enters Israel, it loses its barrenness. When channeled into Jewish hands in holiness, it multiplies so immensely that the manure of Isaac's or Rebbe's mules surpasses the gold and silver of Abimelech or King Shapur. Jewish wealth cannot be compared to gentile wealth, for Jewish wealth is holy while gentile wealth is defiled; but the mules derived from the nations. The mules were purified when entering Israel; yet even their cast-off dung gathered by stable-masters was elevated through Hashem's blessing to surpass royal gold, which the Talmud terms "and she had left" (va-totar)—superfluous abundance!

p: וְעַל זֶה הוּא רְמִיזוֹת דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן חֲנַנְיָה לְסָבֵי דְּבֵי אַתּוּנָא שָׁם (בְּכוֹרוֹת ח׳ סוֹף עַמּוּד ב׳): כְּשֶׁאָמְרוּ לֵיהּ: ״מִלְחָא כִּי סַרְיָא [בְּמַאי מָלְחֵי לַהּ?]״
And toward this point the riddles of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Chananya unto the elders of Athens (Bechoros 8b), when they asked him: "When salt spoils, wherewith is it salted?";
דְּשָׁמַעְתִּי דְּהַכַּוָּונָה: לִ״בְרִית מֶלַח עוֹלָם״ (בַּמִּדְבָּר י״ח:י״ט) דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁחָשְׁבוּ שֶׁכְּבָר נִתְקַלְקְלוּ וְשֶׁמֵּעַתָּה הֵם הַנִּבְחָרִים
for I heard that the reference was to the eternal covenant of salt of Israel, the Athenians assuming Israel had been cast off and that they were now the chosen;
וְעַל זֶה רָמַז לָהֶם דְּהֵם הַ״כּוּדַנְיָיתָא״ שֶׁאֵין עוֹשָׂה פֵּירוֹת כְּלָל
and he hinted unto them that the nations are like the mule (kudneita) which never produces fruit;
וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר כְּלָל לִבְחוֹר בָּהֶם, וְעַל כָּרְחָךְ דְּמִלְחָא לָא סַרְיָא!
it being impossible that they be chosen, and perforce the covenant of salt never spoils!
וְעַל כֵּן כְּשֶׁבֵּירְכָם בְּבִרְכַּת הָעַמִּים אָמַר: ״לֹא יִהְיֶה בְךָ עָקָר [וַעֲקָרָה וּבִבְהֶמְתֶּךָ]״ (דְּבָרִים ז:יד)
Wherefore when Hashem blessed Israel with the blessing of the nations He said: "there shall not be male or female barren among you, or among your cattle" (Devarim 7:14);
שֶׁכְּשֶׁיָּבוֹאוּ הַבְּרָכוֹת לְךָ, לֹא תִּקְלוֹט אוֹתָם כְּמוֹ שֶׁהֵם אֶצְלָם עֲקוּרִים מִלַּעֲשׂוֹת פֵּירוֹת, דְּבָךְ לֹא יִהְיוּ עֲקוּרִים כְּלָל.
that when these blessings arrive unto you, you shall not absorb them in their barren state as they exist among the nations, for within you they will never be barren.
וּכְשֶׁהִגִּיעַ לְיַד יִשְׂרָאֵל בִּקְדוּשָׁה הוּא בְּרִיבּוּי עָצוּם, עַד שֶׁזֶּבֶל הַפְּרֵידוֹת עָדִיף מִכֶּסֶף וְזָהָב הַמְּלָכִים
And when it reaches the hand of Israel in holiness, it multiplies so immensely that the dung of their mules surpasses the gold and silver of kings;
דְּכַסְפּוֹ וּזְהָבוֹ דְּיִצְחָק אוֹ דְּרַבִּי לֹא שַׁיָּיךְ לְהַעֲרִיךְ עִם כַּסְפּוֹ וּזְהָבוֹ שֶׁל אֲבִימֶלֶךְ וְשָׁבוּר מַלְכָּא שֶׁאֵינָם מֵעֵרֶךְ אֶחָד כְּלָל
for the gold and silver of Isaac or Rebbe cannot be compared to that of Abimelech and King Shapur, not being of the same nature;
דְּזֶה בִּקְדוּשָׁה וְזֶה בִּמְסָאֲבוּ
this being in holiness and that in defilement.
רַק הַפְּרֵידוֹת שֶׁהֵם גַּם כֵּן מִדִּידְהוּ — וְגַם כֵּן לֹא הַפְּרֵידוֹת עַצְמָן דְּמִשֶּׁבָּאוּ לְיַד יִשְׂרָאֵל טָהֲרוּ
Only the mules, which originated from the nations—and not the mules themselves, for once acquired by Israel they were purified;
רַק זֶבֶל הַפְּרֵידוֹת הַנִּשְׁלָח לַחוּץ וּלְקָחָם הָאוֹהוֹרְיָירֵיהּ וְהָרוֹעִים
but the manure of the mules cast outside and collected by the stable-masters and shepherds;
וְאַף זֶה, אַחַר שֶׁהִגִּיעַ לִידֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְשָׁרְתָה בִּרְכַּת ה׳, הָיָה יוֹתֵר מִכֶּסֶף וְזָהָב שֶׁלָּהֶם
even this, having passed through Jewish hands under Hashem's blessing, surpassed their royal gold and silver;
וְהַגְּמָרָא קָרֵי לַהּ ״וַתֹּתַר״ (שַׁבָּת קי״ג סוֹף עַמּוּד ב׳), דְּזֶה הָוֵי כְּמוֹתָרוֹת:
and the Talmud terms this "and she had left" (Shabbat 113b), denoting superfluous abundance!

5.h: אוֹת ל״ד — הַמּוֹתָרוֹת דִּימֵי חִזְקִיָּהוּ וִיצְחָק מוּל עָשְׁרוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי, וְהַפְּרֵידוֹת הַמַּזִּיקוֹת כְּ״מַלְאַךְ הַמָּוֶת בְּבֵיתוֹ״ — Section 34: The Abundance of Hezekiah and Isaac vs. Rebbe, and the White Mules as the Angel of Death

The theme: Rebbe elevating superfluities into holiness, and Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair diagnosing the white mules as an unholy intrusion. In Shabbat (113b), "and she had left" is expounded regarding the days of King Hezekiah: eating a single pound of greens at a meal (Sanhedrin 94b), where "a thousand vines at a thousand silverlings shall be for briers and thorns" (Yeshayah 7:23) because they needed nothing. The numeral one thousand is wealth within functional boundaries; for Hezekiah, even that was accounted as superfluous. "And she was sated" (va-tisba) denotes sufficient sustenance without superfluity. But regarding Rebbe, it was immense wealth: regarding Isaac the Midrash states they merely said his dung was greater, whereas with Rebbe his stable-master was literally wealthier than Emperor Shapur! Angels channeled this wealth unto Rebbe because he possessed the spiritual strength in his holiness to elevate all superfluities (motarot) into the Sanctuary, which is the mystery of raising outcast souls. Rebbe was worthy of being Mashiach (Sanhedrin 98b; Eichah Rabbah 4:20), dying not from personal fault, but visiting his home every Friday twilight (Kesubos 103b). Samson fell because the superfluous wealth Delilah accepted injected the yetzer hara into his mission; but Rebbe attributed his superfluities to his stable-master. However, in the era of Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair, when Rebbe had not yet reached consummate holiness, Rabbi Pinchas beheld white mules with white hooves (chivaran reish car'ayeihu) whose kick is dangerous, exclaiming: "The Angel of Death is in his house, and shall I dine with him?!" (Chullin 7b) Rebbe bought them as colts before their legs turned white. Rabbi Pinchas diagnosed that since no evil descends from Heaven, this dangerous defect proved that within Rebbe's heart lingered a subtle trace of desire for superfluities, which attracted the yetzer hara—who is the Satan and the Angel of Death (Bava Batra 16a)—into his house!

p: וּתְחִלָּה דָּרַשׁ שָׁם: ״׳וַתֹּתַר׳ — בִּימֵי חִזְקִיָּה״ (שַׁבָּת קי״ג סוֹף עַמּוּד ב׳)
And initially the Gemara expounded there: "'and she had left'—in the days of Hezekiah" (Shabbat 113b);
וְהוּא לֹא מָצִינוּ בוֹ כָּל כָּךְ עֹשֶׁר מוּפְלָג בַּקְּרָא, רַק נִרְאֶה הַכַּוָּונָה: שֶׁהָיוּ לוֹ מוֹתָרוֹת מִכְּפִי הַצֹּרֶךְ לוֹ
and we do not find exorbitant wealth attributed to him in Scripture, the intent being that he possessed superfluities beyond his personal needs;
דְּהוּא הָיָה אוֹכֵל לִיטְרָא יָרָק בִּסְעוּדָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (סַנְהֶדְרִין צ״ד עַמּוּד ב׳)
for he ate a single pound of greens at a meal (Sanhedrin 94b);
וְ״[הָיָה בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא יִהְיֶה כָל מָקוֹם אֲשֶׁר יִהְיֶה שָּׁם] אֶלֶף גֶּפֶן בְּאֶלֶף כָּסֶף — לַשָּׁמִיר וְלַשַּׁיִת יִהְיֶה״ (יְשַׁעְיָה ז:כג), שֶׁלֹּא הָיוּ צְרִיכִים כְּלוּם
and "a thousand vines at a thousand silverlings, shall even be for briers and thorns" (Yeshayah 7:23), needing nothing;
דְּ״אֶלֶף״ הוּא הַכֶּסֶף שֶׁבִּגְבוּל כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְעֵיל, דְּהַיְינוּ כְּדֵי הַצֹּרֶךְ וְלֹא מוֹתָרוֹת, גַּם זֶה הָיָה אֶצְלָם נֶחְשָׁב לְמוֹתָרוֹת.
the numeral one thousand being wealth within boundaries (essential need without excess), yet even this was accounted by them as superfluous.
וְאַחַר כָּךְ דָּרַשׁ: ״׳וַתִּשְׂבַּע׳ (רוּת ב:יד) — בִּימֵי דָּוִד״, דְּזֶה נִקְרָא רַק שְׂבִיעָה וְאֵין זֶה מוֹתָרוֹת, דְּיֵשׁ צֹרֶךְ יוֹתֵר גַּם כֵּן
And afterward the Gemara expounded: "'and she was sated'—in the days of David," which denotes sufficient sustenance without superfluity;
אֲבָל דְּרַבִּי הוּא מוֹתָרוֹת עֹשֶׁר עָצוּם כָּזֶה.
but in the days of Rebbe it was immense, extraordinary superfluous wealth.
דְּגַבֵּי יִצְחָק נֶאֱמַר רַק שֶׁהָיוּ ״אוֹמְרִים״: זֶבֶל וְכוּלֵיהּ, וְלֹא שֶׁהָיָה בְּפֹעַל כֵּן
For regarding Isaac the Midrash states merely that people said his dung was greater, not that it occurred in actual deed;
וּלְפִי שֶׁהוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַשְׁפָּעַת הָעֲשִׁירוּת בָּעוֹלָם, דְּ״מִצָּפוֹן זָהָב יֶאֱתֶה״ (אִיּוֹב ל״ז:כ״ב), וְהָיָה כָּלוּל בּוֹ גַּם עֹשֶׁר הַשַּׁיָּיךְ לְעֵשָׂו בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
Isaac being the root of gold flowing from the North (Gevurah), containing the wealth destined for Esav in this world;
וְגַבֵּי רַבִּי הָיָה בְּפֹעַל הָאוֹהוֹרְיָירֵיהּ וְכוּלֵיהּ וּכְבָר נִפְרַד מֵעֵשָׂו
whereas with Rebbe his stable-master was literally wealthier than Shapur, having separated from Esav;
אֶלָּא שֶׁמִּכָּל מָקוֹם, הֲרֵי מַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת הִשְׁפִּיעוּ לוֹ עֹשֶׁר כָּזֶה, שֶׁהוּא הָיָה לוֹ כֹּחַ בִּקְדֻשָּׁתוֹ לְהַכְנִיס גַּם כָּל הַמּוֹתָרוֹת אֶל הַקְּדוּשָׁה
yet ministering angels channeled this wealth unto him because he possessed the power in his holiness to elevate all superfluities into the Sanctuary;
דְּגַם מַה שֶּׁנִּרְאָה מוֹתָר בָּעוֹלָם, אַף הוּא מִכְּלַל בְּרִיָּתוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם
for even that which appears superfluous is an integral part of Creation;
וּבָזֶה הוּא הַעֲלָאַת הַנְּפָשׁוֹת הַנִּרְאוֹת כְּמוֹתָרוֹת כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְעֵיל.
and within this lies the elevation of the souls that appear as bodily superfluities as I wrote above.
וְעַל כֵּן גַּם הוּא הָיָה דּוּגְמַת מָשִׁיחַ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּפֶרֶק חֵלֶק (סַנְהֶדְרִין צ״ח סוֹף עַמּוּד ב׳): ״כְּגוֹן רַבִּי״
Wherefore Rebbe was a prototype of Mashiach: "such as Rebbe" (Sanhedrin 98b);
וּבְמִדְרַשׁ אֵיכָה (פָּרָשָׁה ד׳:כ״ב) אָמְרוּ עָלָיו: ״׳רוּחַ אַפֵּינוּ מְשִׁיחַ ה׳ נִלְכַּד בִּשְׁחִיתוֹתָם׳ (אֵיכָה ד:כ) — זֶה רַבִּי״
and in Midrash Eichah (4:22): "'the breath of our nostrils, the anointed of Hashem, was taken in their pits'—this is Rebbe";
הַיְינוּ דְּמַה שֶּׁלֹּא עָלְתָה בְּיָדוֹ הָיָה רַק מִפְּנֵי עֲוֹן הַדּוֹר וּבִשְׁחִיתוֹתֵינוּ וְשֶׁאֵין הַדּוֹר זַכַּאי
meaning that his failure to complete the redemption was due solely to the sins of the generation;
אֲבָל הוּא הָיָה זַכַּאי וְלֹא מֵת, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּכְתוּבּוֹת (ק״ג סוֹף עַמּוּד א׳) דְּכָל בֵּי שִׁמְשֵׁי אָתֵי לְבֵיתֵיהּ
but he personally was righteous and never died, visiting his home every Friday twilight (Kesubos 103b).
וְלֹא כְּשִׁמְשׁוֹן שֶׁחֵטְא עַצְמוֹ גָּרַם
Unlike Samson whose personal fault caused his fall;
וְעַל יְדֵי מוֹתָרוֹת הַמָּמוֹן שֶׁקִּבְּלָה דְּלִילָה מֵהֶם, הוּא מַה שֶּׁכְּדֵי צָרְכָּהּ לֹא הָיָה עַדַיִין מַכְנִיס תַּאֲוַת יֵצֶר הָרָע בְּלִבָּהּ
for through the superfluous wealth Delilah accepted (whereas essential sustenance would not have corrupted her);
רַק הִכְנִיסוּ בָהּ חֶמְדַּת מוֹתָרוֹת, וְהִיא הִכְנִיסָה זֶה בְּשִׁמְשׁוֹן
they injected into her the greed for superfluities, and she transmitted this unto Samson;
לִגְרוֹם קִלְקוּל לְמַה שֶּׁרָצָה לְתַקֵּן אוֹתָם נְפָשׁוֹת הַנִּרְאוֹת כְּמוֹתָרוֹת בָּעוֹלָם שֶׁהָיוּ תְּלוּיִם בִּשְׂעָרוֹתָיו, וְאִשְׁתּוֹ כְּגוּפוֹ
causing the ruin of his mission to rectify those souls appearing as superfluities suspended in his hair, for his wife was as his own body.
אֲבָל אֵצֶל רַבִּי נִתְיַיחֵס הַמּוֹתָרוֹת לַאֲהוֹרְיָירֵיהּ, וְאֶצְלוֹ אַף שֶׁהָיָה בְּגֶדֶר מוֹתָרוֹת, הוּא הָיָה יָכוֹל לְהַכְנִיס הַכֹּל לִקְדוּשָׁה
But with Rebbe the superfluities were attributed unto his stable-master, while he was empowered to elevate all into holiness.

וּבִימֵי רַבִּי פִּנְחָס בֶּן יָאִיר שֶׁלֹּא הִגִּיעַ עַדַיִין לִשְׁלֵימוּת הַקְּדוּשָׁה, רָאָה אֶצְלוֹ הַפְּרֵידוֹת לְבָנוֹת הַמַּזִּיקוֹת, וְאָמַר: ״מַלְאַךְ הַמָּוֶת בְּבֵיתוֹ וְכוּלֵיהּ״ (חֻלִּין ז׳ עַמּוּד ב׳)

Yet in the days of Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair, when Rebbe had not yet attained consummate holiness, Rabbi Pinchas beheld the dangerous white mules, declaring: "The Angel of Death is in his house, and shall I dine with him?!" (Chullin 7b);
וּבְוַדַּאי לֹא הָיָה רַבִּי קוֹנֶה מַזִּיק בְּבֵיתוֹ
and certainly Rebbe would never purchase a harmful beast for his estate;
וְצָרִיךְ לוֹמַר דְּהָיוּ קוֹנִים הַפְּרֵידוֹת קְטַנּוֹת, דִּבְזֶה הָיָה בִּרְכַּת הַצְלָחָה כְּשֶׁיּוּגְדְּלוּ וְיַצְלִיחוּ
but they bought the mules as colts, seeking the blessing of profit as they matured;
וְאָז בְּקַטְנוּתָן לֹא הָיָה אֶפְשָׁר לְהַכִּיר עַדַיִין הָא דִּ״חִוָּורָן רֵישׁ כַּרְעַיְיהוּ״, דְּאַחַר כָּךְ הָיוּ מִתְלַבְּנוֹת, וְזֶהוּ שֶׁאָמַר: ״מַלְאַךְ הַמָּוֶת בְּבֵיתוֹ״.
and in their youth it was impossible to recognize that their hooves were white, turning white only later, which is why he called them the Angel of Death.
וְאַחַר כֵּן אָמַר לוֹ שֶׁאֵין שׁוּם תַּקָּנָה, אֲפִילּוּ לְהָרְגָן אֵין יָכוֹל, וְאִם כֵּן אָנוּס הוּא מַה יַּעֲשֶׂה?
And afterward Rabbi Pinchas told him there was no remedy, unable even to slaughter them; so being in an unavoidable predicament (oness), what was Rebbe to do?
וְצָרִיךְ לוֹמַר דְּהַכַּוָּונָה: אָמַר לוֹ: הִזְמִין הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ תַּקָּלָה זוֹ לְבֵיתוֹ, וְ״אֵין דָּבָר רַע יוֹרֵד מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה נ״א:ג׳)
and one must say the intent was: Hashem brought this stumbling block to his house, and no evil thing descends from Heaven;
וְאִם הַשֶּׁפַע מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לֹא הָיָה נִשְׁפָּע מַלְאַךְ הַמָּוֶת וְדָבָר הַמַּזִּיק
and had this bounty issued purely from Hashem, the Angel of Death and a harmful beast would not have descended;
וְעַל כָּרְחָךְ שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּקֶרֶב לְבָבוֹ עַדַיִין אֵיזֶה חֶמְדָּה לְמוֹתָרוֹת, שֶׁמִּזֶּה בָּא הַשְׁפָּעָה זוֹ מִצַּד הַיֵּצֶר וְלֹא מִצַּד הַקְּדוּשָׁה
perforce proving that within Rebbe's heart lingered an inclination for superfluities, this influx deriving from the yetzer and not from holiness.
וְעַל כֵּן נִזְדַּמֵּן דָּבָר הַמַּזִּיק, וְעַל כֵּן קְרָאוֹ ״מַלְאַךְ הַמָּוֶת״
Wherefore a harmful beast occurred, and wherefore he called it the "Angel of Death";
דְּ״הוּא שָׂטָן, הוּא יֵצֶר הָרָע, הוּא מַלְאַךְ הַמָּוֶת״, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא ט״ז עַמּוּד א׳)
for "he is Satan, he is the yetzer hara, he is the Angel of Death" (Bava Batra 16a);
וּמֵאַחַר שֶׁהוּא מִסִּטְרָא דְּיֵצֶר הָרָע הוּא עַצְמוֹ מַלְאַךְ הַמָּוֶת, וְנִתְלַבֵּשׁ בְּמַלְאַךְ הַמָּוֶת לָבוֹא לְבֵיתוֹ
and being from the yetzer hara it was the Angel of Death himself, clothed within the beasts;
דְּ״יוֹרֵד וּמַסִּית״ תְּחִלָּה בַּחֶמְדָּה, וְאַחַר כָּךְ ״יוֹרֵד וְנוֹטֵל נְשָׁמָה״ בְּאוֹתוֹ דָּבָר שֶׁל הַחֵטְא עַצְמוֹ
who first incites through desire, and then descends to take the soul through the very medium of the sin;
כְּטַעַם: ״[חַטָּאִים] תְּרַדֵּף רָעָה״ (מִשְׁלֵי י״ג:כ״א), הָרָעָה וְהָעֲבֵירָה עַצְמָהּ, דִּ״שְׂכַר עֲבֵירָה — עֲבֵירָה״ (אָבוֹת ד:ב), וְהִיא עַצְמָהּ הִיא הַעוֹנֶשֶׁת וְנוֹטֶלֶת הַנְּקָמָה:
as in "evil pursues sinners" (Mishlei 13:21), the transgression itself being the punishment and retribution!
אוֹת ל״ה — צַעַר בַּעֲלֵי חַיִּים, בַּל תַּשְׁחִית, וְהַר שֶׁהִבְדִּיל בֵּינֵיהֶם — Section 35: Animal Suffering, Bal Tashchit, and the Mountain that Parted Them

The theme: Halachic dilemmas regarding white mules, the prohibition of Tza'ar Ba'alei Chayim, and the mountain separating Rebbe and Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair. Rebbe asked: "Shall I declaw (ne'akrinyahu) or slaughter them?" Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair replied: "There is the prohibition of causing pain to animals (tza'ar ba'alei chayim)" and "the prohibition of wanton destruction (bal tashchit)" (Chullin 7b). Commentators questioned this: since Rabbi Pinchas labeled them the Angel of Death, one is permitted to slay harmful beasts to protect human life, overriding tza'ar ba'alei chayim and bal tashchit! The deeper intent was that Rabbi Pinchas came to demonstrate that Rebbe had not yet attained consummate holiness, and that he was not permitted to dine with him. Rebbe suggested: "I will use them after declawing them, or benefit from their hides after slaughtering them". Rabbi Pinchas answered: If this wealth were a divine blessing, Hashem would not have provided an acquisition that forces you to transgress tza'ar ba'alei chayim or bal tashchit! An acquisition requiring an unlawful act perforce issues from the yetzer hara. Rebbe did not answer, for "a mountain grew between them" (gava tura, Chullin 7b). Rebbe recognized that he had not yet reached Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair's pinnacle of holiness, but knew his soul was destined to achieve it. Man is judged according to his ultimate end (al shem sofo, Sotah 12b), as Moshe was delivered at the Nile because he was destined to receive the Torah. On the verse "in every place where I cause My Name to be mentioned I will come unto you and bless you" (Shemos 20:21), "I will cause My Name to be mentioned" is future tense, while "I will come unto you and bless you" is present tense—Hashem blessing man immediately on account of his future holiness! The "mountain" was a metaphor for a spiritual partition that arose to separate them from speaking further.
וּבֶאֱמֶת מַה שֶּׁאָמַר ״דְּלָא נַעַקְרִינְהוּ וְנִקְטְלִינְהוּ מִשּׁוּם צַעַר בַּעֲלֵי חַיִּים וּבַל תַּשְׁחִית״ (חֻלִּין ז׳ עַמּוּד ב׳), צָרִיךְ עִיּוּן
And in truth that he told him not to declaw or kill them on account of causing pain to animals and wanton destruction (Chullin 7b), requires deep analysis;
כֵּיוָן דְּקַרְיֵיהּ ״מַלְאַךְ הַמָּוֶת״ וּמַזִּיק, פְּשִׁיטָא דְּרַשַּׁאי לְעָקְרוֹ וּלְקָטְלֵיהּ
for since he designated them the "Angel of Death" and a harmful beast, it is self-evident that one is permitted to declaw or kill them;
וְאֵין לָחוּשׁ לְצַעַר בַּעֲלֵי חַיִּים בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁיֵּשׁ חֲשַׁשׁ צַעַר בְּנֵי אָדָם, וַאֲפִילּוּ סַכָּנָה
there being no concern for the pain of animals where there is danger or suffering to human beings;
וְכֵן לֹא לְ״בַל תַּשְׁחִית״ (דְּבָרִים כ:יט), כִּבְכָל הַמַּזִּיקִין דְּכָל הַקּוֹדֵם לְהָרְגָן זָכָה
and so regarding wanton destruction, for with all dangerous beasts whoever kills them first acquires merit;
וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּהַהוּא בְּמוּעָדִין מִתְּחִלָּתָן, וְאֵלּוּ יֵשׁ לוֹמַר דְּאֵינָן כְּמוּעָדִין, רַק עֲלוּלִין לְכָךְ וְאֵין חִיּוּב לְהָרְגָן
and even if these mules were not confirmed attackers from the outset, merely prone to kick;
מִכָּל מָקוֹם אִי חָיֵישׁ לְכָךְ עַד דִּקְרָאָן ״מַלְאַךְ הַמָּוֶת״, וַדַּאי לֹא שַׁיָּיךְ ״בַּל תַּשְׁחִית״ לְהָרְגָן.
nevertheless if he feared them so much as to call them the Angel of Death, wanton destruction certainly does not apply to slaughtering them.
וְנִרְאֶה מִזֶּה גַּם כֵּן כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ: דְּהוּא בָּא לִלְמוֹד מִזֶּה: דְּגַם רַבִּי עַדַיִין אֵינוֹ בִּשְׁלֵימוּת הַקְּדוּשָׁה כָּרָאוּי
And it appears from this that Rabbi Pinchas came to demonstrate: that Rebbe was not yet in consummate holiness as was fitting;
וְאֵינוֹ רַשַּׁאי לֵיהָנוֹת גַּם מִמֶּנּוּ, מִדְּהִזְמִין לְהַשְׁפִּיעַ לוֹ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ דָּבָר כָּזֶה.
and that Rabbi Pinchas was not permitted to dine with him, seeing that Hashem brought such a flawed acquisition to his estate.
וְעַל זֶה אָמַר: ״נַעַקְרִינְהוּ וְנִקְטְלִינְהוּ״
And on this Rebbe suggested: "I will declaw them or slaughter them";
וְרָצָה לוֹמַר: דִּלְכָךְ נִשְׁפַּע לִי, לְהִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ בּוֹ אַחַר שֶׁיַּעַקְרֵן, אוֹ לְקָטְלֵיהּ וְלֵיהָנוֹת מֵעוֹרוֹ
meaning: this bounty was channeled unto me to use them after declawing, or to benefit from their hides after slaughter;
וְשַׁפִּיר אָמַר לֵיהּ: דְּאִיכָּא צַעַר בַּעֲלֵי חַיִּים וּבַל תַּשְׁחִית
and Rabbi Pinchas rightly answered: there is tza'ar ba'alei chayim and bal tashchit!
וַאֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא לִדְחוֹת אִיסּוּרִים אֵלּוּ מִפְּנֵי חֲשַׁשׁ הַתַּקָּלָה לְאָדָם עַל יָדָם
And even if you dismiss these prohibitions on account of human danger;

מִכָּל מָקוֹם לֹא הָיָה לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לְהַזְמִין לְךָ כָּאֵלֶּה וְשֶׁיִּהְיֶה זֶה בִּרְכַּת ה׳ שֶׁתֵּהָנֶה מֵהֶם אַחַר כָּךְ, וְתִצְטָרֵךְ לַעֲבוֹר אַצַּעַר בַּעֲלֵי חַיִּים אוֹ עַל בַּל תַּשְׁחִית
nevertheless the Blessed Name would not have sent you an acquisition as a divine blessing that compels you to violate tza'ar ba'alei chayim or bal tashchit!
וְעַל כָּרְחָךְ הַשְׁפָּעָה זוֹ שֶׁיִּצְטָרֵךְ לַעֲשׂוֹת עַל יְדֵי זֶה דָּבָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ רָאוּי — הוּא מִצַּד הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע.
and perforce an influx that forces an unworthy deed derives from the yetzer hara.
וְלֹא נִזְכַּר שֶׁהֵשִׁיב רַבִּי עַל זֶה כְּלוּם, רַק דַּהֲוָה מְבַתֵּשׁ בֵּיהּ וּגְבָא טוּרָא (חֻלִּין ז׳ עַמּוּד ב׳)
And it is not recorded that Rebbe replied anything to this, but merely that he importuned him and a mountain grew between them (Chullin 7b);
נִרְאֶה דְּהֵבִין רַבִּי דְּעַדַיִין לֹא הִגִּיעַ לְתַכְלִית הַקְּדוּשָׁה כְּרַבִּי פִּנְחָס בֶּן יָאִיר
Rebbe realizing that he had not yet arrived at the zenith of holiness like Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair;
אֲבָל יָדַע בְּנַפְשֵׁיהּ מִכָּל מָקוֹם דְּהוּא כְּלִי מוּכָן לָבוֹא לִשְׁלֵימוּת קְדוּשָׁה כָּמוֹהוּ, וְאֵין אָדָם מַגִּיעַ לִשְׁלֵימוּת מַדְרֵיגָתוֹ מִיָּד
yet knowing in his soul that he was a vessel prepared to attain that consummate holiness, for man does not reach his ultimate level immediately.
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם קַיְימָא לַן בְּכָל מָקוֹם: ״כָּל הָעוֹמֵד לִזְרוֹק — כְּזָרוּק דָּמֵי״, דְּנִידּוֹן מִיָּד כְּפִי מַה שֶּׁהוּא עוֹמֵד לְאוֹתוֹ דָּבָר
And nevertheless the established legal principle is: whatever is destined to occur is considered as already occurred, judged immediately according to its destined state;

וְכֵן הָאָדָם נִידּוֹן ״עַל שֵׁם סוֹפוֹ״, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם דְּנִיצּוֹל, דְּאָמְרוּ מַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת: שֶׁעָתִיד לוֹמַר שִׁירָה אוֹ לְקַבֵּל תּוֹרָה בְּיוֹם זֶה (סוֹטָה י״ב עַמּוּד ב׳)
and so man is judged according to his ultimate end, as stated regarding Moshe who was spared at the Nile because the angels argued he was destined to receive the Torah (Sotah 12b).
וְכֵן שָׁמַעְתִּי עַל פָּסוּק: ״בְּכָל הַמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר אַזְכִּיר אֶת שְׁמִי — אָבוֹא אֵלֶיךָ וּבֵרַכְתִּיךָ״ (שְׁמוֹת כ:כא)
And so have I heard expounded on: "in every place where I cause My Name to be mentioned I will come unto you and bless you" (Shemos 20:21);
דְּ״אַזְכִּיר״ לְשׁוֹן עָתִיד, דִּבְכָל נֶפֶשׁ שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא רוֹאֶה שֶׁעָתִיד לִהְיוֹת הַזְכָּרַת שְׁמוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּקֶרֶב לְבָבוֹ וְשֶׁיַּשְׁרֶה שְׁכִינָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּקִרְבּוֹ
for "where I cause My Name to be mentioned" is future tense, referring to any soul in whom Hashem foresees His Shechinah will dwell;
וְ״אָבוֹא אֵלֶיךָ״ בַּהֹוֶה וּבְנוֹכַח תֵּיכֶף וּבֵרַכְתִּיךָ, אַף דְּעַדַיִין הוּא מְשׁוּקָּע בְּמַה שֶּׁמְּשׁוּקָּע
while "I will come unto you and bless you" is present tense, Hashem descending to bless him immediately even while still submerged in worldly matters;
מִכָּל מָקוֹם הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מְבָרֵךְ עַל שֵׁם הֶעָתִיד
the Blessed Name blessing him on account of his future spiritual elevation.

וְזֶהוּ דְּ״הֲוָה מְבַתֵּשׁ בֵּיהּ וּגְבָא טוּרָא״, נִרְאֶה דְּהוּא לְשׁוֹן מוּשְׁאָל עַל אֵיזֶה דָּבָר הַמַּפְסִיק וְחוֹצֵץ בֵּינֵיהֶם שֶׁנִּזְדַּמֵּן אָז לְשָׁם, שֶׁהִבְדִּילָם מִלְּדַבֵּר עוֹד מִזֶּה:
And "he importuned him and a mountain grew between them" appears as a metaphorical expression for a spiritual barrier that intervened between them, preventing them from speaking further!

5.h: אוֹת ל״ו — פְּטִירַת רַבִּי פִּנְחָס בֶּן יָאִיר בַּיְרוּשַׁלְמִי בְּ״אֶשָׁתָא״, הַנִּיצוֹץ הַמְשֻׁתָּף, וְהָעַרְבוּת דְּ״לַמָּס מֵרֵעֵהוּ חָסֶד״ — Section 36: The Passing of Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair in the Fire, The Shared Soul-Spark, and Mutual Responsibility

The theme: The fire from Heaven in the Jerusalem Talmud as a fever, Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair’s passing, and the mutual accountability of shared soul-sparks. In Yerushalmi Demai (1:3) and Ta'anit (3:1), fire descended from Heaven surrounding Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair, Rebbe crying: "If we did not merit to be sated from him in this world, we shall merit to be sated from him in the World to Come!" The Korban HaEdah comments that Rabbi Pinchas departed the world in that fire. Fire (eshta) denotes the burning fever of a mortal illness, from which Rabbi Pinchas passed away, making further speech impossible. When Rabbi Pinchas cried to his townsmen: "B'nei karta, come near me!" and then "B'nei didi, come near me!" he called upon the angels created from his mitzvos (who are made of fire), or addressed his sufferings as "my sons" (like Rabbi Elazar ben Rabbi Shimon calling his afflictions "my brothers and friends", Bava Metzia 84b). This fatal illness was an accounting for not submitting to Rebbe's holy desire, for Rebbe intended for Heaven to dine with a scholar, which is like enjoying the radiance of the Shechinah and offering libations on the altar (Yoma 71a). Refusing to bestow kindness upon a friend borders on "To him that is afflicted kindness should be showed from his friend" (la-mas me-re'ehu chesed, Iyov 6:14). Furthermore, since Rabbi Pinchas and Rebbe shared the same soul-spark, if Rabbi Pinchas perceived a subtle flaw in Rebbe, he should have realized that a trace of that flaw lingered within himself; for had he completed his personal soul, all sparks belonging to his root would have achieved consummate perfection alongside him!

p: וּבַיְרוּשַׁלְמִי דִּדְמַאי (פֶּרֶק א׳ הֲלָכָה ג׳) וּדְתַעֲנִית (פֶּרֶק ג׳ הֲלָכָה א׳) אִיתָא: שֶׁהִקִּיפַתּוּ אֵשׁ מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם
And in the Jerusalem Talmud (Demai 1:3 and Ta'anit 3:1) it is taught: that fire from Heaven surrounded Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair;
וּדְאָמַר רַבִּי: ״אִם לֹא זָכִינוּ נִשְׂבַּע מִינֵּיהּ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, נִזְכֶּה וְנִשְׂבַּע מִינֵּיהּ בָּעוֹלָם הַבָּא״
and that Rebbe proclaimed: "If we did not merit to be sated from him in this world, we shall merit to be sated from him in the World to Come!"
וְנִרְאֶה נָכוֹן מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בְּ״קָרְבַּן הָעֵדָה״ בְּתַעֲנִית שָׁם: שֶׁנִּסְתַּלֵּק בְּאוֹתוֹ אֵשׁ מִן הָעוֹלָם, עַיֵּין שָׁם
And correct appears what the Korban HaEdah wrote in Ta'anit: that Rabbi Pinchas departed from the world in that fire, see there;
וְנִרְאֶה דְּ״נַחְתָא אֶשָׁתָא מִן שְׁמַיָּא״, הַיְינוּ חוֹלִי אֶשָׁתָא וְחוֹם וְקַדַּחַת שֶׁבָּאָה לְרַבִּי פִּנְחָס בֶּן יָאִיר אָז וְנִפְטַר מִזֶּה
and it appears that "fire descended from Heaven" denotes the burning fever (eshta) and illness that befell Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair from which he passed away;
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה לֹא יָכֹל לְדַבֵּר עִמּוֹ עוֹד שֶׁיִּסְעוֹד אֶצְלוֹ.
wherefore he could speak with Rebbe no further concerning dining with him.
וְשָׁם אִיתָא דְּרַבִּי פִּנְחָס בֶּן יָאִיר אָמַר: ״בְּנֵי קַרְתָּא קְרִיבוּ לִי, בְּנֵי דִידִי קְרִיבוּ לִי״
And there it is recorded that Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair cried: "Sons of the town, draw near to me! My own sons, draw near to me!";
וְעַיֵּין שָׁם בְּ״קָרְבַּן הָעֵדָה״ וְהָרַב רַבִּי אֵלִיָּהוּ פוֹלְדָא מַה שֶּׁפֵּירְשׁוּ, וְלָקוּחַ מֵהַ״יְפֵה מַרְאֶה״
see the commentaries of the Korban HaEdah and Rabbi Eliyahu Fulda, derived from the Yefeh Mareh;
וְלֵיתָא, רַק אָמַר תְּחִלָּה לִבְנֵי עִירוֹ: ״בְּנֵי קַרְתָּא קְרִיבוּ לִי״ — רָצָה לוֹמַר: קִרְבוּ אֵלַי וְהַקִּיפוּנִי, כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יוּכְלוּ שְׁלוּחֵי רַבִּי לָבוֹא אֵלָיו
and rather he initially addressed his townsmen: "draw near and encircle me," so that the messengers of Rebbe could not reach him;

וּלְפִיכָךְ בָּאוּ וְהִקִּיפוּהוּ, וְאַחַר שֶׁהָלְכוּ מִפְּנֵי כְּבוֹדוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי, אָמַר: ״בְּנֵי דִידִי קְרִיבוּ אַתֶּם אֵלַי וְהַקִּיפוּנִי, וְלֹא תָחוּשׁוּ לִכְבוֹדוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי״, וְעַל זֶה נַחְתָא אֶשָׁתָא.
and after they withdrew out of deference to Rebbe's royal honor, he cried: "My own sons, draw near and encircle me, without regard to Rebbe's honor," whereupon the burning fire descended.
וְאִם יִהְיֶה כִּפְשָׁטוֹ ״אֵשׁ מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם״, יִהְיֶה ״בְּנֵי דִידִי״ הַכַּוָּונָה עַל הַמַּלְאָכִים
And if the fire be understood literally, "my own sons" refers to the angels;
וּקְרָאָם ״בָּנָיו״, דְּ״תּוֹלְדוֹתֵיהֶם שֶׁל צַדִּיקִים — מִצְוֹת וּמַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים״ (תַּנְחוּמָא נֹחַ א׳), וּמִכָּל מִצְוָה נִבְרָא מַלְאָךְ (אָבוֹת ד:יא)
calling them his sons because "the offspring of the righteous are mitzvos and good deeds" (Tanchuma, Noach §1), an angel being created from every mitzvah (Avos 4:11);
וְאָמַר לְאוֹתָם מַלְאָכִים שֶׁהֵם בָּנָיו שֶׁיַּקִּיפוּהוּ, וְהַמַּלְאָכִים הֵם אֵשׁ.
commanding those angels who are his spiritual offspring to encircle him, angels being fashioned of fire.
וּכְפִי מַה שֶּׁכָּתַבְתִּי דְּרָצָה לוֹמַר חוֹלִי, יֵשׁ לוֹמַר דְּקָרָא לַיִּסּוּרִין ״בָּנַי״
And according to my explanation that the fire was fever, he designated his afflictions "my sons";
עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁקְּרָאָן רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן: ״בּוֹאוּ אַחַי וְרֵיעָי״ (בָּבָא מְצִיעָא פ״ד רֵישׁ עַמּוּד ב׳)
after the manner of Rabbi Elazar ben Rabbi Shimon who addressed his afflictions: "Come, my brothers and friends!" (Bava Metzia 84b).
וּלְפִי מַה שֶּׁכָּתַבְתִּי דְּנִפְטַר מֵאוֹתוֹ חוֹלִי, נִרְאֶה דְּהָיָה זֶה עֹונֶשׁ עַל שֶׁלֹּא עָשָׂה רְצוֹן רַבִּי, דְּמִכָּל מָקוֹם הוּא רָצָה לְשֵׁם שָׁמָיִם
And according to what I explained that he passed away from that illness, it appears this was a subtle heavenly rebuke for refusing Rebbe's will, for Rebbe intended purely for Heaven;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ לְשׁוֹן: ״נִזְכֶּה וְנִשְׂבַּע מִינֵּיהּ״, דְּכַוָּונָתוֹ שֶׁהִזְמִינוֹ הָיָה כְּדֵי לֵיהָנוֹת מִסְּעוּדָה שֶׁתַּלְמִיד חָכָם מֵסֵב בָּהּ
as reflected in Rebbe's lament: "we shall merit to be sated from him," Rebbe's sole intent in inviting him having been to participate in a meal where a scholar reclines;
שֶׁהוּא ״כְּנֶהֱנֶה מִזִּיו הַשְּׁכִינָה״ (בְּרָכוֹת ס״ד עַמּוּד א׳)
which is accounted "as if enjoying the radiance of the Shechinah" (Berachos 64a);
וְהַמְהַנֶּה לְתַלְמִיד חָכָם כְּמַקְרִיב קָרְבָּן וּמְנַסֵּךְ יַיִן עַל גַּבֵּי מִזְבֵּחַ (יוֹמָא ע״א סוֹף עַמּוּד א׳)
and he who provides for a scholar is as though he offered sacrifices and poured wine libations upon the altar (Yoma 71a);
וְעַל כָּרְחָךְ מִינֵּיהּ וְעַל יָדוֹ הָיָה נִשְׂבָּע וְנֶהֱנֶה מִזִּיו הַשְּׁכִינָה.
and perforce through Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair, Rebbe would have been sated from the radiance of the Shechinah.
וְאִם כֵּן אַף דְּרַבִּי פִּנְחָס בֶּן יָאִיר שֶׁלֹּא רָצָה לֵיהָנוֹת גַּם כֵּן כִּוֵּון לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם
And if so, although Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair in refusing benefit likewise acted for the sake of Heaven;
מִכָּל מָקוֹם הָיָה בִּכְלַל ״לַמָּס מֵרֵעֵהוּ חָסֶד״ (אִיּוֹב ו:יד) בְּדָבָר זֶה, וְאֶפְשָׁר שֶׁאִם הָיָה שׁוֹקֵל זֶה הָיָה לוֹ לְבַטֵּל רְצוֹנוֹ מִפְּנֵי רָצוֹן שֶׁל רַבִּי.

nevertheless in this matter he withheld kindness from a friend ("to him that is afflicted kindness should be showed from his friend", Iyov 6:14), and had he weighed this he should have nullified his will before Rebbe's will.
אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת, מֵאַחַר שֶׁהָיוּ שְׁנֵיהֶם נִיצוֹץ אֶחָד
But in truth, since both issued from a single soul-spark;
אִם רָאָה אֵיזֶה חִסָּרוֹן בְּרַבִּי, הָיָה לוֹ לְהַרְגִּישׁ דְּוַדַּאי יֵשׁ מֵעָוֹן זֶה גַּם בּוֹ
if he perceived a subtle shortcoming in Rebbe, he should have sensed that a trace of this blemish lingered within himself;
דְּאִם הוּא כְּבָר הִשְׁלִים נַפְשׁוֹ, הָיָה מַשְׁלִים גַּם כָּל הַנִּיצוֹצִים הַשַּׁיָּיכִים לְשׁוֹרֶשׁ נַפְשׁוֹ
for had he brought his own soul to absolute completion, he would have perfected all sparks belonging to his soul-root;
וְהָיָה גַּם נֶפֶשׁ רַבִּי בְּתַכְלִית הַשְּׁלֵימוּת כָּמוֹהוּ:
and the soul of Rebbe would have been in consummate perfection alongside him!
יִשְׂרָאֵל קְדוֹשִׁים — פֶּרֶק ה׳, אוֹתִיּוֹת ל״ז–ל״ט; פֶּרֶק ו׳, אוֹתִיּוֹת א׳–ג׳
אוֹת ל״ז — חֶמְדַּת מוֹתָרוֹת לְתִיקּוּן הַנְּפָשׁוֹת הַנִּדָּחוֹת, ״חֲטָא כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּזְכֶּה חֲבֵירָךְ״, וּמְחִיצָתוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי לֶעָתִיד לָבוֹא
Section 37: The Apparent Desire for Superfluities to Rectify Outcast Souls, Self-Sacrifice for Another, and Rebbe's Future Dwelling

5.h: The theme: Rebbe assuming the trace of monetary desire as an ascent through descent (yeridah l'tzorech aliyah), Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair guarding only himself, and their shared soul-root. What appeared to Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair as an inclination toward superfluities within Rebbe was intended to rectify those souls in Israel that pursue monetary excess. Monetary greed is the root of the Serpent, which caused the spiritual ruin of outcast souls who appear as bodily trimmings. A faint trace of this flaw was present in Rebbe as an intentional descent to achieve a cosmic ascent: when he rectified it, it would be rectified in all those souls, restoring them to holiness. Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair followed his own path, fearing lest any subtle flaw touch his own soul, even if that withheld spiritual healing from another. In such a dilemma, one must be concerned for the repair of his fellow, as the Sages said: "sin so that your fellow may merit" (Shabbat 4a). Fearing exclusively for one’s personal spiritual perfection can itself be considered a form of subtle self-interest. When Rabbi Pinchas passed away, Rebbe recognized that justice was with him: Rebbe would ultimately rectify all things and attain Rabbi Pinchas's pinnacle of holiness. Though he had not yet reached that rung in this world, he was confident that in the World to Come he would dwell in his partition, being carved from a single soul-root and spark!

p: וּבֶאֱמֶת מַה שֶּׁהָיָה נִרְאֶה אֵלָיו בְּרַבִּי תְּחִלָּה חֶמְדָּה לְמוֹתָרוֹת
And in truth, that which initially appeared unto Rabbi Pinchas within Rebbe as a desire for superfluities;
הָיָה זֶה לְצֹרֶךְ תִּיקּוּן אוֹתָם הַנְּפָשׁוֹת מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל הַמְבַקְשִׁים מוֹתָרוֹת בְּמָמוֹן
was intended for the rectification of those souls in Israel who pursue superfluities in wealth;
שֶׁזֶּהוּ שׁוֹרֶשׁ נָחָשׁ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְעֵיל, שֶׁמִּזֶּה בָּא קִלְקוּל אוֹתָם הַנְּפָשׁוֹת הַנִּדָּחוֹת מִשּׁוֹרֶשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל וְשֶׁנִּרְאִים כְּמוֹתָרוֹת.
this being the root of the Serpent as I wrote above, whence arose the ruin of those outcast souls banished from Israel's root who appear as bodily superfluities.
וְעַל כֵּן הָיָה שֶׁמֶץ מֵחִסָּרוֹן כָּזֶה גַּם בְּרַבִּי, וְהוּא ״יְרִידָה שֶׁלְּצֹרֶךְ עֲלִיָּה״
Wherefore a faint trace of such an imperfection was present in Rebbe as well, being an intentional descent for the sake of an ascent;
כְּשֶׁיְּתַקְּנוֹ — יְתוּקַּן חִסָּרוֹן זֶה גַּם בִּשְׁאָר נְפָשׁוֹת, וְיְתוּקְּנוּ גַּם אוֹתָן נְפָשׁוֹת.
so that when he would rectify it, this flaw would be healed across other souls, and those outcast souls would be redeemed.
וְרַבִּי פִּנְחָס בֶּן יָאִיר לְטַעְמֵיהּ, דְּחָשַׁשׁ שֶׁלֹּא יַגִּיעַ אֵיזֶה חִסָּרוֹן אֵלָיו, אַף שֶׁיִּמָּנַע עַל יְדֵי זֶה הַטּוֹב מִזּוּלָתוֹ.
And Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair followed his own reasoning, fearing lest any subtle flaw reach himself, even if that withheld spiritual benefit from another.
וּבֶאֱמֶת בִּכְהַאי גַּוְונָא יוֹתֵר רָאוּי לָחוּשׁ לְתִיקּוּן הָאַחֵר
And in truth in such a case it is more fitting to be concerned for the rectification of another;
וְאָמְרִינַן בִּכְהַאי גַּוְונָא: ״לֹא לָאָדָם [צ״ל חֲטוֹא כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּזְכֶּה חֲבֵירָךְ]״ (שַׁבָּת ד׳ עַמּוּד א׳)
and we say in such circumstances: "sin so that your fellow may merit" (Shabbat 4a);
וְאַדְּרַבָּא זֶה יֵשׁ לְהַחְשִׁיב לְחֶמְדָּה וְתַאֲוָה, שֶׁחוֹשֵׁשׁ רַק לְנַפְשׁוֹ וְלֹא לְזוּלָתוֹ.
and on the contrary, this self-protective restraint may be accounted as a subtle desire, being anxious solely for one's own soul and not for another.
וְעַל כֵּן כְּשֶׁנִּפְטַר רַבִּי פִּנְחָס בֶּן יָאִיר עַל יְדֵי זֶה, וְהֵבִין רַבִּי דְּהַדִּין עִמּוֹ
Wherefore when Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair passed away through this, and Rebbe understood that justice was with him;
וְשֶׁהוּא עָתִיד לְתַקֵּן עַל יְדֵי זֶה הַכֹּל, וְיַגִּיעַ בֶּאֱמֶת לִקְדֻשָּׁתוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי פִּנְחָס בֶּן יָאִיר
and that he was destined to rectify all things through this and truly attain the holiness of Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair;
אַף דְּמִכָּל מָקוֹם לְשָׁעָה דְּהַשְׁתָּא בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה לֹא זָכָה עַדַיִין לְהַגִּיעַ לְמַעֲלָתוֹ
even though at that present hour in this world he had not yet merited to reach his stature;
מִכָּל מָקוֹם בָּטַח שֶׁיִּזְכֶּה לְעָלְמָא דְּאָתֵי לִהְיוֹת עִמּוֹ בִּמְחִיצָתוֹ
nevertheless Rebbe was confident that in the World to Come he would merit to dwell with him in his partition;
כַּאֲשֶׁר הֵם מִשּׁוֹרֶשׁ אֶחָד וְנִיצוֹץ אֶחָד, כִּי עָתִיד לְהַגִּיעַ לִשְׁלֵימוּת הַקְּדוּשָׁה:
being from a single root and spark, because he was destined to attain consummate holiness!

אוֹת ל״ח — ״גְּבָא טוּרָא בֵּינַיְיהוּ״ כְּיֵצֶר הָרָע הַנִּדְמֶה לְהַר, עֶשֶׂר קְדוּשׁוֹת בַּשָּׁנָה, וּקְדֻשַּׁת ט״ו בְּאָב וִימוֹת הַחוֹל — Section 38: "A Mountain Grew Between Them", The Yetzer Likened to a Mountain, and Ten Gradations of Sanctity in Time

The theme: The mountain that grew between them, the Bavli versus the Yerushalmi, Rebbe’s acceptance of suffering after Rabbi Elazar ben Rabbi Shimon, and the ten sanctities of the year. Our Babylonian Talmud refrained from detailing the death of Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair, hinting at it through: "a mountain grew between them" (gava tura, Chullin 7b). In Sukkah (52a), the Sages teach that the yetzer hara appears unto the righteous as a mountain: because of their supreme dread of sin, even the slightest impulse appears as an immense mountain. What separated them were arguments regarding that very "mountain" of subtle temptation; Rabbi Pinchas feared it, and his harsh judgment brought about his passing, for "there is no death without sin" (Shabbat 55a). Rebbe lamented: "If during their lifetime they are thus, in their death how much more so!" (Chullin 7b; Maharsha ad loc.). In this world, Rabbi Pinchas was superior; but in the World to Come, Rebbe would dwell with him. Rebbe was not titled "our holy Master" (Rabbeinu HaKadosh) until the end of his days after accepting bodily afflictions, following the death of Rabbi Elazar ben Rabbi Shimon, whose widow sent to Rebbe: "Shall a vessel used for holy matter be used for secular matter?" (Bava Metzia 84b). Rabbi Pinchas, Rabbi Elazar, and Rebbe were the three primary heads of the corporate stature of holiness in that generation. Just as there are ten sanctities in Space (Kelim 1:6–9), so are there ten in Time (Shanah): five explicit in the Torah (Shabbat, Yom Kippur, Yom Tov, Chol HaMoed, Rosh Chodesh); the sixth is Erev Pesach and wood-offering days; the seventh and eighth are Chanukah and Purim (rabbinic); the ninth is Tu B'Av, sanctified through Jewish custom (minhag Yisrael Torah hu, Ta'anit 30b); and the tenth is the holiness within every weekday when engaging in Torah, prayer, and mitzvos—transforming secular weekdays into "secular Sabbaths"!
וּבְתַלְמוּדָא דִּידַן לֹא רָצוּ לְהַזְכִּיר עִנְיָן זֶה, רַק אָמְרוּ בְּרֶמֶז: ״דִּגְבָא טוּרָא בֵּינַיְיהוּ״ (חֻלִּין ז׳ עַמּוּד ב׳)
And in our Babylonian Talmud the Sages preferred not to explicitly mention this passing, alluding to it by saying: "a mountain grew between them" (Chullin 7b);
וְנִרְאֶה דְּרוֹמֵז גַּם כֵּן לְמַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ בְּ״הֶחָלִיל״ (סֻכָּה נ״ב עַמּוּד א׳): ״צַדִּיקִים — נִדְמֶה לָהֶם [יֵצֶר הָרָע] כְּהַר״
and it appears this alludes to what the Sages taught in Perek HeChalil (Sukkah 52a): "unto the righteous the yetzer hara appears like an immense mountain";
כִּי אוֹתוֹ דָּבָר מוּעָט שֶׁל יֵצֶר רָע שֶׁיֵּשׁ אֶצְלָם שֶׁצְּרִיכִים לְנַצְּחוֹ, לְגוֹדֶל פַּחְדָּם מֵהַחֵטְא וּמֵהַיֵּצֶר... הוּא אֶצְלָם כְּהַר
for that slight trace of the yetzer which they must conquer, because of their immense awe of sin lest they violate the slightest will of their Maker, is perceived by them as a mountain;
וְרָצָה לוֹמַר: דְּמַה שֶּׁהִבְדִּיל בֵּינֵיהֶם הוּא עִנְיְנֵי טַעֲנוֹת שֶׁל אוֹתוֹ הַר הַיָּדוּעַ לַצַּדִּיקִים
meaning that what separated them were the spiritual claims surrounding that very mountain known unto the righteous;
דְּרַבִּי פִּנְחָס בֶּן יָאִיר חָשַׁשׁ עָלָיו, וְגָרַם דְּנִתְפַּס גַּם הוּא, וּכְמַאן דְּאָמַר: ״אֵין מִיתָה בְּלֹא חֵטְא״ (שַׁבָּת נ״ה עַמּוּד א׳).
for Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair was overly anxious regarding it, causing that he too was seized by death, matching the opinion: "there is no death without sin" (Shabbat 55a).
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמַר רַבִּי בְּתַלְמוּדָא דִּידַן: ״אִם בְּחַיֵּיהֶם כָּךְ, [בְּמִיתָתָן עַל אַחַת כַּמָּה וְכַמָּה]״ (חֻלִּין שָׁם), עַיֵּין שָׁם בְּמַהַרְשָׁ״א שֶׁנִּדְחַק
And this explains what Rebbe lamented in our Talmud: "If during their lifetime they are thus, in their death how much more so!" (Chullin 7b), see the Maharsha who struggled with this;

וּלְפִי מַה שֶּׁכָּתַבְתִּי דְּנִפְטַר, אָז שַׁפִּיר שַׁיָּיךְ לָשׁוֹן זֶה: דְּאִם בְּחַיֵּיהֶם כָּךְ שֶׁלֹּא זָכָה לִהְיוֹת עִמּוֹ יַחַד כִּי הָיָה גָּדוֹל מִינֵּיהּ, בְּמִיתָתוֹ עַל אַחַת כַּמָּה וְכַמָּה

and according to what I explained that Rabbi Pinchas passed away, this phrasing is beautifully understood: if in his lifetime Rebbe did not merit to sit with him because Rabbi Pinchas was greater, after his passing all the more so;
וְהוּא הִיפּוּךְ מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּיְרוּשַׁלְמִי כַּנִּזְכָּר, וְהָא וְהָא אִיתֵי
this appearing opposite the Yerushalmi's account, yet both perspectives are authentic:
דִּכְפִי מַה שֶּׁהָיָה אָז לְשַׁעְתֵּיהּ... מִסְּתָמָא הַדִּין עִמּוֹ דְּהָיָה גָּדוֹל אָז מִמֶּנּוּ, וְאִם בְּחַיָּיו כָּל שֶׁכֵּן בְּמוֹתוֹ
for at that immediate hour in this world Rabbi Pinchas was greater than Rebbe;
אַךְ לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא, כְּשֶׁיָּבוֹא גַּם רַבִּי לְשָׁם אַחַר שֶׁיַּגִּיעַ לִשְׁלֵימוּת מַעֲלָתוֹ, שַׁפִּיר יִזְכֶּה לִהְיוֹת עִמּוֹ.
but in the World to Come, when Rebbe arrives after achieving his consummate perfection, he will certainly merit to dwell alongside him!
וְנִרְאֶה דְּגַם אַחַר כָּךְ עַד פְּטִירַת רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, לֹא הָיָה עַדַיִין רַבִּי הַמְיוּחָד בַּדּוֹר בִּקְדֻשָּׁתוֹ
And it appears that even afterward, until the passing of Rabbi Elazar the son of Rabbi Shimon, Rebbe was not yet the preeminent soul of the generation in holiness;
וְלֹא קָרוֹ לֵיהּ עַדַיִין ״רַבֵּינוּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ״ עַד אַחַר כָּךְ בְּסוֹף יָמָיו, אַחַר שֶׁקִּבֵּל עָלָיו גַּם כֵּן יִסּוּרִין
and they did not yet crown him "our holy Master" until the end of his days, after he accepted bodily afflictions upon himself;
שֶׁהֲרֵי אִשְׁתּוֹ דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן שָׁלְחָה לֵיהּ: ״כְּלִי שֶׁנִּשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ בּוֹ קֹדֶשׁ [יִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ בּוֹ חוֹל?]״ בְּהַפּוֹעֲלִים שָׁם (בָּבָא מְצִיעָא פ״ד סוֹף עַמּוּד ב׳)
for the widow of Rabbi Elazar ben Rabbi Shimon sent unto Rebbe when he proposed marriage: "Shall a vessel used for holy matter be used for secular matter?" (Bava Metzia 84b);
שֶׁקְּרָאַתּוּ ״חוֹל״ לְגַבֵּי רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, וְדָבָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ כְּלָל לֹא נִכְתַּב בַּתַּלְמוּד
calling Rebbe "secular" relative to Rabbi Elazar, and an untruth would never be recorded in the Talmud;
וְעוֹד שֶׁגַּם הוּא הוֹדָה לָהּ, וְקִבֵּל גַּם הוּא עָלָיו יִסּוּרִין.
and furthermore Rebbe conceded unto her, accepting afflictions upon himself as well.
וְנִרְאֶה לִי דְּגַם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר הָיָה מֵאוֹתוֹ שׁוֹרֶשׁ
And it appears to me that Rabbi Elazar likewise derived from that very soul-root;
וּשְׁלָשְׁתָּן שֶׁהָיוּ גַּם כֵּן בְּדוֹר אֶחָד, הָיוּ ג׳ רִאשׁוֹנִים שֶׁבְּקוֹמַת הַקְּדוּשָׁה שֶׁבְּאוֹתוֹ הַדּוֹר בִּזְמַן שֶׁהָיוּ שְׁלָשְׁתָּן בְּמַעֲמָד אֶחָד בַּחַיִּים.
and these three masters, living in the same generation, formed the three supreme heads of the stature of holiness in that era while all three were alive.
כִּידוּעַ דְּכָל קוֹמָה כָּלוּל מֵעֶשֶׂר, וְהֵם עֶשֶׂר קְדוּשּׁוֹת דִּתְנַן בְּפֶרֶק קַמָּא דְּכֵלִים (מִשְׁנָה ו׳) בְּ״עוֹלָם״, וְכֵן הֵם בְּ״שָׁנָה״:
As is known that every complete stature comprises ten rungs, matching the ten sanctities in Space (Olam, Kelim 1:6), and so in Time (Shanah):
דֶּרֶךְ מָשָׁל: קְדֻשּׁוֹת שַׁבָּת, וְיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים, וְיוֹם טוֹב, וְחוֹל הַמּוֹעֵד, וְרֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ — הֲרֵי חָמֵשׁ קְדוּשּׁוֹת מְפוֹרָשׁוֹת בַּתּוֹרָה;
for example: the sanctities of Shabbat, Yom Kippur, Yom Tov, Chol HaMoed, and Rosh Chodesh—behold five sanctities explicit in the Torah;
וְעֶרֶב פֶּסַח שֶׁקָּדוֹשׁ מִפְּנֵי הַקְרָבַת הַקָּרְבָּן בּוֹ, וּבִכְלָלוֹ פֶּסַח שֵׁנִי, וְכֵן זְמַנֵּי קָרְבַּן עֵצִים לְאוֹתָם מִשְׁפָּחוֹת וְכַדּוֹמֶה — הֲרֵי שֵׁשׁ;
and Erev Pesach sanctified through offering the Paschal lamb (including Pesach Sheni and wood-offering days)—behold six;
וַחֲנֻכָּה וּפוּרִים שֶׁהֵם קְדוּשּׁוֹת מִדִּבְרֵי סוֹפְרִים — הֲרֵי שְׁמוֹנֶה;
and Chanukah and Purim which are rabbinic sanctities—behold eight;
וְטַ״ו בְּאָב שֶׁהוּא קָדוֹשׁ בִּקְדֻשַּׁת יוֹם טוֹב מִצַּד הַמִּנְהָג
and the Fifteenth of Av (Tu B'Av) which is sanctified as a festival by virtue of custom;
שֶׁיֵּשׁ כַּמָּה דְּבָרִים שֶׁאֵינָם לֹא מִדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה וְלֹא מִדִּבְרֵי סוֹפְרִים, רַק מִצַּד מִנְהַג יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁהוּא גַּם כֵּן תּוֹרָה
for there are matters deriving neither from Torah nor the Scribes, but from Jewish custom which is likewise Torah;

וְכָךְ טַ״ו בְּאָב דְּלֹא נִזְכַּר בְּשׁוּם מָקוֹם מִצְוָה שֶׁיִּהְיֶה יוֹם טוֹב כְּלָל, רַק מַה שֶּׁסִּפְּרוּ בְּסוֹף תַּעֲנִית (כ״ו עַמּוּד ב׳): ״דְּלֹא הָיוּ יָמִים טוֹבִים לְיִשְׂרָאֵל כַּחֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר בְּאָב וְכוּלֵיהּ״
and so Tu B'Av is nowhere biblically commanded as a festival, resting solely upon the tradition in Ta'anit (26b): "There were no greater festivals for Israel than the Fifteenth of Av, etc.";
שֶׁנָּהֲגוּ בוֹ יִשְׂרָאֵל יוֹם טוֹב, וּ״מִנְהַג יִשְׂרָאֵל — תּוֹרָה״ (תּוֹסָפוֹת מְנָחוֹת כ׳ עַמּוּד ב׳), שֶׁהֲרֵי אָמְרוּ בּוֹ בַּגְּמָרָא שָׁם אַחַר כָּךְ הַרְבֵּה טְעָמִים עַל שֶׁהָיָה יוֹם טוֹב
Israel adopting it as a festival, and custom is Torah, the Talmud offering numerous historical reasons for the custom;
וְכוּלָּם טְעָמִים לַמִּנְהָג לְבַד, שֶׁהֲרֵי לֹא אָמְרוּ שֶׁמִּפְּנֵי כֵן צָרִיךְ לַעֲשׂוֹתוֹ יוֹם טוֹב, אֶלָּא שֶׁבִּשְׁבִיל כֵּן נָהֲגוּ כֵן
all being explanations for the custom, there being power in Jewish custom to stamp holiness like Torah law.
וְהָעֲשִׂירִית: הוּא הַקְּדוּשָׁה שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּכָל יְמֵי הַחוֹל, בְּעֵת עִסְקוֹ בַּתּוֹרָה וּבִתְפִלָּה וּבְמִצְוֹת, שֶׁאֵין לְךָ יוֹם פָּנוּי מֵהֶם
And the tenth gradation: is the holiness present in all secular weekdays, in the hour when engaging in Torah, prayer, and mitzvos, no day being devoid of them;
וְרֶגַע עֲשִׂיַּית הַמִּצְוָה, וְכָל שֶׁכֵּן עֵסֶק בַּתּוֹרָה וְכֵן בִּתְפִלָּה, הוּא קָדוֹשׁ לֵאלֹהָיו וּמַכְנִיס קְדוּשָׁה בְּאוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה
and the moment of performing a mitzvah, and all the more so toiling in Torah and prayer, is holy unto God, infusing holiness into that hour;
וְהִיא מוֹשֶׁכֶת עִמָּהּ שְׁאָר הַיּוֹם, דִּכְמוֹ דְּיוֹם אֶחָד בַּשָּׁנָה חָשׁוּב שָׁנָה, כֵּן שָׁעָה אַחַת בַּיּוֹם חָשׁוּב יוֹם
and that moment draws with it the remainder of the day, for just as one day in a year is accounted as a year, so one holy hour in a day is accounted as the day;
וְזֶהוּ גַּם כֵּן בִּכְלַל ״שַׁבָּת שֶׁל חוֹל״, שֶׁלֹּא זָזָה שְׁכִינָה בְּאוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה שֶׁמַּמְשִׁיךְ בָּהּ קְדֻשַּׁת הַשַּׁבָּת
this being included within the "secular Sabbath," the Shechinah never departing during that hour wherein one extends the holiness of Shabbat;
וְזֶה הַמַּדְרֵיגָה הָעֲשִׂירִית הַכּוֹלֶלֶת כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ רֵיקָנִין שֶׁבְּיִשְׂרָאֵל מְלֵאִים מִצְוֹת כְּרִמּוֹן (עֵירוּבִין י״ט עַמּוּד א׳)
this being the tenth gradation embracing all Israel, for even the empty ones in Israel are as full of mitzvos as a pomegranate (Eruvin 19a);
כְּמוֹ שֶׁהַקְּדוּשָׁה הָעֲשִׂירִית בַּמָּקוֹם הוּא אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל הַכּוֹלֶלֶת לְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁכּוּלָּם נָטְלוּ חֵלֶק בָּאָרֶץ:
just as the tenth gradation in Space is the Land of Israel embracing all Israel, all possessing a share in the Land!

אוֹת ל״ט — עֶשֶׂר קְדוּשׁוֹת בַּנְּפָשׁוֹת, הִתְבַּטְּלוּת הַדּוֹרוֹת, וְתַכְלִית הַקְּדוּשָׁה בִּימוֹת הַמָּשִׁיחַ — Section 39: Ten Gradations of Sanctity in Souls, Relativity of Generations, and Consummate Holiness in the Messianic Era

The theme: The ten rungs in human souls, the relativity of holiness between eras, and the Messianic climax. Corresponding to Space and Time, there are ten gradations within Souls (Nefesh): the three highest rungs are the great scholars and heads of the generation; the middle three are the disciples of the academy mirroring the body and arms where the heart resides (Zohar II, 29b, Raya Mehemna); the next three are the supporters of Torah who host scholars or marry their daughters unto scholars (corresponding to Yesod); and the tenth is the root of holiness present within all Israel down to the outright transgressor, who will all be refined to inherit the World to Come. If a soul from the tenth rung purifies himself to his utmost capacity, it is accounted unto him as consummate holiness, yet relative to higher rungs it remains as secular, for rungs of holiness are infinite. Even the Holy of Holies of one generation may be as completely secular relative to another generation, as Rebbe exclaimed when questioning a teaching of Rabbi Yose: "Shall we, who are humiliated, challenge Rabbi Yose?! As is the difference between the Holy of Holies and secular matter, so is the difference between our generation and the generation of Rabbi Yose!" (Yerushalmi Gittin 6:7). Although spoken in humility, the historical disparity is absolute. The wilderness generation is the Holy of Holies of all past eras, yet it is as nothing compared to the generation of Mashiach, where the personal holiness of every individual soul will be manifested in the ultimate perfection possible for humanity before entering the World to Come!
וְכָךְ יֵשׁ עֶשֶׂר מַדְרֵיגוֹת גַּם כֵּן בִּנְפָשׁוֹת, כִּי כָּל דָּבָר הוּא בְּ״עוֹלָם, שָׁנָה, נֶפֶשׁ״ (סֵפֶר יְצִירָה פֶּרֶק ג׳)
And so there exist ten gradations in Souls, for everything is structured across Space, Time, and Soul (Olam, Shanah, Nefesh, Sefer Yetzirah 3:3);
וְג׳ רִאשׁוֹנוֹת הֵם הַתַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים הַגְּדוֹלִים רָאשֵׁי הַדּוֹר
and the three highest rungs are the preeminent Torah scholars, the heads of the generation;
וְג׳ אֶמְצָעִיּוֹת הֵם תַּלְמוּדֵי דְּבֵי רַב, שֶׁלָּקֳבֵל אֵיבָרִין דְּגוּפָא הַנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל מֵהַזֹּוהַר (חֵלֶק ב׳ כ״ט עַמּוּד ב׳, רַעְיָא מְהֵימְנָא)
and the three middle rungs are the disciples of the academy, corresponding to the limbs of the body cited from the Zohar;
שֶׁהֵם גַּם כֵּן נִקְרָאִים ״קֹדֶשׁ קָדָשִׁים״, הַיְינוּ לְגַבֵּי הָאֲחֵרִים, לְפִי שֶׁהַזְּרוֹעוֹת הֵם עַנְפֵי הַלֵּב, וְגוּפָא תַּמָּן לִבָּא שַׁרְיָא
who are likewise designated "Holy of Holies" relative to those below them, for the arms branch from the heart, and in the body the heart resides;
וְג׳ אַחֲרוֹנוֹת הֵם: תּוֹמְכֵי אוֹרַיְיתָא, וּמְשַׁמְּשֵׁי תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים, וְהַמְהַנִּים תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים מִנִּכְסֵיהֶם
and the three lower rungs are: supporters of the Torah, attendants of scholars, and those who provide for scholars from their wealth;
וְאֶפְשָׁר דְּנֶגֶד הַיְסוֹד בְּיִחוּד הוּא הַמְאָרֵחַ תַּלְמִיד חָכָם תּוֹךְ בֵּיתוֹ, וְהַמַּשִּׂיא בִּתּוֹ לְתַלְמִיד חָכָם (בְּרָכוֹת ל״ד עַמּוּד ב׳).
and perhaps corresponding specifically to Yesod is one who hosts a scholar in his home and marries his daughter to a scholar (Berachos 34b).
וְהָעֲשִׂירִית: הִיא מַדְרֵיגָה אַחֲרוֹנָה דִּקְדוּשָׁה שֶׁיֶּשְׁנָהּ בְּכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל קְדוֹשִׁים, אֲפִילּוּ בְּפוֹשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
And the tenth: is the final gradation of holiness present in all holy Israel, even the transgressors of Israel;
דִּלְעָתִיד שֶׁ״לֹּא יִדַּח מִמֶּנּוּ נִדָּח״ (שְׁמוּאֵל ב י״ד:י״ד), וְיִזְכּוּ כוּלָּם לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא שֶׁהוּא עוֹלָם שֶׁכּוּלּוֹ שַׁבָּת קֹדֶשׁ
when in the Future no outcast shall be severed, all meriting the World to Come which is entirely holy Shabbat;
וְאֵין שָׁם עוֹד שׁוּם הֲנָאָה דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, רַק יוֹשְׁבִין וְנֶהֱנִין מִזִּיו הַשְּׁכִינָה (בְּרָכוֹת י״ז עַמּוּד א׳)
having no physical pleasures, but sitting and enjoying the radiance of the Shechinah;
הֲרֵי יְבוֹרַר שֶׁכּוּלָּם קְדוֹשִׁים
it will be demonstrated that all are holy;
וְאַף בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה יֵשׁ בָּהֶם שׁוֹרֶשׁ זֶה, אֶלָּא שֶׁהוּא בְּתַכְלִית הַהֶעְלֵם
and even in this world they possess this root, albeit in profound concealment;
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם כָּל אֶחָד יָכוֹל לְהַגִּיעַ לָזֶה אִם יִרְצֶה גַּם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
nevertheless anyone can attain this if he wills it even in this world;
כְּשֶׁיִּשְׁתַּדֵּל כְּסֵדֶר הַמַּדְרֵיגוֹת שֶׁסִּידֵּר רַבִּי פִּנְחָס בֶּן יָאִיר, עַד שֶׁיַּגִּיעַ לְתַכְלִית הַקְּדוּשָׁה הָעֶלְיוֹנָה כְּפִי מַדְרֵיגָתוֹ מִצַּד שׁוֹרֶשׁ נַפְשׁוֹ.
by striving through the rungs arranged by Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair until attaining ultimate holiness according to his soul-root.
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁמִּי שֶׁהוּא מִמַּדְרֵיגָה הָאַחֲרוֹנָה, אֲפִילּוּ יְזַכֵּךְ נַפְשׁוֹ וִיבָרֵר עַצְמוֹ עַד שֶׁיַּגִּיעַ לִשְׁלֵימוּת הַקְּדוּשָׁה שֶׁלֹּא יְכַוֵּון לְגַרְמֵיהּ וַהֲנָאַת עַצְמוֹ
Meaning that one from the lowest rung, even if he purges his soul so that he intends nothing for self-gratification;
הַיְינוּ כְּפִי מַדְרֵיגָתוֹ לֹא יֵחָשֵׁב זֶה הֲנָאַת עַצְמוֹ וּלְגַבֵּי דִּילֵיהּ הוּא תַּכְלִית הַקְּדוּשָׁה
according to his level it is not accounted self-pleasure and for him is ultimate holiness;
אֲבָל לְגַבֵּי מַדְרֵיגוֹת הַגְּדוֹלוֹת מִמֶּנּוּ זֶה נֶחְשָׁב כְּחוֹל, כִּי הַרְבֵּה מַדְרֵיגוֹת קְדוּשָׁה יֵשׁ לְאֵין קֵץ
yet relative unto higher rungs this is accounted as secular, for rungs of holiness are infinite.
וַאֲפִילּוּ מִי שֶׁהוּא בְּמַדְרֵיגַת קֹדֶשׁ קָדָשִׁים בְּאוֹתוֹ דּוֹר... אֶפְשָׁר עַדַיִין שֶׁיִּהְיֶה כְּחוּלֵי חוּלִין לְגַבֵּי דּוֹר אַחֵר
And even one who is Holy of Holies in his generation can be as secular matter relative to an earlier era;

וְכִדְאִיתָא בַּיְרוּשַׁלְמִי סוֹף פֶּרֶק ו׳ דְּגִיטִּין (הֲלָכָה ז׳): ״רַבִּי כַּד הֲוָה בָּעֵי מַקְשְׁיָא אַדְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי, אָמַר: אֲנַן עֲלִיבַיָּא מַקְשְׁיָא עַל דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי?! שֶׁכְּשֵׁם שֶׁבֵּין קֹדֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁים לְחוּלֵי חוּלִין, כָּךְ בֵּין דּוֹרֵינוּ לְדוֹרוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹסֵי!״

as stated in Yerushalmi Gittin (6:7): when Rebbe sought to question Rabbi Yose, he exclaimed: "Shall we, the humiliated, question Rabbi Yose?! As the distance between the Holy of Holies and secular matter, so is the distance between our generation and Rabbi Yose's!"
מִכָּל מָקוֹם גּוּף הַדָּבָר אֱמֶת דְּיֵשׁ דּוֹרוֹת שֶׁהוּא כֵן
Nevertheless the principle itself is true: that generations differ fundamentally;
וְדוֹר הַמִּדְבָּר הַגָּדוֹל מִכָּל הַדּוֹרוֹת הִיא כְּקֹדֶשׁ קָדָשִׁים נֶגֶד כָּל הַדּוֹרוֹת כּוּלָּם
and the wilderness generation is the Holy of Holies relative unto all generations;
וְאַף הוּא עַדַיִין אֵינוֹ כְּלוּם נֶגֶד דּוֹרוֹ שֶׁל מָשִׁיחַ
yet even that generation is as nothing compared to the generation of Mashiach;
שֶׁאָז יְבוֹרַר הַקְּדוּשָׁה דְּכָל נֶפֶשׁ פְּרָטִי מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל, דְּאָז יִהְיֶה תַּכְלִית תֹּקֶף הַקְּדוּשָׁה שֶׁאֶפְשָׁר לְמִין הָאֱנוֹשִׁי שֶׁיַּשִּׂיג
when the sanctity of every individual Jewish soul will be revealed in the supreme perfection possible for humanity;
שֶׁמִּשָּׁם יֵלְכוּ לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא, וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהַשִּׂיג מַדְרֵיגָה יוֹתֵר
whence they will enter the World to Come, it being impossible to attain a higher rung;

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּפֶרֶק שׁוֹאֵל (שַׁבָּת קנ״א עַמּוּד ב׳) עַל פָּסוּק: ״[עַד אֲשֶׁר לֹא יָבֹאוּ יְמֵי הָרָעָה, וְהִגִּיעוּ שָׁנִים אֲשֶׁר תֹּאמַר:] אֵין לִי בָהֶם חֵפֶץ״ (קֹהֶלֶת י״ב:א׳) — אֵלּוּ יְמוֹת הַמָּשִׁיחַ שֶׁאֵין בָּהֶם וְכוּלֵיהּ
as expounded in Shabbat (151b) on "years concerning which you shall say: I have no pleasure in them"—these are the days of Mashiach;
וִיהִי רָצוֹן שֶׁנִּזְכֶּה וְנִחְיֶה וְנִרְאֶה זֶה בִּמְהֵרָה בְיָמֵינוּ!
and may it be Hashem's will that we merit to live and behold this speedily in our days!
פֶּרֶק ו׳ — אוֹת א׳ — הַתּוֹרָה כְּשַׁעַר לַה׳, מַלְכוּת פֶּה — תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, וְאִיסּוּר מְסִירַת דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה לְגוֹי
Chapter 6: Section 1: The Torah as the Portal to God, Malkhut as Oral Torah, and the Prohibition of Transmitting Torah to Gentiles

6.h: The theme: Torah as the entrance to the courtyard of awe, the Oral Torah as the mouth of Kingship (Malkhut), and the prohibition of transmitting the methods of Talmudic pilpul unto gentiles. In Avodah Zarah (20b), holiness is the ladder’s apex, while Torah is its very foundation—the portal unto the courtyard of awe (Yoma 72b). A child begins speech with Torah: "when a child knows how to speak, his father teaches him Torah" (Sukkah 42a), entering the gate of Hashem through the mouth. In the stature of ten sefirot, the ascent begins from below: Malkhut—Peh, which is the Oral Torah (Torah she-b'al Peh), the unique soul-root of Israel: "He has not dealt so with any nation" (Tehillim 147:20). From this Hagigah (13a) derives: "we do not transmit words of Torah unto a gentile". The Sages precisely stated ein mosrin ("we do not transmit") rather than ein melamdin ("we do not teach"), matching Avos (1:1): "and Moshe transmitted it unto Joshua". When Moshe brought the Torah down to earth, it was handed over to the Sages of Israel—"it is not in heaven" (Bava Metzia 59b), where even a Heavenly Voice is not heeded. The Oral Torah interprets the Written Torah, without which no mitzvah can be understood; whatever a seasoned disciple innovates is Oral Torah, distinguishing Israel from the nations (Shemos Rabbah 47:1). Even regarding the Seven Noahide Laws, gentiles possess only what is explicitly written; the oral interpretations are entrusted solely to Jewish Sages (Sanhedrin 56a; Tosafos, Gittin 60b). Transmitting the pilpul and methods of novellae is forbidden to gentiles: "He declares His word unto Jacob" (Tehillim 147:19), all haggadah operating in esoteric wisdom (raza d'chochmata, Zohar, Vayechi 234b). The Oral Torah is attained through the Holy Spirit (Bava Batra 12a; Ramban), descending from the Supernal Wisdom (Chokhmah Ila'ah), while the Written Torah is an external drop of Supernal Wisdom (Bereishis Rabbah 17:5)!

p: וְהִנֵּה כְּפִי נוּסְחָתֵנוּ בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה (כ׳ עַמּוּד ב׳): הַקְּדוּשָׁה הוּא הַמַּדְרֵיגָה הָאַחֲרוֹנָה מֵהַהַתְחָלָה
And behold, according to our text in Avodah Zarah (20b): holiness is the final rung ascending from the beginning;
דְּשָׁם מַתְחִיל בַּתּוֹרָה, שֶׁהוּא ״הַתַּרְעָא לְדָרְתָא״ דְּיִרְאָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּיוֹמָא (ע״ב סוֹף עַמּוּד ב׳), עַיֵּין שָׁם בְּרַשִׁ״י
for the ladder begins with Torah, which is the portal unto the courtyard of awe (Yoma 72b), see Rashi there.
וְהַתְחָלַת הַכְּנִיסָה בְּ״זֶה הַשַּׁעַר לַה׳, צַדִּיקִים יָבֹאוּ בוֹ״ (תְּהִלִּים קי״ח:כ׳) הוּא עַל יְדֵי הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁצָּרִיךְ מִיָּד בְּיַלְדוּת
And the initial entry into "this gate of Hashem, into which the righteous shall enter" (Tehillim 118:20) is through the Torah, beginning in early childhood;
״קָטָן הַיּוֹדֵעַ לְדַבֵּר — אָבִיו לוֹמְדוֹ תּוֹרָה״, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּסֻכָּה (מ״ב עַמּוּד א׳)
"a child who knows how to speak—his father teaches him Torah," as stated in Sukkah (42a);
שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לְהַכְנִיסוֹ מִיָּד בְּהַשַּׁעַר לַה׳ מִיָּד שֶׁנִּפְתַּח פִּיו לְדַבֵּר, שֶׁהוּא הַשַּׁעַר שֶׁל קוֹמַת הָאָדָם
requiring that he be introduced into the gate of Hashem as soon as his mouth opens to speak, the mouth being the gateway of the human stature;
דְּ״כָל עֲמַל אָדָם — לְפִיהוּ״ (קֹהֶלֶת ו:ז), שֶׁהוּא הַתְחָלַת הַקּוֹמָה
for "all the labor of man is for his mouth" (Koheles 6:7), which is the beginning of the bodily stature.
כִּידוּעַ דְּכָל קוֹמָה שְׁלֵימָה יֵשׁ בָּהּ עֶשֶׂר מַדְרֵיגוֹת, וְהַהַתְחָלָה מִתַּתָּא: ״מַלְכוּת — פֶּה, תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה קָרֵינָן לָהּ״ (פָּתַח אֵלִיָּהוּ)
As is known that every complete stature contains ten rungs, beginning from below: "Malkhut is the Mouth, which we designate the Oral Torah" (Patach Eliyahu);
שֶׁזֶּהוּ שׁוֹרֶשׁ כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ: ״לֹא עָשָׂה כֵן לְכָל גּוֹי״ (תְּהִלִּים קמ״ז:כ׳)
which is the soul-root of Knesset Israel: "He has not dealt so with any nation" (Tehillim 147:20);
וּבַחֲגִיגָה (י״ג עַמּוּד א׳) נָפְקָא לֵיהּ מִזֶּה: ״דְּאֵין מוֹסְרִין דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה לְגוֹי״, וְעַיֵּין שָׁם בְּתוֹסָפוֹת שֶׁנִּדְחֲקוּ בָּזֶה
and in Chagigah (13a) the Talmud derives from this: "we do not transmit words of Torah unto a gentile," see Tosafos there.
וּלְדַעְתִּי פָּשׁוּט, דְּדָיֵיק ״מוֹסְרִין״ וְלֹא ״מְלַמְּדִין״
And in my humble opinion the matter is simple, the Baraita precisely stating "we do not transmit" (mosrin) and not "we do not teach" (melamdin);
וְרָצָה לוֹמַר ״מוֹסְרִין״ עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּרֵישׁ אָבוֹת (פֶּרֶק א׳ מִשְׁנָה א׳): ״וּמְסָרָהּ לִיהוֹשֻׁעַ״
meaning "transmitting" after the manner stated in Avos (1:1): "and Moshe transmitted it unto Joshua";
כִּי מִשֶּׁבָּא מֹשֶׁה וְהוֹרִידָהּ לָאָרֶץ, הֲרֵי הִיא מְסוּרָה לְחַכְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, וְ״לֹא בַשָּׁמַיִם הִוא״ (דְּבָרִים ל:יב)
for once Moshe brought the Torah down to earth, it was formally handed over unto the Sages of Israel: "it is not in heaven" (Devarim 30:12);
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּבָבָא מְצִיעָא (נ״ט עַמּוּד ב׳): דְּלֹא הִשְׁגִּיחוּ בְּבַת קוֹל מֵהַאי טַעְמָא, שֶׁכְּבָר נִמְסְרָה הַתּוֹרָה לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
as stated in Bava Metzia (59b): they did not heed the Heavenly Voice because the Torah was already transmitted unto Israel;
כְּדָבָר הַמָּסוּר לְאַחֵר שֶׁהִיא בְּיָדוֹ שֶׁל נִמְסָר לַעֲשׂוֹת כִּרְצוֹנוֹ
like an object handed over to another, resting in the recipient's hand to govern according to his authority.
וְזֶהוּ הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה הַמְפָרֶשֶׁת לַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב
And this is the Oral Torah that elucidates the Written Torah;
דִּבְלֹא הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה אִי אֶפְשָׁר לֵידַע שׁוּם מִצְוָה עַל בֻּרְיָהּ כְּלָל
for without the Oral Torah it is impossible to understand any commandment properly;
וְהִיא נִמְסְרָה לְחַכְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, וְכָל מַה שֶּׁתַּלְמִיד וָתִיק עָתִיד לְחַדֵּשׁ — זֶהוּ תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
and it was entrusted unto the Sages of Israel, so that whatever a seasoned disciple is destined to innovate is Oral Torah;
וְהִיא הַמַּבְדֶּלֶת בֵּין יִשְׂרָאֵל לָאוּמּוֹת, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּשְׁמוֹת רַבָּה רֵישׁ פָּרָשָׁה מ״ז (סִימָן א׳), עַיֵּין שָׁם.
and it is the Oral Law that separates Israel from the nations (Shemos Rabbah 47:1), see there.
וְנִזְכָּר בְּתוֹסָפוֹת גִּיטִּין (ס׳ עַמּוּד ב׳ דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל: ״עַל פִּי״): דְּ״לֹא עָשָׂה כֵן לְכָל גּוֹי״ — גַּם בְּשֶׁבַע מִצְוֹת דִּידְהוּ אֵין לָהֶם אֶלָּא מַה דִּכְתִיבָא וּמַנָּחָא
And it is noted in Tosafos in Gittin (60b): "He has not dealt so with any nation"—even regarding their Seven Noahide Laws they possess only what is explicitly written;
