And such is the divine rule: when a man sanctifies himself a little from below, Heaven sanctifies him abundantly from Above (Yoma 39a);
וְזָכָה לִקְדֻשַּׁת הַבְּרִית שֶׁהִיא עִיקַּר הַהַבְדָּלָה שֶׁבַּגּוּף בֵּין יִשְׂרָאֵל לָעַמִּים
and he merited the holiness of the covenant, the bodily distinction between Israel and the nations;
דְּמִזֶּה נִמְשָׁךְ לָהֶם נַחֲלַת הָאָרֶץ, דְּצַדִּיקִים שׁוֹמְרֵי הַבְּרִית, כִּידוּעַ בַּזֹּוהַר, הֵם יִרְשׁוּ אָרֶץ
whence issues the inheritance of the Land: the righteous guardians of the covenant inherit the earth;
וְאָז זָכָה לְלֵידַת יִצְחָק שֶׁהוּא עַמּוּד הָעֲבוֹדָה בְּיִרְאָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב, שֶׁשָּׁם מִשְׁכַּן הָרוּחַ דִּקְדוּשָׁה הַנִּמְשָׁךְ אַחַר קְדֻשַּׁת הַנֶּפֶשׁ
and then he merited the birth of Isaac, the pillar of divine service in the fear of the heart, the seat of the holy Ruach;
דְּ״זָכָה יַתִּיר — יָהֲבִין לֵיהּ רוּחָא״ (זֹוהַר חֵלֶק א׳ ס״ב עַמּוּד א׳).
for "if he merits more, they bestow upon him a Ruach" (Zohar I, 62a).

וּמִמֶּנּוּ נִקְבַּע בְּזַרְעוֹ הַסִּימָן דְּ״בַּיְישָׁנִים״ (יְבָמוֹת ע״ט עַמּוּד א׳), דְּיָלְפִינַן הָתָם מִקְּרָא דְּ״וּבַעֲבוּר תִּהְיֶה יִרְאָתוֹ עַל פְּנֵיכֶם [לְבִלְתִּי תֶחֱטָאוּ]״ (שְׁמוֹת כ:יז)
And from Isaac was stamped within his seed the trait of "bashfulness" (Yevamos 79a), derived from: "that His fear may be before your faces, that you sin not" (Shemos 20:17);
וְהַיְינוּ הַבּוֹשֶׁת מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁמֵּבִיא הַיִּרְאָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּ״מוֹרֶה נְבוּכִים״ (חֵלֶק ג׳ פֶּרֶק נ״ב) וְהוּבָא בְּהַגָּהַת רַמָ״א רֵישׁ אוֹרַח חַיִּים (סִימָן א׳ סְעִיף א׳)
this being the shame before Hashem that brings awe (Moreh Nevuchim III, ch. 52; Rema, Orach Chaim 1:1);
וְהוּא בְּהַגְדָּרַת עֶרְוָה וְשֶׁלֹּא לְהִסְתַּכֵּל בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁאֵין רָאוּי לְהִסְתַּכֵּל
which manifests in fencing against immorality, withholding the gaze from unseemly places;
דְּעַל יְדֵי זֶה ״לֹא בִּמְהֵרָה הוּא חוֹטֵא״, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּנְדָרִים (כ׳ סוֹף עַמּוּד א׳)
through which "he will not readily sin" (Nedarim 20a);
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁמַּכִּיר דְּ״שֶׁקֶר הַחֵן וְהֶבֶל הַיֹּפִי, [אִשָּׁה יִרְאַת ה׳ הִיא תִתְהַלָּל]״ (מִשְׁלֵי ל״א:ל׳):
recognizing that "favor is deceitful, and beauty is vain, but a woman that fears Hashem, she shall be praised" (Mishlei 31:30)!

אוֹת י״א — תִּשְׁעָה קַבִּין יוֹפִי דִּירוּשָׁלַיִם, יוֹסֵף הַצַּדִּיק, וּשְׁפִירֵי יְרוּשָׁלַיִם בְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן — Section 11: Nine Measures of Beauty in Jerusalem, Joseph the Tzaddik, and Rabbi Yochanan's Radiance

The theme: Physical beauty rooted in the fear of Heaven, Joseph the Tzaddik as the archetype of beauty, and Rabbi Yochanan immune from the evil eye. In Kiddushin (49b), the Sages state: "Ten measures of beauty descended to the world; nine were taken by Jerusalem, and one by the rest of the world". Essential bodily beauty exists exclusively where there is consummate awe and a fence against immorality (Nedarim 20b: "your children are extraordinarily handsome"). Joseph the Tzaddik—who guarded himself against Potiphar's wife and declared: "for I fear God" (Bereishis 42:18)—is the sole man in Scripture described as "of beautiful form, and fair to look upon" (yefeh to'ar vi-yfeh mareh, Bereishis 39:6). While beauty is primarily feminine ("your beauty belongs to women", Bava Metzia 84a), when a man sanctifies himself in awe and chastity, that feminine supernal splendor shines upon him. Rabbi Yochanan was the surviving remnant of the handsome men of Jerusalem (shpeirei Yerushalayim, Bava Metzia 84a), descending from Joseph (Berachos 20a). The Sages questioned him regarding the evil eye (ayin ha-ra), but not regarding the yetzer hara as they questioned Rav Giddel, knowing that through Joseph's virtue he was immune from carnal temptation. Rabbi Yochanan taught that the evil eye dominates only one whose eyes are flawed by looking at unseemly places; one whose eyes are completely purified cannot be harmed by an evil eye. Beauty is perceived through the eyes ("pleasant to the sight", Bereishis 2:9); a blind man cannot perceive beauty. In Ta'anit (24a): "a bride whose eyes are beautiful requires no examination of her body," for beautiful eyes testify to the purity of the entire body!
וְי׳ (עֲשָׂרָה) קַבִּין יוֹפִי יָרְדוּ לָעוֹלָם, ט׳ (תִּשְׁעָה) נָטְלָה יְרוּשָׁלַיִם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּקִדּוּשִׁין (מ״ט עַמּוּד ב׳)
And "ten measures of beauty descended to the world; nine were taken by Jerusalem, and one by the rest of the world," as stated in Kiddushin (49b);
הַיְינוּ דְּעִיקַּר הַיּוֹפִי דְּגוּף אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא בִּמְקוֹם שְׁלֵימוּת הַיִּרְאָה שֶׁהוּא גֶּדֶר עֶרְוָה
meaning: essential bodily beauty exists exclusively where there is consummate awe, which is the fence against immorality;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּנְדָרִים שָׁם (כ׳ סוֹף עַמּוּד ב׳): ״מִכָּל מָקוֹם בָּנַיִךְ יְפֵיפִיִּין בְּיוֹתֵר וְכוּלֵיהּ״, עַיֵּין שָׁם.
as stated in Nedarim (20b): "nevertheless, your children are extraordinarily handsome, etc.," see there.
וְיוֹסֵף הַצַּדִּיק הַגָּדוּר מֵעֶרְוָה, וּכְתִיב בֵּיהּ: ״אֶת הָאֱלֹהִים אֲנִי יָרֵא״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית מ״ב:י״ח)
And Joseph the Tzaddik who fenced himself against immorality, concerning whom it is written: "for I fear God" (Bereishis 42:18);
הוּא אָדָם הַיְחִידִי שֶׁנִּכְתַּב עָלָיו בַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁהָיָה ״יְפֵה תֹאַר וִיפֵה מַרְאֶה״ (שָׁם ל״ט:ו׳)
is the unique man in the Torah concerning whom it is written that he was "of beautiful form, and fair to look upon" (ibid. 39:6);
דְּעִיקַּר הַיּוֹפִי שַׁיָּיךְ בְּנָשִׁים, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּפֶרֶק הַפּוֹעֲלִים (בָּבָא מְצִיעָא פ״ד עַמּוּד א׳): ״שׁוּפְרָךְ — לְנָשֵׁי״
for beauty belongs preeminently to women: "your beauty belongs to women" (Bava Metzia 84a);
הַיְינוּ ״אִשָּׁה יִרְאַת ה׳״, דִּבְלָאו הָכִי הוּא שֶׁקֶר וָהֶבֶל
referring to "a woman that fears Hashem," without which beauty is deceit and vanity;
וּמִצַּד הַגְדָּרַת הָעֶרְוָה וְיִרְאַת ה׳ נִמְשָׁךְ גַּם לַאֲנָשִׁים שׁוּפְרָא דְּנָשֵׁי
and through chastity and the fear of Hashem, this supernal feminine beauty radiates upon men as well;
דְּעִיקַּר יִרְאַת ה׳ הִיא מִסִּטְרָא דְּנוּקְבָא כַּנּוֹדָע.
for the fear of Hashem is rooted in the feminine dimension (Nukva) as is known.
וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן דְּאִשְׁתַּיֵּיר מִשַּׁפִּירֵי יְרוּשָׁלַיִם כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב שָׁם בְּבָבָא מְצִיעָא (פ״ד עַמּוּד א׳), הָיָה מִזַּרְעָא דְּיוֹסֵף, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרָכוֹת (כ׳ עַמּוּד א׳)
And Rabbi Yochanan who was the remnant of the handsome men of Jerusalem (Bava Metzia 84a), descended from the seed of Joseph (Berachos 20a);
וְלֹא שְׁאָלוּהוּ שָׁם: ״לָא מִסְתָּפֵי מָר מִיֵּצֶר הָרָע?״ כִּלְרַב גִּידֵּל שָׁם
and they did not challenge him: "Does the Master not fear the yetzer hara?" as they challenged Rav Giddel;
(וְלוֹ לֹא שָׁאֲלוּ מֵעַיִן הָרָע, דְּלֹא הָיָה מִשַּׁפִּירֵי שֶׁיִּתְּנוּ עַיִן הָרָע בְּהִסְתַּכְּלוּת בְּיוֹפְיוֹ)
(while Rav Giddel was not challenged regarding the evil eye, not being among the handsome men of Jerusalem);
כִּי יָדְעוּ דְּהוּא כְּבָר מוּגְדָּר בָּזֶה בְּכֹחַ יוֹסֵף שֶׁגָּדַר עַצְמוֹ מִן הָעֶרְוָה וְזָכָה לְכָל זַרְעוֹ אַחֲרָיו
for they knew Rabbi Yochanan was fenced through the strength of Joseph who fenced himself against immorality and merited this for all his descendants.
אֲבָל חָשׁוּ לְעַיִן הָרָע, וְהוּא הוֹדִיעָם דְּזֶה נִמְשָׁךְ מִזֶּה
But they feared for him regarding the evil eye, and he informed them that the two are interdependent;
כִּי אֵין כֹּחַ עַיִן הָרָע שׁוֹלֵט אֶלָּא בְּמִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ פְּגָם בְּעֵינָיו לְהִסְתַּכֵּל בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁאֵינוֹ רָאוּי
for the evil eye has power to dominate only one who possesses an imperfection in his eyes by gazing upon unseemly places;
אֲבָל מִי שֶׁכְּבָר תִּיקֵּן עֵינָיו שֶׁאֵין בָּהֶם שׁוּם צַד רָע, אִי אֶפְשָׁר לָעַיִן לִשְׁלוֹט בּוֹ לְרָעָה
but one who has rectified his eyes so that no evil resides in them, it is impossible for an evil eye to dominate him;
שֶׁכֵּן הוּא הַמִּדָּה: דְּאִם זָכָה לְתַקֵּן אֵיזֶה כֹּחַ, אִי אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁיָּבוֹא לוֹ עוֹד קִלְקוּל וְהֶיזֵּק מִצַּד אוֹתוֹ הַכֹּחַ מִסִּטְרָא דְּרָע
for such is the rule: if one has rectified a specific faculty, no harm can approach him through that faculty from the side of evil.
וּמִזֶּה נִמְשָׁךְ גַּם כֵּן הַיּוֹפִי שֶׁהוּא רַק לְמַרְאֵה עֵינַיִם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ: ״נֶחְמָד לְמַרְאֶה״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית ב:ט), וְ״תַאֲוָה הִוא לָעֵינַיִם״ (שָׁם ג:ו)
And from this flows physical beauty which is perceived strictly through the eyes: "pleasant to the sight" (Bereishis 2:9) and "a delight to the eyes" (ibid. 3:6);
וְהַסּוּמָא אֵין מַרְגִּישׁ בְּיוֹפִי הַמַּרְאִית כִּי הַרְגָּשָׁה זוֹ הוּא רַק בְּכֹחַ הָעַיִן
a blind man feeling no sensation of beauty, for this perception exists only through the power of sight;
וְעַל כֵּן עִיקַּר הַיּוֹפִי גַּם כֵּן הוּא רַק בַּעֲיָנַיִם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּתַעֲנִית (כ״ד עַמּוּד א׳): ״כַּלָּה שֶׁעֵינֶיהָ יָפוֹת — אֵין כָּל גּוּפָהּ צָרִיךְ בְּדִיקָה״
wherefore the essence of beauty resides within the eyes: "a bride whose eyes are beautiful requires no examination of her body" (Ta'anit 24a);
כִּי הַיּוֹפִי דְּעֵינַיִם מֵעִיד גַּם עַל הַיּוֹפִי דְּגוּף
beautiful eyes testifying to the beauty of the entire body;
וְכֵן שֶׁ״עֵינֶיהָ טְרוּטוֹת וְכוּלֵיהּ״, דְּכִיעוּר הָעֵינַיִם מֵעִיד עַל כִּיעוּר הַגּוּף
and bleary eyes testifying to bodily ugliness;
דִּכְמוֹ שֶׁאֵין הַיּוֹפִי מוּרְגָּשׁ אֶלָּא בָּעַיִן וְנִיתַּן בּוֹ הַרְגָּשַׁת הַיּוֹפִי, כָּךְ נִיתַּן בּוֹ גַּם כֵּן עֶצֶם הַיּוֹפִי כֵּיוָן שֶׁאֵבֶר זֶה הִיא הַכְּלִי לְדָבָר זֶה:
for just as the perception of beauty was placed in the eye, so the essence of beauty was placed in the eye, the eye being the vessel for this reality!

6.h: אוֹת י״ב — עֵינוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם, יָפְיָהּ שֶׁל וַשְׁתִּי מוּל יוֹסֵף, וְיוֹפְיוֹ שֶׁל אַבְשָׁלוֹם הַנָּזִיר — Section 12: Jerusalem as the Eye of the World, Vashti's False Beauty, and the Purity of Absalom's Locks

The theme: The false beauty of the nations versus eternal beauty in Jerusalem, and Absalom as a Nazirite devoid of bodily blemish. In the falsehood of this world, beauty is corrupted into an instrument of lust—the eye seeing and heart coveting. But when God made man upright (Koheles 7:29), beauty was intended to manifest solely where there is a fence against immorality and the averting of eyes from evil. The nine measures of beauty descended to Jerusalem, the "eye of the world" (eino shel olam, Bava Batra 4a: Herod blinding the Sages who are the eye of the world). The tenth measure expanded across the world: in Israel toward holy beauty, and among the nations toward the harlot's fleeting beauty (hevel ha-yofi). Joseph's beauty is eternal because his chastity was eternal. Vashti’s beauty was not genuine: Ahasuerus sought "to show the peoples and the princes her beauty" (Esther 1:11) to outward eyes submerged in lust. Authentic beauty exists only in the chaste: Absalom was praised: "in all Israel there was none to be so much praised as Absalom for his beauty" (II Shmuel 14:25). Absalom was a Nazirite, abstaining from wine and lust (wherefore he was zealous against Amnon's crime); "from the sole of his foot even to the crown of his head there was no blemish in him" (ibid.)—possessing no spiritual or bodily defect, deceiving all Israel into believing he was a consummate tzaddik ("and Absalom stole the hearts of the men of Israel", ibid. 15:6)!

p: וּמִצַּד הַשֶּׁקֶר דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁהָרָע גּוֹבֵר, שִׁימּוּשׁ הַיּוֹפִי הוּא בְּתַאֲווֹת רָעוֹת, לִהְיוֹת ״עַיִן רוֹאָה וְלֵב חוֹמֵד״ (רַשִׁ״י שְׁלַח ט״ו:ל״ט)
And from the falsehood of this world where evil prevails, beauty is exploited for wicked lusts, the eye seeing and heart coveting;
וּבְרִיאַת הַיּוֹפִי בָּעוֹלָם לֹא הָיָה עַל זֶה
yet the creation of beauty in the world was not for this purpose;
וּמִצַּד מַה שֶּׁ״עָשָׂה הָאֱלֹהִים אֶת הָאָדָם יָשָׁר״ (קֹהֶלֶת ז:כט), עִיקַּר הַיּוֹפִי הוּא רַק בִּמְקוֹם גֶּדֶר עֶרְוָה וַעֲצִימוּת עַיִן מִתַּאֲווֹת רָעוֹת.
but from the perspective of "God made man upright" (Koheles 7:29), the essence of beauty exists solely where there is a fence against immorality and averting the eyes from evil.
וּמֵאוֹתוֹ הַיּוֹפִי שֶׁבַּבְּרִיאָה יָרַד תִּשְׁעָה קַבִּין
And from that primeval beauty in Creation descended nine measures;

רָצָה לוֹמַר: כָּל הַמְשָׁכַת קוֹמַת הַהִשְׁתַּלְשְׁלוּת עַד הַמִּדָּה הָאַחֲרוֹנָה, שֶׁמִּמֶּנָּה הוּא כֹּחַ הַהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת עַד דְּ״רַגְלֶיהָ יֹרְדוֹת מָוֶת״ (מִשְׁלֵי ה:ה) וּמַגִּיעַ גַּם לַחִיצוֹנִים
meaning: the chain of the sefirotic stature down to the final attribute (Malkhut), whence expansion reaches the outer husks;
אֲבָל בְּאוֹתָן הַטֵּי״ת קַבִּין הֵם מַשְׁפִּיעִים אֶחָד לַחֲבֵירוֹ עַד הַיְסוֹד בָּהּ, שֶׁשָּׁם כֹּחַ הַצִּמְצוּם בַּיְסוֹד דִּקְדוּשָׁה שֶׁלֹּא יִתְפַּשֵּׁט רַק בִּמְקוֹם הָרָאוּי
but within those nine measures the attributes channel into Yesod, where the divine contraction restricts expansion to holy places alone;
וּבְכָל אוֹתָן הַטֵּי״ת מִדּוֹת הוּא רַק הַצִּנּוֹר לְהַגִּיעַ לַהַהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת שֶׁהוּא בַּמִּדָּה הָעֲשִׂירִית
those nine attributes being the conduit to reach the tenth attribute (Malkhut);
וְשָׁם הוּא אֲחִיזַת סִטְרָא דְּעֵין הָרָע, טוֹב וָרָע לְהִתְפַּשֵּׁט לְכָל צַד.
and there resides the potential grip of the evil eye, good and evil expanding in all directions.
וְאוֹתָן הַטֵּי״ת קַבִּין שֶׁהוּא עִיקַּר הַיּוֹפִי שֶׁבְּעֶצֶם — יָרַד לִירוּשָׁלַיִם, שֶׁשָּׁם מִשְׁכַּן ״עֵינוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם״
And those nine measures of essential beauty descended unto Jerusalem, the seat of the "eye of the world";
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּבָבָא בַּתְרָא (ד׳ עַמּוּד א׳): ״הוּא סִמָּא עֵינוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם... יַעֲסוֹק בְּעֵינוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם״
as stated in Bava Batra (4a): Herod blinded the Sages who are the eye of the world, let him rebuild the Temple which is the eye of the world;
וְעַל כֵּן שָׁם הוּא עִיקַּר הַיּוֹפִי שֶׁל כָּל הָעוֹלָם
wherefore in Jerusalem resides the true beauty of the whole world;
רַק אָז בִּזְמַן שֶׁהָיָה שָׁם עֵינוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם הַקְּדוּשָׁה, הָיָה שָׁם עִיקַּר הַיּוֹפִי דִּקְדוּשָׁה, שֶׁהוּא הַיּוֹפִי שֶׁל אֱמֶת שֶׁאֵינוֹ הֶבֶל וָשֶׁקֶר
while the Holy Temple stood, the holy beauty of Jerusalem was authentic beauty, neither vain nor false;
וּמִשָּׁם הוּא הִתְפַּשֵּׁט הַקַּב וּמִדָּה אַחֲרוֹנָה יוֹפִי שֶׁנִּתְפַּשֵּׁט בְּכָל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ: בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל בְּסִטְרָא דְּטוֹב, וּבְאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם מִסִּטְרָא דְּרָע
and from there the tenth single measure spread across the earth: unto Israel on the side of good, and unto the nations on the side of the unholy harlot;
וְאֶצְלָם: ״הֶבֶל הַיֹּפִי״ (מִשְׁלֵי ל״א:ל׳), שֶׁהוּא עַצְמוּת הַיּוֹפִי, שֶׁאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ יוֹפִי — הוּא הֶבֶל, כֵּיוָן שֶׁאֵינוֹ יוֹפִי אֲמִיתִּי הַקַּיָּים לָעַד
and among them it is "beauty is vain" (Mishlei 31:30), for though it appears beautiful it is fleeting vanity, not enduring forever;
כְּיוֹפִי דְּיוֹסֵף שֶׁנִּכְתַּב עָלָיו בַּתּוֹרָה הַקַּיֶּימֶת לָעַד שֶׁהָיָה ״יְפֵה תֹאַר״, כִּי הָיָה עַצְמִיּוּתוֹ וְשָׁרְשׁוֹ כֵּן
unlike the beauty of Joseph inscribed in the eternal Torah that he was of beautiful form, his essence and root being holy.
כִּי הַגְדָּרַת הָעֶרְוָה וַעֲצִימוּת הָעַיִן מֵרְאוֹת בְּרָע הוּא יוֹפִי הַגּוּף בְּעֶצֶם שֶׁנִּשְׁאָר קַיָּים לְעוֹלְמֵי עַד, וְכָל יוֹפִי שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בַּכָּתוּב הוּא כֵן
For chastity and shutting the eyes from gazing upon evil is the essential bodily beauty that endures forever, and all beauty praised in Scripture is thus;
וְכֵן הַנֶּאֱמָר בְּנָשִׁים אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא בְּ״אִשָּׁה יִרְאַת ה׳״ הַמּוּגְדָּרִים בַּעֲרָיוֹת
and that which is praised in women applies exclusively unto "a woman that fears Hashem" who is fenced against immorality;
וּבְוַשְׁתִּי לֹא נֶאֱמַר שֶׁהָיְתָה בֶּאֱמֶת, רַק: ״לְהַרְאוֹת הָעַמִּים וְהַשָּׂרִים אֶת יָפְיָהּ״ (אֶסְתֵּר א:יא)
and regarding Vashti it was not stated that she possessed true beauty, but: "to show the peoples and the princes her beauty" (Esther 1:11);
שֶׁלְּמַרְאֵה עֵינֵיהֶם הַשְּׁקוּעִים בְּתַאֲווֹת רָעוֹת וּפְרוּצִים בַּעֲרָיוֹת הָיָה נִרְאֶה יוֹפִי
appearing beautiful to their eyes which were submerged in carnal lusts and promiscuity;
אֲבָל בְּכָל מָקוֹם שֶׁיְּסַפֵּר הַכָּתוּב יוֹפִי בְּעֶצֶם וּבֶאֱמֶת, אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא בְּמִי שֶׁמּוּגְדָּר מֵעֶרְוָה.
but wherever Scripture chronicles essential, authentic beauty, it belongs solely to one fenced against immorality.
וּכְאַבְשָׁלוֹם שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר עָלָיו: ״[וּכְאַבְשָׁלוֹם] לֹא הָיָה אִישׁ יָפֶה בְּכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל לְהַלֵּל מְאֹד״ (שְׁמוּאֵל ב י״ד:כ״ה)
And like Absalom concerning whom it is said: "Now in all Israel there was none to be so much praised as Absalom for his beauty" (II Shmuel 14:25);
הָיָה נָזִיר הַמּוּפְרָשׁ מִתַּאֲווֹת, וְעַל כֵּן קִנֵּא עַל זְנוּת אַמְנוֹן
being a Nazirite abstaining from bodily lusts, wherefore he was zealous against Amnon's incestuous act;
וְכֵן מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב עָלָיו: ״מִכַּף רַגְלוֹ וְעַד קָדְקֳדוֹ לֹא הָיָה בוֹ מוּם״ (שָׁם), וַדַּאי הַכַּוָּונָה מַה שֶּׁהוּא מוּם רָע עַל הָאֱמֶת אֵצֶל הַתּוֹרָה
and what is written: "from the sole of his foot even to the crown of his head there was no blemish in him" (ibid.), refers to what the Torah accounts as a blemish;
דְּהַיְינוּ חִסָּרוֹן וְקִלְקוּל בִּקְדֻשַּׁת שׁוּם אֵבֶר, כִּי הָיָה בְּתַכְלִית הַשְּׁלֵימוּת
meaning a defect in the sanctity of any organ, he being in complete physical perfection;
וְעַל כֵּן טָעוּ כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל אַחֲרָיו, וְנֶאֱמַר: ״וַיְגַנֵּב אַבְשָׁלוֹם אֶת לֵב אַנְשֵׁי יִשְׂרָאֵל״ (שָׁם ט״ו:ו׳), הַיְינוּ בַּמַּה שֶּׁהֶאֱמִינוּ בוֹ שֶׁהוּא צַדִּיק גָּמוּר:
wherefore all Israel erred after him: "So Absalom stole the hearts of the men of Israel" (ibid. 15:6), believing him to be an absolute tzaddik!

6.h: אוֹת י״ג — שָׁרְשׁוֹ שֶׁל אַבְשָׁלוֹם מִיְּפַת תֹּאַר, הַמּוּם הַנֶּעְלָם בַּכֶּתֶר, וּשְׂעָרוֹ כְּמִדַּת הַדִּין — Section 13: Absalom's Concealed Blemish in the Crown, and Hair Manifesting the Attribute of Judgment

The theme: Absalom born of the beautiful captive woman (yefat to'ar), the hidden blemish in his soul-root, and hair representing Din. In truth, Absalom harbored a blemish in his root: he was the son of a captive woman (yefat to'ar, Sanhedrin 107a), becoming a rebellious son (ben sorer u-moreh, Devarim 21:18). From his foot to his crown—from Malkhut to Chokhmah—he was immaculate; his flaw lay concealed above his crown, in the root of Keter. He sought to mask this root flaw and seize the royal crown (Keter Malkhut), demonstrating that his crown was entirely pure. His power of concealment was bound in his hair—which hovers above the head like a crown. A Nazirite bears "the crown of his God upon his head" (nezer Elohav al rosho, Bamidbar 6:7) by abstaining from wine, which fences against immorality (Sotah 2a, 7a). Hair alludes to the attribute of Judgment (Middat HaDin / the Divine Name Elohim); in holiness, it represents conquering the yetzer like Eliyahu "a hairy man" (ish ba'al se'ar, II Melachim 1:8) rooted in the Fear of Isaac (Pachad Yitzchak), whose dross was Esav the hairy man (ish sa'ir)!

p: וּבֶאֱמֶת הָיָה בוֹ חִסָּרוֹן בַּשּׁוֹרֶשׁ, שֶׁהָיָה בֶּן יְפַת תֹּאַר, וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה נַעֲשָׂה ״בֵּן סוֹרֵר וּמוֹרֶה״ (סַנְהֶדְרִין ק״ז עַמּוּד א׳)
And in truth there was an imperfection in Absalom's root: he was the son of a beautiful captive woman (yefat to'ar), through which he became a rebellious son (Sanhedrin 107a);
אֶלָּא שֶׁהָיָה רַק בַּשּׁוֹרֶשׁ, וְהֶעֱלִימוֹ מִכָּל מִדּוֹת הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת שֶׁמִּכַּף רַגְלוֹ עַד קָדְקֳדוֹ
except that it existed strictly in his root, concealed from all active attributes from the sole of his foot to the crown of his head;
שֶׁהוּא מִמִּדָּה הָאַחֲרוֹנָה עַד הַחָכְמָה שֶׁבַּמּוֹחַ, שֶׁשָּׁם תְּחִלַּת הַהִתְגַּלּוּת דְּ״יֵשׁ מֵאַיִן״
which is from Malkhut to the Chokhmah of the brain, the inception of manifestation from Nothingness;
הָיָה כּוּלּוֹ יָפֶה בְּלֹא מוּם, רַק הַמּוּם שֶׁלּוֹ הָיָה בַּשּׁוֹרֶשׁ
being entirely beautiful without blemish, his blemish residing solely in his transcendent root.
וְעַל כֵּן הָיָה מְהוּלָּל בְּיוֹפְיוֹ בְּכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל, כִּי זֶה הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ נֶעְלָם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
Wherefore he was praised for his beauty in all Israel, for that root is veiled in this world;
וְחָשַׁב לְהַעֲלִימוֹ וּלְהַשִּׂיג גַּם כֶּתֶר מַלְכוּת, שֶׁבָּזֶה יְבָרֵר גַּם הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ וְהַכֶּתֶר שֶׁכּוּלּוֹ טוֹב וְיָפֶה.
and Absalom sought to mask it and seize the crown of kingship, intending to demonstrate that his root and crown were wholly good and beautiful.
וְכֹחַ הַהַעֲלָמָה שֶׁלּוֹ הָיָה בִּשְׂעָרוֹ, שֶׁהֵם לְמַעְלָה מֵהַקָּדְקוֹד בִּדְמוּת כֶּתֶר עַל הָרֹאשׁ
And his power of concealment resided in his hair, which hovers above the crown of the head in the likeness of a crown;
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּנָזִיר: ״נֵזֶר אֱלֹהָיו עַל רֹאשׁוֹ״ (בַּמִּדְבָּר ו:ז), עַל יְדֵי שֶׁהִזִּיר עַצְמוֹ מִן הַיַּיִן שֶׁהוּא לְגֶדֶר עֶרְוָה
as stated regarding the Nazirite: "the crown of his God is upon his head" (Bamidbar 6:7) through abstaining from wine as a fence against immorality;
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּרֵישׁ סוֹטָה (ב׳ עַמּוּד א׳): ״הָרוֹאֶה סוֹטָה בְּקִלְקוּלָהּ — יַזִּיר עַצְמוֹ מִן הַיַּיִן״
as stated at the beginning of Sotah (2a): "whoever sees a sotah in her degradation should take a vow of Naziriteship from wine";
וּמִשּׁוּם דְּ״הַרְבֵּה יַיִן עוֹשֶׂה״, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ שָׁם (ז׳ עַמּוּד א׳)
because "wine accomplishes much," as stated there (7a);
וְעַל כֵּן נִקְרָא ״קָדוֹשׁ״ (בַּמִּדְבָּר ו:ה), וְזוֹכֶה לְהַשָּׂגַת ״נֵזֶר אֱלֹהָיו״ — יִחוּד שֵׁם שָׁמַיִם עָלָיו
wherefore the Nazirite is called holy (Bamidbar 6:5), meriting the crown of his God—the unification of the Divine Name upon him;
בְּהַשָּׂגַת שָׁרְשׁוֹ הַנֶּעְלָם שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה מֵהַשָּׂגַת אָדָם שֶׁהוּא חֵלֶק אֱלֹהַּ מִמַּעַל
perceiving his concealed root transcending human grasp, which is a portion of God on High;
וְהוּא שֵׁם ״אֱלֹהִים״ הַמּוֹרֶה דִּין, כִּי כֵן הַשְּׂעָרוֹת רוֹמְזִין לְמִדַּת הַדִּין כַּנּוֹדָע.
this being the Name Elohim denoting strict Judgment, hair symbolizing the attribute of Din as is known.
וְהוּא בִּקְדוּשָׁה: ״גִּבּוֹר הַכּוֹבֵשׁ אֶת יִצְרוֹ״ (אָבוֹת ד:א)
And in holiness this represents the hero who subdues his inclination (Avos 4:1);
כְּאֵלִיָּהוּ: ״אִישׁ בַּעַל שֵׂעָר״ (מְלָכִים ב א:ח) בְּסִימָנָיו, מִסִּטְרָא דְּ״פַחַד יִצְחָק״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית ל״א:מ״ב)
like Eliyahu who was "a hairy man" (II Melachim 1:8), rooted in the Fear of Isaac (Pachad Yitzchak, Bereishis 31:42);
שֶׁהַפְּסֹולֶת מִמֶּנּוּ: עֵשָׂו ״אִישׁ שָׂעִר״ (שָׁם כ״ז:י״א) הַמָּלֵא כַּעַס וּרְצִיחָה:
whose unholy dross was Esau "a hairy man" (ibid. 27:11), filled with wrath and murder!

6.h: אוֹת י״ד — גַּאֲוַת אַבְשָׁלוֹם בִּשְׂעָרוֹ, שְׁלֹשֶׁת הַלְּבָבוֹת שֶׁגָּנַב, וְתַלְיָתוֹ בִּשְׂעָרוֹ — Section 14: Absalom's Pride in his Locks, The Three Hearts he Stole, and Hanging by his Hair

The theme: Absalom stealing the hearts of his father, the Sanhedrin, and Israel, David's error regarding the Yefat To'ar, and hanging by his hair. Absalom took pride in his hair (Sotah 9b), assuming it was the crown of his God. While the evil of the captive woman is physical lust, Absalom was fenced against bodily appetite; his illicit lust was for the royal crown (Keter Malkhut). He stole three hearts (Sotah 9b): the heart of his father (Wisdom in the brain), the heart of the Sanhedrin (Understanding in the heart), and the heart of Israel (vitality spreading across the limbs). The Gemara asks David: "Why did you marry the captive woman?" David replied: "The Merciful One permitted her!" (Sanhedrin 107a). David reasoned that Scripture designated her "of beautiful form" (yefat to'ar), implying an inward woman of piety, for a righteous warrior engaging in holy war harbors no illicit lust. Yet the Torah spoke solely to counter the yetzer hara (Kiddushin 21b); her conversion was insincere, like the lion-converts of the Cutheans (II Melachim 17:28), bound to give birth to a rebellious son who abandons honoring parents—a virtue maintained even by gentiles like Dama ben Netinah (Kiddushin 31a). David’s heart was slain within him (Avodah Zarah 4b); he did not crave her out of base lust, but to demonstrate repentance and because Hashem decreed evil from his own house. Yet his subtle flaw was testing himself (Sanhedrin 107a) without considering adjoining verses. Although Absalom was physically flawless, in the end his concealed root blemish erupted, and he was hanged by his proud hair (II Shmuel 18:9)!

p: וְאַבְשָׁלוֹם נִתְגָּאָה בִּשְׂעָרוֹ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּסוֹטָה (ט׳ עַמּוּד ב׳)
And Absalom took pride in his hair, as stated in Sotah (9b);
הַיְינוּ שֶׁחָשַׁב שֶׁהוּא ״נֵזֶר אֱלֹהָיו״ שֶׁעַל רֹאשׁוֹ.
meaning he assumed it was the crown of his God resting upon his head.
וְשָׁרְשׁוֹ דְּרָע מִיְּפַת תֹּאַר הוּא בַּתַּאֲוָה, וְהוּא הֵיפֶךְ מִזֶּה: מוּגְדָּר בְּכָל תַּאֲווֹת גּוּפָנִיּוֹת
And the root of evil issuing from the captive woman resides in bodily lust, whereas Absalom was the reverse: fenced against physical desires;
וְכֵן ״נֵזֶר אֱלֹהָיו״ הוּא הֵיפֶךְ הַגַּאֲוָה.
and the "crown of his God" is the antithesis of arrogance.
אֲבָל כָּל תַּאֲוָה שֶׁלּוֹ הָיָה לְכֶתֶר הַמַּלְכוּת
But his entire lust was directed toward the royal crown;

וְזֶה הַתַּאֲוָה זָרָה שֶׁהָיָה בוֹ בְּשָׁרְשׁוֹ הַנֶּעְלָם בְּהֶעְלֵם עָצוּם, וּבִגְנֵיבָה גְּמוּרָה בְּכָל ג׳ חֶלְקֵי: נֶפֶשׁ, רוּחַ, נְשָׁמָה שֶׁהֵם מִתְפַּשְּׁטִים בְּכֹחוֹת הַגּוּף וּבְמִדּוֹתָיו, וְאֶפְשָׁר לַמֵּבִין לְהַכִּירָם.
this being the alien lust concealed within his transcendent root in total deception across Nefesh, Ruach, and Neshamah.
וְזֶהוּ הַג׳ לְבָבוֹת שֶׁשָּׁנִינוּ שָׁם (סוֹטָה ט׳ עַמּוּד ב׳): שֶׁגָּנַב ״לֵב אָבִיו״ — הַיְינוּ מִצַּד הַחָכְמָה שֶׁבַּמּוֹחַ;
And these are the three hearts enumerated in Sotah (9b): he stole "the heart of his father"—stemming from Wisdom in the brain;
״וְלֵב בֵּית דִּין״ — הַיְינוּ מִצַּד הַבִּינָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב;
"and the heart of the court"—stemming from Understanding in the heart;
״וְלֵב כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל״ — הַיְינוּ מִצַּד כֹּחוֹת הַנֶּפֶשׁ הַמִּתְפַּשְּׁטִים בְּכָל אֵבְרֵי הַגּוּף
"and the heart of the men of Israel"—stemming from the vitality spreading through the bodily limbs;
וְהִיא שֶׁהֱבִיאַתְהוּ לִהְיוֹת כְּסוֹרֵר וּמוֹרֶה.
and this rebellion brought him to become a rebellious son.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (ק״ז עַמּוּד א׳): ״מַאי טַעְמָא נְסֵיבַת יְפַת תֹּאַר? אָמַר לֵיהּ: רַחֲמָנָא שַׁרְיָהּ!״
And this is what the Sages asked David in Sanhedrin (107a): "Why did you marry the captive woman?" David replied: "The Merciful One permitted her!";
הַיְינוּ דְּהֵבִין מִמַּה דְּהַתּוֹרָה קְרָאַתָּהּ ״יְפַת תֹּאַר״ בְּתוֹאַר עַצְמִי
meaning: David deduced from Scripture calling her "of beautiful form" as an essential title;
עַל כָּרְחָךְ אֵינוֹ עַל הַיּוֹפִי הַגַּשְׁמִי לְבַד שֶׁהוּא הֶבֶל, רַק שֶׁהִיא ״אִשָּׁה יִרְאַת ה׳״
that perforce this does not refer to physical beauty alone which is vanity, but that she was a woman fearing Hashem;

דְּעַל כֵּן יֵשׁ לָאִישׁ הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִי הַנִּכְנָס לְמִלְחַמְתָּן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל, דְּאֵין מִתְיָירֵא מֵעֲבֵירוֹת שֶׁבְּיָדוֹ, שֶׁאֵין בְּיָדוֹ כָּל רַע וְלֹא יַחְפּוֹץ בִּדְבַר אִיסּוּר — חֵשֶׁק בָּהּ
wherefore a righteous warrior engaging in holy war, who fears no sins in his hand, harbored a holy desire for her;
וְכֵן הַסּוֹף שֶׁמִּתְגַּיֶּירֶת, עַל כֵּן חָשַׁב שֶׁהוּא הֶיתֵּר גָּמוּר.
and seeing that in the end she converts, he assumed it was completely permissible.
וּבֶאֱמֶת ״לֹא דִּבְּרָה תּוֹרָה אֶלָּא כְּנֶגֶד יֵצֶר הָרָע״ (קִדּוּשִׁין כ״א עַמּוּד ב׳)
Yet in truth "the Torah spoke solely to counter the yetzer hara" (Kiddushin 21b);
וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּיָצְתָה מִכְּלַל ״אֵשֶׁת זְנוּנִים״ כֵּיוָן דְּמִתְגַּיֶּירֶת וְנַעֲשֵׂית ״אִשָּׁה יִרְאַת ה׳״
and even though she departs from being a harlot once she converts and becomes a God-fearing woman;
מִכָּל מָקוֹם כֵּיוָן דְּאֵינוֹ גֵּירוּת גָּמוּר מֵרְצוֹנָהּ אֶלָּא לְשֵׁם אִישׁ אוֹ מֵאוֹנֶס
nevertheless, since her conversion is not entirely voluntary, but for the sake of a husband or under duress;
שֶׁהוּא דּוּגְמַת הַכּוּתִיִּים ״גֵּרֵי אֲרָיוֹת״ (מְלָכִים ב י״ז:כ״ה–כ״ח): ״אֶת ה׳ הָיוּ יְרֵאִים, וְאֶת אֱלֹהֵיהֶם [הָיוּ עֹבְדִים]״ (שָׁם:ל״ג)
mirroring the Samaritan converts out of fear of lions: "They feared Hashem, and served their own gods" (II Melachim 17:33);
שֶׁלֹּא הָיוּ בִּכְלַל אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם וְלֹא בִּכְלַל יִשְׂרָאֵל, וְכֵן הִיא סוֹפָהּ לְהוֹלִיד בֵּן סוֹרֵר וּמוֹרֶה (סַנְהֶדְרִין ק״ז עַמּוּד א׳).
who belonged neither to the nations nor to Israel, she was destined to give birth to a rebellious son (Sanhedrin 107a).
וּמִצְוַת כִּבּוּד אָב הוּא מִצְוָה שֶׁהֶחֱזִיקוּ בָהּ אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם בְּיֶתֶר שְׂאֵת, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּעֵשָׂו (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה ס״ה:ט״ז)
And the commandment of honoring parents is a precept held with great zeal by the nations, as stated regarding Esau (Bereishis Rabbah 65:16);
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּקִדּוּשִׁין (ל״א עַמּוּד א׳) וּבַיְרוּשַׁלְמִי פֶּרֶק א׳ דְּפֵאָה (הֲלָכָה א׳): ״לִלְמוֹד עַד הֵיכָן מִצְוַת כִּבּוּד מִגּוֹי דָּמָא בֶּן נְתִינָה״
and in Kiddushin (31a) and Yerushalmi Peah (1:1): to learn the boundary of honoring parents from the gentile Dama ben Netinah;
וְשָׁם: ״׳יוֹדוּךָ ה׳ כָּל מַלְכֵי אָרֶץ [כִּי שָׁמְעוּ אִמְרֵי פִיךָ]׳ (תְּהִלִּים קל״ח:ד׳) — כֵּיוָן שֶׁאָמַר: ׳כַּבֵּד אֶת אָבִיךָ וְאֶת אִמֶּךָ׳, הוֹדוּ מַלְכֵי אֶרֶץ״

and there: "All the kings of the earth shall praise You, Hashem, when they hear the words of Your mouth" (Tehillim 138:4)—upon hearing "Honor your father and mother," the kings of the earth praised Him;
וְכֵן אִיתָא בְּתַנָּא דְּבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ רַבָּה (פֶּרֶק כ״ו): ״כִּבּוּד אָב וָאֵם, אִם קִיַּימְתָּ — נִתְקַיֵּים בָּכֶם ׳וְרָאוּ גוֹיִם צִדְקֵךְ׳ (יְשַׁעְיָה ס״ב:ב׳)״
and so in Tanna D'vei Eliyahu Rabbah (ch. 26): "if you fulfill honoring parents, there is fulfilled in you: 'And the nations shall see your righteousness'";
וְזוֹ תּוֹלִיד בֵּן שֶׁיַּעֲבוֹד עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה וְיֵצֵא מִכְּלַל יִשְׂרָאֵל וּמִכְּלַל אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם.
and this captive woman gave birth to a son who rebelled, departing from Israel and from the civilized nations.

וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁדָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הָיָה כְּבָר ״לִבּוֹ חָלָל בְּקִרְבּוֹ״, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה (ד׳ סוֹף עַמּוּד ב׳): דְּעַל כָּרְחָךְ לֹא הָיָה רָאוּי לְאוֹתָהּ מַעֲשֶׂה אֶלָּא לְהוֹרוֹת תְּשׁוּבָה
And even though King David's heart was already slain within him (Avodah Zarah 4b), not being fitting for that act save to instruct repentance;
וְשָׁם שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה לְהוֹרוֹת תְּשׁוּבָה לֹא הָיָה לוֹ חֵשֶׁק מִצַּד יֵצֶר הָרָע
and regarding the captive woman where repentance was not the objective, he possessed no desire from the yetzer hara;
מִכָּל מָקוֹם מֵאַחַר דְּסוֹף אֵירַע לוֹ אוֹתָהּ מַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁהוּצְרַךְ לְהֵיעָנֵשׁ עָלֶיהָ וּלְהָקִים עָלָיו רָעָה מִתּוֹךְ בֵּיתוֹ
nevertheless since that affair of Batsheva occurred, requiring that evil be raised against him from within his house (II Shmuel 12:11);
הִזְמִין לוֹ חֵשֶׁק זֶה, וְנִמְצָא לֹא הָיָה לוֹ הַחֵשֶׁק מִצַּד הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע כְּלָל
Hashem orchestrated this desire, so that it derived not from the yetzer hara at all.
אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם הָיָה מִצַּד הַחֵטְא דֶּעָתִיד, דְּעִיקַּר חֶטְאוֹ הָיָה בַּמַּה שֶּׁהֵבִיא עַצְמוֹ לִידֵי נִסָּיוֹן, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (ק״ז רֵישׁ עַמּוּד א׳)
But nevertheless it derived from the future sin, his primary error having been bringing himself into a trial (Sanhedrin 107a);
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁהוּא בָּטַח בְּנַפְשׁוֹ דְּלִבּוֹ חָלָל וְאֵין לוֹ יֵצֶר הָרָע שֶׁכְּבָר כְּבָשׁוֹ
meaning he trusted within his soul that his heart was slain and that he had conquered his inclination;

וּבֶאֱמֶת הִזְהִירוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה: ״אַל תַּאֲמֵן בְּעַצְמְךָ [עַד יוֹם מוֹתְךָ]״ (אָבוֹת ב:ד), וְ״אִלְמָלֵא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עֲזָרוֹ — לֹא יוֹעִיל כְּלוּם״, וְלֹא יָכֹל לִבְטוֹחַ בְּעַצְמוֹ.
whereas the Sages warned: "do not trust in yourself until the day of your death" (Avos 2:4), and were it not for divine help human effort avails nothing.

וְעַל כֵּן גַּם בִּיפַת תֹּאַר, שֶׁבָּטַח בְּעַצְמוֹ דְּאֵין חֶשְׁקוֹ מִצַּד יֵצֶר רָע — הֲגַם דְּבֶאֱמֶת הָיָה כֵן — מִכָּל מָקוֹם בָּא לִכְלַל הַטָּעוּת דְּלֹא דָּרַשׁ סְמוּכִים (סַנְהֶדְרִין ק״ז עַמּוּד א׳)
Wherefore regarding the captive woman, David trusting that his desire was not from the yetzer—though in truth it was so—erred in failing to expound adjoining verses (Sanhedrin 107a);
וְהֲגַם שֶׁהַנּוֹלָד מִמֶּנָּה הָיָה גַּם כֵּן יָפֶה בֶּאֱמֶת בְּכָל קוֹמַת גּוּפוֹ
and although the son born from her was truly beautiful across his entire bodily stature;
מִכָּל מָקוֹם בַּסּוֹף נִתְגַּלָּה שָׁרְשׁוֹ וְהָעוֹמֶק רֵאשִׁית שֶׁבְּמַחֲשָׁבָה הַנֶּעְלָם, וְעַל כֵּן נִתְלָה בִּשְׂעָרוֹ (שְׁמוּאֵל ב י״ח:ט׳):
nevertheless in the end his concealed root blemish erupted, wherefore he was hanged by his proud hair (II Shmuel 18:9)!

6.h: יִשְׂרָאֵל קְדוֹשִׁים — פֶּרֶק ו׳, סְעִיפִים ט״ו–י״ט

אוֹת ט״ו — תִּיקּוּן אַבְשָׁלוֹם עַל יְדֵי דָּוִד, ״הֶבֶל הַיֹּפִי״ בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין, וְהַחֵן שֶׁל אֶסְתֵּר — Section 15: Absalom's Elevation by David, True Beauty vs. Bodily Vanity, and Esther's Grace

The theme: The posthumous elevation of Absalom, the definition of authentic beauty versus physical vanity, and grace (chen) as unearned favor. Although Absalom's root was flawed through his mother (the captive woman), his beauty was not merely a superficial deception that stole the hearts of men. King David ultimately elevated him through his prayers from the seven compartments of Gehinnom and brought him into the World to Come (Sotah 10b), which corresponds to the eighth rung, Binah. Absalom repaired nine rungs from foot to crown, but could not rectify Chokhmah, for rebelling against his father damaged the root of Chokhmah (termed Abba). Because his soul was redeemed, his beauty endures forever, as does all beauty praised in Scripture. In Sanhedrin (20a), the Sages expound "beauty is vain" (hevel ha-yofi, Mishlei 31:30) regarding Boaz, the generation of Joshua, or the generation of Hezekiah, interpreting bodily beauty as authentic spiritual beauty; yet even then, external form alone remains vanity compared to a woman who fears Hashem in essence. Among the nations, true beauty cannot exist: the body is merely a vessel of decomposing flesh, shame, and worms (Sotah 5b). In contrast, grace (chen) is that which finds unearned favor in the eyes of onlookers, even when physical beauty is lacking. Thus the Sages state regarding Esther that she had a greenish complexion (yerakroket), yet a thread of divine lovingkindness (chut shel chesed) was drawn over her (Megillah 13a; Esther 2:15, 17). Even though Scripture describes her as "fair of form," she was not physically the most beautiful (Bava Batra 15b regarding Job's daughters); she found chen. Grace denotes unearned favor bestowed upon the unworthy ("and I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious", Shemos 33:19; Berachos 7a; Bereishis Rabbah 29:1 regarding Noah), wherefore Scripture calls grace "false" (sheker)—being unmerited—rather than "vain" (hevel).

p: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁמִּשֶּׁנִּתְגַּלָּה שֶׁרֵאשִׁיתוֹ רַע, דְּלֹא הָיָה נָקִי אַגַּב אִמֵּיהּ
And even though once it was revealed that Absalom's root was flawed, not having been cleansed on account of his mother;
הֲרֵי מִמֵּילָא גַּם כָּל מִדּוֹת הַנִּמְשָׁכוֹת מִשּׁוֹרֶשׁ זֶה הוּא כֵן, כִּי: ״מִשֹּׁרֶשׁ נָחָשׁ — יֵצֵא צֶפַע״ (יְשַׁעְיָה י״ד:כ״ט)
automatically all attributes drawn from this root are likewise compromised, for "out of the serpent's root shall come forth a basilisk" (Yeshayah 14:29);
מִכָּל מָקוֹם לֹא הָיָה הַיּוֹפִי לְמַרְאִית הָעַיִן דִּבְנֵי אָדָם בִּלְבַד, וּכְפִי מַה שֶּׁגָּנַב לִבָּם
nevertheless his beauty was not merely an outward deception before human eyes wherewith he stole their hearts;
שֶׁהֲרֵי סוֹף דְּאַסְקֵיהּ דָּוִד מִשִּׁבְעָה מְדוֹרֵי גֵּיהִנָּם וְאַיְיתֵיהּ לְעוֹלָם הַבָּא
for in the end King David raised him from the seven compartments of Gehinnom and brought him into the World to Come;
(שֶׁהוּא נֶגֶד מַדְרֵיגָה הַחְּמִישִׁית [הַשְּׁמִינִית] — הַבִּינָה, דְּרוֹמֶזֶת לְעָלְמָא דְּאָתֵי כַּנּוֹדָע;
(which corresponds to the eighth rung, Binah, which alludes to the World to Come as is known;
וּמִכַּף רַגְלוֹ וְעַד קָדְקֳדוֹ הֵם ט׳ [תֵּשַׁע] מַדְרֵיגוֹת, וְהַחָכְמָה לֹא תִּיקֵּן
and from the sole of his foot to his crown are nine rungs, while Chokhmah he did not rectify;
כִּי הַמְּרִידָה בְּאָבִיו הוּא קִלְקוּל בְּשׁוֹרֶשׁ הַחָכְמָה שֶׁנִּקְרֵאת ״אַבָּא״)
for rebelling against his father was a spiritual breach in the root of Chokhmah, which is designated "Father");
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּסוֹטָה (י׳ סוֹף עַמּוּד ב׳), וְאִם כֵּן נִשְׁאַר הַיּוֹפִי שֶׁלּוֹ קַיָּים לָעַד, וְכָל יוֹפִי שֶׁבַּמִּקְרָא כֵּן.
as stated in Sotah (10b), and if so, his beauty remained enduring forever, and so with all beauty chronicled in Scripture.
וְעַל כֵּן אָמְרוּ עַל פָּסוּק ״הֶבֶל הַיֹּפִי״ (מִשְׁלֵי ל״א:ל׳) בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (כ׳ רֵישׁ עַמּוּד א׳): ״זֶה בֹּעַז, אוֹ דּוֹרוֹ שֶׁל יְהוֹשֻׁעַ, אוֹ דְּחִזְקִיָּה״
And therefore the Sages expounded on "beauty is vain" (Mishlei 31:30) in Sanhedrin (20a): "this is Boaz, or the generation of Joshua, or the generation of Hezekiah";
שֶׁדָּרְשׁוּ גַּם יוֹפִי זֶה עַל יוֹפִי הָאֲמִיתִּי
expounding even this physical beauty as authentic spiritual beauty;
וְעִם כָּל זֶה הוּא עַדַיִין ״הֶבֶל״ שֶׁהוּא רַק יוֹפִי הַמַּרְאֶה, וְ״אִשָּׁה יִרְאַת ה׳״ הִיא בְּעַצְמִיּוּת
yet with all this it remains "vain," being merely external appearance, while "a woman that fears Hashem" is holy in her very essence;
אֲבָל בְּאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם לֹא שַׁיָּיךְ כְּלָל יוֹפִי דְּמַרְאֶה בֶּאֱמֶת
but among the nations of the world, authentic beauty of appearance cannot apply at all;
כִּי מַה יּוֹפִי יֵשׁ בְּחֶמֶת מָלֵא צוֹאָה וְסוֹפוֹ לִהְיוֹת רִמָּה וְתוֹלֵעָה?
for what beauty is there in a flask full of filth destined to become rot and worms?
וּבְסוֹטָה (ה׳ סוֹף עַמּוּד א׳): ״בָּשָׂר — בּוּשָׁה, סְרוּחָה, רִמָּה״, וְלֹא שַׁיָּיךְ בְּיוֹפִי הַבָּשָׂר שֵׁם יוֹפִי עַל הָאֱמֶת כְּלָל, וְהַכֹּל הֶבֶל גָּמוּר.
and in Sotah (5b): "flesh (basar) denotes shame (bushah), stench (seruchah), and worms (rimmah)", the beauty of flesh possessing no true title of beauty, being absolute vanity.
וְהַחֵן הוּא מַה שֶּׁמִּתְקַבֵּל בְּעֵינֵי בְּנֵי אָדָם, שֶׁיֵּשׁ שֶׁמִּתְקַבֵּל אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ יָפֶה כָּל כָּךְ בֶּאֱמֶת
And grace (chen) is that which finds favor in human eyes, for one may find favor even without possessing genuine beauty;
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּאֶסְתֵּר: ״וַתְּהִי אֶסְתֵּר נֹשֵׂאת חֵן בְּעֵינֵי כָּל רֹאֶיהָ״ (אֶסְתֵּר ב:טו), ״וַתִּשָּׂא חֵן וָחֶסֶד לְפָנָיו מִכָּל [הַבְּתוּלוֹת]״ (שָׁם:יז)

as stated regarding Esther: "and Esther obtained favor in the sight of all them that looked upon her" (Esther 2:15), "and she obtained grace and favor in his sight more than all the virgins" (ibid. 2:17);
וּכְפִי הַנִּרְאֶה מִזֶּה גַּם כֵּן סָמַךְ הַמִּדְרָשׁ בִּמְגִלָּה (י״ג עַמּוּד א׳): ״דִּירַקְרֹקֶת הָיְתָה, וְחוּט שֶׁל חֶסֶד מָשׁוּךְ עָלֶיהָ״
and based upon this the Midrash in Megillah (13a) teaches: "she had a greenish complexion, but a thread of divine lovingkindness was drawn over her";
וְאַף שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְהַנַּעֲרָה יְפַת תֹּאַר״ (אֶסְתֵּר ב:ז), לֹא הָיְתָה יָפָה מִכּוּלָּם
and even though it is written "and the maiden was of beautiful form" (Esther 2:7), she was not the fairest of all.

וְכֵן מַשְׁמַע מִמַּה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ בְּבָבָא בַּתְרָא (ט״ו עַמּוּד ב׳): ״אִיּוֹב בִּימֵי אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ הָיָה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ׳וְלֹא נִמְצָא נָשִׁים יָפוֹת כִּבְנוֹת אִיּוֹב׳ (אִיּוֹב מ״ב:ט״ו) וְכוּלֵיהּ״
And so it is implied from Bava Batra (15b): "Job lived in the days of Ahasuerus, for it is said: 'and in all the land were no women found so fair as the daughters of Job' (Iyov 42:15)";
וַהֲרֵי נִמְצֵאת אֶסְתֵּר יָפָה מֵהֶם?! וְעַל כָּרְחָךְ שֶׁגַּם הִיא רַק מָצְאָה חֵן.
for was not Esther found more fair than they?! Rather, perforce, Esther found unearned grace (chen).
וְכַיּוֹצֵא בָּזֶה אָמְרוּ בִּבְרָכוֹת (ז׳ סוֹף עַמּוּד א׳): ״׳וְחַנֹּתִי אֶת אֲשֶׁר אָחֹן׳ (שְׁמוֹת ל״ג:י״ט) — אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ הָגוּן״, דְּכֵן הוּא מַשְׁמָעוּת לְשׁוֹן ״חֵן״
And similarly the Sages stated in Berachos (7a): "'and I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious' (Shemos 33:19)—even though he is unworthy," for such is the precise meaning of grace;
וְכֵן אָמְרוּ בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה רֵישׁ פָּרָשָׁה כ״ט (סִימָן א׳): ״אַף נֹחַ שֶׁנִּשְׁתַּיֵּיר לֹא הָיָה כְּדַאי, אֶלָּא שֶׁמָּצָא חֵן״
and so in Bereishis Rabbah (29:1): "even Noah who was spared was not worthy on his own merit, but found grace";
וְעַל כֵּן אָמַר עַל הַחֵן שֶׁהוּא ״שֶׁקֶר״ (מִשְׁלֵי ל״א:ל׳) וְלֹא ״הֶבֶל״:
wherefore Scripture designates grace as "false" (sheker, Mishlei 31:30)—being unmerited—and not merely "vain" (hevel)!

אוֹת ט״ז — חֵן דְּיוֹסֵף וְדוֹר הַמִּדְבָּר, ״לֹא תְחוֹנֵּם״ בָּעַמִּים, וְשֶׁלֹּא לִיתֵּן לָהֶם מַתְּנַת חִנָּם — Section 16: The Grace of Joseph and the Wilderness Generation, Not Praising Gentiles, and Withholding Free Gifts

The theme: Grace in Joseph and the generation of the wilderness, the prohibition against praising gentiles (lo techonem), and withholding unearned gifts. In Sanhedrin (20a), the Sages expound "grace is false" (sheker ha-chen) regarding Joseph: Sotah (36b) states that he entered to fulfill his desire, his seed issuing from his fingernails; his deliverance from overt sin through the vision of his father's countenance was an act of pure grace (chen) from Hashem, granted because he was of the seed of Jacob whose bed was whole. Similarly, the generation of the wilderness—the most cherished of all generations—merited solely through grace, having rebelled repeatedly and having been submerged in forty-nine gates of defilement in Egypt; yet Hashem bestowed grace upon them, giving them the Torah and establishing them as a "generation of knowledge" ("they found grace in the wilderness", Yirmiyah 31:1; Shir HaShirim Rabbah on 6:12). So too the generation of Joshua merited the conquest of the Land through grace. Among the nations, true beauty is non-existent, leaving only superficial grace; therefore the Torah commands lo techonem—do not attribute grace unto them (Avodah Zarah 20a). Even when they display apparent fences against immorality, it is deceitful like a swine extending its split hooves to declare "see, I am clean!" (Bereishis Rabbah 65:1). True grace and beauty exist only within Israel, who possess inborn bashfulness and fear of Hashem (bayshanut), making brazen public sin impossible. Furthermore, lo techonem prohibits giving gentiles an unearned free gift (matnat chinam, Avodah Zarah 20a), which counters the trait of compassion (rachmanut) inherited from Jacob. Compassion must be governed by divine command: "he who has mercy on the cruel ultimately becomes cruel to the merciful" (Koheles Rabbah 7:16 on Saul).
וּבְסַנְהֶדְרִין שָׁם (כ׳ רֵישׁ עַמּוּד א׳) דָּרְשׁוּ ״חֵן״ אַיּוֹסֵף
And in Sanhedrin (20a) the Sages expounded "grace" (chen) regarding Joseph;
כִּי עָלָיו אָמְרוּ בְּסוֹטָה (ל״ו עַמּוּד ב׳): ״לַעֲשׂוֹת צְרָכָיו נִכְנַס, וְשֶׁיָּצָא שִׁכְבַת זֶרַע מִבֵּין צִפָּרְנֵי יָדָיו״
for regarding him the Talmud states in Sotah (36b): "he entered to fulfill his desire, his seed issuing from between his fingernails";
וְאִם כֵּן אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא שֶׁמָּצָא חֵן בְּעֵינֵי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לְהַצִּילוֹ מִגּוּפָהּ שֶׁל מַעֲשֶׂה עַל יְדֵי דְּמוּת דְּיוֹקְנוֹ שֶׁל אָבִיו
and if so, it was solely that he found grace in the eyes of Hashem to deliver him from the deed itself through the vision of his father's image;
כִּי זֶהוּ שֶׁהִצִּילוֹ עַל יְדֵי שֶׁהָיָה מִזֶּרַע יַעֲקֹב שֶׁכּוּלּוֹ זֶרַע אֱמֶת וְאֵין בְּמִטָּתוֹ פְּסֹולֶת.
this saving him because he was of the seed of Jacob which is entirely truth, having no spiritual blemish in his bed.
וּמַה דְּאָמְרוּ אַדּוֹרוֹ שֶׁל מֹשֶׁה, דְּגַם דּוֹר הַמִּדְבָּר שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה שֶׁהוּא דּוֹר חָבוּב מִכָּל הַדּוֹרוֹת — אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא שֶׁמָּצָא חֵן
And that which the Sages expounded regarding the generation of Moshe: that even the wilderness generation, the most cherished of eras, merited solely through grace;
שֶׁהֲרֵי כַּמָּה הִמְרוּ וְנִסּוּ בְּכַמָּה נִסְיוֹנוֹת
for they rebelled repeatedly and tested Hashem in ten trials;
וְכֵן תְּחִלַּת יְצִיאָתָם מִמִּצְרַיִם שֶׁהָיוּ שְׁקוּעִים בְּמַ״ט (49) שַׁעֲרֵי טוּמְאָה
and at their initial Exodus from Egypt they were submerged in forty-nine gates of defilement;
אֶלָּא שֶׁמָּצְאוּ חֵן, וְנָתַן לָהֶם הַתּוֹרָה וַעֲשָׂאָם ״דּוֹר דֵּעָה״
but they found unmerited grace, Hashem granting them the Torah and making them a "generation of knowledge."

וְכַיּוֹצֵא בָּזֶה אָמְרוּ בְּשִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה ו:יב) עַל פָּסוּק: ״לֹא יָדַעְתִּי נַפְשִׁי שָׂמַתְנִי [מַרְכְּבוֹת עַמִּי נָדִיב]״ (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים ו:יב) — עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל בִּיצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם, שֶׁלֹּא הֶאֱמִינוּ בְּנַפְשָׁם כֵּן

And similarly in Shir HaShirim Rabbah (6:12) on "Before I was aware, my soul set me upon the chariots of my princely people": referring to Israel at the Exodus who could not believe such glory for their souls;
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: ״מָצָא חֵן בַּמִּדְבָּר [עַם שְׂרִידֵי חָרֶב]״ (יִרְמְיָה ל״א:ב׳).
concerning which it is said: "The people that were left of the sword found grace in the wilderness" (Yirmiyah 31:1).
וּלְאִידָךְ מַאן דְּאָמַר: גַּם דּוֹר יְהוֹשֻׁעַ כֵּן, שֶׁזָּכוּ בְּכִיבּוּשׁ הָאָרֶץ מַה שֶּׁלֹּא זָכָה לוֹ שׁוּם דּוֹר, וְאֵינוֹ אֶלָּא חֵן.
And according to the other opinion: the generation of Joshua was likewise thus, meriting the conquest of the Land which no other generation achieved, which was purely unearned grace.
וּבְאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם שֶׁהַיּוֹפִי שֶׁקֶר, אִם כֵּן לְעוֹלָם אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא חֵן, וְאָסוּר לִיתֵּן לָהֶם חֵן (עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה כ׳ עַמּוּד א׳)
And among the nations where true beauty is non-existent, their appeal is merely superficial grace, and it is forbidden to attribute grace unto them (lo techonem);
וְהַיְינוּ אֲפִילּוּ בְּיוֹפִי גָּמוּר שֶׁל הַגְדָּרַת עֶרְוָה וְכַיּוֹצֵא מִמִּדּוֹת טוֹבוֹת, אֵין לִיתֵּן חֵן
meaning even regarding an apparent virtue of chastity or noble traits, one may not praise them;
כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת אֵין בָּזֶה חֵן וְיוֹפִי, כִּי הוּא רַק דֶּרֶךְ פְּשִׁיטוּת טְלָפַיִם כַּחֲזִיר
for in truth this contains neither grace nor beauty, being merely the outward display of split hooves like a swine;
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: ״נֶזֶם זָהָב בְּאַף חֲזִיר — אִשָּׁה יָפָה וְסָרַת טָעַם״ (מִשְׁלֵי י״א:כ״ב)
concerning which it is written: "As a ring of gold in a swine's snout, so is a fair woman that turns aside from discretion" (Mishlei 11:22);
שֶׁהַיּוֹפִי הוּא רַק כַּחֲזִיר הַפּוֹשֵׁט טְלָפָיו: ״רְאוּ טָהוֹר אֲנִי״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה ס״ה:א׳).
whose beauty is like the swine displaying its hooves, boasting: "Behold, I am clean!" (Bereishis Rabbah 65:1).
וְעַל כֵּן לֹא שַׁיָּיךְ בָּהֶם חֵן רַק אֵצֶל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהֶם בַּתּוֹלָדָה מִדַּת הַבּוּשָׁה וְיִרְאַת ה׳ שֶׁעַל הַפָּנִים מִיהַת
Wherefore authentic grace applies exclusively unto Israel, who possess inborn bashfulness and fear of Hashem upon their faces;
שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לַחֲטוֹא בְּגִילּוּי פָּנִים מִיהַת, וְזֶהוּ אַתְחַלְתָּא דְּיִרְאַת ה׳ שֶׁיֶּשְׁנוֹ בְּכָל אֶחָד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל עַל כָּל פָּנִים
making it impossible to sin with brazen shamelessness, this being the inception of the fear of Hashem present within every single Jew;
וּמֵאַחַר שֶׁהֵם ״אִשָּׁה יִרְאַת ה׳״, שַׁיָּיךְ בָּהֶם חֵן וְיוֹפִי.
and because they are "a woman that fears Hashem," grace and authentic beauty apply unto them.

וְזֶהוּ שֶׁהִסְמִיכוּ עַל זֶה מֵעִנְיַן אִיסּוּר הִסְתַּכְּלוּת בִּזְנוּת וְגֶדֶר עֶרְוָה, וּמַאֲמַר רַבִּי פִּנְחָס בֶּן יָאִיר הַנִּזְכָּר בְּעֶשֶׂר מַדְרֵיגוֹת עַד רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ, שֶׁהוּא מִצַּד הַגְדָּרַת הָעֶרְוָה.

And this is why the Talmud juxtaposed this unto the prohibition of gazing upon licentiousness and the ladder of Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair ascending to the Holy Spirit, which is achieved through moral purity.
וְשֶׁלֹּא לִיתֵּן לָהֶם מַתְּנַת חִנָּם (עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה כ׳ עַמּוּד א׳) — הוּא נֶגֶד מִדַּת הָרַחְמָנוּת שֶׁבְּזֶרַע יַעֲקֹב, מִדַּת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
And the prohibition against giving gentiles an unearned gift (matnat chinam, Avodah Zarah 20a) stands opposite the trait of compassion (rachmanut) within the seed of Jacob;
שֶׁבִּכְלָלוֹ מַתְּנַת חִנָּם לְמִי שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לָהּ, דְּזֶהוּ עִיקַּר הָרַחְמָנוּת עַל הַבְּרִיּוֹת.
which includes bestowing a free gift upon the needy, the very essence of mercy upon creatures.
וְ״כָל הַמְרַחֵם עַל אַכְזָרִים — סוֹף נַעֲשָׂה אַכְזָר עַל רַחְמָנִים״ (תַּנְחוּמָא מְצוֹרָע א׳), מִשָּׁאוּל
And "whoever has mercy on the cruel ultimately becomes cruel to the merciful" (Tanchuma, Metzora §1), as demonstrated by King Saul;
עַל כָּרְחָךְ זֶה מִשְּׁלֵימוּת מִדַּת הָרַחְמָנוּת דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁכַּוָּונָתָם רַק לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם וּבִשְׁבִיל מִצְוַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
perforce proving that the perfection of Israel's compassion is acting purely for Heaven according to Hashem's commandment;
וְלֹא מִצַּד טֶבַע תּוֹלָדָה בְּעָלְמָא, כְּשֶׁלֹּא יְרַחֲמוּ בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁאֵין לְרַחֵם:
and not out of mere blind, natural sentiment, knowing to withhold mercy in an arena where mercy is forbidden!
אוֹת י״ז — מִנְחַת יַעֲקֹב לְעֵשָׂו בְּ״עָקָא״, הָרַחְמָנוּת הַמְצוּמְצֶמֶת בִּגְבוּרָה, וּכְפִיַּית הַר כְּגִיגִית כְּמַתָּנָה מִצַּד הַחֶסֶד
Section 17: Jacob's Tribute to Esau in Distress, Compassion Channelled through Gevurah, and Coercing the Mountain as Merciful Chastisement

6.h: The theme: Jacob's sorrow in bestowing a gift unto Esau, compassion channeled through Gevurah, and the Torah as an unearned gift (matnat chinam). Regarding Jacob presenting a gift to Esau, Scripture states: "So the present passed over before him" (Bereishis 32:22); Bereishis Rabbah (76:8) expounds: "he was in distress (af hu b'aka)", grieving that he was forced to give a gift unto the wicked. Compassion originates from Avraham (Beitzah 32b), who extended charity unto uncircumcised gentiles to draw them beneath the wings of the Shechinah through the inn (eshel) he planted; but because Avraham's Chesed was expansive and unchanneled, dross emerged in Ishmael. Jacob represents consummate compassion (tiferet)—compassion restricted through the Gevurah of Isaac, being fierce against enemies. Therefore Jacob is the most merciful Patriarch ("as an eagle stirs up her nest", Devarim 32:11), choosing to receive the hunter's arrow in his own body rather than let it strike his young. The Torah went forth from the side of Gevurah (Zohar)—representing its precise halachic boundaries and penalties; yet the Torah itself is the Truth of Jacob (Emet l'Yaakov, Berachos 5b), bestowed through the lovingkindness of Avraham (Torat Chesed). Holding the mountain over Israel like a cask (Shabbat 88a) was an act of paternal mercy: "as a man chastens his son, so Hashem your God chastens you" (Devarim 8:5). Because Israel shows mercy to mortals in temporal life, Hashem poured immense mercy upon them in eternal life by coercing them to receive the Torah. Hashem did not coerce the nations (Avodah Zarah 2b), for the Torah is an unearned gift (matnat chinam) likened unto water, which is forbidden to be given to gentiles. Coercing the heart's holy desire at Sinai was an absolute gift of unearned love!

p: וְעַל כֵּן נֶאֱמַר בְּיַעֲקֹב: ״וַתַּעֲבֹר הַמִּנְחָה עַל פָּנָיו״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית ל״ב:כ״ב), וְאָמְרוּ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ע״ו:ח׳): ״אַף הוּא בְּעָקָא״
And therefore it is said regarding Jacob: "So the present passed over before him" (Bereishis 32:22), the Midrash stating (Bereishis Rabbah 76:8): "he was in distress (af hu b'aka)";
שֶׁהָיָה בְּצַעַר וְכַעַס עַל זֶה שֶׁהוּצְרַךְ לָתֵת לוֹ מַתָּנָה.
grieving and troubled over having to give a gift unto wicked Esau.
וְזֶהוּ מִדַּת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם דְּ״אָחִיד בִּתְרֵין סִטְרִין״ (זֹוהַר חֵלֶק א׳ רכ״ב עַמּוּד א׳)
And this is the attribute of our father Jacob who grasped both sides (Zohar I, 222a);
כִּי גּוּף הָרַחְמָנוּת נִמְשָׁךְ מִצַּד מִדַּת אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, דִּגְמִילוּת חֲסָדִים גַּם כֵּן הוּא רַחְמָנוּת
for the body of compassion is drawn from Avraham Avinu, lovingkindness being a form of mercy;
וְכֵן אָמְרוּ בְּבֵיצָה (ל״ב עַמּוּד ב׳): ״כָּל הַמְרַחֵם עַל הַבְּרִיּוֹת — בְּיָדוּעַ שֶׁהוּא מִזַּרְעוֹ שֶׁל אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ״
as stated in Beitzah (32b): "whoever has mercy on creatures is known to be of the seed of Avraham Avinu";
וְתָלוּ בְּאַבְרָהָם, דְּגוּף הָרַחְמָנוּת בִּצְדָקָה וָחֶסֶד נִמְשָׁךְ מִמֶּנּוּ.
attributing compassion to Avraham, for the practice of charity and kindness flows from him.
אֶלָּא שֶׁהוּא הָיָה מְרַחֵם עַל בְּנֵי אָדָם עֲרֵלִים וְגוֹיִם, שֶׁלֹּא הָיוּ אֲחֵרִים בְּיָמָיו
Except that Avraham showed mercy unto uncircumcised gentiles, there being no other men in his days;
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁגִּיְּירָם, הֲרֵי אָמְרוּ: לְאַחַר שֶׁאָכְלוּ וְשָׁתוּ אָמַר לָהֶם: ״בָּרְכוּ!״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה מ״ט:ד׳), וְהָרַחְמָנוּת הָיָה מִקּוֹדֶם
and although he converted them, he fed them first and only afterward said: "Bless the Master of the world!" (Bereishis Rabbah 49:4), his mercy preceding their conversion;
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה הוּא שֶׁיָּכוֹל לְהַמְשִׁיכָם אַחַר כָּךְ לְהִתְגַּיֵּיר
through which he drew them to convert;
וְלוּלֵי הָ״אֶשֶׁל״ שֶׁנָּטַע לְהַמְשִׁיךְ בְּנֵי אָדָם אֵלָיו עַל יְדֵי חַסְדּוֹ וְצִדְקָתוֹ עִמָּהֶם, לֹא הָיָה מְגַיְּירָם אַחַר כָּךְ.
and without the inn (eshel, Bereishis 21:33) he planted to draw men through kindness, he could not have converted them.
וְעַל כֵּן הָרַחְמָנוּת וּגְמִילוּת חֲסָדִים שֶׁלּוֹ הָיָה עֲלֵיהֶם בְּעוֹדָם גּוֹיִם
Wherefore his mercy and lovingkindness were extended unto them while they were still gentiles;
(וְאַף אַחַר שֶׁנִּתְגַּיְּירוּ לֹא נִשְׁאֲרוּ תַּחַת כַּנְפֵי הַשְּׁכִינָה, שֶׁהֲרֵי לֹא נִשְׁאַר לְחֵלֶק ה׳ אֶלָּא זֶרַע יִשְׂרָאֵל לְבַד שֶׁקֵּירְבָנוּ לִפְנֵי הַר סִינַי וְנָתַן לָנוּ הַתּוֹרָה)
(and even after converting, their descendants did not remain beneath the wings of the Shechinah, Hashem's eternal portion being Israel alone whom He brought before Sinai);
כִּי מִדָּתוֹ הָיָה בְּהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת שֶׁלֹּא נִתְבָּרְרָה עַדַיִין בְּצִמְצוּמִים כְּפִי הַתּוֹרָה
because Avraham's Chesed was boundless expansion, not yet channeled through the contractions of the Torah;
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה יָצָא מִמֶּנּוּ פְּסֹולֶת בְּיִשְׁמָעֵאל, שֶׁהוּא הַחֶסֶד דְּסִטְרָא אָחֳרָא הַמָּלֵא תַּאֲווֹת רָעוֹת.
through which unholy dross emerged in Ishmael, the unholy Chesed of the Sitra Achra filled with carnal lusts.
אֲבָל יַעֲקֹב הוּא שְׁלֵימוּת הָרַחְמָנוּת כַּאֲשֶׁר הִיא מְצוּמְצֶמֶת בְּכֹחַ הַגְּבוּרָה דְּיִצְחָק, לְהִתְאַכְזֵר עַל הָאוֹיְבִים
But Jacob represents consummate compassion, restricted through the Gevurah of Isaac to be fierce against enemies;
וְעַל כֵּן הוּא הָרַחְמָנִי שֶׁבָּאָבוֹת: ״כְּנֶשֶׁר יָעִיר קִנּוֹ [עַל גּוֹזָלָיו יְרַחֵף]״ (דְּבָרִים ל״ב:י״א)
wherefore Jacob is the most merciful of the Patriarchs: "As an eagle that stirs up her nest, that flutters over her young" (Devarim 32:11);
אָמַר: ״מוּטָב שֶׁיִּכָּנֵס הַחֵץ בִּי, וְאַל יִכָּנֵס בְּבָנַי״ (מְכִילְתָּא בְּשַׁלַּח פָּרָשָׁה ד׳)
the eagle saying: "Better that the arrow pierce me than pierce my fledglings" (Mechilta, Beshalach §4);
וְלִפְנֵי מַתַּן תּוֹרָה נֶאֱמַר: ״וָאֶשָּׂא אֶתְכֶם עַל כַּנְפֵי נְשָׁרִים וָאָבִא [אֶתְכֶם אֵלָי]״ (שְׁמוֹת י״ט:ד׳) גַּם כֵּן בְּמִדָּה זוֹ.
and prior to Sinai it was said: "and how I bore you on eagles' wings, and brought you unto Myself" (Shemos 19:4), in this very attribute.
כִּי הַתּוֹרָה: ״סַם חַיִּים״ לְיִשְׂרָאֵל, וְ״סַם הַמָּוֶת״ לְאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם (יוֹמָא ע״ב עַמּוּד ב׳)
For the Torah is an "elixir of life" unto Israel, and a "deadly poison" unto the nations of the world (Yoma 72b);
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּשַׁבָּת (פ״ח עַמּוּד ב׳): שֶׁיָּרַד חוּרְבָּה וְשִׂנְאָה לְאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם עָלָיו [עַל הַר סִינַי]
as stated in Shabbat (88b): that destruction and hatred descended upon the nations at Mount Sinai;
וְגוּף אוֹרַיְיתָא מִסִּטְרָא דִּגְבוּרָה נָפְקַת, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּזֹּוהַר כַּמָּה פְּעָמִים
and the body of the Torah went forth from the side of Gevurah, as stated repeatedly in the Zohar;
וְהַיְינוּ גּוּפֵי מִשְׁפָּטֶיהָ, וְצִמְצוּם מִצְוֹתֶיהָ, וְאַזְהָרוֹתֶיהָ, וְעָנְשֶׁיהָ, וְזֶהוּ מִצַּד מַעֲשֵׂה הַמִּצְוֹת.
meaning its rigorous statutes, boundaries of commandments, warnings, and penalties, on the part of physical execution.
אֲבָל הַתּוֹרָה עַצְמָהּ, דְּ״אֵין אֱמֶת אֶלָּא תּוֹרָה״ כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרָכוֹת (ה׳ עַמּוּד ב׳) — מִסִּטְרָא דְּ״אֱמֶת לְיַעֲקֹב״ (מִיכָה ז:כ)
But the Torah itself—for "there is no truth save Torah" (Berachos 5b)—derives from the side of "Truth unto Jacob" (Michah 7:20);
וְנִקְרֵאת גַּם כֵּן ״תּוֹרַת חֶסֶד״ (מִשְׁלֵי ל״א:כ״ו) מִסִּטְרָא דְּאַבְרָהָם
and is likewise called "the Torah of lovingkindness" (Mishlei 31:26) from the side of Avraham;
כִּי מַה שֶּׁנִּתְּנָה לְיִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא מִצַּד מִדַּת הַחֶסֶד: ״דְּרָצָה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְזַכּוֹת אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל, לְפִיכָךְ הִרְבָּה לָהֶם תּוֹרָה וּמִצְוֹת״ (מַכּוֹת כ״ג עַמּוּד ב׳)
for its bestowal upon Israel was through Chesed: "the Holy One desired to make Israel meritorious, wherefore He multiplied for them Torah and commandments" (Makkot 23b);
כִּי הִיא בָּאָה מִכֹּחַ כָּל שְׁלֹשֶׁת הָאָבוֹת שֶׁקִּיְּימוּ כָּל הַתּוֹרָה כּוּלָּהּ עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִיתְּנָה (יוֹמָא כ״ח עַמּוּד ב׳)
issuing from the collective strength of all three Patriarchs who fulfilled the entire Torah before it was given (Yoma 28b);

וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם עִיקַּר עַמּוּד הַתּוֹרָה מִסִּטְרָא דְּיַעֲקֹב: ״אִישׁ תָּם, יֹשֵׁב אֹהָלִים״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית כ״ה:כ״ז) — אָהֳלֵי תּוֹרָה, וְנֶאֱמַר: ״מַה טֹּבוּ אֹהָלֶיךָ יַעֲקֹב״ (בַּמִּדְבָּר כ״ד:ה׳).
yet the primary pillar of Torah is from Jacob: "a quiet man, dwelling in tents" (Bereishis 25:27)—the tents of Torah: "How goodly are your tents, O Jacob" (Bamidbar 24:5).
וְ״כָל הַמְרַחֵם עַל הַבְּרִיּוֹת — מְרַחֲמִין עָלָיו מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם״, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּשַׁבָּת (קנ״א עַמּוּד ב׳)
And "whoever has mercy on creatures, Heaven shows mercy unto him" (Shabbat 151b);
וְעַל כֵּן לֹא נִתְּנָה תּוֹרָה אֶלָּא לְיִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁכָּפָה עֲלֵיהֶם הַר כְּגִיגִית (שַׁבָּת פ״ח עַמּוּד א׳)
wherefore the Torah was given exclusively unto Israel, Hashem coercing the mountain over them like a cask (Shabbat 88a);
שֶׁהוּא דֶּרֶךְ כְּפִיָּה וְיִסּוּר וּמִצַּד הָרַחְמָנוּת: ״כַּאֲשֶׁר יְיַסֵּר אִישׁ אֶת בְּנוֹ [ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ מְיַסְּרֶךָּ]״ (דְּבָרִים ח:ה), שֶׁהוּא מֵהָרַחְמָנוּת דְּאָב עַל בָּנִים.
which was an act of coercive discipline flowing from fatherly compassion: "as a man chastens his son, so Hashem your God chastens you" (Devarim 8:5).
וּלְפִי שֶׁהֵם מְרַחֲמִין עַל הַבְּרִיּוֹת בְּחַיֵּי שָׁעָה בְּכֹחַ הָרַחְמָנוּת שֶׁלָּהֶם
And because Israel has mercy on creatures in temporal life through their innate compassion;
מִדָּה טוֹבָה מְרוּבָּה לְרַחֵם עֲלֵיהֶם בְּחַיֵּי עוֹלָם כְּפִי מִדַּת הָרַחְמָנוּת שֶׁלּוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ
the divine measure of goodness multiplied to show mercy unto them in eternal life through His supernal compassion;
וְלֹא עָשָׂה כֵן לַגּוֹיִם, כְּטַעֲנָתָם בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה (ב׳ סוֹף עַמּוּד ב׳): ״כְּלוּם כָּפִיתָ עָלֵינוּ הַר כְּגִיגִית?!״ כִּי אֵין לְרַחֵם עֲלֵיהֶם
not doing so unto the nations, despite their future complaint: "Did You coerce the mountain over us like a cask?!" (Avodah Zarah 2b), for compassion is withheld from them;
וְגַם דְּהַתּוֹרָה מַתָּנָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ: ״וּמִמִּדְבָּר — מַתָּנָה״ (בַּמִּדְבָּר כ״א:י״ח; נְדָרִים נ״ה עַמּוּד א׳), וְנֶאֱמַר: ״[כִּי] לֶקַח טוֹב נָתַתִּי לָכֶם״ (מִשְׁלֵי ד:ב)
and the Torah is an unearned gift: "and from the wilderness to Mattanah [a gift]" (Bamidbar 21:18), "For I give you good doctrine" (Mishlei 4:2);
וְהִיא ״מַתְּנַת חִנָּם״, דְּעַל כֵּן נִיתְּנָה בַּמִּדְבָּר שֶׁהוּא הֶפְקֵר
being a completely free gift (matnat chinam), wherefore it was given in the ownerless wilderness;
וְנִמְשְׁלָה לַמַּיִם שֶׁהֵם חִנָּם לְכָל בָּאֵי עוֹלָם, וְאָסוּר לִיתֵּן לָהֶם מַתְּנַת חִנָּם.
likened unto water which is free unto all, while giving gentiles a free gift is prohibited.

וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהֶחֱזִירָהּ עַל כָּל אוּמָּה וְלָשׁוֹן, אִילּוּ קִבְּלוּהָ בְּרָצוֹן לֹא הָיָה נֶחְשָׁב כָּל כָּךְ מַתְּנַת חִנָּם מֵאַחַר שֶׁהֵם מְשַׁעְבְּדִים עַצְמָם תַּחַת עוֹל מַלְכוּת שָׁמָיִם
And although Hashem offered the Torah to all nations, had they accepted it voluntarily it would not have been a free gift, having subjected themselves unto the yoke of Heaven;
אֲבָל הַכְּפִיָּה, שֶׁהוּא הַכְנָסַת הַחֵשֶׁק בַּלֵּב — זֶהוּ חִנָּם גָּמוּר:
but the coercion—implanting the divine passion into the heart—was a completely unearned free gift!

6.h: אוֹת י״ח — הַשְׁרָאַת שְׁכִינָה עַל מִשְׁפָּחוֹת הַמְיוּחָסוֹת, עִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְעֵילָּא בַּתּוֹרָה, וּבַת קוֹל דְּהַר חוֹרֵב — Section 18: The Shechinah Resting upon Lineaged Families, Heavenly Awakening, and the Heavenly Voice from Mount Horeb

The theme: Prophecy reserved for pedigreed Jewish families, the awakening from Above in the first rung of Torah, and the daily echo from Sinai. The prohibition of giving free gifts to gentiles descended at Sinai because they refused the Torah; therefore they possess no connection to Torah (the first rung of Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair) nor to the tenth rung (the Holy Spirit / the resting of the Shechinah). Even converts do not merit this ultimate level of the Holy Spirit, as stated in Kiddushin (70b): "The Holy One causes His Shechinah to rest only upon the pedigreed families of Israel" (mishpachot ha-meyuchasot). Yet converts are not entirely excluded: through immense personal striving they may attain the Holy Spirit ("and also upon the servants and handmaids in those days will I pour out My spirit", Yoel 3:2). However, spontaneous divine inspiration granted purely through an awakening from Above (itaruta d'le'ila) without preceding human effort is reserved exclusively for pedigreed Jewish families. The ladder of Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair begins with "Torah brings to watchfulness"—not saying "learning or toiling in Torah," but the essence of the Torah itself inspires watchfulness. This is the unearned divine awakening from Hashem stirring the heart: "Every single day a Heavenly Voice goes forth from Mount Horeb proclaiming: Woe to mankind for the insult to the Torah!" (Avos 6:2). These are the spontaneous thoughts of repentance entering human consciousness daily without prior human initiative: "Turn us unto You, Hashem, and we shall be turned; renew our days as of old" (Eichah 5:21; Shir HaShirim 1:4). In the Future, all rungs will be sustained directly by Hashem ("with a mighty hand will I rule over you", Yechezkel 20:33; Yirmiyah 31:32); today this innate heavenly awakening is inherited exclusively by the seed of Israel!

p: וְגַם דְּעִיקַּר הַחוּרְבָּה וְשִׂנְאָה וְאִיסּוּר מַתְּנַת חִנָּם לָהֶם יָרַד בְּהַר סִינַי וּמַתַּן תּוֹרָה
And also the essential destruction, hatred, and the prohibition of giving them free gifts descended at Sinai;
אַחַר שֶׁלֹּא קִבְּלוּהָ הוּא שֶׁהוּזְהֲרוּ עַל זֶה
once the nations refused the Torah, Israel was commanded regarding this;
וּלְפִיכָךְ אֵין לָהֶם שׁוּם שַׁיָּיכוּת לַתּוֹרָה שֶׁהוּא מַדְרֵיגָה הָרִאשׁוֹנָה דְּרַבִּי פִּנְחָס בֶּן יָאִיר
wherefore the nations have no affinity with the Torah, which is the first rung of Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair;
וְכֵן הָאַחֲרוֹנָה שֶׁהוּא הַקְּדוּשָׁה שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה וְאַחֲרֶיהָ רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ שֶׁהִיא הַשְׁרָאַת שְׁכִינָה
nor with the final rung of supernal holiness and the Holy Spirit, which is the resting of the Shechinah;

אֲפִילּוּ הַגֵּרִים אֵין זוֹכִין לָהּ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּקִדּוּשִׁין (ע׳ סוֹף עַמּוּד ב׳): ״דְּאֵין הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מַשְׁרֶה שְׁכִינָתוֹ אֶלָּא עַל מִשְׁפָּחוֹת הַמְיוּחָסוֹת שֶׁבְּיִשְׂרָאֵל״
even converts not meriting this spontaneous divine presence: "the Holy One causes His Shechinah to rest only upon the pedigreed families of Israel" (Kiddushin 70b).
וְהִסְמִיכוּ שָׁם הַמַּאֲמָר: ״מַעֲלָה יְתֵירָה בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל דִּכְתִיב בְּהוּ: ׳וְהָיִיתִי לָכֶם לֵאלֹהִים׳ בְּרֵישָׁא״
And they juxtaposed there: "there is an added virtue in Israel, for it is written: 'and I will be your God' first";
וְהַיְינוּ דְּלֹא נִתְמַעֲטוּ הַגֵּרִים לְגַמְרֵי
meaning converts are not excluded entirely;
שֶׁאִם יַרְבּוּ בְּהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת בְּאִתְעָרוּתָא שֶׁלָּהֶם בְּכָל הַמַּדְרֵיגוֹת עַד שֶׁיִּזְכּוּ שֶׁיִּהְיוּ רְאוּיִם לְהַשָּׂגַת רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ, לֹא יִמְנַע טוֹב לַהֹלְכִים בְּתָמִים
for if they multiply effort through human awakening across all rungs, Hashem will not withhold good from them that walk uprightly;
וּמִקְרָא מְפוֹרָשׁ: ״וְגַם עַל הָעֲבָדִים וְעַל הַשְּׁפָחוֹת בַּיָּמִים הָהֵמָּה — אֶשְׁפּוֹךְ אֶת רוּחִי״ (יוֹאֵל ג:ב).
as it is explicitly written: "And also upon the servants and upon the handmaids in those days will I pour out My spirit" (Yoel 3:2).
אֲבָל מִקְרָא דְּ״לְכָל מִשְׁפְּחוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל״ דְּמַיְיתֵי הָתָם (יִרְמְיָה ל״א:א׳)... מִשּׁוּם דְּהַהוּא לַמִּשְׁפָּחוֹת הַמְיוּחָסוֹת בִּלְבַד
But the verse "unto all the families of Israel" cited there applies to pedigreed families alone;
וְעַל כֵּן דְּרָשׁוּהוּ אַהַשְׁרָאַת שְׁכִינָה בְּרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ וּנְבוּאָה
expounding it regarding the resting of the Shechinah through prophecy and the Holy Spirit;
וְשָׁם כְּתִיב סְתָם ״בֵּית יִשְׂרָאֵל״ — כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁנִּשְׁתַּנּוּ מִגֵּרִים
referring to collective Israel who are distinguished from converts;
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם גַּם הַהִיא בְּהַשְׁרָאַת רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ כְּהַאי גַּוְונָא הַבָּאָה בְּאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְעֵילָּא בְּלֹא אִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא.
denoting that divine inspiration descending purely through an awakening from Above (itaruta d'le'ila) without prior human initiative from below.
וְכָךְ הַתְחָלַת הַדַּרְגִּין דְּרַבִּי פִּנְחָס בֶּן יָאִיר שָׁם: ״בַּתּוֹרָה״
And so the beginning of Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair's ladder: "Torah brings to watchfulness";
לֹא אָמַר ״לִימּוּד״ אוֹ ״עֵסֶק בַּתּוֹרָה״ וּפְעֻלַּת הָאָדָם כְּמוֹ ״זְהִירוּת״ וּ״זְרִיזוּת״ וְהַשְּׁאָר
he did not state "study" or "toil in Torah" as a mortal deed like watchfulness and zeal;
רַק עֶצֶם הַתּוֹרָה עַצְמָהּ מְבִיאָה לִזְהִירוּת
but the essence of the Torah itself inspires watchfulness;
וְהוּא מִצַּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁנָּתַן הַתּוֹרָה לַתַּחְתּוֹנִים לְעוֹרֵר לְבָבָם
this flowing from Hashem Who bestowed the Torah to awaken human hearts.
וְכִידוּעַ עַל מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב: ״בְּכָל יוֹם בַּת קוֹל יוֹצֵאת מֵהַר חוֹרֵב וּמַכְרֶזֶת וְאוֹמֶרֶת: ׳אוֹי לָהֶם לַבְּרִיּוֹת מֵעֶלְבּוֹנָהּ שֶׁל תּוֹרָה׳״ (אָבוֹת פֶּרֶק ו׳ מִשְׁנָה ב׳)
As known regarding: "Every single day a Heavenly Voice goes forth from Mount Horeb, proclaiming: Woe to mankind for the insult to the Torah!" (Avos 6:2);
שֶׁהֵם הַהִרְהוּרִים הַנּוֹפְלִים בְּמַחְשְׁבוֹת אָדָם בְּכָל יוֹם לְעוֹרְרוֹ לְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה
these being the spontaneous thoughts awakening in man's mind daily stirring him to Torah;
וְהוּא מַה שֶּׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מְעוֹרְרוֹ בְּלֹא אִתְעָרוּתָא דִּילֵיהּ הַקּוֹדֶמֶת
Hashem awakening him without prior human initiative;
וּכְבַקָּשָׁתֵנוּ: ״הֲשִׁיבֵנוּ ה׳ אֵלֶיךָ — וְנָשׁוּבָה״ (אֵיכָה ה:כא), ״מָשְׁכֵנִי — אַחֲרֶיךָ נָּרוּצָה״ (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים א:ד).
as we pray: "Turn us unto You, Hashem, and we shall be turned" (Eichah 5:21), "Draw me, we will run after You" (Shir HaShirim 1:4).
וְלֶעָתִיד יִהְיֶה כֵּן הַמְשָׁכַת כָּל הַמַּדְרֵיגוֹת, הַכֹּל עַל יְדֵי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לְבַד
And in the Future the expansion of all rungs will be wrought directly by Hashem alone;
דְּ״בְיָד חֲזָקָה... אֶמְלוֹךְ עֲלֵיכֶם״ (יְחֶזְקֵאל כ:לג), וּבְעַל כָּרְחָם יִמְשְׁכֵם גַּם כֵּן לְעִנְיַן הַקִּיּוּם
where "with a mighty hand will I rule over you" (Yechezkel 20:33), drawing them to fulfill the law;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּיִרְמְיָה (ל״א:ל״ב): ״נָתַתִּי אֶת תּוֹרָתִי בְּקִרְבָּם וְעַל לִבָּם אֶכְתֲּבֶנָּה״
as stated in Jeremiah (31:32): "I will put My law in their inward parts, and in their heart will I write it";
כְּמוֹ שֶׁהָיָה בְּמַתַּן תּוֹרָה בִּכְפִיַּית הַר כְּגִיגִית
exactly as occurred at Sinai through coercing the mountain like a cask;
אֲבָל עַתָּה אֵין לָנוּ אֶלָּא הַתְחָלַת הָאִתְעָרוּתָא עַל יְדֵי הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁזָּכִינוּ לָהּ כְּבָר בִּשְׁעַת מַתַּן תּוֹרָה שֶׁהָיָה בִּכְפִיּוּת
but at present we possess this initial divine awakening through the Torah merited at Sinai through coercion;
וְכֵן הוּא תָּמִיד בְּכָל נֶפֶשׁ בִּפְרָט, וְזֶהוּ רַק בְּזֶרַע יִשְׂרָאֵל לְבַד:
and so it operates within every individual Jewish soul, belonging strictly unto the seed of Israel alone!

6.h: אוֹת י״ט — גִּרְסַת מִשְׁנַת סוֹטָה, רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ בְּעוֹבַדְיָה הַגֵּר, וּמַעֲלַת אַבְרָהָם הָאֶזְרָחִי — Section 19: The Variant in Sotah, Ruach HaKodesh in Obadiah the Convert, and Avraham the Native

The theme: The Sotah variant opening with watchfulness (zehirut), the Holy Spirit bestowed through moral action upon gentiles and women, and why Obadiah's praise exceeds Avraham's. The Mishnah at the end of Sotah (49b) differs: it opens directly with "watchfulness" without listing Torah, and transposes piety and holiness. Both versions are authentic: there exists a category of Holy Spirit that does not derive from Torah study, but is attained through moral deeds alone, as Tanna D'vei Eliyahu Rabbah (ch. 9) teaches: "whether gentile or Jew, man or woman, slave or maidservant, according to the deeds one performs, so does the Holy Spirit rest upon him". Gentiles, slaves, and women are not obligated in analytical Torah study (Chullin 13a; Kesubos 28a; Sotah 20a); their inspiration flows from moral action. This does not contradict Rashi in Ta'anit (4a) that the Holy Spirit does not rest upon a slave or mamzer, for Rashi refers to halachic revelation (gilui halachot). Obadiah the prophet was an Edomite convert (Sanhedrin 39b); his inspiration was achieved through his extraordinary personal striving in the fear of Heaven ("Obadiah feared Hashem greatly", I Melachim 18:3; Berachos 33b). Sanhedrin (39b) states: "Greater is that which is said of Obadiah than that which is said of Avraham!" Avraham is called the "first of converts" (Chagigah 3a), yet he was the founding father of the nation, designated "Eitan the Ezrachi" (Bava Batra 15a; Tehillim 89:1)—an ezrach (native citizen) and not a convert (ger). Divine assistance supported Avraham as the root of Israel; Obadiah, being a complete convert from Edom without inborn ancestry, had to achieve everything through monumental personal effort. In intrinsic soul-stature, Avraham incomparably surpasses Obadiah; but regarding the sheer exertion of personal striving, Obadiah's praise is greater!

p: וְהִנֵּה בְּנוּסַח הַמִּשְׁנָה דְּסוֹף סוֹטָה (מ״ט עַמּוּד ב׳) שֶׁיֵּשׁ שָׁם שִׁינּוּי וְחִילּוּף ״חֲסִידוּת״ בִּ״קְדוּשָׁה״
And behold in the Mishnah at the end of Sotah (49b), there is a textual variation transposing "piety" and "holiness";
וְיֵשׁ עוֹד שִׁינּוּי: דְּפוֹתֵחַ שָׁם בִּ״זְהִירוּת״ וְלֹא מָנָה מִקּוֹדֶם ״תּוֹרָה הַמְבִיאָה לִידֵי זְהִירוּת״, וְהֵם שָׁם עֶשֶׂר מַדְרֵיגוֹת בַּהֲדֵי רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ
and there is another variation: it opens with "watchfulness" without listing "Torah brings to watchfulness," totaling ten rungs including the Holy Spirit;
וְנִרְאֶה לִי דִּשְׁתֵּי הַנּוּסְחָאוֹת אֱמֶת, וְיֵשׁ מַדְרֵיגָה אַחֶרֶת בְּרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ שֶׁאֵין נִמְשָׁךְ בְּכֹחַ הַתּוֹרָה
and it appears to me that both textual traditions are authentic truth, there being another dimension of the Holy Spirit that is not drawn through Torah study;

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּתַנָּא דְּבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ רַבָּה (רֵישׁ פֶּרֶק ט׳): ״דְּגַם גּוֹי וְאִשָּׁה וְעֶבֶד וְשִׁפְחָה — הַכֹּל לְפִי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה שֶׁהוּא עוֹשֶׂה, כָּךְ רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ שׁוֹרָה עָלָיו״, עַיֵּין שָׁם.
as stated in Tanna D'vei Eliyahu Rabbah (ch. 9): "whether gentile or Jew, man or woman, slave or maidservant, according to the deeds he performs, so does the Holy Spirit rest upon him," see there.
וְגוֹי אֵין לוֹ שַׁיָּיכוּת לְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה שֶׁהוּא: ״מוֹרָשָׁה קְהִלַּת יַעֲקֹב״ (דְּבָרִים ל״ג:ד׳)
And a gentile has no connection with words of Torah, which is an inheritance of Jacob;
וְגַם עֶבֶד אָסוּר לְלַמְּדוֹ תוֹרָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּכְתוּבּוֹת (כ״ח סוֹף עַמּוּד א׳)
and a Canaanite slave is forbidden to be taught Torah (Kesubos 28a);
וְכֵן אִשָּׁה, אָסוּר לְלַמֵּד בִּתּוֹ תוֹרָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּסוֹטָה (כ׳ עַמּוּד א׳), וְעַל כֵּן תָּלוּ לַהּ רַק בַּמַּעֲשֶׂה.
and so a woman is not taught Torah (Sotah 20a), wherefore the Midrash conditions this inspiration strictly upon moral deeds.
וּבָזֶה לֹא קָשֶׁה מִמַּה שֶּׁכָּתַב רַשִׁ״י בְּתַעֲנִית (ד׳ סוֹף עַמּוּד א׳): דְּאֵין לָחוּשׁ שֶׁתִּשְׁרֶה רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ אַעֶבֶד וּמַמְזֵר
And through this there is no difficulty from Rashi in Ta'anit (4a) that we do not suspect the Holy Spirit resting upon a slave or mamzer;
דְּהָתָם אַרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ דְּגִילּוּי הֲלָכוֹת וְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה קָאֵי
for Rashi speaks of the Holy Spirit revealing halachic truth and Torah novellae;
וְעַל פִּי זֶה יֵשׁ לוֹמַר דְּלֹא קָשֶׁה גַּם כֵּן מִקְּרָא דְּ״וְגַם עַל הָעֲבָדִים וְגוֹמֵר״ (יוֹאֵל ג:ב)... דְּהַהוּא נַמֵּי לָאו בְּרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ דְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה
and so the verse in Yoel ("and also upon the servants, etc.") refers to moral inspiration and not halachic revelation;
וּבָזֶה יֵשׁ לוֹמַר גַּם אַגְּמָרָא דְּקִדּוּשִׁין (ע׳ סוֹף עַמּוּד ב׳): דְּהַהִיא נַמֵּי הַשְׁרָאַת שְׁכִינָה דְּגִילּוּי דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה שֶׁעָתִיד לְחַדֵּשׁ.
and so the Gemara in Kiddushin (70b) refers to the divine presence revealing original Torah novellae.
וְעוֹבַדְיָה נָבִיא לַה׳, וְגֵר אֲדוֹמִי הָיָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (ל״ט עַמּוּד ב׳), וְאֵינוֹ מִמִּשְׁפַּחַת יִשְׂרָאֵל
And Obadiah was a prophet of Hashem, yet was an Edomite convert (Sanhedrin 39b), not of Israelite lineage;
וּבֶאֱמֶת עוֹבַדְיָה קֵירֵב אֶת עַצְמוֹ בְּהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתוֹ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ: ״דְּהָיָה יָרֵא אֶת ה׳ מְאֹד״ (מְלָכִים א י״ח:ג׳)
and in truth Obadiah drew himself near through his own immense striving: "Obadiah feared Hashem greatly" (I Melachim 18:3);
וְ״הַכֹּל בִּידֵי שָׁמַיִם — חוּץ מִיִּרְאַת שָׁמַיִם״ (בְּרָכוֹת ל״ג עַמּוּד ב׳) מִקְּרָא דְּ״מָה ה׳ שֹׁאֵל מֵעִמָּךְ״, שֶׁדָּבָר זֶה הוּא רַק בְּהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת אָדָם
and "everything is in the hands of Heaven except the fear of Heaven" (Berachos 33b), which depends solely upon human effort.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין שָׁם (ל״ט עַמּוּד ב׳): ״גָּדוֹל מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּעוֹבַדְיָה — מִמַּה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּאַבְרָהָם״
And this is what the Talmud declared in Sanhedrin (39b): "Greater is that which is said of Obadiah than that which is said of Avraham!";
דְּאַבְרָהָם גַּם כֵּן נִקְרָא ״תְּחִלָּה לַגֵּרִים״ בַּחֲגִיגָה (ג׳ עַמּוּד א׳), וּבְהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת עַצְמוֹ זָכָה לְכָל מַה שֶּׁזָּכָה
for Avraham was likewise termed "the first of converts" (Chagigah 3a), meriting through his own striving all that he merited;
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם, לְפִי שֶׁהוּא זָכָה אַחַר כָּךְ לִהְיוֹת הַתְחָלַת אוּמָּה הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִית מִמֶּנּוּ
nevertheless because he became the founding father of the Israelite nation;
וְכֵן אָמְרוּ בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה ס״ג:ז׳): דְּמָצִינוּ אַבְרָהָם נִקְרָא ״יִשְׂרָאֵל״
the Midrash noting that Avraham is explicitly called "Israel";
וּבְבָבָא בַּתְרָא (ט״ו עַמּוּד א׳): ״דְּאֵיתָן הָאֶזְרָחִי (תְּהִלִּים פ״ט:א׳) — זֶה אַבְרָהָם״
and in Bava Batra (15a): "Eitan the Ezrachi is Avraham";
וְנִקְרָא ״אֶזְרָחִי״ כִּלְשׁוֹן הַכָּתוּב: ״כָּל הָאֶזְרָח בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל״ (וַיִּקְרָא כ״ג:מ״ב) שֶׁאֵינוֹ גֵּר, וְיָצָא מִכְּלַל שֵׁם ״גֵּר״ לִהְיוֹת נִקְרָא ״אֶזְרָח״
called an Ezrachi (native-born citizen, Vayikra 23:42), departing from the status of convert to be titled a native;
וּלְפִיכָךְ לֹא הוּצְרַךְ כָּל כָּךְ הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת עַצְמוֹ כְּעוֹבַדְיָה שֶׁהָיָה גֵּר גָּמוּר.
wherefore Avraham did not require such arduous personal striving as Obadiah who was a complete convert.
וְזֶהוּ דִּיּוּק הַלָּשׁוֹן: ״גָּדוֹל הַנֶּאֱמָר בְּעוֹבַדְיָה וְכוּלֵיהּ״, וְלֹא אָמַר ״דְּהָיָה גָּדוֹל בֶּאֱמֶת עוֹבַדְיָה מֵאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ״, דְּחַס וְשָׁלוֹם לְלוֹמַר כֵּן!
And notice the precise language: "Greater is that which is said of Obadiah," and not that Obadiah was intrinsically greater than Avraham, heaven forfend!

וּבֶאֱמֶת אַדְּרַבָּא, גְּדוּלָּתוֹ שֶׁל אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ הִיא שֶׁגָּרְמָה לוֹ שֶׁלֹּא הוּצְרַךְ לְהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת עַצְמוֹ כָּל כָּךְ כְּגֵרִים, רַק הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עֲזָרוֹ כַּמִּשְׁפָּט לְזֶרַע יִשְׂרָאֵל.
for on the contrary, Avraham's supreme stature was what caused that he did not need such arduous effort as converts, Hashem assisting him as fitting for the seed of Israel.
וְנִמְצָא: בְּעִנְיַן מַעֲלַת עַצְמָם בְּנַפְשׁוֹתָם הַקַּיֶּימֶת לְעוֹלְמֵי עַד — אֵין עֵרֶךְ לְעוֹבַדְיָה עִם אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ;
And thus in their essential eternal soul-stature, Obadiah bears no comparison unto Avraham Avinu;
אֲבָל מֵהַנֶּאֱמָר וּמְסֻפָּר עֲלֵיהֶם בְּעִנְיַן הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתָם כָּל אֶחָד בִּשְׁעָתוֹ בִּימֵי חַיֵּיהֶם — הוּא דְּעוֹבַדְיָה גָּדוֹל:
but regarding that which is chronicled concerning their personal striving during their lifetimes, Obadiah's praise is greater!

6.h: יִשְׂרָאֵל קְדוֹשִׁים — פֶּרֶק ו׳, סְעִיפִים כ׳–כ״ג

אוֹת כ׳ — גְּדוּלַּת אִיּוֹב וְעוֹבַדְיָה בְּהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת, קֻשְׁיַת רַשִׁ״י בְּתַעֲנִית, וְסוֹד ״לִהְיוֹת לְךָ לֵאלֹהִים וּלְזַרְעֲךָ אַחֲרֶיךָ״ — Section 20: The Striving of Job and Obadiah, Rashi's Query on Slaves/Mamzerim, and the Covenant of Pedigree

The theme: Praising converts and gentiles for immense personal striving, the pedigree required for the Shechinah, and the requirement of distinct lineage (havchanah). In Bava Batra (15b) the Talmud states: "Greater is that which is said of Job than that which is said of Abraham", which refers strictly to personal striving according to the opinion that Job was a gentile who had to exert extraordinary effort to merit the Holy Spirit. This resolves the question from Obadiah regarding Kiddushin (70b). Yet a difficulty arises on Rashi in Ta'anit (4a): why not say a slave or mamzer could achieve inspiration through exceptional personal striving? In Sanhedrin (39b), the Gemara asks why Obadiah merited prophecy, and Rashi comments that being an Edomite convert, the Shechinah ordinarily rests only upon pedigreed families of Israel, citing: "to be a God unto you, and to your seed after you" (Bereishis 17:7). In Yevamos (42a) regarding the three-month discernment period (havchanah), Rashi explains that the Shechinah rests only on confirmed legitimate lineage. The purpose of man is to be a vessel for the Shechinah, fathering children who recognize Hashem. Those born of unclarified unions are termed "rebels and transgressors" (Nedarim 20b) because they show disregard for the divine indwelling. In Yevamos (100b), Rav Pappa challenges what warning the Torah issued here, explaining the verse regarding a maidservant or gentile woman whose child takes her status and is not an Israelite. Shmuel interprets it as an independent warning within the preservation of the covenant (shemirat ha-brit) to be scrupulous regarding the holy pedigree of one's descendants!

p: וְכַיּוֹצֵא בוֹ גַּם כֵּן בְּבָבָא בַּתְרָא (ט״ו עַמּוּד ב׳): ״גָּדוֹל מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּאִיּוֹב — מִמַּה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּאַבְרָהָם״
And similarly in Bava Batra (15b): "Greater is that which is said of Job than that which is said of Abraham";
וְנִרְאֶה גַּם כֵּן רַק לְעִנְיַן הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת
and it appears this likewise applies strictly to the dimension of personal striving;
וַאֲתָאן לְמַאן דְּאָמַר הָתָם: דְּלֹא הָיָה מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל, וְעַל כֵּן הוּצְרַךְ לְהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת יְתֵירָה שֶׁיִּזְכֶּה לְרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ
aligning with the authority who maintains that Job was not an Israelite, wherefore he required extraordinary exertion to merit the Holy Spirit;
וּלְפִי זֶה לֹא קַשְׁיָא מֵעוֹבַדְיָה אַדְּקִדּוּשִׁין (ע׳ סוֹף עַמּוּד ב׳).
and according to this, the case of Obadiah poses no contradiction to the passage in Kiddushin (70b).
אֲבָל עַל דִּבְרֵי רַשִׁ״י קַשְׁיָא: דַּהֲוָה לֵיהּ לְמֵימַר גַּם שָׁם: דִּלְמָא עֶבֶד וּמַמְזֵר צַדִּיק וִירֵא שָׁמַיִם וְזָכָה בְּהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת עַצְמוֹ, וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם פָּסוּל לָבוֹא בַּקָּהָל

But upon the words of Rashi in Ta'anit (4a) it is difficult: for the Talmud should have similarly answered that perhaps the slave or mamzer was a God-fearing tzaddik who merited through his own striving, yet was disqualified from entering the congregation;
אִם לֹא דְּנֵימָא דְּעֶבֶד וּמַמְזֵר גְּרִיעֵי מִגֵּר
unless we say that a slave and a mamzer are of lower standing than a convert;
וְעַל כָּרְחָךְ אֵין כַּוָּונָתוֹ לַגְּמָרָא דְּקִדּוּשִׁין הַנִּזְכָּר
and perforce Rashi did not refer to that Gemara in Kiddushin;
וּבְמַה שֶּׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְעֵיל לֹא נִתְיַישֵּׁב, דַּהֲרֵי נְבוּאַת עוֹבַדְיָה נִכְתְּבָה בְּדִבְרֵי קַבָּלָה שֶׁהוּא כְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה וְהוּא גִּילּוּי דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה.
