and what I wrote above does not fully resolve it, seeing that Obadiah's prophecy was inscribed in the prophetic canon which is like Torah, constituting a revelation of Torah words.
וּמִיהוּ בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין שָׁם (ל״ט עַמּוּד ב׳) אָמְרוּ: ״מִפְּנֵי מַה זָכָה עוֹבַדְיָה לִנְבִיאוּת? — מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהֶחְבִּיא מֵאָה נְבִיאִים בַּמְּעָרָה וְכוּלֵיהּ״
However in Sanhedrin (39b) the Sages asked: "Why did Obadiah merit prophecy? Because he hid one hundred prophets in a cave, etc.";

וּפֵירֵשׁ רַשִׁ״י: ״שֶׁהֲרֵי גֵּר הָיָה, וְאֵין הַשְּׁכִינָה שׁוֹרָה אֶלָּא עַל הַמְיוּחָסִין שֶׁבְּיִשְׂרָאֵל, כִּדְכְתִיב: ׳לִהְיוֹת לְךָ לֵאלֹהִים וּלְזַרְעֲךָ אַחֲרֶיךָ׳ (בְּרֵאשִׁית י״ז:ז׳)״, עַד כָּאן.

and Rashi explained: "for he was a convert, and the Shechinah rests only upon the pedigreed in Israel, as it is written: 'to be a God unto you, and to your seed after you' (Bereishis 17:7)," thus far.
מְבוֹאָר טַעְמֵיהּ דְּרַשִׁ״י מִקְּרָא אַחֲרִינָא
Rashi's reason is thus explained from a different verse;
וּבְקִדּוּשִׁין מַיְיתֵי קְרָא אַלֶעָתִיד, וְגַם שָׁם אָמַר ״מִשְׁפָּחוֹת הַמְיוּחָסוֹת״
whereas in Kiddushin the Gemara cites a verse referring to the Future, and there too speaks of "pedigreed families";
וְיָלֵיף מִ״מִּשְׁפָּחוֹת״: דְּאִם נִטְמַע פְּסוּל בַּמִּשְׁפָּחָה וְנוֹגֵעַ קְצָת פְּגָם לוֹ, גַּם כֵּן אִמְעוּט, וְזֶהוּ רַק לֶעָתִיד.
deriving from "families" that if a defect was assimilated into a family casting a subtle blemish, it is excluded, which applies strictly to the Future.
וְנִרְאֶה כַּוָּונָתוֹ לְמַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בִּיבָמוֹת (מ״ב עַמּוּד א׳) לְעִנְיַן הַבְחָנָה [שְׁלֹשָׁה חֳדָשִׁים], מִשּׁוּם דְּאָמַר קְרָא: ״לִהְיוֹת לְךָ וְגוֹמֵר״
And it appears Rashi's intention was based on Yevamos (42a) regarding the three-month discernment period (havchanah), because Scripture states: "to be a God unto you, etc.";
וּפֵירֵשׁ רַשִׁ״י: ״שֶׁאֵין הַשְּׁכִינָה שׁוֹרָה אֶלָּא עַל הַוַּדָּאִים וְכוּלֵיהּ״, עַיֵּין שָׁם.
Rashi expounding there: "that the Shechinah rests only upon those of certain, legitimate lineage, etc.," see there.
וְהַיְינוּ דְּאִם לָאו הָכִי, לְאֵיזוֹ צֹרֶךְ הוּא הַבְחָנָה?
For were it not so, for what necessity would this discernment be required?
וְעַל כָּרְחָךְ דְּקָאֵי אַ״לִהְיוֹת לְךָ לֵאלֹהִים״ וְהַשְׁרָאַת שְׁכִינָה
And perforce it relates to "to be a God unto you" and the resting of the Shechinah;
וְאֵין לְהַקְשׁוֹת לְפִי זֶה: מְנָא לֵיהּ דְּחִיּוּבָא הוּא לְכָל אֶחָד?
and one cannot challenge: whence does he derive that this is an obligation upon every single individual?
דְּוַדַּאי זֶה כָּל הָאָדָם: לִהְיוֹת כְּלִי לְהַשְׁרָאַת שְׁכִינָה
For certainly this is the whole duty of man: to become a vessel for the resting of the Shechinah;
וְכָל הוֹלָדַת בָּנִים הוּא שֶׁיַּעַבְדוּ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וְיַכִּירוּ אֱלֹהוּתוֹ.
and the purpose of fathering children is that they serve the Blessed Name and acknowledge His Godliness.
וְיֵשׁ לוֹמַר הַיְינוּ נַמֵּי מַה דְּהוֹסִיף רַשִׁ״י שָׁם מֵהָא דִּנְדָרִים (כ׳ סוֹף עַמּוּד ב׳): דְּקָרֵינַן לְהוּ נַמֵּי ״מוֹרְדִים וּפוֹשְׁעִים״
And one may say this is likewise why Rashi added from Nedarim (20b) that children born without discernment are called "rebels and transgressors";
וְאֶפְשָׁר לוֹמַר דְּהַיְינוּ לְשׁוֹן: ״[וּבָרוֹתִי מִכֶּם הַמֹּרְדִים] וְהַפּוֹשְׁעִים בִּי״ (יְחֶזְקֵאל כ:לח) — שֶׁאֵין חֲפֵצִים וְחוֹשְׁשִׁים בִּי וּבְהַשְׁרָאַת שְׁכִינָתִי.
meaning: "those who transgress against Me" (Yechezkel 20:38), showing no desire or concern for Me and the indwelling of My Shechinah.
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם שָׁם בִּיבָמוֹת (ק׳ סוֹף עַמּוּד ב׳): ״הָתָם מַאי קָא מַזְהַר לֵיהּ רַחֲמָנָא? וְכוּלֵיהּ״, עַיֵּין שָׁם
And nevertheless in Yevamos (100b) the Gemara challenges: "There, what warning did the Merciful One issue? etc.," see there;
וְלֹא נִרְאֶה לֵיהּ לְעִנְיַן הַשְׁרָאַת הַשְּׁכִינָה
the Gemara not accepting this as an admonition concerning the resting of the Shechinah;
אֶפְשָׁר לוֹמַר דְּרַב פַּפָּא דְּהָתָם פָּלֵיג אַדִּשְׁמוּאֵל בְּ״הַחוֹלֵץ״ (שָׁם מ״ב עַמּוּד א׳)
it being possible that Rav Pappa disputes Shmuel in Perek HaCholetz (Yevamos 42a);
וּסְבִירָא לֵיהּ כְּרָבָא שָׁם דְּיָהֵיב טַעְמָא אַחֲרִינָא לְהַבְחָנָה [וְדִבְרֵי רַשִׁ״י בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (ל״ט עַמּוּד ב׳) — לִשְׁמוּאֵל]
aligning with Rava who provides an alternative reason for discernment [Rashi in Sanhedrin (39b) following Shmuel];
וְעַיֵּין שָׁם בְּתוֹסָפוֹת (דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל: ״לְזַרְעֲךָ״) דְּרָמְזוּ לַגְּמָרָא הַנִּזְכָּר, אוּלַי כִּוְּונוּ לָזֶה.
and see Tosafos there (s.v. L'zar'acha) who hinted unto this Gemara.
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם הַקּוּשְׁיָא ״מַאי קָא מַזְהַר״ קַשְׁיָא דְּלֹא אָמַר אַהַשְׁרָאַת שְׁכִינָה
And nevertheless the difficulty remains: why did the Gemara not explain it regarding the resting of the Shechinah?
וְעַל כָּרְחָךְ דְּלֹא מַשְׁמַע לֵיהּ קְרָא כֵּן: דְּאַטּוּ אַכָּל זַרְעוֹ יִהְיֶה הַשְׁרָאַת שְׁכִינָה בְּרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ וּנְבוּאָה?!
Perforce the verse did not imply this unto the Gemara: for would the Shechinah rest through prophecy and the Holy Spirit upon all his biological seed?!
שֶׁזֶּה יִהְיֶה רַק לֶעָתִיד דְּ״אֶשְׁפּוֹךְ [אֶת] רוּחִי עַל כָּל בָּשָׂר״ (יוֹאֵל ג:א)
seeing that this is reserved for the Future: "I will pour out My spirit upon all flesh" (Yoel 3:1);
וְהָךְ ״לִהְיוֹת לְךָ לֵאלֹהִים״ הַיְינוּ כְּמוֹ ״אָנֹכִי ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ״ (שְׁמוֹת כ:ב) וְכַדּוֹמֶה הַרְבֵּה מִקְרָאוֹת
while "to be a God unto you" denotes the covenant of faith, like "I am Hashem your God" (Shemos 20:2);
וְזֶה וַדַּאי גַּם מִי שֶׁאֵין זַרְעוֹ מְיוּחָס אַחֲרָיו בִּכְלָל, דְּאַטּוּ לָאו יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא?!
and this certainly includes anyone whose seed is not legitimately pedigreed, for is he not an Israelite?!
וְעַל כֵּן פָּרִיךְ וּמְשַׁנֵּי: ״בְּשִׁפְחָה וְגוֹיָה, דִּוְלָדָהּ כְּמוֹתָהּ וְלָאו יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא״ (יְבָמוֹת ק׳ סוֹף עַמּוּד ב׳)
Wherefore the Gemara asks and resolves: "regarding a bondwoman and a gentile woman, whose offspring has her legal status and is not an Israelite" (Yevamos 100b);
וְאֶפְשָׁר הַדְּרָשׁ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל בְּ״הַחוֹלֵץ״: דְּזֶה אַזְהָרָה בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָהּ לְעִנְיַן הֲקָמַת הַבְּרִית שֶׁהִיא בִּשְׁמִירַת הַבְּרִית
and perhaps Shmuel's exposition is an independent warning regarding establishing the covenant:
גַּם זֶה מִכְּלַל שְׁמִירַת הַבְּרִית: שֶׁיְּדַקְדֵּק בְּיִחוּס זַרְעוֹ, וְדָחוּק:
that part of guarding the covenant is being scrupulously vigilant regarding the legitimate pedigree of one's seed, though this explanation is strained!
אוֹת כ״א — מַחֲלוֹקֶת רַבִּי מֵאִיר וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אִם ״קְרוּיִין בָּנִים״, דִּמְעַת הָעֲשׁוּקִים דְּמַמְזֵרִים, וְנִבְלִימַת הַנְּבוּאָה אַחַר מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ
Section 21: Are Sinners Called Sons?, The Tears of the Oppressed, and Gentile Prophecy Restricted after Moshe

6.h: The theme: Whether transgressors are termed "sons", the status of a mamzer, and how gentile prophecy ceased after Moshe Rabbeinu. Rashi’s phrase "the Shechinah does not rest" can be interpreted not as prophetic inspiration, but as Hashem being termed their God, since unpedigreed offspring fall under the category of rebels and transgressors. This mirrors the dispute between Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehudah in Kiddushin (36a): whether Israel are called "sons" when they do not conduct themselves as sons. Rabbi Yehudah derives from Hoshea: "you are not My people, and I will not be your God" (Hoshea 1:9), wherefore "to be a God unto you" does not apply to rebels. Yet if a child of flawed parentage is righteous, how is he inferior to a convert? A mamzer suffers because of his ancestors' sin—"the tears of such as were oppressed, and they had no comforter" (Koheles 4:1; Vayikra Rabbah 32:8)—being lower than a convert who is born anew without past lineage. In Ta'anit (4a), a slave and mamzer are excluded because their ancestry is tainted. Furthermore, gentile prophets existed even after Avraham (such as Balaam), and in Berachos (7a) the Talmud explains that Moshe Rabbeinu prayed that the Shechinah not rest upon the nations, which was granted after his death (Bava Batra 15b). In Tanna D'vei Eliyahu Rabbah (ch. 9), the Holy Spirit rests upon gentiles according to their deeds; this refers to moral inspiration, whereas Moshe's prayer eliminated visionary prophecy revealing Torah and biblical canon (such as Balaam's prophecies and the Book of Job)!

p: וְכַוָּונַת רַשִׁ״י ״שֶׁאֵין הַשְּׁכִינָה שׁוֹרָה״ יֵשׁ לְפָרֵשׁ גַּם כֵּן: לָאו אַהַשְׁרָאַת נְבוּאָה וְרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ
And Rashi's meaning that "the Shechinah does not rest" can likewise be interpreted: not referring to prophecy and the Holy Spirit;
אֶלָּא לְעִנְיָן שֶׁיְּהֵא נִקְרָא ״ה׳ אֱלֹהָיו״, וּמִשּׁוּם דְּהֵם בִּכְלַל הַמּוֹרְדִים וְהַפּוֹשְׁעִים.
but regarding whether Hashem is titled "his God," seeing that they are accounted among the rebels and transgressors.
וְאֶפְשָׁר דְּתַלְיָא בִּפְלוּגְתָּא דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּקִדּוּשִׁין (ל״ו עַמּוּד א׳): ״כְּשֶׁאֵין נוֹהֲגִין מִנְהַג בָּנִים — אֵין קְרוּיִין בָּנִים״
And perhaps this hinges upon the dispute between Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehudah in Kiddushin (36a): whether when they do not conduct themselves as sons they are called sons;
דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר מַיְיתֵי: ״[וְהָיָה] בִּמְקוֹם אֲשֶׁר יֵאָמֵר [לָהֶם: לֹא עַמִּי אַתֶּם, יֵאָמֵר לָהֶם: בְּנֵי אֵל חָי]״ (הוֹשֵׁעַ ב:א)
Rabbi Meir deriving that they remain sons from: "in the place where it was said unto them: You are not My people, there it shall be said unto them: You are the sons of the living God" (Hoshea 2:1);
וְיֵשׁ לוֹמַר דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה סְבִירָא לֵיהּ: הַהוּא — לֶעָתִיד
while Rabbi Yehudah maintains that this reconciliation applies strictly to the Future;
וְהוּא דָּיֵיק מֵרֵישֵׁיהּ בְּהוֹשֵׁעַ שָׁם: שֶׁאָמַר ״כִּי אַתֶּם לֹא עַמִּי, וְאָנֹכִי לֹא אֶהְיֶה לָכֶם״ (שָׁם א:ט)
deducing from the preceding verse in Hoshea: "for you are not My people, and I will not be your God" (Hoshea 1:9);
וְעַל כֵּן לָא קָרֵינַן גַּבֵּי מוֹרְדִים וּפוֹשְׁעִים ״לִהְיוֹת לָכֶם לֵאלֹהִים״, אַף דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא.
wherefore regarding rebels we do not apply "to be a God unto you," even though he is an Israelite.
אֲבָל לְפִי זֶה קָשֶׁה דִּבְרֵיהֶם דְּסַנְהֶדְרִין שָׁם: וְתֵינַח הָתָם דַּהֲוָה לֵיהּ ״בְּנֵי עַרְבּוּבְיָא״ דְּקָרֵי לְהוּ מוֹרְדִים
But according to this, the passage in Sanhedrin (39b) remains difficult: granted that children of unclarified unions are termed rebels;
אִי לָא קָרֵינַן גַּבַּיְיהוּ ״וְשָׁכַנְתִּי בְּתוֹכָם״ (שְׁמוֹת כ״ה:ח׳) בִּכְלָל, כָּל שֶׁכֵּן הַשְׁרָאַת רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ וּנְבוּאָה
if we do not apply unto them "and I will dwell among them" (Shemos 25:8), how much less the resting of the Holy Spirit and prophecy!
וְגַם בָּזֶה יֵשׁ לְעַיֵּין: אִם הַבֵּן צַדִּיק, מִי גָּרַע מִגּוֹי הַמִּתְגַּיֵּיר?!
And herein one must analyze: if the son is a righteous tzaddik, how is he inferior to a converting gentile?!
וּמַה יַּעֲשֶׂה אִם אֲבוֹתָיו חָטְאוּ חֵטְא קַל דְּהַבְחָנָה?!
And what could he do if his parents committed the minor infraction of neglecting the three-month discernment?!
וְאוּלַי זֶה בִּכְלַל: ״[וְהִנֵּה] דִּמְעַת הָעֲשֻׁקִים — וְאֵין לָהֶם מְנַחֵם״ (קֹהֶלֶת ד:א), שֶׁדָּרְשׁוּ בְּמִדְרַשׁ קֹהֶלֶת (פָּרָשָׁה ד׳:א׳) עַל מַמְזֵרִים
And perhaps this is included within: "and behold the tears of such as were oppressed, and they had no comforter" (Koheles 4:1), expounded in Midrash Koheles regarding mamzerim;
וּגְרִיעֵי מִגֵּר, דִּכְקָטָן שֶׁנּוֹלַד (יְבָמוֹת כ״ב עַמּוּד א׳) וְאֵין לוֹ אָבוֹת כְּלָל
being lower than a convert, who is like a newborn child without ancestral defect;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן זֶה דְּמִיִּשְׂרָאֵל, וְחַטַּאת אֲבוֹתָיו גָּרְמוּ לוֹ חִסָּרוֹן בְּשָׁרְשׁוֹ.
whereas this child derives from Israel, and the sin of his ancestors caused a defect in his root.
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם תֵּינַח לִלְמוֹד מִזֶּה לְעֶבֶד וּמַמְזֵר דִּבְתַעֲנִית (ד׳ עַמּוּד א׳), דְּגַם כֵּן אֵין נְקִיִּים אַגַּב אִמָּם וַאֲבוֹתָם
Nevertheless, this explains the exclusion of a slave and mamzer in Ta'anit (4a) whose lineage is tainted by their parents;
וְכֵן אָמְרוּ בְּיוֹמָא (פ״ז עַמּוּד א׳): ״אוֹי לָרְשָׁעִים שֶׁמְּחַיְּיבִים לִבְנֵיהֶם... שֶׁהַרְבֵּה בָנִים הָיוּ לוֹ לִכְנַעַן וְכוּלֵיהּ״, עַיֵּין שָׁם;
as stated in Yoma (87a): "Woe to the wicked who cause guilt unto their children... Canaan had many sons, etc.";
אֲבָל גֵּר שֶׁנִּתְגַּיֵּיר, אַחַר שֶׁקֵּירֵב — קָרֵינַן בֵּיהּ דְּהָיָה לוֹ ה׳ לֵאלֹהִים, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּקִדּוּשִׁין (ע׳ סוֹף עַמּוּד ב׳), וְאֵיךְ מְמַעֲטִינַן מֵהַאי קְרָא גֵּר?!
but a convert who drew near, we certainly apply unto him that Hashem is his God (Kiddushin 70b), so how could Rashi exclude a convert from this verse?!
וּבְלָאו הָכִי נַמֵּי, הֲרֵי אֲפִילּוּ גּוֹיִם לֹא נִתְמַעֲטוּ מִנְּבוּאָה גַּם אַחַר אַבְרָהָם, שֶׁהָיוּ נְבִיאֵי אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם
And aside from this, even gentiles were not excluded from prophecy after Avraham, there being prophets of the nations;
וּבִבְרָכוֹת (ז׳ עַמּוּד א׳) מַשְׁמַע: דְּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הוּא שֶׁבִּקֵּשׁ שֶׁלֹּא תִּשְׁרֶה שְׁכִינָה עַל אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם וְנִיתַּן לוֹ;
and in Berachos (7a) it is implied that Moshe Rabbeinu petitioned that the Shechinah not rest upon the nations, and it was granted;
וּבְבָבָא בַּתְרָא (ט״ו עַמּוּד ב׳) אִיתָא: דְּמִכִּי שָׁכֵיב מֹשֶׁה לֹא אִתְנַבּוּ עוֹד מֵאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם, דְּלֹא נִיתַּן לוֹ רַק לְאַחַר מוֹתוֹ
and in Bava Batra (15b): from when Moshe passed away the nations prophesied no more, it being granted only after his death;
וּמִשּׁוּם דְּמָצִינוּ אַחֲרֵי זֶה בְּסוֹף יָמָיו נִתְנַבֵּא בִּלְעָם.
because at the end of Moshe's life Balaam still prophesied.
וְגַם זֶה צָרִיךְ לוֹמַר: רַק בִּנְבוּאָה וְלֹא בְּרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ, דְּלֹא תִּקְשֶׁה הַהוּא דְּתַנָּא דְּבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ (פֶּרֶק ט׳) הַנִּזְכָּר;
And this must refer strictly to visionary prophecy and not to the Holy Spirit, so as not to contradict Tanna D'vei Eliyahu (ch. 9);

דְּדָחוּק לוֹמַר דְּקָאֵי כְּפִי מַה שֶּׁהוּא רָאוּי מִצַּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וּכְמוֹ שֶׁהָיָה מִקַּמֵּי תְּפִלַּת מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, דְּהַלָּשׁוֹן מַשְׁמַע שֶׁהוּא בַּהֹוֶה כֵּן גַּם עַכְשָׁיו וּבְיָמָיו.
for the text clearly implies that this inspiration operates in the present era as well.
וְעַל כָּרְחָךְ כֵּיוָן דִּכְפִי הַנּוּסְחָא דְּסוֹף סוֹטָה (מ״ט עַמּוּד ב׳): ״חֲסִידוּת מְבִיאָה לִידֵי רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ״, וּמָצִינוּ ״חֲסִידֵי אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם״ (סַנְהֶדְרִין ק״ה עַמּוּד א׳)
And perforce since the text of Sotah (49b) states that piety brings to the Holy Spirit, and we find "the pious of the nations of the world" (Sanhedrin 105a);
וְעַיֵּין שָׁם בְּרַשִׁ״י (ק״י סוֹף עַמּוּד ב׳ דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל: ״אֲבָל״): לְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ יֵשׁ חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא גַּם כֵּן
see Rashi there (110b) that according to Rabbi Yehoshua they possess a portion in the World to Come;
וְשַׁיָּיךְ בְּהוּ חֲסִידוּת — שַׁיָּיךְ בְּהוּ רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ גַּם כֵּן.
and where piety applies, a measure of the Holy Spirit applies as well.
אֶלָּא דְּיֵשׁ לוֹמַר דְּהַהוּא עַל כָּרְחָךְ לָאו בְּרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ דְּגִילּוּי דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, דַּהֲרֵי אֵין תּוֹרָה בְּאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם;
Except that this is certainly not the Holy Spirit revealing words of Torah, there being no Torah among the nations;
וְיֵשׁ לְפָרֵשׁ: בַּקָּשַׁת מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הָיָה בְּהַשְׁרָאַת שְׁכִינָה בְּגִילּוּי דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה
and one may explain: Moshe Rabbeinu's petition was that the Shechinah not rest upon gentiles in the revelation of Torah teachings;
כִּנְבוּאַת בִּלְעָם שֶׁנִּכְתַּב בַּתּוֹרָה וְהוּא דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, וּדְאִיּוֹב שֶׁהוּא דִּבְרֵי קַבָּלָה.
such as Balaam's prophecy inscribed in the Torah, and Job's words in the sacred writings.
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם נִרְאֶה נַמֵּי דְּדַוְוקָא ״נְבוּאָה״ אָמַר וְלֹא ״רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ״
And nevertheless it appears that Moshe specifically prayed regarding visionary prophecy and not the Holy Spirit;

וְעַל כָּל פָּנִים אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא דְּגַם רַשִׁ״י שָׁם דַּוְוקָא בִּנְבוּאָה קָאֵי, הֲרֵי מִיהַת הָיָה הַשְׁרָאַת נְבוּאָה גַּם כֵּן אַחַר אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁלֹּא מִזַּרְעוֹ כְּלָל
and even if Rashi refers strictly to prophecy, there existed prophetic inspiration after Avraham among those not of his seed;
וּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הוּצְרַךְ לְהִתְפַּלֵּל עַל זֶה, וְלֹא הֻבְטַח אַבְרָהָם בְּכָךְ כְּלָל;
Moshe having to pray for its cessation, Avraham never being promised that gentile prophecy would cease;
וְעַל כָּרְחָךְ דְּהַהִיא רַק ״לִהְיוֹת לֵאלֹהִים״, וּנְבִיאֵי אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם גַּם כֵּן לֹא נִקְרְאוּ עַמּוֹ:
and perforce that promise to Avraham meant Hashem being their God, while gentile prophets were never designated His covenantal people!
אוֹת כ״ב — הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּבִכּוּרִים: ״אַב הֲמוֹן גּוֹיִם״, יְנִיקַת הַגֵּרִים מֵאַבְרָהָם, וְהַתְּנָאִים שֶׁל נְבוּאָה מוּל רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ
Section 22: The Halachah of Converts in Bikkurim, Seed vs. Children, and Conditions of Prophecy vs. Ruach HaKodesh

6.h: The theme: Converts reciting "the God of our fathers" according to Rabbi Yehudah, the textual definition of zera versus banim, and halachic inspiration in poor and weak scholars. In Yerushalmi Bikkurim (1:4; Tosafos, Bava Batra 81a), the Halachah follows Rabbi Yehudah that a convert brings first-fruits and recites: "which Hashem swore unto our fathers," because Avraham is "the father of a multitude of nations" (Bereishis 17:5). If so, converts are included in Avraham's seed! However, Avraham is called a "father" in wisdom (Megillah 13a), like Elisha crying "My father, my father" (II Melachim 2:12), disciples being called "sons"; yet the term "seed" (zera) applies strictly to biological descendants. Regarding a slave and mamzer, they are excluded from the unqualified term "seed" (Kiddushin 4a; Sanhedrin 64b); though in Kiddushin (67b) the Sages expound "unto his seed after him" to include both fit and unfit seed, Tosafos and Ritva explain that zera includes whoever is legally traced to him. Rashi in Ta'anit (4a) bases his exclusion on Nedarim (38a): all prophets must be wise, mighty, and wealthy, derived from Moshe ("a prophet like me", Devarim 18:15). Obadiah prophesied only against Edom ("from the forest itself comes the axe-handle", Sanhedrin 39b), not unto Israel. Furthermore, these qualifications of wealth and physical strength apply strictly to visionary prophecy; the Holy Spirit of halachic wisdom requires neither wealth nor physical strength! Many Tannaim and Amoraim were impoverished—such as Rabbi Elazar ben Pedat (Ta'anit 25a) and Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa—or physically weak (Nedarim 49b; Sanhedrin 26b), Othniel ben Kenaz being poor (Temurah 16a). Rashi in Ta'anit derived from Nedarim that lineage (yichus) is required even for the Holy Spirit!

p: וְגַם יֵשׁ לְעַיֵּין: דְּבַיְרוּשַׁלְמִי פֶּרֶק א׳ דְּבִכּוּרִים (הֲלָכָה ד׳) וְהוּבָא בְּתוֹסָפוֹת בָּבָא בַּתְרָא (פ״א עַמּוּד א׳ דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל: ״לְמַעוּטֵי״)
And also one must analyze: for in Yerushalmi Bikkurim (1:4), cited by Tosafos in Bava Batra (81a);
אָמְרוּ: ״דַּהֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה: דְּגֵר יָכוֹל לוֹמַר: ׳[לַאֲבֹתֵינוּ]׳, דְּאַבְרָהָם ׳אַב הֲמוֹן גּוֹיִם׳ (בְּרֵאשִׁית י״ז:ה׳)״

the Sages ruled: "the Halachah follows Rabbi Yehudah that a convert brings first-fruits and recites 'which Hashem swore unto our fathers,' for Avraham is 'the father of a multitude of nations' (Bereishis 17:5)";
אִם כֵּן נֵימָא: דְּהַגֵּרִים גַּם כֵּן בִּכְלַל ״זַרְעוֹ אַחֲרָיו״ דְּאַבְרָהָם?!
if so, shall we say that converts are likewise included within "his seed after him" of Avraham?!
דְּאֵין לוֹמַר דְּתַלְמוּדָא דִּידַן דְּסַנְהֶדְרִין שָׁם (ל״ט עַמּוּד ב׳) סְבִירָא לְהוּ כִּסְתַם מִשְׁנָה דְּבִכּוּרִים (פֶּרֶק א׳ מִשְׁנָה ד׳) וְלֹא כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
For one cannot say our Babylonian Talmud in Sanhedrin (39b) holds like the anonymous Mishnah in Bikkurim (1:4) against Rabbi Yehudah;
דְּאִם כֵּן אַמַּאי פָּסְקוּ תּוֹסָפוֹת וְכֵן הָרַמְבַּ״ם (הִלְכוֹת בִּכּוּרִים פֶּרֶק ד׳ הֲלָכָה ג׳) וְהָרַ״שׁ כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְכַיְרוּשַׁלְמִי נֶגֶד תַּלְמוּדָא דִּידַן?!
for if so, why did Tosafos, Rambam (Bikkurim 4:3), and the Rash rule like Rabbi Yehudah and the Yerushalmi against our Talmud?!
וּמִיהוּ עַל זֶה יֵשׁ לוֹמַר: דִּנְהִי דְּהוּא דִּקְרָאוֹ ״אָב״
Yet regarding this one may answer: granted that Scripture designates Avraham a "father";
דְּמָצִינוּ בִּמְגִלָּה (י״ג עַמּוּד א׳): ״אָב בַּתּוֹרָה, אָב בְּחָכְמָה״, וְכֵן אֱלִישָׁע מְצַעֵק: ״אָבִי אָבִי״ (מְלָכִים ב ב:יב)
finding in Megillah (13a): "a father in Torah, a father in wisdom", and Elisha crying: "My father, my father" (II Melachim 2:12);
וְאַף הֵם שַׁיָּיךְ לִקְרוֹתָם ״בָּנִים״, דְּמָצִינוּ הַתַּלְמִידִים נִקְרְאוּ ״בָּנִים״ כְּמוֹ ״בְּנֵי הַנְּבִיאִים״ (שָׁם:ג׳)
and disciples are called sons, as in "the sons of the prophets" (ibid. 2:3);
וְגַם הַגֵּרִים הַהוֹלְכִים בְּעִקְּבוֹת אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁהָיָה ״תְּחִלָּה לַגֵּרִים״ (חֲגִיגָה ג׳ עַמּוּד א׳)
and so converts walking in the footsteps of Avraham who was the first of converts (Chagigah 3a);
מִכָּל מָקוֹם ״זַרְעוֹ״ לֹא נִקְרָא אֶלָּא הַיּוֹצֵא מִזַּרְעוֹ דַּוְוקָא.
nevertheless "his seed" (zaro) is applied strictly to his biological offspring.
וְעַל כָּל פָּנִים אֶפְשָׁר לוֹמַר גַּם בְּדִבְרֵי רַשִׁ״י דְּתַעֲנִית (ד׳ עַמּוּד א׳): דְּכִוֵּון לְהָךְ דְּרָשָׁה מִ״וּלְזַרְעֲךָ אַחֲרֶיךָ״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית י״ז:ז׳) — דְּעֶבֶד לָאו זַרְעוֹ
And at all events one may say regarding Rashi in Ta'anit (4a): he referred to this exposition from "and to your seed after you," a slave not being his seed;
וְכֵן מַמְזֵר אֵינוֹ בִּכְלַל סְתָם לְשׁוֹן ״זֶרַע״, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּקִדּוּשִׁין (ד׳ עַמּוּד א׳) וּבְסַנְהֶדְרִין (ס״ד עַמּוּד ב׳): ״אֵין לִי אֶלָּא זֶרַע כָּשֵׁר, זֶרַע פָּסוּל מִנַּיִן?״
and so a mamzer is excluded from the unqualified term "seed" (Kiddushin 4a; Sanhedrin 64b);
וּמִיהוּ בְּקִדּוּשִׁין (ס״ז עַמּוּד ב׳) דָּרְשִׁינַן: ״׳וּלְזַרְעוֹ אַחֲרָיו׳ — בֵּין זֶרַע כָּשֵׁר בֵּין זֶרַע פָּסוּל״
though in Kiddushin (67b) the Sages expound: "'and to his seed after him'—whether legitimate seed or illegitimate seed";

וּלְפִי תֵּירוּץ הַתּוֹסָפוֹת שָׁם (דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל: ״וּלְזַרְעוֹ״) נִיחָא: דְּגַם כָּאן אִיכָּא בָּנוֹת שֶׁהֵם בִּכְלַל הַשְׁרָאַת שְׁכִינָה, דְּהָא הָיוּ שֶׁבַע נְבִיאוֹת (מְגִלָּה י״ד עַמּוּד א׳);
and according to Tosafos there (s.v. U-l'zaro) this is resolved: for daughters are included in the resting of the Shechinah, there being seven female prophets (Megillah 14a);
וְגַם אִי כְּתִיב ״לְבָנֶיךָ״ הָיָה מַשְׁמַע גַּם גֵּרִים לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן מִלְּשׁוֹן ״זֶרַע״ אִמְעוּטוּ.
and had it written "to your sons," it would have included converts according to Rabbi Yehudah, whereas from "seed" they are excluded.
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם אֶפְשָׁר לְקַיֵּים הַגִּרְסָא בְּרַשִׁ״י כִּדְאָמְרִינַן בִּנְדָרִים (ל״ח עַמּוּד א׳): וְכַוָּונָתוֹ: דְּשָׁם אָמְרוּ: ״וְכוּלָּן — מִמֹּשֶׁה״
And nevertheless one can uphold the received text of Rashi citing Nedarim (38a): his intention being that the Talmud states there: "and all of these qualifications derive from Moshe";

וְנִרְאֶה הַטַּעַם דְּיָלְפִינַן מִמֹּשֶׁה לִהְיוֹת כְּמוֹתוֹ דַּוְוקָא, הַיְינוּ מִלְּשׁוֹן הַכָּתוּב בְּפָרָשַׁת שֹׁפְטִים: ״נָבִיא מִקִּרְבְּךָ מֵאַחֶיךָ כָּמֹנִי יָקִים לְךָ... נָבִיא אָקִים לָהֶם מִקֶּרֶב אֲחֵיהֶם כָּמוֹךָ״ (דְּבָרִים י״ח:ט״ו, י״ח)

and the reason we derive from Moshe that a prophet must be specifically like him is from Parashat Shoftim: "A prophet will Hashem your God raise up unto you, from the midst of you, of your brethren, like unto me... I will raise them up a prophet from among their brethren, like unto you" (Devarim 18:15, 18);

וַהֲרֵי דְּבַפָּרָשַׁת הַנָּבִיא שֶׁהִבְטִיחַ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לְהָקִים וְצִוָּוה לִשְׁמוֹעַ לוֹ, פֵּירֵשׁ בְּהֶדְיָא שֶׁיִּהְיֶה כְּמוֹהוּ דְּמֹשֶׁה, וּמִזֶּה נִתְמַעֵט גַּם גֵּר וְעֶבֶד וּמַמְזֵר.
for in the passage of the prophet whom Hashem promised to raise and commanded to obey, Scripture explicitly specifies that he be "like Moshe," wherefrom are excluded a convert, a slave, and a mamzer.

וְעוֹבַדְיָה שֶׁהָיָה גֵּר, יֵשׁ לוֹמַר: כֵּיוָן דְּלֹא נִתְנַבֵּא אֶלָּא עַל אֱדוֹם וּמִשּׁוּם: ״מִינֵיהּ וּבֵיהּ אַבָּא [לֵיזִיל בֵּיהּ נַרְגָּא]״, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין שָׁם (ל״ט עַמּוּד ב׳)
And Obadiah who was a convert: since he prophesied strictly against Edom, based on the principle "from the forest itself comes the axe-handle" (Sanhedrin 39b);
אֵינוֹ בִּכְלַל הַכָּתוּב דְּ״יָקִים לְךָ״ וְ״אָקִים לָהֶם״, דְּהַיְינוּ לְהִתְנַבֵּא לְיִשְׂרָאֵל דַּוְוקָא.
he does not fall under "raise up unto you" and "raise unto them," which commands one prophesying unto Israel.
וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּרַשִׁ״י אַרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ קָאֵי
And even though Rashi in Ta'anit speaks of the Holy Spirit;
דִּבִנְבוּאָה לֹא יָכוֹל לְגַלּוֹת אוֹתָן הֲלָכוֹת, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ שָׁם בִּתְמוּרָה (ט״ז עַמּוּד א׳): ״דְּאֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לְחַדֵּשׁ דָּבָר״
for through visionary prophecy one cannot reveal halachic jurisprudence, a prophet being forbidden to innovate anything (Temurah 16a);
וְהָנֵי תְּנָאִים דִּנְדָרִים (ל״ח עַמּוּד א׳) נִרְאֶה וַדַּאי דְּאֵינָם אֶלָּא בִּנְבוּאָה
and those conditions in Nedarim (38a) certainly apply to visionary prophecy alone;
דִּלְרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ אֵין צָרִיךְ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה עָשִׁיר וְגִבּוֹר, וְכָל חַכְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הָאֲמִיתִּיִּים — הַתַּנָּאִים וְאָמוֹרָאִים — הִשִּׂיגוּ לְרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ זֶה שֶׁעַל דֶּרֶךְ הַחָכְמָה
for unto the Holy Spirit a sage need not be wealthy or physically mighty, all authentic Tannaim and Amoraim having attained this Holy Spirit through wisdom (Bava Batra 12a);

(וְכֵן מַשְׁמַע מִדִּבְרֵי רַשִׁ״י הַנִּזְכָּרִים: דִּפְשִׁיטָא לֵיהּ דְּמַה דְּאַהְדַּר עָתְנִיאֵל בְּפִלְפּוּלוֹ הוּא בְּרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ, מִיהוּ הָתָם לְכַוֵּון מַה שֶּׁהוּא הֲלָכָה לְמֹשֶׁה מִסִּינַי זֶה וַדַּאי אִי אֶפְשָׁר רַק בְּרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ)
(and so Rashi implies: that Othniel ben Kenaz restoring forgotten laws through pilpul was through the Holy Spirit, aligning with Sinai being impossible otherwise);
וְהַרְבֵּה מֵהֶם הָיוּ עֲנִיִּים גְּדוֹלִים, כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן פְּדָת בְּתַעֲנִית (כ״ה עַמּוּד א׳) שֶׁזָּכָה לְגִילּוּי שְׁכִינָה בַּחֲלוֹם, וְכֵן רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן דּוֹסָא עַיֵּין שָׁם;
and many of them were desperately poor, like Rabbi Elazar ben Pedat (Ta'anit 25a) who merited a revelation of the Shechinah in a dream, and Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa;
וְאַף שֶׁאָמַר עַל עַצְמוֹ בִּבְרָכוֹת (ל״ד עַמּוּד ב׳): ״לֹא נָבִיא אָנֹכִי וְכוּלֵיהּ״, הַיְינוּ נְבוּאָה, אֲבָל זָכָה לְרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ
and though Rabbi Chanina stated: "I am no prophet" (Berachos 34b), this excluded visionary prophecy, while he merited the Holy Spirit;

וְכָל שֶׁכֵּן לְעִנְיַן הַגְּבוּרָה, שֶׁהֲרֵי אִיתָא בִּנְדָרִים (מ״ט רֵישׁ עַמּוּד ב׳): ״מְרֵיעֵי רַבָּנַן״, וּבְרַשִׁ״י בִּבְרָכוֹת (כ״ב עַמּוּד א׳ דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל: ״אֶפְשָׁר״): ״דִּסְתָם תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים — חוֹלִים״, וּבְסַנְהֶדְרִין (כ״ו עַמּוּד ב׳): ״שֶׁמַּתֶּשֶׁת כֹּחוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם״.

and all the more so regarding physical strength, for Nedarim (49b) states that scholars are frail, Rashi in Berachos (22a) notes that scholars are sickly, and Sanhedrin (26b) states that Torah study weakens human physical strength.

וְעַל כָּרְחָךְ דְּלֹא אָמְרוּ אֶלָּא בְּנָבִיא, יֵשׁ לוֹמַר: דִּסְבִירָא לֵיהּ לְרַשִׁ״י הָא דְּנָקַט בִּנְדָרִים שָׁם (ל״ח עַמּוּד א׳) רַק הָנֵי [חָכָם, גִּבּוֹר, עָשִׁיר, עָנָו] וְלֹא אָמַר גַּם כֵּן הָא דְּיִהְיֶה מִמְּיוּחָסִים שֶׁבְּיִשְׂרָאֵל
And perforce since those physical conditions apply to a prophet alone, one must say that Rashi reasoned: Nedarim (38a) listed wisdom, might, wealth, and humility, omitting lineage;
וְעַל כָּרְחָךְ מִשּׁוּם דְּהָנֵי תְּנָאִים רַק בִּנְבוּאָה, אֲבָל הָא דְּיִחוּס הָוֵי גַּם לְרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ, עַל כֵּן לֹא מַנְיַיְהוּ הָתָם
because those conditions apply strictly to visionary prophecy, while legitimate pedigree is required for the Holy Spirit as well, wherefore Nedarim omitted it;
וְשַׁפִּיר לָמַד מֵהַגְּמָרָא דִּנְדָרִים דְּהָתָם דְּגַם לְרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ צָרִיךְ יִחוּס, וּבְסַנְהֶדְרִין הִמְצִיא לוֹ הַדְּרָשָׁה מִ״וּלְזַרְעֲךָ אַחֲרֶיךָ״ כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּיבָמוֹת:
and Rashi properly derived from Nedarim that the Holy Spirit requires pedigree, while in Sanhedrin he provided the exposition from "and to your seed after you" as expounded in Yevamos!

6.h: אוֹת כ״ג — ״מִקֶּרֶב אַחֶיךָ״ לְמַעֵט גֵּר וְעֶבֶד וּמַמְזֵר, מִמֻּבְחָר שֶׁבְּאַחֶיךָ, וְהַבְטָחַת הַנְּבוּאָה לְיִשְׂרָאֵל — Section 23: "From Among Your Brethren" to Exclude Converts, Slaves, and Mamzerim, and the Royal Standard

The theme: The biblical requirement of "from among your brethren" applied to kings and prophets, and the Torah's exclusion of foreign prophecy. One can interpret the requirement of pedigree as explicitly stated in the biblical text: "from the midst of your brethren" (mi-kerev achecha, Devarim 18:15). In Bava Kamma (88a), the Sages expound regarding a king: "from among your brethren shall you set a king over you—from the choice of your brethren (mi-muvchar she-b'achecha)", excluding a convert, a slave, and likewise a mamzer. The Tosefta (cited in Hagahot Maimoniyot, Hilchos Melachim ch. 1) rules that a king is appointed only from families eligible to marry into the priesthood; and the same applies to a prophet, concerning whom identical terminology is written ("from among their brethren like you", Devarim 18:18). In Sifrei Shoftim (§175): "'from the midst of you'—and not from outside the Land; 'of your brethren'—and not from others", meaning gentiles. Furthermore, this verse was not merely a promise to Moshe that the Shechinah not rest upon the nations; for without Moshe's prayer, gentile prophets would have prophesied unto the nations. The verse "a prophet will Hashem your God raise up unto you" means a prophet destined to prophesy unto Israel, establishing from the outset that Hashem will never commission a prophet unto Israel who does not descend from legitimate Jewish ancestry!

p: וּמִיהוּ אֵינוֹ מוּכְרָח, דְּיֵשׁ לוֹמַר: הָתָם מָנֵי רַק מַה דְּיָלְפִינַן מִ״כָּמוֹךָ״ וּמִמֹּשֶׁה וְלֹא אִתְפָּרַשׁ
However, this is not definitive, for one may say: Nedarim (38a) enumerated only that which is derived implicitly from "like you" and from Moshe;
אֲבָל יִחוּס מְפוֹרָשׁ בְּגוּפֵיהּ דִּקְרָא: ״מִקֶּרֶב אַחֵיהֶם״ (דְּבָרִים י״ח:י״ח).
whereas legitimate pedigree is explicitly stated in the very body of the verse: "from among their brethren" (Devarim 18:18).
וּבְבָבָא קַמָּא (פ״ח עַמּוּד א׳) דָּרְשִׁינַן: ״׳מִקֶּרֶב אַחֶיךָ [תָּשִׂים עָלֶיךָ מֶלֶךְ]׳ (דְּבָרִים י״ז:ט״ו) — מִמּוּבְחָר שֶׁבְּאַחֶיךָ״, לְמַעֵט גֵּר וְעֶבֶד, וְהָכִי נַמֵּי מַמְזֵר

And in Bava Kamma (88a) the Sages expound: "'from among your brethren shall you set a king over you' (Devarim 17:15)—from the choice of your brethren," to exclude a convert and a slave, and so too a mamzer;
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּתּוֹסֶפְתָּא הַמּוּבָא בְּהַגָּהוֹת מַיְימוֹנִי פֶּרֶק א׳ מִמְּלָכִים (הֲלָכָה ד׳) מִזֶּה: ״דְּאֵין מְמַנִּין מֶלֶךְ אֶלָּא מֵהַמַּשִּׂיאִין לִכְהֻנָּה״
as stated in the Tosefta cited in Hagahot Maimoniyot (Hilchos Melachim 1:4): "we appoint a king only from families eligible to marry into the priesthood";
וְהוּא הַדִּין לְנָבִיא דִּכְתִיב בֵּיהּ נַמֵּי כֵּן.
and the same law applies unto a prophet, concerning whom identical language is written.

And in Sifrei Shoftim (§175) the Sages expounded: "'from the midst of you'—and not from outside the Land; 'of your brethren'—and not from others";
וְרָצָה לוֹמַר גּוֹיִם, כִּלְשׁוֹן הַגְּמָרָא פְּסָחִים (ה׳ עַמּוּד ב׳), רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה (כ״ד עַמּוּד ב׳), בָּבָא מְצִיעָא (קי״א עַמּוּד א׳), סַנְהֶדְרִין (נ״ב עַמּוּד ב׳) וּבְכַמָּה דּוּכְתֵּי
meaning gentiles, matching the Talmud's usage in Pesachim (5b), Rosh Hashanah (24b), Bava Metzia (111a), and Sanhedrin (52b);

and even though the verse ultimately excludes converts and slaves;
אֶפְשָׁר לוֹמַר דְּאִצְטְרַךְ נַמֵּי גּוֹיִם, כְּשֶׁיִּשְׁלְטוּ עֲלֵיהֶם מַלְכֵי גוֹיִם וְיִהְיֶה מֶלֶךְ שֶׁלֹּא מִקֶּרֶב אַחֶיךָ, סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ דְּיִהְיֶה גַּם נָבִיא כֵּן.
it was necessary to explicitly exclude gentiles, lest one imagine that when foreign monarchs rule over them, a prophet might likewise arise from among them.
וְגַם יֵשׁ לוֹמַר דְּהָךְ קְרָא וַדַּאי אֵינוֹ הַבְטָחָה לִתְפִלַּת מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁלֹּא תִּשְׁרֶה שְׁכִינָה עֲלֵיהֶם
And one may also say that this verse is not a fulfillment of Moshe Rabbeinu's prayer that the Shechinah not rest upon the nations;
דְּהַהִיא אֲפִילּוּ לְעִנְיַן לְהִתְנַבֵּא לַגּוֹיִם לֹא תִּשְׁרֵי עֲלֵיהֶם
for that prayer ensured that the Shechinah not rest upon them even to prophesy unto gentiles;
וְכָאן אָמַר: ״יָקִים לְךָ״ (דְּבָרִים י״ח:ט״ו), וְדָרְשׁוּ בַּסִּפְרֵי שָׁם: ״וְלֹא לַגּוֹיִם״
whereas here Scripture states: "will He raise up unto you" (Devarim 18:15), the Sifrei expounding: "unto you—and not unto the nations";
וְלוּלֵי תְּפִלַּת מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הָיוּ נְבִיאֵי גוֹיִם מִתְנַבְּאִים לַגּוֹיִם
and were it not for Moshe Rabbeinu's prayer, gentile prophets would have prophesied unto the nations;
וְהָךְ קְרָא קָאֵי כְּפִי מִשְׁפַּט הַתּוֹרָה וְחֻקֵּי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּזוּלַת תְּפִלַּת מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
this verse establishing the baseline constitutional law of the Torah independent of Moshe's prayer.
וְאִם כֵּן הֲוֵי סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ: אִם לֹא יִזְכּוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּאֵיזוֹ דוֹר לִנְבִיאִים וְאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם יִזְכּוּ לִנְבִיאִים לָהֶם, שֶׁיָּקוּם מֵהֶם דְּיוּכְלוּ לְנַבֵּא גַּם לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
And if so, it might have entered your mind: if Israel should not merit prophets in some era while the nations merit prophets, that a prophet might arise from among them to prophesy unto Israel;
וּמִעֲטָם כָּאן: דִּלְהִתְנַבֵּא לְיִשְׂרָאֵל מִעֲטָם הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מֵעַצְמוֹ מִצַּד גְּזֵירַת הַתּוֹרָה
wherefore Scripture excluded them here: that from prophesying unto Israel, the Holy One excluded them through the decree of the Torah;
וּמִצַּד תְּפִלַּת מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם נִתְמַעֲטוּ מִנְּבוּאָה לְגַמְרֵי.
while through Moshe Rabbeinu's prayer they were excluded from prophecy entirely.
וּמִיהוּ לֹא נִמְצָא בַּסִּפְרֵי דְּרָשָׁא אַ״מִקֶּרֶב אַחֵיהֶם״ לְמַעֵט גֵּר וְעֶבֶד וּמַמְזֵר
However, an explicit exposition is not found in the Sifrei on "from among their brethren" to exclude a convert, slave, and mamzer;
אֲבָל גַּם גַּבֵּי מֶלֶךְ לֹא נִמְצָא שָׁם, עַיֵּין שָׁם פֶּרֶק קנ״ז:
but regarding a king as well that derivation is not found in the Sifrei, see there (§157)!
יִשְׂרָאֵל קְדוֹשִׁים — פֶּרֶק ו׳, סְעִיפִים כ״ד–כ״ח
אוֹת כ״ד — גִּרְסַת הָרְאֵ״ם בְּסִפְרֵי עַל ״כָּמֹנִי״, תְּנָאֵי הַנְּבוּאָה שֶׁאֵינָם מוּחְלָטִים, וְהַבְחָנָה בֵּין נְבוּאַת קֶבַע לִנְבוּאַת אַקְרַאי
Section 24: The Mizrachi's Text of the Sifrei on "Like Unto Me", Non-Absolute Conditions for Prophecy, and Permanent vs. Occasional Prophecy

The theme: The Sifrei's exposition on "like unto me", why qualifications for prophecy are not absolute barriers, and the distinction between permanent and occasional divine inspiration. In Parashat Shoftim (Devarim 18:15), the Mizrachi (Re'em) cites an extended reading from the Sifrei: "just as Moshe speaks without fear... you might think: just as Moshe was aged and a Levite, so must any prophet be aged and a Levite; Scripture therefore teaches: 'unto him shall you hearken'—from any tribe and age". The Sifrei does not propose that a prophet might not need to be an Israelite of legitimate pedigree, because "from among their brethren" explicitly establishes that requirement. Furthermore, this derivation applies strictly to visionary prophecy and not to the Holy Spirit (Ruach HaKodesh). Even regarding prophecy, these criteria are not absolute barriers, for "like me" and "like you" would technically exclude women, yet Scripture records seven female prophets (Megillah 14a), five of whom lived after Moshe. Perforce, the obligation "unto him shall you hearken" applies strictly to the permanent prophet established by Hashem who possesses all of Moshe's credentials; whereas occasional prophecy (nevu'at akrai) can occur without these prerequisites, though without an obligatory command upon Israel to obey him. In Shitah Mekubetzet on Nedarim, Rabbi Eliezer of Metz explains that the criteria of wealth and might apply strictly to permanent, unceasing prophecy (bikvi'ut), resolving the anomaly of Eliyahu being sustained in poverty by ravens and the widow of Zarephath (I Melachim 17:4, 9). This explains occasional prophecy in Jonah (Yevamos 98a), the seven prophetesses, and Obadiah!
וְרָאִיתִי בַּהְרָאֵ״ם (פָּרָשַׁת שֹׁפְטִים י״ח:י״ד) הֶעְתִּיק מֵהַסִּפְרֵי לָשׁוֹן אָרוֹךְ שֶׁחָסֵר בַּנִּדְפָּס
And I saw in the commentary of the Mizrachi on Parashat Shoftim (Devarim 18:14) where he transcribed an extended passage from the Sifrei that is missing in our printed editions;
דְּרָשׁ עַל מִלַּת ״כָּמֹנִי״ (דְּבָרִים י״ח:ט״ו): ״מַה מֹּשֶׁה מְדַבֵּר דָּבָר וְאֵינוֹ מִתְיָירֵא וְכוּלֵיהּ
expounding upon the word "like unto me" (Devarim 18:15): "just as Moshe speaks the word and fears not, etc.;
יָכוֹל מַה מֹּשֶׁה זָקֵן וּבֶן לֵוִי, אַף נָבִיא זָקֵן וּבֶן לֵוִי?
you might think: just as Moshe was aged and a Levite, so must any future prophet be aged and a Levite?
תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ׳[אֵלָיו] תִּשְׁמָעוּן׳ (שָׁם) — מִכָּל מָקוֹם״
Scripture therefore teaches: 'unto him shall you hearken'—from any category";
וְהִנֵּה רִיבָּה דְּאֵין צָרִיךְ זָקֵן כְּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
and behold the Sifrei includes that a prophet need not be aged like Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him;
וְלֹא אָמַר טְפֵי: ״אִי מַה מֹּשֶׁה יִשְׂרָאֵל וּמְיוּחָס״
yet the Midrash did not raise the possibility: "or just as Moshe was an Israelite of legitimate pedigree";
וְעַל כָּרְחָךְ דְּזֶה צָרִיךְ בֶּאֱמֶת, דְּבָעֵינַן ״מִקֶּרֶב אַחֵיהֶם״ (שָׁם:י״ח) וְלָאו מִ״כָּמֹנִי״
proving perforce that this pedigree is genuinely indispensable, derived from "from among their brethren" (ibid. 18:18) and not from "like unto me";
דְּאִם כֵּן הֲוָה לֵיהּ לְמֵימַר זֶה בְּרֵישָׁא אַ״כָּמֹנִי״: מַה מֹּשֶׁה וְכוּלֵיהּ
for had it been derived from "like unto me," the Sifrei should have stated it first regarding "like unto me: just as Moshe was an Israelite, etc.";
וְעַל כָּל פָּנִים שַׁפִּיר יֵשׁ לוֹמַר גַּם זֶה רַק לְעִנְיַן נְבוּאָה וְלֹא לְרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ.
and at all events one may properly maintain that this requirement applies strictly unto visionary prophecy and not unto the Holy Spirit.
וּבְלָאו הָכִי, אַף לִנְבוּאָה נִרְאֶה דְּעַל כָּרְחָךְ לָאו תְּנָאִים מוּחְלָטִים הֵם לְסַלֵּק הַנְּבוּאָה לְגַמְרֵי בְּזוּלַת זֶה
And aside from this, even regarding prophecy it appears perforce that these are not absolute prerequisites whose absence bars prophecy entirely;
דַּהֲרֵי מִ״כָּמֹנִי״ וְ״כָמוֹךָ״ נְדַיֵּיק נַמֵּי לְמַעֵט אִשָּׁה
for from "like me" and "like you" one would likewise deduce the exclusion of women;
וּבְלָאו הָכִי נַמֵּי מִפְּשָׁטֵיהּ דִּקְרָא: ״נָבִיא״ מַשְׁמַע — לֹא נְבִיאָה
and aside from this, the plain meaning of "a prophet" implies a male and not a female prophet;
כִּדְדָרְשִׁינַן בַּסִּפְרֵי פֶּרֶק קנ״ז: ״׳מֶלֶךְ׳ (דְּבָרִים י״ז:ט״ו) — וְלֹא מַלְכָּה״
just as the Sifrei expounds (§157): "'a king' (Devarim 17:15)—and not a queen";
וַהֲרֵי הָיוּ שֶׁבַע נְבִיאוֹת שֶׁנִּמְנוּ בִּמְגִלָּה (י״ד עַמּוּד א׳), וְה׳ (חָמֵשׁ) מֵהֶם אַחַר מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם!
yet there were seven prophetesses enumerated in Megillah (14a), five of whom lived after Moshe Rabbeinu!
וְעַל כָּרְחָךְ דְּעִיקַּר קְרָא דְּפָתַח לְעִנְיַן אַזְהָרַת ״אֵלָיו תִּשְׁמָעוּן״ (דְּבָרִים י״ח:ט״ו)
And perforce the primary focus of the verse introduced the command: "unto him shall you hearken" (Devarim 18:15);
דְּהַנָּבִיא שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מֵקִים שֶׁחוֹבָה לִשְׁמוֹעַ לוֹ
that the prophet whom Hashem establishes unto whom obedience is legally mandatory;
הַיְינוּ דַּוְוקָא כְּמוֹהוּ דְּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם וּבְאוֹתָם תְּנָאִים
must be specifically like Moshe Rabbeinu, possessing all those required prerequisites;
אֲבָל יֵשׁ שֶׁזּוֹכִים לִנְבוּאָה לְשָׁעָה דֶּרֶךְ אַקְרַאי, שֶׁאֵינָם בִּכְלַל נָבִיא שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מֵקִים כְּשֶׁאֵין לָהֶם הָנֵי תְּנָאִים, וְאֵין חוֹבָה לִשְׁמוֹעַ לוֹ
but there are those who merit occasional prophecy for an hour who do not fall under the established prophet when lacking these prerequisites, wherefore obedience to them is not biblically mandatory;
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁזָּכָה לִנְבוּאַת אֱמֶת
even though he attained genuine prophecy of truth.
וְהָכִי נַמֵּי הָנֵי נְבִיאוֹת — אֵין הָכִי נַמֵּי דְּלֹא הָיוּ בִּכְלַל הַמִּצְוָה לִשְׁמוֹעַ לָהֶם
And so regarding these prophetesses: it is indeed true that they did not fall under the mandatory commandment of absolute obedience.

וְשׁוּב מָצָאתִי בְּ״שִׁטָּה מְקֻבֶּצֶת״ לִנְדָרִים (ל״ח עַמּוּד א׳) הַנִּדְפָּס מֵחָדָשׁ בְּשֵׁם הָרַב רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר מִמִּיץ כָּתַב: ״אֵין הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מַשְׁרֶה שְׁכִינָתוֹ בִּקְבִיעוּת שֶׁלֹּא תִּפְסוֹק מִמֶּנּוּ אֶלָּא וְכוּלֵיהּ״, עַד כָּאן

And subsequently I found in the Shitah Mekubetzet on Nedarim (38a) citing Rabbi Eliezer of Metz, who wrote: "the Holy One causes His Shechinah to rest permanently so that it never departs from him only upon a sage who is mighty and wealthy, etc.," thus far;
הֲרֵי מְבוֹאָר שֶׁבְּאַקְרַאי מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לֵיהּ!
behold it is explicit that occasional prophecy can occur without these traits!

וְאוּלַי הוּכְרַח לָזֶה מִשּׁוּם דְּהוּקְשָׁה לוֹ מֵאֵלִיָּהוּ, כְּשֶׁאָמַר לוֹ: ״לֵךְ צָרְפַתָה... [הִנֵּה צִוִּיתִי שָׁם] אִשָּׁה אַלְמָנָה לְכַלְכְּלֶךָ״ (מְלָכִים א י״ז:ט׳) מִכַּד הַקֶּמַח וּצְפַחַת הַשֶּׁמֶן

And perhaps he was compelled to this distinction because of the difficulty from Eliyahu, whom Hashem instructed: "arise, get you to Zarephath... behold, I have commanded a widow there to sustain you" (I Melachim 17:9) from the barrel of meal and cruse of oil;
וְכֵן כְּשֶׁהָעוֹרְבִים כִּלְכְּלוּהוּ, עַל כָּל פָּנִים עָנִי הָיָה בְּאוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה מִיהַת
and likewise when the ravens sustained him, he was impoverished at that hour;
וְאֵיךְ שָׁרְתָה עָלָיו וְדִבֶּר עִמּוֹ ה׳ גַּם אָז?! וְעַל כָּרְחָךְ דְּבַאֲקְרַאי מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לֵיהּ
and how did the Shechinah rest upon him and Hashem speak with him then?! Perforce, occasional inspiration can be found without wealth;
(יֵשׁ לְעַיֵּין קְצָת מִמַּה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בִּנְדָרִים שָׁם ל״ח עַמּוּד א׳: ״כָּל הַנְּבִיאִים עֲשִׁירִים הָיוּ, מְנָלַן? ...וּמִיּוֹנָה״
(though one must analyze Nedarim 38a: "whence do we derive that all prophets were wealthy? From Jonah";
וַהֲרֵי יוֹנָה כָּל נְבוּאָתוֹ אַקְרַאי, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּיבָמוֹת (צ״ח עַמּוּד א׳): ״שֵׁנִית דִּבְּרָה עִמּוֹ שְׁכִינָה, שְׁלִישִׁית לֹא דִּבְּרָה עִמּוֹ״
yet Jonah's prophecy was occasional, Yevamos 98a stating: "a second time the Shechinah spoke with him, a third time the Shechinah spoke not with him";
וּלְרַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק שָׁם הַיְינוּ לְגַמְרֵי בְּשׁוּם דְּבַר נְבוּאָה, וְעַיֵּין שָׁם בְּתוֹסָפוֹת דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל: ״רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק״)
and according to Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak he ceased prophesying altogether, see Tosafos there);
וְהָכִי נַמֵּי יֵשׁ לוֹמַר בְּשֶׁבַע נְבִיאוֹת וְעוֹבַדְיָה
and so one may answer regarding the seven prophetesses and Obadiah;
וְאִם כֵּן קַשְׁיָא גַּם אַדְּרַשִׁ״י, דְּהָתָם נַמֵּי רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ דְּאַקְרַאי:
and if so, it poses a challenge unto Rashi in Ta'anit (4a), for there too an occasional manifestation of the Holy Spirit might apply!

6.h: אוֹת כ״ה — דְּרָשַׁת הָרַ״ן בִּנְבִיאִים הַנִּשְׁלָחִים לֶהָמוֹן, וְעוֹבַדְיָה כְּמוֹשִׁיעַ נְבִיאִים — Section 25: The Ran on Prophets Sent to the Multitudes, and Obadiah Saving the Prophets

The theme: The Ran's sixth discourse regarding prophets sent to address the multitudes, the psychological role of wealth and might, and Obadiah's singular merit. In his sixth homily (Derashot HaRan, Derush 6), the Ran explains that the criteria of might and wealth were instituted specifically so that the prophet would command authority and respect in the eyes of the common people (hamon). Thus, these prerequisites apply exclusively unto a prophet commissioned to publicly address the multitudes. This resolves the difficulty from Eliyahu: in his era of poverty, he never prophesied publicly before the multitude. The Ran cites Balaam as a temporary exception, but Balaam's prophecy occurred before the general cessation of gentile prophecy. This leaves Rashi's citation in Ta'anit (4a) difficult; perforce, the textual reference to Nedarim (38a) is a scribal error (ta'ut sofer), Rashi's true intent being the passages in Yevamos and Sanhedrin deriving from "to be a God unto you" that the Shechinah requires pure lineage. Although Obadiah broke this rule by meriting prophecy despite being an Edomite convert, this was granted solely on account of his singular, extraordinary merit of saving one hundred prophets from death (I Melachim 18:4), which was nonexistent in the generation of Joshua and Caleb. Slaves are naturally prone to licentiousness, exceptions like Tabi being rare (Yoma 87a); while mamzerim are prone to brazenness (Kiddushin 49b; Avos 5:20; Ta'anit 7b), scholarly mamzerim being uncommon (Horayot 13a), wherefore the Talmud did not account for such anomalies!

p: וְשׁוּב מָצָאתִי גַּם בִּדְרָשַׁת הָרַ״ן (דְּרוּשׁ ו׳) כָּתַב: דִּפְעָמִים יִשְׁתַּנֶּה לְצֹרֶךְ הַשָּׁעָה, יְעוּיַּן שָׁם
And subsequently I found in the homilies of the Ran (Derush 6) where he wrote: that at times prophetic prerequisites change according to temporary necessity, see there;
(וְיֵשׁ לוֹמַר: הַיְינוּ הַאי דְּעוֹבַדְיָה מִכָּל מָקוֹם זָכָה וְכוּלֵיהּ);
(and one may say this explains why Obadiah nevertheless merited prophecy);
אַךְ רְאָיָתוֹ שָׁם מִבִּלְעָם אֵין מוּכְרָח כְּפִי מַה שֶּׁכָּתַבְתִּי: דְּמִקְּרָא דְּ״נָבִיא אָקִים וְגוֹמֵר״ יָלְפִינַן
yet his proof from Balaam is inconclusive, for we derive the criteria from "a prophet will I raise up, etc.";

מִלְּבַד דְּיֵשׁ לוֹמַר: דְּהַיְינוּ רַק מֵאוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה וְאֵילָךְ, הַיְינוּ נַמֵּי רַק בִּנְבִיאֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְגַם כְּשֶׁמְּנַבֵּא לְיִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הֱקִימוֹ לְהִתְנַבֵּא לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
aside from saying that this applies only from that hour onward regarding prophets of Israel commissioned to speak unto Israel.
וְעַיֵּין שָׁם לִפְנֵי זֶה כָּתַב: בְּטַעַם ״גִּבּוֹר וְעָשִׁיר״ — כְּדֵי שֶׁיֵּחָשֵׁב בְּעֵינֵי הַהֲמוֹן, עַיֵּין שָׁם בַּאֲרִיכוּת
And see earlier where the Ran wrote: the reason a prophet must be mighty and wealthy is that he be respected in the eyes of the multitudes, see there at length;
וְאִם כֵּן אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא בְּנָבִיא הַשָּׁלוּחַ לְדַבֵּר לִפְנֵי הַהֲמוֹן
and if so, this applies solely unto a prophet dispatched to address the populace;
וּבָזֶה לֹא קַשְׁיָא מֵאֵלִיָּהוּ, דִּבַּעֲנִיּוּתוֹ לֹא מָצִינוּ לוֹ נְבוּאָה לִפְנֵי הַהֲמוֹן.
whereby there is no difficulty from Eliyahu, for during his period of poverty we find no public prophecy delivered before the multitude.
וְעַל כָּל פָּנִים קַשְׁיָא עַל דִּבְרֵי רַשִׁ״י תַּעֲנִית (ד׳ עַמּוּד א׳), וְעַל כָּרְחָךְ טָעוּת סוֹפֵר הָרְאָיָה מִנְּדָרִים
And at all events, a difficulty remains on Rashi in Ta'anit (4a), and perforce the citation of Nedarim was a scribal error;
וְכַוָּונָתוֹ לְמַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בִּיבָמוֹת (מ״ב עַמּוּד א׳) וְסַנְהֶדְרִין (ל״ט עַמּוּד ב׳), וּסְבִירָא לֵיהּ: דְּ״לִהְיוֹת לֵאלֹהִים״ מַשְׁמַע גַּם הַשְׁרָאַת רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ.
his true reference being Yevamos (42a) and Sanhedrin (39b), holding that "to be a God" includes the resting of the Holy Spirit.
וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּמָצִינוּ דְּיָצָא עוֹבַדְיָה מֵהַכְּלָל וְזָכָה לִנְבוּאָה עַל יְדֵי אֵיזֶה זְכוּת הַגּוֹרֵם אַף שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְיוּחָס
And although Obadiah departed from the rule, meriting prophecy through singular merit despite lacking pedigree;
וְאִם כֵּן הָכִי נַמֵּי נָחוּשׁ לְעֶבֶד וּמַמְזֵר שֶׁיִּזְכֶּה עַל יְדֵי אֵיזֶה זְכוּת?!
and if so, shall we likewise suspect that a slave or mamzer might merit through some extraordinary merit?!
אֶפְשָׁר לוֹמַר: דְּלָא מְהַנֵּי לָזֶה אֶלָּא זְכוּת דְּהַצָּלַת נְבִיאִים מִמָּוֶת, וְלֹא הָיָה מָצוּי זֶה בְּדוֹר יְהוֹשֻׁעַ וְכָלֵב.
one may answer: nothing avails for this save the unique merit of rescuing one hundred prophets from death, which did not exist in the generation of Joshua and Caleb.
וְגַם אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא שֶׁיּוֹעִיל גַּם אֵיזֶה זְכוּת גָּדוֹל אַחֵר, הוּא דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין מָצוּי כְּלָל וְלֹא חָיְישִׁינַן לֵיהּ
And even if another monumental merit could avail, it is an exceedingly rare anomaly which the law does not take into account;
וּסְתָם עֲבָדִים פְּרוּצִים, וְדַי שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה פָּרוּץ
for common slaves are licentious, and it is notable enough if one is merely not profligate;
וְאַף דְּנִמְצָא הָרָאוּי גַּם לִסְמִיכָה כְּטָבִי עֶבֶד רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל (סֻכָּה כ׳ עַמּוּד ב׳), כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּיוֹמָא (פ״ז עַמּוּד א׳) — אֵינוֹ מָצוּי כְּלָל.
and though one worthy of ordination existed like Tabi the slave of Rabban Gamliel (Sukkah 20b; Yoma 87a), such is exceedingly rare.
וְכֵן הַמַּמְזֵרִים עַזֵּי פָּנִים, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּקִדּוּשִׁין (מ״ט עַמּוּד ב׳): ״ט׳ קַבִּין עַזּוּת וְכוּלֵיהּ״
And so mamzerim are prone to brazenness, as stated in Kiddushin (49b): "nine measures of brazenness, etc.";
וּתְנַן בְּסוֹף פֶּרֶק ה׳ דְּאָבוֹת (מִשְׁנָה כ׳): ״עַז פָּנִים — לְגֵיהִנָּם״, וּבְתַעֲנִית (ז׳ עַמּוּד ב׳): ״דְּנִקְרָא רָשָׁע״
and we learned in Avos (5:20): "the brazen-faced is destined for Gehinnom," and in Ta'anit (7b): "he is termed wicked";
וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּמָצִינוּ בַּמִּשְׁנָה סוֹף הוֹרָיוֹת (י״ג עַמּוּד א׳): ״מַמְזֵר תַּלְמִיד חָכָם״
and although the Mishnah states in Horayot (13a): "a mamzer who is a Torah scholar";
מִכָּל מָקוֹם אֵינוֹ מָצוּי, וְעַל כָּרְחָךְ דַּהֲוָה לֵיהּ לָחוּשׁ גַּם לְשֶׁאֵינוֹ מָצוּי:
nevertheless it is rare, and perforce Caleb did not suspect such uncommon anomalies!
אוֹת כ״ו — אוּנְקְלוֹס הַגֵּר בְּרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ, הַשְׂגַּת ״יְפֵה תֹאַר״ עַל רַשִׁ״י, וְיִחוּסָם שֶׁל נְבִיאִים כֹּהֲנִים וּמַלְכֵי בֵּית דָּוִד
Section 26: Onkelos the Convert, The Yefeh To'ar's Critique, and the Lineage of Priestly Prophets and Davidic Kings

6.h: The theme: Onkelos composing the Targum through the Holy Spirit, resolving the Yefeh To'ar, and maternal vs. paternal lineage in biblical prophets. Converts are certainly not excluded from attaining the Holy Spirit: Onkelos the convert composed the Targum through the Holy Spirit (Megillah 3a), and is cited as a Tanna in a Baraita (Bava Batra 99a), his words being the words of the Living God. In Yefeh To'ar (Bereishis Rabbah 60:4), the author challenges Rashi in Ta'anit (4a): how could Nedarim (38a) be cited when its criteria apply strictly to visionary prophecy and not to the Holy Spirit? Furthermore, a slave can be considered wealthy if his master grants him total stewardship over his estate (like Joseph under Potiphar, or royal servants, Shevuot 45a); while humility (anivut) cannot be an absolute requirement for the Holy Spirit because the Baraita of Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair lists rungs sequentially. The Yefeh To'ar questions pedigree by citing Ezekiel as descending from Rahab the harlot and Obadiah as an Edomite convert. This critique is deeply flawed: Scripture explicitly identifies Ezekiel as a consecrated priest (Yechezkel 1:3), descending from Rahab maternally through her marriage to Joshua, which does not compromise priestly paternal lineage. The High Priests of the First Temple descended from Phinehas, who married the daughters of Putiel (Jethro, Bava Batra 109b); and the Kings of the House of David descended from Ruth the Moabitess (Megillah 10b). Mentioning Ezekiel from Rahab was a scribal error for Jeremiah (Megillah 14b). Obadiah's exception was necessitated by the spiritual darkness of Ahab's reign, whereas in the righteous generation of Joshua and Caleb, no temporary crisis existed that would necessitate the Holy Spirit resting upon a slave or mamzer!

p: וְגַם נִרְאֶה דְּאֵין לְהוֹצִיא גֵּר מֵהַשָּׂגַת רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ, דְּאוּנְקְלוֹס הַגֵּר וַדַּאי תַּרְגּוּם הַתּוֹרָה חִבֵּר בִּלְשׁוֹן הַקֹּדֶשׁ [בְּרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ] (מְגִלָּה ג׳ עַמּוּד א׳)

And it likewise appears that one must not exclude a convert from attaining the Holy Spirit, for Onkelos the convert certainly composed his Aramaic translation of the Torah through the Holy Spirit (Megillah 3a);
וְהוּא גַּם כֵּן תַּנָּא דְּבָרַיְיתָא בְּבָבָא בַּתְרָא (צ״ט עַמּוּד א׳)
and he is cited as a Tanna in a Baraita in Bava Batra (99a);
וּמֵאַחַר דְּנִקְבַּע הַמֵּימְרָא בְּבָרַיְיתָא וּבַתַּלְמוּד, וַדַּאי הֵם דִּבְרֵי אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים
and once a teaching is recorded in the Talmud, it represents the words of the Living God;
וּמִכְּלַל חִדּוּשֵׁי תַּלְמִיד וָתִיק שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר לְמֹשֶׁה, דְּהוּא בִּכְלַל רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ שֶׁל הַחֲכָמִים
being of the novellae of a seasoned disciple revealed to Moshe at Sinai, within the Holy Spirit of the Sages.
וְשׁוּב מָצָאתִי בְּ״יְפֵה תֹאַר״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ס׳ סִימָן ד׳) הִקְשָׁה עַל דִּבְרֵי רַשִׁ״י תַּעֲנִית הַנִּזְכָּר
And subsequently I found in the Yefeh To'ar on Bereishis Rabbah (60:4) where he questioned Rashi in Ta'anit (4a):
דְּמַה מַיְיתֵי מִנְּדָרִים (ל״ח עַמּוּד א׳)? עַל כָּרְחָךְ לִנְבוּאָה דַּוְוקָא וְלֹא לְרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ, עַיֵּין שָׁם
why cite Nedarim (38a)? That Gemara applies strictly unto visionary prophecy and not unto the Holy Spirit, see there.

וּלְדַעְתּוֹ זֶה בְּלָאו הָכִי אֵינוֹ כְּלוּם: דְּאַף עַל גַּב דְּעֶבֶד אֵין לוֹ מִשֶּׁל עַצְמוֹ כְּלוּם, מִכָּל מָקוֹם מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לֵיהּ שֶׁיֵּחָשֵׁב עָשִׁיר כְּשֶׁיַּשְׁלִיטוֹ רַבּוֹ כְּפוֹטִיפַר לְיוֹסֵף
And according to his view this is no barrier: for though a slave owns nothing independently, he can be accounted wealthy if his master gives him dominion like Potiphar unto Joseph;
וְכֵן עַבְדֵי שְׁלֹמֹה וְכָל עַבְדֵי מְלָכִים וַדַּאי נִקְרָאִים עֲשִׁירִים, וְאִיתָא בִּשְׁבוּעוֹת (מ״ז עַמּוּד ב׳): ״עֶבֶד מֶלֶךְ — מֶלֶךְ״
and so royal servants are called wealthy: "the servant of a king is like a king" (Shevuot 47b);
וְעֶבֶד הָרָאוּי לִזְכּוֹת לְרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ וַדַּאי יִמְצָא חֵן בְּעֵינֵי רַבּוֹ
and a slave worthy of the Holy Spirit would find favor in his master's eyes.
וּמַה שֶּׁהֵבִיא עוֹד הָא דִּיחֶזְקֵאל מִבְּנֵי רָחָב הַזּוֹנָה, תָּמוּהַּ: הֲרֵי מְפוֹרָשׁ בַּקְּרָא דְּהָיָה כֹּהֵן (יְחֶזְקֵאל א:ג)
And what the Yefeh To'ar cited that Ezekiel descended from Rahab is astonishing: for Scripture explicitly states Ezekiel was a priest (Yechezkel 1:3);
וְעַל כֵּן רַק מִצַּד אֵם הָיָה מִמֶּנָּה, וְגַם זֶה הֲרֵי נִשֵּׂאת לִיהוֹשֻׁעַ (מְגִלָּה י״ד עַמּוּד ב׳), וְאֵין זֶה חוֹצֵץ בְּיִחוּס הַמִּשְׁפָּחָה כְּלָל
being descended from her solely maternally through her marriage to Joshua, which does not compromise priestly paternal lineage whatsoever!
דְּמִי לָנוּ מִשְׁפָּחוֹת מְיוּחָסוֹת יוֹתֵר מִכֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל וּמְלָכִים?
For whom do we possess of higher pedigree than High Priests and Davidic monarchs?
וְכָל כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל דְּבַיִת רִאשׁוֹן מִזֶּרַע אֶלְעָזָר נָסֵיב מִבְּנוֹת פּוּטִיאֵל (שְׁמוֹת ו:כה) דַּאֲבוּהָ אוֹ אִמָּהּ הָיוּ מִיִּתְרוֹ (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא ק״ט עַמּוּד ב׳)
Yet every High Priest of the First Temple descended from Eleazar who married the daughters of Putiel (Jethro, Bava Batra 109b);
וְכֵן כָּל מַלְכֵי בֵּית דָּוִד — מֵרוּת הַמּוֹאֲבִיָּה, וְכֵן יְשַׁעְיָהוּ מֵרוּת
and all kings of the House of David descended from Ruth the Moabitess, as did Isaiah;
וְגַם מַה שֶּׁכָּתַב ״יְחֶזְקֵאל״ טָעוּת סוֹפֵר, דִּבִמְגִלָּה (י״ד סוֹף עַמּוּד ב׳) לֹא מָנֵי יְחֶזְקֵאל בַּהֲדַיְיהוּ, וְצָרִיךְ לוֹמַר ״יִרְמְיָה״.
and writing "Ezekiel" was a scribal error for "Jeremiah," who was among the eight priestly prophets descending from Rahab (Megillah 14b).
וְגַם מַה שֶּׁכָּתַב לְכָלֵב לָחוּשׁ לְצֹרֶךְ שָׁעָה — לֵיתָא:
And what the Yefeh To'ar argued that Caleb should have suspected a temporary necessity—is entirely incorrect:
דְּלֹא שַׁיָּיךְ צֹרֶךְ שָׁעָה אֶלָּא בְּעוֹבַדְיָה בְּדוֹר אַחְאָב שֶׁהָיוּ עוֹבְדֵי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה וְהָרַג נְבִיאֵי ה׳, וְלֹא נִשְׁאַר צַדִּיק גָּמוֹר הָרָאוּי לִנְבוּאָה אֶלָּא הוּא
for a temporary crisis applied only to Obadiah in the generation of Ahab when Jezebel slaughtered the prophets of Hashem, leaving no righteous man worthy save him;

אֲבָל בְּדוֹר יְהוֹשֻׁעַ וְכָלֵב, וְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל תַּלְמִידֵי מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, אֵיךְ סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה צֹרֶךְ שָׁעָה לִשְׁרוֹת רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ עַל עֶבֶד וּמַמְזֵר דַּוְוקָא?!

but in the generation of Joshua and Caleb, where all Israel were the righteous disciples of Moshe Rabbeinu, how could it enter your mind that a crisis would require the Holy Spirit to rest upon a slave or mamzer?!
אוֹת כ״ז — גִּילּוּי הֲלָכוֹת שֶׁנִּשְׁכְּחוּ בִּימֵי אֶבְלוֹ שֶׁל מֹשֶׁה, טָבִי עֶבֶד רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל, וְהַשְׁוָואַת כַּוָּונַת הַלֵּב בְּפִלְפּוּל
Section 27: Halachot Forgotten during Moshe's Mourning, Tabi the Scholar-Slave, and Aligning with Sinai via Ruach HaKodesh

The theme: Why it would be a disgrace (gnai) for forgotten halachot to be revealed to a slave or mamzer, and Tabi's exceptional scholarship. In Temurah (16a), three hundred halachot were forgotten during the mourning for Moshe, which Israel toiled to restore through their intellect. It would be a severe disgrace (gnai) unto collective Israel if Heaven revealed these communal halachic treasures through a slave or mamzer in a generation of such stature, rather than through an upright leader like Othniel ben Kenaz. For individual personal matters, the Holy Spirit might rest upon a slave or mamzer if his deeds warrant it (Tanna D'vei Eliyahu); but restoring communal halachot requires public honor. Some suggest the restoration of these forgotten laws occurred through analytical pilpul alone without the Holy Spirit; yet Bava Batra (12a) explicitly teaches that deducing a teaching that aligns precisely with an ancient Halachah le-Moshe mi-Sinai through pilpul is impossible without prophetic inspiration and the Holy Spirit! Although teaching a slave Torah is prohibited, a slave may learn on his own, as demonstrated by Tabi the slave of Rabban Gamliel, who was an accomplished scholar worthy of rabbinic ordination (Sukkah 20b; Yoma 87a).
וְעַיֵּין שָׁם מַסִּיק: דְּרַשִׁ״י מִסְּבָרָא אָמַר: ״דִּגְנַאי הַדָּבָר״
And see the Yefeh To'ar concluding that Rashi in Ta'anit (4a) spoke from logical deduction: that it would be a disgrace (gnai) unto Israel;
וְאִם כֵּן אֶפְשָׁר דְּזֶהוּ רַק שָׁם בְּהַזְכָּרַת אוֹתָן הַהֲלָכוֹת שֶׁנִּשְׁכְּחוּ שֶׁהָיָה צֹרֶךְ כְּלַל יִשְׂרָאֵל
and if so, this disgrace applies specifically to restoring those forgotten halachot which were the vital need of collective Israel;

דִּכְלַל יִשְׂרָאֵל הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּ וְיָגְעוּ בָּזֶה בְּשִׂכְלָן לְהַחֲזִירָן, וּבְוַדַּאי גְּנַאי הַדָּבָר שֶׁלֹּא יְגַלּוּ זֶה מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם רַק לְעֶבֶד וּמַמְזֵר, וּבִפְרָט בְּדוֹר חָשׁוּב כָּמוֹהוּ.

for all Israel toiled with their intellect to restore them, and it would certainly be a disgrace if Heaven revealed them exclusively to a slave or mamzer, especially in such an illustrious generation.

אֲבָל שְׁאָר רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ דְּעָלְמָא לְשָׁעָה וּלְאֵיזֶה דָּבָר פְּרָטִי... דְּאֵין גְּנַאי — שַׁפִּיר יִשְׁרֶה עָלָיו אִם רָאוּי מִצַּד מַעֲשָׂיו, וְלֹא קַשְׁיָא הָא דְּתַנָּא דְּבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ רַבָּה.
But general, temporary Holy Spirit for a private matter, where no communal disgrace exists, may rest upon him if his personal deeds are worthy, posing no contradiction to Tanna D'vei Eliyahu.
וְאַף דְּכָתַב עוֹד שָׁם: דְּיֵשׁ לוֹמַר דִּסְבִירָא לֵיהּ דַּחֲזָרַת הַהֲלָכוֹת הָיָה עַל יְדֵי פִּלְפּוּל לְבַד וְלֹא בְּרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ
And though the Yefeh To'ar further suggested that restoring the halachot occurred through pilpul alone without the Holy Spirit;
אִשְׁתְּמִיטֵיהּ בָּזֶה סִיּוּם הַגְּמָרָא דְּבָבָא בַּתְרָא (י״ב עַמּוּד ב׳) שֶׁמֵּבִיא בְּעַצְמוֹ בִּתְחִלַּת דְּבָרָיו
he overlooked the conclusion of Bava Batra (12b) which he himself cited:
דִּמְבוֹאָר שָׁם: דִּלְמֵימַר מִילְּתָא לְכַוֵּון אַהֲלָכָה לְמֹשֶׁה מִסִּינַי דְּיָהֵיב טַעְמָא בְּפִלְפּוּל וּסְבָרָא — אִי אֶפְשָׁר אֶלָּא בִּנְבוּאָה וְרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ, עַיֵּין שָׁם.
for it is explicit there that deducing a teaching through pilpul that matches a Halachah le-Moshe mi-Sinai is impossible without prophetic inspiration and the Holy Spirit!
וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּזֶה אֱמֶת דְּאָסוּר לְלַמֵּד עַבְדּוֹ תּוֹרָה (כְּתוּבּוֹת כ״ח עַמּוּד א׳), הַיְינוּ שֶׁיְּלַמְּדֶנּוּ הָאָדוֹן; אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לֵיהּ שֶׁיִּלְמוֹד הוּא מֵעַצְמוֹ
And although it is true that a master is forbidden to teach his slave Torah (Kesubos 28a), that applies to the master teaching him, whereas a slave can learn on his own;
שֶׁהֲרֵי טָבִי עַבְדּוֹ שֶׁל רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל הָיָה תַּלְמִיד חָכָם כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּסֻכָּה (כ׳ עַמּוּד ב׳) וְהָיָה רָאוּי לִסְמִיכָה
for Tabi the slave of Rabban Gamliel was an accomplished scholar worthy of ordination (Sukkah 20b);
וְעַל כֵּן גַּם בַּחֲזָרַת הָנֵי הֲלָכוֹת הוּצְרַךְ רַשִׁ״י לְמֵיתֵי מִשּׁוּם רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ, וְלֹא בִּפְשִׁיטוּת דְּלָא מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לֵיהּ עֶבֶד תַּלְמִיד חָכָם מִשּׁוּם דְּאָסוּר לְלַמְּדוֹ:
wherefore regarding the restoration of these forgotten laws Rashi had to exclude him on account of the Holy Spirit, and not simply because a scholar-slave cannot exist!

6.h: אוֹת כ״ח — תּוֹרַת בְּרוּרְיָה, דְּבוֹרָה וּבָרָק, וְהַקְּדוּשָׁה הַנִּמְשֶׁכֶת לְאֵבֶר הַבְּרִית — Section 28: Beruriah's Scholarship, Deborah and Barak, and Sanctifying the Organ of the Covenant

The theme: Women scholars like Beruriah, Deborah meriting prophecy through deeds rather than study, and sanctifying physical intimacy like Jacob. Women can master Torah, as demonstrated by Beruriah, the wife of Rabbi Meir (Pesachim 62b; Tosefta Kelim Bava Metzia 1:6), and gentiles in their seven mitzvos are likened to High Priests (Sanhedrin 59a). Yet Tanna D'vei Eliyahu Rabbah (ch. 9) emphasizes that Deborah's inspiration derived from her deeds: her husband Lapidot (Barak) was unlearned, and she fashioned thick wicks for the Tabernacle so his portion would be with the righteous. Although Deborah taught Torah publicly, she merited prophecy through pious deeds rather than study, for women are not commanded in study, and teaching a woman Torah can be degraded into vanity (Sotah 20a). Barak, though unlearned, joined her in singing the Song of Deborah (Shoftim 5:1), meriting the Holy Spirit like the maidservant at the Red Sea who saw greater visions than Ezekiel (Mechilta, Beshalach §3). This Holy Spirit—treated at the conclusion of Sotah—depends upon the holiness of the foundation (Yesod), guarding against the unholy harlot. Greek philosophers viewed the sense of touch as a pure disgrace (cherpah), unable to perceive holiness in bodily intimacy. In sublime contrast, our father Jacob exclaimed unto Laban: "Give me my wife, for my days are fulfilled" (Bereishis 29:21)—phrasing that even the basest of men would hesitate to utter—feeling zero shame, because his mind was focused purely on fathering the twelve tribes without a trace of carnal lust!

p: וְכֵן אִשָּׁה, מָצִינוּ בְּרוּרְיָה דְּבֵיתְהוּ דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר דְּלָמְדָה תּוֹרָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּפְסָחִים (ס״ב עַמּוּד ב׳) וּבְכַמָּה דּוּכְתֵּי
And so regarding a woman, we find that Beruriah the wife of Rabbi Meir studied Torah, as stated in Pesachim (62b) and numerous passages;
וְהִיא גַּם כֵּן תַּנָּא דְּבָרַיְיתָא בְּתוֹסֶפְתָּא דְּכֵלִים (בָּבָא מְצִיעָא פֶּרֶק א׳ מִשְׁנָה ו׳)
and she is cited as an authority in the Tosefta of Kelim (Bava Metzia 1:6);
וּבְגוֹי מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לֵיהּ בְּשֶׁבַע מִצְוֹת דִּידְהוּ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (נ״ט עַמּוּד א׳): ״דְּגוֹי הָעוֹסֵק בַּתּוֹרָה — כְּכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל״.
and regarding a gentile it is found in the Seven Noahide Laws: "a gentile who engages in Torah study is like a High Priest" (Sanhedrin 59a).
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם הָאֱמֶת יוֹרֶה דַּרְכּוֹ, וְקוּשְׁטָא קָאֵי מִפַּשְׁטוּת לְשׁוֹן הַתַּנָּא דְּבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ שָׁם: דְּתָלוּי בַּמַּעֲשֶׂה וְלֹא בַּתּוֹרָה
Nevertheless truth guides its own path, rooted in the plain wording of Tanna D'vei Eliyahu: that inspiration is conditioned upon moral deeds and not upon study;
וְכֵן מֵהָעִנְיָן שָׁם שֶׁאָמַר: ״מַה טִיבָהּ שֶׁל דְּבוֹרָה? ...בַּעְלָהּ עַם הָאָרֶץ הָיָה, אָמְרָה לוֹ אִשְׁתּוֹ: בֹּא וְאֶעֱשֶׂה לְךָ פְּתִילוֹת וְכוּלֵיהּ״, עַיֵּין שָׁם
and from the narrative there: "Why was Deborah chosen? Her husband was an unlearned man; his wife said to him: Come, and I will make thick wicks for the Sanctuary, etc.," see there;
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁדְּבוֹרָה הָיְתָה מְלַמֶּדֶת תּוֹרָה בָּרַבִּים כִּדְאִיתָא הָתָם אַחַר כָּךְ
and even though Deborah taught Torah publicly as stated there subsequently;
וּמִשּׁוּם דְּ״אֵין הַנְּבוּאָה שׁוֹרָה אֶלָּא עַל חָכָם״ (נְדָרִים ל״ח עַמּוּד א׳), וְעַל כָּרְחָךְ דְּהָיָה בָּהּ חָכְמָה
and because prophecy rests only upon a wise person, proving perforce she possessed wisdom;
מִכָּל מָקוֹם זָכְתָה לְכָךְ לֹא מִצַּד הַתּוֹרָה, דְּאִשָּׁה אַף שֶׁלּוֹמֶדֶת, כֵּיוָן דְּאֵינָהּ ״מְצֻוָּה וְעוֹשָׂה״ (קִדּוּשִׁין ל״א עַמּוּד א׳) אֵין בָּזֶה זְכוּת כָּל כָּךְ
nevertheless she merited this not through Torah study, for a woman who studies is not commanded, having less merit than one commanded.
וְגַם לְחַד מַאן דְּאָמַר בְּסוֹטָה שָׁם (כ׳ עַמּוּד א׳): ״דִּכְמְלַמְּדָהּ תִּפְלוּת״, וְאִיסּוּרָא נַמֵּי אִיכָּא
And according to one opinion in Sotah (20a): "teaching her Torah is like teaching her frivolity," carrying an actual prohibition;
וְעַל כֵּן אֵין כֹּחַ לְהַכְנִיס קְדוּשָׁה בְּלִבּוֹת הַנָּשִׁים גַּם כֵּן, וּמִתּוֹךְ שֶׁ״דַּעְתָּן קַלָּה״ (שַׁבָּת ל״ג עַמּוּד ב׳) מוֹצִיאָהּ לְתִפְלוּת
wherefore study cannot infuse consummate holiness into women, whose minds are impressionable, often misdirecting intellect into frivolity;
וְעַל כָּל פָּנִים אֵינָן יְכוֹלוֹת לִזְכּוֹת עַל יְדֵי זֶה לְרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ וּנְבוּאָה, רַק עַל יְדֵי זְכוּת הַמַּעֲשִׂים.
unable to merit the Holy Spirit through study, but exclusively through righteous deeds.
וְגַם בַּעְלָהּ שֶׁהוּא בָּרָק כִּדְאִיתָא הָתָם... הָיָה עַם הָאָרֶץ כַּנִּזְכָּר
And her husband Barak was an unlearned man as stated;
וְזָכָה לִיטָּפֵל אֵלֶיהָ בַּאֲמִירַת הַשִּׁירָה (שׁוֹפְטִים ה:א), וְאַף דְּלֹא זָכָה לִנְבוּאָה לְפִי שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה תַּלְמִיד חָכָם
yet merited to join her in reciting the Song of Deborah (Shoftim 5:1), and though he did not merit prophecy because he was not a scholar;
מִדְּנִטְפַּל לַשִּׁירָה מַשְׁמַע דְּזָכָה לְרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ מִיהַת
joining in the song proves he attained at least the Holy Spirit;

(וּכְמוֹ כָל יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁשָּׁרוּ עַל הַיָּם עִם מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, וְאִיתָא: ״דְּרָאֲתָה שִׁפְחָה מַה שֶּׁלֹּא רָאָה יְחֶזְקֵאל״ (מְכִילְתָּא בְּשַׁלַּח פָּרָשָׁה ג׳), דְּזָכוּ כוּלָּם לְרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ)
(just as all Israel sang at the Red Sea, where even a maidservant saw higher visions than Ezekiel, all meriting the Holy Spirit);
וּמֵרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ זֶה הוּא שֶׁדִּבְּרוּ בְּסוֹף סוֹטָה וּקְבָעוּהוּ שָׁם
and this is the Holy Spirit expounded at the end of Sotah;
כִּי עִיקַּר קְדֻשַּׁת הַמַּעֲשֶׂה אִי אֶפְשָׁר אֶלָּא עַל יְדֵי קְדֻשַּׁת הַיְסוֹד וְהַגְדָּרַת עֶרְוָה, בְּהַרְחָקָה מֵאֵשֶׁת זְנוּנִים וְסוֹטָה בְּקִלְקוּלָהּ
for holiness in action is impossible save through the purity of Yesod, fencing against immorality and distancing from the suspected adulteress.
וְכָל רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ שֶׁהוּא רוּחַ קְדוֹשָׁה אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא בִּמְקוֹם גֶּדֶר עֶרְוָה
And every manifestation of the Holy Spirit resides exclusively where there is a fence against sexual immorality;
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִסְמֵית עֵינוֹ שֶׁל אוֹתוֹ רָשָׁע [בִּלְעָם], שֶׁאָמַר: ״מִי שֶׁהוּא קָדוֹשׁ וּמְשָׁרְתָיו קְדוֹשִׁים יִסְתַּכֵּל בָּרָז זֶה?!״ (עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה כ׳ עַמּוּד ב׳)
whereby the eye of Balaam was blinded, who protested: "He Who is holy and Whose ministers are holy, should He gaze upon intimacy?!" (Avodah Zarah 20b);
שֶׁהַגּוֹיִם שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם שַׁיָּיכוּת לְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה, אֶצְלָם חוּשׁ הַמִּישׁוּשׁ חֶרְפָּה גְּמוּרָה כַּאֲשֶׁר אָמַר הַפִּילוֹסוֹף הַיְּוָנִי
for the gentiles who have no connection to Torah view the sense of touch as an absolute disgrace, as the Greek philosopher declared;
וְהַקְּדוּשָׁה אֵינָהּ אֶלָּא בִּפְרִישׁוּת הַגְּמוּרָה, כִּי לֹא יְכוֹלִים לְהַשִּׂיג קְדוּשָׁה בָּעִנְיָנִים הַגּוּפָנִיִּם הַמְלֵאִים אֶצְלָם זוּהֲמָא וְזִמָּה
their concept of holiness requiring total ascetic withdrawal, being incapable of sanctifying bodily matters which among them are steeped in filth.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם אָמַר: ״הָבָה אֶת אִשְׁתִּי [כִּי מָלְאוּ יָמָי וְאָבוֹאָה אֵלֶיהָ]״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית כ״ט:כ״א)
Unlike our father Jacob, peace be upon him, who declared unto Laban: "Give me my wife, for my days are fulfilled, that I may go in unto her" (Bereishis 29:21);
מַה שֶּׁקַּל שֶׁבַּקַּלִּים אֵינוֹ אוֹמֵר כֵּן (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה ע:יח), וְלֹא הִרְגִּישׁ גְּנוּת וְחֶרְפָּה בָּזֶה
words which even the most dissolute man would hesitate to utter (Bereishis Rabbah 70:18), feeling neither shame nor disgrace;
כִּי לֹא נִתְכַּוֵּון אֶלָּא לְהַעֲמִיד תּוֹלָדוֹת, וְלֹא הָיָה לוֹ שׁוּם כַּוָּונָה אַחֶרֶת וְשׁוּם הִרְהוּר שֶׁל תַּאֲוָה גּוּפָנִית כְּלָל
for he intended purely to establish the twelve tribes, having no other motive or lustful bodily thought whatsoever;
אִם כֵּן הַכֹּל בִּקְדוּשָׁה, וְזֶהוּ הַקְּדוּשָׁה הַנִּמְשֶׁכֶת מֵהַתּוֹרָה דְּ״לֹא עָשָׂה כֵן לְכָל גּוֹי״ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְעֵיל:
thus all was enveloped in holiness, this being the supreme sanctity drawn from the Torah which "He has not dealt so with any nation" as I wrote above!
יִשְׂרָאֵל קְדוֹשִׁים — פֶּרֶק ו׳, סְעִיפִים כ״ט–ל״ג

אוֹת כ״ט — קְדֻשַּׁת עַמֵּי הָאָרֶץ בְּהֶעְלֵם, טַל תּוֹרָה מֵאַחֲרֵי שֵׁם הֲוָיָ״ה, וְעֶצֶם הַלּוּז — Section 29: The Latent Holiness of the Commoners, The Dew of Torah (Tal = 39), and the Indestructible Luz Bone

The theme: The hidden connection of unlearned Israelites (amei ha-aretz) to Torah and holiness, ascending through the lower seven attributes to Binah, and the reviving dew (tal Torah) preserving the Luz bone. Even unlearned Jews possess a soul-connection to the Torah and holiness as descendants of Israel; yet because this holiness is not consciously manifest in their hearts, it remains concealed in this world, expressed primarily through external moral restraint. In Sotah (49b), piety (chasidut) replaces holiness as the preceding stage because "an unlearned person cannot be pious" (Avos 2:5), and without Torah there is no fear of God (Avos 3:17). Once the unlearned Jew rectifies his lower seven emotional traits through action—culminating in humility (anivut) through recognizing his lowliness—he enters the heart's understanding (Binah), where his soul-root holds onto Torah. This awakens fear and the intellect in the brain (Chokhmah), pulling him out of the status of an absolute am ha-aretz. He can then attain piety and the Holy Spirit, which revives the dead through the dew of Torah (tal Torah, Kesubos 111b). The letters following the Tetragrammaton (כוז״ו / בומ״ו) equal thirty-nine in gematria, matching Tal (טַ״ל = 39). While the Name Havayah represents the explicit Torah delivered publicly by Moshe, the dew is its concealed, unceasing flow. When a pure vessel absorbs this dew, it binds with the 248 spiritual organs and endures after death within the bodily moisture (havla d'garmei) of the Luz bone, which never decays!
וְהָעַמֵּי הָאֲרָצוֹת, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהֵם מִזֶּרַע יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁכָּל אֶחָד יֵשׁ לוֹ אֲחִיזָה בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה וְיֵשׁ לוֹ גַּם כֵּן שַׁיָּיכוּת לִקְדוּשָׁה
And the unlearned commoners (amei ha-aretz), even though they derive from the seed of Israel, where every single person possesses a hold in the words of Torah and an intrinsic connection to holiness;
מִכָּל מָקוֹם, כֵּיוָן שֶׁאֵינוֹ בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת לִבּוֹ, אֵין קְדוּשָׁה זוֹ מִתְגַּלֵּית אֶצְלוֹ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה גַּם כֵּן, וְהַקְּדוּשָׁה שֶׁלּוֹ הוּא רַק בְּהַגְדָּרָה
nevertheless, because it is not consciously manifest in his heart, this holiness is not revealed within him in this world either, his sanctity being expressed strictly through defensive restraint;
וְעַל כֵּן לֹא נִמְנֵית עוֹד בָּאַחֲרוֹנָה בְּסוֹף סוֹטָה (מ״ט עַמּוּד ב׳), וּבָאָה הַחֲסִידוּת בִּמְקוֹמָהּ, מִשּׁוּם דְּ״לֹא עַם הָאָרֶץ חָסִיד״, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּאָבוֹת (פֶּרֶק ב׳ מִשְׁנָה ה׳)
wherefore holiness was not listed last in the Mishnah at the end of Sotah (49b), piety taking its place because "an unlearned person cannot be pious," as taught in Avos (2:5);
וְכֵן: ״אִם אֵין תּוֹרָה — אֵין יִרְאָה״ (שָׁם פֶּרֶק ג׳ מִשְׁנָה י״ז).
and likewise: "if there is no Torah, there is no fear" (ibid. 3:17).
עַל כֵּן, אַחַר שֶׁהִשְׁלִים נַפְשׁוֹ בְּשֶׁבַע תַּחְתּוֹנוֹת שֶׁהֵם כֹּחַ הַמַּעֲשֶׂה
Therefore, after he has perfected his soul across the lower seven attributes which constitute the power of practical deed;

(אֲשֶׁר הָאַחֲרוֹנָה שֶׁבָּהֶם הָעֲנָוָה בְּהַכָּרַת שִׁפְלוּתוֹ, כִּי כָּל שְׁלֵימוּת עַם הָאָרֶץ הוּא בְּכֹחַ הַמַּעֲשֶׂה וּבָזֶה צָרִיךְ לַעֲנָוָה, מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בְּחָכְמָה וּבִינָה אֵין צָרִיךְ לַעֲנָוָה;

(the final trait among them being humility through recognizing his lowliness, for the entire perfection of an am ha-aretz resides in action where humility is required, whereas in Chokhmah and Binah he needs no humility;
אֲבָל הַתַּלְמִיד חָכָם עִיקַּר הָעֲנָוָה שֶׁצָּרִיךְ הוּא כְּשֶׁמַּגִּיעַ לְג׳ רִאשׁוֹנוֹת וּלְהַבִּינָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב שֶׁלֹּא יִתְגָּאֶה בָּהּ, וּלְכָךְ אֶצְלוֹ הָעֲנָוָה הַשְּׁמִינִית)

whereas for a scholar, the primary humility needed is when reaching the three upper intellectual crowns and the understanding of the heart, that he not grow arrogant, wherefore with him humility is eighth);
וּבָא לַבִּינָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב שֶׁשָּׁם בְּמַעֲמַקֵּי הַלֵּב שׁוֹרֶשׁ נַפְשׁוֹ יֵשׁ לוֹ שַׁיָּיכוּת וַאֲחִיזָה בְּאֵיזֶה דִּבְרֵי תּוֹרָה
and arrives at Binah in the heart, where in the deepest chambers of his soul-root he possesses an intrinsic hold in some words of Torah;
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה זוֹכֶה לְיִרְאָה, וּמִשָּׁם לַחָכְמָה שֶׁבַּמּוֹחַ, הוּא מְעוֹרֵר בּוֹ קְצָת רוּחַ חָכְמָה יוֹתֵר
through this he merits fear, and thence unto Chokhmah in the brain, awakening within himself an added spirit of wisdom;
וְאָז יָכוֹל לִזְכּוֹת גַּם לַחֲסִידוּת, כִּי כְּבָר יָצָא מִשֵּׁם ״עַם הָאָרֶץ״ גָּמוּר
then is he empowered to merit piety as well, having already departed from the definition of an absolute am ha-aretz;
וְאָז זוֹכֶה אַחַר כָּךְ גַּם לְרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ, דְּוַדַּאי אִי אֶפְשָׁר בְּעַם הָאָרֶץ גָּמוּר, רַק שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ רֵיחַ תּוֹרָה עַל כָּל פָּנִים
and subsequently he merits the Holy Spirit, which is impossible for an absolute am ha-aretz, requiring at least the fragrance of Torah;

כִּי רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ מְבִיאָה לִידֵי תְּחִיַּיִת הַמֵּתִים (סוֹטָה מ״ט עַמּוּד ב׳), דְּהַיְינוּ חַיֵּי עוֹלָם, וְזֶה אִי אֶפְשָׁר אֶלָּא עַל יְדֵי טַל תּוֹרָה הַמְחַיֵּיהוּ (כְּתוּבּוֹת קי״א עַמּוּד ב׳).
for the Holy Spirit brings unto the Resurrection of the Dead (Sotah 49b), which is eternal life, achievable solely through the reviving dew of Torah (Kesubos 111b)!
וְרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ הוּא הַטַּל תּוֹרָה הַיּוֹרֵד מִלְּמַעְלָה עַל הַנְּפָשׁוֹת דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
And the Holy Spirit is that very dew of Torah descending from on High upon the souls of the Children of Israel;
כִּידוּעַ דְּאוֹתִיּוֹת שֶׁאַחֲרֵי שֵׁם הֲוָיָ״ה [כ-ו-ז-ו / ב-ו-מ-ו] הֵם בְּגִימַטְרִיָּא ״טַל״ (39)
as is known that the letters following the Tetragrammaton (Havayah) equal thirty-nine in numerical value, matching Tal
(טַ״ל = 39); כִּי שֵׁם הֲוָיָ״ה הוּא הִתְגַּלּוּת הַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה בְּפֹעַל, וְהוּא הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁהוֹרִיד לָנוּ מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם וּמְסָרָהּ לִבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּפֻמְבֵּי
for the Name Havayah is the active revelation of Torah words, the Torah that Moshe Rabbeinu brought down and delivered publicly unto Israel;
וְהַטַּל הוּא הָאֲחוֹרַיִּים וְהַנֶּעְלָם מִמֶּנָּה, וְהוּא שׁוֹפֵעַ תָּמִיד וְלֹא מִיעֲצָר
while the dew (Tal) represents the posterior and concealed light of the Torah, flowing perpetually without cessation;
רַק כַּאֲשֶׁר יִהְיֶה כְּלִי מוּכָן וְרָאוּי לְקַבֵּל אוֹתוֹ הַטַּל דִּבְרָכָה
only when a vessel is prepared and worthy to receive that dew of blessing;
אָז הוּא נִקְלָט בְּכָל רַמַ״ח (248) אֵיבָרָיו הָרוּחָנִיִּים הַמְחַיִּים לְהַגּוּפָנִיִּים
is it absorbed across all his 248 spiritual organs that animate the physical limbs;
וְנִקְשָׁר בָּהֶם עַד שֶׁאֵין נִפְרָד, גַּם לְאַחַר מָוֶת וְהִסְתַּלְּקוּת הַנֶּפֶשׁ
becoming bound within them so that it never separates, remaining even after death and the departure of the soul;
הוּא נִשְׁאָר תּוֹךְ הַ״הֶבְלָא דְּגַרְמֵי״ שֶׁבְּעֶצֶם הַלּוּז, שֶׁאֵין נִרְקָב וְכָלֶה לְעוֹלָם כְּדִבְרֵי רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה כ״ח:ג׳):
residing within the bodily moisture (havla d'garmei) of the Luz bone, which never rots or disintegrates, as taught by our Sages (Bereishis Rabbah 28:3)!

6.h: אוֹת ל׳ — ״יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ לֹא מֵת״, ״מִבְּשָׂרִי אֶחֱזֶה אֱלוֹהַּ״, וּשְׁפִיכַת רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ עַל כָּל בָּשָׂר — Section 30: "Our Father Jacob Did Not Die", "From My Flesh I Shall Behold God", and Pouring the Spirit upon All Flesh

The theme: Jacob's body sanctified entirely unto Hashem, the immortality of the righteous, and the resurrection through the sanctification of the flesh. Total sanctification means all bodily functions are dedicated solely unto Hashem. Therefore the Talmud declares: "Our father Jacob did not die" (Ta'anit 5b), for when physical existence is holy like Jacob's, death cannot apply. Embalming and burial were strictly for outward appearance in this world of falsehood. All Israel—even commoners—are called by Jacob's name (Bava Metzia 33b), possessing this concealed holiness. When an unlearned Jew attains the Holy Spirit, he connects to his root in Torah ("they shall all know Me", Yirmiyah 31:33), meriting the Resurrection through his own essence rather than merely through attachment to a scholar. In the Future, Hashem will pour His spirit upon all flesh (Yoel 3:1), revealing the holiness latent within even the lowliest bodily faculties. The term "flesh" (basar) alludes to the organ of the covenant (ever ha-brit, Vayikra 15:2–3; Yirmiyah 11:15; Yechezkel 16:26, 23:20). The Holy Spirit depends upon guarding this organ: where the uncircumcised nations sink into base lust, the circumcised of Israel attain consummate sanctity. On this Job exclaimed: "And from my flesh shall I behold God" (Iyov 19:26)—through the holiness of the bodily flesh one merits the Holy Spirit! In this world, because all Israel forms one corporate body, the righteous suffer for the sins of their generation, just as a headache is felt when the foot aches. But Jacob incorporated all future generations; when he rectified his soul, the entire stature was whole, wherefore he never died!

p: וְדָבָר זֶה הוּא עַל יְדֵי הַקְּדוּשָׁה הַגְּמוּרָה שֶׁבְּזֶרַע יַעֲקֹב, שֶׁגַּם כָּל עִנְיָנָיו הַגּוּפָנִיִּם הֵם כּוּלָּם לַה׳ לְבַדּוֹ
And this reality is attained through the consummate holiness within the seed of Jacob, where even all physical matters are dedicated unto Hashem alone;
דְּעַל כֵּן אָמְרוּ בְּתַעֲנִית (ה׳ סוֹף עַמּוּד ב׳): ״יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם — לֹא מֵת״
wherefore the Sages stated in Ta'anit (5b): "Our father Jacob, peace be upon him, did not die";
כִּי מִי שֶׁכָּל עִנְיָנָיו הַגּוּפָנִיִּם בִּקְדוּשָׁה כְּיַעֲקֹב, לֹא שַׁיָּיךְ בֵּיהּ מִיתָה כְּלָל.
for unto one whose physical functions are in holiness like Jacob, death does not apply at all.
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁ״חָנְטוּ חָנְטַיָּא וְקָבְרוּ קָבְרַיָּא״ (שָׁם), הָיָה רַק לְמַרְאִית עַיִן בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה עָלְמָא דְּשִׁקְרָא
And although "the embalmers embalmed him and the gravediggers buried him," it was merely to outward appearance in this world of falsehood;
שֶׁאֵין הָאֱמֶת דְּיַעֲקֹב נִגְלֶה בּוֹ לְעֵין כֹּל
where the truth of Jacob is not revealed before all eyes;
וְגַם כָּל זַרְעוֹ, אַף בְּעַמֵּי הָאֲרָצוֹת, נִקְרָאִים בְּשֵׁם ״יַעֲקֹב״, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּבָבָא מְצִיעָא (ל״ג עַמּוּד ב׳)
and all his descendants, even the unlearned commoners, are designated by the name "Jacob" (Bava Metzia 33b);
שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהֶם גַּם כֵּן קְדוּשָׁה זוֹ, אֶלָּא שֶׁהוּא בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה בְּהֶעְלֵם עָצוּם.
possessing this holiness as well, albeit in profound concealment in this world.
וּמִי שֶׁזּוֹכֶה לְהַשְׁלִים מַדְרֵיגָתוֹ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה עַד שֶׁיַּגִּיעַ לְמַדְרֵיגַת רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ
And one who merits to complete his rung in this world until he reaches the Holy Spirit;
שֶׁהוּא הַמַּדְרֵיגָה הָאַחֲרוֹנָה וְהָעֶלְיוֹנָה שֶׁיּוּכַל לְהַגִּיעַ אֵלֶיהָ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
which is the final and highest rung achievable in this world;
