אֲפִילּוּ הָעַם הָאָרֶץ, לְאַחַר שֶׁהִגִּיעַ לְכָךְ כְּבָר הִגִּיעַ לְשׁוֹרֶשׁ אֲחִיזָתוֹ בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה, דִּלְעָתִיד: ״[כִּי] כֻלָּם יֵדְעוּ [אוֹתִי] וְגוֹמֵר״ (יִרְמְיָה ל״א:ל״ג)
even the unlearned man, once reaching this, has accessed his root in Torah, fulfilling: "for they shall all know Me" (Yirmiyah 31:33);
וּלְאָדָם שֶׁטּוֹב מַטְעִימִין מִפְּרִי מַעֲשָׂיו בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, וְזוֹכֶה לְשֶׁמֶץ מֵאוֹתָהּ יְדִיעָה
and a good man is granted a foretaste of the fruit of his deeds in this world, meriting a trace of that knowing;
וְהוּא הָרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ שֶׁמַּשִּׂיג שֶׁפַע הַטַּל תּוֹרָה הַמְחַיֵּיהוּ.
which is the Holy Spirit receiving the influx of the dew of Torah that revives him.
כִּי בְּהַשָּׂגַת רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ הוּא זוֹכֶה מִמֵּילָא גַּם כֵּן לִקְדוּשָׁה זוֹ הָעֶלְיוֹנָה — קְדֻשַּׁת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם — שֶׁכָּל מַעֲשָׂיו לְשֵׁם שָׁמָיִם
For in attaining the Holy Spirit he automatically merits this supernal holiness of Jacob, where all deeds are purely for Heaven;
וְאָז זוֹכֶה לִתְחִיַּיִת הַמֵּתִים מִצַּד עַצְמוֹ, וְלֹא מִצַּד דִּיבּוּקוֹ לְתַלְמִיד חָכָם כִּשְׁאָר עַם הָאָרֶץ
meriting the Resurrection through his own intrinsic right, and not merely through attachment to a scholar like ordinary commoners;
כִּי כְּבָר יָצָא מִכְּלַל עַם הָאָרֶץ אַחַר שֶׁזָּכָה לְרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ, וּמִצִּדּוֹ הוּא תְּחִיַּיִת הַמֵּתִים לְאַלְתַּר.
having departed from the status of an am ha-aretz upon meriting the Holy Spirit, the Resurrection becoming actualized for him immediately.
וּכְמוֹ לֶעָתִיד, כְּשֶׁיִּזְכּוּ כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל לְהַשְׁלִים נַפְשׁוֹתָם, עַד שֶׁ״אֶשְׁפּוֹךְ אֶת רוּחִי עַל כָּל בָּשָׂר״ (יוֹאֵל ג:א)
And as will occur in the Future, when all Israel will merit to perfect their souls until: "I will pour out My spirit upon all flesh" (Yoel 3:1);
אֲפִילּוּ הָעֲבָדִים וּשְׁפָחוֹת וְעַמֵּי הָאֲרָצוֹת
even upon the slaves, handmaids, and commoners;
וְיִתְגַּלֶּה אָז הַקְּדוּשָׁה שֶׁיֵּשׁ גַּם בְּכָל כֹּחוֹת הַגּוּפָנִיִּים הַיּוֹתֵר פְּחוּתִים שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל
revealing the holiness latent within even the lowest bodily faculties in Israel;
שֶׁעַל זֶה רוֹמֵז הַשֵּׁם ״בָּשָׂר״ כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּסוֹטָה (ה׳ עַמּוּד א׳)
alluding to the term "flesh" (basar, Sotah 5a);
וּבְכָל מָקוֹם בַּכָּתוּב נִקְרָא כֵּן אֵבֶר הַבְּרִית: ״זָב מִבְּשָׂרוֹ״, ״רָר בְּשָׂרוֹ״, ״הֶחְתִּים בְּשָׂרוֹ״ (וַיִּקְרָא ט״ו:ב׳–ג׳)
designating throughout Scripture the organ of the covenant: "his issue out of his flesh," "his flesh run with his issue," "his flesh be stopped" (Vayikra 15:2–3);
וּבְיִרְמְיָה (י״א:ט״ו): ״וּבְשַׂר קֹדֶשׁ יַעַבְרוּ מֵעָלָיִךְ״, פֵּירוּשׁ רַשִׁ״י: עַל הַמִּילָה
and in Jeremiah (11:15): "and the holy flesh is passed from you"—Rashi explaining: this is circumcision;
וּבִיחֶזְקֵאל (ט״ז:כ״ו) עַל מִצְרַיִם: ״גִּדְלֵי בָשָׂר״, וְשָׁם (כ״ג:כ׳): ״[אֲשֶׁר] בְּשַׂר חֲמוֹרִים בְּשָׂרָם, וְזִרְמַת [סוּסִים זִרְמָתָם]״.
and in Ezekiel (16:26) of Egypt: "great of flesh," and (23:20): "whose flesh is as the flesh of asses".
וְיָדוּעַ דְּעִיקַּר הַשָּׂגַת רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ תָּלוּי בְּהַגְדָּרַת אֵבֶר זֶה
And it is known that the attainment of the Holy Spirit depends preeminently upon fencing this organ;
כִּי כַּאֲשֶׁר הַיְסוֹד קָדוֹשׁ — אָז הַכֹּל קָדוֹשׁ, כִּי הוּא יְסוֹד הַכֹּל
for when Yesod is holy, all is holy, being the foundation of all;
וְהַמָּקוֹם שֶׁבּוֹ תֹּקֶף הַפְּחִיתוּת אֵצֶל אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם הָעֲרֵלִים — שָׁם הוּא עִיקַּר הַקְּדוּשָׁה אֵצֶל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הַנִּימּוֹלִים, שֶׁהַכֹּל אֶצְלָם בִּקְדוּשָׁה
and the place where extreme degradation reigns among the uncircumcised nations is the very seat of holiness among the circumcised of Israel;
וְכָל מָקוֹם שֶׁנִּרְאֶה יוֹתֵר פְּחִיתוּת, כַּאֲשֶׁר יֵשׁ בּוֹ קְדוּשָׁה — הֲרֵי הוּא תֹּקֶף קְדוּשָׁה יוֹתֵר
and wherever deeper baseness appears, when sanctified it manifests an even greater intensity of holiness;
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: ״וּמִבְּשָׂרִי — אֶחֱזֶה אֱלוֹהַּ״ (אִיּוֹב י״ט:כ״ו), שֶׁעַל יְדֵי קְדֻשַּׁת הַבָּשָׂר הַגּוּפָנִי זוֹכֶה לְרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ
concerning which it is said: "Yet from my flesh shall I behold God" (Iyov 19:26), through the holiness of bodily flesh one meriting the Holy Spirit!
וּכְשֶׁיִּתְגַּלֶּה קְדוּשָׁה זוֹ שֶׁבִּכְלַל יִשְׂרָאֵל, יִהְיֶה שְׁפִיכַת הָרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ עַל כָּל בָּשָׂר, וְאָז יִהְיֶה תְּחִיַּיִת הַמֵּתִים לִכְלַל יִשְׂרָאֵל.
And when this holiness is revealed across collective Israel, the Holy Spirit will be poured upon all flesh, bringing the Resurrection unto all Israel.
אֲבָל בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, אַף אִם אֵיזֶה יְחִידִים זָכוּ לָזֶה, הֲרֵי לֹא זָכוּ לָזֶה עַדַיִין כָּל הַכְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל
But in this world, even if exceptional individuals attained this, collective Knesset Israel has not yet achieved it;
וְכוּלָּם קוֹמָה אַחַת, וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְתַקֵּן אֵבֶר מִמֶּנָּה וּלְהַפְרִידוֹ מִכְּלַל הַקּוֹמָה שֶׁזֶּהוּ פֵּירוּד מִשָּׁרְשׁוֹ
all forming a single corporate stature, impossible to sever one limb from the body without cutting it from its root;
וּלְפִיכָךְ צָרִיךְ כָּל אֶחָד לִסְבּוֹל בִּשְׁבִיל זוּלָתוֹ, וַאֲפִילּוּ הַצַּדִּיקִים גְּמוּרִים סוֹבְלִים עֲווֹנוֹת שְׁאָר בְּנֵי דוֹרָם לִהְיוֹתָם מִקּוֹמָה אַחַת
wherefore each must suffer for his fellow, consummate tzaddikim bearing the iniquities of their contemporaries because all are one body;
כְּמוֹ כַּאֲשֶׁר הָרֶגֶל כּוֹאֵב — סוֹבֵל גַּם הָרֹאשׁ הַיִּסּוּרִין שֶׁיֵּשׁ מִכְּאֵב שֶׁבָּרֶגֶל.
just as when the foot aches, the head suffers the pain of the foot.
אֲבָל יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, שֶׁהוּא הָיָה בְּדוֹרוֹ כּוֹלֵל הַכְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל כּוּלּוֹ
But our father Jacob, who in his generation embodied collective Knesset Israel in its entirety;
וְכֵן כָּל דּוֹרוֹת הָעֲתִידִים לָצֵאת מִמֶּנּוּ כּוּלָּם כְּלוּלִים בּוֹ, כַּאֲשֶׁר הוּא תִּיקֵּן נַפְשׁוֹ — הֲרֵי כָּל הַקּוֹמָה שְׁלֵימָה
and all future generations were encompassed within him, when he rectified his soul, the entire stature was made complete;
וּלְפִיכָךְ מִצַּד עַצְמוֹ לֹא מֵת כְּלָל בֶּאֱמֶת, רַק מִצַּד הַהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת דְּדוֹרוֹתָיו בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁלֹּא נִתְבָּרְרוּ עַדַיִין, לֹא נִתְגַּלָּה זֶה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה:
wherefore he truly never died, veiled in this world only because his future generations were not yet refined!

6.h: אוֹת ל״א — רַבֵּינוּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ כְּנִיצוֹץ יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ, מָשִׁיחַ שֶׁבְּדוֹרוֹ, וְתִיקּוּן כָּל הַנְּפָשׁוֹת הַנִּתְלוֹת בּוֹ — Section 31: Rabbeinu HaKadosh as the Spark of Jacob, the Potential Messiah, and His Friday Twilight Visits

The theme: Rabbi Yehudah HaNasi (Rebbe) embodying the spark of Jacob, rectifying his entire generation, and visiting his home every Friday twilight. Rabbeinu HaKadosh—titled "holy" unconditionally because he attained the apex of holiness achievable in this world—was the soul-spark of our father Jacob (Arizal, Sefer Yayin HaMeshumar). Therefore, he did not die, returning to his home every Friday twilight to recite Kiddush (Kesubos 103a). As Nasi and shepherd of the era, he encompassed all souls of his generation; attaining absolute holiness meant that no defect could touch him, having rectified all souls bound to him. Thus Sanhedrin (98b) states: "If Mashiach is among the living, he is someone like our holy Master," for he was worthy of being Mashiach, having rectified his contemporaries alongside himself. Yet the era was not ripe for open redemption, because future generations issuing from them were not yet purified. Rebbe rectified his own soul and all souls of his generation and his descendants unto the end of time; but the descendants of his contemporaries across future generations were not yet purified, preventing the End of Days and the Resurrection. Personally, Rebbe never died, codifying the Mishnah which is the essential reviving dew of Torah (tal Torah) and the Holy Spirit of the Sages!

p: וְכֵן רַבֵּינוּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ שֶׁנִּקְרָא כֵּן בִּסְתָם, כִּי נִתְיַיחֵד בְּתֹקֶף הַקְּדוּשָׁה שֶׁאֶפְשָׁר לְהַשִּׂיג בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
And so our holy Master (Rabbeinu HaKadosh), who is titled "holy" without qualification because he was uniquely distinguished in the highest holiness achievable in this world;
הָיָה נִיצוֹץ יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, כִּידוּעַ מֵהָאֲרִיזַ״ל [עַיֵּין בְּסֵפֶר ״יַיִן הַמְשֻׁמָּר״ וְזוּלָתוֹ]
was the soul-spark of our father Jacob, as known from the Arizal (Sefer Yayin HaMeshumar);
דְּעַל כֵּן ״אָתֵי כָּל בֵּי שִׁמְשֵׁי לְבֵיתֵיהּ״, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּכְתוּבּוֹת (ק״ג סוֹף עַמּוּד א׳), דְּגַם כֵּן לֹא מֵת
wherefore "he visited his home every twilight" on Friday evening (Kesubos 103a), he likewise having never died;
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁהוּא הָיָה נָשִׂיא וּפַרְנַס הַדּוֹר וְכוֹלֵל כָּל נַפְשׁוֹת דּוֹרוֹ
meaning he was the Nasi and shepherd of the generation, encompassing all souls of his era;
וּכְשֶׁהִשְׁלִים נַפְשׁוֹ כָּל כָּךְ עַד שֶׁיִּזְכֶּה לְשֵׁם ״קָדוֹשׁ״ סְתָם — הַיְינוּ כְּשֶׁלֹּא יַגִּיעַ לוֹ שׁוּם פְּגָם עוֹד
and when he perfected his soul so completely as to merit the title "holy" unconditionally, no flaw could reach him;
וְעַל כָּרְחָךְ שֶׁהִשְׁלִים גַּם נַפְשׁוֹת כָּל דּוֹרוֹ הָאֲחוּזִים בּוֹ.
proving perforce that he had rectified the souls of his entire generation bound unto him.
וּלְפִיכָךְ אִיתָא בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (צ״ח סוֹף עַמּוּד ב׳): ״אִי מִן חַיַּיָּא הוּא — כְּגוֹן רַבֵּינוּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ״
And therefore Sanhedrin (98b) states: "If Mashiach is among the living, he is someone like our holy Master";
שֶׁחָשְׁבוּ עָלָיו שֶׁהוּא מָשִׁיחַ, כִּי כְּבָר תִּיקֵּן נַפְשׁוֹ כָּל כָּךְ עַד שֶׁהִמְשִׁיךְ וְתִיקֵּן כָּל דּוֹרוֹ עִמּוֹ
for they considered him Mashiach, having rectified his soul so extensively as to rectify his entire generation with him;
אֶלָּא שֶׁעַדַיִין לֹא הָיָה הַדּוֹר כְּדַאי שֶׁיִּהְיֶה גַּם אֶצְלָם בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת כֵּן
except that the generation was not yet worthy that this be openly manifest;
כִּי עַדַיִין לֹא נִתְקְנוּ גַּם הַדּוֹרוֹת הַבָּאִים הַכְּלוּלִים בָּהֶם, דִּלְעוֹלָם נַפְשׁוֹת הַבָּנִים כְּלוּלִים בַּאֲבוֹתָם.
because future generations encompassed within them were not yet refined, the souls of children being rooted in their ancestors.
וְרַבֵּינוּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ תִּיקֵּן נַפְשׁוֹ לְגַמְרֵי עִם כָּל הַנִּתְלֶה בּוֹ מִזַּרְעוֹ עַד סוֹף כָּל הַדּוֹרוֹת, וְכֵן מִנַּפְשׁוֹת כָּל בְּנֵי דּוֹרוֹ
And our holy Master rectified his own soul and all souls of his descendants unto the end of time, as well as the souls of his contemporaries;
אֲבָל מַה שֶּׁנִּתְלוּ בְּנַפְשׁוֹת דּוֹרוֹ מִדּוֹרוֹתֵיהֶם אַחֲרֵיהֶם עַד סוֹף כָּל הַדּוֹרוֹת — זֶה לֹא נִתְקַן עַדַיִין, דְּזֶה לֹא הָיָה נִתְלֶה בְּתִיקּוּנוֹ
but the future generations issuing from his contemporaries were not yet rectified, not depending upon his personal repair;
וּלְפִיכָךְ לֹא זָכוּ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה אָז עֵת קֵץ וּתְחִיַּיִת הַמֵּתִים, וְשֶׁיִּהְיֶה הוּא הַמָּשִׁיחַ.
wherefore they did not merit the final End and the Resurrection, nor that he be actualized Mashiach.
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם הוּא זָכָה לְנַפְשֵׁיהּ דְּמִצַּד עַצְמוֹ לֹא מֵת, אֶלָּא שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת בָּרוּר מִצַּד הַדּוֹר
Nevertheless he merited for himself that he never died, veiled only on account of the generation;
וְהוּא יִסַּד הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, שֶׁזֶּהוּ עִיקַּר הַטַּל תּוֹרָה הַמְחַיֵּיהוּ וְרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ דַּחֲכָמִים הַמֵּבִיא לִתְחִיַּיִת הַמֵּתִים:
and he compiled the Mishnah, which is the essential reviving dew of Torah (tal Torah) and the Holy Spirit of the Sages that brings to the Resurrection!

6.h: אוֹת ל״ב — ״מִשֶּׁמֵּת רַבִּי בָּטְלָה עֲנָוָה וְיִרְאַת חֵטְא״, עִקְבוֹת מָשִׁיחַ, וְרַב נַחְמָן כְּמַחֲזִיר הָעֲטָרָה — Section 32: "When Rebbe Died, Humility and Fear of Sin Ceased", The Footsteps of Mashiach, and Rav Nachman Restoring the Crown

The theme: The conclusion of Mishnah Sotah, Rebbe's passing as the destruction of the Temple in soul, and Rav Nachman restoring the crown in Babylon. Mishnah Sotah concludes: "When Rebbe died, humility and fear of sin ceased" (Sotah 49a)—the two rungs directly preceding holiness in Avodah Zarah (20b). These three constitute the three upper intellectual faculties (Gimmel Rishonot) of a scholar. Holiness itself cannot cease, for Hashem's salvation never ceases; cessation applies only to human striving (anivut in Binah and yir'at chet in Chokhmah). With Rebbe's death, the manifest presence of these rungs departed, leaving only the lower seven practical attributes (Zat) fencing against immorality. Rebbe's passing was parallel to the destruction of the Holy Temple: the Temple was the sanctuary of holiness in Space (Olam), while Rebbe was the sanctuary in Soul (Nefesh), marking the onset of the "footsteps of Mashiach" (ikvata d'Meshicha). Later Sages appended the Baraita of Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair to conclude with hope. In Babylon, the Amoraim re-established Torah in darkness ("He has set me in dark places", Eichah 3:6; Sanhedrin 24a). The Gemara concludes Sotah with Rav Nachman declaring: "Do not teach that fear of sin ceased, for there is I!" (Sotah 49b). Rav Nachman proclaimed in Sanhedrin (98b): "If Mashiach is among the living, he is someone like me," being the second after Rebbe worthy of being Mashiach, completing all rungs from within the darkness of exile!

p: וּמִשְׁנָיוֹת מַסֶּכֶת סוֹטָה מְסַיֵּים: ״מִשֶּׁמֵּת רַבִּי — בָּטְלָה עֲנָוָה וְיִרְאַת חֵטְא״ (סוֹטָה מ״ט עַמּוּד א׳)
And the Mishnah of Tractate Sotah concludes: "When Rebbe died, humility and fear of sin ceased" (Sotah 49a);
שֶׁהֵם ב׳ מַדְרֵיגוֹת הַקּוֹדְמוֹת לִקְדוּשָׁה, כְּפִי הַסֵּדֶר שֶׁבְּמַסֶּכֶת עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה (כ׳ עַמּוּד ב׳), שֶׁהוּא שְׁלֵימוּת הַקְּדוּשָׁה שֶׁזָּכָה לָהּ רַבִּי
which are the two rungs preceding holiness in the sequence of Avodah Zarah (20b), representing the consummate holiness Rebbe achieved;
וְאֵלֶּה הַשְּׁלֹשָׁה הֵם ג׳ רִאשׁוֹנוֹת שֶׁל הַקּוֹמָה הַשְּׁלֵימָה דְּתַלְמִיד חָכָם הַמַּתְחִיל בַּתּוֹרָה.
and these three are the three upper intellectual faculties (Gimmel Rishonot) of a scholar beginning in Torah.
וְהַקְּדוּשָׁה הִיא הַמַּדְרֵיגָה עֶלְיוֹנָה שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה מִקּוֹמַת אָדָם, שֶׁהוּא מַה שֶּׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עוֹזְרוֹ
And holiness is the supernal rung transcending human stature, bestowed when Hashem assists him;
וּבָהּ לֹא שַׁיָּיךְ בִּיטּוּל, דִּישׁוּעַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אֵינָהּ בְּטֵלָה חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, וְשִׁפְעוֹ אֵינוֹ פּוֹסֵק
wherein cessation cannot apply, for Hashem's salvation never ceases, God forbid, and His bounty never halts;
וְהַבִּיטּוּל שַׁיָּיךְ רַק בְּמַה שֶּׁבְּהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת אָדָם, וְהֵם ב׳ הַקּוֹדְמוֹת [עֲנָוָה וְיִרְאַת חֵטְא]
cessation applying strictly unto human striving, namely the two preceding rungs [humility and fear of sin];

שֶׁהָעֲנָוָה הוּא בַּבִּינָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב, וְהַיִּרְאַת חֵטְא הוּא בַּחָכְמָה שֶׁבַּמּוֹחַ, שֶׁהוּא תַּכְלִית שְׁלֵימוּת הַיִּרְאָה שֶׁעַל יְדֵי הַכָּרַת הַנֹּכַח דַּ״ה׳ לְנֶגְדִּי תָמִיד״ (תְּהִלִּים ט״ז:ח׳)
humility residing in Binah in the heart, and fear of sin in Chokhmah in the brain, achieved through perceiving "I set Hashem always before me" (Tehillim 16:8);
וּמִשֶּׁמֵּת רַבִּי שֶׁהוּא שְׁלֵימוּת הַקְּדוּשָׁה הַנִּמְצָא בְּנַפְשׁוֹת דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה — בָּטְלוּ גַּם ב׳ אֵלֶּה.
and when Rebbe died, who embodied manifest holiness in this world, these two rungs ceased as well.
וְנִשְׁאַר רַק הַשֶּׁבַע תַּחְתּוֹנוֹת שֶׁהֵם שְׁלֵימוּת כֹּחוֹת הַמַּעֲשֶׂה הַכּוֹלְלִים הַקְּדוּשָׁה שֶׁבְּפֹעַל בְּהַגְדָּרַת עֶרְוָה
Leaving merely the lower seven attributes of action, which comprise practical holiness in fencing against immorality;
וְשׁוֹנֵי הַמִּשְׁנָיוֹת בַּדּוֹרוֹת הַמְאוּחָרִים חִבְּרוּ אַחֲרֵי זֶה הַבָּרַיְיתָא דְּ״מִשֶּׁחָרַב בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ״ וְ״עִקְבְתָא דִּמְשִׁיחָא״ (סוֹטָה מ״ט עַמּוּד ב׳)
and the Redactors in later generations appended following this the Baraita of "from when the Temple was destroyed" and "the footsteps of Mashiach" (Sotah 49b);
כִּי מִיתַת רַבֵּינוּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ... הִיא מַמָּשׁ חוּרְבַּן בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ
for the death of Rabbeinu HaKadosh was literally like the destruction of the Holy Temple;
שֶׁהוּא מִשְׁכַּן הַקְּדוּשָׁה בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל בַּמָּקוֹם וּמִצַּד הָעוֹלָם, וְרַבִּי הָיָה מִשְׁכַּן הַקְּדוּשָׁה מִצַּד הַנֶּפֶשׁ.
the Temple being the sanctuary of holiness in Space (Olam), while Rebbe was the sanctuary of holiness in Soul (Nefesh).
הוּא הָרִאשׁוֹן אַחַר הַחֻרְבָּן שֶׁהָיָה רָאוּי לִהְיוֹת מָשִׁיחַ אִלְמָלֵא זָכוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל, וּמִמֶּנּוּ הַתְחָלַת עִקְּבוֹת מָשִׁיחַ
He was the first after the Destruction worthy of being Mashiach had Israel merited, and from him began the footsteps of Mashiach;
וּכְדֵי לְסַיֵּים בְּטוֹב, סִיְּימוּ בַּבָּרַיְיתָא דְּרַבִּי פִּנְחָס בֶּן יָאִיר בְּסֵדֶר הַשְׁלָמַת הָאָדָם מִצַּד הַגְדָּרַת הַמַּעֲשִׂים לְבַד
and to conclude on a good note, they concluded with the Baraita of Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair tracing human completion through moral action;
וּלְפִי מַה שֶּׁהָיָה הַדּוֹר אָז אַחַר זְמַן רַבִּי, הָיָה בִּיטּוּל גָּמוּר לַעֲנָוָה וְיִרְאַת חֵטְא.
for in the generation following Rebbe, there was a total cessation of manifest humility and fear of sin.

אֲבָל בַּדּוֹרוֹת שֶׁאַחַר כָּךְ, מִכִּי אֲתוֹ רַב לְבָבֶל וְהִרְבִּיץ תּוֹרָה הַרְבֵּה שָׁם, וְקָמוּ דּוֹרוֹת הָאָמוֹרָאִים שֶׁסִּיגְּלוּ תּוֹרָה הַרְבֵּה בִּקְדוּשָׁה וּבְטָהֳרָה וּבְרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ שֶׁבָּהֶם
But in subsequent eras, when Rav arrived in Babylonia and disseminated Torah, the Amoraim arose acquiring Torah in holiness and the Holy Spirit;
עַד שֶׁהוֹסִיפוּ הַתַּלְמוּד עַל הַמִּשְׁנָיוֹת שֶׁיִּסַּד רַבִּי, שֶׁהוּא הַשְׁלָמַת הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
adding the Gemara unto Rebbe's Mishnah, completing the Oral Torah;
הוֹסִיפוּ שָׁם: ״לָא תִּיתְנוּ [עֲנָוָה דְּאִיכָּא אֲנָא... לָא תִּיתְנוּ יִרְאַת חֵטְא] דְּאִיכָּא אֲנָא״ (סוֹטָה מ״ט סוֹף עַמּוּד ב׳) בְּדִבְרֵי רַב נַחְמָן
they concluded Sotah (49b) with the declaration of Rav Nachman: "Do not teach that fear of sin ceased, for there is I!"
וְרַב נַחְמָן הוּא שֶׁאָמַר עַל עַצְמוֹ גַּם כֵּן שָׁם בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (צ״ח סוֹף עַמּוּד ב׳): ״אִי מִן חַיַּיָּא הוּא — כְּגוֹן אֲנָא״
And Rav Nachman declared concerning himself in Sanhedrin (98b): "If Mashiach is among the living, he is someone like me";
וּכְפִי הַנִּרְאֶה הוּא הָיָה הַשֵּׁנִי אַחַר רַבִּי שֶׁהָיָה רָאוּי לִהְיוֹת מָשִׁיחַ אִם הָיוּ הַדּוֹר כְּדַאי
being the second after Rebbe worthy of being Mashiach had the generation possessed merit;
שֶׁהָיָה גַּם כֵּן רֹאשׁ בְּדוֹרוֹ הַכּוֹלֵל כָּל נַפְשׁוֹת דּוֹרוֹ, וְהִשְׁלִים עַצְמוֹ בְּתַכְלִית הַשְּׁלֵימוּת בְּכָל מַדְרֵיגוֹת קוֹמָתוֹ
serving as the head encompassing all souls of his era, having perfected himself across all rungs of his stature;
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא נִקְרָא בְּשֵׁם ״קָדוֹשׁ״ כְּרַבִּי, לְפִי שֶׁהָיָה מִצַּד הַמַּחֲשַׁכִּים וְהַהֶעְלֵם וְלֹא בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת לַכֹּל:
though not titled "holy" like Rebbe, because he operated within the darkness and concealment of Babylonia and not in open manifestation!

6.h: אוֹת ל״ג — רַב נַחְמָן בְּ״דִינֵי מָמוֹנוֹת״, רַב יוֹסֵף שֶׁנִּסְתַּמָּא לִקְדוּשָׁה, וְתִיקּוּן עֵינוֹ שֶׁל בִּלְעָם הָרָשָׁע — Section 33: Rav Nachman Deciding Monetary Law Alone, Rav Yosef Blinding Himself for Holiness, and Rectifying Balaam's Eye

The theme: Rav Nachman testifying about himself in monetary law, Rav Yosef blinding his eyes against worldly lust, and rectifying the evil eye of Balaam. Rav Nachman’s fear of sin was revealed only unto himself; he testified about himself to restore the crown to its pristine glory. He restored the rung of Chokhmah, declaring: "Someone like me may judge monetary cases alone" (Sanhedrin 5a), monetary law being the height of wisdom (Bava Batra 175b; Bechoros 37a). Scripture states: "Let another praise you, and not your own mouth" (Mishlei 27:2); but the Zohar (Balak 193b) expounds: "if no stranger is there to praise you, your mouth may speak" to declare the halachic standard without arrogance. Before Rav Nachman, Rav Yosef initiated the restoration of these rungs by willingly becoming blind so that he would never gaze upon unseemly matters (Teshuvot HaGeonim, Sha'arei Teshuvah §178). While Balaam was blinded because he denied that Israel’s physical desires were holy—his evil heart bursting his eye (shuryana d'eina b'liba, Avodah Zarah 28b, 65a)—Rav Yosef chose blindness out of passionate yearning that all his faculties be holy, conquering the eye to purge the heart! A blind man is accounted as dead (Nedarim 64b), neutralizing worldly cravings and attaining consummate humility (anivut) through Binah. Rav Nachman succeeded him, completing the ladder of Sotah so that every Jew, even an am ha-aretz, can ascend from rung to rung until all his deeds are dedicated purely for the sake of Heaven, holy unto Hashem!

p: וְאַף הַיִּרְאַת חֵטְא שֶׁהוּא תְּחִלַּת הַגִּלּוּי, לֹא נִתְגַּלָּה אֶלָּא לוֹ לְבַד
And even fear of sin, which is the beginning of manifestation, was revealed unto Rav Nachman alone;
וְהוּא שֶׁהֵעִיד וְגִילָּה עַל עַצְמוֹ: ״דְּאִיכָּא אֲנָא״ — הַשָּׁלֵם בְּיִרְאַת חֵטְא כְּרַבִּי
he testifying concerning himself: "there is I"—complete in the fear of sin like Rebbe;
וּבָזֶה הֶחֱזִיר הָעֲטָרָה לְיוֹשְׁנָהּ, דְּאַחֲרָיו כָּל אֶחָד יִמְשׁוֹךְ לִזְכּוֹת וּלְהַגִּיעַ לִשְׁלֵימוּת כָּל הַמַּדְרֵיגוֹת
restoring the crown to its pristine glory, so that every subsequent sage might strive to attain all rungs;
דְּמִשֶּׁמֵּת רַב נַחְמָן — לֹא בָּטְלָה עוֹד.
for from when Rav Nachman passed away, it ceased no longer.
וְרַב נַחְמָן הֶחֱזִיר הַיִּרְאַת חֵטְא שֶׁהוּא מַדְרֵיגַת הַחָכְמָה
And Rav Nachman restored fear of sin, which is the rung of Chokhmah;
וְעַל כֵּן אָמַר עַל עַצְמוֹ בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (ה׳ רֵישׁ עַמּוּד א׳): ״כְּגוֹן אֲנָא דָּיֵין דִּינֵי מָמוֹנוֹת בְּיְחִידִי״, שֶׁהוּא מִצַּד שְׁלֵימוּת הַחָכְמָה
wherefore he stated in Sanhedrin (5a): "Someone like me may judge monetary cases alone," flowing from consummate wisdom;
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּסוֹף בָּבָא בַּתְרָא (קע״ה עַמּוּד ב׳): ״הָרוֹצֶה שֶׁיִּתְחַכֵּם — יַעֲסוֹק בְּדִינֵי מָמוֹנוֹת״
as stated in Bava Batra (175b): "He who wishes to acquire wisdom, let him engage in monetary law";
וְכֵן בִּבְכוֹרוֹת (ל״ז רֵישׁ עַמּוּד א׳): ״דְּחָכָם מַתִּיר לְבַדּוֹ, אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: כְּגוֹן אֲנָא״.
and in Bechoros (37a): "an expert sage permits a blemish alone—Rav Nachman saying: such as I".
וְאַף עַל פִּי דְּמִקְרָא צֹוֵוחַ: ״יְהַלֶּלְךָ זָר — וְלֹא פִיךָ״ (מִשְׁלֵי כ״ז:ב׳)
And even though Scripture proclaims: "Let another man praise you, and not your own mouth" (Mishlei 27:2);
אֲבָל הוּא לֹא בָּא לְהַלֵּל אֶת עַצְמוֹ, רַק לְהוֹדִיעַ הַדִּין גֶּדֶר הַמּוּמְחֶה וְהֶחָכָם
Rav Nachman came not to praise himself, but to declare the halachic definition of an expert judge;
וְלֹא אָמַר עַל אַחֵר כִּי לֹא הִגִּיעַ לִשְׁלֵימוּת הַחָכְמָה אֶלָּא הוּא
and could not state it regarding another because none had attained that wisdom save he;
וּבָטַח לִבּוֹ שֶׁמַּכִּיר עֶרְכּוֹ בֶּאֱמֶת וְלֹא מִגַּסּוּת הָרוּחַ
his heart knowing his true stature without arrogance;
וְזֶה עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּנְדָרִים (ס״ב עַמּוּד א׳): ״שְׁרֵי לְאוֹדוֹעֵי בְּאַתְרָא דְּלָא יָדְעוּ לֵיהּ״
after the manner of Nedarim (62a): "it is permitted to make oneself known where one is not known".

וּבִתְשׁוּבוֹת הָרַשְׁבָּ״א (חֵלֶק א׳ סִימָן פ״ד) הֵבִיא: ״דַּאֲמַר לֵיהּ לְרַב פַּפָּא: מַה שִּׁמְךָ? אָמַר לֵיהּ: רַב פַּפָּא. אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וְהָכְתִיב: ׳יְהַלֶּלְךָ זָר׳? אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וְאִי אֵין זָר — פִּיךָ!״

And Responsa Rashba (I, §84) cites: "they asked Rav Pappa: What is your name? He said: Rav Pappa. They challenged: Is it not written 'let another praise you'? He answered: If there is no stranger, your own mouth!";
וּבַזֹּוהַר בָּלָק (קצ״ג סוֹף עַמּוּד ב׳) אִיתָא: דְּהַיְינוּ לִפְתּוֹחַ פִּיו בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה וְלֹא לְשַׁבֵּחַ נַפְשֵׁיהּ
and the Zohar (Balak 193b) teaches: this means opening one's mouth in Torah novellae and not for self-praise.
וְרַב יוֹסֵף הָיָה לְפָנָיו הַמַּתְחִיל בְּהַחְזָרַת מַדְרֵיגוֹת אֵלּוּ
And Rav Yosef preceded him, initiating the restoration of these rungs;
וְהוּא נִסְתַּמָּא עַל יְדֵי שֶׁלֹּא רָצָה לְהַבִּיט מִצְּדָדִין וּלְפָנָיו, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּתְשׁוּבוֹת הַגְּאוֹנִים (שַׁעֲרֵי תְּשׁוּבָה סִימָן קע״ח)
becoming blind because he refused to gaze sideways and forward (Sha'arei Teshuvah §178);
וּמִפְּנֵי שֶׁרָצָה לְסַלֵּק עַצְמוֹ מֵחֵיזוּ דְּהַאי עָלְמָא דְּ״עַיִן רוֹאָה וּמַכְנִיס הִרְהוּרִים לַלֵּב לִהְיוֹת חוֹמֵד״
wishing to withdraw from worldly vanities where the eye sees and the heart covets.
וְעֵינוֹ שֶׁל אוֹתוֹ רָשָׁע בִּלְעָם נִסְתַּמָּא בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁלֹּא הֶאֱמִין בִּקְדֻשַּׁת יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁיִּהְיוּ גַּם חֶמְדוֹתֵיהֶם שֶׁבָּעִנְיָנִים הַגּוּפָנִיִּם מָלֵא קְדוּשָׁה
While the eye of wicked Balaam was blinded because he denied Israel's holiness, refusing to believe their bodily desires were holy;
וְהוּא מִפְּנֵי לִבּוֹ שֶׁהָיָה מָלֵא זוּהֲמָא, וְ״שׁוּרְיָינָא דְּעֵינָא — בְּלִבָּא תַּלְיָא״, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה (כ״ח עַמּוּד ב׳)
his heart being filled with defilement, and "the optic nerves of the eye depend upon the heart" (Avodah Zarah 28b);
וּמִזֶּה הָיָה לוֹ עַיִן רָעָה, וְעַל כֵּן פָּקְעָה עֵינוֹ
whence he possessed an evil eye, wherefore his eye burst.
וְעֵינוֹ שֶׁל אוֹתוֹ צַדִּיק [רַב יוֹסֵף] נִסְתַּמָּא עַל יְדֵי שֶׁחָפֵץ וְנִשְׁתּוֹקֵק גַּם כֵּן לִזְכּוֹת לִקְדוּשָׁה זוֹ שֶׁיִּהְיוּ כָּל חֶמְדוֹתָיו בִּקְדוּשָׁה
Whereas the eyes of that tzaddik [Rav Yosef] were blinded because he yearned that all his desires be in holiness;
וְנִתְרַצָּה לְהִסְתַּמֵּא לְגַמְרֵי כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יִרְאֶה שׁוּם דָּבָר שֶׁיָּבִיא חֶמְדָּה זָרָה לַלֵּב, וְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עָשָׂה רְצוֹנוֹ
willing to become blind so that he would never gaze upon anything introducing alien lust, and Hashem fulfilled his desire;
וְ״הַסּוּמָא — חָשׁוּב כְּמֵת״ (נְדָרִים ס״ד עַמּוּד ב׳), וּבָזֶה נִתְבַּטְּלוּ אֶצְלוֹ כָּל חֶמְדוֹת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה
and "a blind man is accounted as dead" (Nedarim 64b), neutralizing all worldly desires;
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה זָכָה לַעֲנָוָה הַשְּׁלֵימָה הַבָּאָה מִכֹּחַ הַבִּינָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב שֶׁהוּא הָאַתְחַלְתָּא לַקְּדוּשָׁה הַשְּׁלֵימָה
through which he attained consummate humility stemming from Binah, the gateway to complete holiness;
וּבָזֶה הָיָה אַתְחַלְתָּא לְהַשָּׂגַת ג׳ רִאשׁוֹנוֹת וְעַד שְׁלֵימוּת הַקְּדוּשָׁה וְרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ הַגָּמוּר, וּבָא רַב נַחְמָן אַחֲרָיו וְהִשְׁלִים הַכֹּל.
this serving as the inception for attaining the three upper crowns unto the Holy Spirit, followed by Rav Nachman who completed all.
וְזֶהוּ הַשְׁלָמַת מַסֶּכֶת סוֹטָה בְּהַגְדָּרָה בְּפֹעַל כְּפִי הָאֶפְשָׁר
And this is the completion of Tractate Sotah in practical moral restraint;
שֶׁמִּזֶּה כָּל אֶחָד וַאֲפִילּוּ עַם הָאָרֶץ יוּכַל לְהַגִּיעַ מִמַּדְרֵיגָה לְמַדְרֵיגָה עַד סוֹף כָּל דַּרְגִּין
through which every Jew, even an unlearned commoner, can ascend from rung to rung unto the very summit;
בְּהַשְׁפָּעַת הַקְּדוּשָׁה הַגְּמוּרָה לַלֵּב, שֶׁיִּהְיוּ כָּל מַעֲשָׂיו לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם — כּוּלּוֹ קֹדֶשׁ לַה׳:
drawing down consummate holiness into the heart, so that all his deeds are dedicated for Heaven, entirely holy unto Hashem!

7.h: יִשְׂרָאֵל קְדוֹשִׁים — פֶּרֶק ז׳

אוֹת א׳ — שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַקְּדוּשָׁה בַּשַּׁבָּת, בְּחִירַת יַעֲקֹב מִבֶּטֶן, וְהַאֲחָזָה בַּעֲקֵבוֹ שֶׁל עֵשָׂו — Section 1: The Sabbath as the Root of Holiness, Jacob Chosen from the Womb, and Heeled to Esau

The theme: The primordial appearance of holiness in Shabbat, its descent into space (Sinai) and soul (firstborns and Israel), and Jacob seizing Esau's heel. The word "holiness" (kedushah) appears first in the Torah concerning Shabbat: "And God blessed the seventh day, and sanctified it" (Bereishis 2:3). In Midrash Rabbah, the first occurrence of a word reveals its foundational root: the root of all holiness is the immutable sanctity of Shabbat, established by Hashem as a distinct realm of blessing whence supernal sanctity descends. Human preparation is secondary to the divine bestowal; from time, holiness descended into Space—first manifest at Mount Horeb ("the place whereon you stand is holy ground", Shemos 3:5), prepared for the Giving of the Torah. In Soul, holiness was manifest first at the Exodus in the sanctification of the firstborn ("Sanctify unto Me all the firstborn", Shemos 13:2), and subsequently at Sinai in collective Israel: "a kingdom of priests, and a holy nation" (Shemos 19:6). Hashem chose Jacob unconditionally before human striving: "Was not Esau Jacob's brother? yet I loved Jacob" (Malachi 1:2). Although twins issuing from a single drop (Yevamos 98a)—identical in physical origin—Esau was an apostate Israelite (Yisrael mumar, Kiddushin 19a) who could lose his Jewish title before Jacob's final selection. Isaac erred, seeking to bless Esau as the firstborn; but Jacob took the birthright and blessings by stealth (b'okvah), for in the reality of this world darkness precedes light (reisha chashocha v'hadar nehora, Berachos 2a). Every righteous man is paired opposite a wicked counterpart ("God has made the one opposite the other", Koheles 7:14), through which each can take the other's portion in Gan Eden or Gehinnom (Chagigah 15a)!

p: וּפַעַם רִאשׁוֹן שֶׁנִּזְכַּר בַּתּוֹרָה מִלַּת ״קְדוּשָׁה״ — הוּא אֵצֶל יוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת, מִיָּד בִּבְרִיאַת הָעוֹלָם בְּפָרָשַׁת בְּרֵאשִׁית: ״וַיְבָרֶךְ [אֱלֹהִים אֶת יוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי] וַיְקַדֵּשׁ אֹתוֹ״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית ב:ג)

And the first time the word "holiness" (kedushah) is mentioned in the Torah is in connection with the Sabbath day, immediately at the creation of the world in Parashat Bereishis: "And God blessed the seventh day, and sanctified it" (Bereishis 2:3);
וְקִבַּלְתִּי שֶׁבִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה, וְעִנְיָן: בְּמָקוֹם שֶׁמִּלָּה זוֹ נִזְכָּר פַּעַם רִאשׁוֹנָה בַּתּוֹרָה — שָׁם הוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ הָעִנְיָן
and I received by tradition from Bereishis Rabbah a fundamental principle: in the place where a word is mentioned for the first time in the Torah, there lies the essential root of that matter.
וְכֵן שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַקְּדוּשָׁה שֶׁיֶּשְׁנוֹ בָּעוֹלָם הוּא קְדֻשַּׁת יוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת
And so the foundational root of holiness that exists in the world is the sanctity of the Sabbath day;
שֶׁהִיא קְדוּשָׁה קְבִיעָא וְקַיָּימָא, שֶׁקָּבַע הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּעוֹלָמוֹ זְמַן מְיוּחָד לִבְרָכָה וּקְדוּשָׁה, שֶׁבֵּירְכוֹ וְקִדְּשׁוֹ
which is an immutable, perpetual holiness (kedushah k'vi'a v'kayma) established by the Blessed Name in His world as a distinct realm for blessing and sanctity, having blessed and sanctified it.
וְהַקְּדוּשָׁה נִמְשֶׁכֶת מֵהַבְּרָכָה שֶׁהִיא הַשְׁפָּעָה עֶלְיוֹנָה
And holiness is drawn from blessing, which is supernal divine influx;
וּמִמֵּילָא כְּשֶׁמְּקוּשָּׁר לְשֶׁלְּמַעְלָה, נִמְשַׁךְ עָלָיו רוּחַ קְדוּשָׁה מִלְּמַעְלָה
and automatically, when one is bound unto the realm Above, a spirit of holiness descends upon him from Above;
וְזֶהוּ עִיקַּר הַקְּדוּשָׁה: לִזְכּוֹת שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מְקַדְּשָׁם
this being the core of holiness: to merit that the Blessed Name sanctifies them;
אֲבָל הֲכָנַת אָדָם לִקְדוּשָׁה מַה הִיא חֲשׁוּבָה, וְכַמָּה יָכוֹל לְקַדֵּשׁ עַצְמוֹ
for what is mortal preparation for holiness worth, and how much can man sanctify himself through his own power?
וְגַם זֶה אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא אַחַר שֶׁקִּידֵּשׁ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ יוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת וְנָתַן קְדוּשָׁה בַּזְּמַן, מִזֶּה נִמְשַׁךְ גַּם לַמָּקוֹם וְלַנֶּפֶשׁ
And even this human preparation exists only after Hashem sanctified Shabbat and infused holiness into Time (Zman), whence it expanded into Space (Makon) and Soul (Nefesh).
וּבַמָּקוֹם — הַקְּדוּשָׁה הָרִאשׁוֹנָה הָיָה בְּהַר הָאֱלֹהִים חֹרֵב
And in Space—the initial manifestation of holiness occurred at the mountain of God, Horeb;
דְּשָׁם נֶאֱמַר לְמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בְּפָרָשַׁת שְׁמוֹת: ״[כִּי] הַמָּקוֹם [אֲשֶׁר אַתָּה עוֹמֵד עָלָיו — ] אַדְמַת קֹדֶשׁ [הוּא]״ (שְׁמוֹת ג:ה)
where it was said unto Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him, in Parashat Shemot: "for the place whereon you stand is holy ground" (Shemos 3:5);
וּלְפִי שֶׁכְּבָר נִתְקַדֵּשׁ אָז לְמַתַּן תּוֹרָה מִשֶּׁבָּא מֹשֶׁה לְשָׁם, שֶׁהָיָה מוּכָן לְקַבָּלַת תּוֹרָה עָלָיו
because Mount Sinai was already consecrated for the Giving of the Torah once Moshe arrived there, being prepared to receive the Torah upon it.
וּבַנֶּפֶשׁ — מִתְּחִלָּה בִּיצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם הַבְּכוֹרוֹת: ״קַדֶּשׁ לִי כָל בְּכוֹר״ (שְׁמוֹת י״ג:ב׳)
And in Soul—initially at the Exodus from Egypt among the firstborns: "Sanctify unto Me all the firstborn" (Shemos 13:2);
וְאַחַר כָּךְ בְּמַתַּן תּוֹרָה כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל: ״[וְאַתֶּם תִּהְיוּ לִי] מַמְלֶכֶת כֹּהֲנִים וְגוֹי קָדוֹשׁ״ (שָׁם י״ט:ו׳)
and subsequently at the Giving of the Torah across collective Israel: "and you shall be unto Me a kingdom of priests, and a holy nation" (ibid. 19:6);
כִּי הַכֹּהֲנִים הֵם הַקְּדוֹשִׁים, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ: ״לְקַדְּשׁוֹ לְכַהֲנוֹ לִי״ (שְׁמוֹת כ״ח:ג׳), וְעוֹד טוּבָא
for Kohanim are the consecrated ones: "to sanctify him, that he may minister unto Me in the priest's office" (ibid. 28:3), and many passages;
וְהַבְּכוֹרוֹת שִׁמְּשׁוּ בִּכְהֻנָּה עַד הָעֵגֶל (זְבָחִים קי״ב עַמּוּד ב׳)
and the firstborns officiated in the priesthood until the sin of the Golden Calf (Zevachim 112b);
וּבְמַתַּן תּוֹרָה נַעֲשׂוּ כוּלָּם ״מַמְלֶכֶת כֹּהֲנִים״, וְהַיְינוּ ״גּוֹי קָדוֹשׁ״
and at Sinai all Israel were established as a kingdom of priests, which means a holy nation;
וְהַכֹּל מִצַּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, דְּ״יַעֲקֹב בָּחַר לוֹ יָהּ״ (תְּהִלִּים קל״ה:ד׳) בְּלֹא שׁוּם טַעַם
all stemming from the Blessed Name, for "Hashem has chosen Jacob unto Himself" (Tehillim 135:4) without any prior cause;
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ: ״הֲלוֹא אָח עֵשָׂו לְיַעֲקֹב... וָאֹהַב אֶת יַעֲקֹב״ (מַלְאָכִי א:ב)
as Scripture declares: "Was not Esau Jacob's brother? says Hashem; yet I loved Jacob" (Malachi 1:2);
וּמִבֶּטֶן נִבְחַר יַעֲקֹב, בְּטֶרֶם הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתוֹ
Jacob being selected from the womb, prior to any human striving.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה ס״ג:ו׳) עַל פָּסוּק ״וַיִּתְרֹצֲצוּ״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית כ״ה:כ״ב): ״בְּטֶרֶם אֶצָּרְךָ בַבֶּטֶן יְדַעְתִּיךָ״ (יִרְמְיָה א:ה)
As stated in Bereishis Rabbah (63:6) on "and the children struggled together within her" (Bereishis 25:22): "Before I formed you in the belly I knew you" (Yirmiyah 1:5);
וְעַל פָּסוּק ״וַיִּגְדְּלוּ [הַנְּעָרִים]״ (שָׁם:כ״ז): מָשָׁל לַהֲדַס וְעַצְבּוֹנִית וְכוּלֵיהּ
and on "and the boys grew" (Bereishis 25:27): a parable of a myrtle and a briar growing together, etc.
וְאַף דִּשְׁנֵיהֶם בְּבֶטֶן אֶחָד, צֶאֱצָאֵי יִצְחָק וְרִבְקָה, וּתְאוֹמִים דְּטִיפָּה אַחַת וְנֶחְלְקָה לִשְׁתַּיִם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּיבָמוֹת (צ״ח עַמּוּד א׳)
And though both shared one womb, offspring of Isaac and Rebecca, twins formed from a single drop divided into two (Yevamos 98a);
וְאִם כֵּן הָיוּ שָׁוִים מַמָּשׁ בְּמַחֲשָׁבָה וְכַוָּונַת הַלֵּב וּבְמַעֲשֶׂה, וְאֵין חֵלֶק לְהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת וְכַוָּונַת יִצְחָק וְרִבְקָה גַּם כֵּן בָּזֶה
being identical in parental conception, heart-intention, and deed, human striving having no part in this distinction;
וְלֹא לְחִנָּם נִקְרָא בְּשֵׁם ״אָח״, כִּי יֵשׁ לוֹ אַחֲוָה מַמָּשׁ
and not in vain is Esau termed "brother," possessing an authentic fraternity;
שֶׁהֲרֵי גַּם עֵשָׂו נִקְרָא בְּקִדּוּשִׁין (י״ח עַמּוּד א׳): ״יִשְׂרָאֵל מוּמָר״
for Esau is explicitly termed in Kiddushin (18a): an "apostate Israelite";
דְּמִתּוֹלַדְתּוֹ הָיָה יִשְׂרָאֵל, וּמִסְּתָמָא דְּנִימּוֹל לִשְׁמוֹנָה
being an Israelite from birth, and certainly circumcised at eight days;
אֶלָּא שֶׁאַחַר כָּךְ הֵמִיר, וְרַק בְּזֶרַע יַעֲקֹב גַּם יִשְׂרָאֵל מוּמָר יֵשׁ לוֹ דִּין יִשְׂרָאֵל לְכָל דָּבָר, אֲבָל קוֹדֶם שֶׁנִּבְחַר יַעֲקֹב הָיָה אֶפְשָׁר לְהָמִיר שֶׁיֹּאבַד שֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל

except that he subsequently apostatized; and while within Jacob's seed an apostate remains an Israelite for all matters (Sanhedrin 44a), prior to Jacob's definitive selection apostasy could sever the title of Israel entirely.
וְזֶה הָיָה אַחַר שֶׁקִּבֵּל יַעֲקֹב הַבְּרָכוֹת, וּתְחִלָּה טָעָה בוֹ יִצְחָק לְבָרְכוֹ
And this rupture unfolded after Jacob received the blessings, Isaac having initially erred in seeking to bless Esau;
וְהַבְּרָכָה הִיא גּוֹרֶמֶת אַחֲרֶיהָ הַמְשָׁכַת הַקְּדוּשָׁה כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל
blessing triggering after it the expansion of holiness as explained above;
דַּחֲשָׁבוֹ כְּלִי מוּכָן לִקְדוּשָׁה, דְּעַל כֵּן נוֹצַר בְּכוֹר
Isaac viewing Esau as a prepared vessel for holiness, wherefore he was formed as firstborn;
וְאַף דְּעַדַיִין לֹא נִתְקַדְּשׁוּ בְּכוֹרוֹת, אָבוֹת קִיְּימוּ כָּל הַתּוֹרָה כוּלָּהּ וְיָדַע דַּעֲתִידִין בְּכוֹרוֹת לְהִתְקַדֵּשׁ
and though firstborns were not yet biblically sanctified, the Patriarchs fulfilled the entire Torah, Isaac knowing firstborns were destined for sanctity.
אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת יַעֲקֹב נָטַל מִמֶּנּוּ הַבְּכוֹרָה וְהַבְּרָכוֹת, כִּי הַכֹּל שַׁיָּיךְ לוֹ בֶּאֱמֶת
But in truth Jacob took the birthright and blessings from him, for all belonged to Jacob in truth;
וְהַבְּכוֹרָה קוֹדֶם, אַף דְּהַקְּדוּשָׁה אַחַר הַבְּרָכָה, כִּי הַבְּכוֹרָה לֹא הָיְתָה אָז הַקְּדוּשָׁה עַצְמָהּ רַק הֲכָנָה לִקְדוּשָׁה
and the birthright preceded, for the birthright was not holiness itself, but the preparation for holiness;
וְהוּצְרַךְ לִיטּוֹל כָּל זֶה בְּעָקְבָה מֵעֵשָׂו
and Jacob was compelled to seize all this by stealth (b'okvah) from Esau;
שֶׁמִּצַּד דִּמְיוֹן הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הָיָה נִרְאֶה תְּחִלָּה דְּהַכֹּל לְעֵשָׂו
for from the illusory perspective of this world it appeared that all belonged to Esau;
כִּי כָּךְ בְּרִיָּתוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם: ״בְּרֵישָׁא חֲשׁוֹכָא וַהֲדַר נְהוֹרָא״, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּרֵישׁ בְּרָכוֹת (ב׳ עַמּוּד ב׳)
for such is the structure of Creation: "first darkness and then light," as stated in Berachos (2b);
דְּעַל כֵּן הִקְדִּימוּ קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע שֶׁל עַרְבִית
wherefore the Sages established the evening Shema first;
כִּי הַקְּרִיאַת שְׁמַע שֶׁהוּא הַכָּרַת הַיִּחוּד — עַל זֶה הָיָה עִיקַּר בְּרִיָּתוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם, וְלֹא נְתָנוֹ אֶלָּא לְיִשְׂרָאֵל, דְּעַל כֵּן אוֹמְרִים ״שְׁמַע יִשְׂרָאֵל וְגוֹמֵר״
for the Shema, which is the declaration of absolute Oneness, is the purpose of Creation, given exclusively unto Israel: "Hear, O Israel, etc."
וּבְרֵישָׁא צָרִיךְ לְהַכִּיר מִתּוֹךְ הַחֹשֶׁךְ וְהַהֶעְלֵם
And first one must perceive divine unity from within darkness and concealment;
כִּי זֶה הָיָה כָּל עִנְיַן הַבְּרִיאָה, דְּ״זֶה לְעֻמַּת זֶה עָשָׂה הָאֱלֹהִים״ (קֹהֶלֶת ז:יד), מַמָּשׁ זֶה דּוֹמֶה לָזֶה
for this is the mystery of Creation: "God has made the one opposite the other" (Koheles 7:14), the dark mirroring the holy;
וְזֶה כָּל הָאָדָם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה: לְהַכִּיר וּלְהַבְדִּיל הַטּוֹב מִן הָרָע, וְזֶהוּ הָאַחֲוָה דְּעֵשָׂו וְיַעֲקֹב
and this is the whole duty of man in this world: to discern and separate good from evil, this being the brotherhood of Esau and Jacob.
כִּי אֵין לְךָ שׁוּם צַדִּיק שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה לוֹ כְּנֶגְדּוֹ חָבֵר רָשָׁע, שֶׁהוּא מְחוּבָּר בְּהִתְחַבְּרוּת לוֹ מִצַּד הַזֶּה לְעֻמַּת זֶה שֶׁעָשָׂה הָאֱלֹהִים
For there is no righteous man who does not possess opposite him a wicked counterpart linked unto him through this divine polarity;
וּמִצַּד הָעִרְבּוּבְיָא דְּטוֹב וָרָע שֶׁנַּעֲשָׂה אַחַר חֵטְא אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן, יֵשׁ בְּכָל אֶחָד עֵירוּב טוֹב וָרָע
and through the mixture of good and evil born from Adam's sin, every person contains a mixture of good and evil.

וְעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ בַּחֲגִיגָה (ט״ו עַמּוּד א׳): ״כָּל אֶחָד יֵשׁ לוֹ [שְׁנֵי חֲלָקִים: אֶחָד בְּגַן עֵדֶן וְאֶחָד בְּגֵיהִנָּם]; זָכָה צַדִּיק — נוֹטֵל חֶלְקוֹ וְחֵלֶק חֲבֵירוֹ בְּגַן עֵדֶן; נִתְחַיֵּיב רָשָׁע — נוֹטֵל חֶלְקוֹ וְחֵלֶק חֲבֵירוֹ בְּגֵיהִנָּם״

And concerning this the Sages stated in Chagigah (15a): "Every person has two portions, one in Gan Eden and one in Gehinnom; if the righteous merits, he takes his portion and his fellow's portion in Gan Eden; if the wicked is condemned, he takes his portion and his fellow's portion in Gehinnom";
וְלֹא לְחִנָּם קְרָאוּהוּ ״חֲבֵירוֹ״, עַל כָּרְחָךְ דְּעַל יְדֵי כֵן חִיבּוּר יַחַד, דְּעַל יְדֵי כֵן אֶחָד יוּכַל לִיטּוֹל חֵלֶק חֲבֵירוֹ: זֶה בַּטּוֹב וְזֶה בְּהֵיפוּךְ:
and not casually did they term him his "fellow," for through this cosmic connection one takes the portion of the other: this one in good, and that one in evil!

7.h: אוֹת ב׳ — עֵרֶב וָבֹקֶר בִּכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל, בַּעֲלֵי תְּשׁוּבָה קְרוֹבִים לַמֶּלֶךְ, וְשַׁבָּת שֶׁל אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן — Section 2: Evening and Morning in Israel, Ba'alei Teshuvah Nearer the King, and Adam's First Sabbath

The theme: The corporate unity of Israel encompassing tzaddikim and transgressors, the supreme ascent of the ba'al teshuvah, and the two Sabbaths. In the architecture of the Jewish nation, Jacob and Esau represented this cosmic divide; yet within Jacob's seed no soul is ever banished ("He devises means that no outcast be expelled", II Shmuel 14:14), for all Israel are companions bound in one bundle ("He founded His bundle upon the earth", Amos 9:6; Keritot 6b). Evening and morning become "one day": just as praise ascends from the righteous, so does it ascend from the wicked, for even the empty in Israel are full of mitzvos like a pomegranate (Eruvin 19a), their transgressors full of remorse. On "and he smelled the smell of his raiment (begadav)" (Bereishis 27:27), Sanhedrin (37a) expounds: "the smell of his traitors (bogedav)"—such as Yokim of Tzerorot (Alcimus), who entered Gan Eden an hour before his uncle, the righteous martyr Yose ben Yoezer (Bereishis Rabbah 65:22)! A ba'al teshuvah ascends in a single hour (Zohar I, 129b), standing closer to the King than consummate tzaddikim because he extracts fallen sparks from the lowest depths, transmuting darkness into light. In Bereishis Rabbah (3:8): "'darkness' denotes the deeds of the wicked... I know not which of them Hashem desires more"—until Scripture states: "And God saw the light, that it was good" (Bereishis 1:4), His ultimate delight residing in the tzaddik. In Creation, six workdays preceded Shabbat; but Adam HaRishon rested on the first day and then counted six (Shabbat 69b). Creation was arranged with work first so that creatures would not eat the "bread of shame" (nahama d'chisufa); but because man’s heart is besieged by the yetzer, Hashem granted him an initial unearned divine gift on his first Sabbath, empowering him to toil through the ensuing six workdays to merit the second Sabbath through his own effort!

p: וּבְבִנְיַן כְּלַל אוּמָּה הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִית הָיוּ כֵּן יַעֲקֹב וְעֵשָׂו
And in the architecture of the collective Israelite nation, Jacob and Esau represented this polarity;
וּבְזֶרַע יַעֲקֹב: ״לֹא יִדַּח [מִמֶּנּוּ] נִדָּח״ (שְׁמוּאֵל ב י״ד:י״ד), דְּאַף הָרָשָׁע אֵין נֶאֱבָד
while within the seed of Jacob: "no outcast is banished from Him" (II Shmuel 14:14), for even the wicked is never lost;
כִּי כָל יִשְׂרָאֵל חֲבֵירִים בַּאֲגֻדָּה אַחַת, וְ״אֲגֻדָּתוֹ עַל אֶרֶץ יְסָדָהּ״ (עָמוֹס ט:ו), כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּכְרֵיתוֹת (ו׳ עַמּוּד ב׳) עַל פָּסוּק זֶה
for all Israel are companions bound in one bundle: "and has founded His bundle upon the earth" (Amos 9:6), as expounded in Keritot (6b).
כִּי מֵהָעֶרֶב וְהַבֹּקֶר נַעֲשָׂה: ״יוֹם אֶחָד״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית א:ה)
For from the evening and the morning is forged: "one day" (Bereishis 1:5);
וּכְשֵׁם שֶׁקִּילוּסוֹ עוֹלֶה מֵהַצַּדִּיקִים, כָּךְ עוֹלֶה מֵהָרְשָׁעִים
and just as His praise ascends from the righteous, so does it ascend from the wicked;
דְּגַם רֵיקָנִין שֶׁבְּיִשְׂרָאֵל מְלֵאִים מִצְוֹת כְּרִמּוֹן (עֵירוּבִין י״ט עַמּוּד א׳), וּפוֹשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מְלֵאִים חֲרָטָה
for even the empty in Israel are as full of mitzvos as a pomegranate (Eruvin 19a), and Jewish transgressors are filled with remorse;
וְעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (ל״ז עַמּוּד א׳): ״׳וַיָּרַח אֶת רֵיחַ בְּגָדָיו׳ (בְּרֵאשִׁית כ״ז:כ״ז) — רֵיחַ בּוֹגְדָיו״
and concerning this the Sages expounded in Sanhedrin (37a): "'and he smelled the smell of his raiment (begadav)' (Bereishis 27:27)—the smell of his traitors (bogedav)";

וּבִבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה ס״ה:כ״ב) אִיתָא עַל זֶה: כְּגוֹן יוֹקִים אִישׁ צְרוֹרוֹת, שֶׁקִּידֵּם לְשָׁעָה קַלָּה לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא לְיוֹסֵי בֶּן יוֹעֶזֶר שֶׁהָיָה צַדִּיק גָּמוּר וְיָגַע כָּל יָמָיו

and in Bereishis Rabbah (65:22) it is cited: such as Yokim of Tzerorot, who preceded by a brief hour into the World to Come his uncle Yose ben Yoezer, who was a consummate tzaddik toiling all his days.
כִּי בַּעַל תְּשׁוּבָה זוֹכֶה לָזֶה בְּשַׁעֲתָא חֲדָא, בְּרִגְעָא חֲדָא, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּזֹּוהַר (חַיֵּי שָׂרָה קכ״ט סוֹף עַמּוּד א׳ — עַמּוּד ב׳)
For a ba'al teshuvah merits this in a single hour, in a single instant, as stated in the Zohar (Chayei Sarah 129a–b);
דְּעַל כֵּן: ״בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁבַּעֲלֵי תְּשׁוּבָה עוֹמְדִין [אֵין צַדִּיקִים גְּמוּרִים יְכוֹלִין לַעֲמוֹד]״ (בְּרָכוֹת ל״ד עַמּוּד ב׳), דְּאִינּוּן קְרִיבִין לְמַלְכָּא יַתִּיר
wherefore "in the place where penitents stand, consummate tzaddikim cannot stand" (Berachos 34b), for they are nearer unto the King.
וְנִרְאֶה דְּעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה ב׳:ה׳): ״׳חֹשֶׁךְ׳ — זֶה מַעֲשֵׂיהֶן שֶׁל רְשָׁעִים... אֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ בְּמִי חָפֵץ יוֹתֵר וְכוּלֵיהּ״
And it appears that concerning this the Midrash states in Bereishis Rabbah (2:5): "'darkness' denotes the deeds of the wicked... I know not which of them He desires more, etc.";
וְאֵיךְ סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ שֶׁיַּחְפּוֹץ בְּמַעֲשֵׂה רְשָׁעִים?!
for how could it enter your mind that Hashem desires the deeds of the wicked?!
רַק הַכַּוָּונָה כְּפִי הַבְּרִיאָה, דְּ״עָשָׂה הָאֱלֹהִים אֶת הָאָדָם יָשָׁר״ (קֹהֶלֶת ז:כט)
But the intent reflects the order of Creation, that "God made man upright" (Koheles 7:29);
וְאַף דְּבָרָא רְשָׁעִים וְיֵצֶר הָרָע, בָּרָא תּוֹרָה תַּבְלִין (קִדּוּשִׁין ל׳ עַמּוּד ב׳)
and though He created the yetzer hara, He created the Torah as its seasoning antidote (Kiddushin 30b);
לִהְיוֹת: ״נֵר לְרַגְלִי [דְבָרֶךָ, וְאוֹר לִנְתִיבָתִי]״ (תְּהִלִּים קי״ט:ק״ה)
to be "a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path" (Tehillim 119:105);
דְּ״גַּם כִּי אֵשֵׁב בַּחֹשֶׁךְ — ה׳ אוֹר לִי״ (מִיכָה ז:ח), וְ״גַּם כִּי אֵלֵךְ בְּגֵיא [צַלְמָוֶת לֹא אִירָא רָע, כִּי] אַתָּה עִמָּדִי״ (תְּהִלִּים כ״ג:ד׳)
that "though I sit in darkness, Hashem shall be a light unto me" (Michah 7:8), and "though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for You are with me" (Tehillim 23:4).
וְאַף דְּסוֹף דִּקְרִיבִין יַתִּיר, כִּי הוּא מַעֲלֶה נִיצוֹצוֹת קְדוֹשִׁים מִמְּקוֹמוֹת חַיּוּתוֹ שְׁפֵלִים, וּמְהַפֵּךְ חֲשׁוֹכָא לִנְהוֹרָא
And though the penitent stands nearer, elevating holy sparks from the lowest depths and transforming darkness into light;
וְסָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ חָפֵץ זֶה יוֹתֵר
wherefore one might think Hashem desires this more;
עַל זֶה אָמְרוּ: ״וַיַּרְא [אֱלֹהִים אֶת] הָאוֹר כִּי טוֹב״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית א:ד), דְּמִכָּל מָקוֹם עִיקַּר חֶפְצוֹ וּרְצוֹנוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ בַּצַּדִּיק ״כִּי טוֹב״
concerning this the Midrash concludes: "And God saw the light, that it was good" (Bereishis 1:4), His primary desire residing in the righteous tzaddik who is good.
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם דָּבָר זֶה שֶׁבְּסֵדֶר הַבְּרִיאָה ״בְּרֵישָׁא וְכוּלֵיהּ״ נוֹקֵב וְיוֹרֵד בַּכֹּל, דְּגַם צַדִּיק גָּמוּר אֵינוֹ זוֹכֶה מִיָּד לְ״הָאוֹר כִּי טוֹב״
Nevertheless this order of Creation—darkness preceding light—penetrates all things, for even a consummate tzaddik does not merit immediately the light that is good;
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּזֹּוהַר (חַיֵּי שָׂרָה שָׁם): דְּצַדִּיקִים בְּכַמָּה שְׁנִין וְכוּלֵיהּ, עַיֵּין שָׁם
as stated in the Zohar (Chayei Sarah ad loc.): tzaddikim ascend only after many years of laborious toil, see there;
וְכֵן בְּכָל הַמַּדְרֵיגוֹת, כִּי גַּם אַחַר שֶׁהִגִּיעַ לָאוֹר, עַדַיִין יֵשׁ יְמֵי הַחוֹל וְיוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת
and so across all rungs, for even after reaching the light there remain the secular workdays and Shabbat;
שֶׁזֶּהוּ הַתַּכְלִית: לְהַגִּיעַ לַהַבְּרָכָה וּקְדוּשָׁה שֶׁבּוֹ הַשְּׁבִיתָה וְהַמְּנוּחָה מִכָּל מְלָאכָה וְהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת
this being the ultimate goal: to reach the blessing and holiness wherein lies rest from all labor and human striving.
דִּכְשֶׁהִגִּיעַ לְמַדְרֵגַת הַקְּדוּשָׁה, אֵין צָרִיךְ עוֹד לְהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת וִיגִיעַת בָּשָׂר
For when one attains the rung of holiness, he no longer requires bodily exertion;
דְּעִיקָּרָהּ בַּקֶּרֶב וּבִפְנִימִיּוּת, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ: ״וּבְקֶרֶב קְדוֹשִׁים [תִּתְהַלָּל]״
its essence residing within the interior heart: "and in the midst of the holy shall You be praised".
וּבְרִיָּתוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם הָיָה תְּחִלָּה שֵׁשֶׁת יְמֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה וְאַחַר כָּךְ שַׁבָּת
And Creation was structured with six workdays first and then Shabbat;
וּמִצַּד אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן לְהֵיפֶךְ: הוּא שָׁמַר יוֹם אֶחָד וּמָנָה שִׁשָּׁה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּשַׁבָּת (ס״ט עַמּוּד ב׳)
whereas from Adam HaRishon it was reversed: he observed the first day (Shabbat) and then counted six workdays (Shabbat 69b).
הַיְינוּ דִּבְרִיאַת הָעוֹלָם הָיָה כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּזְכּוּ הַנִּבְרָאִים עַל יְדֵי הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתָם, וְלֹא יֹאכְלוּ ״נַהֲמָא דִּכְסוּפָא״ כַּנּוֹדָע
Meaning: Creation was arranged so that creatures merit reward through their own toil without eating the "bread of shame" (nahama d'chisufa);
וְעַל יְדֵי הַטֹּרַח דְּשֵׁשֶׁת יְמֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה הַקּוֹדְמִים, יִזְכּוּ לֶאֱכוֹל בְּיוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת, בְּעוֹלָם שֶׁכּוּלּוֹ שַׁבָּת וּמְנוּחָה וּקְדוּשָׁה
through the toil of the preceding six workdays meriting to dine on Shabbat, in the world that is entirely holy rest.
אֲבָל מִצַּד הָאָדָם, דְּ״יֵצֶר לִבּוֹ רַק רַע״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית ו:ה), וְ״אִלְמָלֵא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עוֹזְרוֹ — [אֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לוֹ]״ (סֻכָּה נ״ב עַמּוּד ב׳)
But from the perspective of man, whose inclination is naturally drawn to evil, and were it not that the Holy One assists him he could not prevail (Sukkah 52b);
הוּצְרַךְ לְהַקְדִּים לְפָנָיו הַסַּיַּיעְתָּא דִּשְׁמַיָּא בִּקְדֻשַּׁת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּיוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת
it was necessary to precede divine assistance through Hashem's holiness on Shabbat;
שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מִצַּד עַצְמוֹ שׁוֹפֵעַ קְדוּשָׁה בַּלֵּב בְּלֹא הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת אָדָם
Hashem pouring holiness directly into the heart without prior human effort;
וְזֶה הֲכָנָה לוֹ לְשֵׁשֶׁת יְמֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה שֶׁאַחַר כָּךְ, לְהִשְׁתַּדֵּל בְּעָמָל שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם
this serving as the essential preparation for the ensuing six workdays, to toil in spiritual labor;
שֶׁיִּזְכֶּה אַחַר כָּךְ לִקְדֻשַּׁת הַשַּׁבָּת הַשֵּׁנִית עַל יְדֵי הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתוֹ בְּשֵׁשֶׁת יְמֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה שֶׁלְּפָנָיו:
so that he merits the sanctity of the second Sabbath through his personal striving during the six workdays preceding it!
אוֹת ג׳ — שְׁתֵּי שַׁבָּתוֹת בִּיצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם וּמַתַּן תּוֹרָה, וּגְאוּלָּה לְאַלְתַּר — Section 3: The Two Sabbaths of the Exodus and Sinai, and Immediate Redemption

The theme: The first day of Pesach as the first unearned Sabbath, the 49 days of the Omer, and Sinai as the second earned Sabbath. This is the mystery of the two Sabbaths in Shabbat (118b): "If Israel observed two Sabbaths properly, they would be redeemed immediately". This mirrors the Exodus from Egypt and the Giving of the Torah: the first day of Pesach is designated "Shabbat" ("on the morrow after the Shabbat", Vayikra 23:15), being the first unearned Sabbath which Hashem sanctifies directly from Himself. Hashem extracted "a nation from the midst of another nation" (Devarim 4:34) while Israel was naked of mitzvos and submerged in fifty gates of defilement, requiring a hurried departure (be-chipazon). Then Israel merited the sanctity of the firstborn—the congenital holiness from the womb—all Jews being included within Jacob who won the birthright ("Israel is My son, My firstborn", Shemos 4:22). Afterward came the forty-nine days of the Omer to purify the seven emotional traits through human effort, culminating at Sinai where they became "a holy nation" through their own striving ("and you shall be unto Me", Shemos 19:6). Through these two Sabbaths—Pesach and Sinai—Israel attained complete freedom from foreign empires, which would have endured eternally had they not sinned!
וְזֶהוּ הַשְּׁתֵּי שַׁבָּתוֹת שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּשַׁבָּת (קי״ח עַמּוּד ב׳): ״דְּאִלְמָלֵי שָׁמְרוּ [יִשְׂרָאֵל שְׁתֵּי שַׁבָּתוֹת כְּהִלְכָתָן — מִיָּד נִגְאָלִים]״
And these are the two Sabbaths mentioned in Shabbat (118b): "If Israel observed two Sabbaths properly, they would be redeemed immediately";
וְהוּא גַּם כֵּן עִנְיַן יְצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם וּמַתַּן תּוֹרָה
which is likewise the theme of the Exodus from Egypt and the Giving of the Torah;
דְּיוֹם רִאשׁוֹן דְּפֶסַח נִקְרָא ״שַׁבָּת״, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ: ״מִמָּחֳרַת הַשַּׁבָּת״ (וַיִּקְרָא כ״ג:ט״ו; מְנָחוֹת ס״ה עַמּוּד ב׳)
the first day of Pesach being called "Shabbat": "from the morrow after the Shabbat" (Vayikra 23:15; Menachos 65b);
וְהוּא הַשַּׁבָּת הָרִאשׁוֹנָה דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַקְדִּישׁ מִצַּד עַצְמוֹ
being the first Sabbath which the Blessed Name sanctifies directly from Himself;
כִּי הוֹצִיא ״[גּוֹי] מִקֶּרֶב גּוֹי״ (דְּבָרִים ד:לד), כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה: ״הַלָּלוּ [עוֹבְדֵי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה] וְהַלָּלוּ [עוֹבְדֵי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה]״
extracting "a nation from the midst of another nation" (Devarim 4:34), the angels protesting: "these are idolaters and these are idolaters";
וְהָיוּ ״עֵרֹם וְעֶרְיָה״ (יְחֶזְקֵאל ט״ז:ז׳) מִמִּצְוֹת, וּשְׁקוּעִים בְּנ׳ (חֲמִשִּׁים) שַׁעֲרֵי טוּמְאָה
Israel being "naked and bare" of mitzvos (Yechezkel 16:7), submerged in the gates of defilement;
דְּעַל כֵּן הוּצְרְכוּ לָצֵאת בְּחִפָּזוֹן כַּנּוֹדָע
wherefore they were compelled to depart in haste (be-chipazon);
וְאָז זָכוּ לִקְדֻשַּׁת הַבְּכוֹרוֹת, שֶׁהוּא הַקְּדוּשָׁה מֵרֶחֶם שֶׁמִּצַּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
and then they merited the sanctity of the firstborn, which is the congenital holiness from the womb bestowed by Hashem;
וּכְלַל יִשְׂרָאֵל כְּלוּלִים בִּקְדוּשָׁה זוֹ, שֶׁהֵם זֶרַע יַעֲקֹב שֶׁזָּכָה בַּבְּכוֹרָה, כִּי הָיָה בְּכוֹר לִיצִירָה
and collective Israel are included within this sanctity, being the seed of Jacob who acquired the birthright as the firstborn in creation;
וְנֶאֱמַר: ״בְּנִי בְכֹרִי יִשְׂרָאֵל״ (שְׁמוֹת ד:כב)
and it is said: "Israel is My son, My firstborn" (Shemos 4:22).
וְאַחַר כָּךְ מַ״ט (49) יְמֵי הַסְּפִירָה: לְהִטָּהֵר וּלְהִתְקַדֵּשׁ וְלִזְכּוֹת עַל יְדֵי הַהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת לִהְיוֹת ״גּוֹי קָדוֹשׁ״ בְּמַתַּן תּוֹרָה
And afterward came the forty-nine days of the Omer: to become purified and merit through human striving to become a holy nation at Sinai;
דְּ״[וְ]אַתֶּם תִּהְיוּ לִי [מַמְלֶכֶת כֹּהֲנִים וְגוֹי קָדוֹשׁ]״ (שְׁמוֹת י״ט:ו׳) — מַשְׁמַע ״אַתֶּם״ בְּהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתָם
for "and you shall be unto Me" implies "you" through your own active striving.
וְאַחַר יְצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם יָכְלוּ לִזְכּוֹת לְמַתַּן תּוֹרָה, שֶׁאָז נַעֲשׂוּ חֵרוּת מִמַּלְכִיּוֹת אִלְמָלֵא חָזְרוּ וְחָטְאוּ
And following the Exodus they were able to merit the Giving of the Torah, becoming free from imperial subjugation had they not sinned;
כִּי זָכוּ לִשְׁמִירַת שְׁתֵּי הַשַּׁבָּתוֹת, דְּמִיָּד נִגְאָלִים:
having observed the two Sabbaths, through which redemption is immediate!

אוֹת ד׳ — תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים וְעַמֵּי הָאָרֶץ כְּשַׁבָּת וְחוֹל, שֵׁמוֹת יַעֲקֹב וְיִשְׂרָאֵל, וְעָמָל שֶׁל תּוֹרָה מוּל שִׂיחָה — Section 4: Scholars and Commoners, the Names Jacob and Israel, and Toil of Torah vs. Mundane Speech

The theme: Commoners as the unearned first Sabbath, scholars as the earned second Sabbath, Jacob grasping Esau's heel, and mundane conversation elevating sparks. Within Israel there are scholars and commoners, answering to Shabbat and weekdays. The holiness of the am ha-aretz derives from the first Sabbath (inborn soul-sanctity from Hashem); scholars attain the second Sabbath through their toil in Torah. Jacob embodies both, bearing two names: "Jacob" (the commoner grasping the heel) and "Israel" (the scholar wrestling with the angel). He was named Jacob because his hand seized the heel of Esau, whose life was immersed in corporeal action; Jacob grasped the upper extremity of this realm, knowing that "not study is primary, but deed" (Avos 1:17) and "man is born unto toil" (Iyov 5:7). In Sanhedrin (99b): "I know not whether he was created for the toil of the mouth or the toil of physical labor". Moving the lips in speech is a deed, Malkhut being the Mouth; while deeds must exceed wisdom (as six workdays exceed Shabbat), vocal Torah study is the highest deed. The Gemara asks: "whether for the toil of Torah or the toil of mundane conversation (sichah)?" The mundane conversation of scholars is Torah; the conversation of the Patriarchs' servants surpasses the children's Torah (Bereishis Rabbah 60:8). Elevating sparks from lower worldly matters through discerning conversation is profound; yet the Gemara concludes: "man was created for the toil of Torah," for Torah vitalizes all, and through consummate Torah all evil is annihilated and the holy sparks are resurrected!
וּבִכְלַל אוּמָּה הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִית יֵשׁ תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים וְעַמֵּי הָאָרֶץ, שֶׁהֵם דּוּגְמַת יְמֵי חוֹל וְשַׁבָּת, וְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל קְדוֹשִׁים
And within the collective Israelite nation there are Torah scholars and commoners, mirroring weekdays and Shabbat, all Israel being holy;
רַק דִּקְדֻשַּׁת עַם הָאָרֶץ הוּא מִצַּד הַשַּׁבָּת הָרִאשׁוֹנָה, הַיְינוּ הַקְּדוּשָׁה שֶׁבְּשָׁרְשָׁם מִצַּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
the holiness of the unlearned deriving from the first Sabbath (the inborn soul-sanctity bestowed directly by Hashem);
וְהַתַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים הֵם זוֹכִים לִקְדֻשַּׁת הַשַּׁבָּת הַשֵּׁנִית עַל יְדֵי הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתָם בַּתּוֹרָה
while Torah scholars merit the sanctity of the second Sabbath through their striving in Torah;
שֶׁזֶּהוּ עִיקַּר קְדֻשַּׁת הַשַּׁבָּת שֶׁבִּבְרִיאַת עוֹלָם, וְזָכוּ לָהּ כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּמַתַּן תּוֹרָה שֶׁנַּעֲשׂוּ אָז כּוּלָּם תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים
which is the primary sanctity of Shabbat at Creation, merited by all Israel at Sinai when all became scholars.
וְיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם כּוֹלֵל הָאוּמָּה, כָּלוּל מִשְּׁנֵיהֶם
And our father Jacob, encompassing the nation, is composed of both dimensions;
דְּעַל כֵּן נִקְרָא בִּבְתֵי הַשֵּׁמוֹת: ״יַעֲקֹב״ וְ״יִשְׂרָאֵל״, הָרוֹמֵז לְעַם הָאָרֶץ וְתַלְמִיד חָכָם
wherefore he is designated by two names: "Jacob" and "Israel," alluding to the commoner and the scholar;
וּתְחִלָּה נִקְרָא ״יַעֲקֹב״, דְּיָדוֹ — הַיְינוּ כֹּחַ הַמַּעֲשֶׂה וְהַפְּעֻלָּה — אוֹחֶזֶת בַּעֲקֵב עֵשָׂו
initially named "Jacob" because his hand—the power of action—seized the heel of Esau;
דִּשְׁמוֹ מוֹרֶה עַל כֹּחוֹ וְעִנְיָנוֹ, דְּעִיקָּרוֹ בְּמַעֲשִׂים וּפְעֻלּוֹת וְהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁהוּא עוֹלַם הַהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת
Esau's name denoting action and striving in this world of action;
וְגַם יַעֲקֹב הָלַךְ בְּעִקְּבוֹ וְאָחַז בְּסוֹף הַמַּדְרֵיגָה דִּילֵיהּ
and Jacob walked in his footsteps, seizing the upper boundary of his rung.
כִּי הוּא [עֵשָׂו] נִשְׁתַּקַּע בְּכָל קוֹמָתוֹ בַּעֲשִׂיּוֹת גּוּפָנִיּוֹת דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, לִהְיוֹת זֶה כָּל חַיּוּתוֹ וְתַכְלִית כַּוָּונָתוֹ לְהִשְׁתַּקַּע בָּזֶה בִּלְבַד
For Esau submerged his entire stature in bodily actions, this being his sole vitality and purpose;
כִּי אֵין לוֹ חַיּוּת יוֹתֵר אֶלָּא בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה עוֹלַם הַמַּעֲשֶׂה
possessing no life beyond this physical world of action;
וְיַעֲקֹב אָחַז בָּעֲקֵבַיִים דְּמַדְרֵיגָה זוֹ
while Jacob seized the heels of this rung;
כִּי כָל קוֹמָתוֹ ״יֹשֵׁב אֹהָלִים״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית כ״ה:כ״ז), רַק מִכָּל מָקוֹם: ״לֹא הַמִּדְרָשׁ עִיקָּר — אֶלָּא הַמַּעֲשֶׂה״ (אָבוֹת פֶּרֶק א׳ מִשְׁנָה י״ז)
for his essence is "dwelling in tents" (Bereishis 25:27), yet "not study is primary, but deed" (Avos 1:17);
וְ״[אֲשֶׁר אָנֹכִי מְצַוְּךָ] הַיּוֹם — לַעֲשׂוֹתָם״ (דְּבָרִים ז:יא) כְּתִיב, וְ״אָדָם לְעָמָל יוּלָּד״ (אִיּוֹב ה:ז)
and "which I command you this day, to do them" (Devarim 7:11), and "man is born unto toil" (Iyov 5:7).
וְאִיתָא בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (צ״ט רֵישׁ עַמּוּד ב׳): ״אֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ אִם לַעֲמַל פֶּה אוֹ לַעֲמַל מְלָאכָה וְכוּלֵיהּ״
And in Sanhedrin (99b): "I know not whether he was created for the toil of the mouth or the toil of labor, etc.";
כִּי גַּם עֲקִימַת שְׂפָתָיו הָוֵי מַעֲשֶׂה (סַנְהֶדְרִין ס״ה עַמּוּד ב׳), אֶלָּא שֶׁהוּא מַדְרֵיגָה אַחֲרוֹנָה בְּמַדְרֵגַת הַמַּעֲשִׂים
for moving the lips is considered a deed (Sanhedrin 65b), being the final boundary of action;
וְכִידוּעַ דְּ״מַלְכוּת — פֶּה״ שֶׁזֶּהוּ סוֹף הַקּוֹמָה
and Malkhut is the Mouth, the conclusion of the stature;

דְּאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לִהְיוֹת מַעֲשָׂיו מְרוּבִּין מֵחָכְמָתוֹ (אָבוֹת פֶּרֶק ג׳ מִשְׁנָה ט׳), וּכְמוֹ שֶׁיְּמֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה הֵם שֵׁשׁ פְּעָמִים נֶגֶד הַשַּׁבָּת — הַיְינוּ נֶגֶד הַחָכְמָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב
for although deeds must exceed wisdom (Avos 3:9), matching the six workdays exceeding Shabbat;
אֲבָל לִימּוּד הַתּוֹרָה בַּפֶּה הֲרֵי הוּא בִּכְלַל מַעֲשֶׂה, וְגַם תַּלְמוּד תּוֹרָה הִיא אַחַת מִמִּצְוֹתֶיהָ שֶׁל תּוֹרָה וַעֲדִיפָא מִכּוּלָּם
vocal study is included in action, and Torah study is an independent mitzvah surpassing all others.
וּמַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ: ״אֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ אִם לַעֲמַל תּוֹרָה אִם לַעֲמַל שִׂיחָה״
And what the Gemara asked: "I know not whether for the toil of Torah or the toil of conversation";
הַיְינוּ דְּתַלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים כָּל שִׂיחָתָן תּוֹרָה, וּמָצִינוּ: ״יָפָה שִׂיחָתָן שֶׁל עַבְדֵי אָבוֹת מִתּוֹרָתָן שֶׁל בָּנִים״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה ס׳:ח׳)
for the conversation of scholars is Torah: "the conversation of the Patriarchs' servants is more beloved than the Torah of the children" (Bereishis Rabbah 60:8);

וְיָדוּעַ שֶׁהַעֲלָאַת הַנִּיצוֹצוֹת הַקְּדוֹשִׁים מִדְּבָרִים הַתַּחְתּוֹנִים — שֶׁזֶּהוּ תַּכְלִית הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה — הוּא עַל יְדֵי שִׂיחָה בְּעִנְיְנֵי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה בַּבִּינָה הָרְאוּיָה יוֹתֵר מֵעַל יְדֵי תּוֹרָה, כַּנּוֹדָע בְּסִפְרָן שֶׁל צַדִּיקִים
and elevating holy sparks from mundane matters is accomplished through holy conversation in worldly affairs even more than through pure Torah, as known from the books of tzaddikim.
וְזֶהוּ הַסָּלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ ״אֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ וְכוּלֵיהּ״, מֵעֵין דּוּגְמַת הַבְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה הַנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל ״אֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ בְּמִי חָפֵץ וְכוּלֵיהּ״
This being the initial hypothesis "I know not," mirroring the Midrash "I know not which He desires more";
וּפָשְׁטוּ: ״דִּלְעֲמַל תּוֹרָה״ (סַנְהֶדְרִין צ״ט עַמּוּד ב׳), דְּמִכָּל מָקוֹם עִיקַּר הַכֹּל הוּא הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁמִּמֶּנָּה חַיּוּת הַכֹּל
resolving: "unto the toil of Torah" (Sanhedrin 99b), the Torah being the vital source of all;

וּכְשֶׁמַּגִּיעַ לִשְׁלֵימוּת דִּבְרֵי תּוֹרָה, שֶׁהוּא תַּכְלִית שְׁלֵימוּת הַקְּדוּשָׁה עַד רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ וּתְחִיַּיִת הַמֵּתִים — מִמֵּילָא נֶאֱבָד כָּל הָרָע וּמִתְעַלֶּה כָּל הַטּוֹב וְהַנִּיצוֹצוֹת קְדוֹשִׁים, שֶׁזֶּהוּ תְּחִיַּיִת הַמֵּתִים כַּנּוֹדָע:
and when attaining consummate Torah unto the Holy Spirit and the Resurrection, evil is destroyed and the holy sparks are resurrected!
אוֹת ה׳ — שֵׁם ״יִשְׂרָאֵל״, בֵּית קֶבַע וְסֻכּוֹת עֲרַאי, וְרוֹגְזוֹ שֶׁל יוֹסֵף — Section 5: The Name Israel, The Permanent House vs. Temporary Sukkos, and Joseph's Turmoil

The theme: Jacob becoming Israel, building a permanent house and temporary sukkos, and the turmoil of Joseph (rogzo shel Yosef). Jacob, the root of Torah ("Truth unto Jacob", Michah 7:20; Berachos 5b), operated through vocal toil: "the voice is the voice of Jacob" (Bereishis 27:22). Conquering the angelic prince of Esau, he merited the name Israel ("for you have striven with God and with men, and have prevailed", Bereishis 32:29), reigning over active faculties. He built a permanent house (bayit) for his inner essence, while for his cattle—his physical active faculties—he fashioned temporary booths (sukkos, Bereishis 33:17). Seeking to settle in tranquility (yishev b'shalvah) like the Sabbath rest, the anguish of Joseph pounced upon him (Bereishis Rabbah 84:3). The angel struck the hollow of Jacob's thigh, hinting at his descendants whose souls are distributed in practical action. Their root is Joseph the Tzaddik, who provided grain to all the people of the land (mashbir bar), and his descendant Joshua who settled the Land in bodily labor—planting olives and tilling soil in holiness. Moshe was entirely Torah, leading them in the wilderness where no seed grew, eating angelic bread; Joshua began the refinement of physical action through derech eretz. "Torah is good together with derech eretz" (Avos 2:2); the leaves (derech eretz) preserve the fruit clusters (scholars). The Torah was not given to ministering angels; its purpose is bodily commandments in this world, wherefore Moshe yearned to enter the Land of Israel!
וְיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם עַצְמוֹ שֶׁהוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַתּוֹרָה, מִדַּת ״אֱמֶת לְיַעֲקֹב״ (מִיכָה ז:כ), ״אֵין אֱמֶת אֶלָּא תּוֹרָה״ כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרָכוֹת (ה׳ עַמּוּד ב׳)
And our father Jacob, peace be upon him, who is the root of Torah: "Truth unto Jacob" (Michah 7:20), for "there is no truth save Torah" (Berachos 5b);

וְהוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ כָּל הַתַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים, עַל כֵּן מִדָּתוֹ רַק ״יֹשֵׁב אֹהָלִים״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית כ״ה:כ״ז), וּקְדֻשַּׁת הַמַּעֲשֶׂה שֶׁלּוֹ הָיָה רַק בְּ״הַקֹּל קוֹל יַעֲקֹב״ (שָׁם כ״ז:כ״ב) וּבַעֲמַל פֶּה
being the root of all scholars, his trait was "dwelling in tents" (Bereishis 25:27), his action consisting of: "the voice is the voice of Jacob" (ibid. 27:22) and the toil of the mouth.
וְאַחַר שֶׁנִּצַּח לְשָׂרוֹ שֶׁל עֵשָׂו, זָכָה לְשֵׁם ״יִשְׂרָאֵל״: ״כִּי שָׂרִיתָ [עִם אֱלֹהִים וְעִם אֲנָשִׁים וַתּוּכָל]״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית ל״ב:כ״ט) — לְהִשְׂתָּרֵר עַל כָּל כֹּחוֹת הַמַּעֲשֶׂה
And having vanquished the prince of Esau, he merited the name "Israel": "for you have striven with God and with men, and have prevailed" (Bereishis 32:29), reigning over all faculties of action;
״וַיִּבֶן לוֹ בָּיִת״ (שָׁם ל״ג:י״ז) — הַיְינוּ לִפְנִימִיּוּתוֹ עָשָׂה דִּירַת קֶבַע
"and built him a house" (ibid. 33:17)—fashioning an established dwelling for his inward essence;
״וּלְמִקְנֵהוּ [עָשָׂה סֻכֹּת]״ — הֵם הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת כֹּחוֹת הַגּוּפָנִיִּים וְהַמַּעֲשֶׂה — ״סֻכּוֹת״, אֹהֶל עֲרַאי
"and made booths for his cattle"—his physical active faculties—"sukkos," a temporary tent.
וְזֶהוּ שֶׁבִּקֵּשׁ אַחַר כָּךְ ״לֵישֵׁב בְּשַׁלְוָה״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה פ״ד:ג׳)
And this is why he sought afterward to dwell in tranquility (Bereishis Rabbah 84:3);
הַיְינוּ בִּמְנוּחָה וּשְׁבִיתָה מִכָּל מַעֲשֶׂה כִּקְדֻשַּׁת יוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת
resting from all labor like the sanctity of Shabbat;
אֶלָּא שֶׁ״קָפַץ עָלָיו רוֹגְזוֹ שֶׁל יוֹסֵף״ (שָׁם)
except that "the turmoil of Joseph pounced upon him";

הַיְינוּ דְּמִצַּד זַרְעוֹ עַדַיִין צָרִיךְ לְבֵירוּרִים, שֶׁזֶּהוּ הַנְּגִיעָה בְּכַף יֶרֶךְ יַעֲקֹב, הַיְינוּ בְּיוֹצְאֵי יְרֵכוֹ, שֶׁכָּל כֹּחוֹתָיו נִתְחַלְּקוּ בְּזַרְעוֹ בִּנְפָשׁוֹת פְּרָטִיּוֹת
meaning that on the part of his seed spiritual refinement was still needed, symbolized by the touch upon the hollow of Jacob's thigh, his progeny who divided his faculties into individual souls.
וְנַפְשׁוֹת וְכֹחוֹת הַמַּעֲשֶׂה בְּהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת בִּפְרָטִיּוּת: יֵשׁ נְפָשׁוֹת שֶׁכָּל כֹּחָם בְּמַעֲשֶׂה בְּפֹעַל
And regarding the faculties of action in detailed manifestation: there are souls whose entire power is practical action;
וְשָׁרְשָׁם יוֹסֵף הַצַּדִּיק, הוּא ״הַמַּשְׁבִּיר בָּר לְכָל עַם הָאָרֶץ״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית מ״ב:ו׳) לִהְיוֹת זָן וּמְפַרְנֵס
their root being Joseph the Tzaddik, who provided sustenance unto all the people of the land (Bereishis 42:6), feeding the world;

וּמִזַּרְעוֹ יְהוֹשֻׁעַ הַמַּנְחִיל הָאָרֶץ, שֶׁהוּא קְדֻשַּׁת הַמַּעֲשִׂים הַגּוּפָנִיִּים שֶׁהִתְחִילוּ בְּבִיאַת הָאָרֶץ: זֶה פּוֹנֶה לְזֵיתוֹ וְכוּלֵיהּ, אֲבָל הַכֹּל בִּקְדוּשָׁה וּבְקִיּוּם מִצְוֹתֶיהָ
and from his seed Joshua who apportioned the Land, initiating bodily holiness in agriculture, all executed in holiness.
כִּי מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם כּוּלּוֹ תּוֹרָה, עַל כֵּן הוֹלִיכָם בַּמִּדְבָּר חוּץ לַיִּשּׁוּב וְעוֹלַם הַמַּעֲשֶׂה
For Moshe Rabbeinu was entirely Torah, leading them in the wilderness outside settled civilization and the world of physical labor;
מְקוֹם ״אֲשֶׁר אֵין זֶרַע [וּתְאֵנָה וְגֶפֶן וְרִמּוֹן]״ (בַּמִּדְבָּר כ:ה), רַק לֶחֶם שֶׁמַּלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת אוֹכְלִין
a place devoid of agriculture, nourished solely by angelic bread;
וִיהוֹשֻׁעַ הִתְחִיל לְבָרֵר קְדֻשַּׁת הַמַּעֲשֶׂה הַגּוּפָנִית וְלִהְיוֹת עוֹסְקִים בְּדֶרֶךְ אֶרֶץ, וְגַם זֶה הַכֹּל עַל פִּי הַתּוֹרָה
while Joshua began to refine physical deed through derech eretz, all governed by Torah;
וְ״טוֹב תּוֹרָה עִם דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ״ (אָבוֹת פֶּרֶק ב׳ מִשְׁנָה ב׳), וְ״אִם אֵין דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ — אֵין תּוֹרָה״ (שָׁם פֶּרֶק ג׳ מִשְׁנָה י״ז)
for "Torah is good together with derech eretz" (Avos 2:2), and "if there is no derech eretz, there is no Torah" (ibid. 3:17).
וְהַדֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ הוּא חֵלֶק הָעַם הָאָרֶץ וְהוּא הַקּוֹדֶמֶת לַתּוֹרָה, דְּגַם זֶה צָרִיךְ לְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה
And derech eretz is the share of the commoner which precedes the Torah, being indispensable to words of Torah;
דְּ״אִי לָא עַלְיָא — לָא מִתְקַיְּימוּ אִתְכָּלְיָא״ (חֻלִּין צ״ב עַמּוּד א׳)
for "without the protecting leaves, the fruit clusters cannot endure" (Chullin 92a);
וְלֹא נִתְּנָה תוֹרָה לְמַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת לְבַד, כְּמוֹ שֶׁהָיָה בְּדוֹר הַמִּדְבָּר
and the Torah was not given to ministering angels alone as in the wilderness;
וְעִיקַּר הַתּוֹרָה הוּא לִימּוּד מַעֲשֵׂה הַמִּצְוֹת שֶׁהֵם בְּמַעֲשִׂים גּוּפָנִים שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
the purpose of Torah being the performance of physical mitzvos in this world;
דְּעַל כֵּן נִתְאַוָּה מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם לִיכָּנֵס לְאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל: לְקַיֵּים מִצְוֹתֶיהָ (סוֹטָה י״ד עַמּוּד א׳):
wherefore Moshe yearned to enter the Land of Israel: to fulfill its physical commandments (Sotah 14a)!

7.h: אוֹת ו׳ — יוֹסֵף שִׂטְנוֹ שֶׁל עֵשָׂו, שׁוֹרֶשׁ לֵאָה וְרָחֵל, וְתַמָּר וִיהוּדָה — Section 6: Joseph as the Adversary of Esau, Leah and Rachel, and the Secret of Judah and Tamar

The theme: Joseph consuming the straw of Esau, the hidden world of Leah versus the manifest world of Rachel, and Judah rectifying Tamar in the mystery of Mashiach. Joseph is the adversary of Esau ("the house of Jacob shall be a fire, and the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of Esau for stubble", Ovadiah 1:18). Both engage in physical action; but while Esau claims "my power and the might of my hand" (Devarim 8:17), Joseph acts with the fear of God ("for I fear God", Bereishis 42:18), keeping His commandments. His divine flame burns the straw of Esau—the four hundred men representing Esau's worldly might. The children of Leah (the concealed world, alma d'itkasya) embody Torah, scholars, and the Sanhedrin; the children of Rachel (the revealed world, alma d'itgalya) embody practical mitzvos. Joseph brought an evil report of Leah's sons, criticizing their lack of external derech eretz; measure for measure, Joseph was sold as a slave into physical labor. Vanquishing his yetzer against Potiphar's wife, Joseph was elevated to kingship. The internal holiness of Leah's line was tested in Judah: descending into degradation, he united with Tamar who appeared as a harlot (kedeshah) by the crossroads (Bereishis 38:14, 21). In Hebrew roots, words often signify a concept and its opposite (derech v'hiphucho): a kedeshah represents the basest profligacy, opposite true kedushah. Judah seemed submerged in darkness; yet in truth from Hashem it was orchestrated to birth Perez and Zerah—the royal soul of King Mashiach! Two Messiahs arise: Mashiach ben Yosef vanquishing Amalek in external action, and Mashiach ben David revealing the internal secrets of the Torah!

p: וְעַל כֵּן יוֹסֵף הוּא שִׂטְנוֹ שֶׁל עֵשָׂו (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה ע״ג:ז׳), כִּי גַּם הוּא מִשְׁתַּדֵּל בְּמַעֲשֶׂה דּוּגְמַת עֵשָׂו
Wherefore Joseph is the adversary of Esau (Bereishis Rabbah 73:7), for he likewise engages in practical action like Esau;
אֲבָל כָּל מַעֲשָׂיו לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם, דְּ״אֶת הָאֱלֹהִים אֲנִי יָרֵא״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית מ״ב:י״ח), וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה מִצְוֹתָיו שְׁמוּר
but all his actions are for Heaven, fearing God (Bereishis 42:18) and guarding His commandments;
הֵיפֶךְ עֵשָׂו דִּכְתִיב בֵּיהּ: ״וְלֹא יָרֵא אֱלֹהִים״ (דְּבָרִים כ״ה:י״ח), שֶׁהוּא הַפְּסֹולֶת דְּמִדַּת הַגְּבוּרָה
the reverse of Esau: "and feared not God" (Devarim 25:18), the unholy dross of Gevurah;
לַחְשׁוֹב: ״כֹּחִי וְעֹצֶם יָדִי עָשָׂה לִי [אֶת הַחַיִל הַזֶּה]״ (שָׁם ח:יז)
boasting: "My power and the might of my hand has gotten me this wealth" (ibid. 8:17);
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן הַיָּרֵא, שֶׁיּוֹדֵעַ שֶׁכָּל גְּבוּרוֹתָיו וְכֹחַ פְּעֻלָּתוֹ מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, וְהוּא מִתְגַּבֵּר לִכְבּוֹשׁ יִצְרוֹ
unlike the God-fearing who attributes all power to Hashem, conquering his inclination;
וּמִזֶּה בָּא: ״וּבֵית יוֹסֵף לֶהָבָה״ (עֹבַדְיָה א:יח) לִשְׂרוֹף הַקַּשׁ דְּעֵשָׂו, שֶׁהֵם אַרְבַּע מֵאוֹת אִישׁ שֶׁעִמּוֹ, שֶׁזֶּהוּ הַמִּסְפָּר שֶׁל כָּל תֹּקֶף כֹּחוֹתָיו בְּהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתוֹ
whence "the house of Joseph is a flame" (Ovadiah 1:18) to consume the straw of Esau—the 400 men embodying his worldly strength.
וְזֶהוּ הָרוֹגְזָא דְּיוֹסֵף, שֶׁמִּצַּד מִדַּת הַיִּרְאָה נִמְשָׁךְ הַכַּעַס עַל עוֹבְרֵי רְצוֹנוֹ
And this was the agitation of Joseph, zeal against transgressors flowing from fear;
וְכָל זְמַן שֶׁלֹּא נִתְבָּרְרוּ זֶרַע יַעֲקֹב לְגַמְרֵי, הֵבִיא גַּם דִּבָּתָם רָעָה אֶל אֲבִיהֶם (בְּרֵאשִׁית ל״ז:ב׳)
bringing an evil report of Leah's sons unto their father (Bereishis 37:2);
כִּי בְּזַרְעָא דְּלֵאָה הוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַתּוֹרָה, וְכָל צוּרְבָא מֵרַבָּנַן דְּמוֹרֵי, וְרוּבָּן שֶׁל סַנְהֶדְרִין, כִּי הִיא ״עָלְמָא דְּאִתְכַּסְיָא״
for in the seed of Leah lies the root of Torah, the judges, and the Sanhedrin, she being the concealed world;
וְשׁוֹרֶשׁ מַעֲשֵׂה הַמִּצְוֹת בְּזַרְעָא דְּרָחֵל, ״עָלְמָא דְּאִתְגַּלְיָא״
while the root of practical mitzvos lies in the seed of Rachel, the revealed world.
וּמִזֶּה נִמְשַׁךְ הָרוֹגְזָא שֶׁל יוֹסֵף שֶׁלֹּא הִנִּיחַ לְיַעֲקֹב לֵישֵׁב בְּשַׁלְוָה, שֶׁזָּכָה לָהּ עַל יְדֵי שֶׁ״לְעֶבֶד נִמְכַּר יוֹסֵף״ (תְּהִלִּים ק״ה:י״ז)
And from this issued the turmoil of Joseph, who was sold as a slave (Tehillim 105:17);
מִדָּה כְּנֶגֶד מִדָּה נִתְעוֹרֵר קִיטְרוּג עַל מַדְרֵיגָתוֹ גַּם כֵּן... וְנִמְכַּר לְעֶבֶד שֶׁהוּא הִשְׁתַּעְבְּדוּת בִּפְעֻלַּת וְעַבְדוּת בְּמַעֲשֶׂה
being sold into physical servitude measure for measure;
וְאַחַר שֶׁנִּתְבָּרַר בִּכְבִישַׁת הַיֵּצֶר זָכָה לִמְלוּכָה
and once refined through conquering his yetzer, he merited royal dominion;
וְכֵן יְצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם, שֶׁהוּא הַיְצִיאָה מֵהָעַבְדוּת דּוּגְמַת יְצִיאַת יוֹסֵף מִבֵּית הָאֲסוּרִים לִמְלוֹךְ, קָדַם לְמַתַּן תּוֹרָה
and the Exodus from Egyptian slavery, like Joseph emerging from prison to reign, preceded Sinai;
וְאָז זָכָה יַעֲקֹב לְאוֹתָהּ יְשִׁיבָה בְּשַׁלְוָה שֶׁבִּקֵּשׁ תְּחִלָּה, בְּאוֹתָן י״ז (17) שָׁנִים שֶׁבְּמִצְרַיִם
whereupon Jacob merited to dwell in tranquility during his final seventeen years in Egypt.
וּקְדֻשַּׁת זַרְעָא דְּלֵאָה בִּפְנִימִיּוּת וְאִתְכַּסְיָא נִתְבָּרַר בִּיהוּדָה אַחַר הַיְרִידָה מֵאֶחָיו
And the inward concealed holiness of Leah's line was clarified in Judah following his descent from his brothers;
שֶׁהָיָה בִּירִידָה וְשִׁפְלוּת, עַד שֶׁהָיָה נִרְאֶה הֵיפֶךְ הַקְּדוּשָׁה לְהִתְחַבֵּר עִם ״הַקְּדֵשָׁה בָעֵינַיִם״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית ל״ח:כ״א)
descending until it appeared the antithesis of holiness in uniting with Tamar as a harlot (kedeshah, Bereishis 38:21);
וְ״הַקְּדֵשָׁה״ הִיא הַמֻּפְקֶרֶת לְתַאֲווֹת רָעוֹת הֵיפֶךְ הַקְּדוּשָׁה, דְּעַל כֵּן נִקְרֵאת כֵּן
a kedeshah denoting one abandoned to lust, the reverse of holiness;
כִּידוּעַ דְּכָל שָׁרְשֵׁי לְשׁוֹן הַקֹּדֶשׁ מוֹרִים עַל דֶּרֶךְ וְהֵיפִיכוֹ
all Hebrew roots alluding to a concept and its opposite.
וְהִנֵּה זֶהוּ תַּכְלִית הַיְרִידָה, שֶׁנִּדְמֶה לִשְׁקוֹעַ בַּחֹשֶׁךְ הַגָּמוּר
This appearing as the ultimate descent into total darkness;
אֲבָל מִצַּד הָאֱמֶת לֹא הָיְתָה בָּזֶה ״קְדֵשָׁה״, וְכוּלּוֹ בִּקְדוּשָׁה
yet in absolute truth it was no harlotry, but consummate holiness;
דְּמֵאִתּוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ יָצְאוּ כְּבוּשִׁים לִבְרוֹא אוֹרוֹ שֶׁל מָשִׁיחַ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פ״ה:א׳), שֶׁהוּא תַּכְלִית וְשׁוֹרֶשׁ מְצִיאוּת הַקְּדוּשָׁה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
orchestrated from Hashem to create the light of Mashiach, the root of holiness in this world.
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁזֶּרַע יַעֲקֹב י״ב (12) שְׁבָטִים, בִּכְלָל חֲלוּקִים לִשְׁנַיִם: יְהוּדָה וְיוֹסֵף, שֶׁכָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל נִקְרָאִים עַל שְׁמָם, וּמֵהֶם תְּרֵין מְשִׁיחִין
And all twelve tribes divide fundamentally between Judah and Joseph, whence issue two Messiahs:
מָשִׁיחַ בֶּן יוֹסֵף הוּא הַנִּלְחָם עִם הָאוּמּוֹת וּמוֹחֶה זֶרַע עֲמָלֵק, מְבָרֵר הַקְּדוּשָׁה דְּעָלְמָא דְּאִתְגַּלְיָא בִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל:
Mashiach ben Yosef waging war against the nations to blot out Amalek, clarifying holiness in the revealed world!

7.h: אוֹת ז׳ — מָשִׁיחַ בֶּן דָּוִד, עֵשָׂו כְּ״אִישׁ שָׂדֶה״ בְּדֶרֶךְ אֶרֶץ, וְהַלְעָטַת הָאָדֹם הָאָדֹם — Section 7: Mashiach ben David, Esau's Superficial "Derech Eretz", and the Lentil Stew

The theme: Mashiach ben David revealing the hidden mysteries of Torah, Isaac loving Esau as the archetype of action, and Jacob taking the good while Esau swallows the red stew. Mashiach ben David reveals the esoteric mysteries of the Torah and the inward holiness of Israel, when death will be swallowed up forever (Yeshayah 25:8) and Hashem alone shall lead them. Rebecca foresaw that her twin sons represented the roots of the twelve tribes, assuming both were holy, for Esau was circumcised and bore the covenantal title of Israel from birth. Isaac loved Esau, seeking to bless him to channel holiness into him. Seeing Esau as "a man of the field" (Bereishis 25:27), Isaac thought Esau embodied the derech eretz that precedes Torah (Avos 3:17), scrupulously honoring his father. But Esau acted strictly from human intellect while despising the Torah. A gentile who observes Noahide laws out of human intellect is merely "among their wise men" rather than "the pious of the nations" (Rambam, Hilchos Melachim 8:11); creating new religious rituals is punishable by death (Sanhedrin 59a). Prior to the blessings, the potential good in physical action was trapped in exile within Esau; Jacob extracted this good, fathering Joseph who is the holy adversary of Esau. The dross of Adam's sin within Jacob was swallowed by Esau through the red lentil stew ("feed me with that same red stew", Bereishis 25:30), operating like the scapegoat (se'ir) bearing away iniquity on Yom Kippur, which occurred on the day Avraham passed away!

p: וּמָשִׁיחַ בֶּן דָּוִד הוּא הַמְגַלֶּה כָּל רָזֵי הַתּוֹרָה הַנֶּעְלָמִים וְהַקְּדוּשָׁה שֶׁבִּפְנִימִיּוּת זֶרַע יִשְׂרָאֵל
And Mashiach ben David is the one who reveals all the concealed mysteries of the Torah and the inward holiness of the seed of Israel;
כִּי: ״צוּר לְבָבִי וְחֶלְקִי אֱלֹהִים לְעוֹלָם״ (תְּהִלִּים ע״ג:כ״ו), וְאָז: ״ה׳ בָּדָד יַנְחֶנּוּ״ (דְּבָרִים ל״ב:י״ב)
for "God is the rock of my heart and my portion forever" (Tehillim 73:26), and then "Hashem alone did lead him" (Devarim 32:12);
כִּי ״בִּלַּע הַמָּוֶת לָנֶצַח״ (יְשַׁעְיָה כ״ה:ח׳) וְשׁוֹרֶשׁ הָרָע מִן הָעוֹלָם
when He will swallow up death forever (Yeshayah 25:8) and abolish the root of evil from the cosmos.
וּב׳ שְׁבָטִים אֵלּוּ הֵם שׁוֹרֶשׁ כָּל הַשְּׁנֵים עָשָׂר
And these two tribes are the root of all twelve tribes;
וְרִבְקָה שֶׁחָשְׁבָה לְהוֹלִיד י״ב שְׁבָטִים... חָשְׁבָה אֵלֶּה הַב׳ הֵם שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַי״ב, כִּי חָשְׁבָה דִּשְׁנֵיהֶם בִּקְדוּשָׁה
and Rebecca, who anticipated bearing the twelve tribes, assumed these two twins were their holy root, thinking both were in holiness;
כִּי גַּם עֵשָׂו מִלֵּידָתוֹ בְּשֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל יְכוּנֶּה
for Esau likewise from birth was designated by the covenantal title of Israel.
וּמִזֶּה נִצְמַח אַהֲבַת יִצְחָק לוֹ וְשֶׁחָפֵץ לְבָרְכוֹ, כִּי חָשַׁב שֶׁיּוּכַל לְהַמְשִׁיךְ קְדוּשָׁה בּוֹ שֶׁיִּבְחַר בַּטּוֹב
And from this sprang Isaac's love for him, desiring to bless him to draw holiness into him that he might choose the good;
וְיִתְקַדֵּשׁ בִּקְדֻשַּׁת הַבְּכוֹרָה הַבָּאָה לִקְדֻשַּׁת הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת בְּמַעֲשִׂים
becoming sanctified with the holiness of the birthright governing practical action;
וְחָשַׁב דְּיַעֲקֹב הוּא תּוֹרָה, וְעֵשָׂו שֶׁקְּדָמוֹ בַּלֵּידָה הוּא דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ הַקּוֹדֵם לַתּוֹרָה
Isaac assuming Jacob represented Torah, while Esau who preceded him represented derech eretz that precedes Torah;
וְזֶהוּ שֶׁנִּזְהַר בְּכִבּוּד אָב וָאֵם הַרְבֵּה
wherefore Esau was scrupulous in honoring his father.
וּבֶאֱמֶת הוּא מָאַס בַּתּוֹרָה וּבָחַר בָּזֶה רַק מִצַּד שֵׂכֶל אֱנוֹשִׁי, וְאִם כֵּן אֵינוֹ כְּלוּם
Yet in truth Esau despised the Torah, honoring his parents purely from human intellect, which is spiritually void;
