שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ בְּשֶׁבַע מִצְוֹת בֶּן נֹחַ, אִם עָשָׂה מִצַּד שִׂכְלָן וְלֹא לְפִי שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ צִוָּוה — אֵין נִקְרָא מֵחֲסִידֵי אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם אֶלָּא מֵחַכְמֵיהֶם (רַמְבַּ״ם הִלְכוֹת מְלָכִים פֶּרֶק ח׳ הֲלָכָה י״א)

for even in the Seven Noahide Laws, if observed from philosophy and not because Hashem commanded them, he is not of the pious of the nations, but of their philosophers (Rambam, Hilchos Melachim 8:11);
אֶלָּא נֶעֱנָשׁ גַּם כֵּן בְּמִצְוֹת מְחוּדָּשׁוֹת שֶׁעוֹשֶׂה (שָׁם פֶּרֶק י׳ הֲלָכָה ט׳)
being punishable if inventing new religious commandments (ibid. 10:9);
וְהוּא בִּכְלַל ״גּוֹי שֶׁשָּׁבַת אוֹ עָסַק בַּתּוֹרָה — שֶׁחַיָּיב מִיתָה״ (סַנְהֶדְרִין נ״ט עַמּוּד א׳)
falling under a gentile who rests on Shabbat or studies Torah, who incurs the death penalty (Sanhedrin 59a).
וְעַד קַבָּלַת יַעֲקֹב הַבְּרָכוֹת, הָיָה מִצַּד הָעֵירוּב דְּטוֹב וָרָע כֹּחַ הַטּוֹב שֶׁבְּעִנְיַן הָעֲשִׂיָּה בְּפֹעַל גָּנוּז בְּתַכְלִית הַהֶעְלֵם בְּעֵשָׂו
And until Jacob received the blessings, the good of physical action was trapped within Esau;
וְזֶהוּ חֶלְקוֹ בְּגַן עֵדֶן שֶׁזָּכָה יַעֲקֹב וּנְטָלוֹ עַל יְדֵי נְטִילַת הַבְּרָכוֹת
this being Esau's portion in Gan Eden which Jacob extracted through taking the blessings;
הַיְינוּ חֵלֶק הַטּוֹב שֶׁהָיָה בְּגָלוּת אֶצְלוֹ קְלָטוֹ הוּא, וְהוֹצִיא בִּלְעוֹ מִפִּיו וְהִפְרִידוֹ מֵהָרָע
absorbing the good sparks held in exile, extracting his swallowed prey and separating it from evil;
וְהוֹלִיד עַל יְדֵי זֶה אַחַר כָּךְ בִּקְדוּשָׁה נֶפֶשׁ יוֹסֵף שִׂטְנוֹ שֶׁל עֵשָׂו, שֶׁהוּא כֹּחַ הָעֲשִׂיָּה דִּקְדוּשָׁה נִפְרָד מֵהָרָע
fathering in holiness the soul of Joseph, the holy adversary of Esau, embodying physical action purified of evil.
וְחֶלְקוֹ דְּיַעֲקֹב בְּגֵיהִנָּם — הַיְינוּ חֵלֶק הָרָע שֶׁהוּא מִצַּד הָעִרְבּוּב דְּטוֹב וָרָע שֶׁהָיָה בוֹ בַּתּוֹלָדָה עַל יְדֵי חֵטְא אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן
And Jacob's portion in Gehinnom—the dross of Adam's sin within him from birth;
קְלָטוֹ עֵשָׂו מִמֶּנּוּ בְּהַלְעָטַת ״הָאָדֹם הָאָדֹם״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית כ״ה:ל׳)
Esau swallowed from him through gulping the red lentil stew (Bereishis 25:30);
שֶׁהָיָה כְּעִנְיַן נְשִׂיאַת הַשָּׂעִיר עֲוֹנוֹתָם: כָּל עֲוֹנוֹת ״תָּם״ (שָׁם:כ״ז; יוֹמָא ס״ז עַמּוּד ב׳)
operating like the scapegoat (se'ir) bearing away all the iniquities of Jacob the wholesome (tam, Yoma 67b);
וְזֶה הָיָה בְּיוֹם שֶׁמֵּת אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, שֶׁהוּא מִדַּת הַחֶסֶד:
and this occurred on the very day Avraham Avinu passed away, who embodied the attribute of Chesed!
יִשְׂרָאֵל קְדוֹשִׁים — פֶּרֶק ז׳, סְעִיפִים ח׳–י״ב
אוֹת ח׳ — פְּטִירַת אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ, מַעֲשֵׂי הַצַּדִּיק כִּדְרָבוֹנוֹת, כְּפִירַת עֵשָׂו בִּתְחִיַּיִת הַמֵּתִים, וְצִמְצוּמוֹ שֶׁל יִצְחָק
Section 8: The Passing of Abraham, Words of the Wise as Goads, Esau's Denial of the Resurrection, and Isaac's Constriction

The theme: The spiritual impact of the passing of the righteous, Abraham's universal revelation of divine judgment versus Isaac's inward contraction (tzimtzum), and why Jacob studied at the academy of Shem and Eber. At the hour of a righteous person's passing from this world, his lifelong deeds become deeply fixed within the hearts of his disciples and children who walk in his ways: "The words of the wise are as goads... given from one shepherd" (Koheles 12:11)—meaning when their master is gathered from the world (Koheles Rabbah 12:11). But unto those who are his opposite, that departure turns to a stumbling block, just as at the Giving of the Torah destruction descended upon the nations who could not endure the holy voice. On the very day Abraham died, Esau cast off all restraint, denying the Resurrection of the Dead and blaspheming: "There is no judgment and there is no Judge" (Bava Batra 16b; Bereishis Rabbah 63:10). Abraham was the first to publicize divine sovereignty throughout the world—that there is judgment, a Judge, and two worlds (this world and the World to Come). Abraham’s trait was expansive lovingkindness (Chesed), actively converting men while Sarah converted women. In contrast, Isaac did not make converts; his trait was strict inward contraction (Gevurah / Tzimtzum), seeing that Abraham's converts reverted to idolatry after Abraham passed away. Isaac's tzimtzum was so intense that he concealed Torah even from the worthy, which explains why Jacob left home to study in the academy of Shem and Eber (Megillah 16b). Although Isaac possessed far more Torah knowledge than Shem and Eber—having absorbed it from Abraham whose kidneys welled with Torah like two springs (Bereishis Rabbah 61:1), and himself embodying the very root of Torah that went forth from the side of Gevurah—Isaac's academy operated in profound hiddenness and contraction!
וְכָל עֲבוֹדוֹת הָאָדָם בְּחַיָּיו, בְּיוֹם מוֹתוֹ וְהִסְתַּלְּקוֹ מִן הָעוֹלָם הוּא נִקְבָּע בְּלֵב בָּנָיו וְתַלְמִידָיו הַנִּשְׁאָרִים אַחֲרָיו הַהוֹלְכִים בִּדְרָכָיו

And all the spiritual labors of a man during his lifetime, on the day of his death and departure from the world become permanently engraved within the hearts of his children and disciples who remain after him walking in his ways;

שֶׁעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ בְּקֹהֶלֶת רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה י״ב:י״א): ״אֵימָתַי ׳דִּבְרֵי חֲכָמִים כַּדָּרְבֹנוֹת [וּכְמַשְׂמְרוֹת נְטוּעִים] וְגוֹמֵר׳ (קֹהֶלֶת י״ב:י״א)? — בִּזְמַן שֶׁבַּעֲלֵיהֶם נֶאֱסָפִים מֵהֶם״

concerning which the Sages expounded in Koheles Rabbah (12:11): "When are 'the words of the wise as goads, and as nails well fastened, etc.' (Koheles 12:11)? At the time when their masters are gathered from them".
וּלְאוֹתָם שֶׁהֵם הַהֵיפֶךְ נֶהְפַּךְ לָהֶם לְרוֹעֵץ
And unto those who are his opposite, that passing turns into an active stumbling block;
כְּמוֹ בְּמַתַּן תּוֹרָה: יָרְדָה שִׂנְאָה וְחוּרְבָּה לְאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם (שַׁבָּת פ״ט עַמּוּד א׳)
just as at the Giving of the Torah: destruction and hatred descended upon the nations of the world (Shabbat 89a);
דְּ״אַתָּה שָׁמַעְתָּ — וַיֶּחִי״ (דְּבָרִים ד:לג), וְהֵם שׁוֹמְעִים וּמֵתִים
for Israel heard the divine voice and lived (Devarim 4:33), while the heathen hear and expire.
וְכֵן עֵשָׂו מֵאוֹתוֹ יוֹם יָצָא לְתַרְבּוּת רָעָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא ט״ז עַמּוּד ב׳)
And so Esau from that very day departed unto wicked ways, as the Sages stated (Bava Batra 16b);
וְכָפַר אָז בִּתְחִיַּיִת הַמֵּתִים, וְאָמַר: ״אַף בְּאוֹתוֹ זָקֵן שָׁלְטָה מִדַּת הַדִּין... לֵית דִּין וְלֵית דַּיָּין״ (שָׁם)
and denied then the Resurrection of the Dead, declaring: "Even over that elder [Abraham] the attribute of strict justice ruled; there is no judgment and there is no Judge!".
וְאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הוּא הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁפִּרְסֵם אֱלֹהוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ בָּעוֹלָם: שֶׁאִית דִּין וְאִית דַּיָּין, וְשֶׁיֵּשׁ שְׁנֵי עוֹלָמוֹת
And Abraham our father, peace be upon him, was the very first who publicized Hashem's Godliness in the world: that there is judgment, there is a Judge, and that two worlds exist;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה ס״א:ג׳): דְּכָל שֶׁאֵינוֹ מוֹדֶה בִּשְׁנֵי עוֹלָמוֹת אֵין לוֹ חֵלֶק בְּזֶרַע אַבְרָהָם
and as stated in Bereishis Rabbah (61:3): whoever does not acknowledge two worlds has no portion in the seed of Abraham.
וְזֶהוּ הַבְטָחַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ: ״לִהְיוֹת לְךָ לֵאלֹהִים וּלְזַרְעֲךָ אַחֲרֶיךָ״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית י״ז:ז׳), שֶׁיַּכִּירוּ אֱלֹהוּתוֹ, וְהֵם יַעֲקֹב וְזַרְעוֹ
And this is the promise of the Blessed Name: "to be a God unto you, and to your seed after you" (Bereishis 17:7), that they acknowledge His Divinity, which is Jacob and his seed;
וְכָל הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת אַבְרָהָם כָּל יָמָיו הָיָה בָּזֶה
and all the striving of Abraham throughout his days was focused upon this.
וְזֶהוּ מִדַּת הַחֶסֶד בְּהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת, וְרָצָה שֶׁיִּתְפַּרְסֵם זֶה לְכָל בָּאֵי עוֹלָם, וְהוּא מְגַיֵּיר הָאֲנָשִׁים וְשָׂרָה הַנָּשִׁים (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה ל״ט:י״ד)

And this is the attribute of Chesed in boundless outward expansion, wishing that this truth be publicized unto all inhabitants of the world, he converting the men and Sarah the women (Bereishis Rabbah 39:14).
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן יִצְחָק אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, לֹא מָצִינוּ שֶׁגִּיֵּיר גֵּרִים
Not so Isaac our father, peace be upon him, regarding whom we do not find that he converted converts;
כִּי הוּא מִדַּת הַצִּמְצוּם, שֶׁלֹּא יִתְפַּשֵּׁט אֶלָּא לַמָּקוֹם הָרָאוּי
for his is the attribute of contraction (Tzimtzum), that the light expand only unto an authentically fitting place;
כִּי רָאָה שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה תוֹעֶלֶת מִכָּל אוֹתָן גֵּרִים, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה: דְּאַחַר מִיתַת אַבְרָהָם חָזְרוּ כוּלָּם לְסוּרָן
for he saw that no permanent benefit emerged from all those converts, the Sages stating that after Abraham's death they all reverted to their unholy ways;
וּמִמֵּילָא וַדַּאי כָּל מַה שֶּׁלִּמְּדָן אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ נֶהְפַּךְ לָהֶם לְסַם הַמָּוֶת
and automatically, all that Abraham had taught them turned for them into a deadly poison;

דַּאֲפִילּוּ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁלֹּא זָכָה נַעֲשֵׂית לוֹ סַם הַמָּוֶת (יוֹמָא ע״ב עַמּוּד ב׳), כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּשַׁבָּת וּבִפְסָחִים (מְנָחוֹת ק״ט סוֹף עַמּוּד ב׳): ״שָׁנָה וּפֵירַשׁ — קָשֶׁה מִכּוּלָּן״.
for even with a Jew, if he does not merit, Torah becomes a poison of death (Yoma 72b), the Sages stating: "one who studied and departed is harsher than all" (Menachos 109b).
אֲבָל הוּא צִמְצוּם בְּיוֹתֵר, שֶׁלֹּא לְגַלּוֹת גַּם לָרְאוּיִין
But Isaac practiced an extreme contraction, not revealing Torah openly even unto the worthy;
שֶׁהֲרֵי יַעֲקֹב, אִיתָא בִּמְגִלָּה (י״ז עַמּוּד א׳) שֶׁהָלַךְ לִלְמוֹד לְבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ שֶׁל שֵׁם וָעֵבֶר
for behold regarding Jacob, Megillah (17a) states that he went to study in the house of study of Shem and Eber;
וּבְוַדַּאי יִצְחָק אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם יָדַע תּוֹרָה יוֹתֵר מֵהֶם, שֶׁקִּבֵּל מֵאַבְרָהָם דְּהָיוּ כִּלְיוֹתָיו כִּשְׁתֵּי מַעְיָנוֹת נוֹבְעוֹת תּוֹרָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ס״א:א׳)
and certainly Isaac our father knew far more Torah than they, having received from Abraham whose kidneys welled with Torah like two springs (Bereishis Rabbah 61:1);
וְקִיֵּים כָּל הַתּוֹרָה כוּלָּהּ עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִיתְּנָה (יוֹמָא כ״ח עַמּוּד ב׳)
and who fulfilled the entire Torah before it was given (Yoma 28b);
וְגַם מִצַּד עַצְמוֹ: דְּעִיקַּר הַתּוֹרָה מִסִּטְרָא דִּגְבוּרָה נָפְקַת (זֹוהַר), וְהוּא עִיקַּר הַתְחָלַת הַתּוֹרָה
and also on his own account: for the body of Torah goes forth from the side of Gevurah, and Isaac is the foundational origin of Torah;
אַף דִּשְׁנֵי אֲלָפִים תּוֹרָה הִתְחִילוּ ״מֵאֶת הַנֶּפֶשׁ אֲשֶׁר עָשׂוּ בְחָרָן״ (עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה ט׳ עַמּוּד א׳; בְּרֵאשִׁית י״ב:ה׳)
and though the two thousand years of Torah began from "the souls that they had gotten in Haran" (Avodah Zarah 9a; Bereishis 12:5);
מִכָּל מָקוֹם הוּא הַנֶּפֶשׁ הָרִאשׁוֹן בִּקְדוּשָׁה שֶׁנּוֹלְדָה אַחַר הַתְחָלַת שְׁנֵי אֲלָפִים תּוֹרָה
nevertheless Isaac was the very first holy soul born after the commencement of the two thousand years of Torah;
דְּאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ נוֹלַד מִקּוֹדֶם זֶה וְעַל כֵּן הָיָה ״תְּחִלָּה לַגֵּרִים״ (חֲגִיגָה ג׳ עַמּוּד א׳)
Abraham our father having been born prior to this, wherefore he was the first of converts (Chagigah 3a);
אֲבָל יִצְחָק נוֹלַד אַחַר כָּךְ וְנִמְשַׁךְ בּוֹ שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַתּוֹרָה בַּתּוֹלָדָה
while Isaac was born afterward, the root of the Torah being drawn into him congenitally from birth.
וְעַל כָּל פָּנִים וַדַּאי אַבְרָהָם וְיִצְחָק יָדְעוּ יוֹתֵר דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה מִשֵּׁם וָעֵבֶר
And at all events, Abraham and Isaac certainly knew more Torah than Shem and Eber;
וְגַם יִצְחָק וַדַּאי לָמַד תּוֹרָה לְבָנָיו, וּמֵעוֹלָם לֹא פָּסְקָה יְשִׁיבָה מֵאֲבוֹתֵינוּ
and Isaac certainly taught Torah unto his sons, the study session never having ceased from our Patriarchs;
וְגַם ״יִצְחָק זָקֵן וְיוֹשֵׁב בִּישִׁיבָה הָיָה״, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּיוֹמָא (כ״ח עַמּוּד ב׳)
and "Isaac was an elder sitting in the academy," as stated in Yoma (28b);
אֲבָל הָיָה בְּתַכְלִית הַצִּמְצוּם וְהַהֶעְלֵם:
but his teaching was governed by absolute contraction (tzimtzum) and concealment!
אוֹת ט׳ — כְּהֵיוֹן עֵינָיו שֶׁל יִצְחָק, הַזְכָּרַת הַשֵּׁם אַחַר שְׁתֵּי תֵּיבוֹת בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל, וְהַמַּחֲנוֹת לִפְנֵי מַחֲנֵה שְׁכִינָה
Section 9: The Dimming of Isaac's Eyes, Mentioning the Divine Name after Two Words, and The Camps Preceding the Shechinah

7.h: The theme: Isaac's blindness as inward concealment, the Sanhedrin as eyes of the congregation, and why Israel mentions the Divine Name after two words while angels require three. This explains the dimming of Isaac's eyes (kei'on einav, Bereishis 27:1). The Sanhedrin are titled "the eyes of the congregation" (einei ha-eidah), overseeing worldly conduct and publicizing Torah; but within Isaac, the light remained concealed. Abraham and Isaac are two extremes: pure expansion (hitpashtut) versus pure contraction (tzimtzum), whereas Jacob integrates both. When Isaac remarked: "Because Hashem your God sent me good speed" (Bereishis 27:20), the Sages noted: "The Name of Heaven was not habitual on Esau's lips" (Rashi ad loc.). Ramban struggled with this, for Isaac thought Esau was righteous; yet Isaac's contraction demanded that the Name of Heaven never be uttered casually, but only after profound preparation. In Chullin (91b), Israel are beloved because they mention the Divine Name after two words ("Hear, Israel: Hashem...", Devarim 6:4), whereas ministering angels require three words ("Holy, holy, holy, is Hashem of hosts", Yeshayah 6:3). There are three camps preceding the Shechinah—wind, earthquake, and fire (I Melachim 19:11–12)—mirroring the three unholy husks in Ezekiel (Yechezkel 1:4) before reaching the stillness where Hashem is revealed. Israel’s partition is within the angels (Yerushalmi Shabbat 6:9), issuing directly from the Throne of Glory; therefore two words suffice, matching the two camps (Israel and Levi) before the camp of the Shechinah. In Berachos (58a), earthly royalty mirrors heavenly royalty: when Elijah stood on the mountain, two heraldic bands passed before the King arrived. Elijah was an angel who never sinned; yet ba'alei teshuvah stand on an even higher partition, reaching Hashem through two rungs alone!

p: וְזֶה עִנְיַן כְּהֵיוֹן עֵינָיו (בְּרֵאשִׁית כ״ז:א׳)
And this is the inner meaning of the dimming of Isaac's eyes (Bereishis 27:1);
דְּסַנְהֶדְרִין נִקְרָאִים ״עֵינֵי הָעֵדָה״ (בַּמִּדְבָּר ט״ו:כ״ד), שֶׁהֵם הַמַּשְׁגִּיחִים עַל הַנְהָגַת כָּל הָעוֹלָם וּלְלַמְּדָם תּוֹרָה וּמִצְוֹת בְּפִרְסוּם לַכֹּל, וְאֶצְלוֹ הָיָה בְּהֶעְלֵם
for the Sanhedrin are termed "the eyes of the congregation" (Bamidbar 15:24), supervising the world and teaching Torah publicly, whereas with Isaac the vision operated in concealment.
כִּי אַבְרָהָם וְיִצְחָק הֵם ב׳ קְצוֹת: זֶה בְּהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת לְבַד, וְזֶה בְּצִמְצוּם לְבַד
For Abraham and Isaac represent two polar extremities: this one in pure expansion, and that one in pure contraction;
וְיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם מְחוּבָּר מִשְּׁנֵיהֶם לְהִתְנַהֵג בְּכָל אֶחָד בַּמָּקוֹם הָרָאוּי
and our father Jacob was synthesized from both, utilizing each in its appropriate domain.
וְזֶהוּ ״הַקֹּל קוֹל יַעֲקֹב״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית כ״ז:כ״ב), דְּאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה שֶׁאָמַר יִצְחָק: ״אֵין שֵׁם שָׁמַיִם שָׁגוּר בְּפִי עֵשָׂו״ (רַשִׁ״י שָׁם:כ׳)
And this is "the voice is the voice of Jacob" (Bereishis 27:22), the Sages explaining that Isaac remarked: "The Name of Heaven is not habitual upon Esau's lips" (Rashi on 27:20);
וְנִתְקַשָּׁה הָרַמְבַּ״ן: שֶׁהֲרֵי הוּא הֶחֱזִיק עֵשָׂו לְצַדִּיק
and the Ramban struggled with this: seeing that Isaac held Esau to be a tzaddik;

רַק הוּא מִצַּד צִמְצוּמוֹ, כִּי הוּא [עֵשָׂו] מִסְּתָמָא הָיָה רוֹצֶה לְהִתְדַּמּוֹת לְגַמְרֵי לְמַעֲשֵׂה יִצְחָק אָבִיו, כֵּיוָן שֶׁעָשָׂה רַק לִפְנִים וּלְהִתְדַּמּוֹת וְלֹא מִצַּד עַצְמוֹ וְכֹחַ קְדוּשָׁה שֶׁבּוֹ
but this was from Isaac's own contraction, for Esau sought to mimic Isaac's conduct externally without inward sanctity;

שֶׁזֶּה מִדַּת יִצְחָק אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם: לְצַמְצֵם עַצְמוֹ גַּם כֵּן שֶׁלֹּא לַהֲרוֹס לַעֲלוֹת אֶל ה׳, וְשֶׁלֹּא לְהַזְכִּיר תָּדִיר שֵׁם שָׁמַיִם רַק אַחַר הַכַּוָּונָה הָרְאוּיָה וּבַזְּמַן הָרָאוּי וּבַמָּקוֹם הָרָאוּי
it being Isaac's trait to contract himself not to break through to ascend, never uttering the Divine Name casually, but only with profound intent in an appropriate time and place;
וְלֹא מִיָּד בִּתְחִלַּת דִּבּוּרוֹ שֶׁנִּרְאֶה כְּמַזְכִּיר בְּלֹא הֲכָנָה וְכַוָּונָה כְּלָל, רַק שֶׁשָּׁגוּר בְּפִיו.
and not in casual opening speech where it appears without inward preparation.
וּבֶאֱמֶת צִמְצוּם זֶה הָיָה צָרִיךְ רַק לְיִצְחָק שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה מִטָּתוֹ שְׁלֵימָה וְיָצָא מִמֶּנּוּ פְּסֹולֶת
And in truth this severe contraction was necessary for Isaac whose bed was not whole, unholy dross emerging from him;
וּמִפְּנֵי אוֹתוֹ הַפְּסֹולֶת הָיָה צָרִיךְ לְצַמְצֵם עַצְמוֹ גַּם כֵּן
and on account of that dross he was compelled to contract himself;
אֲבָל יַעֲקֹב שֶׁכּוּלּוֹ קֹדֶשׁ לַה׳ וּמִטָּתוֹ שְׁלֵימָה, לֹא הָיָה צָרִיךְ עוֹד צִמְצוּמִים בְּעַצְמוֹ וְנַפְשׁוֹ.
but Jacob, whose bed was whole and entirely holy unto Hashem, required no such anxious contractions in his soul.

וּבְחֻלִּין (צ״א סוֹף עַמּוּד ב׳): ״חֲבִיבִין יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁמַּזְכִּירִין אֶת הַשֵּׁם אַחַר שְׁתֵּי תֵּיבוֹת [׳שְׁמַע יִשְׂרָאֵל ה׳׳], וּמַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת אַחַר שָׁלֹשׁ [׳קָדוֹשׁ קָדוֹשׁ קָדוֹשׁ ה׳׳]״

And in Chullin (91b): "Beloved are Israel, who mention the Divine Name after two words ('Hear, Israel: Hashem...'), while the ministering angels mention it after three ('Holy, holy, holy, is Hashem...')".
וְהָעִנְיָן: כִּי יֵשׁ ג׳ (שָׁלֹשׁ) מַחֲנוֹת לִפְנֵי מַחֲנֵה שְׁכִינָה
And the explanation is: there are three camps preceding the camp of the Shechinah;
כַּכָּתוּב בְּאֵלִיָּהוּ: ״רוּחַ״, וְ״רַעַשׁ״, ״אֵשׁ״, וְאַחַר כָּךְ ״קוֹל דְּמָמָה דַקָּה״ (מְלָכִים א י״ט:י״א–י״ב) שֶׁשָּׁם נִגְלָה כְּבוֹד ה׳
as written regarding Elijah: "wind," "earthquake," "fire," and afterward "a still small voice" (I Melachim 19:11–12) where Hashem's glory was revealed;
וְכֵן בָּעוֹלָמוֹת עֶלְיוֹנִים: אַרְבַּע עוֹלָמוֹת: אֲצִילוּת, בְּרִיאָה, יְצִירָה, עֲשִׂיָּה, וּבַאֲצִילוּת מִשְׁכַּן קָדְשׁוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ
and so in the supernal worlds: Atzilut, Beriah, Yetzirah, and Asiyah, the Sanctuary of the Blessed One resting in Atzilut;
וְכֵן בַּקְּלִיפָּה ״זֶה לְעֻמַּת זֶה״: ג׳ — ״רוּחַ סְעָרָה״, וְ״עָנָן [גָּדוֹל]״, וְ״אֵשׁ מִתְלַקַּחַת״, וְאַחַר כָּךְ ״וְנֹגַהּ לוֹ סָבִיב״ (יְחֶזְקֵאל א:ד)
and so in the unholy husk, opposite them: "a stormy wind," "a great cloud," and "a fire infolding itself," followed by "a brightness round about it" (Yechezkel 1:4);
וְכֵן הוּא דֶּרֶךְ הַהַשָּׂגָה: צָרִיךְ לַעֲבוֹר ג׳ מַדְרֵיגוֹת הַקּוֹדְמִים כִּי אָוְושִׁי, לְהַסְעִיר הַנֶּפֶשׁ שֶׁיּוּכַל לְקַבֵּל קְדֻשַּׁת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
such being the order of spiritual perception: traversing the three turbulent stages that storm the soul so it can receive His holiness.

וְיִשְׂרָאֵל מְחִיצָתָן לִפְנִים מִמַּלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּיְרוּשַׁלְמִי דְּשַׁבָּת (פֶּרֶק ו׳ הֲלָכָה ט׳) עַל הַפָּסוּק ״כָּעֵת יֵאָמֵר לְיַעֲקֹב וּלְיִשְׂרָאֵל מַה פָּעַל אֵל״ (בַּמִּדְבָּר כ״ג:כ״ג)
And Israel dwell in an interior partition within the ministering angels (Yerushalmi Shabbat 6:9 on Bamidbar 23:23);
כִּי הֵם אֲצוּלִים מִכִּסֵּא הַכָּבוֹד שֶׁהוּא לְמַעְלָה מֵעוֹלַם הַמַּלְאָכִים, סַגִּי לְהוּ בִּבְתֵּי תֵּיבוֹת
for being emanated from the Throne of Glory which transcends the angels, two words suffice for them;
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּחֻלִּין שָׁם בָּאוֹפַנִּים וְחַיּוֹת שֶׁהֵם מִכִּסֵּא הַכָּבוֹד עַצְמוֹ דְּסַגִּי לְהוּ בִּבְתֵּי תֵּיבוֹת (חֻלִּין צ״ב רֵישׁ עַמּוּד א׳)
as stated in Chullin regarding the Ophanim and Chayot who derive from the Throne of Glory itself, for whom two words suffice;
כְּמוֹ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל, כְּשֶׁיָּרְדָה שְׁכִינָה לְמַטָּה הָיָה רַק שְׁתֵּי מַחֲנוֹת: מַחֲנֵה יִשְׂרָאֵל וּמַחֲנֵה לְוִיָּה לִפְנֵי מַחֲנֵה שְׁכִינָה.
just as in the desert, when the Shechinah descended, there were only two camps—the camp of Israel and the camp of Levi—before the camp of the Shechinah.
וּבִבְרָכוֹת (נ״ח עַמּוּד א׳): ״דְּמַלְכוּתָא דְּאַרְעָא כְּעֵין מַלְכוּתָא דִּרְקִיעָא״, הָיָה רַק ב׳ נֶגְדִּי: כִּי אָוְושָׁא וְכוּלֵיהּ, שְׁתִיקֵי וְאָתֵי מַלְכָּא
And in Berachos (58a): "earthly royalty is patterned after heavenly royalty," there were only two heraldic troops before the king arrived;
וּמַיְיתֵי קְרָא דְּאֵלִיָּהוּ, וַהֲרֵי שָׁם הָיָה שָׁלֹשׁ?
and the Talmud cites the verse of Elijah where three phenomena appeared?
רַק דְּשָׁם לְגַבֵּי אֵלִיָּהוּ שֶׁהוּא מַלְאָךְ כְּאַחַד מִמַּלְאֲכֵי מָרוֹם, כִּי לֹא חָטָא מֵעוֹלָם
but regarding Elijah who was an angel, having never sinned;
וְעַל כֵּן לֹא זָכָה לְחֵילָא יַתִּיר דְּבַעֲלֵי תְּשׁוּבָה שֶׁמּוֹשְׁכִין בְּכֹחַ טְפֵי, וּ״בִמְקוֹם שֶׁבַּעֲלֵי תְּשׁוּבָה עוֹמְדִין וְכוּלֵיהּ״
he did not merit the extraordinary power of ba'alei teshuvah who pull with greater strength, standing in that highest partition;
וְ״אֵין אָדָם צַדִּיק בָּאָרֶץ וְכוּלֵיהּ״ (קֹהֶלֶת ז:כ), וְהַכֹּל בַּעֲלֵי תְּשׁוּבָה חוּץ מֵאֵלִיָּהוּ, דְּעַל כֵּן נֶהְפַּךְ לְמַלְאָךְ שֶׁאֵינוֹ בְּגֶדֶר אָדָם
and all mortals are ba'alei teshuvah except Elijah who was transformed into an angel;
דְּאָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁכָּל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ נִטְבָּעִים בִּדְיוֹקְנוֹ חָטָא וְהוּצְרַךְ לִתְשׁוּבָה
Adam HaRishon having sinned and requiring repentance;
דְּעַל זֶה הָיָה בְּרִיאַת הָאָדָם: שֶׁיַּגִּיעַ לִמְקוֹם שֶׁבַּעֲלֵי תְּשׁוּבָה עוֹמְדִין שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה מִמַּדְרֵיגַת הַמַּלְאָכִים
this being the ultimate purpose of man's creation: to attain the station of ba'alei teshuvah transcending the angels;
וְעַל כֵּן מַלְכוּתָא דְּאַרְעָא הַמּוּשָׂג לְלִבְּבוֹת דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל — סַגִּי בִּבְתֵּי מַחֲנוֹת:
wherefore for the hearts of Israel, two camps suffice to perceive the King!

7.h: אוֹת י׳ — ״קִידּוּשׁ הַשֵּׁם אַחַר שְׁתֵּי תֵּיבוֹת בְּיַעֲקֹב, הָאוֹר הַגָּנוּז בְּאַבְרָהָם, וְהָאֵשׁ וְהֶעָשָׁן בְּמַתַּן תּוֹרָה — Section 10: Jacob Mentioning Hashem after Two Words, Abraham's Primordial Light, and Fire and Smoke at Sinai

The theme: Jacob uttering the Divine Name after two words, Abraham’s light versus Isaac’s smoke and dark mirror, and Moshe’s glowing countenance. This supreme love for Israel began with our father Jacob, named Israel, unto whom host-camps of angels were dispatched to escort him (Bereishis 32:2–3). This was "the voice of Jacob" saying the Divine Name after two words: "Because Hashem [word three] your God sent me good speed" (Bereishis 27:20). Abraham began publicizing the Name of Hashem ("and Abraham called on the name of Hashem, the Everlasting God", Bereishis 21:33), acting in boundless expansion. Abraham was the primordial light emerging after two thousand years of chaos ("Let there be light—this is Abraham", Bereishis Rabbah 2:3). That light was the primordial light of the Seven Days of Creation, which was hidden away from the wicked; Isaac came and concealed that blinding light, for an overpowering light blinds eyes unready to absorb it ("He made darkness His secret place", Tehillim 18:12). At Sinai, the mountain burned with fire wrapped in thick smoke: fire illuminates, but smoke is the dark cloud that veils the light. The people stood afar, beholding the smoke; Moshe approached the thick darkness (arafel) into the camp of the Shechinah, Aaron stood in the camp of Levi, and Israel in the camp of Israel. All Israel perceived the light through a dark mirror (aspaklaria she-einah me'irah, Yevamos 49b), while Moshe perceived it through a luminous mirror (aspaklaria ha-me'irah). Jacob represents the central balancing line (amuda d'emtza'ita) harmonizing expansion and contraction. Isaac was the dark side (Chashocha, Zohar I, 168b), whose dross was Esau; his eyes grew dim through beholding the supernal light at the Binding of Isaac (Akeidah) and the smoke of Esau’s wives. In Moshe, whose eyes never dimmed ("his eye was not dim", Devarim 34:7), the internal and external were united. In Jacob, a trace of Esau's darkness was present until Abraham died, whereupon Abraham's light pushed that darkness completely into Esau!

p: וַחֲבִיבוּת זֶה דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל הִתְחִיל מִיַּעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁנִּקְרָא שְׁמוֹ ״יִשְׂרָאֵל״
And this supreme love for Israel began with our father Jacob, peace be upon him, who was named "Israel";
דְּעָלָיו נֶאֱמַר: ״כָּעֵת יֵאָמֵר לְיַעֲקֹב וּלְיִשְׂרָאֵל מַה פָּעַל אֵל״ (בַּמִּדְבָּר כ״ג:כ״ג), וְעַל כֵּן נִשְׁלְחוּ לוֹ מַחֲנוֹת מַלְאָכִים לְלַוּוֹתוֹ, מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בְּאַבְרָהָם וְיִצְחָק

concerning whom it is said: "Now shall it be said of Jacob and of Israel: What has God wrought!" (Bamidbar 23:23), wherefore host-camps of angels were dispatched to escort him (Bereishis 32:2–3), which did not occur with Abraham and Isaac.
וְזֶהוּ ״קוֹל יַעֲקֹב״: שֶׁאָמַר הַשֵּׁם אַחַר שְׁתֵּי תֵּיבוֹת: ״כִּי הִקְרָה — ה׳״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית כ״ז:כ׳)
And this is "the voice of Jacob": uttering the Divine Name after two words: "Because Hashem [word 3] your God sent me good speed" (Bereishis 27:20).
וּתְחִלַּת הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת זֶה דְּהַכָּרַת קְדֻשַּׁת הַשֵּׁם בִּבְרוּאֵי מַטָּה הוּא מֵאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
And the inception of this expansion—the recognition of the sanctity of Hashem among lower creations—began from Abraham our father;
דִּכְתִיב בֵּיהּ: ״וַיִּקְרָא שָׁם [אַבְרָהָם] בְּשֵׁם ה׳ אֵל עוֹלָם״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית כ״א:ל״ג), שֶׁהוּא פִּרְסֵם דָּבָר זֶה: שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הוּא כֹּחַ כָּל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ שֶׁהַכֹּל מִמֶּנּוּ
for it is written: "and Abraham called there on the name of Hashem, the Everlasting God" (Bereishis 21:33), publicizing that Hashem is the vital force of all Creation.
אֶלָּא שֶׁאַבְרָהָם וְיִצְחָק ב׳ קְצוֹת, וְכָל אֶחָד נָטָה בְּמִדָּתוֹ לַקָּצֶה הָאַחֲרוֹן
Except that Abraham and Isaac represented two opposite poles, each leaning toward an extreme;
וְעַל כֵּן מִצַּד אַבְרָהָם הָיָה תַּכְלִית הַהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת, שֶׁחָשַׁב שֶׁיְּפֻרְסַם לְגַמְרֵי אֱלֹהוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּכָל הַלְּבָבוֹת בְּלִי שׁוּם הַגְדָּרָה
Abraham operating in boundless expansion, seeking to publicize Divinity across all hearts without any contraction;
וְהִזְכִּיר הַשֵּׁם גַּם אַחַר תֵּיבָה אַחַת
uttering the Divine Name even after a single word;
וְהוּא הַתְחָלַת הָאוֹרָה שֶׁאַחַר הַחֹשֶׁךְ דִּשְׁנֵי אֲלָפִים תֹּהוּ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה ב׳:ג׳): ״׳יְהִי אוֹר׳ (בְּרֵאשִׁית א:ג) — זֶה אַבְרָהָם״
being the initial light emerging after the two thousand years of chaos: "'Let there be light'—this is Abraham" (Bereishis Rabbah 2:3).

וְהוּא הָאוֹר דְּשִׁבְעַת יְמֵי בְּרֵאשִׁית שֶׁאָדָם צוֹפֶה בּוֹ מִסּוֹף הָעוֹלָם וְעַד סוֹפוֹ, וְנִגְנַז בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה מִפְּנֵי הָרְשָׁעִים שֶׁאֵין רְאוּיִם לְאוֹר כָּזֶה (חֲגִיגָה י״ב עַמּוּד א׳)
And that was the primordial light of the Seven Days of Creation by which man gazed from one end of the world to the other, which was hidden away from the wicked who are unworthy of it (Chagigah 12a).
וְעַל כֵּן בָּא יִצְחָק אַחַר כָּךְ וְגָנַז אוֹר בָּהִיר הַזֶּה
Wherefore Isaac arose afterward and hid this brilliant light;
כִּי אוֹר חָזָק לְמִי שֶׁאֵין רָאוּי לְקַבְּלוֹ — מַכְהֶה עֵינָיו, וְעַל כֵּן נֶאֱמַר: ״יָשֶׁת חֹשֶׁךְ סִתְרוֹ״ (תְּהִלִּים י״ח:י״ב)
for an intense light blinds the eyes of one unprepared to receive it, concerning which it is said: "He made darkness His secret place" (Tehillim 18:12).
וְכֵן בְּמַתַּן תּוֹרָה: ״וְהָהָר בֹּעֵר בָּאֵשׁ... חֹשֶׁךְ עָנָן וַעֲרָפֶל״ (דְּבָרִים ד:יא), דְּאַף שֶׁהָאֵשׁ מֵאִיר, הֶעָשָׁן שֶׁסְּבִיבוֹתָיו הוּא חֹשֶׁךְ הַמַּעֲלִים הָאוֹר
And so at Sinai: "and the mountain burned with fire... with darkness, clouds, and thick darkness" (Devarim 4:11), the smoke veiling the flame;
וּ״מֹשֶׁה נִגַּשׁ אֶל הָעֲרָפֶל״ (שְׁמוֹת כ:יח) לְמַחֲנֵה שְׁכִינָה, וְאַהֲרֹן בְּמַחֲנֵה לְוִיָּה, וְהֵם בְּמַחֲנֵה יִשְׂרָאֵל
Moshe drawing near unto the thick darkness to the camp of the Shechinah, Aaron in the camp of Levi, and Israel in the camp of Israel;
שֶׁזָּכוּ לָהּ כָּל זֶרַע יַעֲקֹב לְהַשִּׂיג עַל כָּל פָּנִים הֶעָשָׁן הַמִּתְפַּשֵּׁט מֵהָאֵשׁ, וְאֵין זֶה חֹשֶׁךְ גָּמוּר רַק כְּעַרְפְלֵי טֹהַר
meriting to perceive the smoke spreading from the fire, which is not absolute darkness but translucent clouds of purity;
וְהָאוֹר מוּשָׂג מִתּוֹכוֹ כִּמְסְתַּכֵּל בְּאַסְפַּקְלַרְיָא שֶׁאֵינָהּ מְאִירָה
the light perceived from within it like gazing through a dim mirror (aspaklaria she-einah me'irah);
דְּרַק מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הִסְתַּכֵּל בְּאַסְפַּקְלַרְיָא הַמְּאִירָה (יְבָמוֹת מ״ט עַמּוּד ב׳)
for Moshe Rabbeinu alone gazed through the luminous mirror (Yevamos 49b).
וְזֶהוּ מִדַּת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם — קַו הָאֶמְצָעִי הַמְחַבֵּר שְׁתֵּי הַקְּצוֹת לֶאֱחוֹז בַּדֶּרֶךְ הַמְמוּצָּע
And this is the attribute of Jacob: the central column uniting both extremes to seize the golden mean;
כִּי יִצְחָק אָחַז בַּקָּצֶה הָאַחֲרוֹן שֶׁהוּא תַּכְלִית הַצִּמְצוּם וְהַהֶעְלֵם, וְכֵן אִיתָא בַּזֹּוהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (וַיִּשְׁלַח קס״ח רֵישׁ עַמּוּד ב׳): ״יִצְחָק דְּאִיהוּ חֲשׁוֹכָא״, עַיֵּין שָׁם
for Isaac seized the extreme of absolute contraction and concealment, the Zohar stating: "Isaac who is darkness," see there;
וְעַל כֵּן הַפְּסֹולֶת שֶׁלּוֹ הוּא חֹשֶׁךְ גָּמוּר מִסִּטְרָא דְּ״אַחְשֵׁךְ אַנְפֵּי בִּרְיָין״ (זֹוהַר)
wherefore his dross is absolute darkness, darkening the faces of creations.
וְזֶהוּ גַּם כֵּן כְּהֵיוֹן עֵינָיו, שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה: דְּהָיָה עַל יְדֵי הִסְתַּכְּלוּתוֹ בָּעֲקֵידָה, וְעַל יְדֵי נְשֵׁי עֵשָׂו (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה ס״ה:י׳)
And this is the inner cause of Isaac's blindness: stemming from beholding the Shechinah at the Binding (Akeidah) and the smoke of the incense of Esau's wives (Bereishis Rabbah 65:10);
וְהָא בְּהָא תַּלְיָא: דְּאוֹתוֹ אוֹר מוּפְלָא שֶׁהִשִּׂיג בָּעֲקֵידָה שֶׁגָּרַם כְּהֵיוֹן עֵינָיו לִזְקְנוּתוֹ, הָיָה אַחַר שֶׁנִּתְבָּרַר פְּסֹולֶת הָרָע שֶׁיָּצָא מִמֶּנּוּ בִּנְשֵׁי עֵשָׂו.
both causes being interdependent: the transcendent light he gazed upon at the Akeidah caused his blindness in old age after the evil dross issuing from him was manifest in Esau's wives.
וּבְיַעֲקֹב הָיָה תְּחִלָּה גַּם כֵּן שֶׁמֶץ מֵאוֹתוֹ פְּסֹולֶת דְּעֵשָׂו מִצַּד ״הַהוּצֵי שֶׁסְּבִיב הָאָסָא״ (סַנְהֶדְרִין מ״ד עַמּוּד א׳)
And within Jacob there was initially a subtle trace of that dross of Esau, like the thorns encircling the myrtle (Sanhedrin 44a);

עַד יוֹם שֶׁמֵּת אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, שֶׁאָז נִקְלַט בּוֹ הַקְּדוּשָׁה דְּאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ, וְאוֹרוֹ דָּחָה הַחֹשֶׁךְ לַמָּקוֹם הָרָאוּי לוֹ שֶׁהוּא בְּעֵשָׂו, וְנִתְמַלֵּא כוּלּוֹ בְּחֹשֶׁךְ גָּמוּר:
until the day Abraham died, whereupon Abraham's holiness was absorbed into Jacob, his light driving the darkness into Esau, who became filled with absolute darkness!

7.h: אוֹת י״א — מְכִירַת הַבְּכוֹרָה, עֲדָשִׁים עֲגוּלִים דְּאַבְרָהָם מוּל גַּוֶּון הָאָדֹם דְּיִצְחָק, וְהַלְעָטַת עֵשָׂו — Section 11: The Sale of the Birthright, Abraham's Round Lentils vs. Isaac's Red Hue, and Esau's Devouring

The theme: The birthright as congenital holiness, the funeral meal (se'udat havra'ah) of red lentils, and Esau devouring the dross. The birthright (bechorah) was the congenital sanctity of the firstborn. In Esau this sanctity was rooted in his ancestors, yet he had the power to exchange it. Jacob prepared red lentils as the mourning meal (se'udat havra'ah) for his father Isaac upon Abraham's death. Isaac's attribute of strict Judgment was the opposite of Abraham's Southern expansion (Chesed); Jacob synthesized the two. Lentils are round, symbolizing the spherical dimension (Iggulim) of Abraham where all souls are equal without divisions; while red is the color of Isaac and the linear dimension of strict gradations (Yosher). Cooking red lentils for Abraham's mourning united Iggulim and Yosher. But Esau demanded: "Feed me with that same red stew" (Bereishis 25:30)—mentioning neither lentils nor the meal, but solely the red color. Esau possessed no connection to the holy unification of attributes, absorbing all the dross of red Judgment, thereby selling the birthright. Through swallowing the red stew, all the dross of that color latent within Jacob transferred unto Esau, who became the sum of all cosmic darkness, while Jacob retained the spiritual birthright!

p: וְזֶהוּ מְכִירַת הַבְּכוֹרָה, כִּי קְדוּשָׁה זוֹ הוּא מַה שֶּׁבַּתּוֹלָדָה שֶׁנּוֹצַר בְּכוֹר
And this is the mystery of the sale of the birthright, for this sanctity was the congenital holiness of being formed as firstborn;
וְרַק בְּעֵשָׂו הָיָה קְדוּשָׁה בַּתּוֹלָדָה מֵאֲבוֹתָיו, אֲבָל הָיָה בְּכֹחוֹ לַהֲמִירָהּ וּלְסַלְּקוֹ
and in Esau this holiness was inherited from his ancestors, yet he possessed the power to exchange it and cast it off.

וְכֵן הָיָה בְּכֹחוֹ מְכִירַת הַבְּכוֹרָה, וְהוּא עַל יְדֵי הַלְעָטַת הָעֲדָשִׁים מִסְּעוּדַת הַבְרָאָה דְּאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא ט״ז עַמּוּד ב׳) וּבְרַשִׁ״י (בְּרֵאשִׁית כ״ה:ל׳)
And so the sale of the birthright occurred through gulping the lentils from the mourning meal of Abraham our father (Bava Batra 16b; Rashi on Bereishis 25:30);
דְּיַעֲקֹב בִּשֵּׁל זֶה לְהַבְרוֹת לְאָבִיו בִּסְעוּדָה רִאשׁוֹנָה דַּאֲכִילָתוֹ, שֶׁהוּא לְנַחֲמוֹ: שֶׁהַמֵּת יָמוּת, וְהַבָּא בַּחַיִּים יִחְיֶה וְיִסְעַד לְבָבוֹ
Jacob cooking this to comfort his father at his first meal: that the dead dies, while the living must live and sustain his heart;
כִּי אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁזֶּה מֵת, חַיּוּתוֹ שָׁבַק לְכָל חָי.
for though Abraham died, his spiritual vitality was bequeathed unto all living.

וּלְפִי שֶׁדַּרְגָּא דְּיִצְחָק הִיא הֵיפֶךְ דַּרְגָּא דְּאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם: זֶה בִּקְצֵה הַדָּרוֹם: ״הָלוֹךְ וְנָסוֹעַ הַנֶּגְבָּה״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית י״ב:ט׳), וְזֶה בִּקְצֵה הַצָּפוֹן (גְּבוּרָה)
And because Isaac's rung was the polar opposite of Abraham's: Abraham in the South of Chesed ("going on still toward the South", Bereishis 12:9), and Isaac in the North of strict Gevurah;
עַל יְדֵי יַעֲקֹב הָיָה הִתְחַבְּרוּת שְׁתֵּי הַמַּדְרֵיגוֹת
through Jacob occurred the unification of both rungs;
וְעַל כֵּן כָּל סְעוּדַת הַבְרָאָה עַל יְדֵי אֲחֵרִים, כִּי כָּל אָב וּבֵן הֵם מֵעֵין דּוּגְמָא קְצָת לִבְתֵּי קְצוֹת, וְצָרִיךְ לְחַבֵּר עַל יְדֵי אֶמְצָעִי.
wherefore the meal of condolence is served by another, every father and son representing two poles requiring mediation by a central third.
וּבִישׁוּל עֲדָשִׁים אֲדֻמּוֹת: דְּגַוֶּון הָאָדוֹם הוּא מִסִּטְרָא דְּיִצְחָק, וַעֲדָשִׁים עֲגוּלִים דַּרְגָּא דְּאַבְרָהָם
And cooking red lentils: the red hue is from Isaac, while the round shape of lentils is the rung of Abraham;
כִּידוּעַ ״עִגּוּלִים״ וְ״יֹשֶׁר״: שֶׁבְּעִגּוּל אֵין חִילּוּק מַדְרֵיגוֹת, וְעוֹלָם כְּכַדּוּר הַכֹּל שָׁוֶה
as known in the mystery of Iggulim and Yosher: in a circle there are no hierarchical divisions, all points of the sphere being equidistant;
וְזֶהוּ מִדַּת אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁרָצָה לְאַחוֹת כָּל בָּאֵי עוֹלָם לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּלֹא מַדְרֵיגוֹת
this being Abraham's trait of Chesed, desiring to unite all humanity unto Hashem without hierarchical separations;

וְדָבָר זֶה אֵינוֹ עַדַיִין בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, רַק לְעֵת קֵץ: כְּשֶׁ״עָמְדוּ רַגְלָיו [עַל הַר הַזֵּיתִים]״ (זְכַרְיָה י״ד:ד׳) וְיִכְלֶה קוֹמַת הַיֹּשֶׁר וְיִתְגַּלֶּה הָעִגּוּלִים כַּנּוֹדָע
which is not yet openly manifest in this world, reserved for the End of Days when His feet stand upon the Mount of Olives (Zechariah 14:4) and Iggulim are revealed;
וְיִצְחָק הוּא נֶגֶד הַיֹּשֶׁר, שֶׁהוּא בְּצִמְצוּם וְקַו חָלוּק לְמַדְרֵיגוֹת
while Isaac corresponds to Yosher, linear contraction divided into precise rungs;
וְעַל כֵּן נְזִיד הָעֲדָשִׁים הָאֲדֻמִּים לִסְעוּדָה זוֹ בְּמִיתַת אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם — הוּא חִבּוּר שְׁתֵּי הַמַּדְרֵיגוֹת יַחַד.
wherefore the red lentil stew cooked upon Abraham's death was the cosmic union of both dimensions!
וְעֵשָׂו אָמַר: ״הַלְעִיטֵנִי [נָא] מִן הָאָדֹם [הָאָדֹם הַזֶּה]״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית כ״ה:ל׳), לֹא הִזְכִּיר עֲדָשִׁים רַק הַגַּוֶּון הָאָדוֹם
But Esau said: "Feed me, I pray you, with that same red stew" (Bereishis 25:30), mentioning not lentils, but solely the red color;
כִּי הוּא אֵין לוֹ שַׁיָּיכוּת לְחִבּוּר הַמִּדּוֹת שֶׁהֵם מִצַּד הַקְּדוּשָׁה
having no connection to the holy unification of attributes;
וְהוּא קָלַט כָּל הָרָע שֶׁהוּא תַּכְלִית הָאַדְמִימוּת וְכָל הַפְּסֹולֶת שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּעוֹלָם מִצַּד מִדָּה זוֹ
absorbing all the evil of absolute redness and the dross of unmitigated Judgment;
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה מִמֵּילָא מָכַר הַבְּכוֹרָה
and through this he automatically sold the birthright;
שֶׁבְּהַלְעָטַת הָאָדוֹם כָּל הַפְּסֹולֶת שֶׁבְּגַוֶּון זֶה שֶׁהָיָה אֵצֶל יַעֲקֹב נִקְלַט לוֹ, וְנַעֲשָׂה הוּא כְּלָלוּת הַחֹשֶׁךְ שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם
for in gulping the red stew, all dross of that color latent within Jacob was absorbed into Esau, who became the sum of cosmic darkness;
וּמִמֵּילָא נִדְחָה קְדֻשַּׁת הַבְּכוֹרָה שֶׁהוּא מְעַט הָאוֹר שֶׁבַּתּוֹלָדָה
the congenital holiness of the birthright being cast out from him;
שֶׁהָיָה בוֹ מִסִּטְרָא דְּאַבְרָהָם שֶׁהָיָה כֹּהֵן, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ: ״אַתָּה כֹהֵן לְעוֹלָם״ (תְּהִלִּים ק״י:ד׳; נְדָרִים ל״ב עַמּוּד ב׳)
which he possessed from Abraham the Priest (Nedarim 32b on Tehillim 110:4);
וְאָז הָיָה הָעֲבוֹדָה בַּבְּכוֹרוֹת שֶׁהֵם הָיוּ כֹּהֲנִים (זְבָחִים קי״ב עַמּוּד ב׳).
when divine service was performed by firstborns who served as priests.
וְיַעֲקֹב בְּכוֹר לִיצִירָה, דְּהַיְינוּ מִצַּד הָאֱמֶת הַנֶּעְלָם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
And Jacob was firstborn in creation, from the vantage of the truth hidden in this world;
אֲבָל מִצַּד הִתְגַּלּוּת בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה בַּלֵּידָה, הָיָה עֵשָׂו בְּכוֹר לְמַרְאִית עַיִן
but in physical birth, Esau emerged first to outward appearance;
כִּי הָעֲבוֹדָה הוּא בְּמַעֲשֶׂה וְכֹחַ הַפְּעֻלָּה, וְעֵשָׂו הוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ כֹּחַ הַמַּעֲשִׂים
for temple service involves physical action, and Esau was the archetype of action.
וְכָל זְמַן שֶׁהָיָה אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם עַצְמוֹ בַּחַיִּים מְלוּבָּשׁ בְּגוּף גַּשְׁמִי בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
And so long as Abraham was alive clothed in a physical body;
הָיָה הִתְלַבְּשׁוּת גַּשְׁמִי מִמַּדְרֵיגָתוֹ מִצַּד הָעֵירוּב דְּטוֹב וָרָע שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם הַגּוּפָנִי בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה גַּם בְּעֵשָׂו
a physical garment of his rung resided within Esau through the mixture of good and evil in the corporeal world;
אֲבָל בִּפְטִירָתוֹ, דְּנִשְׁאַר הַקְּדוּשָׁה הָרוּחָנִית שֶׁלּוֹ בְּלֹא הִתְלַבְּשׁוּת גַּשְׁמִי בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, לָזֶה לֹא הָיָה עוֹד שַׁיָּיכוּת לְעֵשָׂו
but upon Abraham's passing, when his holiness remained purely spiritual without physical garb, Esau had no connection to it;
שֶׁכָּל כֹּחוֹ מִצַּד הִתְלַבְּשׁוּת הַגַּשְׁמִי דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, מִצַּד זֶה יוּכַל לִפְשׁוֹט טְלָפָיו וּלְהַרְאוֹת עַצְמוֹ טָהוֹר כִּי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה עָלְמָא דְּשִׁקְרָא
his power existing strictly in physical garments where he displayed his hooves as clean in this world of falsehood;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן מִצַּד ״אֱמֶת לְיַעֲקֹב״ (מִיכָה ז:כ), וְעַל כֵּן הָרוּחָנִיּוּת קָלַט רַק יַעֲקֹב, וְאָז: ״וַיָּזֶד יַעֲקֹב נָזִיד״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית כ״ה:כ״ט):
whereas Jacob absorbed the pure spiritual essence, whereupon "Jacob sod pottage" (Bereishis 25:29)!

7.h: אוֹת י״ב — מַאֲכָלוֹ שֶׁל יִצְחָק גָּדוֹל מִקָּרְבַּן הָאַיִל, שְׂעִיר עֲזָאזֵל, וְתִיקּוּן מַאֲכַל אֲבֵלִים — Section 12: Isaac's Meal Greater than Sacrifices, The Scapegoat, and Rectifying the Mourner's Food

The theme: Jacob's first deed in the world of Asiyah, holy eating surpassing the sacrifice of the ram at the Akeidah, and rectifying the primeval curse of eating in sorrow. The deeds of the Patriarchs inscribed in the Torah are cosmic milestones. Cooking the pottage was Jacob's first recorded action in the world of Asiyah—where deed is primary. Jacob, dwelling in tents of Torah, knew this physical world is predominantly evil and feared that acting in physical labor would give a foothold to Esau's dross; only upon Abraham's death, when the light separated from the darkness, was he empowered to act. Holy eating in this world is likened unto sacrifices: the table is an altar (Chagigah 27a), wine is a libation, and honoring a scholar is like offering first-fruits (Berachos 10b; Kesubos 105b). In Bereishis Rabbah (67:2) on "Because Hashem sent me good speed": if Hashem orchestrates animals for sacrifices, how much more so for the food of the righteous! Isaac's meal was greater than the ram offered in his stead at the Akeidah: a sacrifice is consumed by fire on the altar, whereas food consumed by a tzaddik enters a living consuming fire (esh ochelah), fire being the very attribute of Isaac! Gulping the stew mirrored the scapegoat (se'ir la-Azazel): two identical goats are cast by lot, where Hashem supports the holy lot for Himself while the unholy goat carries away iniquity (Yoma 67b). Esau gulped like a beast (Bereishis Rabbah 63:12: "one may gulp a camel on the Sabbath"), acting as a beast whose sacrifice is animal food. Man lives by the spiritual word of Hashem within food; animals live merely by the physical matter. Animals cannot cook to separate dross; cooking is human rectification. By cooking this mourner's meal, Jacob initiated the cosmic repair of Adam's sin—rectifying the primeval curse: "in sorrow shall you eat of it" (b'itzavon tochlena, Bereishis 3:17), itzavon denoting mourning (Bereishis Rabbah 11:2). Scripture chronicles the cooking of the stew and not the eating, for Jacob's spiritual labor was in the preparation; the eating of mourning is transient, destined to be swallowed up when death is abolished forever!

p: וְכָל פְּעֻלַּת הָאָבוֹת לֹא הָיוּ דְּבָרִים רֵיקִים, וְכָל שֶׁכֵּן אוֹתָם שֶׁנִּכְתְּבוּ בַּתּוֹרָה לְעוֹלְמֵי עַד
And all the actions of the Patriarchs were never empty matters, all the more so those inscribed in the eternal Torah;
וְכָל שֶׁכֵּן בִּפְעֻלָּה זוֹ הָרִאשׁוֹנָה דְּיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁנִּזְכַּר בַּתּוֹרָה — וַדַּאי עִנְיָן גָּדוֹל
and all the more so this first recorded deed of our father Jacob in the Torah, which is certainly a monumental reality;
כִּי זֶה הָיָה הִתְגַּלּוּת כֹּחַ הַמַּעֲשֶׂה הָרִאשׁוֹן דְּיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בְּעוֹלַם הָעֲשִׂיָּה, שֶׁלֹּא הַמִּדְרָשׁ עִיקָּר בּוֹ אֶלָּא הַמַּעֲשֶׂה
for this was the first manifestation of Jacob's power of practical action in the world of Asiyah, where not study is primary but deed.
וְיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם יוֹשֵׁב אָהֳלֵי תּוֹרָה, שֶׁהוּא גַּם כֵּן מִסִּטְרָא דִּגְבוּרָה
And our father Jacob dwelled in the tents of Torah, which also stems from the side of Gevurah;
וְכֹחַ הַמַּעֲשֶׂה שֶׁמִּסִּטְרָא דִּגְבוּרָה חָשַׁב דְּשַׁיָּיךְ לְעֵשָׂו, כִּי רָאָה דְּעוֹלַם הָעֲשִׂיָּה הַגּוּפָנִי הַזֶּה רוּבּוֹ רַע וְנוֹטֶה לִמְקוֹם טוּמְאָה
and he initially assumed the power of physical action from Gevurah belonged to Esau, seeing that this physical world of action is predominantly evil and veers toward defilement;
וְכָל זְמַן שֶׁהִרְגִּישׁ בּוֹ עַדַיִין קְצָת פְּסֹולֶת הַשַּׁיָּיךְ לְעֵשָׂו, נִתְיָירֵא לִפְעוֹל שׁוּם פְּעֻלָּה וַעֲבוֹדָה בְּמַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה אֲחִיזָה בּוֹ גַּם לְסִטְרָא דְּרָע
and so long as he sensed within himself a subtle trace of Esau's dross, he was afraid to execute any physical labor lest the unholy husk seize a foothold;
עַד יוֹם פְּטִירָתוֹ דְּאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, שֶׁקָּלַט אוֹרוֹ וְנִפְרַד הַחֹשֶׁךְ.
until the day Abraham passed away, whereupon Jacob absorbed his light and the darkness was severed.
וְיָדוּעַ: כָּל אֲכִילוֹת שֶׁבִּקְדוּשָׁה דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה — דּוּגְמַת קָרְבָּנוֹת
And it is known: all holy eating in this world mirrors the sacrifices;

כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ: ״שֻׁלְחָן — דּוֹמֶה לַמִּזְבֵּחַ״ (בְּרָכוֹת נ״ה עַמּוּד א׳), וְדוֹרוֹן לְתַלְמִיד חָכָם כְּבִכּוּרִים (כְּתוּבּוֹת ק״ה סוֹף עַמּוּד ב׳), וְיַיִן כִּנְסָכִים (יוֹמָא ע״א סוֹף עַמּוּד א׳)
as stated: "the table is likened unto an altar" (Berachos 55a), honoring a scholar is like first-fruits (Kesubos 105b), and wine is like libations (Yoma 71a);
וּבִבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה ס״ז:ב׳) עַל פָּסוּק ״כִּי הִקְרָה ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית כ״ז:כ׳): ״אִם לְקָרְבָּנְךָ הִמְצִיא, לְמַאֲכָלְךָ עַל אַחַת כַּמָּה וְכַמָּה״
and in Bereishis Rabbah (67:2) on "Because Hashem sent me good speed": "if He prepared animals for your sacrifice, for your personal food how much more so!".
מְבוֹאָר: דַּאֲכִילַת יִצְחָק אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הָיָה גָּדוֹל מִקָּרְבָּן
It is thus demonstrated that Isaac's holy eating was greater than a sacrifice;
אֲפִילּוּ מִקָּרְבַּן אוֹתוֹ אַיִל שֶׁהָיָה תְּמוּרַת יִצְחָק וְנֶחְשַׁב כַּעֲקֵידַת יִצְחָק, דְּוַדַּאי הָיָה בוֹ קְדוּשָׁה גְּדוֹלָה מִשְּׁאָר קָרְבָּנוֹת
even greater than the ram offered in his stead at the Akeidah which possessed immense holiness;
הָאֲכִילָה עוֹד גְּדוֹלָה יוֹתֵר: כִּי זֶה נִשְׂרַף בָּאֵשׁ, וְזֶה נִכְנַס לְגוּף הַצַּדִּיק שֶׁהוּא ״אֵשׁ אוֹכְלָה״ (דְּבָרִים ד:כד), כִּידוּעַ דְּאֵשׁ — דַּרְגָּא דְּיִצְחָק
the eating being far greater: for the sacrifice is burned on external fire, while the food enters the body of the tzaddik which is a "consuming fire," fire being the attribute of Isaac!
וְאוֹתוֹ נָזִיד לְהַאֲכִיל אֶת יִצְחָק אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הוּא תְּחִלַּת עֲבוֹדַת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
And cooking that pottage to feed Isaac was the inception of Jacob's divine service in this world;
וּלְפִי שֶׁהָעֲבוֹדָה בַּבְּכוֹרוֹת, עַל כֵּן זָכָה אָז בַּבְּכוֹרָה.
and because divine service was performed by the firstborn, he merited then the birthright.
וְהַהַלְעָטָה לְעֵשָׂו מִתַּבְשִׁיל זֶה הַדּוֹמֶה לְקָרְבָּן — הוּא דּוּגְמַת הַשָּׂעִיר לַעֲזָאזֵל
And gulping this sacrificial stew unto Esau was like the scapegoat sent to Azazel;
דְּלוֹקְחִין שְׁנַיִם הַשָּׁוִין בְּמַרְאֶה וְקוֹמָה וְדָמִים, וּמַגְרִילִין עֲלֵיהֶם (יוֹמָא ס״א עַמּוּד ב׳)
where two goats identical in appearance, stature, and value are taken and lots cast over them (Yoma 61b);
כִּי בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה נִרְאִים שְׁנֵיהֶם שָׁוִים, כִּי אֵין שׁוּם הִתְגַּלּוּת וְהֶיכֵּר בְּעָלְמָא דְּשִׁקְרָא בֵּין טוֹב וָרָע לְאָדָם הָרוֹאֶה לַעֵינַיִם
for in this world both appear identical to outward eyes in the realm of falsehood;
רַק ה׳ הָרוֹאֶה לַלֵּבָב: ״בַּחֵיק יוּטַל אֶת הַגּוֹרָל, וּמֵה׳ כָּל מִשְׁפָּטוֹ״ (מִשְׁלֵי ט״ז:ל״ג)
Hashem alone looking into the heart: "The lot is cast into the lap, but the whole disposing thereof is of Hashem" (Mishlei 16:33);
לִהְיוֹת: ״אַתָּה תּוֹמִיךְ גּוֹרָלִי״ (תְּהִלִּים ט״ז:ה׳) עַל חֵלֶק הַטּוֹב, וְגוֹרַל עֵשָׂו עַל חֵלֶק הָרָע.
supporting Jacob's lot upon the good, and Esau's lot upon the evil.
וּמִצַּד עֵירוּב דְּטוֹב וָרָע, הוּכְרַח לְהַפְרִיד מֵאוֹתוֹ תַּבְשִׁיל חֵלֶק הָרָע הַשַּׁיָּיךְ לְעֵשָׂו, שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה נַעֲשָׂה הוּא כּוּלּוֹ רַע כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל
And from the mixture of good and evil, Jacob had to separate the evil portion belonging to Esau, through which Esau became entirely evil;
דֶּרֶךְ ״הַלְעָטָה״, שֶׁהוּא דֶּרֶךְ לִבְהֵמָה, דְּהֵבִיא בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה ס״ג:י״ב) עַל זֶה מַתְנִיתִין דְּ״אֵין מַלְעִיטִין אֶת הַגָּמָל״ (שַׁבָּת קנ״ה עַמּוּד ב׳)
through "gulping" (hal'atah), the feeding mode of beasts, Bereishis Rabbah (63:12) citing the Mishnah: "one may not cram a camel on Shabbat" (Shabbat 155b);
עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּסוֹטָה (ט״ו עַמּוּד ב׳): ״הִיא עָשְׂתָה מַעֲשֵׂה בְּהֵמָה — לְפִיכָךְ קָרְבָּנָהּ מַאֲכַל בְּהֵמָה״, וְכֵן עֵשָׂו בְּאוֹתוֹ יוֹם.
like Sotah (15b): "she committed a bestial act, therefore her offering is animal fodder," and so Esau that day.
וּבְכָל מַאֲכָל יֵשׁ רוּחָנִיּוּת, וְהוּא: ״מוֹצָא פִי ה׳״ (דְּבָרִים ח:ג) שֶׁבּוֹ שֶׁעָלָיו יִחְיֶה הָאָדָם
And within every food resides a spiritual element, the word of Hashem upon which man lives;
וְגַשְׁמִיּוּתוֹ הוּא מַאֲכַל עַם הַדּוֹמֶה לַחֲמוֹר וּבְהֵמָה, שֶׁאֵין חַיּוּתָהּ אֶלָּא מֵהַגַּשְׁמִיּוּת שֶׁבַּמַּאֲכָל
while its physical matter is the food of the beast, sustained solely by physical density;
וְהַבְּהֵמָה אֵין בְּכֹחָהּ לְתַקֵּן מַאֲכָל בְּבִישׁוּל וְכַיּוֹצֵא בוֹ, דְּכָל זֶה תִּיקּוּנִים לְהַפְרִיד הַפְּסֹולֶת שֶׁבּוֹ בַּתּוֹלָדָה וִיצִירָה
an animal being unable to prepare food through cooking, cooking being the human act of separating the dross;
וּבְמִין הָאָדָם יֵשׁ גַּם כֵּן אוֹתָם שֶׁהֵם רַק כְּקוֹף הַמִּדַּמֶּה לְאָדָם
and within humanity there are those who merely mimic man like an ape.
וְכָךְ גַּם בַּתַּבְשִׁיל הַמּוּכָן לְמַאֲכַל אָדָם, יֵשׁ מִמֶּנּוּ הַמּוּכָן לְאוֹתוֹ אָדָם בְּלִיַּיעַל הַשַּׁיָּיךְ לוֹ
And so within food prepared for human consumption, there is that which is destined for the Corrupt Man;
וְזֶהוּ שֶׁהִפְרִיד יַעֲקֹב בְּאוֹתָהּ הַהַלְעָטָה מִנְּזִיד הָעֲדָשִׁים שֶׁהוּא מַאֲכַל אֲבֵלִים
this being what Jacob separated through that feeding of the lentil pottage of mourners;

הַיְינוּ מַאֲכָל שֶׁמִּצַּד קִלְלַת אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן דִּכְתִיב בֵּיהּ: ״בְּעִצָּבוֹן תֹּאכֲלֶנָּה״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית ג:יז), וְ״עִצָּבוֹן״ הוּא אֲבֵילוּת, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה י״א:י׳) עַל פָּסוּק ״וְלֹא יוֹסִף עֶצֶב עִמָּהּ״ (מִשְׁלֵי י:כב)
the food issuing from Adam's primeval curse: "in sorrow shall you eat of it" (Bereishis 3:17), sorrow denoting mourning (Bereishis Rabbah 11:10 on Mishlei 10:22);

וְיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הִתְחִיל לְתַקֵּן בָּזֶה חֵטְא אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן בְּתַאֲוַת אֲכִילָה, וּלְתַקֵּן עַל יְדֵי זֶה קִלְלַת הָאֲכִילָה בְּעִצָּבוֹן, וְזֶה הָיָה פְּעֻלָּתוֹ בְּבִישׁוּל הַמַּאֲכָל שֶׁהוּא תִּיקּוּן הָאֲכִילָה.
and Jacob began to rectify Adam's sin of food-lust and the curse of eating in sorrow, his spiritual labor embodied in cooking the food.
וְלֹא נִזְכַּר בַּכָּתוּב מֵהָאֲכִילָה כְּלוּם, לֹא דְּיַעֲקֹב וְלֹא דְּיִצְחָק, רַק מֵהַבִּישׁוּל שֶׁזֶּהוּ עִיקַּר פְּעֻלַּת וַעֲבוֹדַת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בָּזֶה
And Scripture chronicles nothing of the eating, neither of Jacob nor of Isaac, mentioning solely the cooking, which was Jacob's essential spiritual labor;
וְהָאֲכִילָה דַּאֲבֵילוּת דְּיִצְחָק לֹא שַׁיָּיךְ לְהַזְכִּיר בַּכָּתוּב, כִּי כָּל הָאֲבֵילוּת הוּא רַק לְשָׁעָה כְּמוֹ הַמִּיתָה שֶׁהוּא רַק לְשָׁעָה
and Isaac's meal of mourning is omitted because all mourning is temporary, just as death is temporary;
וַעֲתִידִים לָקוּם וְלִחְיוֹת חַיֵּי עוֹלָם, וּ״בִלַּע הַמָּוֶת [לָנֶצַח, וּמָחָה ה׳ אֱלֹהִים דִּמְעָה מֵעַל כָּל פָּנִים]״ (יְשַׁעְיָה כ״ה:ח׳) וַאֲבֵילוּת:
all being destined to rise and live eternally when Hashem swallows up death forever and wipes away every tear and all mourning (Yeshayah 25:8)!
יִשְׂרָאֵל קְדוֹשִׁים — פֶּרֶק ז׳, סְעִיפִים י״ג–י״ח

אוֹת י״ג — מְנוּחַת יַעֲקֹב וַעֲבוֹדַת הַשַּׁבָּת מוּל פְּרִיקַת עֹל שֶׁל עֵשָׂו וְאַשָּׁהּ שֶׁל גֵּיהִנָּם — Section 13: Jacob's Rest and Sabbath Service vs. Esau's Lawlessness and the Fire of Gehinnom

The theme: Jacob overcoming mortality, Esau seeking effortless consumption to cast off the yoke of Heaven, and the fire of Gehinnom transformed into Tiberias hot springs. Our father Jacob merited even in this world that he did not die (Ta'anit 5b), achieving the complete rectification of Adam's sin on his part. The pottage cooked by Jacob was intended to banish mourning; Scripture records the eating of this stew only regarding Esau, for Jacob separated the sorrowful consumption (achilat itzavon) and relegated it unto Esau and his seed. The wicked eat only after exhausting toil ("if he toils not, he bites not"); here Esau sought to consume that which was already prepared by Jacob to siphon a portion of Jacob's power without effort. Quiet rest is beneficial to the righteous and to the world, but harmful to the wicked (Sanhedrin 71b): the righteous desire rest from financial anxiety in order to immerse in Torah—which was given only to those who ate the Manna—whereas the wicked seek leisure to indulge physical lusts. Esau sought leisure to cast off all restraint, despising the birthright of divine service. True rest for the righteous is relentless spiritual exertion: "they go from strength to strength" (Tehillim 84:8), running to perform a mitzvah even on Shabbat (Berachos 6b), and communal sacrifices overriding Shabbat (Pesachim 66a). Bearing the yoke of Torah removes the yoke of worldly government and secular anxiety (Avos 3:5). In contrast, Esau cast off the yoke of Heaven, eating the "bread of sorrows" (lechem ha-atzavim, Tehillim 127:2). Jacob fed him glowing coals of broom ("for you will heap coals of fire upon his head", Mishlei 25:21–22), transferring all the fire of Gehinnom unto Esau's portion. The unholy dross of fire is the furnace of Gehinnom; but for Israel, its heat bypasses the entrance of Tiberias (Chamei Tveryah), providing hot baths to cleanse the body in honor of Shabbat. "Rakkath is Tiberias" (Megillah 6a): even the empty (reikanin) in Tiberias are full of mitzvos, using the fire of Gehinnom as hot water to luxuriate in honor of the Sabbath!
וְיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם זָכָה לָזֶה גַּם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה: ״דְּלֹא מֵת״, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּתַעֲנִית (דַּף ה׳ עַמּוּד ב׳)
And our father Jacob, peace be upon him, merited this even in this world: "that he did not die," as the Sages stated in Ta'anit (5b);
דְּזֶהוּ שְׁלֵימוּת הַתִּיקּוּן לְחֵטְא אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁזָּכָה לוֹ מִצִּדּוֹ.
for this was the consummate rectification for the sin of Adam HaRishon which Jacob merited on his part.
וְהַהַתְחָלָה בְּנָזִיד זֶה: לְסַלֵּק הָאֲבֵילוּת, וְעַל כֵּן נִזְכַּר אֲכִילַת נָזִיד זֶה רַק לְעֵשָׂו
And the beginning occurred in this stew: to remove mourning, wherefore the consumption of this pottage is recorded strictly regarding Esau;
שֶׁהִפְרִיד אֲכִילַת הָעִצָּבוֹן וְהָאֲבֵילוּת לַמָּקוֹם שֶׁהוּא שַׁיָּיךְ, שֶׁאֵינוֹ אֶלָּא לְעֵשָׂו וְזַרְעוֹ
Jacob having separated the sorrowful eating of mourning unto the place where it belongs, which is exclusively unto Esau and his seed;
דְּ״אִי לָא לָעֵי — לָא נָגֵיס״, וְכָל עֲמָלוֹ לְמַאֲכַל פִּיהוּ בִּיגִיעָה בְּצֵידָה וְאַחַר יֹאכַל.
for "if he toils not, he bites not," all his labor being for the food of his mouth through exhausting hunting before he can eat.
וְכָאן רָצָה לֶאֱכוֹל מִן הַמּוּכָן כְּבָר עַל יְדֵי יַעֲקֹב, כִּי הוּא יָדַע שֶׁבָּזֶה יִקְלוֹט דָּבָר מַה מִכֹּחַ יַעֲקֹב
And here Esau desired to eat from that which was already prepared by Jacob, knowing that through this he would siphon something of Jacob's power;
וַאֲכִילָה בְּלֹא יְגִיעָה אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא חֶלְקוֹ שֶׁל יַעֲקֹב ״יֹשֵׁב אֹהָלִים״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית כ״ה:כ״ז)
eating without physical toil being the rightful portion of Jacob, who dwells in the tents of Torah;
כִּי: ״מְנוּחָה וָשֶׁקֶט לַצַּדִּיקִים — הֲנָאָה לָהֶם וַהֲנָאָה לָעוֹלָם; וְלָרְשָׁעִים — בְּהֵיפוּךְ״, כִּדִתְנַן בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (ע״א סוֹף עַמּוּד ב׳).
for: "rest and tranquility for the righteous is beneficial for them and beneficial for the world; but for the wicked it is the reverse," as taught in the Mishnah in Sanhedrin (71b).
כִּי הַצַּדִּיקִים מְבַקְשִׁים מְנוּחָה כְּדֵי לַעֲסוֹק בַּתּוֹרָה, שֶׁלֹּא נִתְּנָה אֶלָּא לְאוֹכְלֵי הַמָּן שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה לָהֶם טִרְדַּת פַּרְנָסָה (מְכִילְתָּא בְּשַׁלַּח פָּרָשָׁה ב׳)
For the righteous seek rest in order to toil in Torah, which was given only to those who ate the Manna, who were free from financial worry (Mechilta, Beshalach §2);
וְהָרְשָׁעִים יְבַקְשׁוּ זֶה כְּדֵי שֶׁיּוּכְלוּ לְמַלֹּאות כָּל תַּאֲוַת יִצְרָם.
whereas the wicked seek leisure so that they can sate all the lusts of their inclination.
וְכָךְ עֵשָׂו חָשַׁב לִקְלוֹט בָּזֶה כֹּחַ הַמְּנוּחָה שֶׁלֹּא יִצְטָרֵךְ לִיגִיעָה כָּל כָּךְ
And so Esau schemed to absorb through this the power of rest so that he would not need such physical labor;
אֲבָל לִהְיוֹת זֶה ״לְרַע לוֹ וְרַע לָעוֹלָם״, כִּי יַעֲשֶׂה כָּל מַה שֶּׁלִּבּוֹ חָפֵץ, וְזֶהוּ בִּזּוּי הַבְּכוֹרָה שֶׁהוּא הָעֲבוֹדָה לַה׳.
but this was to his own ruin and the ruin of the world, for he intended to perform all that his heart desired, which was the despising of the birthright of divine service.
כִּי מְנוּחַת יַעֲקֹב הוּא: ״מְנוּחָה שְׁלֵימָה שֶׁאַתָּה רוֹצֶה בָּהּ״
For Jacob's rest is "the consummate rest that You desire";
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ: ״צַדִּיקִים אֵין לָהֶם מְנוּחָה, לֹא בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה וְלֹא בָּעוֹלָם הַבָּא, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ׳יֵלְכוּ מֵחַיִל אֶל חָיִל׳ (תְּהִלִּים פ״ד:ח׳)״ (בְּרָכוֹת ס״ד עַמּוּד א׳)
as stated: "the righteous have no rest, neither in this world nor in the World to Come: 'they go from strength to strength' (Tehillim 84:8)" (Berachos 64a);
כִּי זֶה כָּל מְנוּחָתָם: כְּשֶׁיּוּכְלוּ לִרְדּוֹף אַחֲרֵי ה׳
for this is their entire rest: when they are empowered to run after Hashem;
דְּעַל כֵּן מִצְוָה לָרוּץ לִדְבַר מִצְוָה וּדְבֵרֵי תוֹרָה אֲפִילּוּ בְּשַׁבָּת, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרָכוֹת (ו׳ עַמּוּד ב׳)
wherefore it is a mitzvah to run to a commandment or to words of Torah even on Shabbat (Berachos 6b);
וְכֵן קָרְבְּנוֹת צִבּוּר דּוֹחִין שַׁבָּת (פְּסָחִים ס״ו עַמּוּד א׳), שֶׁזֶּהוּ מְנוּחָתָן שֶׁזּוֹכִין לַעֲבוֹד אֶת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בֶּאֱמֶת
and communal sacrifices override Shabbat (Pesachim 66a), their true rest being to serve the Blessed Name in truth.
וְ״כָל הַמְקַבֵּל עָלָיו עוֹל תּוֹרָה — מַעֲבִירִין מִמֶּנּוּ עוֹל מַלְכוּת וְעוֹל דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ״ (אָבוֹת פֶּרֶק ג׳ מִשְׁנָה ה׳)
And "whoever receives upon himself the yoke of Torah, they remove from him the yoke of government and the yoke of worldly labor" (Avos 3:5);
וְיֵשׁ לוֹ מְנוּחָה מִטִּרְדַּת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה עַל יְדֵי זֶה שֶׁמְּקַבֵּל עָלָיו עוֹל תּוֹרָה וְעוֹל מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם בֶּאֱמֶת.
gaining rest from worldly anxieties through accepting the yoke of Torah and the yoke of the Kingdom of Heaven in truth.
וְעֵשָׂו בָּחַר בִּפְרִיקַת עֹל לְגַמְרֵי
But Esau chose the complete casting off of the yoke;
וּכְשֶׁאָכַל וְשָׁתָה בִּמְנוּחָה פָּרַק עוֹל מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם לְגַמְרֵי, וּבִזָּה הַבְּכוֹרָה וְהָעֲבוֹדָה
and eating and drinking in indolent leisure, he threw off the yoke of Heaven entirely, despising the birthright and the holy service;
אֲבָל לֹא יָדַע כִּי בְּנַפְשׁוֹ הוּא
yet he did not realize that this was at the cost of his very life;
דְּאַדְּרַבָּא בָּזֶה אָכַל ״לֶחֶם הָעֲצָבִים״ (תְּהִלִּים קכ״ז:ב׳), וְנִשְׁרַשׁ בּוֹ שׁוֹרֶשׁ הָאֲכִילָה דְּעִצָּבוֹן שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁמִּסִּטְרָא דְּרָע
for on the contrary, he ate the "bread of sorrows" (Tehillim 127:2), rooting within himself the sorrowful eating of this world that issues from evil;
דְּעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: ״אִם רָעֵב שֹׂנַאֲךָ — הַאֲכִלֵהוּ [לָחֶם]... כִּי גֶחָלִים אַתָּה חֹתֶה [עַל רֹאשׁוֹ]״ (מִשְׁלֵי כ״ה:כ״א–כ״ב)
concerning which it is said: "If your enemy be hungry, give him bread to eat... for you will heap coals of fire upon his head" (Mishlei 25:21–22);
וְהֶאֱכִילָהוּ בָּזֶה ״גַּחֲלֵי רְתָמִים״ (תְּהִלִּים ק״כ:ד׳) לִהְיוֹת ״אִשּׁוֹ לֹא תִכְבֶּה״ (יְשַׁעְיָה ס״ו:כ״ד)
Jacob feeding him the fiery coals of broom, that his unholy flame never be quenched (Yeshayah 66:24);
כִּי נָטַל כָּל אִשּׁוֹ שֶׁל גֵּיהִנָּם גַּם דְּיַעֲקֹב לְחֶלְקוֹ.
Esau taking all the fire of Gehinnom, including Jacob's potential portion, into his own lot.
כִּי הַפְּסֹולֶת מִסִּטְרָא דְּאֵשׁ הוּא אֵשׁ שֶׁל גֵּיהִנָּם, וּרְשָׁעִים נִידּוֹנִין בּוֹ
For the dross of fire is the fire of Gehinnom wherein the wicked are judged;
וְחַמֵּי טְבֶרְיָה חָלְפֵי אַפִּתְחֵיהּ לְיִשְׂרָאֵל לְהִתְעַנֵּג בָּהֶם (עֵירוּבִין י״ט עַמּוּד א׳)
while the hot springs of Tiberias pass over the entrance of Gehinnom for Israel to luxuriate in them (Eruvin 19a);
וְעַל כֵּן ״רַקַּת — זוֹ טְבֶרְיָה״, ״שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ רֵיקָנִין שֶׁבָּהּ מְלֵאִים מִצְוֹת [כְּרִמּוֹן]״, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּמְגִלָּה (ו׳ עַמּוּד א׳)
wherefore "Rakkath is Tiberias—for even the empty (reikanin) within it are full of mitzvos like a pomegranate" (Megillah 6a);
דְּעַל כֵּן הָאוּר שֶׁל גֵּיהִנָּם הָרְאוּיָה לְרֵיקָנִין הוּא לָהֶם מַיִם חַמִּין לִרְחוֹץ הַגּוּף מִצּוֹאָתוֹ
wherefore the subterranean fire of Gehinnom destined for the empty is transformed for them into soothing hot water to cleanse the body;
וּלְהִתְעַנֵּג לִכְבוֹד שַׁבָּת שֶׁרוֹחֲצִין בְּחַמִּין, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּפֶרֶק בַּמֶּה מַדְלִיקִין (שַׁבָּת כ״ה עַמּוּד ב׳)
and to luxuriate in honor of Shabbat by washing in hot water (Shabbat 25b);
דְּהוּא הָאוֹת בֵּינוֹ וּבֵין בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל (שְׁמוֹת ל״א:י״ז), וְלֹא עָשָׂה כֵן לְכָל גּוֹי
Shabbat being the eternal sign between Hashem and the Children of Israel (Shemos 31:17), which He gave not to the nations;
שֶׁהֵם: ״יוֹמָם וָלַיְלָה לֹא יִשְׁבֹּתוּ״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית ח:כב; סַנְהֶדְרִין נ״ח עַמּוּד ב׳) בִּיגִיעַת בָּשָׂר, בְּעוֹל מַלְכוּת וְעוֹל דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ, מֵאַחַר שֶׁאֵין עֲלֵיהֶם עוֹל תּוֹרָה.
the nations toiling day and night without rest (Bereishis 8:22; Sanhedrin 58b) under the yoke of tyrants and secular labor, having cast off the yoke of Torah.
דְּ״אַל תִּתֵּן ה׳ מַאֲוַיֵּי רָשָׁע, זְמָמוֹ אַל תָּפֵק״ (תְּהִלִּים ק״מ:ט׳)
For "Grant not, Hashem, the desires of the wicked; further not his evil device" (Tehillim 140:9);
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר רָבָא לְבַר שִׁישַׁךְ בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה (ס״ה עַמּוּד א׳): ״אַתּוּן אִיכָּא עֲלַיְיכוּ אֵימְתָא דְּמַלְכוּתָא״
as Rava told the Persian magnate Bar Sheishach in Avodah Zarah (65a): "you are subjugated beneath the dread of the imperial monarchy";
וְעוֹל מַלְכוּת לְמִי שֶׁאֵין לוֹ עוֹל דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ, מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן זֶרַע יִשְׂרָאֵל הַנִּכְנָסִין תַּחַת עוֹל תּוֹרָה וּמִצְוֹת:
the yoke of kings crushing one who lacks the yoke of Torah, unlike Israel who enter beneath the sweet yoke of Torah and mitzvos!
אוֹת י״ד — צְחוֹק שֶׁל עֵשָׂו וּשְׂחוֹק שֶׁל מַעְלָה, עֲדָשִׁים שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהֶם אֵבֶל וְשִׂמְחָה, וּ״בְנִי אַתָּה אֲנִי הַיּוֹם יְלִדְתִּיךָ״
Section 14: Esau's Mockery and Heavenly Laughter, Lentils of Mourning and Joy, and "You Are My Son, Today I Have Begotten You"

7.h: The theme: Esau's cynical scoffing, divine mockery of the scoffers, and the lentils containing mourning and joy. In Bereishis Rabbah (63:14), Esau said: "Let us eat of his stew and laugh at him; and since they were jesting, the Holy One agreed and laughed with them". Esau sought to mock Jacob, consuming his food to siphon his power while ridiculing his asceticism. But "He that sits in heaven laughs, Hashem has them in derision" (Tehillim 2:4) on "Let us break their bands asunder, and cast away their cords from us" (ibid. 2:3). The wicked seek mockery (leitzanut), but Hashem scoffs at the scoffers ("Surely He scoffs at the scoffers", Mishlei 3:34): their mockery tightens their bonds ("Now therefore be not scoffers, lest your bands be made strong", Yeshayah 28:22). Esau despised the birthright to throw off the yoke of divine service, viewing the cords of mitzvos—the thread of Tzitzit and the straps of Tefillin—as heavy chains. For Israel, these cords are the bands of love (avotot ahavah). Esau laughed that Jacob took on this yoke; but through this very transaction Hashem proclaimed: "Israel is My son, My firstborn" (Shemos 4:22). Service of a son to a father is performed with love and joy, not slavish drudgery. Bereishis Rabbah (63:14) notes that lentils contain both mourning and joy (avel v'simchah): the mourning over Abraham's passing—wherein Jacob absorbed Abraham's holiness—generated the joy of acquiring the birthright. On that day Jacob was crowned a son unto Hashem: "You are My son, this day have I begotten you" (Tehillim 2:7), causing supreme joy in the celestial worlds ("A man child is born unto you; making him very glad", Yirmiyah 20:15)!

p: וּבִבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (סוֹף פָּרָשָׁה ס״ג:י״ד): ״דְּעֵשָׂו אָמַר: נֵיכוֹל דִּידֵיהּ וְנֵיחוּךְ עֲלֵיהּ וְכוּלֵיהּ; וּלְפִי שֶׁהָיוּ כִּמְשַׂחֲקִים, אַף הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא הִסְכִּים וְשָׂחַק עִמָּהֶם וְכוּלֵיהּ״
And in Bereishis Rabbah (63:14): "Esau said: Let us eat of his stew and mock him; and because they acted as jesters, the Holy One likewise agreed and laughed with them";
כִּי הוּא חָשַׁב לִשְׂחוֹק עָלָיו בַּאֲכִילָה זוֹ מִשֶּׁלּוֹ שֶׁיִּקְלוֹט מַה שֶּׁטּוֹב לוֹ
for Esau schemed to deride Jacob through this meal, imagining he would absorb the good while scorning the toil;
וְלֹא יָדַע: דְּ״יוֹשֵׁב בַּשָּׁמַיִם יִשְׂחָק, ה׳ יִלְעַג לָמוֹ״ (תְּהִלִּים ב:ד)
yet he knew not that "He that sits in heaven laughs, Hashem has them in derision" (Tehillim 2:4);
עַל מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״נְנַתְּקָה [אֶת מוֹסְרוֹתֵימוֹ,] וְנַשְׁלִיכָה [מִמֶּנּוּ] עֲבֹתֵימוֹ״ (שָׁם:ג׳) לִפְרוֹק עוֹל
regarding their scheme: "Let us break their bands asunder, and cast away their cords from us" (ibid. 2:3) to throw off the yoke;
וְזֶהוּ חֶפְצָם בִּשְׂחוֹק וְלֵיצָנוּת, וְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מִתְלוֹצֵץ מֵהֶם
this being their desire in mockery and scoffing, while the Holy One derides them;
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ: ״אִם לַלֵּצִים — הוּא יָלִיץ״ (מִשְׁלֵי ג:לד; עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה י״ח עַמּוּד ב׳)
as stated: "Surely He scoffs at the scoffers" (Mishlei 3:34; Avodah Zarah 18b);
דְּאַדְּרַבָּא עַל יְדֵי זֶה נִכְנָסִים לְעוֹל יוֹתֵר, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ: ״אַל תִּתְלוֹצָצוּ — פֶּן יֶחְזְקוּ מוֹסְרֵיכֶם״ (יְשַׁעְיָה כ״ח:כ״ב; עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה שָׁם).
for on the contrary, through scoffing their chains are tightened: "Now therefore be not scoffers, lest your bands be made strong" (Yeshayah 28:22; Avodah Zarah 18b).
וּבִזּוּי הַבְּכוֹרָה הָיָה בִּשְׁבִיל חֶפְצוֹ בִּפְרִיקַת עוֹל
And the despising of the birthright was motivated by Esau's desire to cast off the yoke;
דְּהָעֲבוֹדָה אֶצְלוֹ עוֹל כָּבֵד, לִהְיוֹת אָסוּר בְּמוֹסְרוֹת וַעֲבוֹתוֹת הָעֲבוֹדָה
the holy service being viewed by him as an onerous burden, binding man in cords and ropes;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה עַל פָּסוּק ״מוֹסְרוֹתֵימוֹ וַעֲבֹתֵימוֹ״: עַל חוּט שֶׁל צִיצִית וּרְצוּעָה דִּתְפִלִּין (מִדְרַשׁ תְּהִלִּים ב:ג)
as the Sages expounded on "their bands and their cords": referring to the thread of Tzitzit and the straps of Tefillin (Midrash Tehillim 2:3);
וְאֵצֶל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הֵם ״עֲבוֹתוֹת אַהֲבָה״ (הוֹשֵׁעַ י״א:ד׳).
whereas for the Children of Israel these are cords of love (Hoshea 11:4).
וְזֶהוּ ״גִּיחוּךְ עָלֶיהָ״ — שֶׁהוּא [יַעֲקֹב] יִכָּנֵס לְעוֹל זֶה
And this was Esau's derision: laughing that Jacob should enter beneath this yoke;
אֲבָל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא קְרָאוֹ עַל יְדֵי זֶה: ״בְּנִי בְכֹרִי יִשְׂרָאֵל״ (שְׁמוֹת ד:כב)
but the Holy One crowned Jacob through this: "Israel is My son, My firstborn" (Shemos 4:22);
וַעֲבוֹדַת בֵּן לָאָב אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא מֵאַהֲבָה וְשִׂמְחָה וְלֹא כַּעֲבוֹדַת עֶבֶד.
the service of a son unto a father being rendered out of love and joy, and not like the servitude of a slave.
וְזֶה שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה שָׁם (ס״ג:י״ד): ״דַּעֲדָשִׁים יֵשׁ בָּהֶם אֵבֶל וְשִׂמְחָה וְכוּלֵיהּ״
And this is what is stated in Bereishis Rabbah (63:14): "lentils contain both mourning and joy, etc.";
וְהָאֵבֶל דְּמִיתַת אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, וְקָלַט יַעֲקֹב אוֹתָהּ קְדוּשָׁה, הוּא גָּרְמָה הַשִּׂמְחָה דִּקְנִיַּית הַבְּכוֹרָה
and the mourning over Abraham's death, wherein Jacob absorbed his holiness, generated the joy of acquiring the birthright;
דְּעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִקְרָא ״בְּנִי בְכוֹרִי״, וְזָכָה לִיקָּרֵא ״בֵּן״ לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
through which Jacob was designated "My firstborn son," meriting to be titled a son unto the Blessed Name;
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: ״בְּנִי אַתָּה, אֲנִי הַיּוֹם יְלִדְתִּיךָ״ (תְּהִלִּים ב:ז)
concerning which it is said: "You are My son, this day have I begotten you" (Tehillim 2:7);
שֶׁבְּאוֹתוֹ יוֹם שֶׁזּוֹכֶה לִיקָּרֵא בֵּן לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, הוּא כְּאִילּוּ בְּאוֹתוֹ יוֹם נוֹלַד לוֹ לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
for on the day one merits to be titled a son unto Hashem, it is as though on that day he was born unto Him;
וְגוֹרֵם שִׂמְחָה בָּעוֹלָמוֹת עֶלְיוֹנִים, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּיִרְמְיָה (כ:טו): ״[אָרוּר] הָאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר בִּשַּׂר אֶת אָבִי לֵאמֹר: יֻלַּד לְךָ בֵּן זָכָר, שַׂמֵּחַ שִׂמְּחָהוּ״:
generating joy in the celestial worlds: "the man who brought tidings to my father, saying: A man child is born unto you; making him very glad" (Yirmiyah 20:15)!

7.h: אוֹת ט״ו — אַבְרָהָם כְּ״אַב הָעוֹלָם״, נֶצַח יִשְׂרָאֵל, שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַגֵּרִים, וְ״בְּהִבָּרְאָם — בְּאַבְרָהָם״ — Section 15: Abraham as Father of the World, Eternity of Israel, Root of Converts, and "BeHibaram / B'Avraham"

The theme: Abraham as the cosmic father of all enduring reality, converts rooted in "the souls gotten in Haran", and truth veiled in the world of falsehood. Abraham is the "father of the world" (Av HaOlam), corresponding to the first blessing of the Amidah (Avot), the head of the Patriarchs who is "the father of a multitude of nations" (Bereishis 17:5). That which is fleeting is falsehood (kezav); the essential cosmos is that which endures forever: "the earth abides forever" (Koheles 1:4)—referring to Israel ("you shall be a delightsome land", Malachi 3:12). Israel was exiled among the nations to gather converts (Pesachim 87b) who are titled with the name of Israel (Yeshayah 44:5). Converts possess an eternal hold in holiness through Abraham, the father of converts, wherefore they recite "which Hashem swore unto our fathers" (Yerushalmi Bikkurim 1:4). Their souls derive from "the souls that they had gotten in Haran" (Bereishis 12:5), Abraham having spiritually begotten them. On "in the day that Hashem God made the earth and the heavens" (Bereishis 2:4), the Sages expound: be-hibar'am ("when they were created") is an anagram for b'Avraham ("through Abraham", Bereishis Rabbah 12:9)—the entire cosmos being created for this soul. Yet in this world of falsehood, Abraham appeared childless, and Lot viewed him as a sterile mule whose estate he would inherit. Just as Moshe, the humblest of men, was accused of seeking royal dominion (Bamidbar 16:13), so Abraham, destined to be the father of the world, appeared initially without offspring!

p: וְאַבְרָהָם נִקְרָא ״אַב הָעוֹלָם״, כִּידוּעַ דְּג׳ בְּרָכוֹת רִאשׁוֹנוֹת: אָבוֹת, גְּבוּרוֹת, וּקְדוּשׁוֹת — נֶגֶד ג׳ אֲבָהָן
And Abraham is designated "father of the world," as known that the first three blessings of the Amidah—Avot, Gevurot, and Kedushot—correspond unto the three Patriarchs;
וְ״אָבוֹת״ הוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם רֹאשׁ לַג׳ אָבוֹת, שֶׁהוּא ״אַב הֲמוֹן גּוֹיִם״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית י״ז:ה׳)
and Avot is the root of Abraham our father, head of the Patriarchs, who is "the father of a multitude of nations" (Bereishis 17:5);
וּבַתְּחִלָּה ״אַב לַאֲרָם״ [אַבְרָם] וְאַחַר כָּךְ לְכָל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ [אַבְרָהָם] (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה מ״ו:ח׳)
initially "father of Aram" [Abram] and subsequently father of the whole world [Abraham] (Bereishis Rabbah 46:8).
כִּי אֵין נִקְרָא ״עוֹלָם״ מַה שֶּׁהוּא בַּדִּמְיוֹן וּלְשָׁעָה לְבַד: הַיּוֹם כָּאן וּמָחָר אֵינֶנּוּ
For that which exists in illusion and for a fleeting moment is not termed "world": here today and gone tomorrow;
שֶׁזֶּה נִקְרָא ״כָּזָב״ וְדָבָר הַפּוֹסֵק, שֶׁגַּם עַתָּה כְּמוֹ שֶׁאֵינוֹ וְאֵין לוֹ תְּפִיסָה אֶלָּא מִצַּד הַכְּזָב הַשּׁוֹטֵט בְּעָלְמָא דְּשִׁקְרָא.
which is called falsehood and a transient thing, possessing no substance save within this realm of lies.
אֲבָל עִיקַּר הָעוֹלָם הוּא מַה שֶּׁנִּשְׁאַר מִמֶּנּוּ קַיָּים לְעוֹלְמֵי עַד
But the authentic essence of the world is that which endures from it forever;
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ: ״וְהָאָרֶץ — לְעוֹלָם עֹמֶדֶת״ (קֹהֶלֶת א:ד), וְהֵם יִשְׂרָאֵל, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ: ״[וְאִשְּׁרוּ אֶתְכֶם כָּל הַגּוֹיִם] כִּי תִהְיוּ אַתֶּם לִי אֶרֶץ חֵפֶץ״ (מַלְאָכִי ג:יב)
as it is written: "and the earth abides forever" (Koheles 1:4), which is Israel: "for you shall be a delightsome land unto Me" (Malachi 3:12).
וְגָלוּ לְבֵין הָאוּמּוֹת כְּדֵי לִקְלוֹט גֵּרִים מֵהֶם (פְּסָחִים פ״ז עַמּוּד ב׳)
And Israel was exiled among the nations in order to absorb converts from them (Pesachim 87b);
וְהֵם אֲשֶׁר: ״[וּבְשֵׁם יַעֲקֹב יִקְרָא,] וּבְשֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל יְכַנֶּה״ (יְשַׁעְיָה מ״ד:ה׳), וְאֵין לָהֶם שַׁיָּיכוּת לְעֶצֶם יִשְׂרָאֵל וְזֶרַע יַעֲקֹב רַק עַל דֶּרֶךְ הַכִּינּוּי
they being those who "surname themselves by the name of Israel" (Yeshayah 44:5), having connection to the essence of Jacob's seed strictly by surname;
אֲבָל שַׁיָּיכוּת שֶׁלָּהֶם לִקְדוּשָׁה שֶׁיִּשָּׁאֵר גַּם מֵהֶם אֵיזֶה מִכָּל אוּמָּה לְעוֹלְמֵי עַד, הוּא מִצַּד אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, דְּהוּא ״אַב לַגֵּרִים״
but their connection to holiness, that an enduring remnant remain from every nation forever, is through Abraham who is the father of converts;
דְּעַל כֵּן יְכוֹלִים לוֹמַר: ״[הָאֲדָמָה] אֲשֶׁר נָתַן לַאֲבֹתֵינוּ״, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּיְרוּשַׁלְמִי דְּבִכּוּרִים (פֶּרֶק א׳ הֲלָכָה ד׳)
wherefore they may recite: "the land which Hashem swore unto our fathers," as stated in Yerushalmi Bikkurim (1:4);
כִּי הֵם כּוּלָּם שָׁרְשָׁם מֵ״אֶת הַנֶּפֶשׁ אֲשֶׁר עָשׂוּ בְחָרָן״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית י״ב:ה׳), דִּכְאִילּוּ יְלָדָם.
for they are all rooted in "the souls that they had gotten in Haran" (Bereishis 12:5), Abraham having spiritually begotten them.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה י״ב:ט׳) עַל פָּסוּק: ״בְּהִבָּרְאָם״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית ב:ד) — ״בְּאַבְרָהָם״
And this is what the Sages expounded in Bereishis Rabbah (12:9) on "when they were created" (be-hibar'am): read it b'Avraham ("through Abraham");
שֶׁהוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַמְכֻוָּון שֶׁל כָּל בְּרִיאַת עוֹלָם: לִהְיוֹת נוֹצָר נֶפֶשׁ זֶה בָּעוֹלָם שֶׁמִּמֶּנּוּ הִשְׁתַּלְשְׁלוּת כָּל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ.
he being the primary purpose of the creation of the world, that this soul be formed whence the cosmos unfolds.
וּמִצַּד הַחֲשׁוֹכָא דִּבְרֵישָׁא הַמַּעֲלִים אוֹר הָאֱמֶת בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, חָשַׁב עַצְמוֹ: ״[וְאָנֹכִי] הוֹלֵךְ עֲרִירִי״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית ט״ו:ב׳)
Yet through the initial darkness that veils the light of truth in this world, Abraham thought of himself: "and I go childless" (Bereishis 15:2);
וְכֵן לוֹט הֶחֱשִׁיבוֹ לִפְרֵדָה עֲקָרָה שֶׁהוּא יִירָשֶׁנּוּ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה מ״א:ח׳)
and so Lot regarded him as a sterile mule whose estate he would inherit (Bereishis Rabbah 41:8);
כִּי כָּל הָעוֹלָם מִדַּת עָלְמָא דְּשִׁקְרָא, לִהְיוֹת הַנִּרְאָה בוֹ לָאָדָם הָרוֹאֶה לַעֵינַיִם מַמָּשׁ הֵיפֶךְ הָאֱמֶת
for this world operates in falsehood, that which appears to outward eyes being the exact opposite of truth;

וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ עַל מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁהָיָה עָנָו מִכָּל הָאָדָם: ״כִּי תִשְׂתָּרֵר עָלֵינוּ גַּם הִשְׂתָּרֵר״ (בַּמִּדְבָּר ט״ז:י״ג), לְחָשְׁדוֹ מְבַקֵּשׁ הִשְׂתָּרְרוּת וְגַאֲוָה
just as Moshe, the humblest of men, was accused: "that you make yourself altogether a prince over us?" (Bamidbar 16:13), suspecting him of arrogance;
וְעַל כֵּן אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁהָיָה מוּכָן לִהְיוֹת אַב הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ, הָיָה נִדְמֶה תְּחִלָּה מַמָּשׁ לְהֵיפֶךְ: שֶׁאֵין לוֹ שׁוּם תּוֹלָדָה:
wherefore Abraham our father, destined to be the father of the whole world, appeared initially the exact reverse: lacking any child!

7.h: אוֹת ט״ז — גְּבוּרַת יִצְחָק מוּל גְּבוּרַת עוֹג, מִיתַת צַדִּיקִים כִּשְׁנָה, וּבִרְכַּת מְחַיֵּה הַמֵּתִים — Section 16: Isaac's Spiritual Might vs. Og's Material Giantism, Sleep of the Patriarchs, and the Blessing of Resurrection

The theme: Isaac as the root of cosmic Gevurah, Og seeking to crush him with his finger, and true might demonstrated through the Resurrection. Isaac was the root of Gevurah in the world. Bereishis Rabbah (53:10) states that a baby’s cradle was rocked for the first time in Abraham's home; Og the giant mocked the newborn Isaac, boasting: "With my finger I could crush him!" Isaac was born in extreme frailty, born to aged parents in the natural decay of their reproductive powers. Yet Isaac was the root of all cosmic might, and Og the giant eventually fell into the hands of Isaac's descendants (Bamidbar 21:35). Illusory physical strength weakens with age and vanishes in death; Isaac's might resides in Torah: "as elder scholars age, their wisdom deepens" (Kinnim 3:6). When mortal strength ceases in death, the spiritual might of Torah intensifies to enter the Heavenly Academy ("when you lie down in the grave, it shall watch over you", Mishlei 6:22), and from it descends the dew of resurrection (tal techiyah). Death for the righteous is merely sleep: "when he slept" (kad damach), the Patriarchs being called the "sleepers of Hebron" (yeshenei Chevron). Hashem reveals their reward prior to death, and they fall asleep in peace; "the abundance of the rich will not suffer him to sleep" (Koheles 5:11)—meaning they are escorted to academies of Torah on High (Vayikra Rabbah 28:1). Therefore the blessing of Gevurah in the Amidah is established upon the Resurrection of the Dead (mechayei ha-metim), true might having no cessation or humiliation (shefilut). Physical death is called shefilut (Tanchuma, Vayechi §3); the poor and blind are called dead because they endure extreme humiliation. Resurrection clarifies that death was "very good" (Bereishis Rabbah 9:5)—an awakening into renewed strength—whereas Esau’s physical might ends in absolute ruin!

p: וְכָךְ יִצְחָק שֶׁהוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַגְּבוּרָה שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם
And so Isaac, who is the root of Gevurah in the world;
אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה נ״ג:י׳): ״דְּלֹא נִדְנְדָה עֲרִיסָה תְּחִלָּה אֶלָּא בְּבֵיתוֹ שֶׁל אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ״
the Sages stated in Bereishis Rabbah (53:10): "a cradle was never rocked first save in the house of Abraham our father";
וְעוֹג אָמַר עָלָיו: ״שֶׁבְּאֶצְבָּעוֹ מְעָכְנוֹ״ (שָׁם), כִּי נוֹלַד בְּתַכְלִית הַחֻלְשָׁה שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה עַדַיִין יֶלֶד כָּמוֹהוּ בָּעוֹלָם
and Og declared concerning him: "with my finger I could crush him," for he was born in extreme frailty;
וְכָךְ הָיָה רָאוּי כְּפִי טֶבַע הָעוֹלָם, כְּפִי מַה שֶּׁנּוֹלַד לְעֵת זִקְנוּת אַבְרָהָם וְשָׂרָה וּתְשׁוּת כֹּחוֹת הַהוֹלָדָה בָּהֶם.
as was natural according to the laws of nature, born in the old age of Abraham and Sarah when reproductive vigor had waned.
וּבֶאֱמֶת הוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ כָּל כֹּחַ הַגְּבוּרָה שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם, וְסוֹף עוֹג הַגִּבּוֹר מִכָּל הָאָדָם נָפַל בְּיַד זַרְעוֹ
Yet in truth Isaac was the root of all might in the universe, and ultimately Og, the mightiest of men, fell into the hand of his descendants (Bamidbar 21:35);
כִּי הַגְּבוּרָה דְּדִמְיוֹן שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה סוֹפָהּ כְּשֵׁילָה, וְכָל זְמַן שֶׁיַּזְקִין יֶחְלַשׁ כֹּחוֹ עַד שֶׁיֹּאבַד לְגַמְרֵי
for illusory physical strength in this world ends in failure, waning with age until it perishes completely.

וּגְבוּרַת יִצְחָק אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הוּא בְּהֵיפוּךְ, דִּגְבוּרָתוֹ הוּא בַּתּוֹרָה: ״וְזִקְנֵי תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים, כָּל זְמַן שֶׁמַּזְקִינִין — דַּעְתָּן מִתְיַשֶּׁבֶת עֲלֵיהֶן״ (קִנִּים פֶּרֶק ג׳ מִשְׁנָה ו׳)
But the might of Isaac our father is the exact reverse, his strength being in the Torah: "as elder scholars age, their mind becomes settled upon them" (Kinnim 3:6);
וּבַמִּיתָה שֶׁנִּפְסְקָה גְּבוּרַת בָּשָׂר וָדָם לְגַמְרֵי, גְּבוּרַת הַתּוֹרָה מִתְגַּבֶּרֶת יוֹתֵר לִיכָּנֵס לִישִׁיבָה שֶׁל מַעְלָה
and in death, when mortal strength ceases entirely, the might of Torah intensifies to enter the Heavenly Academy;
וְגַם: ״בְּשָׁכְבְּךָ — תִּשְׁמֹר עָלֶיךָ״ (מִשְׁלֵי ו:כב), בַּקֶּבֶר; וּמִמֶּנָּה הַטַּל שֶׁל תְּחִיָּה לָקוּם בִּתְחִיַּיִת הַמֵּתִים
"when you lie down in the grave, it shall watch over you" (Mishlei 6:22), and from it descends the dew of resurrection;
שֶׁאָז יִתְגַּלֶּה שֶׁהַמִּיתָה הָיָה רַק כְּמוֹ שֵׁינָה, וְכִלְשׁוֹן רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּמִיתַת הַצַּדִּיקִים: ״כַּד דְּמַךְ וְכוּלֵיהּ״ — לְשׁוֹן שֵׁינָה
revealing then that death was merely like sleep, as the Sages term the passing of tzaddikim: "when he slept (kad damach)";
וְכֵן נִקְרְאוּ הָאָבוֹת: ״יְשֵׁנֵי חֶבְרוֹן״ (סוֹטָה י״ג עַמּוּד א׳)
and so the Patriarchs are called "the sleepers of Hebron" (Sotah 13a);
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה: דְּהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מַרְאֶה לַצַּדִּיקִים שְׂכָרָן קוֹדֶם מוֹתָן וִישֵׁינִים לָהֶם
the Holy One showing the righteous their reward before death, whereupon they sleep in peace;
וְ״הַשָּׂבָע לֶעָשִׁיר — אֵינֶנּוּ מַנִּיחַ לוֹ לִישׁוֹן״ (קֹהֶלֶת ה:יא), שֶׁמּוֹלִיכִין אוֹתוֹ לִישִׁיבוֹת שֶׁל תּוֹרָה (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה כ״ח:א׳).
and "the abundance of the rich will not suffer him to sleep" (Koheles 5:11), escorting him unto academies of Torah on High (Vayikra Rabbah 28:1).
וְעַל כֵּן יוֹם [צ״ל הוּקְבַּע] בִּרְכַּת ״גְּבוּרוֹת״ בִּ״מְחַיֵּה הַמֵּתִים״, שֶׁזֶּהוּ תֹּקֶף הַגְּבוּרָה: כְּשֶׁאֵין לוֹ הֶפְסֵק וְהַשְׁפָּלָה
Wherefore the blessing of Gevurot was established upon "Reviver of the Dead," for this is consummate might: possessing no cessation or humiliation;
וּ״מָוֶת״ — לְשׁוֹן הַשְׁפָּלָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּתַנְחוּמָא פָּרָשַׁת וַיְחִי (סִימָן ג׳)
death denoting humiliation (Tanchuma, Vayechi §3);
