וְעַל כֵּן עָנִי וְסוּמָא וְכוּלֵיהּ נִקְרָאִים ״מֵתִים״ (נְדָרִים ס״ד עַמּוּד ב׳), שֶׁהֵם בְּתַכְלִית הַשִּׁפְלוּת בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה מְרוּחָק מִכָּל טוֹבָה.
wherefore the poor and blind are called "dead" (Nedarim 64b), being in extreme worldly degradation.
וּתְחִיַּיִת הַמֵּתִים הוּא בֵּירוּר שֶׁהַמִּיתָה ״טוֹב מְאֹד״, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה ט׳:ה׳)
And the Resurrection demonstrates that death was "very good" (Bereishis Rabbah 9:5);
וּכְמוֹ הַשֵּׁינָה, כִּי בְּקוּמוֹ נַעֲשָׂה בְּרִיָּה חֲדָשָׁה וּמַחֲלִיף כֹּחַ וּגְבוּרָה
like sleep, where upon awakening one becomes a new creation, renewing strength;
וְזֶהוּ שְׁלֵימוּת הַגְּבוּרָה הָאֲמִיתִּית כְּשֶׁקַּיֶּימֶת לְעוֹלְמֵי עַד, שֶׁזֶּהוּ כְּשֶׁאֵין בָּהּ שׁוּם חֻלְשָׁה לְהַפְסִיק כֹּחַ הַגְּבוּרָה וּלְבַטְּלָהּ
this being authentic might which endures forever, having no weakness to halt it;
וּגְבוּרַת עֵשָׂו בְּהֵיפוּךְ: בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה נִרְאָה בְּתַכְלִית הַתֹּקֶף, וְסוֹפוֹ לַאֲבַדּוֹן, וְאֵין זוֹ גְּבוּרָה עַל הָאֱמֶת כְּלָל רַק מִצַּד הַדִּמְיוֹן בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה:
whereas Esau's might is the reverse: appearing intensely powerful in this world, yet ending in utter ruin, being no true might at all!

7.h: אוֹת י״ז — קְדֻשַּׁת יַעֲקֹב בְּ״אַתָּה קָדוֹשׁ״, הַנְּזִיד עֲדָשִׁים וְעוֹלָם כְּכַדּוּר הַמִּתְגַּלְגֵּל — Section 17: Jacob's Sanctity in "You Are Holy", The Pottage of Lentils, and the World as a Rolling Sphere

The theme: Jacob's image engraved upon the Throne of Glory, the transition from father to son, and the spherical world of perpetual motion. Jacob trampled the angelic prince of Esau under his feet; his attribute is Holiness (Kedushah)—the ultimate detachment from worldly desires. He is cleaved directly unto the Tetragrammaton (Havayah), his image engraved upon the Throne of Glory (Chullin 91b) in the likeness of the Man upon the Throne (Yechezkel 1:26), answering to the third blessing of the Amidah (Kedushat Hashem / Attah Kadosh). Jacob merited to be called a son unto Hashem: a son issues from the father's brain (mocha d'abba). By absorbing the light of Abraham (the father of the world) and combining it with Isaac's contraction (tzimtzum), the light expanded exclusively unto Jacob and his seed; thus Abraham’s status as "father" (Av) was transformed into Jacob’s status as "son" (Ben), receiving supernal holiness to be separated from worldly vanity. This is the pottage of lentils containing both mourning and joy. Matnot Kehunah cites Rashi that lentils are served at meals of celebration as well as mourning. Lentils are the food of the impoverished (Kesubos 67b: "will you roll with me in lentils?"). Poverty is a wheel that revolves in the world (galgal ha-chozer ba-olam, Shabbat 151b); lentils are round like a rolling ball (kaddur), having no rest (Yeshayah 22:18). The cosmos is spherical (Yerushalmi Avodah Zarah 3:1), filled with relentless motion. In this world of movement, man is born to toil; angels are called stationary (omdim, Zechariah 3:7), fixed on one rung, while man is an ascender (mehalech), moving from rung to rung!

p: וְיַעֲקֹב שֶׁדָּבוּק בֶּאֱמֶת, רָפַשׂ לְשָׂרוֹ שֶׁל עֵשָׂו תַּחַת רַגְלָיו
And Jacob, who is cleaved unto Truth, trampled the angelic prince of Esau beneath his feet;
וּמִדָּתוֹ הוּא הַקְּדוּשָׁה, שֶׁהוּא תַּכְלִית הַפְּרִישׁוּת וְהַרְחָקָה מִכָּל עִנְיְנֵי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה בְּתַכְלִית
his attribute being Holiness, which is the ultimate abstinence and total detachment from worldly matters;
כִּי הוּא דָּבוּק בִּקְדוּשָׁה עֶלְיוֹנָה מַמָּשׁ בְּשֵׁם הֲוָיָ״ה בָּרוּךְ הוּא
being cleaved unto supernal holiness in the Name Havayah, blessed be He;
דְּעַל כֵּן צוּרָתוֹ חֲקוּקָה בְּכִסֵּא הַכָּבוֹד בִּדְמוּת אָדָם שֶׁעַל הַכִּסֵּא (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה ס״ח:י״ב; יְחֶזְקֵאל א:כו)
wherefore his image is engraved upon the Throne of Glory in the likeness of the Man upon the Throne (Bereishis Rabbah 68:12; Yechezkel 1:26);
דְּכֹחָן שֶׁל נְבִיאִים: ״לְדַמּוֹת צוּרָה לְיוֹצְרָהּ״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה כ״ז:א׳)
the prophets possessing the power "to compare the form to its Creator" (Bereishis Rabbah 27:1);
כִּי כָּךְ גָּדוֹל קְדֻשַּׁת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, שֶׁנֶּגְדּוֹ בִּרְכַּת ״קְדוּשׁוֹת״ דְּ״אַתָּה קָדוֹשׁ וְגוֹמֵר״
for so vast was the holiness of Jacob, corresponding to the blessing of Kedushot: "You are holy, etc.";
וְעַל כֵּן זָכָה לִיקָּרֵא ״בֵּן״ לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, כִּי הַבֵּן נִמְשָׁךְ מִמּוֹחַ הָאָב וּבְדוֹמֶה לוֹ
wherefore he merited to be designated a "son" unto Hashem, a son issuing from the father's brain and resembling him.
וְהוּא עַל יְדֵי קְלִיטַת אוֹר אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁהָיָה ״אַב הָעוֹלָם״ לְהַמְשִׁיךְ שֶׁפַע הַשָּׂגַת אוֹרוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ בַּתַּחְתּוֹנִים
And this occurred through absorbing the light of Abraham our father who was the "father of the world," channeling divine light unto lower creations;
וּכְשֶׁהִגִּיעַ אוֹר זֶה לְיַעֲקֹב, שֶׁנִּתְחַבֵּר לוֹ מִדַּת הַצִּמְצוּם שֶׁלֹּא יוּשְׁפַּע אֶלָּא לַמָּקוֹם הָרָאוּי, שֶׁאֵינוֹ אֶלָּא יַעֲקֹב וְזַרְעוֹ לְבַד
and when this light reached Jacob, combined with Isaac's contraction that it expand only unto the worthy (Jacob and his seed);
וְנִמְשַׁךְ כָּל הָאוֹר בּוֹ לְבַד, נֶתְהַפֵּךְ מִתֹּאַר ״אָב״ וְהַמְשָׁכָה לְזוּלַת שֶׁלְּמַטָּה מִמֶּנּוּ, לְתֹאַר ״בֵּן״ שֶׁהוּא הַמְקַבֵּל וְהַמַּמְשִׁיךְ כֹּחַ שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה מִמֶּנּוּ אֵלָיו
all the light descending into him alone, transforming the title "Father" into the title "Son," who receives and draws the supernal power unto himself;
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה זָכָה לְהִתְקַדֵּשׁ בִּקְדֻשָּׁתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ, לִיבָּדֵל לְגַמְרֵי מֵהָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה.
meriting through this to be sanctified in His holiness, separated completely from this world.
וְזֶהוּ הַנְּזִיד עֲדָשִׁים שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ ״אֵבֶל וְשִׂמְחָה״ כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל מֵהַמִּדְרָשׁ
And this is the pottage of lentils containing both mourning and joy as cited above from the Midrash;
וְעַיֵּין שָׁם בְּ״מַתְּנוֹת כְּהֻנָּה״ בְּשֵׁם רַשִׁ״י שֶׁגַּם בִּסְעוּדוֹת שִׂמְחָה אוֹכְלִין אוֹתָן
and see there in Matnot Kehunah citing Rashi that lentils are consumed at festive meals as well;
וְעִיקָּרוֹ מַאֲכַל עֲנִיִּים, כִּדְמַיְיתֵי בִּכְתוּבּוֹת (ס״ז עַמּוּד ב׳): ״רְצוֹנְךָ שֶׁתִּתְגַּלְגֵּל עִמִּי בַּעֲדָשִׁים?״
being fundamentally the food of the poor, as cited in Kesubos (67b): "Are you willing to roll with me in lentils?";
וְאוֹתוֹ עָנִי בֶּן טוֹבִים שֶׁהָיָה מְפוּנָּק בְּיוֹתֵר לֹא יָכֹל לִסְבּוֹל וָמֵת
and that pampered nobleman who had become impoverished could not endure it and died;
וְאָמְרוּ עַל זֶה: ״אוֹי לוֹ דְּלָא בָּעֵי לְפַנּוֹקֵי נַפְשֵׁיהּ״
and the Sages remarked: "Woe unto him who pampered himself so much!";
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּפְסָחִים (קי״ד עַמּוּד א׳): ״אֱכוֹל [בְּצָלִים וְשֵׁב בַּצֵּל,] וְלֹא תֵיכוֹל [אַוְזִין וְתַרְנְגוֹלִין] וִיהֵא לִבְּךָ רוֹדֵף עָלֶיךָ״
as stated in Pesachim (114a): "Eat onions and dwell in the shade, and eat not geese and chickens lest your heart pursue you";
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמַר ״שֶׁתִּתְגַּלְגֵּל״, כִּי הָעֲנִיּוּת ״גַּלְגַּל הַחוֹזֵר בָּעוֹלָם״, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּשַׁבָּת (קנ״א עַמּוּד ב׳) עַל פָּסוּק ״כִּי בִּגְלַל״ (דְּבָרִים ט״ו:י׳)
and that he said "roll," for poverty is a revolving wheel in the world (Shabbat 151b on Devarim 15:10).
וְכֵן עֲדָשִׁים דּוֹמִין לְגַלְגַּל וְכַדּוּר, וּתְמוּנַת הַכַּדּוּר הִיא מִתְגַּלְגֶּלֶת תָּדִיר וְאֵין לָהּ מְנוּחָה
And so lentils resemble a wheel and a ball, the shape of a sphere rolling perpetually without rest;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״[צָנוֹף יִצְנָפְךָ צְנֵפָה] כַּדּוּר אֶל אֶרֶץ [רַחֲבַת יָדָיִם]״ (יְשַׁעְיָה כ״ב:י״ח)
as it is written: "He will violently turn and toss you like a ball into a large country" (Yeshayah 22:18);
וְכֵן ״עוֹלָם — כְּכַדּוּר״, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּיְרוּשַׁלְמִי (עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה פֶּרֶק ג׳ הֲלָכָה א׳) עַל פָּסוּק ״כָּל הַצְּלָמִים״
and so the world is shaped like a sphere (Yerushalmi Avodah Zarah 3:1);
כִּי הָעוֹלָם מָלֵא טִרְדָּא וְאֵין בּוֹ מְנוּחָה
for this world is filled with turmoil and devoid of physical rest.
דְּעַל כֵּן אָמְרוּ: ״בְּהִתְהַלֶּכְךָ תַּנְחֶה אֹתָךְ״ (מִשְׁלֵי ו:כב) — בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, שֶׁהוּא זְמַן הַהִילוּךְ, דְּ״אָדָם לְעָמָל יוּלָּד״ (אִיּוֹב ה:ז)
Wherefore the Sages expounded on "when you walk, it shall lead you" (Mishlei 6:22): this refers to this world, which is the time of walking, for "man is born unto toil" (Iyov 5:7);
אֲבָל יֵשׁ שֶׁעֲמָלוֹ בְּדַעַת וּבְכִשְׁרוֹן הַמַּעֲשֶׂה וְהִילוּכוֹ בִּקְדוּשָׁה
but there is one whose toil is in wisdom and skillful deed, walking in holiness;
וְהַמַּלְאָכִים נִקְרָאִים ״עוֹמְדִים״, שֶׁהֵם עַל מַדְרֵיגָה אַחַת כְּמוֹת שֶׁנִּבְרְאוּ
the angels being called "standing" (omdim), fixed upon a single static rung as they were created;
אֲבָל הָאָדָם ״מְהַלֵּךְ״ תָּמִיד מִמַּדְרֵיגָה לְמַדְרֵיגָה, וְאֵין לוֹ מְנוּחָה כַּצַּדִּיקִים הַנִּזְכָּר, וְזֶהוּ תַּכְלִית הַמְּנוּחָה בֶּאֱמֶת.
while man is an "ascender" (mehalech), moving perpetually from rung to rung, having no static rest like the righteous, this being the ultimate true rest!
וְהָרְשָׁעִים בְּהֵיפוּךְ: כְּשֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶם שַׁלְוָה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה וְרוֹב טוֹבָה שֶׁחוֹשְׁבִים שֶׁהֵם בִּמְנוּחָה
And the wicked are the exact reverse: when they possess tranquility and abundant wealth in this world, imagining they are at rest;

וּבֶאֱמֶת זֶהוּ תַּכְלִית הַטִּרְדָּא, שֶׁמְּשׁוּעְבָּד לְכָל שְׁרִירוּת לִבּוֹ וְתַאֲוַת נַפְשׁוֹ בִּרְדִיפַת ״קִנְאָה וְתַאֲוָה וְכָבוֹד הַמּוֹצִיאִין הָאָדָם מִן הָעוֹלָם״ (אָבוֹת פֶּרֶק ד׳ מִשְׁנָה כ״א):
in truth this is the height of turmoil, being enslaved to the stubborn lusts of the heart in pursuit of envy, lust, and glory which remove a man from the world (Avos 4:21)!

7.h: אוֹת י״ח — עֲדָשִׁים מַאֲכַל אֲבֵלִים וַחֲתָנִים, עוֹלָמוֹת עֲגוּלִים כְּגִלְדֵי בְּצָלִים, וְלֵב חֲכָמִים בְּבֵית אֵבֶל — Section 18: Lentils for Mourners and Grooms, Concentric Spheres, and the Wise Heart in the House of Mourning

The theme: Lentils as food for mourners and grooms, the universe fashioned like layers of an onion, and the tranquility of contentment versus the anxiety of feasting. Lentils are the food of mourners: the mourner sits quietly, resting from worldly labor; yet in his heart he is in profound turmoil, filled with sorrow. Death is termed "rest" in Scripture: "there the weary be at rest" (Iyov 3:17), which refers to the wicked who are freed from physical struggle; and regarding the righteous: "his soul rested" (nach nafshieh), for in death they are released from the commandments (Shabbat 30a). But this rest is merely external: the wicked are pursued by their sins into greater torments in Gehinnom; while the righteous ascend from strength to strength, granted "free access among these that stand by" (Zechariah 3:7) to toil in the divine perception of Torah. All the heavenly spheres are concentric orbs like the layers of an onion (gildei betzalim), their circular rotation alluding to perpetual motion as they rejoice to perform the will of their Maker, "as a bridegroom coming out of his chamber" (Tehillim 19:6). A groom is preoccupied with a mitzvah (tarud d'mitzvah), exempt from the Shema (Berachos 11a), resembling a king whose heart is hidden in deep counsel (Pirkei d'Rabbi Eliezer; Mishlei 25:3). Lentils are served to grooms and mourners: being the food of the poor, they appear as affliction, yet bring genuine rest to one who is content with his portion (same'ach b'chelko). "The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning" (Koheles 7:4)—this holy sorrow brings true rest from worldly lusts; while "the heart of fools is in the house of mirth"—their illusory leisure causing their desires to pursue and destroy them!

p: וְעַל כֵּן עֲדָשִׁים מַאֲכַל אֲבֵלִים, שֶׁהֵם גַּם כֵּן בִּמְנוּחָה מִיגִיעַת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה: יוֹשֵׁב וְדוֹמֵם וְאָסוּר בַּעֲשִׂיַּית מְלָאכָה
And therefore lentils are the food of mourners, who likewise rest from worldly labor: sitting in silence, forbidden to perform work;
וּבֶאֱמֶת הֵם בְּתַכְלִית הַטִּרְדָּא בְּלֵב מָלֵא יָגוֹן וַאֲנָחָה, וְאֵין לָהֶם שׁוּם מְנוּחָה בַּלֵּב
yet in truth they are in deep turmoil, their heart filled with grief and sighing, possessing no inward rest;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרָכוֹת (י״א עַמּוּד א׳): ״דְּטָרוּד טִרְדָּא דִּרְשׁוּת״, וְהַטִּרְדָּא הֵיפֶךְ הַמְּנוּחָה.
as stated in Berachos (11a): "he is preoccupied with an optional sorrow," turmoil being the opposite of rest.
וְכֵן הַמִּיתָה נִקְרָא ״מְנוּחָה״ בִּלְשׁוֹן הַכָּתוּב: ״וְשָׁם יָנוּחוּ יְגִיעֵי כֹחַ״ (אִיּוֹב ג:יז), וְשָׁם קָאֵי אַרְשָׁעִים
And so physical death is termed "rest" in Scripture: "and there the weary be at rest" (Iyov 3:17), which speaks of the wicked;
וְכֵן אַצַּדִּיקִים כִּלְשׁוֹן חֲכָמִים: ״דְּנָח נַפְשֵׁיהּ״
and regarding the righteous as the Sages phrase it: "his soul rested";
כִּי בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה מְסוּבָּלִים בְּמִצְוֹת, וּבַמֵּתִים: ״בַּמֵּתִים חָפְשִׁי״ (תְּהִלִּים פ״ח:ו׳) — מִן הַמִּצְוֹת (שַׁבָּת ל׳ עַמּוּד א׳), וְאֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ נִפְטְרוּ מֵעֲמַל דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה.
for in this world they are burdened with mitzvos, while in death they are free from the commandments (Shabbat 30a), both being released from earthly toil.
אֲבָל זֶהוּ מִצַּד הַמְּנוּחָה הַנִּגְלֵית שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
But this is strictly from the perspective of visible rest in this world;
אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת: ״[חַטָּאִים] תְּרַדֵּף רָעָה״ (מִשְׁלֵי י״ג:כ״א), וְהֵם שָׁם בִּיגִיעָה וְעָמָל יוֹתֵר
yet in truth: "evil pursues sinners" (Mishlei 13:21), they enduring far greater torment in Gehinnom;
וְהַצַּדִּיקִים גַּם כֵּן: ״יֵלְכוּ מֵחַיִל אֶל חָיִל״ (תְּהִלִּים פ״ד:ח׳), וּבָעוֹלָמוֹת עֶלְיוֹנִים: ״וְנָתַתִּי לְךָ מַהְלְכִים בֵּין הָעֹמְדִים הָאֵלֶּה״ (זְכַרְיָה ג:ז)
while the righteous ascend from strength to strength, granted access among the standing angels (Zechariah 3:7);
וִיגִיעָתָם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה בְּהַשָּׂגַת הַלֵּב בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה הוּא שָׁם יוֹתֵר וְיוֹתֵר הַרְבֵּה מְאֹד, וְהוֹלְכִים וּמִתְעַלִּים תָּמִיד יוֹתֵר וְיוֹתֵר.
their worldly toil in Torah expanding immensely on High as they ascend higher and higher.
וְזֶהוּ עִנְיַן כָּל הָעוֹלָמוֹת שֶׁהֵם עֲגוּלִים וְכַדּוּרִים ״כְּגִלְדֵי בְּצָלִים״
And this is the nature of all the heavenly worlds: circular and spherical like the layers of an onion (gildei betzalim);
דִּתְמוּנַת הַכַּדּוּר רוֹמֶזֶת עַל הַהִילוּךְ תָּמִיד כְּגַלְגַּל הָרָקִיעַ דְּהָדַר, וְזֶהוּ מְנוּחָתָן: שֶׁשָּׂשִׂים וּשְׂמֵחִים לַעֲשׂוֹת רְצוֹן קוֹנָם
the spherical shape hinting at perpetual motion like the rotating celestial orb, this being their rest: rejoicing to perform the will of their Maker;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְהוּא כְּחָתָן יֹצֵא מֵחֻפָּתוֹ, [יָשִׂישׂ כְּגִבּוֹר לָרוּץ אֹרַח]״ (תְּהִלִּים י״ט:ו׳).
as it is said: "Which is as a bridegroom coming out of his chamber, and rejoices as a strong man to run his course" (Tehillim 19:6).
וְגַם הֶחָתָן טָרוּד, דְּעַל כֵּן פָּטוּר מִקְּרִיאַת שְׁמַע (בְּרָכוֹת י״א עַמּוּד א׳), אֶלָּא שֶׁהוּא ״טָרוּד טִרְדָּא דְּמִצְוָה״
And the groom is likewise preoccupied, wherefore he is exempt from reciting the Shema, his preoccupation being the turmoil of a mitzvah (tarud d'mitzvah, Berachos 11a);

וְכֵן אִיתָא בְּפִרְקֵי דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר (פֶּרֶק ט״ז): ״דְּדוֹמֶה לְמֶלֶךְ״ — שֶׁנִּרְאֶה כִּבְתַכְלִית הַמְּנוּחָה וְהוּא בְּתַכְלִית הַטִּרְדָּא, דְּ״לֵב מְלָכִים — אֵין חֵקֶר״ (מִשְׁלֵי כ״ה:ג׳).
and in Pirkei d'Rabbi Eliezer (ch. 16): "a groom resembles a king"—who appears in total serenity yet bears supreme responsibility: "the heart of kings is unsearchable" (Mishlei 25:3).
וְזֶהוּ עִנְיַן עֲדָשִׁים שֶׁהוּא מַאֲכַל חֲתָנִים וַאֲבֵלִים, כִּי עִיקָּרוֹ מַאֲכַל עֲנִיִּים שֶׁנִּרְאָה בְּצַעַר וְטִרְדָּא וְהֵיפֶךְ הַמְּנוּחָה
And this explains why lentils are the food of both grooms and mourners: being the food of the poor, appearing as affliction and turmoil;
וּבֶאֱמֶת זֶהוּ הַמְּנוּחָה לְמִי שֶׁשָּׂמֵחַ בְּחֶלְקוֹ וְחָפֵץ בָּזֶה: שֶׁלֹּא יִטָּרֵד בְּבַקָּשַׁת צְרָכָיו הַמּוֹתָרוֹת, כִּי יִסְתַּפֵּק בַּמּוּעָט.
yet in truth offering genuine rest to one who is content with his portion, refusing to be anxious over superfluous desires, satisfied with the minimal.
וְכָךְ: ״אֵבֶל וְשִׂמְחָה״: ״לֵב חֲכָמִים — בְּבֵית אֵבֶל״ (קֹהֶלֶת ז:ד), דְּנִרְאָה כְּטִרְדָּא בַּלֵּב, אֲבָל טִרְדָּא זוֹ מְבִיאַתּוּ לִמְנוּחָה מִכָּל טִרְדַּת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה
And so with mourning and joy: "The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning" (Koheles 7:4)—which appears as emotional grief, yet brings enduring peace from worldly anxieties;
״וְלֵב כְּסִילִים — בְּבֵית שִׂמְחָה״ (שָׁם), שֶׁיַּחְשְׁבוּהוּ לִמְנוּחָה, וְהוּא בֶּאֱמֶת טִרְדָּא דְּעַל יְדֵי זֶה לִבּוֹ רוֹדֵף עָלָיו:
whereas "the heart of fools is in the house of mirth"—which they imagine to be rest, but is in truth deep turmoil wherein the heart pursues and destroys itself!
יִשְׂרָאֵל קְדוֹשִׁים — פֶּרֶק ז׳, סְעִיפִים י״ט–כ״ג

אוֹת י״ט — קְדֻשַּׁת יַעֲקֹב בְּ״יֹשֵׁב אֹהָלִים״ מוּל צְבִיעוּת עֵשָׂו בְּדֶרֶךְ אֶרֶץ, וְהַלְעָטַת הָעֲדָשִׁים — Section 19: Jacob's Holiness in the Tents vs. Esau's Hypocritical Derech Eretz, and Gulping the Stew

The theme: Jacob's absolute sanctity appearing as idleness to the outside world, Esau's pretense of labor, and the fatigue of fulfilled lust. Just as Abraham and Isaac's spiritual realities appeared outwardly opposite to superficial eyes, so it was with Jacob. When Esau saw Jacob "dwelling in tents" (Bereishis 25:27), he presumed Jacob sought idle leisure to indulge bodily desires without toiling in worldly occupation (derech eretz), since Isaac’s house was wealthy without financial anxiety. In contrast, Esau—displaying split hooves like a swine—pretended to embrace the toil of derech eretz that banishes sin (Avos 2:2) to avoid idleness that leads to promiscuity (Kesubos 59b), feigning contempt for worldly pleasures. In truth, Esau's hunting led directly to severe transgressions (Bereishis Rabbah 63:12 on "and he was faint", Bereishis 25:29). His purpose was evil; once lust is consumed, man is left exhausted, hollow, and full of sorrow. Envious of Jacob's holy tranquility, Esau demanded: "Feed me, I pray you, with that same red stew" (Bereishis 25:30), wishing to eat the poor man's lentils to attain effortless rest. Yet his eating was merely bestial gulping (hal'atah), incapable of bringing contentment. Jacob's physical striving in this world was to crush and subdue the yetzer hara that tempts daily, mastering it by sufficing with the absolute minimum!
וְיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם גַּם כֵּן דּוּגְמַת זֶה: שֶׁהוּא בְּתַכְלִית הַקְּדוּשָׁה וּפְרִישׁוּת מֵעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
And our father Jacob, peace be upon him, was likewise a prototype of this: being in consummate holiness and abstinence from this world;
וּבְוַדַּאי, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְעֵיל בְּאַבְרָהָם וְיִצְחָק, דִּלְמַרְאִית הָעַיִן הָיָה נִרְאָה בְּהֵיפוּךְ — מִסְּתָמָא גַּם הוּא כֵּן.
and certainly, as I wrote above regarding Abraham and Isaac, where to outward appearance it seemed the reverse, so it was with him as well.
וְעֵשָׂו שֶׁרְאָהוּ ״יֹשֵׁב אֹהָלִים״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית כ״ה:כ״ז), חָשַׁב: זֶהוּ מִצַּד חֶפְצוֹ בִּמְנוּחָה לְמַלֹּאות כָּל תַּאֲווֹתָיו
And Esau, seeing him "dwelling in tents" (Bereishis 25:27), assumed: this stems from his desire for leisure to sate all his bodily lusts;
וְאֵינוֹ רוֹצֶה לְיַגֵּעַ עַצְמוֹ וְלַעֲסוֹק בְּדֶרֶךְ אֶרֶץ
refusing to weary himself and engage in worldly occupation (derech eretz);
כִּי בֵּית יִצְחָק הָיָה מָלֵא כָּל טוּב, דְּהָיָה עָשִׁיר מֵאֲבִימֶלֶךְ, וְלֹא הוּצְרְכוּ לַעֲמוֹל עַל פַּרְנָסָה
for Isaac's household was filled with all goodness, being wealthier than Abimelech, not needing to toil for livelihood;
וְעֵשָׂו, בִּפְשִׁיטַת טְלָפָיו, הָיָה מַרְאֶה עַצְמוֹ בּוֹחֵר בִּיגִיעַת דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ הַמַּשְׁכַּחַת עָוֹן, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּאָבוֹת (פֶּרֶק ב׳ מִשְׁנָה ב׳)
and Esau, displaying his split hooves, pretended to choose the toil of derech eretz which causes sin to be forgotten (Avos 2:2);
וְשֶׁלֹּא לֵילֵךְ בָּטֵל, שֶׁהַבַּטָּלָה מְבִיאָה לִידֵי זִמָּה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּכְתוּבּוֹת (נ״ט עַמּוּד ב׳)
and not to walk idle, for idleness leads to promiscuity (Kesubos 59b);
וְשֶׁהוּא מוֹאֵס בָּזֶה בְּתַאֲווֹת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה, וְרוֹצֶה לַעֲסוֹק בְּדֶרֶךְ אֶרֶץ אַף שֶׁאֵין צָרִיךְ.
pretending that he despiseth worldly lusts and wisheth to engage in labor even though not financially required.
וּבֶאֱמֶת יְגִיעָתוֹ הֱבִיאַתּוּ לְכָל עֲבֵירוֹת, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה ס״ג:י״ב) עַל פָּסוּק: ״וְהוּא עָיֵף״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית כ״ה:כ״ט)
But in truth his toil brought him unto all manner of sins, as the Sages stated in Bereishis Rabbah (63:12) on "and he was faint" (Bereishis 25:29);
כִּי כַּוָּונָתוֹ הָיָה בָּזֶה בֶּאֱמֶת לְרַע וּלְמַלֹּאות תַּאֲוָתוֹ
for his inward intent was truly for evil and to sate his carnal desires;
וְאַחַר מִלּוּי הַתַּאֲוָה שֶׁכְּבָר עָבְרָה, נִשְׁאַר עָיֵף וְיָגֵעַ וּמָלֵא יָגוֹן וַאֲנָחָה
and once the transient lust passed, he remained faint, exhausted, and filled with grief and sighing;
וְקִנֵּא בְּיַעֲקֹב שֶׁיּוֹשֵׁב בִּמְנוּחָה
and envied Jacob who sat in tranquility;
וְזֶהוּ בַּקָּשָׁתוֹ: ״הַלְעִיטֵנִי נָא [מִן הָאָדֹם הָאָדֹם הַזֶּה]״ (שָׁם:ל׳)
and this was his petition: "Feed me, I pray you, with that same red stew" (ibid. 25:30);
שֶׁגַּם הוּא יְבַקֵּשׁ לֶאֱכוֹל עֲדָשִׁים מַאֲכַל עֲנִיִּים, וְלִהְיוֹת בִּמְנוּחָה.
seeking likewise to eat the lentils of the poor and attain effortless rest.
אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת גַּם זֶה הָיָה דֶּרֶךְ ״הַלְעָטָה״ שֶׁמּוֹרֶה רַק לְמִלּוּי תַּאֲוָה, וּמִמֵּילָא אִי אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁיִּסְתַּפֵּק בָּזֶה כְּלָל.
Yet in truth this too was through "gulping" (hal'atah), signifying carnal appetite, making it impossible that he ever be sated.
וְכָל הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת יַעֲקֹב בִּיגִיעַת בָּשָׂר בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה — הוּא לְבַטֵּשׁ וּלְהַכְנִיעַ אֶת הַיֵּצֶר הַמִּתְגַּבֵּר בְּכָל יוֹם, וּמַסִּית לְהִשְׁתַּדֵּל בְּתַאֲווֹת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה
While Jacob's striving in bodily weariness in this world was to crush and subdue the yetzer hara that attacks daily, inciting man to pursue worldly lusts;
וְהוּא מִתְגַּבֵּר נֶגְדּוֹ לְהִסְתַּפֵּק בַּמּוּעָט הָאֶפְשָׁרִי:
Jacob conquering it by sufficing with the absolute minimal necessity!
אוֹת כ׳ — נְזִיד הָעֲדָשִׁים וּמְכִירַת הַבְּכוֹרָה: בִּיטּוּל הַהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, ״הִנֵּה אָנֹכִי הוֹלֵךְ לָמוּת״, וְהַשְּׁבוּעָה
Section 20: The Pottage as Jacob's Spiritual Inception, "Behold, I Am at the Point to Die", and Demanding the Oath

7.h: The theme: The pottage as the nullification of worldly striving, Esau seeking effortless lust, and Jacob sealing the transfer through an oath. Cooking the pottage was Jacob's first practical deed in the world of Asiyah, the realm where Esau claimed priority through physical labor. Jacob’s striving was to attain the complete nullification of worldly toil for the sake of spiritual elevation. Yet an opposite hazard exists: one may despise worldly labor merely to indulge in lazy physical leisure. This was Esau's desire for the stew: he envied Jacob's rest, not to dwell in tents of Torah, but imagining that leisure offered greater carnal gratification. Jacob told him: "Sell me this day your birthright" (Bereishis 25:31)—sell me the power of striving in action, since you choose indolent rest and wish to be weary no longer. The birthright represented the holiness within practical action, which Jacob sought to extract from Esau. Esau realized: "Behold, I am at the point to die" (Bereishis 25:32): all travel (halichah) is turmoil (tirda, Berachos 11a), and in this world of perpetual movement, Esau—denying the World to Come—saw his life marching inexorably toward death, asking: "what profit shall the birthright do to me?" Jacob demanded: "Swear to me this day" (Bereishis 25:33). Holiness cannot be transferred through ordinary commercial acquisition (kinyan), just as a Kohen cannot sell his priesthood to a non-priest; but Esau's birthright was entirely of this world, his holiness being merely the outward display of split hooves like a swine. Because his birthright was not intrinsic, it lacked tangible substance (davar she-ein bo mamash); therefore Jacob required an oath to finalize the transfer, exchanging the pottage for the holy sparks within Esau!

p: וְזֶהוּ הַנָּזִיד שֶׁהוּא הַתְחָלַת וְרֹאשׁ הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתוֹ בְּמַעֲשֶׂה הַנִּזְכָּר בַּתּוֹרָה
And this pottage was the first recorded deed of Jacob's active striving in the Torah;
שֶׁמִּצַּד הַהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת בְּמַעֲשֶׂה הָיָה בְּכוֹרַת עֵשָׂו בְּעוֹלַם הַמַּעֲשֶׂה.
for on the side of physical action lay Esau's claim of the birthright in the world of deed.
וְהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת יַעֲקֹב הוּא לָבוֹא לְבִיטּוּל הַהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
And Jacob's striving was to arrive at the total nullification of worldly labor;
וּלְפִי שֶׁעַדַיִין יֵשׁ גַּם בָּזֶה צַד נְטִיָּה לַהַהֵיפֶךְ חַס וְשָׁלוֹם
and because there can exist even within this a subtle pitfall toward the opposite, God forbid:
דְּיֵשׁ מוֹאֵס בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה בִּשְׁבִיל הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, כִּי חָפֵץ בְּבַטָּלָה וּמְנוּחָה
where one despiseth worldly labor for the sake of worldly indulgence, desiring lazy idleness;
וְזֶה הָיָה חֶשְׁקוֹ שֶׁל עֵשָׂו אֶל נָזִיד זֶה: שֶׁקִּנֵּא לְיַעֲקֹב בִּמְנוּחָה
and this was Esau's craving for this stew: envying Jacob's tranquility;
וְלֹא שֶׁבָּחַר לִהְיוֹת יוֹשֵׁב אָהֳלֵי תּוֹרָה כָּמוֹהוּ, רַק שֶׁחָשַׁב: בָּזֶה יֵשׁ מִלּוּי תַּאֲוָה יוֹתֵר
not that he chose to dwell in the tents of Torah, but imagining that leisure yielded greater carnal pleasure;
וְזֶהוּ מַה שֶּׁהָיָה שַׁיָּיךְ לוֹ וּלְחֶלְקוֹ בְּאוֹתוֹ נָזִיד
and this was what belonged unto his share in that pottage;

כִּי יֵשׁ בְּכָל דָּבָר טוֹב וָרָע, וְצַד הָרָע שֶׁבּוֹ קְלָטוֹ עֵשָׂו, וּמִזֶּה נִצְמַח הַחֵשֶׁק שֶׁלּוֹ לְאוֹתוֹ נָזִיד בְּאוֹתוֹ חֵלֶק שֶׁהָיָה שַׁיָּיךְ לוֹ, דְּכָל אֶחָד חוֹשֵׁק לְדָבָר הַשַּׁיָּיךְ לוֹ כַּנּוֹדָע.
for good and evil exist in all things, Esau absorbing the unholy aspect, each person craving that which corresponds to his root.
וְעַל כֵּן אָמַר לוֹ יַעֲקֹב: ״מִכְרָה כַיּוֹם [אֶת] בְּכֹרָתְךָ [לִי]״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית כ״ה:ל״א) — הַיְינוּ כֹּחַ הַהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת
Wherefore Jacob told him: "Sell me this day your birthright" (Bereishis 25:31)—namely the spiritual power of striving in action;
כֵּיוָן שֶׁאַתָּה בּוֹחֵר בִּמְנוּחָה, וְאֵין רְצוֹנְךָ לִהְיוֹת עוֹד עָיֵף בִּיגִיעָה כָּל כָּךְ.
since you choose leisure, and no longer desire to be faint with physical weariness.
וְהַבְּכוֹרָה הוּא צַד הַקְּדוּשָׁה שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּזֶה, וּמֵהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת שֶׁמִּצַּד הַקְּדוּשָׁה רָצָה יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם לִקְלוֹט אָז מִמֶּנּוּ כְּשֶׁהִתְחִיל בְּהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתוֹ.
And the birthright is the holy dimension of action, which Jacob sought to extract from Esau as he initiated his own active spiritual service.

וְעֵשָׂו הִשִּׂיג: ״[הִנֵּה אָנֹכִי] הוֹלֵךְ לָמוּת״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית כ״ה:ל״ב), וְכָל הֲלִיכָה הוּא טִרְדָּא, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרָכוֹת (י״א עַמּוּד א׳) עַל פָּסוּק ״וּבְלֶכְתְּךָ בַדֶּרֶךְ״ (דְּבָרִים ו:ז): ״בְּלֶכֶת דִּידָךְ וְכוּלֵיהּ״
And Esau perceived: "behold, I am at the point to die" (Bereishis 25:32), all walking (halichah) being turmoil, as stated in Berachos (11a) on "and when you walk by the way" (Devarim 6:7);
וְזֶהוּ כָּל יְמֵי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁהוּא זְמַן הַהִילוּךְ כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל
this representing the days of this world which are the time of walking;
וְאָמַר: דְּכָל הִילוּכוֹ הוּא לָמוּת, דְּסוֹף אָדָם לָמוּת, וְהוּא לֹא הֶאֱמִין בִּשְׁנֵי עוֹלָמוֹת
and Esau said: his entire march was toward death, and denying the existence of the World to Come;
וְרָאָה דְּכָל הִילוּכוֹ וְהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתוֹ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא הוֹלֵךְ וּמִתְקָרֵב בְּכָל יוֹם אֶל הַמָּוֶת
he saw that all his worldly striving was merely approaching death with each passing day;
עַל כֵּן: ״[וְ]לָמָּה זֶּה לִי בְּכֹרָה״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית שָׁם) וְכֹחַ הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת? וּמוּטָב לוֹ מִלּוּי תַּאֲוָה דִּלְשָׁעָה בִּמְנוּחָה.
wherefore he said: "what profit shall the birthright do to me?" preferring the temporary gratification of leisure.
וְאָמַר לוֹ: ״הִשָּׁבְעָה לִּי [כַיּוֹם, וַיִּשָּׁבַע לוֹ]״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית כ״ה:ל״ג)
And Jacob told him: "Swear to me this day; and he swore unto him" (Bereishis 25:33);
כִּי עִנְיַן מְכִירַת בְּכוֹרָה, דְּהַיְינוּ הַקְּדוּשָׁה שֶׁבָּזֶה, הוּא דָּבָר דְּלֹא שַׁיָּיךְ עָלָיו קִנְיָן כְּלָל
for the sale of a spiritual birthright is not subject to ordinary legal acquisition (kinyan);
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכֹּהֵן לֹא יָכוֹל לִמְכּוֹר כְּהֻנָּתוֹ לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
just as a Kohen cannot sell his priesthood unto a common Israelite;
אֲבָל כָּל בְּכוֹרוּת עֵשָׂו הָיָה מִצַּד עוֹלָם הַזֶּה, וְצַד הַקְּדוּשָׁה שֶׁל בְּכוֹרָה שֶׁהָיָה בוֹ הָיָה רַק דֶּרֶךְ פְּשִׁיטַת טְלָפַיִם
but Esau's birthright was purely of this world, his holiness being merely the outward display of split hooves;
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם פְּשִׁיטַת טְלָפַיִם גַּם כֵּן אִי אֶפְשָׁר אֶלָּא מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ אֵיזֶה שֶׁמֶץ מַה שֶּׁל שַׁיָּיכוּת לִקְדוּשָׁה
yet displaying hooves is impossible without some subtle link unto holiness;
דְּעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִרְאֶה בְּעֵינָיו מִצַּד הָרָע שֶׁבּוֹ גַּוֶּון זֶה לְרַמּוֹת בּוֹ
through which the evil inclination perceives an outward guise to deceive;
וְרַק חֲזִיר יֵשׁ בּוֹ הַטְּלָפַיִם דְּטָהֳרָה וְלֹא שְׁאָר בַּעֲלֵי חַיִּים הַטְּמֵאִים, וְהוּא הַמְשׁוּקָּץ וּמְטוּנָּף מִכָּל הַבַּעֲלֵי חַיִּים
and only the swine possesses split hooves of purity among unclean animals, yet is the most abominable of beasts;
וְכֵן עֵשָׂו: ״[הִנֵּה] קָטֹן נְתַתִּיךָ בַּגּוֹיִם, בָּזוּי אַתָּה מְאֹד״ (עֹבַדְיָה א:ב)
and so Esau: "Behold, I have made you small among the nations; you are greatly despised" (Ovadiah 1:2);
כִּי אוֹתוֹ מְעַט סִימָן מִטָּהֳרָה נַעֲשָׂה לוֹ לְסַם הַמָּוֶת וּלְרַע לוֹ וּלְהִיטַּמֵּא עוֹד יוֹתֵר, כֵּיוָן שֶׁמִּשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ בּוֹ רַק לְרַמּוֹת
for that faint sign of purity became a deadly poison, defiling him further since he utilized it merely to deceive;
וְזֶהוּ שֶׁהִרְגִּישׁ שֶׁעַל יְדֵי הַבְּכוֹרָה הוּא הוֹלֵךְ לָמוּת, דְּנַעֲשֵׂית לוֹ סַם הַמָּוֶת
this being why he sensed that through the birthright he was marching to death, it becoming a poison of death unto him;
וְכֵיוָן שֶׁאֵינָהּ קִנְיָן לוֹ בְּעֶצֶם, רַק מִצַּד דִּמְיוֹן הָעָלְמָא דְּשִׁקְרָא הַמְעֹרָב טוֹב וָרָע
and not being his intrinsic possession, existing merely through the illusions of this world;
הָיָה יָכוֹל לִקְלוֹט קְדוּשָׁה זוֹ מִמֶּנּוּ, וּבַחֲלִיפִין דְּהַלְעָטַת הַנָּזִיד שֶׁהוּא קְלִיטַת צַד הָרָע שֶׁיֵּשׁ בִּישִׁיבַת אָהֳלִים וּבַקָּשַׁת מְנוּחָה:
Jacob was able to extract this holiness in exchange for the pottage, which absorbed the negative dross of seeking passive leisure!

7.h: אוֹת כ״א — דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ מַמָּשׁ בְּדִינֵי קִנְיָנִים, שְׁבוּעָה כְּקַיָּימָא, וְדִינֵי בְּנֵי נֹחַ — Section 21: Intangible Property in Halachah, Oaths as Binding Covenants, and Noahide Jurisprudence

The theme: Halachic mechanisms of acquiring intangible property (davar she-ein bo mamash), the eternal validity of Torah law across all worlds, and oaths under Noahide law. In Torah law, an acquisition executed upon an intangible entity (davar she-ein bo mamash, Bava Batra 157a) is legally revocable. Torah jurisprudence penetrates all worlds, physical and spiritual alike, enduring eternally. In spiritual realms, halachic acquisitions likewise operate: "the righteous merits and takes his fellow's share in Gan Eden" (Chagigah 15a). When an acquisition touches an intrinsic reality—such as a Hebrew servant (eved ivri) whose physical life-force is acquired—it cannot be absolute in Israel, for he goes free in the seventh year and Jubilee; and taking a fellow's portion in Gan Eden reverts to its owner in the seventh millennium or the Great Jubilee (Yovel HaGadol / Tar'a d'Cheiru). But with Esau, the birthright was not intrinsic; Jacob could acquire it permanently, never to return. Yet because it lacked tangible substance, a regular kinyan was ineffective; therefore Jacob required an oath (shevuah). In Aramaic, shevuah is translated kayama (a permanent establishment). Noahides seal all legal covenants with an oath (as Abimelech and Laban did with Abraham and Jacob, Bereishis 21:23, 31:53). Although not one of the Seven Noahide Laws, oaths fall under Dinin (civil jurisprudence, Ramban on Bereishis 34:13; Rema §6), which mandates legal mechanisms to prevent societal breakdown. For an Israelite, an oath creates a religious prohibition; for a Noahide, an oath operates as a binding proprietary kinyan where other acquisitions cannot function. Esau, having cast off the Torah, was governed strictly by Noahide law; therefore Jacob demanded: "Swear to me this day"—a clear, unassailable sale (mechirah berurah, Rashi) that can never be revoked!

p: אֶלָּא דְּהַקִּנְיָן עַל ״דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ מַמָּשׁ״ בַּדִּין יָכוֹל לַחֲזוֹר בּוֹ (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא קנ״ז עַמּוּד א׳)
However, a legal acquisition executed upon an intangible reality (davar she-ein bo mamash) can legally be retracted (Bava Batra 157a);
וְכָל מִשְׁפְּטֵי הַתּוֹרָה נוֹקְבִים וְיוֹרְדִים בְּכָל הָעוֹלָמוֹת וּבְכָל הָעִנְיָנִים, בֵּין בְּגַשְׁמִיּוּת בֵּין בְּרוּחָנִיּוּת
and all statutes of the Torah penetrate across all worlds and dimensions, corporeal and spiritual alike;
כִּי הֵם קַיָּימִים לְעוֹלְמֵי עַד גַּם כְּשֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה שׁוּם דָּבָר מֵעִנְיְנֵי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה
for they endure eternally even when nothing of this physical world remains;
וְגַם בְּרוּחָנִיּוּת יֵשׁ מִשְׁפְּטֵי קִנְיָנִים מַה שֶּׁאֶפְשָׁר לִקְנוֹת אֶחָד מֵחֲבֵירוֹ
and in spiritual dimensions there exist laws of acquisition governing what one may acquire from another;
וְהוּא מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ: ״זָכָה [צַדִּיק] — נוֹטֵל [חֶלְקוֹ וְחֵלֶק חֲבֵירוֹ בְּגַן עֵדֶן] וְכוּלֵיהּ״ (חֲגִיגָה ט״ו עַמּוּד א׳).
this being what the Sages stated: "the righteous merits and takes his portion and his fellow's portion in Gan Eden" (Chagigah 15a).
וְיֵשׁ בַּדָּבָר הָעַצְמִי לוֹ שֶׁהוּא דָּבָר שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ מַמָּשׁ דְּשַׁיָּיךְ קִנְיָן
And regarding an intrinsic entity which possesses tangible substance, a valid kinyan applies;
וְזֶהוּ קִנְיַן עֶבֶד עִבְרִי דְּיֵשׁ לוֹ קִנְיָן בְּעַצְמוּת חַיּוּתוֹ
this being the acquisition of a Hebrew servant whose master acquires his bodily life-force;
וְזֶה אִי אֶפְשָׁר בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל לַחֲלוּטִין, דְּסוֹף יֵצֵא לַחָפְשִׁי בִּשְׁמִיטָה וְיוֹבֵל
yet this can never be absolute in Israel, for he goes free in the seventh year and Jubilee;
וְכֵן עִנְיַן נְטִילַת חֵלֶק חֲבֵירוֹ בְּגַן עֵדֶן, סוֹף יַחֲזוֹר לִבְעָלָיו בָּאֶלֶף הַשְּׁבִיעִי שֶׁהוּא ״יוֹם שֶׁכּוּלּוֹ שַׁבָּת״ (תָּמִיד פֶּרֶק ז׳ מִשְׁנָה ד׳)
and so taking a fellow's share in Gan Eden ultimately reverts to its owner in the Seventh Millennium which is the day of total Shabbat;
אוֹ בַּיּוֹבֵל הַגָּדוֹל שֶׁשָּׁם ״תַּרְעָא דְּחֵירוּ״, שֶׁכָּל אֶחָד חוֹזֵר לְשָׁרְשׁוֹ כַּנּוֹדָע (זֹוהַר).
or in the Great Jubilee which is the Portal of Freedom (Tar'a d'Cheiru), where all reverts to its pristine root as is known.
אֲבָל בְּעֵשָׂו הָיָה אֶפְשָׁר לִקְנוֹת לְגַמְרֵי שֶׁלְּעוֹלְמֵי עַד לֹא יָשׁוּב לוֹ עוֹד
But with Esau it was possible to acquire permanently, never to return unto him throughout eternity;
כִּי אֵין זֶה קִנְיָן עַצְמִי לוֹ כְּאֵצֶל יִשְׂרָאֵל
for the birthright was not an intrinsic acquisition unto him as it is with an Israelite.
אֲבָל מֵאַחַר שֶׁאֵינוֹ עַצְמִי, אִם כֵּן הוּא ״דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ מַמָּשׁ״ דְּלָא חָשֵׁיב קִנְיָן
Yet because it was not intrinsic, it was an intangible entity (davar she-ein bo mamash) where an ordinary acquisition does not take effect;
עַל כֵּן הוּצְרַךְ לִשְׁבוּעָה שֶׁבּוֹ הִיא קִיּוּם הַדָּבָר
wherefore Jacob required an oath, which establishes permanent validation;
דְּעַל כֵּן תַּרְגּוּם ״שְׁבוּעָה״ — ״קַיָּימָא״ בִּלְשׁוֹן אֲרַמִּי
wherefore the Aramaic Targum translates shevuah as kayama (an enduring covenant);
שֶׁבָּזֶה מִתְקַיֵּים הַדָּבָר לִהְיוֹת נִשְׁאָר קָבוּעַ וְקַיָּים כֵּן.
through which the matter is established to remain permanently ratified.
וּמָצִינוּ גַּם בִּבְנֵי נֹחַ: לְקַיֵּים כָּל דָּבָר עָשׂוּ בִּשְׁבוּעָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּאֲבִימֶלֶךְ (בְּרֵאשִׁית כ״א:כ״ג) וְלָבָן (שָׁם ל״א:נ״ג)
And we find among the sons of Noah: establishing all legal covenants through an oath, as with Abimelech (Bereishis 21:23) and Laban (ibid. 31:53);
וְהִנֵּה אֵין זֶה מִשֶּׁבַע מִצְוֹת בְּנֵי נֹחַ שֶׁלֹּא יַעֲבוֹר עַל שְׁבוּעָה
and this is not one of the Seven Noahide Laws forbidding violating an oath;
וְצָרִיךְ לוֹמַר דְּהוּא בִּכְלַל ״דִּינִין״ שֶׁנִּצְטַוּוּ לַחְקוֹק חֻקִּים וְדִינִים וְנִימוּסִים בַּמַּה שֶּׁבֵּין אָדָם לַחֲבֵירוֹ שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה עוֹלָם הֶפְקֵר
and one must say this falls under Dinin (civil laws) commanding them to enact statutes and customs in interpersonal relations to prevent chaos
[עַיֵּין בָּרַמְבַּ״ן פָּרָשַׁת וַיִּשְׁלַח (בְּרֵאשִׁית ל״ד:י״ג) גַּבֵּי שְׁכֶם, וּבִתְשׁוּבוֹת רַמָ״א סִימָן י׳];
[see Ramban on Bereishis 34:13 regarding Shechem, and Responsa Rema §10];
וְקָבְעוּ קִנְיָן לְכָל דָּבָר אֵיךְ יִהְיֶה מִתְקַיֵּים, וְדָבָר דְּלָא שַׁיָּיךְ בְּהוּ קִנְיָן עָשׂוּ קִיּוּמוֹ עַל שְׁבוּעָה
and they instituted legal acquisitions to validate agreements, and where ordinary kinyan cannot function they established validity through an oath;
וּבָזֶה מִתְקַיֵּים הַדָּבָר שֶׁלֹּא יוּכַל לַחֲזוֹר עוֹד.
through which the matter is ratified, making retraction impossible.
וּבְיִשְׂרָאֵל אֵין הַשְּׁבוּעָה עוֹשָׂה קִנְיָן, רַק אִיסּוּר שְׁבוּעָה עָלָיו שֶׁלֹּא יוּכַל לַעֲבוֹר מִפְּנֵי הָאִיסּוּר
And in an Israelite an oath does not effect a property transfer, but places a religious prohibition upon him not to transgress;
וּבִבְנֵי נֹחַ לֵיכָּא אִיסּוּר, אֶלָּא רַק הוּא קִנְיָן בְּדָבָר דְּלָא שַׁיָּיךְ קִנְיָן אַחֵר
while for a Noahide there is no religious oath prohibition, acting strictly as a proprietary kinyan where no other acquisition applies;
נִקְנָה וְנִתְקַיֵּים הַדָּבָר שֶׁלֹּא יָכוֹל לְשַׁנּוֹתוֹ עוֹד עַל יְדֵי הַשְּׁבוּעָה.
the matter being acquired and ratified through the oath, rendering alteration impossible.
וַאֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא דְּהָאָבוֹת יָצְאוּ מִכְּלַל בְּנֵי נֹחַ, עֵשָׂו שֶׁלֹּא קִיֵּים הַתּוֹרָה וַדַּאי לֹא יָצָא מִכְּלָלָם
And even if the Patriarchs departed from the category of Noahides, Esau who rejected the Torah certainly remained in their category;
וְאַף דְּנִקְרָא ״יִשְׂרָאֵל מוּמָר״ (קִדּוּשִׁין י״ח עַמּוּד א׳), הַיְינוּ רַק מַה שֶּׁנּוֹלַד מִזֶּרַע יִצְחָק וְרִבְקָה
and though called an "apostate Israelite" (Kiddushin 18a), that was strictly by virtue of being born of Isaac and Rebecca;
וְגַם זֶה הָיָה עַדַיִין רָפוּי בְּיָדוֹ שֶׁהָיָה יָכוֹל לַהֲמִירוֹ וּלְהַחְלִיפוֹ
and even this was tenuous in his grasp, being able to exchange it;
וְאַחַר שֶׁחָטָא נֶעֱקַר שֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל מִמֶּנּוּ לְגַמְרֵי וְנִידּוֹן בְּדִינֵי בְנֵי נֹחַ.
and once he sinned, the title of Israel was uprooted from him entirely, being governed by Noahide law.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמַר: ״הִשָּׁבְעָה לִּי כַיּוֹם״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית כ״ה:ל״ג), וְרַשִׁ״י פֵּירֵשׁ עַל ״מִכְרָה כַיּוֹם״: ״מְכִירָה בְּרוּרָה״ (שָׁם:ל״א)
And this is why Jacob said: "Swear to me this day" (Bereishis 25:33), Rashi expounding on "sell me this day": "an unassailable, clear sale" (mechirah berurah, ibid. 25:31);
וְהַיְינוּ לְפִי שֶׁהַמְּכִירָה בְּדָבָר שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ מַמָּשׁ, אָמַר לוֹ: שֶׁיִּמְכּוֹר מְכִירָה שֶׁלֹּא יוּכַל לְעַרְעֵר, וְהַיְינוּ עַל יְדֵי שְׁבוּעָה.
meaning because selling an intangible entity is easily disputed, Jacob demanded a sale that could never be challenged, namely via an oath.

וּלְפִי שֶׁגַּם בִּשְׁבוּעָה יֵשׁ חִילּוּק: כִּי שְׁבוּעַת הַתּוֹרָה הוּא מִצַּד הָאִיסּוּר, שֶׁזֶּה דַּי גֶּדֶר לִבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל שׁוֹמְרֵי תּוֹרָה דִּכְתִיב בְּהוּ: ״סוּגָה בַּשּׁוֹשַׁנִּים״ (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים ז:ג; סַנְהֶדְרִין ל״ז עַמּוּד א׳)
For in oaths there is a fundamental distinction: a Torah oath operates as a religious prohibition, which is an impenetrable fence for Israel: "hedged with roses" (Shir HaShirim 7:3; Sanhedrin 37a);
דִּבְגֶדֶר הַתּוֹרָה הָרַךְ כַּשּׁוֹשַׁנָּה דַּי שֶׁלֹּא יִפְרְצוּ פְּרָצוֹת, אֲבָל לְאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם לָא סַגִּי בְּגֶדֶר שֶׁל אִיסּוּר
the Torah fence being soft as a rose yet sufficient to halt breaches, whereas for the nations a religious prohibition does not suffice;
אֲבָל הַשְּׁבוּעָה אֶצְלָם כְּמוֹ קִנְיָן הַמְקַיֵּים הַדָּבָר שֶׁלֹּא יָכוֹל לְשַׁנּוֹתוֹ כְּלָל מִצַּד הִתְקַיְּימוּת עֶצֶם הַדָּבָר, שֶׁהוּא מֵעַתָּה כֵּן וְלֹא מִפְּנֵי הָאִיסּוּר:
but an oath among Noahides functions as a property acquisition ratifying the reality itself, and not merely out of religious restraint!
אוֹת כ״ב — הַתָּרַת שְׁבוּעָה בִּבְנֵי נֹחַ מוּל יִשְׂרָאֵל, שְׁבוּעַת יוֹסֵף לְפַרְעֹה וּלְיַעֲקֹב, וּבֵירוּר עֵץ הַדַּעַת טוֹב וָרָע
Section 22: Absolving Oaths under Noahide Law vs. Torah Law, Joseph's Oaths to Pharaoh and Jacob, and Sifting the Tree of Knowledge

7.h: The theme: The legal difference in oath annulment between Israelites and Noahides, Pharaoh and Joseph’s oaths, and the cosmic separation of good and evil through the sale of the birthright. A halachic difference exists regarding absolving an oath (hatarat shevuah): absolution applies strictly unto a Torah oath which is a religious prohibition; but for a Noahide, where an oath functions as an irreversible civil kinyan, absolution cannot apply! This illuminates Sotah (36b): Pharaoh told Joseph regarding Jacob’s burial: "Go and seek absolution for your oath!" Joseph replied: "If so, I will also seek absolution for my oath to you!" (regarding not revealing that Joseph knew one more language than Pharaoh). Pharaoh elevated Joseph on account of that oath, making unilateral absolution impermissible without Pharaoh's consent (Yoreh De'ah §225); whereas Joseph’s oath unto Jacob was an act of pure kindness (chesed shel emet) which could be annulled. Joseph told Pharaoh: The Patriarchs observed the entire Torah; Pharaoh treated Joseph’s oath as a Torah vow subject to absolution. Joseph countered: "My oath to you was governed by Noahide law, acting as an irreversible kinyan with no absolution; but if you claim I can annul oaths, I will annul my oath to you as well!" Esau likewise sought to display split hooves to act like an Israelite; Jacob demanded an absolute oath to strip him of any possibility of absolution. By swearing, Esau forfeited his ancestral connection, departing from Israel into the status of a Noahide; wherefore Scripture states: "and he swore unto him, and he sold his birthright" (Bereishis 25:33). Through Adam's eating from the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil, good and evil became intermingled throughout the universe and within all eating. Jacob—who did not die (Ta'anit 5b)—came to separate this mixture. Jacob is the root of Torah, the Tree of Life (Etz HaChayim) which is pure good; while Esau is the root of defilement and Amalek. In the womb they were mixed; through the pottage, Jacob extracted the good, leaving Esau entirely evil!

p: וְנָפְקָא מִינַּהּ נַמֵּי לְעִנְיַן שְׁאֵלָה וְהַתָּרָה הַנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל: דְּלָא מְהַנֵּי אֶלָּא לְעִנְיַן שְׁבוּעָה שֶׁל תּוֹרָה, שֶׁהוּא מִצַּד אִיסּוּר הַתּוֹרָה
And a practical legal difference issues regarding seeking absolution and annulment: it is effective only regarding a Torah oath, which operates as a religious prohibition;
אֲבָל שְׁבוּעַת בֶּן נֹחַ, כְּפִי מַה שֶּׁכָּתַבְתִּי דְּהוּא בִּכְלַל הַדִּינִין וְעַל דְּבַר קִנְיָן — לֹא שַׁיָּיךְ בּוֹ שְׁאֵלָה כְּלָל כִּבְכָל קִנְיָנִים.
whereas for a Noahide oath, which falls under Dinin and operates as an acquisition, absolution cannot apply at all, just as acquisitions cannot be dissolved.
וּבָזֶה יוּבַן מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ בְּסוֹטָה (ל״ו סוֹף עַמּוּד ב׳): ״דְּפַרְעֹה אֲמַר לֵיהּ לְיוֹסֵף: אִיתְשִׁיל אַשְׁבוּעֲתָךְ! וַאֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֶתְשִׁיל נַמֵּי אַדִּידָךְ!״
And through this is understood Sotah (36b): "Pharaoh said unto Joseph: Go seek absolution for your oath! Joseph replied: Then I will likewise seek absolution for my oath unto you!";
וּמַה הַתְּלוּת יֵשׁ זֶה בָּזֶה?
and what legal dependency exists between the two?
וְכִי לֹא הָיָה יָכוֹל לִשָּׁאֵל מִקּוֹדֶם עַל שְׁבוּעַת פַּרְעֹה?
could Joseph not have sought absolution previously regarding his oath to Pharaoh?
אֲבָל לְפִי מַה שֶּׁכָּתַבְתִּי יֵשׁ לוֹמַר: כִּי יָדוּעַ דְּאָבוֹת קִיְּימוּ כָּל הַתּוֹרָה כוּלָּהּ
But according to what I wrote, one may explain: for it is known that the Patriarchs fulfilled the entire Torah;
וּפַרְעֹה דַּאֲמַר לֵיהּ ״אִיתְשִׁיל״ — הַיְינוּ דְּהוּא מִתְנַהֵג עַל פִּי הַתּוֹרָה, וּשְׁבוּעָתוֹ כִּשְׁבוּעַת הַתּוֹרָה לְנֶדֶר שֶׁל אִיסּוּר בִּלְבַד, וּמְהַנֵּי שְׁאֵלָה
and Pharaoh in saying "seek absolution" assumed Joseph operated under Torah law where an oath is an actionable prohibition subject to absolution;
וְיוֹסֵף אֲמַר לֵיהּ: דִּשְׁבוּעָתוֹ כִּשְׁבוּעַת בֶּן נֹחַ, וְלָא מְהַנֵּי שְׁאֵלָה
and Joseph answered: his oath was governed by Noahide law where no absolution exists;
וְאָמַר לוֹ: שֶׁיּוֹדֶה לוֹ עַל זֶה שֶׁיִּהְיֶה דִּינוֹ כְּבֶן נֹחַ, דְּזוֹ מַעֲלִיּוּתָא הוּא גַּם לְדִידָךְ: דְּאִם לֹא כֵן, אוּכַל לִשְׁאוֹל גַּם אַדִּידָךְ!
telling Pharaoh: acknowledge that my oath is binding as a Noahide, which protects you as well, for otherwise I could seek absolution on my oath to you!
וְהִנֵּה עֵשָׂו גַּם כֵּן פָּשַׁט טְלָפָיו לְהִתְנַהֵג כְּיִשְׂרָאֵל, וְאִם כֵּן יַחְשׁוֹב שְׁבוּעָתוֹ כִּשְׁבוּעַת יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁיּוּכַל לִשְׁאוֹל עָלָיו
And behold Esau likewise displayed his hooves to act like an Israelite, assuming his oath was an Israelite oath subject to absolution;
וְעַל כֵּן אָמַר לֵיהּ שֶׁיִּשָּׁבַע לוֹ שְׁבוּעָה בְּרוּרָה כַּיּוֹם הַבָּרוּר, שֶׁלֹּא יוּכַל לִישָּׁאֵל עָלֶיהָ
wherefore Jacob demanded he swear an unassailable oath like the clear day, where absolution could never apply;
וְהוּא עָשָׂה כֵן, כִּי בַּמְּכִירָה הַזּוֹ נִפְקַע מִמֶּנּוּ גַּם אֵיזֶה שׁוֹרֶשׁ מְעַט שֶׁהָיָה בוֹ מֵאֲבוֹתָיו, וְיָצָא מִכְּלַל יִשְׂרָאֵל לִכְלַל בֶּן נֹחַ
and Esau did so, for through this sale he was stripped of his ancestral root, departing from Israel into the category of a Noahide;
וְעַל כֵּן הִקְדִּים: ״וַיִּשָּׁבַע לוֹ, וַיִּמְכֹּר״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית כ״ה:ל״ג), דְּעַל יְדֵי הַשְּׁבוּעָה הָיָה הַמְּכִירָה.
wherefore Scripture states: "and he swore unto him, and he sold his birthright" (Bereishis 25:33), the sale being ratified via the oath.
וְאַחַר כָּךְ: ״וְיַעֲקֹב נָתַן [לְעֵשָׂו]״ (שָׁם:ל״ד), שֶׁכְּבָר נָתַן, מַה שֶּׁשַּׁיָּיךְ לוֹ לְחֶלְקוֹ וּלְשָׁרְשׁוֹ
And afterward: "And Jacob gave Esau" (ibid. 25:34)—what was already given, allocating unto Esau that which belonged to his root.
כִּי עַל יְדֵי אֲכִילַת אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן מֵעֵץ הַדַּעַת טוֹב וָרָע, נִתְעָרֵב בְּכָל הָעוֹלָם טוֹב וָרָע וְגַם בְּכָל הָאֲכִילוֹת
For through Adam HaRishon's eating from the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil, good and evil were intermingled throughout the universe and within all eating;
וְיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁהוּא הַמְתַקֵּן לְחֶטְאוֹ, דְּעַל כֵּן ״לֹא מֵת״ (תַּעֲנִית ה׳ עַמּוּד ב׳), הוּא בָּא לְהַפְרִיד עֵירְבּוּב זֶה וּלְהַבְדִּיל הַטּוֹב מִן הָרָע
and our father Jacob who rectified Adam's sin—wherefore he did not die (Ta'anit 5b)—came to separate this mixture and sever good from evil.
וְהוּא הָיָה שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַטּוֹב וְהַקְּדוּשָׁה שֶׁבְּכָל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ, שֶׁאֵין קְדוּשָׁה וְטוֹב אֶלָּא בְּזֶרַע יַעֲקֹב
And Jacob was the root of good and holiness in the entire world, holiness existing exclusively within Jacob's seed;

Section 23: Bread and Pottage as the Tree of Life vs. Esau's Drinking, "He Rose and Went His Way and Despised", and Famine following Evil Eating

The theme: Jacob giving bread with the pottage to rectify wheat as the Tree of Knowledge, Esau's unrecorded wine drinking, and famine striking the Land. Once the sale severed them, Jacob’s gift became manifest as completely independent of his own holy portion. Esau demanded "some of that red stew," wishing to take part of Jacob's holy share; but Jacob gave him an entire pottage of his own, and added bread which Esau had not requested. Bread is the primary medium of refinement according to the opinion that the Tree of Knowledge was wheat (Sanhedrin 70b; Berachos 40a), wheat sustaining physical life. Bread from the Tree of Life is the word of Hashem within it ("man does not live by bread only, but by every word that proceeds out of the mouth of Hashem", Devarim 8:3), nourishing eternal life; while corporeal bread issues from the Tree of Knowledge. Jacob separated the coarse dross and gave it to Esau. Esau added drinking on his own initiative—"and he drank" (va-yisht, Bereishis 25:34) denoting wine—rejoicing in the meal, unaware that he was heaping coals upon his head. "And he rose up, and went his way" (ibid.)—walking (halichah) being turmoil (tirda), compounding his anxiety through the very worldly leisure he sought. "And Esau despised his birthright" (ibid.): previously his split hooves of pretense found favor in his eyes to deceive Isaac and Rebecca; but once the evil was isolated, he openly despised the birthright, discarding even the pretense of holiness. Only the evil portion of the meal was chronicled in Scripture, because Jacob's holy portion remained concealed, awaiting future refinement in his seed (Ta'anit 5b). Immediately following, Scripture states: "And there was a famine in the land" (Bereishis 26:1), for the revelation of evil eating drags famine in its wake (whereas holy eating, like the brothers eating bread before Joseph was sold, channeled food unto the entire world, Bereishis Rabbah 91:5). Then Isaac was granted blessings (Bereishis 26:3–4), Abraham having withheld blessings until Esau and Jacob were separated, clarifying that the blessing of "in Isaac shall your seed be called" applied exclusively to Jacob!

And following the sale, when they were severed one from another, this giving was revealed as separated, and not from Jacob's holy portion;

but Jacob gave him "pottage" (ibid. 25:34) and not "of the pottage" (which would imply part of his own), but an independent stew of his own;

each being separated, having no connection between them whatsoever.

אֲבָל אָז זָכָה יִצְחָק לַבְּרָכוֹת (בְּרֵאשִׁית כ״ו:ג׳–ד׳)
But then Isaac merited the divine blessings (Bereishis 26:3–4);
שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה: דְּאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם לֹא בֵּירְכוֹ שֶׁלֹּא יִתְבָּרֵךְ עֵשָׂו, וְאָמַר: ״יָבוֹא בַּעַל הַבְּרָכוֹת [וִיבָרֵךְ]״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה ס״א:ו׳)
the Sages stating: Abraham did not bless Isaac lest Esau be included, declaring: "Let the Master of blessings come and bless whom He pleases" (Bereishis Rabbah 61:6);
וְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ גַּם כֵּן הִמְתִּין עַד שֶׁיִּפָּרְדוּ זֶה מִזֶּה לְגַמְרֵי
and Hashem likewise waited until the twins were completely severed from one another;

וְנִתְבָּרַר דִּ״בְיִצְחָק יִקָּרֵא [לְךָ זָרַע]״ (שָׁם כ״א:י״ב) — ״וְלֹא כָל יִצְחָק״ (נְדָרִים ל״א עַמּוּד א׳), שֶׁאֵין עֵשָׂו קָרוּי זַרְעוֹ כְּלָל, וּבִרְכַּת זַרְעוֹ לֹא קָאֵי אֶלָּא עַל יַעֲקֹב.
clarifying that "in Isaac shall your seed be called" (Bereishis 21:12)—"and not all of Isaac" (Nedarim 31a), Esau not being termed his seed, the blessing resting exclusively upon Jacob.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן מִקּוֹדֶם הָיָה אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁיּוּכְלַל גַּם עֵשָׂו, וְהוּא הֵיפֶךְ הַבְּרָכָה, כִּי: ״בִּרְכַּת ה׳ הִיא תַעֲשִׁיר, וְלֹא יוֹסִף עֶצֶב עִמָּהּ״ (מִשְׁלֵי י:כב)
Whereas previously Esau might have been included, which is the antithesis of blessing, for "the blessing of Hashem makes rich, and He adds no sorrow with it" (Mishlei 10:22);
וְהוּא הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ דְּקִלְלַת אָדָם מִצַּד עֵירוּב הָרָע שֶׁל שׁוֹרֶשׁ עֵשָׂו: ״בְּעִצָּבוֹן תֹּאכֲלֶנָּה״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית ג:יז), שֶׁאֲכִילָתוֹ הֵבִיאָה עִצָּבוֹן וְרָעָבוֹן
this sorrow being the root of Adam's curse through the mixture of Esau's evil: "in sorrow shall you eat of it" (Bereishis 3:17), his eating bringing sorrow and famine.
וְיִצְחָק לֹא הִרְגִּישׁ בְּכָל זֶה, כִּי חָשַׁב אֶת עַצְמוֹ שֶׁנִּימּוֹל לִשְׁמוֹנָה לִהְיוֹת קָדוֹשׁ מִלֵּידָה מִבֶּטֶן, שֶׁכְּבָר זָכָה לְשֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל לִהְיוֹת מִטָּתוֹ שְׁלֵימָה.
And Isaac was unaware of this, assuming that because he was circumcised at eight days and holy from the womb, he had already merited the name Israel and that his bed was whole.
וְהָאֱמֶת הָיָה כֵן, דְּמִשֶּׁנִּתְבָּרַר יַעֲקֹב לְחֵלֶק ה׳ לִהְיוֹת מִטָּתוֹ שְׁלֵימָה — אָז גַּם אַבְרָהָם וְיִצְחָק לֹא נִקְרְאוּ אָבוֹת אֶלָּא לְזֶרַע יַעֲקֹב
And in absolute truth it was indeed so: once Jacob was clarified as Hashem's portion whose bed was whole, Abraham and Isaac were titled Patriarchs exclusively unto the seed of Jacob;

וְאַף אַבְרָהָם נִקְרָא ״יִשְׂרָאֵל״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ס״ג:ז׳), כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה: דְּנִקְרָא ״אֶזְרָחִי״ (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא ט״ו עַמּוּד א׳), שֶׁזָּכָה לִהְיוֹת אֶזְרָח בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל
and Abraham was titled "Israel" (Bereishis Rabbah 63:7), called "the Ezrachi" (Bava Batra 15a) to be a native citizen in Israel;
כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת גַּם מִטָּתָם שְׁלֵימָה, כִּי רַק: ״בְּיִצְחָק יִקָּרֵא לְךָ זָרַע״ — וְלֹא כָל יִצְחָק, וְאֵין עֵשָׂו וְיִשְׁמָעֵאל זַרְעוֹ כְּלָל, רַק יַעֲקֹב שֶׁמִּטָּתוֹ שְׁלֵימָה
for in truth their beds were whole, Ishmael and Esau not being accounted their seed at all, Jacob alone being their eternal progeny;
וְזֶהוּ אַחַר שֶׁנִּתְבָּרַר יַעֲקֹב לִהְיוֹת מִטָּתוֹ שְׁלֵימָה בְּלֹא פְּסֹולֶת — אָז נִתְבָּרְרוּ גַּם הֵם, כִּי הַפְּסֹולֶת נִדְחָה מִלִּיקָּרֵא זַרְעָם כְּלָל:
and once Jacob was clarified as possessing a bed whole without dross, Abraham and Isaac were retroactively clarified as well, all dross being rejected from being called their seed!

7.h: יִשְׂרָאֵל קְדוֹשִׁים — פֶּרֶק ז׳, סְעִיפִים כ״ד–ל׳

אוֹת כ״ד — בֵּירוּר הַמִּטָּה שְׁלֵימָה עַל יְדֵי לְבוּשׁ עֵשָׂו, תְּפִלַּת יִצְחָק עַל הָרְשָׁעִים, וְהַמְתָּקַת הַמַּר בְּמַר — Section 24: Refining the Whole Bed through Esau's Garments, Isaac's Defense of Transgressors, and Sweetening Bitter with Bitter

The theme: Jacob's acquisition of the birthright clarifying his personal righteousness, while the flawlessness of his bed (mitah sheleimah)—guaranteeing that even the worst sinners of Israel retain their sacred name and are never banished—was finalized only through donning Esau's garments to receive the blessings. Isaac sought to bless Esau not out of blind ignorance, but out of his unique attribute to defend even the wicked of his seed so that they would not be destroyed, as in Shabbat (89b) where Isaac took upon himself their punishment ("half upon me") while Abraham and Jacob said "let them be erased". Abraham did not pray for children, preferring to remain childless rather than father wicked descendants who anger Hashem (Bereishis Rabbah 44:10); and Jacob told Rachel: "Am I in God's stead, Who has withheld from you the fruit of the womb?" (Bereishis 30:2), submitting to strict Justice (Elohim) out of dread of fathering wicked progeny. But regarding Abraham and Jacob the Gemara remarks: "there is no counsel among the elders," for they did not perceive that Hashem devises wondrous counsels (eitzot) for everything, turning crimson sins to white snow and sweetening bitter with bitter. The Torah is called "counsel and sound wisdom" (eitzah v'tushiyah, Mishlei 8:14), going forth from Gevurah to provide remedies for all blemishes. In the second blessing of the Amidah (Gevurot), Hashem revives the dead, supports the fallen, and heals the sick, demonstrating how strict Judgment (Middat HaDin) contains the deepest counsels to sweeten bitter through bitter, as Moshe was commanded to cast a bitter tree into bitter water to make it sweet (Shemos 15:25; Tanchuma, Beshalach §24; Shemos Rabbah 43:3)!

p: וּבֵירוּר יַעֲקֹב בִּלְקִיחַת הַבְּכוֹרָה הָיְתָה מִצַּד עַצְמוֹ שֶׁהוּא כּוּלּוֹ טוֹב
And Jacob's refinement through acquiring the birthright was on his own personal account, he being entirely good;
וְעַדַיִין לֹא נִתְבָּרַר שְׁלֵימוּת הַמִּטָּה
yet the consummate flawlessness of his bed was not yet clarified;
הַיְינוּ אֲפִילּוּ אִם יִהְיֶה מִזַּרְעוֹ מִי שֶׁלֹּא כֵן, מִכָּל מָקוֹם ״לֹא יִדַּח [מִמֶּנּוּ] נִדָּח״ (שְׁמוּאֵל ב י״ד:י״ד)
meaning that even if there arise among his descendants someone who is not righteous, nevertheless "no outcast is banished from Him" (II Shmuel 14:14);
וְשֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל לֹא נֶעֱקַר מִמֶּנּוּ, אֲפִילּוּ יַגְדִּיל עֲווֹנוֹת עַד לַשָּׁמַיִם
and the name of Israel is never uprooted from him, even if he multiplies iniquities unto the heavens;
שֶׁזֶּהוּ עִנְיַן שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ פְּסֹולֶת, דָּבָר זֶה לֹא נִתְבָּרַר עַדַיִין עַד קַבָּלַת הַבְּרָכוֹת עַל יְדֵי לְבִישַׁת הַלְּבוּשׁ שֶׁל עֵשָׂו.
this being the principle that his bed contains no unholy dross, which remained unclarified until receiving the blessings through donning the garments of Esau.
כִּי הִנֵּה עִנְיַן יִצְחָק שֶׁבִּקֵּשׁ לְבָרֵךְ אֶת עֵשָׂו: וְכִי סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ שֶׁרִבְקָה יָדְעָה שֶׁיַּעֲקֹב צַדִּיק וְעֵשָׂו רָשָׁע, וְהוּא לֹא יָדַע?!
For behold the matter of Isaac seeking to bless Esau: could it enter your mind that Rebecca knew Jacob was a tzaddik and Esau wicked, while Isaac was ignorant?!
אֲבָל זֶה כָּל עִנְיַן יִצְחָק: לְבַקֵּשׁ גַּם בְּעַד הָרְשָׁעִים מִזַּרְעוֹ שֶׁלֹּא יֹאבְדוּ
Rather, this was the entire essence of Isaac: to intercede even for the wicked among his seed that they perish not;
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּשַׁבָּת (פ״ט עַמּוּד ב׳): דְּאַבְרָהָם וְיַעֲקֹב הֵשִׁיבוּ ״יִמָּחוּ וְכוּלֵיהּ״
as stated in Shabbat (89b): that Abraham and Jacob responded to Hashem regarding sinners, "let them be erased, etc.";
וְיִצְחָק טָעַן גַּם בְּעַד הָרְשָׁעִים שֶׁבְּיִשְׂרָאֵל, וְקִיבֵּל עַל עַצְמוֹ עָנְשָׁם: ״פַּלְגָא עָלַי וְכוּלֵיהּ״.
while Isaac pleaded on behalf of the transgressors of Israel, accepting upon himself their punishment: "half is upon me, etc."
וְכֵן אַבְרָהָם לֹא נִמְצָא בַּכָּתוּב שֶׁהִתְפַּלֵּל עַל בָּנִים, וְכֵן הוּא בַּזֹּוהַר (תּוֹלְדוֹת קל״ז רֵישׁ עַמּוּד ב׳) דְּלָא צַלִּי
And so regarding Abraham, it is nowhere recorded in Scripture that he prayed for children, the Zohar stating likewise (Toldot 137b) that he did not pray;
וּבִבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה מ״ד:י׳) דְּאָמַר: ״אִם עָתִיד אֲנִי לְהַעֲמִיד בָּנִים וּלְהַכְעִיסְךָ, מוּטָב: ׳וְאָנֹכִי הוֹלֵךְ עֲרִירִי׳ (בְּרֵאשִׁית ט״ו:ב׳)״
and in Bereishis Rabbah (44:10) where he declared: "If I am destined to bring forth children who anger You, it is better that 'I go childless' (Bereishis 15:2)";
וּמַשְׁמַע דְּמִטַּעַם זֶה לֹא נִתְפַּלֵּל, כִּי יָדַע וַדַּאי: אִם מוּכָן לְהוֹלִיד צַדִּיקִים גַּם הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מֵעַצְמוֹ לֹא יִמְנַע הַטּוֹב
implying that for this reason he withheld prayer, knowing that were he prepared to father only righteous children, Hashem would not withhold good;
וְלָמָּה כָּל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ מוֹלִידִים וְהוּא אֵינוֹ מוֹלִיד? וְחָשַׁב: עַל כֵּן הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא יוֹדֵעַ שֶׁיֵּצְאוּ מִמֶּנּוּ רְשָׁעִים.
reasoning: why does all the world bear children while he is barren? Perforce the Holy One knows wicked descendants will issue from him.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁבֶּאֱמֶת גַּם שׁוֹרֶשׁ הָרָע שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם שֶׁהוּא עֵשָׂו וַעֲמָלֵק גַּם כֵּן עֲתִידִין לָצֵאת מִמֶּנּוּ
As indeed the root of cosmic evil—Esau and Amalek—was destined to emerge from him;
וְעַל כֵּן הִנִּיחַ הַדָּבָר לִפְנֵי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁמַּה שֶּׁיִּרְצֶה יַעֲשֶׂה
wherefore Abraham surrendered the matter unto the Blessed Name to do as He willed;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁלֹּא בֵּירַךְ לְיִצְחָק מִטַּעַם זֶה: שֶׁלֹּא יִתְבָּרֵךְ אִילָן שֶׁל סַם הַמָּוֶת הֶעָתִיד לָצֵאת מִמֶּנּוּ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה ס״א:ו׳), וְהִנִּיחַ הַדָּבָר לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
just as he did not bless Isaac lest the tree of deadly poison (Esau) issuing from him be blessed (Bereishis Rabbah 61:6), leaving the blessing unto Hashem.
וְגַם יַעֲקֹב הֵשִׁיב לְרָחֵל: ״הֲתַחַת אֱלֹהִים אָנֹכִי, אֲשֶׁר מָנַע [מִמֵּךְ פְּרִי בָטֶן]״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית ל:ב)
And Jacob likewise answered Rachel: "Am I in God's stead, Who has withheld from you the fruit of the womb?" (Bereishis 30:2);
וְגַם הִיא יָדְעָה מִזֶּה, וּמַה שֶּׁאָמְרָה ״הָבָה [לִּי בָנִים]״ (שָׁם:א׳) הַיְינוּ שֶׁיִּתְפַּלֵּל לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
she knowing this as well, her petition "Give me children" being that he pray for her;
אֲבָל הוּא הֵשִׁיב: מֵאַחַר שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הוּא וַדַּאי בְּדִין, כִּי הוּא שׁוֹפֵט צֶדֶק, וּמִסְּתָמָא יָדַע שֶׁיֵּצְאוּ רְשָׁעִים
but he replied: since the Blessed Name acts with righteous judgment, He knows that wicked progeny might issue.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁהִרְגִּישׁוּ הַשְּׁבָטִים בְּיוֹסֵף וְרָצוּ לְהָרְגוֹ מִפְּנֵי כֵן: שֶׁאָמַר ״עָתִיד זֶה לְהַשִּׂיאָם לַבְּעָלִים״, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה פ״ד:י׳)
Just as the tribes suspected Joseph and sought to slay him, saying: "he is destined to wed our daughters unto pagan masters" (Bereishis Rabbah 84:10);
כֵּן חָשַׁב גַּם הוּא שֶׁעַדַיִין לֹא יָדַע זֶה דְּאֵין פְּסֹולֶת בְּזַרְעוֹ כְּלָל וַאֲפִילּוּ בָּרְשָׁעִים
so Jacob reasoned, not yet knowing that his seed contained no unholy dross even among the wicked;
וְעַל כֵּן אָמַר ״הֲתַחַת אֱלֹהִים״ — שֵׁם דְּמִדַּת הַדִּין
wherefore he said "Am I instead of Elohim"—the Divine Name of strict Judgment;
וְכִי אֲנִי אֶהְיֶה דַּיָּין וְאֵשֵׁב לָדוּן בִּמְקוֹמוֹ, וְאוֹמַר שֶׁהוּא עִוֵּות מִשְׁפָּט חַס וְשָׁלוֹם?!
shall I sit as judge in His place, claiming that He perverted justice, God forbid?!
וַהֲלֹא בְּוַדַּאי הוּא עָשָׂה כֵן שֶׁלֹּא יוֹלִיד רְשָׁעִים, וּלְהוֹלִיד רְשָׁעִים גַּם הוּא אֵין רוֹצֶה כְּלָל, וּמוּטָב שֶׁלֹּא תֵּלֵד.
for certainly Hashem closed her womb so as not to bear the wicked, and Jacob likewise had no desire to father wicked sons, preferring she remain childless.
אֲבָל עֲלֵיהֶם אָמְרוּ בְּשַׁבָּת שָׁם (פ״ט עַמּוּד ב׳): ״לָא בְּסָבֵי טַעְמָא, וְלָא בְּדַרְדַּקֵּי עֵצָה״
But regarding Abraham and Jacob the Gemara remarks in Shabbat (89b): "there is no taste in the elders, nor counsel in the youth";
וְגַם ״טַעַם״ לְשׁוֹן ״עֵצָה״, כְּמוֹ בְּדָנִיֵּאל (ב:יד): ״הֲתִיב עֵטָא וּטְעֵם״
"taste" (ta'ama) also signifying counsel, as in Daniel (2:14): "he returned counsel and wisdom";
כִּי הֵם לֹא יָדְעוּ שֶׁיֵּשׁ לְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עֵצוֹת עַל כָּל דָּבָר, וְחָשְׁבוּ: דְּהוֹאִיל וְהֵם רְשָׁעִים — יִמָּחוּ וְאֵין לָהֶם תַּקָּנָה.
for they did not realize that the Holy One possesses marvelous counsels for everything, assuming that since sinners are wicked they must be erased without remedy.
וּבֶאֱמֶת לַכֹּל יֵשׁ תַּקָּנָה וְעֵצָה, וְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ יָכוֹל לַעֲשׂוֹת מִשָּׁנִים שֶׁלֶג (יְשַׁעְיָה א:יח), וּמִזְּדוֹנוֹת — זְכֻיּוֹת (יוֹמָא פ״ו עַמּוּד ב׳), וּלְהַמְתִּיק אֶת הַמַּר

Yet in truth for all things there is a remedy and counsel, Hashem being able to make scarlet sins as white as snow (Yeshayah 1:18), transmuting intentional sins into merits (Yoma 86b), sweetening the bitter.
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר בַּתּוֹרָה לְשׁוֹן ״עֵצָה וְתוּשִׁיָּה״ (מִשְׁלֵי ח:יד): שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה יֵשׁ עֵצוֹת לְכָל דָּבָר
And concerning this Scripture says of the Torah: "Counsel is mine, and sound wisdom" (Mishlei 8:14), the Torah containing divine counsels for every broken reality;
וּמְסַיֵּים הַכָּתוּב שָׁם: ״לִי גְבוּרָה״, כִּי אוֹרַיְיתָא מִסִּטְרָא דִּגְבוּרָה נָפְקַת, וּמִשָּׁם הֵם הָעֵצוֹת לְתַקֵּן כָּל מִינֵי הַקִּלְקוּלִים
the verse concluding: "I am understanding, I have might (Gevurah)," for the Torah went forth from Gevurah, whence issue the counsels to heal all blemishes;
דְּעַל כֵּן בְּבִרְכַּת הַגְּבוּרוֹת נֶאֱמַר: ״מְחַיֵּה מֵתִים, סוֹמֵךְ נוֹפְלִים, וְרוֹפֵא חוֹלִים, וּמַתִּיר אֲסוּרִים״
wherefore in the blessing of Gevurot we praise: "Reviver of the dead, Supporter of the fallen, Healer of the sick, and Releaser of the bound".
כִּי כְּשֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מִתְנַהֵג בְּחֶסֶד וְרַחֲמִים, אֵין קִלְקוּל וָרַע כְּלָל
For when the Blessed Name conducts the world through Chesed and mercy, no blemish or evil can exist;
אֲבָל כְּשֶׁהָרָע גּוֹבֵר, וְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ יוֹשֵׁב עַל כִּסֵּא דִּין: ״לִפְנֵי זַעְמוֹ מִי יַעֲמוֹד״ (נַחוּם א:ו)
but when evil ascends and Hashem sits upon the throne of Judgment: "Who can stand before His indignation?" (Nachum 1:6);
עַל כֵּן בְּמִדַּת הַדִּין עַצְמָהּ, שָׁם הוּא קְבִיעוּת הָעֵצוֹת שֶׁלָּהּ: תִּיקּוּנִים, וְשֶׁיּוּכְלוּ לִזְכּוֹת גַּם בַּדִּין
wherefore within Judgment itself are established its counsels: remedies whereby souls are vindicated even within strict Judgment;
וְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַמְתִּיק אֶת הַמַּר — בַּמַּר, וְלֹא בַּמָּתוֹק
the Blessed Name sweetening the bitter specifically through the bitter, and not through the sweet;

כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּתַנְחוּמָא בְּשַׁלַּח (סִימָן כ״ד) עַל פָּסוּק ״וַיּוֹרֵהוּ ה׳ עֵץ״ (שְׁמוֹת ט״ו:כ״ה): ״עַכְשָׁיו אַתָּה צָרִיךְ לִלְמוֹד וְכוּלֵיהּ; ׳וַיַּרְאֵהוּ׳ לֹא נֶאֱמַר, אֶלָּא ׳וַיּוֹרֵהוּ׳ — הוֹרָהוּ דַּרְכּוֹ״

as stated in Tanchuma (Beshalach §24) on "and Hashem showed him (va-yorehu) a tree" (Shemos 15:25): "now you must learn; it says not 'He showed him' (va-yar'ehu), but 'He instructed him' (va-yorehu)—teaching him His ways";
[וּבִשְׁמוֹת רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה מ״ג:ג׳ מְבוֹאָר יוֹתֵר: שֶׁמֹּשֶׁה הִרְהֵר ׳לָמָּה נִבְרָא מַר זֶה?׳ וְאָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: ׳הַכֹּל לְצֹרֶךְ, וְכָךְ אֱמוֹר: עֲשֵׂה הַמַּר — מָתוֹק׳;

[and in Shemos Rabbah 43:3 it is explained: Moshe questioned why this bitter tree was created, and Hashem told him all is for a purpose, instructing him to make bitter water sweet through the bitter tree;
וּדְזֶה הָיָה טַעֲנָתוֹ: ״לֹא כָּךְ אָמַרְתָּ וְכוּלֵיהּ? וְאַף עַכְשָׁיו: חֲלֵי מְרִירוּתָן!״ יְעוּיַּן שָׁם בַּמִּדְרָשׁ עַל פָּסוּק ״וַיְחַל מֹשֶׁה״ (שְׁמוֹת ל״ב:י״א)]
and this was Moshe's prayer at the Golden Calf: "Did You not tell me to sweeten bitter with bitter? Now sweeten the bitterness of Israel!" (Shemos 32:11)];
דְּדָבָר זֶה לִימּוּד עֵצָה בִּידִיעַת דַּרְכֵי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ כַּאֲשֶׁר הָרָע גּוֹבֵר חַס וְשָׁלוֹם
this being the deep instruction in Hashem's ways when evil ascends, God forbid;
שֶׁאֵין מָקוֹם לְהַמְשִׁיךְ שֶׁפַע מִמִּדַּת הַחֶסֶד וְהָרַחֲמִים שֶׁהוּא בְּלֹא הַגְבָּלָה וְצִמְצוּם, וְיוּכַל חַס וְשָׁלוֹם הָרָע לְהִתְגַּבֵּר יוֹתֵר
where one cannot channel unbounded Chesed lest the wicked twist it to evil, leisure for the wicked being harmful to them and the world;
רַק לִמְצוֹא עֵצוֹת לְהַמְשִׁיךְ שֶׁפַע עַל יְדֵי מִדַּת הַדִּין דַּוְוקָא.
but finding counsels to draw divine influx specifically through strict Judgment!
וּכְעִנְיַן יִצְחָק בִּקֵּשׁ יִסּוּרִין (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה ס״ה:ט׳), וְהֵם מַעֲבִירִין עַל דַּעַת קוֹנוֹ לִפְעָמִים בְּבִיטּוּל תּוֹרָה וַעֲבוֹדָה
As Isaac petitioned for afflictions (Bereishis Rabbah 65:9), which at times disrupt study and divine service;
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם הֵם ״כַּמֶּלַח הַמַּמְתִּיק אֶת הַבָּשָׂר״ (בְּרָכוֹת ה׳ עַמּוּד א׳)
yet afflictions operate "like salt sweetening meat" (Berachos 5a).
וְכַיּוֹצֵא בוֹ יֵשׁ תִּיקּוּנִים גַּם לְתַקֵּן הָרָע הַקּוֹדֵם וְהַכֹּל בְּמִשְׁפָּט
And similarly there are remedies to rectify past evil, all guided by divine justice;
וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ: ״דִּין דְּלָא כְּתִיב בֵּיהּ אֱמֶת — הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עוֹשֶׂה לִפְנִים מִשּׁוּרַת הַדִּין״
as stated: "judgment where truth is not written, the Holy One executes beyond the strict line of justice";
וְהַיְינוּ דְּגַם זֶה ״דִּין״, כִּי הוּא אֶחָד מִדִּינֵי וּמִשְׁפְּטֵי הַתּוֹרָה לַעֲשׂוֹת גַּם כֵּן לִפְנִים מִשּׁוּרַת הַדִּין
meaning this too is codified law, being one of the statutes of the Torah to act beyond the letter of the law;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּבָבָא מְצִיעָא (פ״ג עַמּוּד א׳): ״דִּינָא הָכִי? אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִין, דִּכְתִיב: ׳לְמַעַן תֵּלֵךְ בְּדֶרֶךְ טוֹבִים׳ (מִשְׁלֵי ב:כ)״
as stated in Bava Metzia (83a): "Is this the law? He replied: Yes, for it is written: 'That you may walk in the way of good men' (Mishlei 2:20)";
שֶׁגַּם זֶה דִּין מַמָּשׁ, דְּזֶהוּ הַמְתָּקַת הַדִּינִים עַל יְדֵי מִדַּת הַדִּין עַצְמָהּ בִּדְרָכָיו שֶׁל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
this being actual law, representing the sweetening of judgments through Judgment itself, to sweeten the bitter specifically through the bitter!

7.h: אוֹת כ״ה — יִצְחָק וּכְבִישַׁת הַכַּעַס בַּדִּין, ״פַּלְגָא עָלַי וּפַלְגָא עֲלָךְ״, וְהַמְתָּקַת הַדִּינִים בְּשָׁרְשָׁם — Section 25: Isaac Subduing Wrath in Judgment, "Half Upon Me and Half Upon You", and Sweetening Judgments at their Root

The theme: Isaac using Gevurah to conquer Gevurah, the soul surrendered at the Akeidah, and converting evil into "very good" (tov me'od). Isaac, embodying strict Judgment (Middat HaDin), is uniquely the one who rescues transgressors from Judgment. His spiritual might consists of conquering his wrath through law, subduing contraction through contraction (kol zina l'zineih). Evil issues from the dross of strict decrees and contractions that caused darkness in the world; therefore Isaac said: "Half the sin is upon me, because my attribute of Gevurah caused this; and half is upon You, for all issues from You, seeing that I offered my soul before You at the Akeidah". This is the sweetening of judgments at their supernal root (hamtakat ha-dinim b'shorshan), restoring all to the highest source where all is pure good and no evil descends from Heaven. Therefore Isaac prayed for children through an intense, overturning plea (va-ye'etar, Bereishis 25:21), the Sages noting in Sukkah (14a) that he overturned the decree like a pitchfork (atar). He knew a poisonous tree (Esau) was destined to emerge, yet prayed because Hashem can overturn death into life and evil into good. "And behold it was very good" (Bereishis 1:31)—this is death and the yetzer hara (Bereishis Rabbah 9:5): when evil is sweetened into good, it becomes "very good," surpassing intrinsic good, like a king rejoicing over a captured son returning home. Hashem declares: "and what I have done evil" (Michah 4:6); since all issues from Him, He possesses the power to return all to its root, transmuting darkness into radiant light!

p: וְדַוְוקָא יִצְחָק שֶׁהוּא מִדַּת הַדִּין, הוּא הִצִּיל הָרְשָׁעִים מִמִּדַּת הַדִּין
And specifically Isaac, who is the attribute of Judgment, delivered the wicked from strict Judgment;
וְהֵן הֵן גְּבוּרוֹתָיו: שֶׁהוּא כּוֹבֵשׁ כַּעֲסוֹ בַּדִּין
and these are his very triumphs of might: subduing wrath through the mechanism of law;
וּכְבִישָׁה הוּא מִדַּת הַגְּבוּרָה, שֶׁיָּכוֹל לִכְבּוֹשׁ אֵיזֶה דָּבָר שֶׁלֹּא יִתְפַּשֵּׁט יוֹתֵר
subduing being the trait of Gevurah, holding back an entity that it expand no further;
וְהוּא מִתְגַּבֵּר נֶגֶד מִדַּת הַגְּבוּרָה עַצְמָהּ, וְ״כָל זִינָא — לְזֵינֵיהּ״
he conquering Gevurah through Gevurah itself, each species matching its own kind.
וְשׁוֹרֶשׁ הָרָע נִמְשָׁךְ מִפְּסֹולֶת הַדִּינִין וְהַצִּמְצוּם שֶׁגָּרְמוּ הַחֹשֶׁךְ וְהַהֶעְלֵם בָּעוֹלָם
And the root of evil is drawn from the dross of judgments and the contraction that caused darkness in the cosmos;
וְעַל כֵּן אָמַר יִצְחָק: ״פַּלְגָא עָלַי״ (שַׁבָּת פ״ט עַמּוּד ב׳) — שֶׁאֲנִי וּמִדָּתִי הוּא הַגּוֹרֵם לָזֶה
wherefore Isaac argued: "Half is upon me"—for I and my attribute of Gevurah caused this;
״וּפַלְגָא עֲלָךְ״ — כִּי מִמְּךָ הַכֹּל, ״דְּהָא קָרֵיבִית נַפְשִׁי קַמָּךְ״, שֶׁמָּסַרְתִּי נַפְשִׁי כוּלָּהּ לָךְ
"and half is upon You"—for all issues from You, seeing that I offered my soul before You at the Akeidah.
וְזֶהוּ עִנְיַן הַמְתָּקַת הַדִּינִין בְּשָׁרְשָׁן, שֶׁמַּחֲזִיר הַכֹּל לַמָּקוֹר וְשׁוֹרֶשׁ הָעֶלְיוֹן
And this is the sweetening of judgments at their supernal root, returning all unto the highest source;
דְּשָׁם הַכֹּל בִּקְדוּשָׁה וְכוּלּוֹ טוֹב, וְ״אֵין דָּבָר רַע יוֹרֵד מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה נ״א:ג׳).
where all is in holiness and pure good, no evil thing ever descending from Heaven.
וְעַל כֵּן יִצְחָק הֶעְתִּיר עַל בָּנִים, וְאִיתָא בְּסֻכָּה (י״ד עַמּוּד א׳): ״דְּהָפַךְ כְּעָתֶר״
Wherefore Isaac pleaded for children, the Sages stating in Sukkah (14a): he overturned the decree like a pitchfork (atar);
הַיְינוּ דְּגַם הוּא יָדַע כְּאַבְרָהָם דְּסַם הַמָּוֶת עָתִיד לָצֵאת
meaning he likewise knew, as Abraham knew, that a deadly poison was destined to emerge;
וְעִם כָּל זֶה נִתְפַּלֵּל, כִּי הֲלֹא הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ יָכוֹל לַהֲפֹךְ הַדָּבָר, וְלַעֲשׂוֹת מִמָּוֶת — חַיִּים, וּמֵרַע — טוֹב
yet nevertheless he prayed, knowing Hashem can overturn death into life and evil into good;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ עַל פָּסוּק: ״וְהִנֵּה טוֹב מְאֹד״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית א:לא) — ״זֶה מָוֶת״, ״זֶה יֵצֶר הָרָע״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה ט:ה, ז)
as expounded on "And behold it was very good" (Bereishis 1:31): this is death, this is the yetzer hara (Bereishis Rabbah 9:5, 7);
שֶׁכְּשֶׁנִּמְתַּק וְנַעֲשָׂה מִן הָרָע טוֹב — הוּא ״טוֹב מְאֹד״ יוֹתֵר מִטּוֹב בְּעֶצֶם.
for when evil is sweetened into good, it becomes "very good," surpassing intrinsic good.
וְכִידוּעַ הַמָּשָׁל: מִמֶּלֶךְ שֶׁשָּׂמַח מִבְּנוֹ שֶׁהָיָה בַּשִּׁבְיָה וְחָזַר אֵלָיו, הַרְבֵּה יוֹתֵר מִשִּׂמְחָתוֹ בְּבָנָיו שֶׁבְּבֵיתוֹ מֵעוֹלָם
And as the celebrated parable: a king rejoices over a captured son returning home far more than over sons who dwelled safely in his palace.
וַהֲרֵי אֵין שׁוּם דָּבָר עוֹשֶׂה אֶת עַצְמוֹ, וְהַכֹּל מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, דְּעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: ״[וַאֲשֶׁר פָּזַרְתִּי] וַאֲשֶׁר הֲרֵעֹתִי״ (מִיכָה ד:ו)
And behold nothing creates itself, all issuing from Hashem: "and whom I have afflicted" (Michah 4:6);
דְּלוּלֵי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, וַדַּאי לֹא הָיָה מְצִיאוּת כְּלָל לְשׁוּם דָּבָר, וְגַם מַה שֶּׁהוּא הַהֵיפֶךְ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הַכֹּל הוּא מִמֶּנּוּ
for without the Blessed Name nothing could exist, and even that which appears as the opposite in this world is from Him;
וְאִם כֵּן בְּיָדוֹ לְהָשִׁיב הַדָּבָר לְשָׁרְשׁוֹ, דְּעַל יְדֵי זֶה יִתְהַפֵּךְ הַדָּבָר לְ״טוֹב מְאֹד״, כְּשֶׁיַּחֲזוֹר הַכֹּל לִמְקוֹרוֹ וְיָשׁוּבוּ לְבֵית הַמֶּלֶךְ מַלְכּוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם:
wherefore it is in His hand to return all to its root, transmuting it into "very good" when returning to the King of the universe!

7.h: אוֹת כ״ו — הַגָּלוּת לְהוֹסִיף גֵּרִים, מִיצוּי הַחַיּוּת דְּעֵשָׂו בְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר, וְטָעוּתוֹ שֶׁל יִצְחָק בְּעֵשָׂו — Section 26: Exile to Gather Converts, Siphoning Esau's Vitality through Rabbi Meir, and Isaac's Error

The theme: Israel exiled to gather converts, absorbing the good sparks of Esau, and Isaac's mistaken assumption that Esau was the evil turning into "very good". This transformation of evil into "very good" is accomplished exclusively through the seed of Jacob. In Pesachim (87b): "Israel was exiled among the nations solely to add converts," meaning to absorb the holy sparks concealed within the husks, on account of which the nations exist until those good mules (peridot tovot) are extracted and grafted into Israel. Then the remaining husk will be burned like cut thorns (kotzim kesuchim, Yeshayah 33:12). The spark of vitality Hashem granted unto Esau ("and You preserve them all", Nechemiah 9:6) is gradually extracted and absorbed into Israel through converts like Rabbi Meir (descended from Nero, Gittin 56a) until at the End of Days no vitality remains in Esau and he perishes. When Isaac saw his prayer answered, he knew Hashem agreed to transform evil into "very good"; he assumed this applied to Esau. Isaac was not mistaken in his theological principle, but in his identification of Esau: before the blessings, he assumed that "the one people shall be stronger than the other" (Bereishis 25:23) meant Jacob was pure good, while Esau was the evil destined to be transmuted into "very good"!

p: וּבֶאֱמֶת כָּל הִתְהַפְּכוּת זֶה מֵרַע לְ״טוֹב מְאֹד״ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא עַל יְדֵי זֶרַע יַעֲקֹב
And in truth this entire transformation from evil into "very good" is accomplished solely through the seed of Jacob;
וְעַל זֶה אִיתָא: ״דְּלֹא גָּלוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל [לְבֵין הָעַמִּים] אֶלָּא כְּדֵי לְהוֹסִיף עֲלֵיהֶם גֵּרִים״ (פְּסָחִים פ״ז עַמּוּד ב׳)
and on this the Talmud states: "Israel was exiled among the nations solely to add converts unto them" (Pesachim 87b);
הַיְינוּ לִקְלוֹט כָּל מְעַט טוֹב הַגָּנוּז בְּתוֹךְ סִטְרָא דְּרָע
meaning to absorb every subtle spark of good hidden within the Sitra Achra;

שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה הוּא כָּל מְצִיאוּת שֶׁלָּהֶם בָּעוֹלָם, בִּשְׁבִיל אוֹתָם ״פְּרֵידוֹת טוֹבוֹת״ שֶׁעָתִיד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לְהַפְרִיד מֵהֶם וּלְהַרְכִּיב בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל (בָּבָא קַמָּא ל״ח עַמּוּד ב׳)
on account of which the nations exist in the world: for the sake of those "good mules" Hashem will extract from them and graft into Israel (Bava Kamma 38b).
וְאָז הַנִּשְׁאָר: ״[וְהָיוּ עַמִּים מִשְׂרְפוֹת שִׂיד,] קוֹצִים כְּסוּחִים בָּאֵשׁ יִצַּתּוּ״ (יְשַׁעְיָה ל״ג:י״ב), שַׁלְהֶבֶת מִדַּת הַדִּין תְּלַהֲטֵם.
And then the remaining husk: "as thorns cut down, that are burned in the fire" (Yeshayah 33:12), the flame of strict Judgment consuming them.
וְכֵן מְעַט הַחַיּוּת דְּעֵשָׂו שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּרָאוֹ וְהִנִּיחוֹ לְהִתְגַּדֵּל בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, ״וְאַתָּה מְחַיֶּה אֶת כֻּלָּם״ (נְחֶמְיָה ט:ו) כְּתִיב
And so the spark of vitality within Esau which Hashem created, for "You preserve them all" (Nechemiah 9:6);
אוֹתוֹ חַיּוּת הוּא נִפְרָד וְהוֹלֵךְ מִמֶּנּוּ מְעַט מְעַט וְנִכְנָס בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל
that vitality is gradually severed from Esau and absorbed into Israel;
אִם עַל יְדֵי גֵּרִים, כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר מִזֶּרַע נִירוֹן (גִּיטִּין נ״ו עַמּוּד א׳) וְכַיּוֹצֵא, דִּ״בְשֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל יְכַנֶּה״ (יְשַׁעְיָה מ״ד:ה׳)
whether through converts like Rabbi Meir from the seed of Nero (Gittin 56a), surnameing themselves by Israel;
אוֹ עַל יְדֵי הַרְבֵּה דְּרָכִים אֲחֵרִים לַמָּקוֹם, כִּידוּעַ לַמַּשְׂכִּילִים עַל דֶּרֶךְ אֱמֶת
or through the numerous hidden ways of the Omnipresent, known to esoteric masters;
עַד עֵת קֵץ שֶׁלֹּא יִשָּׁאֵר בּוֹ עוֹד שׁוּם חַיּוּת — יֹאבַד מִן הָעוֹלָם.
until at the End of Days, when no vitality remains in Esau, he perishes from the earth.
וְיִצְחָק, כְּשֶׁרָאָה שֶׁנַּעֲנָה בִּתְפִלָּתוֹ, יָדַע שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הִסְכִּים עִמּוֹ שֶׁיֵּהָפֵךְ הָרָע לְ״טוֹב מְאֹד״
And Isaac, seeing his prayer answered, knew Hashem consented to transform evil into "very good";
חָשַׁב שֶׁזֶּה בִּכְלַל זַרְעוֹ, וְלֹא טָעָה בְּעַצְמוּתוֹ, כִּי הוּא מִצְדּוֹ בֶּאֱמֶת כֵּן
he assuming this would unfold within his seed, which was true in principle;
רַק טָעָה בְּעֵשָׂו, כִּי קוֹדֶם קַבָּלַת הַבְּרָכוֹת לֹא נִתְבָּרַר עַדַיִין דָּבָר זֶה
erring only in Esau, for prior to the blessings this distinction was not yet manifest;
וְחָשַׁב שֶׁפֵּירוּד ״וּלְאֹם מִלְאֹם יֶאֱמָץ״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית כ״ה:כ״ג) הַיְינוּ: שֶׁיַּעֲקֹב כּוּלּוֹ טוֹב שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ שׁוּם רַע כְּלָל, וְהָרָע הַמִּתְהַפֵּךְ לְ״טוֹב מְאֹד״ — זֶהוּ בָּרָע דְּעֵשָׂו:
assuming "the one people shall be stronger than the other" (Bereishis 25:23) meant Jacob was pure good, while the evil transmuting into "very good" resided in Esau!
אוֹת כ״ז — יַעֲקֹב מֻבְחַר הָאָבוֹת בְּשֵׁם הֲוָיָ״ה, כְּהֵיוֹן עֵינָיו שֶׁל יִצְחָק, וְ״יִצְחָק מַחֲוֵי לְהוּ קֻדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא בְּעֵינַיְיהוּ״
Section 27: Jacob as the Choicest Patriarch in the Name Havayah, Isaac's Blindness, and Isaac Showing the Holy One

7.h: The theme: Jacob cleaved unto the ineffable Name Havayah, Isaac’s blindness as disembodiment from this world, and Isaac pointing out Hashem to the righteous. Jacob is the choicest of the Patriarchs (shebechar she-ba'Avot, Bereishis Rabbah 76:1), cleaved directly unto the attribute of Truth (Emet l'Yaakov) and the Tetragrammaton (Havayah)—the essential Name transcending El and Elohim (the attributes of Abraham and Isaac, which are divine designations). Being pure good, Jacob did not need Isaac's special blessing. But Esau was the dross of Isaac's attribute of strict Judgment, drawn from his darkness and the dimming of his eyes at the Akeidah. Hashem "makes darkness His secret place" (Tehillim 18:12); "man shall not see Me and live" (Shemos 33:20)—unless he is blind, who is accounted as dead (Nedarim 64b). Isaac represents Fear (Yir'ah), sharing the letters of Vision (Re'iyah). From his contraction (tzimtzum) flows the supreme capacity of spiritual vision in greeting the Shechinah, as in Shabbat (89b) where Isaac points out the Holy One directly unto their eyes ("Isaac shows them the Holy One with their eyes")! To attain this spiritual vision, he had to become blind to the physical sights of this world.

p: וְנוֹדַע שֶׁיַּעֲקֹב מֻבְחָר שֶׁבָּאָבוֹת (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה ע״ו:א׳), וְהוּא דָּבוּק בְּמִדָּה בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָהּ מִמִּדּוֹתָיו שֶׁל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, וְהוּא מִדַּת ״אֱמֶת לְיַעֲקֹב״ (מִיכָה ז:כ)
And it is known that Jacob is the choicest of the Patriarchs (Bereishis Rabbah 76:1), cleaved unto an independent attribute of Hashem: "Truth unto Jacob" (Michah 7:20);

וְגָדוֹל מִמֶּנּוּ [מִיִּצְחָק], כִּי הוּא דָּבוּק בְּשֵׁם הֲוָיָ״ה שֶׁהוּא שֵׁם הָעֶצֶם הַמְיוּחָד שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה מִשְּׁאָר הַשֵּׁמוֹת: דְּ״אֵל״ וְ״אֱלֹהִים״ מִדַּת אַבְרָהָם וְיִצְחָק, שֶׁהֵם רַק כִּינּוּיִים
being greater than Isaac, cleaved unto the Name Havayah—the essential Name transcending El and Elohim of Abraham and Isaac which are designations;
