וּמֵאַחַר שֶׁכּוּלּוֹ טוֹב וּמָלֵא קְדוּשָׁה, אֵין צָרִיךְ לְאַהֲבָתוֹ וְקִרְבָתוֹ וּבִרְכָתוֹ.
and since Jacob was pure good and full of holiness, he did not require Isaac's drawn-down blessing.
אַךְ עֵשָׂו יָדַע שֶׁהוּא הַפְּסֹולֶת דְּמִדָּתוֹ, וְנִמְשָׁךְ מִן הַחֹשֶׁךְ שֶׁלּוֹ וּכְהֵיוֹן עֵינָיו שֶׁהָיָה עַל יְדֵי רְאִיַּית פְּנֵי הַשְּׁכִינָה בָּעֲקֵידָה
But Esau, Isaac knew, was the dross of his own attribute of Judgment, drawn from his darkness and the dimming of his eyes at the Akeidah;
כִּי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ: ״יָשֶׁת חֹשֶׁךְ סִתְרוֹ״ (תְּהִלִּים י״ח:י״ב), וְ״לֹא יִרְאַנִי הָאָדָם וָחָי״ (שְׁמוֹת ל״ג:כ׳), אִם לֹא הַסּוּמָא הֶחָשׁוּב כְּמֵת (נְדָרִים ס״ד עַמּוּד ב׳).
for Hashem "makes darkness His secret place" (Tehillim 18:12), and "man shall not see Me and live" (Shemos 33:20)—unless he is blind, who is accounted as dead (Nedarim 64b).
וּלְפִי שֶׁיִּצְחָק הוּא מִדַּת הַיִּרְאָה — אוֹתִיּוֹת ״רְאִיָּה״ — שֶׁהוּא מִצַּד מִדָּתוֹ מִדַּת הַצִּמְצוּם
And because Isaac is Fear (Yir'ah), sharing the letters of Vision (Re'iyah), which through contraction yields the power of spiritual sight;
הוּא כֹּחַ הָרְאִיָּה בְּהַקְבָּלַת פְּנֵי הַשְּׁכִינָה, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּשַׁבָּת (פ״ט עַמּוּד ב׳): ״דְּמַחְוֵי לְהוּ יִצְחָק הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בְּעֵינַיְיהוּ״
the power of vision to behold the Shechinah, as in Shabbat (89b): "Isaac shows them the Holy One directly unto their eyes";
שֶׁזֶּהוּ מִצַּד מַדְרֵיגָתוֹ, לָכֵן הוּצְרַךְ לְהִסְתַּמֵּא מֵחֵיזוּ דְּהַאי עָלְמָא, וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה זָכָה לִרְאִיָּה בְּרוּחָנִיּוּת:
wherefore he had to become blind to worldly sights, meriting through this transcendent spiritual vision!

7.h: אוֹת כ״ח — ״כִּי צַיִד בְּפִיו״, הַכָּרַת הַלֵּב, ״כּוֹפִין אוֹתוֹ עַד שֶׁיֹּאמַר רוֹצֶה אָנִי״, וְהַהַמְשָׁכָה מֵהַפֶּה לַלֵּב — Section 28: "Game Was in His Mouth", The Heart's Inward Intention, Coercion unto Willingness, and Drawing the Mouth to the Heart

The theme: Isaac perceiving Esau's heart, loving him to draw his darkness into holy light, and the mouth's profession awakening the heart. "Man looks on the outward appearance, but Hashem looks on the heart" (I Shmuel 16:7). When Isaac's physical eyes dimmed, he saw into the inward heart, knowing that Esau's trapping was purely in his mouth: "for game was in his mouth" (ki tzayid b'fiv, Bereishis 25:28)—meaning his righteousness was merely verbal while his heart was far removed. Yet Isaac loved him precisely because he recognized Esau as the dross of his own Gevurah, whose darkness could be transformed into "very good" if drawn back to its source. Esau sought at least to mimic righteousness externally with his mouth. In Israel, verbal profession is powerful: "they flattered Him with their mouth... yet their heart was not right with Him; but He, being full of compassion, forgave their iniquity" (Tehillim 78:36–38). Rambam (Hilchos Gerushin 2:20) explains regarding coercing a husband to divorce: we compel him until he says "I am willing," for in the depths of his Jewish heart he desires to fulfill the mitzvot, his refusal stemming merely from the yetzer. "The lips of the righteous know what is acceptable" (Mishlei 10:32): holy speech (sefat tzaddik) awakens and draws authentic willingness into the heart. Isaac assumed Esau was like this: seeing that Esau flattered with his mouth, Isaac loved him to draw him back unto his holy root!

p: וְהִנֵּה: ״הָאָדָם יִרְאֶה לַעֵינַיִם, וַה׳ יִרְאֶה לַלֵּבָב״ (שְׁמוּאֵל א ט״ז:ז׳)
And behold: "for man looks on the outward appearance, but Hashem looks on the heart" (I Shmuel 16:7);
וְאָז כְּשֶׁכָּהוּ עֵינָיו הַגַּשְׁמִיִּים מִפְּנֵי הָרְאִיָּה הָרוּחָנִית, מִסְּתָמָא גַּם הוּא הָיָה יָכוֹל לִרְאוֹת לַלֵּבָב
and when Isaac's physical eyes dimmed before spiritual vision, he likewise was able to see into the inward heart;
וְהִכִּיר יָפֶה אֶת עֵשָׂו, דְּעַל כֵּן נֶאֱמַר: ״כִּי צַיִד בְּפִיו״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית כ״ה:כ״ח)
and recognized Esau thoroughly, wherefore it is written: "because he did eat of his venison [game was in his mouth]" (Bereishis 25:28);
רָצָה לוֹמַר: שֶׁהוּא יָדַע זֶה דְּצֵידוֹ רַק בְּפִיו, וְלִבּוֹ בַּל עִמּוֹ כְּלָל.
meaning: Isaac knew that Esau's righteous trapping was merely in his mouth, while his heart was not with him at all.
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם מִפְּנֵי זֶה אֲהֵבוֹ, כִּי הִרְגִּישׁ בָּזֶה שֶׁהוּא הַפְּסֹולֶת שֶׁל מִדָּתוֹ
And nevertheless for this very reason Isaac loved him, sensing that Esau was the dross of his own Gevurah;
שֶׁמִּמֶּנּוּ נִמְשָׁךְ הַחֹשֶׁךְ הַגָּמוּר דְּ״מַחְשִׁיךְ אַנְפֵּי בִּרְיָין״, וְיוּכַל לְהִתְהַפֵּךְ לְ״טוֹב מְאֹד״ כְּשֶׁיִּתְגַּלֶּה סִתְרוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁבְּתוֹךְ חֹשֶׁךְ זֶה
whence issues absolute darkness, which could be transmuted into "very good" when Hashem's hidden light within that darkness is revealed;
וְעַל כֵּן אֲהֵבוֹ: שֶׁבְּאַהֲבָה זוֹ שֶׁיִּתְקָרֵב אֵלָיו בְּהִתְקָרְבוּת, יִגְרוֹם בָּזֶה שֶׁיָּשׁוּב לוֹ לִמְקוֹרוֹ שֶׁהוּא מְקוֹר הַקְּדוּשָׁה
wherefore he loved him: that through this love, drawing Esau near, he would cause him to return to his source of holiness;
וְזֶה עַל יְדֵי שֶׁ״צַיִד בְּפִיו״, שֶׁרָאָה שֶׁרוֹצֶה עַל כָּל פָּנִים לְהִתְדַּמּוֹת לְפָנִים וּלְמַרְאִית עַיִן לְטוֹב.
through "game in his mouth," seeing that Esau at least desired to mimic the good externally.
וּבְיִשְׂרָאֵל גַּם דָּבָר זֶה טוֹב, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ: ״וַיְפַתּוּהוּ בְּפִיהֶם, וּבִלְשׁוֹנָם יְכַזְּבוּ לוֹ, וְלִבָּם לֹא נָכוֹן עִמּוֹ... וְהוּא רַחוּם יְכַפֵּר עָוֹן״ (תְּהִלִּים ע״ח:ל״ו–ל״ח)

And in Israel even this verbal profession is valued: "they flattered Him with their mouth, and lied unto Him with their tongue; for their heart was not right with Him... but He, being full of compassion, forgives iniquity" (Tehillim 78:36–38).
וְכִידוּעַ דִּבְרֵי הָרַמְבַּ״ם (פֶּרֶק ב׳ מֵהִלְכוֹת גֵּירוּשִׁין הֲלָכָה כ׳) בְּטַעַם ״כּוֹפִין אוֹתוֹ עַד שֶׁיֹּאמַר: ׳רוֹצֶה אָנִי׳״
And as known from Rambam (Hilchos Gerushin 2:20) on why we compel a man until he says "I am willing";
דְּמַה שֶּׁבַּלֵּב אֵין רוֹצֶה רַק מִצַּד הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע
for that his heart refuses is merely from the instigation of the yetzer hara;
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: ״שִׂפְתֵי צַדִּיק — יֵדְעוּן רָצוֹן״ (מִשְׁלֵי י:לב)
concerning which it is said: "The lips of the righteous know what is acceptable" (Mishlei 10:32);
וְקִבַּלְתִּי הַפֵּירוּשׁ: דְּגַם כְּשֶׁרוֹאֶה שֶׁאֵין רְצוֹן לִבּוֹ עַדַיִין לָזֶה, הַדִּבּוּר בַּפֶּה לְטוֹב שֶׁנִּקְרָא ״שִׂפְתֵי צַדִּיק״ — מוֹעִיל לְלַמֵּד וּלְהַמְשִׁיךְ רָצוֹן לַלֵּב גַּם כֵּן
and I received by tradition: even when the heart does not yet will it, holy speech of the lips (sefat tzaddik) avails to awaken and draw divine willingness into the heart as well.
וְחָשַׁב יִצְחָק גַּם עֵשָׂו כֵּן: מֵאַחַר שֶׁרָאָהוּ עַל כָּל פָּנִים מְפַתֶּה בַּפֶּה, עַל זֶה אֲהֵבוֹ — לְהַמְשִׁיכוֹ אֵלָיו לִמְקוֹרוֹ:
And Isaac assumed Esau was like this: seeing him flatter with his mouth, Isaac loved him to draw him back unto his holy root!

7.h: אוֹת כ״ט — ״וְיִתֶּן לְךָ הָאֱלֹהִים״, נְגִיעַת שַׂר עֵשָׂו בְּכַף יְרֵכוֹ, וְאוֹר הַצִּיצִית הַמְסַמֵּא אֶת הָעַמִּים — Section 29: "God Give You", The Angel Striking the Thigh, and Tzitzit Subduing the Nations

The theme: The blessings of Isaac transferring the power of transforming evil into "very good" unto Jacob, the angel striking Jacob's descendants, and Tzitzit commanding foreign reverence. Isaac sought to bless Esau: "God give you" (ve-yiten lecha ha-Elohim, Bereishis 27:28)—which the Sages expound: "May He give you His Godliness" (Bereishis Rabbah 66:3). Hashem orchestrated that Jacob receive these blessings of transmuting evil into "very good," a power rooted in Isaac's Gevurah. Isaac would never have bestowed this blessing upon Jacob directly, viewing Jacob as pure good who had already separated from evil. When the angelic prince of Esau wrestled with Jacob, he could inject no evil into Jacob's personal soul; he touched merely the hollow of his thigh—symbolizing the future generations of his offspring. When the sun rose, Jacob was healed from his limping (Bereishis 32:32), for Hashem will gather the lame and cast off (Michah 4:6) when darkness turns to light. This sun rises specifically for Israel: "for darkness shall cover the earth... but Hashem shall arise upon you" (Yeshayah 60:2), that blinding light blinding the nations. The remnant of the nations will survive to serve Israel: "strangers shall stand and feed your flocks" (Yeshayah 61:5)—which Shabbat (32b) states is the reward for Tzitzit, the blue thread of Techelet manifesting the awe of Isaac. Through this fear of God, reverence falls upon the nations ("and all the peoples of the earth shall see that you are called by the name of Hashem, and they shall be afraid of you", Devarim 28:10), serving Israel for whose service the cosmos was created!

p: וְכֵן רָצָה לְבָרְכוֹ שֶׁיִּתְהַפֵּךְ אָז גַּם לִבּוֹ לְטוֹב, דְּעַל זֶה אָמַר: ״וְיִתֶּן לְךָ הָאֱלֹהִים״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית כ״ז:כ״ח), שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה ס״ו:ג׳): ״יִתֶּן לְךָ אֱלֹהוּתוֹ״
And so Isaac sought to bless him that his heart be transformed unto good, declaring: "God give you" (Bereishis 27:28)—expounded: "May He give you His Godliness".
וְהַכֹּל מֵאֵת ה׳: שֶׁיְּקַבֵּל יַעֲקֹב הַבְּרָכוֹת שֶׁל הִתְהַפְּכוּת הָרָע לְ״טוֹב מְאֹד״, שֶׁדָּבָר זֶה עִיקָּרוֹ מִכֹּחַ יִצְחָק
And all was from Hashem: that Jacob receive the blessings of transforming evil into "very good," which derives from the power of Isaac;
וְהוּא לֹא הָיָה מְבָרֵךְ לְיַעֲקֹב בָּזֶה, שֶׁרְאָהוּ טוֹב גָּמוּר וּבָא לְתַקֵּן חֵטְא אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן, וְחָשַׁב שֶׁאֵין מְצִיאוּת לְרַע אֶצְלוֹ עוֹד כְּלָל
for Isaac would not have blessed Jacob with this, viewing him as pure good who needed no transformation of evil.

וְהָאֱמֶת כֵּן הָיָה, כִּי שָׂרוֹ שֶׁל עֵשָׂו שֶׁהוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ הָרָע כְּשֶׁנֶּאֱבַק עִמּוֹ (בְּרֵאשִׁית ל״ב:כ״ה), לֹא יָכֹל לוֹ לְהַכְנִיס בּוֹ שׁוּם דָּבָר רָע, כִּי הוּא כְּבָר נִבְדָּל מֵהָרָע לְגַמְרֵי
And in truth it was so: for the prince of Esau, the root of evil, when wrestling with Jacob could inject no evil into him, Jacob being separated from evil entirely;
אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם נָגַע בְּכַף יְרֵכוֹ (שָׁם:כ״ו) — הַיְינוּ בַּדּוֹרוֹת יוֹצְאֵי יְרֵכוֹ, שֶׁבָּהֶם יֵשׁ אֲחִיזַת רַע
yet touched the hollow of his thigh (ibid. 32:26)—meaning in future generations issuing from his thigh where evil has a grip;
אֲבָל גַּם זֶה בִּנְגִיעָה בְּעָלְמָא, וּכְשֶׁזָּרַח לוֹ הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ נִתְרַפָּא מִצַּלְעָתוֹ (שָׁם:ל״ב; חֻלִּין צ״א עַמּוּד ב׳)
yet this was merely an external touch, and when the sun rose he was healed of his limping (Chullin 91b);
דְּסוֹף הַכֹּל: ״[בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא נְאֻם ה׳ אֹסְפָה] הַצֹּלֵעָה, וְהַנִּדָּחָה אֲקַבֵּצָה״ (מִיכָה ד:ו), כְּשֶׁיִּתְהַפֵּךְ חֲשׁוֹכָא לִנְהוֹרָא
for in the end: "I will assemble her that limps, and I will gather her that is driven away" (Michah 4:6), when darkness turns to light.
אֲבָל זְרִיחָה זוֹ הוּא לוֹ דַּוְוקָא, דִּלְכָל הָאוּמּוֹת אַדְּרַבָּא אָז חָפֵי חֲשׁוֹכָא: ״[כִּי הִנֵּה] הַחֹשֶׁךְ יְכַסֶּה אֶרֶץ... וְעָלַיִךְ יִזְרַח ה׳״ (יְשַׁעְיָה ס:ב)
But this sunrise is specifically for Israel, while over the nations darkness covers: "For behold, the darkness shall cover the earth... but Hashem shall arise upon you" (Yeshayah 60:2);
כִּי אוֹר זֶה הַגָּדוֹל הוּא מְסַמֵּא אֶת עֵינֵיהֶם הַתְּרוּטוֹת, וְעַל כֵּן אוֹר זֶה נֶהְפַּךְ לָהֶם לְחֹשֶׁךְ
for this transcendent light blinds their flawed eyes, turning into darkness for them;
וְהוּא לְתוֹעֶלֶת לָהֶם, לְאוֹתָם הַנִּשְׁאָרִים מֵהָאוּמּוֹת שֶׁלֹּא יֹאבְדוּ לְגַמְרֵי: כִּי יִשָּׁאֲרוּ מֵהֶם עֲבָדִים לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
which is for their benefit, that a surviving remnant endure as servants unto Israel;
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְעָמְדוּ זָרִים [וְרָעוּ צֹאנְכֶם, וּבְנֵי נֵכָר] אִכָּרֵיכֶם וְכֹרְמֵיכֶם״ (שָׁם ס״א:ה׳), וְהוּא בִּשְׂכַר מִצְוַת צִיצִית, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּשַׁבָּת (ל״ב עַמּוּד ב׳)
as it is said: "And strangers shall stand and feed your flocks, and the sons of the alien shall be your plowmen and your vinedressers" (ibid. 61:5), which is the reward of Tzitzit (Shabbat 32b);
הַיְינוּ לְבוּשׁ שֶׁל יִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם, כִּידוּעַ דְּחוּט שֶׁל תְּכֵלֶת הוּא גַּוֶּון מִדַּת יִצְחָק אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
this being the garment of the fear of Heaven, the blue thread of Techelet manifesting the attribute of Isaac;
וּמִצִּדּוֹ הוּא בִּרְכַּת: ״יַעַבְדוּךָ עַמִּים״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית כ״ז:כ״ט), עַל יְדֵי יִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם יִהְיֶה מוֹרָאוֹ עַל הָאוּמּוֹת.
whence flows the blessing: "Let people serve you" (Bereishis 27:29), the fear of God casting dread upon the nations!
אוֹת ל׳ — ״הֱוֵה גְבִיר לְאַחֶיךָ״ בְּמַעֲלַת בַּעֲלֵי תְּשׁוּבָה, לְבוּשׁוֹ שֶׁל עֵשָׂו בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל, וּכְפִיַּית הַר כְּגִיגִית בִּפְנִימִיּוּת הָרָצוֹן
Section 30: "Be Lord Over Your Brethren", The Garments of Esau on Jewish Transgressors, and Coercing the Mount Sinai Will

The theme: "Be lord over your brethren" addressing the ba'al teshuvah, Jewish sins existing merely as an outer garment, and the internal willingness of Israel at Mount Sinai. Isaac blessed: "Be lord (gvir) over your brethren, and let your mother's sons bow down to you" (Bereishis 27:29). Thinking he blessed Esau, Isaac assumed Esau would become a ba'al teshuvah; and in the place where ba'alei teshuvah stand, even consummate tzaddikim cannot stand (Berachos 34b). The term gvir denotes overcoming the yetzer with greater might (gevurah), wherefore tzaddikim bow before the ba'al teshuvah out of holy awe. In this blessing, Isaac did not say "let your brethren serve you," for Jacob would never be a slave; bowing denotes self-nullification (bittul) before the supernal light. But when Isaac recounted the blessings to Esau, he said: "Behold, I have made him your lord, and all his brethren have I given to him for servants" (Bereishis 27:37). Once he realized he blessed Jacob, he understood these blessings apply to Jacob when clothed in Esau’s garments: even when an Israelite appears wicked, his sin is merely an external garment (levush)! In the depths of the Jewish heart it is revealed: "It is our will to do Your will, but the leaven in the dough and subjugation of empires withhold us" (Berachos 17a). The leaven and foreign empires are briars surrounding the rose, but the inward heart is cleaved unto Hashem: "God is the rock of my heart" (Tehillim 73:26). Isaac smelled Jacob's garments (begadav)—expounded as his traitors (bogedav, Sanhedrin 37a)—smelling "the smell of a field which Hashem has blessed" (Bereishis 27:27): an apple orchard where fruit precedes leaves, mirroring Israel putting Na'aseh before Nishma (Shabbat 88a)! All Jewish generations stood at Sinai, even transgressors; for them the mountain was coerced like a cask (k'feeyat har k'gigit)—coercing him until he says "I am willing," because in his inward depths he truly desires it. For the nations, their good is merely an external pretense while their inward will rejects Hashem; therefore Hashem never coerced the nations, but coerced Israel whose innermost will yearned for His service!
וְאָמַר לוֹ: ״הֱוֵה גְבִיר לְאַחֶיךָ, [וְיִשְׁתַּחֲווּ לְךָ בְּנֵי אִמֶּךָ]״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית כ״ז:כ״ט), כְּפִי מַחֲשַׁבְתּוֹ שֶׁהוּא עֵשָׂו
And Isaac said unto him: "Be lord over your brethren, and let your mother's sons bow down to you" (Bereishis 27:29), according to his thought that he was blessing Esau;
הַיְינוּ שֶׁיִּתְהַפֵּךְ לְ״טוֹב מְאֹד״, וְיִהְיֶה גָּדוֹל בָּזֶה מִיַּעֲקֹב, דִּ״בִמְקוֹם שֶׁבַּעֲלֵי תְּשׁוּבָה עוֹמְדִין [אֵין צַדִּיקִים גְּמוּרִים יְכוֹלִין לַעֲמוֹד]״ (בְּרָכוֹת ל״ד עַמּוּד ב׳)
meaning that Esau would turn into "very good," surpassing Jacob: for "in the place where penitents stand, consummate tzaddikim cannot stand" (Berachos 34b).
וְזֶהוּ טַעַם לְשׁוֹן ״גְּבִיר״: רָצָה לוֹמַר שֶׁהוּא יִהְיֶה בְּהִתְגַּבְּרוּת יוֹתֵר, כִּי בַּעַל תְּשׁוּבָה צָרִיךְ הִתְגַּבְּרוּת יוֹתֵר נֶגֶד הַיֵּצֶר
And this is the reason for the term "lord" (gvir): meaning he would possess greater might (gevurah), a ba'al teshuvah requiring greater exertion against the yetzer;

וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה יִהְיֶה מוֹרָאוֹ עָלָיו וְ״יִשְׁתַּחֲווּ וְכוּלֵיהּ״ גַּם כֵּן, כִּי הַבַּעַל תְּשׁוּבָה צָרִיךְ לִהְיוֹת דָּבוּק בְּמִדַּת הַיִּרְאָה בְּיוֹתֵר, וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה גַּם צַדִּיקִים גְּמוּרִים יְרֵאִים מִמֶּנּוּ.
through which awe falls upon others, tzaddikim revering the ba'al teshuvah who is cleaved unto supreme awe.

וְהִשְׁתַּחֲוָאָה הוּא בִּיטּוּל שֶׁמֵּחֲמַת יִרְאָה, וְלֹא אָמַר בִּבְרָכָה זוֹ ״וְיַעַבְדוּךָ״ גַּבֵּי אֶחָיו, כִּי הוּא חָשַׁב שֶׁמְּבָרֵךְ לְעֵשָׂו, וְלֹא עָלָה עַל דַּעְתּוֹ שֶׁיַּעֲקֹב יַעַבְדֶנּוּ חַס וְשָׁלוֹם
And bowing is self-nullification born of awe; Isaac not saying "let your brethren serve you," for he never imagined Jacob would be a slave, God forbid;
רַק לְפִי שֶׁכְּשֶׁמִּתְגַּלֶּה סִתְרוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁבַּחֹשֶׁךְ שֶׁהוּא אוֹר הַנֶּעלָם, הוּא גִּילּוּי אוֹר עֶלְיוֹן לְמַעְלָה מַעְלָה מֵאוֹר הַמּוּשָׂג
but when Hashem's hidden light in darkness is revealed, it is an illumination transcending ordinary light;
עַד שֶׁהוּא כְּאַיִן נֶגְדּוֹ, עַל זֶה שַׁיָּיךְ לְשׁוֹן ״הִשְׁתַּחֲוָאָה״ שֶׁהוּא הַבִּיטּוּל לִהְיוֹת כְּאַיִן וּכְעָפָר.
before which all is accounted as naught, whereunto applies "bowing"—the nullification into dust.
אַךְ כְּשֶׁחָזַר וְסִפֵּר הַבְּרָכוֹת לְעֵשָׂו אָמַר לוֹ: ״[הֵן גְּבִיר שַׂמְתִּיו לָךְ,] וְאֶת כָּל אֶחָיו נָתַתִּי לוֹ לַעֲבָדִים״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית כ״ז:ל״ז)
But when Isaac recounted the blessings unto Esau, he said: "Behold, I have made him your lord, and all his brethren have I given to him for servants" (Bereishis 27:37);
וְהִנֵּה לָשׁוֹן זֶה לֹא אָמַר בְּבִרְכָתוֹ כְּלָל עַל אֶחָיו, אֶלָּא עַל עַמִּים
which he had not stated in the original blessing regarding brethren, but regarding nations!
אַךְ כְּשֶׁנּוֹדַע לוֹ שֶׁבֵּירַךְ אֶת יַעֲקֹב, וְיָדַע שֶׁכָּל בְּרָכוֹת אֵלּוּ שַׁיָּיכִים לְיַעֲקֹב כְּשֶׁמִּתְלַבֵּשׁ בִּלְבוּשׁ דְּעֵשָׂו
But once Isaac knew he had blessed Jacob, he recognized that these blessings belong to Jacob when clothed in Esau's garments;
הַיְינוּ שֶׁנִּרְאָה גַּם כֵּן רַע, רַק אֶצְלוֹ הוּא עַל הַלְּבוּשׁ
meaning that Jacob's descendants might appear outwardly wicked, yet with them evil is merely an external garment;
כִּי מַעֲמַקֵּי הַלֵּב: ״גָּלוּי וְיָדוּעַ לְפָנֶיךָ שֶׁרְצוֹנֵנוּ לַעֲשׂוֹת רְצוֹנָךְ, וּמִי מְעַכֵּב? — שְׂאוֹר שֶׁבָּעִיסָה וְשִׁעְבּוּד מַלְכִיּוֹת״ (בְּרָכוֹת י״ז עַמּוּד א׳)

for in the inward depths of the heart: "It is revealed and known before You that our true will is to do Your will; and what withholds us? The leaven in the dough and subjugation of empires" (Berachos 17a);
שֶׁהֵם הַחוֹחִים הַסּוֹבְבִים לַשּׁוֹשַׁנָּה וּמַלְבִּישִׁים אוֹתָהּ: זֶה מִבַּחוּץ וְזֶה מִבִּפְנִים
these being the briars encircling the rose, clothing it from without and within.
אֲבָל הַכֹּל רַק לְבוּשׁ וְלֹא הָעַצְמִיּוּת שֶׁהוּא עֹומֶק לִבּוֹ
But all this is merely an outer garment, and not his essential inward heart;

שֶׁשָּׁם עִיקַּר חַיּוּת עַצְמִיּוּתוֹ זֶה דָּבוּק בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ עַל פָּסוּק: ״צוּר לְבָבִי [וְחֶלְקִי אֱלֹהִים לְעוֹלָם]״ (תְּהִלִּים ע״ג:כ״ו) — ״שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לִבָּן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל״ (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה ה:ב).
where his vital essence is cleaved unto Hashem: "God is the rock of my heart" (Tehillim 73:26)—"the Holy One is the heart of Israel" (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 5:2).
וְיָדַע דְּאַף דְּיַעֲקֹב כּוּלּוֹ טוֹב, מִכָּל מָקוֹם יוּכַל לְהִתְלַבֵּשׁ עַדַיִין פְּעָמִים בִּלְבוּשׁ דְּעֵשָׂו
And Isaac knew that though Jacob was pure good, he could clothe himself at times in Esau's garb;
״וַיָּרַח אֶת רֵיחַ בְּגָדָיו״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית כ״ז:כ״ז), שֶׁהֵם הַלְּבוּשִׁים דְּעֵשָׂו, שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה: ״רֵיחַ בּוֹגְדָיו״ (סַנְהֶדְרִין ל״ז עַמּוּד א׳)
"and he smelled the smell of his raiment" (Bereishis 27:27)—the garments of Esau—expounded: "the smell of his traitors" (Sanhedrin 37a);
שֶׁהַפּוֹשְׁעִים דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל הֵם מִצַּד הַלְּבוּשִׁים דְּעֵשָׂו הַמַּלְבִּישִׁים אוֹתָם בִּשְׂאוֹר שֶׁבָּעִיסָה וְשִׁעְבּוּד מַלְכִיּוֹת.
the transgressors of Israel sinning merely through Esau's garments clothing them in the leaven of the dough and foreign subjugation.
וְרָאָה שֶׁגַּם הֵם מְרִיחִים ״כְּרֵיחַ שָׂדֶה [אֲשֶׁר בֵּרֲכוֹ ה׳]״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית שָׁם)
And Isaac perceived that even they smell "as the smell of a field which Hashem has blessed" (ibid.);
וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּשַׁבָּת (פ״ח עַמּוּד א׳): ״שְׂדֵה שֶׁל תַּפּוּחִין״
the Sages stating in Shabbat (88a): "a field of apples";
וְהוּא מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״מָה תַּפּוּחַ פִּרְיוֹ קוֹדֵם לְעָלָיו — כָּךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל הִקְדִּימוּ ׳נַעֲשֶׂה׳ לְ׳נִשְׁמַע׳״ (שָׁם)
expounding: "as the apple tree whose fruit precedes its leaves, so Israel put Na'aseh before Nishma" (ibid.);
וְזֶהוּ בְּמַעֲמַד הַר סִינַי שֶׁהָיוּ כָּל הַנְּפָשׁוֹת מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל כוּלָּם שֶׁבְּכָל הַדּוֹרוֹת וַאֲפִילּוּ הַפּוֹשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
this occurring at Sinai where all Jewish souls of all generations stood, even the transgressors;
וּבִשְׁבִילָם הוּצְרַךְ הַכְּפִיַּית הַר כְּגִיגִית, שֶׁהוּא הַכְּפִיָּה ״עַד שֶׁיֹּאמַר: ׳רוֹצֶה אָנִי׳״, דִּמְהַנֵּי כְּפִיָּה.
and for their sake was needed the coercion of the mountain like a cask, coercing him until he says "I am willing," where coercion is effective.
אַף דְּהוּא רַק בְּפִיהֶם וְלִבָּם לֹא נָכוֹן, זֶהוּ בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת הַלֵּב לְבַד וְלֹא בַּמַּעֲמַקִּים
For though their flattery was verbal and their conscious heart faltered, that was in the external heart alone and not in its profound depths.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בָּאוּמּוֹת הֵם בְּהֵיפוּךְ: שֶׁהַמְעַט טוֹב שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהֶם אֵינוֹ בְּעַצְמִיּוּת רַק דֶּרֶךְ לְבוּשׁ
Unlike the nations who are the reverse: the faint good within them is merely an external garment, not their essence;
וַאֲפִילּוּ מַה שֶּׁהוּא בַּלֵּב, עַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: ״לֹא יַחְפֹּץ כְּסִיל בִּתְבוּנָה, כִּי אִם בְּהִתְגַּלּוֹת לִבּוֹ״ (מִשְׁלֵי י״ח:ב׳)
and regarding their heart it is said: "A fool has no delight in understanding, but only that his heart may reveal itself" (Mishlei 18:2);
שֶׁהוּא חִיצוֹנִיּוּת הַלֵּב, לֹא שֶׁיִּכָּנֵס הַבִּינָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב לְמַעֲמַקָּיו, שֶׁאֵינוֹ רוֹצֶה בָּזֶה כְּלָל.
which is the superficial exterior, refusing to allow understanding to enter the inward depths.
וְעַל כֵּן לֹא כָּפָה לָאוּמּוֹת שֶׁלֹּא רָצוּ לְקַבֵּל הַתּוֹרָה, אֶלָּא לְיִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁהֵם רְצוֹנָם בְּכָךְ שֶׁיִּכְפֶּה אוֹתָם לַעֲבוֹדָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ
Wherefore Hashem did not coerce the nations who refused the Torah, coercing exclusively Israel whose inward will yearned to be compelled unto His service!
וְכֵן לֶעָתִיד אִם אֵין הַדּוֹר זַכַּאי, נֶאֱמַר: ״כִּי בְּיָד חֲזָקָה... אֶמְלוֹךְ עֲלֵיכֶם״ (יְחֶזְקֵאל כ:לג), וְהוּא כְּפֵירוּשׁ דְּמַתַּן תּוֹרָה
And so in the Future, if the generation lacks merit, it is said: "surely with a mighty hand... will I rule over you" (Yechezkel 20:33), exactly as expounded at Sinai;
וְאָנוּ מְקַוִּים וּמְצַפִּים לָזֶה: ״דְּכָל כִּי הַאי רִתְחָא — לִירְתַּח עֲלַן וְלִפְרוֹקִינַן!״ (סַנְהֶדְרִין ק״ה עַמּוּד א׳)
and we hope and yearn for this: "Let such holy wrath rage against us, so that He redeem us!" (Sanhedrin 105a);
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן הָאוּמּוֹת, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאִם כְּפָאוּם עַל כָּרְחָם הָיוּ מִתְרַצִּים, מִכָּל מָקוֹם הֵם לֹא רָצוּ זֶה שֶׁיִּכְפְּאוּם
unlike the nations, who even if coerced would have submitted, never desired to be coerced;
כִּי מַה שֶּׁלֹּא רָצוּ לְקַבֵּל הַתּוֹרָה הָיָה מִצַּד עֶצֶם רְצוֹנָם, שֶׁאֵין רוֹצִים לַעֲשׂוֹת רְצוֹנוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ כְּלָל, וְלֹא מִצַּד הַשְּׂאוֹר הַמַּסִּית כְּלָל:
their refusal to receive the Torah stemming from their very essence which rejects His will, and not from the external instigation of the leaven!

7.h: יִשְׂרָאֵל קְדוֹשִׁים — פֶּרֶק ז׳, סְעִיפִים ל״א–ל״ו

אוֹת ל״א — טַעֲנַת הָאוּמּוֹת בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה, חֶטְאוֹ שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל מִלְּבַר, וְהַשִּׂנְאָה שֶׁיָּרְדָה לָעוֹלָם — Section 31: The Nations' Claim in Avodah Zarah, Sin Merely External in Israel, and the Hatred Descended at Sinai

The theme: The nations' future claim regarding the coercion of the mountain, why compulsion cannot alter an uncircumcised heart, and the eternal separation between Israel and the nations descending at Sinai. In Avodah Zarah (2b), the nations of the world will claim in the Future: "Master of the Universe! Did You coerce the mountain over us like a cask as You did unto Israel?!" The Blessed Name replies to them: "Let them declare the former things" (Yeshayah 43:9)—meaning that even had He coerced them to accept the Torah, they would not have fulfilled it. If the inward heart is fundamentally unwilling, what value is there in external coercion where the lips declare "I am willing" while the heart rejects it? Such an acceptance is void: once the coercive pressure is lifted, the person returns to his true nature, refusing to fulfill the commandments. At the Giving of the Torah, hatred and destruction descended upon the nations of the world (Shabbat 89a), because Israel was permanently chosen as a distinct, separated people: "lo, the people shall dwell alone, and shall not be reckoned among the nations" (Bamidbar 23:9). Even those in Israel whose actions appear identical to the heathen are never reckoned among the nations, for "an Israelite, even though he has sinned, remains an Israelite" (Sanhedrin 44a), included within Israel in every respect. Through this absolute separation, all other nations were permanently rejected from this covenantal bond; whence issues their enduring hatred and destruction, having no spiritual connection with Israel. Hashem's eternal love is granted exclusively unto Jacob: "Was not Esau Jacob's brother? says Hashem; yet I loved Jacob, and I hated Esau" (Malachi 1:2–3)—Esau embodying the antithesis of Jacob once severed from him completely!

p: וּבַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה (ב׳ סוֹף עַמּוּד ב׳): ״דַּעֲתִידִים אוּמּוֹת [הָעוֹלָם] לִטְעוֹן: ׳כְּלוּם כָּפִיתָ עָלֵינוּ הַר כְּגִיגִית?!׳
And in Avodah Zarah (2b): "The nations of the world will in the Future argue: 'Did You coerce the mountain over us like a cask [as You did unto Israel]?!';
וְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מְשִׁיבָם: ״׳רִאשֹׁנוֹת יַשְׁמִיעֻנוּ׳ (יְשַׁעְיָה מ״ג:ט׳) וְכוּלֵיהּ״
and the Blessed Name answers them: "'let them declare the former things' (Yeshayah 43:9), etc.";
הַיְינוּ דְּגַם אִם כְּפָאָם לְקַבֵּל, לֹא הָיוּ מְקַיְּימִים
meaning that even had He coerced them to accept the Torah, they would not have fulfilled it;
דְּאִם הַלֵּב בֶּאֱמֶת אֵין רוֹצֶה, מַה תּוֹעֶלֶת בִּכְפִיָּה שֶׁיֹּאמַר: ״רוֹצֶה אָנִי״
for if the inward heart is genuinely unwilling, what value is there in coercion whereby his lips utter: "I am willing";
וְאָנוּ יוֹדְעִים דִּבְלִבּוֹ אֵין רוֹצֶה, וְאֵין זוֹ קַבָּלָה, לִכְשֶׁתָּסוּר הַכְּפִיָּה — לֹא יִרְצֶה וְלֹא יְקַיֵּים.
when we know that in his heart he does not desire it, this being no valid acceptance, for as soon as the pressure departs he will refuse and not fulfill!
וּמִמַּתַּן תּוֹרָה יָרְדָה שִׂנְאָה וְחוּרְבָּה לְאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּשַׁבָּת (פ״ט עַמּוּד א׳)
And from the Giving of the Torah hatred and destruction descended upon the nations of the world, as stated in Shabbat (89a);
הַיְינוּ דְּמִשֶּׁנִּבְחֲרוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל לְעַם בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ: דְּ״[הֶן עָם] לְבָדָד יִשְׁכֹּן, וּבַגּוֹיִם לֹא יִתְחַשָּׁב״ (בַּמִּדְבָּר כ״ג:ט׳)
meaning that once Israel was chosen as an exclusive people: "lo, the people shall dwell alone, and shall not be reckoned among the nations" (Bamidbar 23:9);
הַיְינוּ אֲפִילּוּ אוֹתָם הָרְאוּיִם לְהִתְדַּמּוֹת לַגּוֹיִם מִצַּד מַעֲשֵׂיהֶם, מִכָּל מָקוֹם לֹא יִתְחַשְּׁבוּ עִמָּהֶם
meaning that even those who appear similar to the heathen on account of their misdeeds are nevertheless not reckoned among them;
דְּ״אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁחָטָא — יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא״ (סַנְהֶדְרִין מ״ד עַמּוּד א׳), וְנֶחְשָׁב בִּכְלַל יִשְׂרָאֵל לְכָל דָּבָר.
for "an Israelite, even though he has sinned, remains an Israelite" (Sanhedrin 44a), accounted within Israel in every respect.
וְזֶהוּ הַבֵּירוּר וְהַהֶבְדֵּל הַגָּמוּר שֶׁבֵּין יִשְׂרָאֵל לָעַמִּים
And this is the definitive clarification and boundary separating Israel from the nations;
מִכָּל מָקוֹם נִדְחוּ עַל יְדֵי זֶה כָּל הָאוּמּוֹת מֵעַתָּה, שֶׁנִּפְרְדוּ לְגַמְרֵי, וְאֵין לָהֶם שַׁיָּיכוּת עוֹד עִמָּהֶם
through this all other nations being permanently distanced, severed completely, having no affinity with them;
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה הוּא הַשִּׂנְאָה וְהַחוּרְבָּה לָהֶם, מֵאַחַר שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם עוֹד שׁוּם חִיבּוּר עִם יִשְׂרָאֵל
and through this hatred and destruction descend upon them, possessing no connection with Israel;
כִּי אַהֲבַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא לְיַעֲקֹב, וְ״[וָאֹהַב אֶת יַעֲקֹב,] וְאֶת עֵשָׂו שָׂנֵאתִי״ (מַלְאָכִי א:ב–ג) כְּתִיב
for Hashem's eternal love is reserved solely for Jacob: "and I loved Jacob, and I hated Esau" (Malachi 1:2–3);
וְהַיְינוּ לְפִי שֶׁהוּא שׂוֹנֵא אֶת יַעֲקֹב אַחַר שֶׁנִּפְרַד מִמֶּנּוּ לְגַמְרֵי, וְהֵם ב׳ הֲפָכִים זֶה לָזֶה:
because Esau hates Jacob once severed from him, the two standing as irreconcilable opposites!

7.h: אוֹת ל״ב — גֵּיהִנָּם נִכְנְסָה עִם עֵשָׂו, רֵיחַ בּוֹגְדָיו שֶׁל זֶרַע יַעֲקֹב, וּ״כָל אֶחָיו נָתַתִּי לוֹ לַעֲבָדִים״ — Section 32: Gehinnom Entering with Esau, The Traitors of Jacob's Seed, and All Brethren Made Servants

The theme: The absolute severance between Jacob and Esau finalized through the blessings, Isaac perceiving the smoke of Gehinnom, and Esau grouped with the nations. Once Jacob received the blessings, the separation was finalized. At the sale of the birthright, the division occurred merely between the holy portion of Jacob and the evil of Esau. But a subtle lingering connection still remained between Esau and the future Jewish transgressors (posh'ei Yisrael); this connection accounted for Isaac's love, assuming that Esau, bearing the inborn title of an Israelite, belonged to the category of Jewish sinners who are worthy of blessing, unaware that the Holy One hated him. Only after Jacob received the blessings was it revealed that the fragrant scent of the field belonged exclusively to the traitors of Jacob's seed (bogedav, Sanhedrin 37a), whereas Esau possessed no kinship even with Jewish transgressors, being grouped with the heathen. Therefore, when Esau entered immediately following, Isaac perceived Gehinnom entering with him (Bereishis Rabbah 67:2)—not the first time he had entered, but now he was cast into Gehinnom entirely, having no future hope or connection to the title of Israel. Isaac told him: "Behold, I have made him your lord, and all his brethren have I given to him for servants" (Bereishis 27:37), for Esau was now subjugated under the blessing "let peoples serve you"!

p: וְאַחַר שֶׁקִּבֵּל יַעֲקֹב הַבְּרָכוֹת — אָז נִפְרַד לְגַמְרֵי
And after Jacob received the blessings, the severance became absolute;
כִּי בַּתְּחִלָּה בִּלְקִיחַת הַבְּכוֹרָה הָיָה הַפֵּירוּד רַק לְחֵלֶק הַטּוֹב שֶׁבְּיַעֲקֹב מִן הָרָע דְּעֵשָׂו
for initially at the acquisition of the birthright, the separation occurred merely between the good portion in Jacob and the evil in Esau;
אֲבָל עַדַיִין הָיָה לוֹ חִיבּוּר עִם הַפּוֹשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁבְּזֶרַע יַעֲקֹב
but there still lingered a connection between Esau and the transgressors of Israel within Jacob's seed;
וּמִצַּד הַזֶּה הָיָה אַהֲבַת יִצְחָק, שֶׁחָשַׁב שֶׁגַּם הוּא שֶׁהָיָה עָלָיו שֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא בִּכְלַל הַפּוֹשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל רָאוּי לִבְרָכָה
and from this perspective flowed Isaac's love, assuming that Esau, bearing the inborn title of Israel, was akin to Jewish sinners who are worthy of blessing;
וְלֹא יָדַע שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא שׂוֹנְאוֹ.
and Isaac did not know that the Holy One hated Esau.
עַד אַחַר קַבָּלַת יַעֲקֹב הַבְּרָכוֹת, שֶׁנִּתְבָּרַר שֶׁרַק הַבּוֹגְדִים שֶׁמִּזַּרְעוֹ הוּא שֶׁמְּרִיחִין כֵּן
Until after Jacob received the blessings, when it was clarified that only the traitors of his own seed smell as the fragrance of the blessed field;
וְאֵין לְעֵשָׂו יַחַס גַּם עִם הַפּוֹשְׁעִים שֶׁבְּזֶרַע יַעֲקֹב, כִּי הוּא בִּכְלַל כָּל הָאוּמּוֹת
and Esau bears no kinship even with the transgressors of Jacob's seed, being categorized among the heathen;
וְעַל כֵּן כְּשֶׁנִּכְנַס אַחַר כָּךְ עֵשָׂו, רָאָה שֶׁנִּכְנְסָה עִמּוֹ גֵּיהִנָּם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (רֵישׁ פָּרָשָׁה ס״ז:ב׳)
wherefore when Esau entered immediately following, Isaac perceived that Gehinnom entered with him (Bereishis Rabbah 67:2);
וְלֹא הַפַּעַם הָרִאשׁוֹן הוּא שֶׁנִּכְנַס אֶצְלוֹ, אֶלָּא שֶׁאָז נִדְחָה לְגֵיהִנָּם לְגַמְרֵי
and this was not the first time Esau had entered before him, but now he was cast into Gehinnom entirely;
כִּי נִתְבָּרַר שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ עוֹד תּוֹחֶלֶת וְאֵין לוֹ עוֹד שַׁיָּיכוּת לְשֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל וּלְפוֹשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
for it was clarified that no spiritual hope remained in him, having no further link to the name of Israel or its transgressors;
עַל כֵּן אָמַר לוֹ: ״[וְאֶת] כָּל אֶחָיו נָתַתִּי לוֹ לַעֲבָדִים״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית כ״ז:ל״ז), כִּי גַּם הוּא בִּכְלַל ״יַעַבְדוּךָ עַמִּים״ (שָׁם:כ״ט):
wherefore Isaac told him: "and all his brethren have I given to him for servants" (Bereishis 27:37), for Esau was now included under "let peoples serve you"!

7.h: אוֹת ל״ג — רֹאשׁוֹ שֶׁל עֵשָׂו בִּמְעָרַת הַמַּכְפֵּלָה, ״וְאֶת אָחִיךָ תַּעֲבֹד״, וּמַפַּלַת עֲמָלֵק בְּפָרְקוֹ עֹל — Section 33: Esau's Head in the Cave of Machpelah, Serving Jacob as Esau's Elevation, and Amalek's Collapse

The theme: Esau's head buried in the Cave of Machpelah, why Isaac said "all his brethren" regarding Esau's descendants, and Amalek as the embodiment of casting off the yoke. Isaac phrased his words with precision: "Behold, I have made him your lord (gvir)"—addressing Esau individually—yet regarding servitude he did not say "I have given you as a servant," for Esau retained a faint inborn connection as an apostate Israelite (Yisrael mumar). Because of this inborn connection, Esau merited that his severed head was buried within the Cave of Machpelah in the lap of Isaac (Sotah 13a; Pirkei d'Rabbi Eliezer ch. 39). "All his brethren" refers to Esau's descendants: nephews are termed brothers ("for we are brethren", Bereishis 13:8), and Esau’s offspring became gentile nations having no connection to Israel. When Isaac blessed Esau directly, he commanded: "and you shall serve your brother" (Bereishis 27:40)—innovating that Esau personally must serve Jacob. This servitude was the sole authentic blessing for Esau, the ultimate spiritual elevation of Esau and the nations existing when they are subjugated as servants unto Israel! "And it shall come to pass when you shall break loose, that you shall shake his yoke from off your neck" (ibid.): breaking loose (tarid) is their ultimate spiritual degradation (yeridah). The term ve-haya ("and it shall come to pass") denotes joy: although the Holy One does not rejoice over the fall of the nations (Megillah 10b), regarding Amalek (the seed of Esau) Scripture commands: "you shall blot out the remembrance of Amalek" (Devarim 25:19). Converts are never accepted from Amalek (Mekhilta, Beshalach §2), and as long as his seed exists, the Divine Name and Throne are incomplete (Rashi on Shemos 17:16); wherefore Hashem rejoices over his destruction. Esau’s desire to cast off Israel's yoke is rooted in the power of Amalek, which triggers his downfall!

p: וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם דָּיֵיק וְאָמַר: ״גְּבִיר שַׂמְתִּיו לָךְ״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית כ״ז:ל״ז) — לוֹ בְּיִחוּד, וְעַל הָעַבְדוּת לֹא אָמַר: ״אוֹתְךָ נָתַתִּי״
And nevertheless Isaac was precise, saying: "Behold, I have made him your lord" (Bereishis 27:37)—unto Esau individually; while regarding servitude he did not say: "I have given you as a servant";
כִּי עֵשָׂו שֶׁנִּקְרָא ״יִשְׂרָאֵל מוּמָר״ (קִדּוּשִׁין י״ח עַמּוּד א׳), הֲרֵי הָיָה לוֹ עַדַיִין קְצָת שַׁיָּיכוּת לְשֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל וּפוֹשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
for Esau being termed an "apostate Israelite" (Kiddushin 18a), still retained a subtle link to the name of Israel and its transgressors;
דְּעַל כֵּן זָכָה לִהְיוֹת רֹאשׁוֹ קָבוּר בִּמְעָרַת הַמַּכְפֵּלָה בְּעִיטְפֵיהּ דְּיִצְחָק (סוֹטָה י״ג עַמּוּד א׳)
wherefore he merited that his head was buried in the Cave of Machpelah within the lap of Isaac (Sotah 13a);
וּמַה שֶּׁכָּתַב אַחַר כָּךְ ״כָּל אֶחָיו״ לֹא קָאֵי עָלָיו עַצְמוֹ, דְּלָא שַׁיָּיךְ לְשׁוֹן ״כָּל״ עַל חַד
and what Isaac stated subsequently: "and all his brethren," does not refer to Esau himself, for the term "all" cannot apply to a single individual;
רַק רָצָה לוֹמַר עַל בָּנָיו, דִּבְנֵי אַחִים נִקְרָאִים ״אַחִים״, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּאַבְרָהָם וְלוֹט: ״[כִּי] אֲנָשִׁים אַחִים אֲנָחְנוּ״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית י״ג:ח׳)
but refers to Esau's sons, nephews being termed brothers: "for we are brethren" (Bereishis 13:8);
וְעַבְדוּת לֹא נִזְכַּר בַּבְּרָכָה עַל אֶחָיו רַק עַל עַמִּים, וּבָנָיו שַׁפִּיר הֵם בִּכְלַל כָּל הָעַמִּים וְאֵין לָהֶם שׁוּם שַׁיָּיכוּת לְשֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל עוֹד.
servitude not being mentioned in Jacob's blessing regarding brethren but regarding nations, and Esau's descendants became gentile nations without any link to Israel.
אֲבָל בְּבִרְכָתוֹ לְעֵשָׂו אָמַר לוֹ: ״וְאֶת אָחִיךָ תַּעֲבֹד״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית כ״ז:מ׳)
But in Isaac's blessing directly unto Esau he declared: "and you shall serve your brother" (Bereishis 27:40);
וְזֶה חִדֵּשׁ עַתָּה בְּבִרְכָתוֹ לוֹ שֶׁגַּם הוּא עַצְמוֹ יַעֲבוֹד
innovating in this blessing that Esau personally must serve Jacob;
וְזֶה לְבַד הוּא הַבְּרָכָה לוֹ, כִּי הִרְגִּישׁ שֶׁאֵין רָאוּי לִבְרָכָה מֵעַתָּה
this alone being the authentic blessing for him, Isaac sensing Esau was unworthy of independent blessing;
וְרַק מַה שֶּׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּרָאוֹ וְנוֹתֵן לוֹ חַיּוּת מַה שֶּׁרָאָה גַּם בּוֹ צֹרֶךְ בַּבְּרִיאָה וְלֹא לְהוֹסִיף עוֹד
granting merely what Hashem decreed for his physical sustainment;
וְעַל כֵּן מַה שֶּׁאָמַר תְּחִלָּה: ״הִנֵּה מִשְׁמַנֵּי [הָאָרֶץ יִהְיֶה מוֹשָׁבֶךָ]״ (שָׁם:ל״ט), אָמַר בִּלְשׁוֹן ״הִנֵּה״
wherefore he opened: "Behold, of the fat places of the earth shall be your dwelling" (ibid. 27:39), utilizing the term "behold" (hinei);
דְּמַשְׁמַע שֶׁזֶּה דָּבָר נָכוֹן וּמְזוּמָּן לְפָנָיו וְלֹא שֶׁהוּא בֵּירְכוֹ בָּזֶה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר לְיַעֲקֹב: ״וְיִתֶּן לְךָ״ (שָׁם:כ״ח)
implying that this was an existing natural reality and not an active blessing, unlike the blessing of Jacob: "So God give you" (ibid. 27:28);
רַק שֶׁסִּפֵּר לוֹ מַה שֶּׁרוֹאֶה בְּרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ מַה שֶּׁהוּא מוּכָן לוֹ מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
merely reporting through the Holy Spirit what was naturally prepared for him by Hashem.
וְהוּא בֵּירְכוֹ שֶׁיַּעֲבוֹד לְיַעֲקֹב, שֶׁזֶּהוּ תַּכְלִית שְׁלֵימוּת עֵשָׂו וְכָל הָאוּמּוֹת: כְּשֶׁיִּהְיוּ עֲבָדִים לְיִשְׂרָאֵל.
And Isaac blessed him that he serve Jacob, for this is the supreme elevation of Esau and the nations: when they are servants unto Israel.

וְ״רַק כַּאֲשֶׁר תָּרִיד״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית כ״ז:מ׳) — שֶׁתִּהְיֶה בְּתַכְלִית הַיְרִידָה, אָז: ״וּפָרַקְתָּ עֻלּוֹ [מֵעַל צַוָּארֶךָ]״ (שָׁם), שֶׁזֶּהוּ יְרִידָתְךָ, אֲבָל מַעֲלָתְךָ הוּא שֶׁתַּעַבְדֶנּוּ.

"And it shall come to pass when you shall break loose (tarid)" (Bereishis 27:40)—when you descend into ultimate degradation (yeridah)—then: "you shall shake his yoke from off your neck," this being your spiritual ruin, your elevation consisting solely in serving him.
וְאִיתָא עַל זֶה: ״וְהָיָה״ — שֶׁהוּא לְשׁוֹן שִׂמְחָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה ס״ז:ז׳)
And on this the Midrash notes: "and it shall come to pass" (ve-haya) denotes joy (Bereishis Rabbah 67:7);
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא שָׂמֵחַ בְּמַפַּלְתָּן שֶׁל רְשָׁעִים אֲפִילּוּ מֵאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם (מְגִלָּה י׳ עַמּוּד ב׳)
and although the Holy One does not rejoice over the fall of the wicked even among the nations (Megillah 10b);
הַיְינוּ שְׁאָר אוּמּוֹת, אֲבָל עֲמָלֵק מִזֶּרַע עֵשָׂו כְּתִיב בֵּיהּ: ״תִּמְחֶה [אֶת זֵכֶר עֲמָלֵק]״ (דְּבָרִים כ״ה:י״ט)
that applies unto other nations, whereas regarding Amalek of the seed of Esau it is written: "you shall blot out the remembrance of Amalek" (Devarim 25:19);
וַאֲפִילּוּ גֵּרִים אֵין מְקַבְּלִים מֵהֶם (מְכִילְתָּא בְּשַׁלַּח פָּרָשָׁה ב׳), וְכֵן לֶעָתִיד לֹא יִשָּׁאֵר מֵהֶם כְּלוּם
converts never being accepted from them (Mechilta, Beshalach §2), and in the Future nothing remaining of them;
דְּכָל זְמַן שֶׁיֵּשׁ מִזַּרְעוֹ בָּעוֹלָם — אֵין הַשֵּׁם שָׁלֵם וְאֵין הַכִּסֵּא שָׁלֵם (תַּנְחוּמָא כִּי תֵצֵא י״א), וַדַּאי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שָׂמֵחַ בְּמַפַּלְתּוֹ.
for as long as his seed exists in the world, the Name is not whole and the Throne is not whole (Tanchuma, Ki Teitzei §11), wherefore Hashem certainly rejoices over his demise.
וְשׁוֹרֶשׁ הַפְּרִיקַת עוֹל דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל מֵעָלָיו שֶׁבְּעֵשָׂו הוּא בְּכֹחַ עֲמָלֵק, וְזֶהוּ תַּכְלִית הַיְרִידָה שֶׁלּוֹ
And the root of casting off Israel's yoke in Esau resides in the power of Amalek, this being his ultimate spiritual ruin;
וּלְעוֹלָם מַפַּלַת עֲמָלֵק הוּא כַּאֲשֶׁר רוֹצֶה לִפְרוֹק עוֹל שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל מֵעָלָיו:
and the downfall of Amalek occurs perpetually whenever he attempts to shake off the yoke of Israel!

7.h: אוֹת ל״ד — שִׂמְחַת הַפּוּרִים, מַפַּלַת הָמָן בְּגַאֲוָתוֹ, וְתִיקּוּן אוֹתִיּוֹת הַשֵּׁם — Section 34: The Joy of Purim, Haman's Fall through Arrogance, and the Unification of the Divine Name

The theme: The opening of Megillah expounding "and it shall come to pass as Hashem rejoiced", Haman seeking to eradicate Israel, and the joy of the Divine Name restored to wholeness. This illuminates the joy of Purim. In Megillah (10b), the Gemara opens the Megillah reading with: "And it shall come to pass, that as Hashem rejoiced over you to do you good... so will Hashem rejoice over you to cause you to perish" (Devarim 28:63). The Gemara challenges: "Does the Holy One rejoice over the fall of the wicked?! Rather, He causes others to rejoice"—meaning He caused the enemies of Israel to rejoice. Why is this the prophetic opening for the miracle of Purim? The phrasing ve-haya denotes joy: while Hashem does not rejoice over Israel's fall, He causes their enemies to rejoice, because their joy triggers their own annihilation! Israel’s arch-enemy is the seed of Amalek; in Esther, "those who hated them" refers to Amalek, who rejoiced to cast off Israel's yoke completely. Because the existence of Israel is a crushing yoke upon Amalek (the Divine Name and Throne being incomplete as long as Amalek lives), Haman alone schemed to annihilate every Jewish soul. But in Amalek, every action rebounds upon his own head: at the height of his arrogance he plunges into the abyss! Haman was originally sold as a slave to Mordechai for a loaf of bread (Megillah 15b); when he rebelled to throw off that yoke, his ruin began. When he boasted to Zeresh and demanded the royal attire, he fell. When the wicked celebrate Israel’s downfall, the prophet proclaims: "Rejoice and be glad, O daughter of Edom... the cup also shall pass through unto you" (Eichah 4:21). The rejoicing of enemies brings the destruction of Amalek, whereby evil is abolished from Israel. Sins in Israel exist only because Amalek exists—Amalek being the root of the "leaven in the dough" that separates the first two letters of the Name (Yud-Hei, representing Hashem’s Wisdom and Understanding) from the final two letters (Vav-Hei, representing the wills of Israel, the Son and Daughter). Purim is the unification of the letters of the Divine Name, the reversal (ve-nahafoch hu) of the enemy's joy into eternal salvation!

p: וְזֶהוּ שִׂמְחַת יְמֵי הַפּוּרִים
And this is the profound joy of the days of Purim;
וְעַיֵּין שָׁם בִּמְגִלָּה (י׳ סוֹף עַמּוּד ב׳) בְּפֶתַח פִּתְחָא: ״׳וְהָיָה כַּאֲשֶׁר שָׂשׂ [ה׳ עֲלֵיכֶם לְהֵיטִיב אֶתְכֶם... כֵּן] יָשִׂישׂ [ה׳ עֲלֵיכֶם לְהַאֲבִיד אֶתְכֶם]׳ (דְּבָרִים כ״ח:ס״ג)

see Megillah (10b) where the Sage opens the reading of the Megillah with: "'And it shall come to pass, that as Hashem rejoiced over you to do you good... so will Hashem rejoice over you to cause you to perish' (Devarim 28:63);
וּמִי חָדֵי?! ...אֶלָּא: ׳לַאֲחֵרִים מֵשִׂישׂ׳״
and does the Holy One rejoice?! Rather: He causes others to rejoice";
עַיֵּין שָׁם בְּרַשִׁ״י: דְּאוֹיְבֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל שָׂמְחוּ
see Rashi there: that the enemies of Israel rejoiced;
וְלִכְאוֹרָה מַה פְּתִיחָה הוּא זֶה לְעִנְיַן הַמְּגִלָּה וְנֵס דְּפוּרִים?
and ostensibly what connection does this opening have to the Megillah and the miracle of Purim?
רַק מִשּׁוּם דְּשָׁם נַמֵּי ״וְהָיָה״ — לְשׁוֹן שִׂמְחָה
Rather, because there too "and it shall come to pass" (ve-haya) denotes joy;
לוֹמַר: שֶׁאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שָׂמֵחַ בְּמַפַּלְתָּן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, בָּזֶה הוּא שָׂמֵחַ: בַּמַּה שֶּׁמֵּשִׂישׂ עַל יְדֵי זֶה אוֹיְבֵיהֶם
teaching that while Hashem never rejoices over Israel's fall, He rejoices in causing their enemies to rejoice;
וְעִיקַּר אוֹיְבֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הֵם זֶרַע עֲמָלֵק, וּבִמְגִלַּת אֶסְתֵּר שֶׁכָּתוּב סְתָם: ״וְהָרֹג בְּשֹׂנְאֵיהֶם״ (אֶסְתֵּר ט:ה), הַכַּוָּונָה עַל עֲמָלֵק
for the primary enemies of Israel are the seed of Amalek: "and slew of their foes" (Esther 9:5) referring specifically to Amalek;
וְהֵם הֵם שֶׁהָיוּ שְׂמֵחִים לִפְרוֹק עוֹל יִשְׂרָאֵל מֵעֲלֵיהֶם לְגַמְרֵי.
they being the ones who rejoiced to cast off the yoke of Israel entirely.
כִּי מַה שֶּׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל נִמְצָאִים בָּעוֹלָם, זֶהוּ גַּם כֵּן לְעוֹל עַל עֲמָלֵק
For Israel's existence in the world is a heavy yoke upon Amalek;
כְּמוֹ שֶׁמְּצִיאוּת עֲמָלֵק הוּא לְעוֹל עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁהֲרֵי עַל יְדֵי זֶה אֵין הַשֵּׁם וְהַכִּסֵּא שָׁלֵם, כָּךְ בְּהֵיפוּךְ לָהֶם, כִּי הֵם ״זֶה לְעֻמַּת זֶה״ (קֹהֶלֶת ז:יד)
just as Amalek's existence is a burden upon Israel, the Name and Throne being incomplete; and so in reverse unto them, being polar opposites;
וְעַל כֵּן לֹא הָיָה מִי שֶׁחָשַׁב וְגָזַר לְאַבֵּד לְגַמְרֵי כָּל זֶרַע יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶלָּא הָמָן שֶׁמִּזֶּרַע עֲמָלֵק
wherefore none plotted to totally destroy all the seed of Israel save Haman of the seed of Amalek;
שֶׁכְּמוֹ שֶׁהַמִּצְוָה לִמְחוֹת שְׁמוֹ וְזִכְרוֹ לְגַמְרֵי מִן הָעוֹלָם, כָּךְ חָשַׁב הוּא לְהֵיפֶךְ, וּמַחֲשַׁבְתּוֹ נֶהֶפְכָה עַל רֹאשׁוֹ
for just as the mitzvah is to blot out his memory from the earth, so he plotted the reverse, his scheme rebounding upon his own head;

כִּי כָּךְ עִנְיַן עֲמָלֵק: לִהְיוֹת כָּל פְּעֻלּוֹתָיו נֶהְפָּכִים עָלָיו, וְכַאֲשֶׁר הוּא בְּתַכְלִית הַגַּאֲוָה — הוּא בְּתַכְלִית הַיְרִידָה וְהַשִּׁפְלוּת, וְכָל מַעֲלָתוֹ הוּא כְּשֶׁיִּהְיֶה עֶבֶד לְאֶחָיו.
for such is the destiny of Amalek: all his deeds turning against him, and when at the zenith of arrogance he plunges into deepest degradation, his sole elevation being a slave unto his brother.
וְהָמָן, כְּשֶׁהָיָה תְּחִלָּה ״עַבְדָּא דְּמִזְדַּבַּן בְּטֻלְמֵי״ [בְּכִכַּר לֶחֶם] לְמָרְדֳּכַי (מְגִלָּה ט״ו עַמּוּד ב׳), אָז הָיָה בִּשְׁלֵימוּת מַעֲלָתוֹ
And Haman, when he was originally sold as a slave for a loaf of bread unto Mordechai (Megillah 15b), was in his proper elevation;
וּכְשֶׁהִתְחִיל לְהִתְגָּאוֹת וְלִפְרוֹק עוֹל יִשְׂרָאֵל — הִתְחִילָה יְרִידָתוֹ
and when he grew arrogant and sought to shake off the yoke of Israel, his ruin began;
וְכָל מַה שֶּׁנִּתְגָּאָה יוֹתֵר כְּפִי הַשָּׁעָה הַמְשַׂחֶקֶת לוֹ, עַל הָאֱמֶת הָיָה לוֹ יְרִידָה יוֹתֵר
and the more he boasted in his temporary triumph, the deeper his actual descent;
וּכְמוֹ בִּתְכְלִית גְּאוֹנוֹ שֶׁהִתְפָּאֵר: ״אַף לֹא הֵבִיאָה [אֶסְתֵּר הַמַּלְכָּה...] וְגַם לְמָחָר [אֲנִי קָרוּא לָהּ]״ (אֶסְתֵּר ה:יב), וְעָשָׂה הָעֵץ (שָׁם:יד)
as when at the height of his arrogance he boasted: "Esther the queen let no man come in with the king unto the banquet... and tomorrow am I invited unto her also" (Esther 5:12), erecting the gallows;
וְאָמַר לַמֶּלֶךְ עַל: ״הָאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר הַמֶּלֶךְ חָפֵץ בִּיקָרוֹ״ (שָׁם ו:ו), שֶׁחָשַׁב: ״לְמִי יַחְפֹּץ [הַמֶּלֶךְ לַעֲשׂוֹת יְקָר יוֹתֵר מִמֶּנִּי]״
advising the king regarding the man whom the king delights to honor, thinking: "To whom would the king delight to do honor more than to myself?" (ibid. 6:6);
שֶׁהָיָה אָז בְּתַכְלִית הָרוֹמְמוּת לְפִי מַחֲשַׁבְתּוֹ, בֶּאֱמֶת אָז הָיָה בְּתַכְלִית הַיְרִידָה וְהַשִּׁפְלוּת, כִּי הָיָה זֶה בֶּאֱמֶת הַכֹּל בְּהֵיפוּךְ: כְּדֵי לְהַאֲבִידוֹ
standing then in absolute degradation, all orchestrating his destruction.
וְכֵן כְּשֶׁהֵם בְּתַכְלִית הַשִּׂמְחָה עַל מַפַּלְתַּ יִשְׂרָאֵל חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, אָז הוּא תַּכְלִית עִצְבוֹנָם וְאֶבְלָם
And so when the wicked are in peak joy over Israel's distress, that is the inception of their eternal grief;
וְעַל כֵּן אָמַר הַנָּבִיא: ״שִׂישִׂי וְשִׂמְחִי בַּת אֱדוֹם [יוֹשֶׁבֶת בְּאֶרֶץ עוּץ,] גַּם עָלַיִךְ תַּעֲבָר כּוֹס [תִּשְׁכְּרִי וְתִתְעָרִי]״ (אֵיכָה ד:כא)
wherefore the prophet proclaimed: "Rejoice and be glad, O daughter of Edom... the cup also shall pass through unto you; you shall be drunken, and shall make yourself naked" (Eichah 4:21);
שֶׁצִּוָּם לִשְׂמוֹחַ, כִּי עַל יְדֵי זֶה ״גַּם עָלַיִךְ וְגוֹמֵר״.
commanding them to rejoice, for through that very joy their cup of retribution arrives!
וְזֶהוּ הַשִּׂמְחָה דְּ״יָשִׂישׂ ה׳ וְגוֹמֵר״: מַה שֶּׁהֵם יָשִׂישׂוּ, עַל יְדֵי זֶה שִׂמְחָה לְפָנָיו, כִּי זֶהוּ עִיקַּר הַגּוֹרֵם לִמְחִיַּית עֲמָלֵק
And this is the joy of "Hashem will cause them to rejoice": their joy bringing joy before Him, being the instrument of Amalek's destruction;
וּבָזֶה מִמֵּילָא מִתְבַּטֵּל הָרָע מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל
through which evil is abolished from Israel;
כִּי כָל חֲטָאֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל גַּם כֵּן הוּא רַק כָּל זְמַן שֶׁזַּרְעוֹ שֶׁל עֲמָלֵק מְצוּיִים בָּעוֹלָם
for all sins of Israel endure only as long as the seed of Amalek exists;
שֶׁהֵם שׁוֹרֶשׁ ״הַשְּׂאוֹר שֶׁבָּעִיסָה וְשִׁעְבּוּד מַלְכִיּוֹת״ הַמְעַכְּבִין רְצוֹנֵנוּ מִלַּעֲשׂוֹת רְצוֹנוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ
they being the root of the leaven in the dough and foreign subjugation that hinder our will from performing His will;
שֶׁזֶּהוּ פֵּירוּד אוֹתִיּוֹת הַשֵּׁם: ב׳ הָרִאשׁוֹנוֹת [י-ה] מֵהָאַחֲרוֹנוֹת [ו-ה].
this being the separation of the first two letters of the Name (Yud-Hei) from the final two (Vav-Hei).
שֶׁ״אֵין הַשֵּׁם שָׁלֵם״ — הַיְינוּ שֶׁאֵין יִחוּד אֶחָד לִרְצוֹנֵנוּ עִם רְצוֹנוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ
"The Name is not whole"—meaning our inward will is not yet in consummate union with His will;
שֶׁב׳ רִאשׁוֹנוֹת [י-ה] הֵם רוֹמְזִים לִרְצוֹנוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ, שֶׁהֵם חָכְמָתוֹ וּבִינָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ כַּנּוֹדָע
the first two letters hinting at His will: His Chokhmah and Binah;
וּב׳ אַחֲרוֹנוֹת [ו-ה] הֵם הָרְצוֹנוֹת שֶׁל זֶרַע יִשְׂרָאֵל בָּנָיו שֶׁל מָקוֹם, בְּסוֹד ״אַבָּא וְאִמָּא, בֵּן וּבַת״
and the final two letters representing the wills of Israel, the children of the Omnipresent, in the mystery of Father, Mother, Son, and Daughter.
וְזֶהוּ רֹאשׁ שִׂמְחָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ כַּאֲשֶׁר יִתְחַבְּרוּ יַחַד אוֹתִיּוֹת הַשֵּׁם וְיִהְיֶה יִחוּד הַגָּמוּר
And this is the pinnacle of His joy: when the four letters of the Divine Name unite in consummate oneness;
וְכָל כַּוָּונַת הַגְּזֵירָה דְּהָמָן הָיָה לְתַכְלִית זֶה: שֶׁיִּגְרוֹם שִׂמְחָה לְאוֹיְבֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, הֵם זַרְעוֹ שֶׁל עֲמָלֵק, וְיָבוֹא לִמְחִיַּית עֲמָלֵק.
the decree of Haman being designed that the joy of Amalek trigger Amalek's annihilation;
וְעַל כֵּן פֶּרֶק זֶה הוּא פְּתִיחָה דִּמְגִלַּת פּוּרִים, כִּי זֶהוּ עִיקַּר שִׂמְחַת פּוּרִים שֶׁנּוֹבֵעַ מֵאוֹתָהּ שִׂמְחָה שֶׁלָּהֶם: דְּ״נַהֲפוֹךְ הוּא״ (אֶסְתֵּר ט:א):
wherefore this passage is the opening of the Megillah, the joy of Purim flowing from the reversal of their malicious joy: "it was turned to the contrary" (Esther 9:1)!

7.h: אוֹת ל״ה — מִשְׁתֵּה אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ, הָמָן וּקְדֻשַּׁת הַזְּמַנִּים, וּ״בְּכוֹסוֹ אָדָם נִיכָּר״ בִּימֵי הַפּוּרִים — Section 35: Ahasuerus's Feast, Haman's Envy of Jewish Festivals, and A Man Recognized Through His Cup

The theme: Ahasuerus rejoicing over the calculation of the seventy years, Haman envying Israel’s holy Sabbath rest, and wine revealing the inward holiness of Israel on Purim. The Megillah opens with the banquet of Ahasuerus, who rejoiced because he miscalculated that seventy years of Babylonian exile had elapsed without redemption (Megillah 11b). Ahasuerus was the "brother of the head" (ibid. 11a)—Nebuchadnezzar, the golden head of the unholy image (Daniel 2:38)—rooted in the "first of the nations," concerning whom it is written: "We would have healed Babylon, but she is not healed" (Yirmiyah 51:9), converts never being accepted from them just as from Amalek. Ahasuerus allied with Haman; once the decree of extermination was sealed, "the king and Haman sat down to drink" (Esther 3:15). When the enemy rejoices maliciously, Hashem turns His wrath away from Israel: "rejoice not when your enemy falls... lest Hashem see it, and it displease Him, and He turn away His wrath from him" (Mishlei 24:17–18). Just as Hashem rejoices to do good from the wellspring of Chesed, so His causing enemies to rejoice turns the wheel upon them to bring banquet and joy unto Israel! Haman cast an evil eye upon the sacred festivals of Israel, protesting: "they waste the entire year, saying: today is Sabbath, today is Passover!" (Megillah 13b). His envy targeted Israel's capacity to draw holiness into secular weekdays through Sabbath rest, enjoying divine blessing in their labor. When Israel eats and drinks, they utter songs and praises; whereas the nations engage in vulgarity. "In his cup a man is recognized" (b'koso adam nikar, Eruvin 65b): on Purim, one is obligated to drink (chayav livsumei, Megillah 7b) so that through his cup Israel's hidden holiness is revealed: "when wine enters, the secret emerges" (Eruvin 65a), manifesting that in the depths of their hearts the Children of Israel are cleaved unto Hashem, the Rock of their heart!

p: וְעַל כֵּן הַתְחָלַת הַמְּגִלָּה מִמִּשְׁתֵּה אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ
And therefore the Megillah opens with the banquet of Ahasuerus;
שֶׁהָיָה גַּם כֵּן שִׂמְחָתוֹ עַל ״דִּמְטוֹ שִׁבְעִים [שָׁנִים] וְלָא אִיפְרִיקוּ״, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּמְגִלָּה (י״א עַמּוּד ב׳)
whose joy was likewise celebrating that seventy years had elapsed without Israel being redeemed (Megillah 11b);
״אֲחִיו שֶׁל רֹאשׁ״ (שָׁם עַמּוּד א׳) — הוּא נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּר, שֶׁהוּא רֵישָׁא דְּצַלְמָא הַטָּמֵא (דָּנִיֵּאל ב:לח)
Ahasuerus being the "brother of the head" (ibid. 11a)—Nebuchadnezzar, the head of the defiled image (Daniel 2:38);
כִּי הוּא גַּם כֵּן מִשּׁוֹרֶשׁ דְּ״רֵאשִׁית גּוֹיִם״ (בַּמִּדְבָּר כ״ד:כ׳)
issuing likewise from the root of the "first of the nations" (Bamidbar 24:20);
דְּעַל כֵּן אִיתָא: ״רִפִּינוּ אֶת בָּבֶל — וְלֹא נִרְפָּאָה״ (יִרְמְיָה נ״א:ט׳), שֶׁלֹּא רָצוּ לְהַכְנִיס מִזַּרְעוֹ תַּחַת כַּנְפֵי הַשְּׁכִינָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאֵין מַכְנִיסִין מִזֶּרַע עֲמָלֵק.
concerning which it is written: "We would have healed Babylon, but she is not healed" (Yirmiyah 51:9), Heaven refusing to accept converts from his seed just as from Amalek.
וְכֵן אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ נִתְחַבֵּר לְהָמָן, וְגַם אָז אַחַר שֶׁהִסְכִּים בַּגְּזֵירָה נֶאֱמַר: ״[וְהַמֶּלֶךְ וְהָמָן] יָשְׁבוּ לִשְׁתּוֹת״ (אֶסְתֵּר ג:טו)
And Ahasuerus allied with Haman, and once agreeing to the decree: "the king and Haman sat down to drink" (Esther 3:15);

וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה הֵשִׁיב הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אַפּוֹ מֵעַל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ: ״בִּנְפֹל [אוֹיִבְךָ אַל תִּשְׂמָח... פֶּן יִרְאֶה ה׳ וְרַע בְּעֵינָיו] וְהֵשִׁיב מֵעָלָיו אַפּוֹ״ (מִשְׁלֵי כ״ד:י״ז–י״ח)
through which Hashem turned His wrath away from Israel: "Rejoice not when your enemy falls... lest Hashem see it, and it displease Him, and He turn away His wrath from him" (Mishlei 24:17–18).
וְזֶהוּ ״וְהָיָה כַּאֲשֶׁר וְגוֹמֵר״: מַמָּשׁ כֹּחַ הַשִּׂמְחָה דִּלְהֵיטִיב שֶׁהָיָה בְּחֵשֶׁק וְשִׂמְחָה וְנִמְשָׁךְ מִמְּקוֹר הַחֶסֶד הַמַּרְבֶּה לְהֵיטִיב
And this is "and it shall come to pass": just as the joy to do good flows with passion from the wellspring of Chesed;
כֵּן מַה שֶּׁיָּשִׂישׂ אֶת שׂוֹנְאֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לְהָרַע חַס וְשָׁלוֹם — זֶהוּ גַּם כֵּן הַמְשָׁכַת חֲסָדִים טוֹבִים לְעַמּוֹ יִשְׂרָאֵל
so His causing the enemies of Israel to rejoice over their distress is likewise a conduit of lovingkindness for Israel;
כִּי עַל יְדֵי זֶה יְבוּטַּל הַדָּבָר, וְאַדְּרַבָּא יֵהָפֵךְ הַגַּלְגַּל עֲלֵיהֶם, וְיִהְיֶה מִזֶּה שִׂמְחָה וּמִשְׁתֶּה לְיִשְׂרָאֵל.
for through their malicious joy the decree is shattered, the wheel reversing upon them to bring joy and feasting unto Israel!
וְהָמָן הִכְנִיס עַיִן רָעָה בִּקְדֻשַּׁת הַזְּמַנִּים דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל: דְּ״מַפְקֵי לְכוּלֵּי שַׁתָּא: ׳שַׁבָּת הַיּוֹם׳, ׳פֶּסַח הַיּוֹם׳״ (מְגִלָּה י״ג עַמּוּד ב׳)
And Haman cast an evil eye upon the holy festivals of Israel, protesting: "they waste the entire year, saying: today is Sabbath, today is Passover!" (Megillah 13b);
כָּל קִנְאָתוֹ שֶׁל אוֹתוֹ רָשָׁע עַל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁעִיקַּר הַקְּדוּשָׁה אֶצְלָם בִּשְׁבִיתָה וְנִיחָא
the entire jealousy of that wicked man targeting Israel because their primary holiness resides in rest;
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה מַמְשִׁיכִים קְדוּשָׁה לִימֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה שֶׁיּוּכְלוּ גַּם כֵּן לֵישֵׁב עַל הַתּוֹרָה וַעֲבוֹדָה
channeling through this holiness into secular weekdays to sit in Torah and divine service;
וְלֹא יִצְטָרְכוּ לְיַגֵּעַ בְּעִנְיְנֵי הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, וּמְלַאכְתָּן מִתְבָּרֶכֶת, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּחֲסִידִים הָרִאשׁוֹנִים (בְּרָכוֹת ל״ב עַמּוּד ב׳)
their labor being blessed without exhausting toil, as stated of the early pious men (Berachos 32b);
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בַּגּוֹיִם, דְּ״יוֹמָם וָלַיְלָה לֹא יִשְׁבֹּתוּ״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית ח:כב).
unlike the heathen, who "day and night shall not cease" from grinding labor (Bereishis 8:22).
אֲבָל כְּשֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל אוֹכְלִין וְשׁוֹתִין וּשְׂמֵחִים — עוֹסְקִין בְּשִׁירוֹת וְתִשְׁבָּחוֹת; וְאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם — בְּדִבְרֵי תִּפְלוּת (מְגִלָּה י״ב עַמּוּד ב׳)
But when Israel eats, drinks, and rejoices, they engage in songs and praises of God; whereas the nations engage in vulgar frivolity (Megillah 12b);
וּ״בְכוֹסוֹ — אָדָם נִיכָּר״ (עֵירוּבִין ס״ה עַמּוּד ב׳)
and "in his cup a man is recognized" (Eruvin 65b);
וְזֶהוּ הַמּוֹעֵד שֶׁנּוֹסַד עַל מַפַּלַת הָמָן שֶׁ״חַיָּיב לְבַסּוֹמֵי בּוֹ״ (מְגִלָּה ז׳ עַמּוּד ב׳)
this being the festival established upon Haman's fall where "one is obligated to become intoxicated through wine";
לִהְיוֹת נִיכָּר בְּכוֹסוֹ, שֶׁבּוֹ הוּא הַהַכָּרָה לְתֹקֶף קְדֻשַּׁת יִשְׂרָאֵל
to be recognized through his cup, wherein is demonstrated the supreme holiness of Israel:
כִּי ״נִכְנַס יַיִן — יָצָא סוֹד״ (עֵירוּבִין ס״ה עַמּוּד א׳), וְנִתְגַּלָּה הַנֶּעְלָם שֶׁבְּמַעֲמַקֵּי לִבּוֹ דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל
for "when wine enters, the secret emerges" (Eruvin 65a), revealing the hidden holiness in the depths of the Jewish heart;
קְדוֹשִׁים דְּבֵקִים בְּמַעֲמַקֵּי לִבָּם בִּקְדֻשַּׁת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, ״צוּר לְבָבָם וְחֶלְקָם״ (תְּהִלִּים ע״ג:כ״ו)
being cleaved in their innermost essence unto Hashem, the Rock of their heart and their portion;
וְיוֹנְקִים מִקְּדֻשַּׁת הַשַּׁבָּת דִּקְבִיעָא וְקַיָּימָא, וּמִמֶּנּוּ מַמְשִׁיכִים קְדוּשָׁה לְכָל הַזְּמַנִּים דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל מְקַדְּשֵׁי
nursing from the immutable holiness of Shabbat, channeling holiness into all festivals sanctified by Israel;
וּמִשָּׁם הַקְּדוּשָׁה חוֹפֶפֶת עֲלֵיהֶם בְּכָל יְמוֹת הַשָּׁנָה כוּלָּהּ, וַאֲפִילּוּ שֶׁהַנִּגְלֶה לֹא יֵרָאֶה כֵן.
whence holiness hovers over them throughout the entire year, even when outwardly it appears not so.
וּמֵאוּמּוֹת בְּהֵיפוּךְ: אֲפִילּוּ פּוֹשֵׁט טְלָפַיִם בַּנִּגְלֶה, בִּפְנִימִיּוּת אֵין לָהֶם שַׁיָּיכוּת לִקְדוּשָׁה כְּלָל
While the nations are the reverse: even when displaying split hooves outwardly, inwardly they have no connection to holiness;
וְ״סוּרוּ טָמֵא קָרְאוּ לָמוֹ״ (אֵיכָה ד:טו) עַל מַעֲמַקֵּיהֶם:
"Depart! Unclean! they cried unto them" (Eichah 4:15) regarding their inward depths!

7.h: אוֹת ל״ו — קְדֻשַּׁת הַמַּעֲמַקִּים בְּפוּרִים, ״עַד דְּלֹא יָדַע״, אֶסְתֵּר סוֹף כָּל הַנִּסִּים, וְנַעֲוָץ סוֹפָן בִּתְחִלָּתָן — Section 36: The Hidden Holiness of Purim, "Ad d'Lo Yada", Esther as End of All Miracles, and Wedging the End in the Beginning

The theme: The secret of drinking on Purim "until one knows not", tasting the rest of Shabbat on a weekday, and Esther linking the end of the festivals to the primordial Sabbath. The profound holiness of Israel's inward depths—an esoteric mystery that cannot be openly manifest in this world—is revealed on Purim through holy intoxication (bisum): the day wherein the Jews rested from their enemies (Esther 9:22), meriting to taste on a secular weekday a foretaste of the rest of Shabbat! That rest is the hour of blotting out Amalek: "And it shall be, when Hashem your God has given you rest (be-haniyach)... you shall blot out the remembrance of Amalek" (Devarim 25:19). Be-haniyach denotes the consummate rest of Shabbat which Jacob and his children merited. Jacob and his sons total thirteen; Joseph dividing into Ephraim and Menashe totals fourteen; and including Joseph himself totals fifteen. These correspond to the 13th and 14th of Adar as the days of vanquishing Amalek, and the 14th and 15th as the days of resting! "Esther is the end of all miracles" (Yoma 29a), marking the conclusion of all sacred festivals: reaching a holy day that contains no cessation from manual labor (Israel accepting only feasting and joy, without a prohibition of work, Megillah 5b). This final festival is wedged in the inception of all sacred seasons (na'utz sofan bi-tchillatan)—the holiness of Shabbat, the head of all miracles in the creation of the universe ex nihilo, wrought purely by Hashem before Israel existed to sanctify it. Purim reveals that all holiness sanctified by Israel (Yisrael d'mkedshi le-zmanei) derives not from human striving, but from the immutable, congenital holiness established within their souls. This is demonstrated when intoxicated "until one knows not" (ad d'lo yada, Megillah 7b)—revealing that their essential being is entirely holy unto Hashem!

p: וּקְדֻשַּׁת הַמַּעֲמַקִּים דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁהוּא סוֹד שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהִתְגַּלּוֹת כְּלָל בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
And the profound holiness in the inward depths of Israel, which is a mystery that cannot be openly revealed in this world;
הוּא הַמִּתְגַּלֶּה בְּפוּרִים עַל יְדֵי הַבִּיסּוּם: ״יְמֵי אֲשֶׁר נָחוּ בָהֶם הַיְּהוּדִים מֵאֹיְבֵיהֶם״ (אֶסְתֵּר ט:כב)
is revealed on Purim through holy wine-intoxication: "as the days wherein the Jews rested from their enemies" (Esther 9:22);
שֶׁזָּכוּ לִטְעוֹם בְּחוֹל מֵעֵין הַמְּנוּחָה דְּשַׁבָּת
meriting to taste on a secular weekday a foretaste of the rest of Shabbat;
שֶׁאָז הוּא זְמַן דִּמְחִיַּית עֲמָלֵק: ״וְהָיָה בְּהָנִיחַ [ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ לְךָ מִכָּל אֹיְבֶיךָ מִסָּבִיב...] תִּמְחֶה [אֶת זֵכֶר עֲמָלֵק]״ (דְּבָרִים כ״ה:י״ט)
which is the hour of blotting out Amalek: "And it shall be, when Hashem your God has given you rest from all your enemies round about... you shall blot out the remembrance of Amalek" (Devarim 25:19);
וּ״בְהָנִיחַ״ — הוּא קְדֻשַּׁת הַשַּׁבָּת: ״מְנוּחָה שְׁלֵימָה שֶׁאַתָּה רוֹצֶה בָּהּ״, שֶׁזָּכוּ לָזֶה יַעֲקֹב וּבָנָיו שֶׁיָּנוּחוּ בוֹ.
and "when He gives you rest" (be-haniyach) is the sanctity of Shabbat: "the consummate rest that You desire," which Jacob and his children merited.
וְיַעֲקֹב וּבָנָיו הֵם י״ג (שְׁלֹשָׁה עָשָׂר), וְיוֹסֵף נֶחְלַק לִשְׁנַיִם הֵם י״ד (אַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר), וְעִם יוֹסֵף הֵם ט״ו (חֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר)
And Jacob and his sons total thirteen; Joseph dividing into two [Ephraim and Menashe] makes fourteen; and including Joseph himself makes fifteen;
וְהֵם י״ג וְי״ד יְמֵי הַמְּחִיָּה דַּעֲמָלֵק, וְי״ד וְט״ו יְמֵי הַנּוֹחַ.
corresponding to the 13th and 14th of Adar as the days of vanquishing Amalek, and the 14th and 15th as the days of rest.
וְ״אֶסְתֵּר — סוֹף כָּל הַנִּסִּים״ (יוֹמָא כ״ט עַמּוּד א׳), הוּא סוֹף כָּל קְדֻשַּׁת הַזְּמַנִּים
And "Esther is the end of all miracles" (Yoma 29a), marking the conclusion of all sacred appointed times;
עַד שֶׁהִגִּיעַ לִקְדֻשַּׁת יוֹם שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ שְׁבִיתָה מִמְּלָאכָה, דְּיוֹם טוֹב לֹא קִבְּלוּ, רַק ״מִשְׁתֶּה וְשִׂמְחָה״ (מְגִלָּה ה׳ עַמּוּד ב׳)
reaching the sanctity of a day containing no prohibition of manual labor, having accepted only feasting and joy (Megillah 5b);
וְהוּא נָעוּץ בִּתְחִלָּתָן שֶׁל קְדֻשַּׁת הַזְּמַנִּים, שֶׁהוּא קְדֻשַּׁת יוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת
being wedged in the inception of all sacred seasons (na'utz sofan bi-tchillatan), which is the holiness of Shabbat;
שֶׁהוּא רֹאשׁ כָּל הַנִּסִּים בִּבְרִיאַת עוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ יֵשׁ מֵאַיִן, וְהַכֹּל בִּשְׁבִיל יִשְׂרָאֵל
the first of all miracles in the creation of the universe ex nihilo, all for the sake of Israel;
אֶלָּא שֶׁלֹּא נַעֲשָׂה בְּאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּידְהוּ וְשֶׁהֵם מְקַדְּשֵׁי, דְּעַדַיִין לֹא הָיוּ בָּעוֹלָם
except that it was not wrought through human initiative or Jewish sanctification, Israel not yet existing in the world.
וְהַסּוֹף, שֶׁהוּא יְמֵי הַפּוּרִים, בּוֹ נִתְגַּלָּה דְּגַם כָּל הַקְּדוּשָׁה דְּ״יִשְׂרָאֵל מְקַדְּשֵׁי לִזְמַנֵּי״ (בְּרָכוֹת מ״ט עַמּוּד א׳) אֵינוֹ מִצַּד עַצְמָם וְהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתָם
And the final culmination in Purim reveals that even all festival holiness sanctified by Israel (Berachos 49a) does not derive merely from human striving;
רַק הַכֹּל בִּקְדוּשָׁה דִּקְבוּעָא וְקַיָּימָא בְּקִרְבָּם
but issues from the immutable, congenital holiness firmly rooted within them;
וְזֶה מִתְבָּרֵר בִּשְׁעַת הַבִּיסּוּם ״עַד דְּלֹא יָדַע״ כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל (מְגִלָּה ז׳ עַמּוּד ב׳)
and this is clarified at the hour of intoxication "until one knows not" (Megillah 7b);
דְּמִתְגַּלֶּה דְּעַצְמִיּוּתָם — כּוּלּוֹ קֹדֶשׁ לַה׳:
revealing that their essential core is entirely holy unto Hashem!

8.h: יִשְׂרָאֵל קְדוֹשִׁים — פֶּרֶק ח׳

אוֹת א׳ — שָׁלֹשׁ קְדוּשׁוֹת שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה: הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת, קְדֻשַּׁת אָבוֹת, וּקְדֻשַּׁת הַשֵּׁם מִלְּמַעְלָה — Section 1: Three Levels of Holiness in the Torah: Human Striving, Ancestral Heritage, and Divine Sanctification

The theme: The three ascending dimensions of holiness in the Torah, the distinction between born Jews and converts, and why divine holiness transcends the angels. The Torah proclaims three levels of holiness in a single verse: "And you shall sanctify yourselves, and you shall be holy; for I am holy, Hashem your God" (Vayikra 11:44, 20:7). The first level, "and you shall sanctify yourselves" (ve-hitkadishtem), is the initial sanctification a person achieves through his own effort and human awakening from below (itaruta d'letata), which is essential in this world of free choice. Following this, he merits "and you shall be holy" (ve-heyitem kedoshim)—the congenital holiness inherited from the Patriarchs, by virtue of which an Israelite who has sinned remains an Israelite, and even a Jewish transgressor surpasses the prophets of the nations. This is the difference between born Israelites and converts: regarding Israel, Scripture writes first: "and I will be their God," and only afterward: "and they shall be My people" (Kiddushin 70b), meaning Hashem remains their God even against their will, as at Sinai where He coerced the mountain like a cask, and in the Future where He will rule with a mighty hand (Yechezkel 20:33). Finally, "for I am holy" (ki kadosh Ani) denotes the supernal holiness wherewith Hashem directly sanctifies man from Above—the fountainhead of all sanctity. In Torat Kohanim, the Sages expound: "You might think you can become holy like Me; therefore Scripture states: 'for I am holy'—My holiness is above your holiness". While angels cannot enter a place of filth or defilement (saying "depart, holy ones" outside a privy), Hashem’s holiness contracts no impurity ("no filth can defile You", Shir HaYichud). Israel is rooted in this transcendent holiness; yet they must prepare themselves below, for the degree of heavenly inspiration (hashra'ah) descending from Above corresponds directly to the preparation of man below!

p: וְשָׁלֹשׁ קְדוּשׁוֹת נֶאֶמְרוּ בַּתּוֹרָה: ״וְהִתְקַדִּשְׁתֶּם, וִהְיִיתֶם קְדֹשִׁים, כִּי קָדוֹשׁ אֲנִי ה׳ [אֱלֹהֵיכֶם]״ (וַיִּקְרָא י״א:מ״ד, כ:ז)
And three gradations of holiness are stated in the Torah: "And you shall sanctify yourselves, and you shall be holy; for I am holy, Hashem your God" (Vayikra 11:44, 20:7);
הַיְינוּ מַה שֶּׁהָאָדָם מִתְקַדֵּשׁ מֵעַצְמוֹ בְּהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתוֹ וְאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּילֵיהּ
that is, what man sanctifies himself through his own active striving and personal awakening from below;
וְזֶהוּ הַהַתְחָלָה שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לִהְיוֹת מִצַּד הָאָדָם בְּאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא וְהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתָא דִּידֵיהּ
and this is the foundational beginning that must arise from man through awakening from below (itaruta d'letata) and personal effort;
כִּי הוּא הָעִיקָּר בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁהוּא עוֹלַם הַבְּחִירָה.
for this is paramount in this world, which is the world of free choice.
וְאַחַר כָּךְ זוֹכֶה לְהַקְּדוּשָׁה שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ בַּשּׁוֹרֶשׁ מוֹרָשָׁה מֵאָבוֹת
And subsequently he merits the holiness he possesses within his spiritual root as an inheritance from the Patriarchs;
שֶׁנּוֹצַר מִזֶּרַע יִשְׂרָאֵל קְדוֹשִׁים, וְהוּא כְּבָר קָדוֹשׁ בַּתּוֹלָדָה מֵאֲבוֹתָיו
having been formed from the seed of holy Israel, already consecrated congenitally from his ancestors;
דְּ״אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁחָטָא — יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא״ (סַנְהֶדְרִין מ״ד עַמּוּד א׳)
for "an Israelite, even though he has sinned, remains an Israelite" (Sanhedrin 44a);
וַאֲפִילּוּ פּוֹשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל עֲדִיפֵי מִנְּבִיאֵי אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם
and even the transgressors of Israel surpass the prophets of the nations of the world;
וְדָבָר זֶה לֹא בְּהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתָם, רַק מִצַּד הַקְּדוּשָׁה שֶׁבַּתּוֹלָדָה בְּכָל זֶרַע יִשְׂרָאֵל.
and this reality exists not through personal striving, but through the inborn congenital sanctity within all the seed of Israel.

וְזֶהוּ הַחִילּוּק שֶׁבֵּין יִשְׂרָאֵל לְגֵרִים, שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּקִדּוּשִׁין (ע׳ סוֹף עַמּוּד ב׳): ״זוֹ מַעֲלָה יְתֵירָה, דִּבְיִשְׂרָאֵל כְּתִיב: ׳וְהָיִיתִי לָהֶם [לֵאלֹהִים]׳ (יִרְמְיָה ל״א:ל״ב) וְאַחַר כָּךְ ׳וְהֵמָּה [יִהְיוּ לִי לְעָם]׳״

And this is the distinction between native Israelites and converts, as stated in Kiddushin (70b): "this is an added virtue, for regarding Israel it is written: 'and I will be their God' (Yirmiyah 31:32) first, and only afterward: 'and they shall be My people'";
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הוּא עַל כָּרְחָם לָהֶם לֵאלֹהִים, רוֹצִים וְלֹא רוֹצִים
meaning that the Blessed Name is their God even against their will, whether they will it or not;
וּכְמוֹ בְּמַתַּן תּוֹרָה שֶׁכָּפָה הַר כְּגִיגִית (שַׁבָּת פ״ח עַמּוּד א׳), וְכֵן לֶעָתִיד: ״[חַי אָנִי...] אִם לֹא בְּיָד חֲזָקָה... אֶמְלוֹךְ עֲלֵיכֶם״ (יְחֶזְקֵאל כ:לג)
just as at Sinai He coerced the mountain like a cask (Shabbat 88a), and in the Future: "surely with a mighty hand... will I rule over you" (Yechezkel 20:33);
וְזֶהוּ רַק בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל מִצַּד הַקְּדוּשָׁה שֶׁלָּהֶם בַּתּוֹלָדָה מֵאֲבוֹתָם, מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בְּגֵרִים.
this applying strictly unto Israel by virtue of their congenital holiness from their ancestors, and not unto converts.
וְאַחַר כָּךְ: ״כִּי קָדוֹשׁ אָנִי״ (וַיִּקְרָא י״א:מ״ד) — הַיְינוּ מַה שֶּׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מְקַדֵּשׁ הָאָדָם מִלְּמַעְלָה
And following this: "for I am holy" (Vayikra 11:44)—meaning that the Blessed Name sanctifies man directly from Above;
שֶׁזֶּהוּ עִיקָּר וְשׁוֹרֶשׁ וּמְקוֹר כָּל הַקְּדוּשָׁה דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל.
which is the primary source, root, and wellspring of all the holiness of Israel.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ: ״קְדֹשִׁים תִּהְיוּ כִּי קָדוֹשׁ אֲנִי ה׳״ (וַיִּקְרָא י״ט:ב׳), ״וְאַתֶּם הַדְּבֵקִים בַּה׳ [אֱלֹהֵיכֶם חַיִּים כֻּלְּכֶם הַיּוֹם]״ (דְּבָרִים ד:ד), צָרִיךְ שֶׁתִּהְיוּ כְּמוֹתוֹ
And as stated: "You shall be holy, for I Hashem am holy" (Vayikra 19:2), and "you that cleave unto Hashem your God are alive every one of you this day" (Devarim 4:4), requiring that you be like Him;
וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה אָמְרוּ בְּתוֹרַת כֹּהֲנִים (קְדוֹשִׁים פָּרָשָׁה א׳): ״יָכוֹל כָּמוֹנִי? — תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ׳[כִּי קָדוֹשׁ] אֲנִי ה׳׳ — קְדֻשָּׁתִי לְמַעְלָה מִקְּדֻשַּׁתְכֶם״
yet our Sages taught in Torat Kohanim: "You might think you can be holy like Me? Scripture therefore states: 'for I Hashem am holy'—My holiness is above your holiness";
הַיְינוּ מִשּׁוּם דְּ״קְדֹשִׁים תִּהְיוּ״ פֵּירֵשׁ בַּזֹּוהַר שָׁם (וַיִּקְרָא פ״ו עַמּוּד א׳): ״תִּהְיוּ״ — וַדַּאי, מִדְּלֹא אָמַר ״הֱיוּ״
for "you shall be holy" is expounded in the Zohar (III, 86a): "you shall be (tihyu)" is an absolute promise, rather than the command "be (heyu)";
וְהַיְינוּ מִתּוֹךְ דְּבֵיקוּתָם בְּשָׁרְשָׁם בִּמְקוֹר הַקְּדוּשָׁה
meaning through their intrinsic cleaving unto the fountainhead of holiness;
וְאִם כֵּן סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ ״כָּמוֹנִי״: דְּאֵין שׁוּם טוּמְאָה חוֹצֶצֶת בִּפְנֵי קְדֻשָּׁתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ
whereupon it might enter your mind "like Me": that no impurity can partition before His holiness;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ: ״׳וְעָבַרְתִּי [בְאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם]׳ (שְׁמוֹת י״ב:י״ב) — אֲנִי וְלֹא מַלְאָךְ וְכוּלֵיהּ״ (הַגָּדָה שֶׁל פֶּסַח)
as stated: "'And I will pass through the land of Egypt' (Shemos 12:12)—I and not an angel" (Passover Haggadah);
כִּי מִצְרַיִם מָלֵא טִינּוּפֶת עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה, וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לִקְדֻשַּׁת הַמַּלְאָכִים לִיכָּנֵס שָׁם
for Egypt was saturated with the filth of idolatry, where the holiness of angels could not enter;
וְכֵן בְּבֵית הַכִּסֵּא אוֹמְרִים: ״הִתְכַּבְּדוּ מְכֻבָּדִים קְדוֹשִׁים וְכוּלֵיהּ״ (בְּרָכוֹת ס׳ עַמּוּד ב׳), כִּי לִקְדֻשָּׁתָם אֵין יְכוֹלִים לִיכָּנֵס לִמְקוֹם טִינּוּפֶת
and in a privy one recites: "Be honored, holy honored ministers" (Berachos 60b), for in their holiness angels cannot enter a place of filth;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עַצְמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר בְּשִׁיר הַיִּחוּד: ״כָּל טִינּוּפֶת לֹא תְּטַנְּפֶךָ״
whereas regarding Hashem Himself it is sung in the Shir HaYichud: "no filth can ever defile You";

וְסָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ דְּגַם יִשְׂרָאֵל כֵּן, שֶׁקְּדֻשָּׁתָם לְמַעְלָה מִקְּדֻשַּׁת מַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת, וְיוּכְלוּ לְהִשְׁתַּקַּע בְּכָל מָקוֹם שֶׁיִּשְׁתַּקַּע וְעִם כָּל זֶה הַקְּדוּשָׁה לֹא תָּזוּז
and one might think that Israel is likewise thus, their sanctity transcending the angels so that they could sink into any defilement and their holiness remain completely intact.
וְעַל זֶה אָמַר: ״אֲנִי ה׳ — קְדֻשָּׁתִי לְמַעְלָה״
Upon this Scripture states: "I am Hashem—My holiness is above your holiness";
דְּזֶהוּ שֵׁם הֲוָיָ״ה הַמּוֹרֶה עַל כָּל קוֹמַת הַקְּדוּשָׁה כּוּלָּהּ עַד רֵישָׁא דְּכָל רֵישִׁין כַּנּוֹדָע
the Name Havayah indicating the entire corporate stature of holiness unto the Head of all heads;
וְהַגַּם שֶׁהַכֹּל יִחוּד אֶחָד, וְ״אוֹרַיְיתָא וְיִשְׂרָאֵל וְקֻדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא כּוּלָּא חַד״ (זֹוהַר חֵלֶק ג׳ ע״ג עַמּוּד א׳), וְהֵם ג׳ קְדוּשׁוֹת הַנַּזְכָּרוֹת לְעֵיל:
and although all is one absolute unity, and "the Torah, Israel, and the Holy One are all one" (Zohar III, 73a), corresponding to these three levels of holiness:
״אוֹרַיְיתָא״ — הֵם מַה שֶּׁהָאָדָם מִשְׁתַּדֵּל בְּעַצְמוֹ עַל יְדֵי הַתּוֹרָה, שֶׁהִיא עִיקַּר הַקְּדוּשָׁה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּזֹּוהַר (קְדוֹשִׁים שָׁם);
"Torah"—is what man achieves through his personal striving in Torah, which is the core of holiness (Zohar ad loc.);
״וְיִשְׂרָאֵל״ — הוּא קְדֻשַּׁת כָּל הַכְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּשָׁרְשָׁם מֵאָבוֹת;
"and Israel"—is the collective holiness of Knesset Israel rooted in their Patriarchal ancestry;
״וְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא״ — הוּא מַה שֶּׁהוּא מְקַדְּשָׁם בִּקְדֻשָּׁתוֹ שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה, וְהַכֹּל אֶחָד בְּיִחוּד גָּמוּר.
"and the Holy One, blessed is He"—is what He directly sanctifies them with His supernal holiness from Above, all united as one.

וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם קְדֻשַּׁת יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא לְמַטָּה, שֶׁהֵם יוֹנְקִים מֵהַקְּדוּשָׁה שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה הַמַּשְׁפִּיעַ לַקְּדוּשָׁה שֶׁבָּהֶם מֵעַצְמָם וּמֵאֲבוֹתָם, וְעַל כֵּן צְרִיכִים לִקְדֻשַּׁת עַצְמָם גַּם כֵּן

Nevertheless, Israel's holiness resides below, nursing from the supernal holiness above which channels into their personal and ancestral sanctity, wherefore they require personal sanctification as well;
וְאַף דִּ״[אֲנִי ה׳] הַשֹּׁכֵן אִתָּם בְּתוֹךְ טֻמְאֹתָם״ (וַיִּקְרָא ט״ז:ט״ז) כְּתִיב
and though it is written: "I am Hashem that dwells among them in the midst of their uncleanness" (Vayikra 16:16);
מִכָּל מָקוֹם הַכֹּל כְּפִי הֲכָנַת הָאָדָם עַצְמוֹ מִלְּמַטָּה
nevertheless all divine inspiration descends according to the preparation of man himself from below;

וַאֲפִילּוּ פּוֹשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל — כְּפִי הֲכָנַת הַקְּדוּשָׁה שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּשָׁרְשָׁם מֵאָבוֹת, מַה שֶּׁלֹּא נִיתַּק מֵהֶם בְּהַגְדָּלַת הַחֲטָאִים, כִּי אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְנַתֵּק כָּל הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ דְּיַהֲדוּת
and even transgressors receive according to their inborn ancestral root which can never be severed completely by sin;
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם הוּא מִתְמַעֵט וְהוֹלֵךְ עַל יְדֵי הַחֲטָאִים, וּלְעוֹלָם הַשְׁרָאַת הַקְּדוּשָׁה דִּלְמַעְלָה — כְּפִי הַקְּדוּשָׁה דִּלְמַטָּה:
yet that light is progressively diminished through sins, the supernal inspiration from Above perpetually matching the sanctification from below!

8.h: אוֹת ב׳ — מִילַת יִצְחָק לִשְׁמוֹנָה כְּקִידּוּשׁ מֵרֶחֶם, סְעוּדַת הֶעָתִיד לָבוֹא, וִיעָקֹב כְּ״חוּט הַמְשֻׁלָּשׁ שֶׁלֹּא יִנָּתֵק״ — Section 2: Isaac Circumcised at Eight Days, The Messianic Feast, and Jacob as the Threefold Cord

The theme: Isaac as the prototype of inborn holiness from the womb, the banquet when Hashem bestows kindness upon Isaac's seed, and the Three Patriarchs corresponding to the three holinesses. Isaac was the first human circumcised at eight days, consecrated unto Hashem from birth and conception without prior human striving. At his birth, celestial joy multiplied: "God has made laughter for me; every one that hears will laugh with me" (Bereishis 21:6). Abraham made a great banquet on the day Isaac was weaned (b'yom higamel, ibid. 21:8)—which the Midrash expounds as the day of his circumcision at eight days (he-gei mem-lamed = 8th day circumcision). This completed the cosmic joy of Creation ("let Hashem rejoice in His works", Tehillim 104:31). In Pesachim (119b), the Sages expound this banquet regarding the Great Feast of the Future, when Hashem bestows kindness (k'she-yigmol chesed) upon the seed of Isaac, when Israel's sanctity will be clarified after all historical siftings. The banquet is attributed specifically to Isaac because Abraham was the "first of converts" whose conception was not in holiness, and Ishmael was an outright gentile; whereas Isaac was conceived and born in holiness. Esau was termed an apostate Israelite (Yisrael mumar), but before Jacob arrived to weave the "threefold cord that is not quickly broken" (Koheles 4:12), the title could still be severed through sin, as occurred with Esau. In Jacob’s seed, whose bed is consummate (mitato sheleimah), the title of Israel can never be uprooted. The three Patriarchs embody the three holinesses: Abraham—first of converts—is human striving (itaruta d'letata); Isaac is inborn holiness from the womb; and Jacob—the likeness of the Man upon the Throne (Yechezkel 1:26; Bereishis Rabbah 68:12)—attained the supernal root where he was titled "God" (El, Bereishis 33:20; Megillah 18a). Jacob never died (Ta'anit 5b), his human form enduring eternally!

p: וְיִצְחָק הוּא הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁנִּימּוֹל לִשְׁמוֹנָה, לִהְיוֹת מִלֵּידָה מִבֶּטֶן מְקוּדָּשׁ לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
And Isaac was the very first who was circumcised at eight days, being holy unto the Blessed Name from the womb without personal effort;
שֶׁזֶּהוּ הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל הַמְקוּדָּשִׁים לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בַּתּוֹלָדָה בְּלֹא הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתָם
this being the root of Israel who are consecrated unto Hashem congenitally from birth without human striving;
וְעַל כֵּן נֶאֱמַר בּוֹ: ״צְחֹק עָשָׂה לִי אֱלֹהִים, כָּל הַשֹּׁמֵעַ יִצְחַק לִי״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית כ״א:ו׳)
wherefore it was said concerning him: "God has made laughter for me; every one that hears will laugh with me" (Bereishis 21:6);
שֶׁנִּתְרַבָּה הַצְּחוֹק וְהַחֶדְוָה בָּעוֹלָם בְּלֵידָתוֹ
celestial joy and gladness multiplying in the world upon his birth;
וְנֶאֱמַר: ״וַיַּעַשׂ [אַבְרָהָם] מִשְׁתֶּה גָדוֹל בְּיוֹם הִגָּמֵל [אֶת יִצְחָק]״ (שָׁם:ח׳), וְלֹא נִמְצָא מִקּוֹדֶם ״מִשְׁתֶּה״ בַּתּוֹרָה
and it is said: "And Abraham made a great feast on the day that Isaac was weaned" (ibid. 21:8), a feast never before appearing in the Torah;
וְזֶה הָיָה בְּיוֹם ה׳ (הַשְּׁמִינִי) גָּמוּל מִילָה (פְּסִיקְתָּא רַבָּתִי פָּרָשָׁה מ״ג)
this occurring on the eighth day when he was circumcised (he-gei mem-lamed);
כִּי שִׂמְחַת ה׳ בְּמַעֲשָׂיו: ״[יִשְׂמַח ה׳] בְּמַעֲשָׂיו״ (תְּהִלִּים ק״ד:ל״א), הַיְינוּ בָּעוֹלָם שֶׁבָּרָא — נִשְׁלַם אָז בְּלֵידַת יִצְחָק וּמִילָתוֹ לִשְׁמוֹנָה
for Hashem's joy in His works (Tehillim 104:31) was brought to completion upon Isaac's birth and eighth-day circumcision;
שֶׁזֶּהוּ הָאוֹת הַבְּרִית שֶׁבִּבְשָׂרוֹ דִּמְקוּדָּשׁ לַשָּׁמַיִם, דְּעַל כָּל פָּנִים הָיָה כְּלַל הַבְּרִיאָה בִּשְׁבִיל יִשְׂרָאֵל (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה ל״ו:ד׳).
