Jacob merited this even in this world: demanding his wife solely to establish the twelve tribes (Bereishis 29:21), wherefore he never died (Ta'anit 5b). He limped merely on account of his future descendants; but when the sun rose, Jacob was healed from his limping, for in Israel the foreskin is an external husk, and "that which is destined to be cut off is considered as already cut off" (kol ha-omed lachitoch k'chatuch dami)!

p: וְיָדוּעַ דְּשֵׁם ״רַע״ בְּעֵינֵי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ — הוּא בִּפְגַם הַבְּרִית
And it is known that the title "evil" in the eyes of Hashem—refers specifically to the blemish of the covenant;
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּעֵר: ״וַיְהִי עֵר בְּכוֹר יְהוּדָה — רַע בְּעֵינֵי ה׳, [וַיְמִתֵהוּ ה׳]״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית ל״ח:ז׳)
as written regarding Er: "And Er, Judah's firstborn, was evil in the sight of Hashem; and Hashem slew him" (Bereishis 38:7);
וּבְדָוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בְּאוֹתָהּ מַעֲשֶׂה: ״וְהָרַע בְּעֵינֶיךָ עָשִׂיתִי״ (תְּהִלִּים נ״א:ו׳).
and regarding King David in that incident: "and done this evil in Your sight" (Tehillim 51:6).
וְזֶהוּ שׁוֹרֶשׁ הָרָע שֶׁבַּבְּרִיאָה: שֶׁהוּא בְּרִיאַת הָעָרְלָה הַחוֹפֶפֶת עַל הַבְּרִית קֹדֶשׁ
And this is the cosmic root of evil in Creation: the formation of the foreskin (orlah) veiling the holy covenant;
שֶׁאֵינָהּ נִקְרֵאת אֶלָּא עַל שֵׁם הַגּוֹיִם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ: ״[כִּי] כָל הַגּוֹיִם עֲרֵלִים״ (יִרְמְיָה ט:כה), כִּדִתְנַן בִּנְדָרִים (ל״א עַמּוּד ב׳)
which is named exclusively after the nations: "for all the nations are uncircumcised" (Yirmiyah 9:25; Nedarim 31b);
דְּזֶהוּ שׁוֹרֶשׁ הָרָע דְּגוֹיִם שֶׁהוּא בַּבְּרִיאָה.
this being the root of the nations' evil implanted in Creation.
וְעַל זֶה נִיתְּנָה מִצְוַת מִילָה לְיִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁהֵם יְכוֹלִים לְהָסִיר אוֹתוֹ הָרָע שֶׁבַּתּוֹלָדָה
And for this was the commandment of circumcision granted unto Israel, who possess the power to excise this inborn evil;
כִּי אֶצְלָם אֵינוֹ בַּשּׁוֹרֶשׁ, רַק כְּקוֹצִים הַסּוֹבְבִים לַשּׁוֹשַׁנָּה (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה ב:ב) וְהוּצֵי לְאָסָא (סַנְהֶדְרִין מ״ד עַמּוּד א׳).
for within them it is not intrinsic, but like thorns encircling the rose or briers around the myrtle.
וְהַגַּם דְּגַם בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל יֵשׁ אֲחִיזָה לָרָע בְּאוֹתוֹ אֵבֶר: דְּזֶהוּ הַנְּגִיעָה בְּכַף יֶרֶךְ יַעֲקֹב
And although even in Israel evil has a tenuous grip upon that organ: this being the angel striking the hollow of Jacob's thigh (Bereishis 32:26);
שֶׁהָיָה כֹּחַ לְמַלְאָכוֹ שֶׁל עֵשָׂו לְקַטְרֵג שָׁם, דְּשָׁם יֵשׁ שׁוֹרֶשׁ מַה לְסִכְלוּת מְעַט שֶׁבַּתּוֹלָדָה
the prince of Esau finding power to prosecute there, where lingers a trace of inborn folly;

שֶׁעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ: ״בְּעָוֹן מָלֵא — אֲפִילּוּ חָסִיד שֶׁבַּחֲסִידִים אֵין מִתְכַּוֵּון אֶלָּא לַהֲנָאַת עַצְמוֹ״ (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה י״ד:ה׳ עַל פָּסוּק: ״הֵן בְּעָווֹן חוֹלָלְתִּי״, תְּהִלִּים נ״א:ז׳)
concerning which it is expounded: "in iniquity full of passion—even the most pious intends somewhat for his own physical pleasure" (Vayikra Rabbah 14:5 on Tehillim 51:7);
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: ״וַהֲסִרֹתִי אֶת לֵב הָאֶבֶן מִבְּשַׂרְכֶם, וְנָתַתִּי לָכֶם לֵב בָּשָׂר״ (יְחֶזְקֵאל ל״ו:כ״ו)
on this Scripture promises: "and I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you a heart of flesh" (Yechezkel 36:26);
וְדָרְשׁוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה: ״לֵב לְהוֹצִיא בָּשָׂר״ (פְּסִיקְתָּא)
the Sages expounding: a heart to bring forth holy bodily offspring;
דְּדָבָר זֶה יִהְיֶה רַק לֶעָתִיד עַל יְדֵי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁיָּסִיר לֵב הָאֶבֶן בִּזְבִיחַת הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע (סֻכָּה נ״ב עַמּוּד א׳).
which will be fully realized in the Future when Hashem slaughters the yetzer hara (Sukkah 52a).
וְאַף דְּיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם זָכָה לָזֶה גַּם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
And though Jacob our father merited this even in this world;

כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ עַל פָּסוּק: ״הָבָה אֶת אִשְׁתִּי״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית כ״ט:כ״א) — ״לֹא נֶאֱמַר אֶלָּא לְהַעֲמִיד תּוֹלָדוֹת״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה ע:יח), וְעַל כֵּן אִיתָא דְּ״לֹא מֵת״ (תַּעֲנִית ה׳ עַמּוּד ב׳)
demanding his wife solely to establish the tribes (Bereishis Rabbah 70:18), wherefore he never died (Ta'anit 5b);
מִכָּל מָקוֹם מִצַּד יוֹצְאֵי יְרֵכוֹ שֶׁאֵינָם כֵּן — הָיָה לוֹ נְגִיעָה בְּכַף יְרֵכוֹ.
nevertheless on account of his future offspring who had not reached this level, his thigh was struck.
אֲבָל כָּל זֶה רַק לְשָׁעָה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁדּוֹמֶה לְלַיְלָה, דְּהוּא עָלְמָא דְּשִׁקְרָא דְּ״עַד אַרְגִּיעָה״ (מִשְׁלֵי י״ב:י״ט)
Yet this limping was temporary in this world which resembles night, the realm of falsehood enduring for a moment (Mishlei 12:19);
וּמִיָּד שֶׁזָּרְחָה לוֹ הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ — נִתְרַפָּא מִצַּלְעָתוֹ (חֻלִּין צ״א עַמּוּד ב׳)
and as soon as the sun rose, he was healed of his limping (Chullin 91b);
כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת אַף עַרְלֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל נִקְרָאִים ״מוּלִים״, דְּהָעָרְלָה אֵינוֹ אֶצְלָם בַּשּׁוֹרֶשׁ כְּלָל, וְ״הָעוֹמֵד לַחְתּוֹךְ — כְּחָתוּךְ דָּמֵי״:
for in truth even uncircumcised Jews are called circumcised, the foreskin not being intrinsic, and "whatever is destined to be severed is considered as already severed"!

10.h: אוֹת ה׳ — חוֹבַת הָאָב לָמוּל אֶת בְּנוֹ, ״מִשְׁכָא דְחִוְיָא״, וּמִילַת הַלֵּב שֶׁל כְּלַל יִשְׂרָאֵל — Section 5: The Father's Duty to Circumcise, The Serpent's Skin, and the Inborn Circumcision of Israel

The theme: The father’s obligation to circumcise his infant son demonstrating that circumcision is an inborn ancestral inheritance, the foreskin as the sloughed skin of the Serpent, and Israel's inward perfection. Therefore the Torah placed the obligation of circumcision upon the father to circumcise his eight-day-old son (Kiddushin 29a), rather than commanding the child to perform it upon reaching adulthood through his own striving. This proves that circumcision is an inborn congenital holiness inherited from the father: in their essential root, the seed of Israel are already circumcised from the womb! The foreskin is merely an external garment—the sloughed skin of the Serpent (mishka d'chivya, Zohar)—surrounding the holy organ: "the wicked walk on every side" (Tehillim 12:9). Because the nations exist in the world—and the foreskin is named after them—and Israel is the microcosm of the universe (olam katan) encompassing all cosmic reality, a layer of foreskin naturally covers the holy sign at birth, mirroring the order of Creation: "first darkness and then light" (reisha chashocha v'hadar nehora, Berachos 2a). The spiritual power to excise that skin is likewise an inborn inheritance from the Patriarchs: "and your people shall be all righteous, they shall inherit the land forever" (Yeshayah 60:21), the sign of the covenant separating Israel from the nations!

p: וְעַל כֵּן הָאָב חַיָּיב לָמוּל אֶת בְּנוֹ (קִדּוּשִׁין כ״ט עַמּוּד א׳)
And therefore the father is obligated to circumcise his son (Kiddushin 29a);
וְאֵין עִיקַּר הַמִּצְוָה עַל הָאָדָם בְּעַצְמוֹ כְּשֶׁיַּגְדִּיל שֶׁיְּהֵא בְּהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתוֹ כִּשְׁאָר כָּל הַמִּצְוֹת
the primary obligation not being delayed until the child reaches adulthood through his own striving like other commandments;
רַק שֶׁהוּא כֵּן בַּתּוֹלָדָה מִצַּד הָאָב הַמּוֹלִידוֹ
but executed congenitally by the father who begot him;
כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת הֵם בַּשּׁוֹרֶשׁ כֵּן מוּלִים, וְהָעָרְלָה אֵינוֹ אֶצְלָם אֶלָּא לְבוּשׁ חִיצוֹנִי: ״מִשְׁכָא דְּחִוְיָא״ (זֹוהַר)
for in their essential root they are already circumcised, the foreskin being merely an outer garment: the sloughed skin of the Serpent;
דְּ״סָבִיב רְשָׁעִים יִתְהַלָּכוּן״ (תְּהִלִּים י״ב:ט׳).
for "the wicked walk on every side" (Tehillim 12:9).
וּמִצַּד שֶׁיֵּשׁ גּוֹיִם בָּעוֹלָם שֶׁהָעָרְלָה נִקְרֵאת עַל שְׁמָם שֶׁהֵם שׁוֹרֶשׁ הָעָרְלָה
And because the nations exist in the world, the foreskin being named after them as its root;
וְיִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁנִּקְרְאוּ ״אָדָם״ (יְבָמוֹת ס״א עַמּוּד א׳) הֵם ״עוֹלָם קָטָן״ וְכוֹלְלִים כָּל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ
and Israel who are called "Adam" (Yevamos 61a) are the microcosm (olam katan) encompassing the entire universe;
עַל כֵּן מִצַּד מְצִיאוּת הַגּוֹיִם יֵשׁ גַּם כֵּן בָּהֶם מְצִיאוּת עוֹר עָרְלָה הַמַּקִּיף וּמְכַסֶּה אֶת הַקְּדוּשָׁה
wherefore from the presence of the nations, a layer of foreskin naturally covers and veils their holiness;
כִּבְרִיָּתוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם: ״בְּרֵישָׁא חֲשׁוֹכָא וַהֲדַר נְהוֹרָא״ (בְּרָכוֹת ב׳ עַמּוּד ב׳).
matching the order of Creation: "first darkness and then light" (Berachos 2b).
וְכֹחַ הֲסָרָתָהּ מֵהֶם — הוּא גַּם כֵּן בָּא לָהֶם מִתּוֹלָדָה
And the spiritual power to excise it from them—is likewise an inborn congenital heritage from the Patriarchs;
וְזֶהוּ אוֹת הַבְּרִית הַמַּבְדִּיל בֵּין יִשְׂרָאֵל לָעַמִּים, וְ״עַמֵּךְ כֻּלָּם צַדִּיקִים״ (יְשַׁעְיָה ס:כא):
this being the sign of the covenant separating Israel from the nations: "And your people shall be all righteous" (Yeshayah 60:21)!

10.h: אוֹת ו׳ — ״צוּר לְבָבִי וְחֶלְקִי״, אַבְרָהָם לֹא מְבַשְׁקַר לֵיהּ וְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא רוֹאֶה לַלֵּבָב, וּמַעֲלַת ״לֵב טוֹב״ — Section 6: Tzaddik as Guardian of the Covenant, The Heart Cleaved to Hashem, and the Primacy of a Good Heart

The theme: Every Jew titled "tzaddik" through the covenant, Abraham failing to recognize the sinner at Gehinnom while Hashem sees his circumcised heart, and the heart as the wellspring of life. The title "tzaddik" designates the guardian of the covenant (shomer ha-brit), applying even unto those who stumbled, seeing that uncircumcised Israelites are halachically called circumcised. Even regarding one who cohabits with a gentile woman—where Eruvin (19a) states that his foreskin is drawn forward so that Abraham does not recognize him—that concealment exists merely before mortal sight. A drawn foreskin (mashuch) requires a second circumcision strictly by rabbinic decree (mi-drabbanan) on account of appearance; while biblically he remains fully circumcised (Yevamos 72b). Abraham looks on outward appearance; but the Holy One, Who searches the heart, sees that his inward heart is circumcised! In the depths of the Jewish heart it is revealed: "It is revealed and known before You that our true will is to do Your will; and what withholds us? The leaven in the dough" (Berachos 17a). The yetzer hara crouches upon the entrances of the heart, preventing the inward secret from emerging; yet the fountainhead of all life resides in the heart ("keep your heart with all diligence, for out of it are the issues of life", Mishlei 4:23). Therefore, when Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai asked his disciples to discern the good path to cleave unto and the evil path to shun, Rabbi Elazar ben Arach answered: "A good heart" and "an evil heart" (Avos 2:9), his master declaring that his words encompass all others. When the heart is directed unto Heaven, even an apparent transgression is greater than a mitzvah performed not for Heaven ("greater is a transgression for the sake of Heaven", Nazir 23b); while one who studies Torah with an arrogant heart to provoke—his study becomes a deadly poison!

p: וְיָדוּעַ דְּשֵׁם ״צַדִּיק״ — הַיְינוּ שׁוֹמֵר הַבְּרִית, וְאַף אוֹתָם שֶׁפָּגְמוּ
And it is known that the title "tzaddik" designates the guardian of the covenant, applying even unto those who stumbled;
שֶׁהֲרֵי גַּם הָעֲרֵלִים [בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל] נִקְרָאִים ״מוּלִים״ (נְדָרִים ל״א עַמּוּד ב׳)
for even uncircumcised Jews are halachically called circumcised (Nedarim 31b);
וַאֲפִילּוּ בּוֹעֵל אֲרַמִּית שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּעֵירוּבִין (י״ט עַמּוּד א׳): ״דְּמִימַּשְׁכָא עָרְלָתֵיהּ וְלָא מְבַשְׁקַר לֵיהּ [אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ]״
and even regarding one who cohabits with a gentile woman, where Eruvin (19a) states that his foreskin is drawn forward and Abraham does not recognize him;
הַיְינוּ רַק לְמַרְאִית הָעַיִן שֶׁאֵינוֹ נִיכָּר
that is strictly to outward appearance where the mark is hidden;
וְהַמָּשׁוּךְ צָרִיךְ לַחֲזוֹר וּלְמוּלוֹ רַק מִדְּרַבָּנָן מִשּׁוּם מַרְאִית הָעַיִן (יְבָמוֹת ע״ב עַמּוּד ב׳)
a drawn foreskin requiring a second incision merely by rabbinic decree on account of appearance (Yevamos 72b);
וְהַיְינוּ מִצַּד הָאָדָם אֲשֶׁר ״יִרְאֶה לַעֵינַיִם״ (שְׁמוּאֵל א ט״ז:ז׳), וְעַל כֵּן אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם לָא מְבַשְׁקַר לֵיהּ
from the perspective of man who looks on outward appearance, wherefore Abraham does not recognize him;
אֲבָל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא דְּ״יִרְאֶה לַלֵּבָב״ (שָׁם) — הוּא רוֹאֶה דְּגַם זֶה מָהוּל בֶּאֱמֶת
but the Holy One Who looks upon the heart sees that he is truly circumcised;
וְעַל כֵּן מִן הַתּוֹרָה אֵין צָרִיךְ לַחֲזוֹר וּלְמוּלוֹ, כִּי מַעֲמַקֵּי לְבָבוֹ שֶׁל כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל דָּבוּק בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
biblically needing no second circumcision, for the inward depths of every Jew are cleaved unto Hashem;
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרָכוֹת (י״ז עַמּוּד א׳): ״גָּלוּי וְיָדוּעַ לְפָנֶיךָ שֶׁרְצוֹנֵנוּ [לַעֲשׂוֹת רְצוֹנָךְ], וּמִי מְעַכֵּב? — שְׂאוֹר שֶׁבָּעִיסָה [וְשִׁעְבּוּד מַלְכִיּוֹת]״
as stated in Berachos (17a): "It is revealed and known before You that our true will is to do Your will; and what withholds us? The leaven in the dough and the subjugation of empires";
וּ״לְפָנֶיךָ״ דַּוְוקָא הוּא גָּלוּי, שֶׁאַתָּה יוֹדֵעַ תַּעֲלוּמוֹת לֵב
"before You" specifically it is revealed, for You alone know the secrets of the heart;
רַק שֶׁהַיֵּצֶר הָרָע הַיּוֹשֵׁב עַל שְׁנֵי מִפְתְּחֵי הַלֵּב (שָׁם ס״א עַמּוּד א׳) — שֶׁהֵם הַפְּתָחִים שֶׁמִּשָּׁם יוֹצְאִים כֹּחוֹת הַלֵּב לְפֹעַל — מְעַכֵּב בְּעַד הַתַּעֲלוּמוֹת לְהִתְגַּלּוֹת.
the yetzer hara sitting upon the two portals of the heart hindering that inward secret from being manifest in action.
וְעִיקַּר הַחַיּוּת הוּא בַּלֵּב, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ: ״כִּי מִמֶּנּוּ — תּוֹצְאוֹת חַיִּים״ (מִשְׁלֵי ד:כג)
And the core of vitality resides in the heart: "for out of it are the issues of life" (Mishlei 4:23);
וְעַל כֵּן כְּלַל דֶּרֶךְ טוֹבָה שֶׁיִּדְבַּק הָאָדָם וְרָעָה שֶׁיִּתְרַחֵק — הוּא: ״לֵב טוֹב״ וְ״לֵב רָע״
wherefore the quintessential good path to cleave unto and the evil to shun are: "a good heart" and "an evil heart";
כְּדִבְרֵי רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲרָךְ (אָבוֹת פֶּרֶק ב׳ מִשְׁנָה ט׳), שֶׁאָמַר עָלָיו רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי: ״דְּדִבְרֵי כוּלָּם בִּכְלַל דְּבָרָיו״, כִּי זֶהוּ שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַכֹּל.
as taught by Rabbi Elazar ben Arach (Avos 2:9), his master declaring that his words encompass all others, this being the root of all.
וְכַאֲשֶׁר לִבּוֹ לַשָּׁמַיִם, אֲפִילּוּ הַמַּעֲשֶׂה לֹא טוֹב — ״גְּדוֹלָה עֲבֵירָה לִשְׁמָהּ [מִמִּצְוָה שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ]״ (נָזִיר כ״ג עַמּוּד ב׳)
And when his heart is directed toward Heaven, even if the external deed was flawed: "greater is a transgression for the sake of Heaven than a mitzvah not for the sake of Heaven" (Nazir 23b);
וְהַהֵיפֶךְ בְּהֵיפוּךְ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ: ״הַלּוֹמֵד עַל מְנָת לְקַנְטֵר — נוֹחַ לוֹ שֶׁלֹּא נִבְרָא, וְשֶׁנֶּהֶפְכָה שִׁלְיָתוֹ עַל פָּנָיו״ (יְרוּשַׁלְמִי שַׁבָּת פֶּרֶק א׳ הֲלָכָה ב׳)
and the reverse in reverse: "he who studies in order to provoke—it were better had he not been created, his afterbirth turning upon his face" (Yerushalmi Shabbat 1:2);
וְ״לַמַּשְׂמְאִילִים בָּהּ — סַמָּא דְּמוֹתָא״ (שַׁבָּת פ״ח עַמּוּד ב׳), רַחֲמָנָא לִיצְלַן!
and "unto those who turn to the left in it—the Torah becomes a deadly poison" (Shabbat 88b), may the Merciful One preserve us!

אוֹת ז׳ — עוֹר הָעָרְלָה כִּלְבוּשׁ הַנָּחָשׁ, פְּסִיקַת הַזּוּהֲמָא בְּסִינַי, וּכְפִיַּית הַר כְּגִיגִית — Section 7: The Foreskin as the Serpent's Sloughed Garment, The Cessation of Defilement at Sinai, and Coercing the Mountain

The theme: The foreskin as the external garment of the Serpent, the cessation of primordial defilement (zuhamat ha-nachash) at Sinai and in Jacob, and the eternal covenant established through the coercion of the mountain. The foreskin (orlah) represents the manifest root of evil created in the cosmos as an encompassing garment. God made man upright (Koheles 7:29) and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life (Bereishis 2:7), and "he who breathes forth, breathes from within his innermost essence". This is the mystery of "For Hashem's portion is His people; Jacob is the lot of His inheritance" (Devarim 32:9), expounded in Shir HaShirim Rabbah (5:2): "The Holy One is the heart of Israel, as it is said: God is the rock of my heart and my portion forever" (Tehillim 73:26). Initially, the yetzer hara was merely a passing wayfarer (helech, Sukkah 52b; II Shmuel 12:4), possessing power to enter the heart only if admitted by man, who held the power to expel it immediately. Adam's sin occurred through the external incitement of the Serpent; from this issued the skin of the foreskin, which after the transgression became coats of skin (kotnot or, Bereishis 3:21) enveloping the entire body from the sloughed skin of the Serpent (mishka d'chivya, Zohar). Adam was formed circumcised and drew forward his foreskin through sin (Sanhedrin 38b). When the Serpent cohabited with Eve and cast defilement into her (Shabbat 146a), evil penetrated the inward heart. The nations never stood at Mount Sinai, wherefore their defilement never ceased; but for Israel who stood at Sinai, that defilement ceased entirely! According to another opinion (Shabbat 146a), defilement ceased from our ancestors through three generations, Jacob fathering twelve tribes with no dross. Both opinions are the living words of God: Jacob attained a "heart of flesh" (lev basar), uprooting the root of evil from the threshold of his heart so that no bodily lust could enter even as a passing wayfarer, wherefore he never died (Ta'anit 5b). Yet to forge an entire nation that can never be severed—where even if they multiply sins unto heaven they cannot return the defilement into the depths of their hearts nor assimilate among the nations ("and that which comes into your mind shall not be at all... with a mighty hand will I rule over you", Yechezkel 20:32–33)—the mountain was coerced over them like a cask at Sinai (k'feeyat har k'gigit), making them an eternal covenantal nation even against their mortal will!
וְהָעָרְלָה הוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ הָרָע שֶׁבַּהִתְגַּלּוּת עַל דֶּרֶךְ לְבוּשׁ מַקִּיף — וְזֶהוּ שׁוֹרֶשׁ הָרָע שֶׁנִּבְרָא בָּעוֹלָם.
And the foreskin is the manifest root of evil structured as an encompassing outer garment—this being the root of evil created in the cosmos.
דְּ״עָשָׂה הָאֱלֹהִים אֶת הָאָדָם יָשָׁר״ (קֹהֶלֶת ז:כט), ״וַיִּפַּח בְּאַפָּיו נִשְׁמַת חַיִּים״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית ב:ז), וּ״מַאן דְּנָפַח — מִתּוֹכוֹ נָפַח״ [וּמִפְּנִימִיּוּתוֹ].

For "God made man upright" (Koheles 7:29), "and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life" (Bereishis 2:7), and "he who breathes forth, breathes from within himself" and from His innermost essence.
וְזֶהוּ: ״כִּי חֵלֶק ה׳ עַמּוֹ, יַעֲקֹב חֶבֶל נַחֲלָתוֹ״ (דְּבָרִים ל״ב:ט׳);
And this is: "For Hashem's portion is His people; Jacob is the lot of His inheritance" (Devarim 32:9);

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּשִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה ה:ב) עַל פָּסוּק ״[אֲנִי יְשֵׁנָה] וְלִבִּי עֵר״ (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים ה:ב): ״הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא — לִבָּן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ׳צוּר לְבָבִי וְחֶלְקִי [אֱלֹהִים לְעוֹלָם]׳ (תְּהִלִּים ע״ג:כ״ו)״.

and as stated in Shir HaShirim Rabbah (5:2) on "I sleep, but my heart wakes" (Shir HaShirim 5:2): "The Holy One is the heart of Israel, as it is said: God is the rock of my heart, and my portion forever" (Tehillim 73:26).
וּתְחִלָּתוֹ שֶׁל יֵצֶר הָרָע נִקְרָא ״הֵלֶךְ״ (שְׁמוּאֵל ב י״ב:ד׳; סֻכָּה נ״ב עַמּוּד ב׳), שֶׁהוּא בָּא מִבַּחוּץ דֶּרֶךְ אַקְרַאי בְּדֶרֶךְ הִילוּכוֹ
And the inception of the yetzer hara is termed a "wayfarer" (helech, II Shmuel 12:4; Sukkah 52b), arriving from without casually along its path;
וְזֶהוּ בְּרִיאַת הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע: שֶׁהָיָה לוֹ רַק הַכֹּחַ לִיכָּנֵס לַלֵּב אִם יַנִּיחוֹ הָאָדָם לִיכָּנֵס
this being the primeval creation of the yetzer hara: possessing power to enter the heart only if man permitted it to enter;
וְאָז לְבַסּוֹף נַעֲשָׂה ״אִישׁ״ [אוֹרֵחַ] וּ״בַעַל הַבַּיִת״ (סֻכָּה שָׁם)
whereupon ultimately it became a "guest" and the "master of the house" (Sukkah 52b);
אֲבָל בְּיָדוֹ הָיָה לְגָרְשׁוֹ מִיָּד שֶׁלֹּא לְהַנִּיחוֹ לִיכָּנֵס כְּלָל.
while man held the power to expel it immediately without permitting it to enter at all.
וּבָזֶה הָיָה חֵטְא אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן עַל יְדֵי הֲסָתַת נָחָשׁ, שֶׁהוּא חִיצוֹנִי הַבָּא מִבַּחוּץ לְהַסִּית
And in this consisted the sin of Adam HaRishon through the seduction of the Serpent, an external agent coming from outside to incite;
וּמִמֶּנּוּ הוּא עוֹר הָעָרְלָה, שֶׁנַּעֲשָׂה אַחַר הַחֵטְא ״כָּתְנוֹת עוֹר״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית ג:כא) לְכָל הַגּוּף מִ״מִּשְׁכָא דְּחִוְיָא״ (זֹוהַר חֵלֶק א׳ ל״ו עַמּוּד ב׳).
and from the Serpent issued the skin of the foreskin, which after the sin became "coats of skin" (Bereishis 3:21) for the entire body from the sloughed skin of the Serpent.
לְפִי שֶׁהָאָדָם כּוֹלֵל כָּל הַנִּבְרָאִים, וּמִצַּד כֹּחַ הַנָּחָשׁ שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּעוֹלָם לִהְיוֹת לָאָדָם סְבִיבָיו צָרָיו, [נִבְרָא] בָּאָדָם עַצְמוֹ עוֹר הָעָרְלָה
Because man encompasses all creatures, and from the presence of the Serpent surrounding man as an adversary, the skin of the foreskin was formed upon man himself;
[וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם ״עָשָׂה הָאֱלֹהִים אֶת הָאָדָם יָשָׁר״ (קֹהֶלֶת ז:כט) שֶׁנּוֹלַד מָהוּל וּמָשַׁךְ עָרְלָתוֹ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (ל״ח סוֹף עַמּוּד ב׳)
[and nevertheless "God made man upright" (Koheles 7:29), Adam having been born circumcised and drawing forward his foreskin through sin (Sanhedrin 38b);
שֶׁנּוֹצַר בְּעִנְיָן זֶה שֶׁיּוּכַל לְהַמְשִׁיךְ עָרְלָתוֹ בְּחֶטְאוֹ, וְעַל יְדֵי הַחֵטְא שֶׁלּוֹ הִמְשִׁיכָהּ עָלָיו וְנִתְלַבֵּשׁ בָּהּ].
being created with the latent potential to draw forward his foreskin, and through his transgression he pulled it over himself and became clothed in it].
וּכְשֶׁבָּא נָחָשׁ עַל חַוָּה וְהֵטִיל בָּהּ זוּהֲמָא (שַׁבָּת קמ״ו רֵישׁ עַמּוּד א׳), נִכְנַס כֹּחַ הָרָע בִּפְנִימִיּוּת הַלֵּב
And when the Serpent cohabited with Eve and cast defilement into her (Shabbat 146a), the power of evil penetrated into the inward heart;
וְאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם שֶׁלֹּא עָמְדוּ עַל הַר סִינַי — לֹא פָּסְקָה זוּהֲמָתָן, וְנִשְׁאָר שׁוֹרֶשׁ הָרָע קָבוּעַ בְּלִבָּן
and the nations of the world who never stood at Mount Sinai—their defilement never ceased, the root of evil remaining fixed in their hearts;
אֲבָל יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁעָמְדוּ עַל הַר סִינַי — פָּסְקָה אוֹתָהּ זוּהֲמָא (שַׁבָּת שָׁם).
but for Israel who stood at Mount Sinai—that defilement ceased completely (ibid.)!
וּלְחַד מַאן דְּאָמַר (שַׁבָּת קמ״ו רֵישׁ עַמּוּד א׳): ״לֹא פָּסְקָה זוּהֲמָא מֵאֲבוֹתֵינוּ עַד שְׁלֹשָׁה דּוֹרוֹת... יַעֲקֹב הוֹלִיד י״ב (שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר) שְׁבָטִים שֶׁלֹּא [הָיָה בָּהֶם דֹּפִי]״
And according to one authority in Shabbat (146a): "defilement did not cease from our ancestors until three generations... Jacob fathered twelve tribes in whom there was no blemish";
וְאֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ דִּבְרֵי אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים:
and both opinions are the living words of God:
דְּיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם זָכָה לְ״לֵב בָּשָׂר״ (יְחֶזְקֵאל ל״ו:כ״ו) כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל
for our father Jacob, peace be upon him, merited a "heart of flesh" (Yechezkel 36:26) as explained above;
וְתִיקֵּן חֵטְא אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן לַעֲקוֹר כָּל שׁוֹרֶשׁ הָרָע מִפֶּתַח לִבּוֹ לְגַמְרֵי
rectifying the sin of Adam HaRishon by completely uprooting the root of evil from the threshold of his heart;
שֶׁלֹּא יָכֹל לִיכָּנֵס גַּם דֶּרֶךְ ״הֵלֶךְ״ בְּהִתְעוֹרְרוּת שׁוּם תַּאֲוָה גּוּפָנִית, דְּעַל כֵּן ״לֹא מֵת״ כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל (תַּעֲנִית ה׳ עַמּוּד ב׳)
so that it could not enter even as a casual wayfarer through the arousal of bodily lust, wherefore he never died (Ta'anit 5b);
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה זָכָה גַּם כֵּן לְצֶאֱצָאָיו אַחֲרָיו לִהְיוֹת מִטָּתוֹ שְׁלֵימָה בְּלֹא שׁוּם פְּסֹולֶת.
meriting through this that all his descendants formed a whole bed without any dross.
אֲבָל לִהְיוֹת נִבְנֶה אוּמָּה שְׁלֵימָה: לִהְיוֹת עֵדָה כּוּלָּם קְדוֹשִׁים לַה׳ וְחֶבֶל נַחֲלָתוֹ שֶׁאֵין יָכוֹל לִיפָּסֵק עוֹד
But to forge a collective nation: an entire congregation holy unto Hashem and the lot of His inheritance that can never be severed;
דַּאֲפִילּוּ יַגְדִּילוּ עֲווֹנוֹת עַד אֵין קֵץ, לֹא יוּכְלוּ לְהַחֲזִיר הַזּוּהֲמָא לְמַעֲמַקֵּי הַלֵּב
that even should they multiply sins without end, they can never return that defilement into the depths of their hearts;

וְלִהְיוֹת חַס וְשָׁלוֹם ״כְּכָל הַגּוֹיִם בֵּית יִשְׂרָאֵל״, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ: ״וְהָעֹלָה עַל רוּחֲכֶם — הָיוֹ לֹא תִהְיֶה... [חַי אָנִי...] אִם לֹא בְּיָד חֲזָקָה... אֶמְלוֹךְ עֲלֵיכֶם״ (יְחֶזְקֵאל כ:לב–לג)
to become, heaven forfend, like the nations: "and that which comes into your mind shall not be at all... with a mighty hand... will I rule over you" (Yechezkel 20:32–33).
וְזֶהוּ כְּפִיַּית הַר כְּגִיגִית שֶׁהָיָה בְּמַעֲמַד הַר סִינַי (שַׁבָּת פ״ח עַמּוּד א׳)
And this was the coercion of the mountain like a cask at Mount Sinai (Shabbat 88a):
שֶׁפְּסִיקַת הַזּוּהֲמָא הָיָה בְּעַל כָּרְחָם וּבְיָד חֲזָקָה
that the cessation of defilement was effected even against their will and with a mighty hand;
שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ יִרְצוּ לִהְיוֹת כְּכָל הַגּוֹיִם — לֹא יוּכְלוּ עוֹד, וּבְעַל כָּרְחָם הֵם יִשְׂרָאֵל
that even should they desire to become like the nations, they cannot, remaining an Israelite against their mortal will;
דָּבָר זֶה נִתְחַדֵּשׁ אָז בְּקַבָּלַת הַתּוֹרָה בְּהַר סִינַי
this covenantal reality having been established upon the receiving of the Torah at Sinai;
וְזֶה שֶׁכָּתוּב הַלָּשׁוֹן: ״שֶׁעָמְדוּ עַל הַר סִינַי״ (שַׁבָּת קמ״ו עַמּוּד א׳)
and this explains the precise phrasing: "who stood at Mount Sinai" (Shabbat 146a);
כִּי פְּסִיקָה זוֹ לְגַמְרֵי מֵהֶם הוּא עַל יְדֵי עֲמִידַת הָהָר — עַל יְדֵי כְּפִיַּית הָהָר כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל:
for this absolute eradication of defilement was accomplished through the standing of the mountain, through coercing the mountain over them as explained above!

אוֹת ח׳ — הַמֵּתִים בִּשְׁלֹשֶׁת יְמֵי אֲפֵלָה, אוֹתִיּוֹת הַתּוֹרָה, וְ״דּוֹרְשֵׁי רְשִׁימוֹת״ שֶׁבְּכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל — Section 8: Those Who Died in the Three Days of Darkness, Letters of the Torah, and the "Seekers of Impressions"

The theme: Why those who died in the plague of darkness possessed no root in the letters of the Torah, and how the "Seekers of Impressions" (dorshei reshimot) establish that all Israel possess a share in the World to Come. Those who perished during the three days of darkness in Egypt—failing to depart and receive the Torah at Sinai—evidently possessed no root in holiness. The Sages state that had even a single individual been missing from the sixty myriads at Sinai, the Torah could not have been given (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:1), for the Holy One, the Torah, and Israel are one. The Torah is Hashem’s wisdom, and He and His wisdom are absolute unity; it encompasses the roots of all Jewish souls hewn from the 600,000 letters of the Torah. Had one soul been absent, a letter or tittle of the Torah would have been missing, invalidating the entire scroll! Perforce, those who died in Egypt possessed no root in the letters of the Torah: though biologically descended from Jacob, by submerging themselves in the Egyptian "nakedness of the land" (ervat ha-aretz) they drew the Serpent's defilement back into the depths of their hearts, severing their souls from the cord of His inheritance. But from Sinai onward, a Jewish soul can never be severed; no outcast is banished from Him (II Shmuel 14:14), for defilement ceased from the heart forever. Therefore, the Mishnah opens: "All Israel have a portion in the World to Come" (Sanhedrin 90a). This world is the world of action (Asiyah), while the World to Come is the realm of Binah (understanding in the heart). Those listed in the Mishnah as lacking a share in the World to Come were souls from the mixed multitude (eirev rav) who assimilated into Israel (Zohar); whereas regarding the individual Jewish kings and commoners listed (Jeroboam, Ahab, Doeg, Ahithophel), the "Seekers of Impressions" (dorshei reshimot, Sanhedrin 104b) revealed that they all possess a share in the World to Come! They are termed dorshei reshimot because wherever divine light and holiness once resided, even if departed, an indelible impression (reshimu) remains. By their grievous sins, the actual light departed, wherefore on their own they lost their portion; yet through the remaining holy impression (reshimu), they retain their share in the World to Come! On that holy impression the name of Israel endures, which can never be uprooted; unlike the nations whose root derives from the Serpent's defilement, where holiness never dwelled!
אֲבָל מִקּוֹדֶם, אוֹתָן שֶׁמֵּתוּ בִּשְׁלֹשֶׁת יְמֵי אֲפֵלָה שֶׁלֹּא זָכוּ לָצֵאת מִמִּצְרַיִם וּלְקַבֵּל הַתּוֹרָה בְּמַעֲמַד הַר סִינַי
But prior to Sinai, those who perished during the three days of darkness (Shemos 10:22–23; Rashi ad loc.) who did not merit to depart from Egypt and receive the Torah at Mount Sinai;
מִסְּתָמָא לֹא הָיָה בָּהֶם שׁוֹרֶשׁ מִקְּדוּשָׁה
evidently possessed no innate root of holiness;
שֶׁהֲרֵי אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה: שֶׁאִלּוּ הָיָה חָסֵר אֶחָד מֵהֶם, לֹא נִיתְּנָה תּוֹרָה (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה א:א)
for the Sages stated: had even a single person been missing from them, the Torah could not have been given (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:1);
כִּי: ״קֻדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא, וְאוֹרַיְיתָא, וְיִשְׂרָאֵל — כּוּלָּא חַד״ (זֹוהַר חֵלֶק ג׳ ע״ג עַמּוּד א׳).
for: "the Holy One, the Torah, and Israel are all one" (Zohar III, 73a).
כִּי הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁהִיא חָכְמָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ, שֶׁהוּא וְחָכְמָתוֹ אֶחָד הוּא
For the Torah is His supernal wisdom, and He and His wisdom are absolute unity;
גַּם כֵּן כּוֹלֶלֶת כָּל שָׁרְשֵׁי הַנְּפָשׁוֹת מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁשָּׁרְשָׁם מֵאוֹתִיּוֹת הַתּוֹרָה כַּנּוֹדָע
likewise encompassing all the soul-roots of Israel, who are hewn from the letters of the Torah as is known;
וְאִם הָיָה חָסֵר אֶחָד, הָיָה חָסֵר אוֹת אַחַת מֵהַתּוֹרָה אוֹ קוּצּוֹ שֶׁל אוֹת הַמְעַכֵּב וּפוֹסֵל.
and had a single soul been missing, an entire letter or tittle of the Torah would have been absent, invalidating the scroll.
וְאִם כֵּן עַל כָּרְחָךְ אוֹתָם שֶׁמֵּתוּ מִקּוֹדֶם — לֹא הָיָה לְנַפְשׁוֹתָם אֲחִיזָה בְּאוֹתִיּוֹת הַתּוֹרָה
And if so, perforce those who died previously had no hold in the letters of the Torah;
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהָיוּ זֶרַע יַעֲקֹב, עַל יְדֵי שְׁקִיעָתָם בְּטֻמְאַת מִצְרַיִם ״עֶרְוַת הָאָרֶץ״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית מ״ב:ט׳)
and although they were biologically of Jacob's seed, by submerging themselves in the defilement of Egypt, the "nakedness of the land" (Bereishis 42:9);
שֶׁהוּא עַצְמוֹ זוּהֲמַת הַנָּחָשׁ שֶׁהֶחֱזִירוּהָ לְמַעֲמַקֵּי לִבָּם, עַד שֶׁנִּפְסְקוּ עַל יְדֵי זֶה מִלִּהְיוֹת ״חֶבֶל נַחֲלָתוֹ״ (דְּבָרִים ל״ב:ט׳).
which is the Serpent's defilement, they dragged it back into their inward hearts until they were severed from being the lot of His inheritance (Devarim 32:9).
אֲבָל מִמַּתַּן תּוֹרָה וְאֵילָךְ — אִי אֶפְשָׁר לִיפָּסֵק עוֹד, וְ״לֹא יִדַּח [מִמֶּנּוּ] נִדָּח״ (שְׁמוּאֵל ב י״ד:י״ד)
But from the Giving of the Torah onward—it is impossible for any soul to be severed, and "no outcast is banished from Him" (II Shmuel 14:14);
כִּי אָז פָּסְקָה לְגַמְרֵי הַזּוּהֲמָא שֶׁבַּלֵּב מִכָּל זֶרַע יִשְׂרָאֵל לְגַמְרֵי
for then the defilement of the heart ceased completely from all the seed of Israel;
דְּעַל כֵּן: ״כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל יֵשׁ לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא״ (סַנְהֶדְרִין צ׳ עַמּוּד א׳)
wherefore: "All Israel have a portion in the World to Come" (Sanhedrin 90a);
כִּידוּעַ דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הוּא עוֹלַם הַמַּעֲשֶׂה, וְעוֹלָם הַבָּא הוּא עוֹלַם הַבִּינָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב.
as known that this world is the realm of action, while the World to Come is the realm of Binah in the heart.
וּמִמַּה שֶּׁכָּתוּב תְּחִלָּה דֶּרֶךְ כְּלָל: ״כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל וְכוּלֵיהּ״, וְאַחַר כָּךְ ״וְאֵלּוּ שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא״ (שָׁם)
And from the Mishnah stating first collectively: "All Israel, etc." and immediately following: "And these are they that have no portion in the World to Come" (ibid.);
שָׁמְעַתְּ מִנַּהּ מִזֶּה: דְּאוֹתָן אֵינָן בִּכְלַל ״כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל״, וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁהֵם מִנַּפְשׁוֹת הָעֵרֶב רַב שֶׁנִּטְמְעוּ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל כִּידוּעַ בַּזֹּוהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
you deduce: those excluded are not included in collective Israel, being souls of the mixed multitude (eirev rav) who assimilated into Israel (Zohar);
וְאוֹתָן מְלָכִים וְהֶדְיוֹטוֹת שֶׁנִּמְנוּ בִּפְרָט (סַנְהֶדְרִין שָׁם) — כְּבָר ״דּוֹרְשֵׁי רְשִׁימוֹת״ אָמְרוּ שֶׁכּוּלָּם יֵשׁ לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא (סַנְהֶדְרִין ק״ד עַמּוּד ב׳).
while regarding the specific kings and commoners enumerated, the "Seekers of Impressions" (dorshei reshimot) established that they all possess a portion in the World to Come (Sanhedrin 104b)!
וְנִרְאֶה מַה שֶּׁנִּקְרְאוּ ״דּוֹרְשֵׁי רְשִׁימוֹת״: כִּי יָדוּעַ שֶׁבְּכָל מָקוֹם שֶׁהָיָה שָׁם אוֹר וּקְדוּשָׁה, אַף שֶׁנִּסְתַּלֵּק — הָ״רְשִׁימוּ״ נִשְׁאָר
And it appears that they are called dorshei reshimot: for wherever divine light and holiness once resided, even if departed, an indelible impression (reshimu) remains;
וְהַחוֹטֵא בְּדָבָר שֶׁהַמִּשְׁפָּט שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא — הַיְינוּ שֶׁעַל יְדֵי אוֹתָן חֲטָאִים נִסְתַּלְּקָה כָּל שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַקְּדוּשָׁה שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּלִבְּבוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
and one who commits sins that carry forfeiture of the World to Come, through those sins the manifest root of holiness departs from his heart;
אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם הָרְשִׁימוּ נִשְׁאָר
nevertheless the holy impression (reshimu) remains;
וְעַל כֵּן מִצַּד עַצְמוּתָם אֵין לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא, שֶׁכְּבָר נִסְתַּלֵּק עַצְמוּת הָאוֹר וְהַקְּדוּשָׁה שֶׁהָיָה בָּהֶם
wherefore from their own active standing they possess no share in the World to Come, the essence of the light having departed;
אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם מִצַּד הָרְשִׁימוּ הַנִּשְׁאָר — יֵשׁ לָהֶם!
yet on the part of the remaining indelible impression—they retain a share!
וְעַל כֵּן ״דּוֹרְשֵׁי רְשִׁימוֹת״ שֶׁדָּרְשׁוּ וְחָקְרוּ עַל אוֹר הָרְשִׁימוּ הַנִּשְׁאָר, הֵם אָמְרוּ שֶׁכּוּלָּם יֵשׁ לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא מִצַּד אוֹר הָרְשִׁימוּ מִיהַת
Wherefore the dorshei reshimot, investigating that remaining light, declared that all possess a portion in the World to Come through that enduring impression;
וּמִצַּד הַזֶּה גַּם כֵּן אִי אֶפְשָׁר לַעֲקוֹר שֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל מִמֶּנּוּ
and from this vantage it is impossible to uproot the name of Israel from a Jew;
שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ שֶׁיַּעַקְרוּ בַּחֲטָאָיו, מִכָּל מָקוֹם הָרְשִׁימוּ נִשְׁאָר, וְעַל אוֹתוֹ הָרְשִׁימוּ גַּם כֵּן יֵשׁ שֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל
for even if uprooted through sins, the impression remains bearing the name of Israel;
וְזֶה אִי אֶפְשָׁר כְּלָל לַעֲקוֹר שֶׁלֹּא יִשָּׁאֵר רְשִׁימוּ
which can never be eradicated;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם שֶׁשָּׁרְשָׁם מֵאוֹתָהּ זוּהֲמָא רָעָה, וְלֹא הָיָה שָׁם קְדוּשָׁה מֵעוֹלָם:
unlike the nations whose root derives from the Serpent's defilement, where holiness never dwelled!

אוֹת ט׳ — קְדֻשַּׁת הַשַּׁבָּת: בְּרִית עוֹלָם, מַתָּנָה טוֹבָה בְּבֵית גְּנָזָיו, וּשְׂכַר מִצְוָה — מִצְוָה — Section 9: The Inborn Sabbath Holiness, An Everlasting Covenant, and The Divine Gift in the Treasury

The theme: The primordial sanctity of Shabbat granted unconditionally unto Israel, why a gentile observing Shabbat incurs death, and holiness in the heart as the reward of the mitzvah. This immutable holiness within the hearts of Israel—implanted without human striving—is the sanctity of Shabbat. It was established by the Blessed Name at the dawn of Creation when He sanctified the seventh day (Bereishis 2:3); wherefore Scripture proclaims: "it is a sign between Me and the children of Israel forever" (Shemos 31:17). A gentile who observes Shabbat incurs the death penalty (Sanhedrin 58b), possessing no connection to this holiness, like one who inserts his cloak between a lion and lioness uniting! In Shabbat (10b) on "that you may know that I am Hashem Who sanctifies you" (Shemos 31:13): "The Holy One said to Moses: I have a precious gift in My treasury, and Shabbat is its name; go and inform Israel". The Gemara asks: If the reward of mitzvos is not revealed in this world, why reveal Shabbat's reward? The answer is: By declaring "that I am Hashem Who sanctifies you," Hashem informed them that the reward is the divine sanctification itself! "The reward of a mitzvah is a mitzvah" (Avos 4:2): the mitzvah itself infuses holiness into the heart ("Who has sanctified us with His commandments"), which is the reward of the World to Come—rejoicing in the radiance of the Shechinah (nehenin mi-ziv ha-Shechinah, Berachos 17a)! Shabbat is a foretaste of the World to Come (Berachos 57b), where man attains this supernal radiance, which then radiates across the six workdays, Hashem dwelling among them even in their impurity!
וּקְדוּשָׁה זוֹ שֶׁבַּשּׁוֹרֶשׁ בְּלִבְּבוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּלֹא הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתָם כְּלָל — זֶהוּ קְדֻשַּׁת הַשַּׁבָּת
And this holiness within the root of Jewish hearts independent of human striving—is the sanctity of Shabbat;
שֶׁהוּא הַקְּדוּשָׁה דִּקְבִיעָא מִצַּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מִתְּחִלַּת בְּרִיאַת עוֹלָם שֶׁקִּידֵּשׁ אֶת יוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי (בְּרֵאשִׁית ב:ג)
which is the immutable holiness established by Hashem from the dawn of Creation when He sanctified the seventh day (Bereishis 2:3);
וְעַל כֵּן נֶאֱמַר בְּשַׁבָּת: ״[וְשָׁמְרוּ בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת... לְדֹרֹתָם] בְּרִית עוֹלָם, בֵּינִי וּבֵין בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל [אוֹת הִוא לְעֹלָם]״ (שְׁמוֹת ל״א:ט״ז–י״ז)
wherefore it is said regarding Shabbat: "to observe the sabbath throughout their generations, for a perpetual covenant; it is a sign between Me and the children of Israel forever" (Shemos 31:16–17);
וְ״גוֹי שֶׁשָּׁבַת — חַיָּיב מִיתָה״ (סַנְהֶדְרִין נ״ח עַמּוּד ב׳), כִּי הֵם אֵין לָהֶם שַׁיָּיכוּת לִקְדוּשָׁה זוֹ
and "a gentile who rests on Shabbat incurs the death penalty" (Sanhedrin 58b), for they possess no connection to this holiness;
וְזֶה דּוֹמֶה לִ״מַכְנִיס כְּסוּתוֹ בֵּין לָבִיא לִלְבִיאָה כְּשֶׁנִּזְקָקִין זֶה לָזֶה״ (סַנְהֶדְרִין ק״ו עַמּוּד א׳).
and this is like one who inserts his cloak between a lion and lioness uniting (Sanhedrin 106a)!

וְכֵן אִיתָא בְּשַׁבָּת (י׳ עַמּוּד ב׳) עַל פָּסוּק ״לָדַעַת כִּי אֲנִי ה׳ מְקַדִּשְׁכֶם״ (שְׁמוֹת ל״א:י״ג): ״מַתָּנָה טוֹבָה יֵשׁ לִי בְּבֵית גְּנָזַי וְשַׁבָּת שְׁמָהּ, וַאֲנִי מְבַקֵּשׁ לִיתְּנָהּ לְיִשְׂרָאֵל, לֵךְ וְהוֹדִיעָם״

And so in Shabbat (10b) on "that you may know that I am Hashem Who sanctifies you" (Shemos 31:13): "I have a precious gift in My treasury and Shabbat is its name, and I wish to give it to Israel; go and inform them";
וְעַל מַתַּן שְׂכָרָהּ דְּלָא עֲבִיד לְאִגַּלּוֹי אָמַר: ״לָדַעַת וְכוּלֵיהּ״
and regarding the reward which is ordinarily unrevealed in this world, Scripture states: "that you may know, etc.";
וְעַל כָּרְחָךְ דִּבְמַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב ״כִּי אֲנִי ה׳ מְקַדִּשְׁכֶם״ הוֹדִיעָם בָּזֶה מַתַּן שְׂכָרָהּ: שֶׁהוּא מַה דַּ״אֲנִי ה׳ מְקַדִּשְׁכֶם״.
and perforce by declaring "that I am Hashem Who sanctifies you," He informed them of the reward: that Hashem Himself is their sanctification!
כִּי: ״שְׂכַר מִצְוָה — מִצְוָה״ (אָבוֹת פֶּרֶק ד׳ מִשְׁנָה ב׳), הַיְינוּ הַמִּצְוָה עַצְמָהּ מַה שֶּׁמַּכְנֶסֶת קְדוּשָׁה לַלֵּב
For: "the reward of a mitzvah is a mitzvah" (Avos 4:2), the mitzvah itself infusing holiness into the heart;
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאוֹמְרִים: ״אֲשֶׁר קִדְּשָׁנוּ בְּמִצְוֹתָיו וְצִוָּנוּ״
as we recite: "Who has sanctified us with His commandments and commanded us";
וְזֶהוּ הַמַּתַּן שָׂכָר דְּ״לְמָחָר — לְקַבֵּל שְׂכָרָם״ (עֵירוּבִין כ״ב עַמּוּד א׳)
this being the ultimate reward reserved for tomorrow in the World to Come;
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי הַקְּדוּשָׁה שֶׁבַּלֵּב זוֹכֶה לְחַיֵּי עוֹלָם הַבָּא, שֶׁאֵינוֹ אֶלָּא הַרְגָּשַׁת קְדוּשָׁה עֶלְיוֹנָה וְאוֹר עֶלְיוֹן
through holiness in the heart meriting eternal life, which is the perception of supernal light;
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרָכוֹת (י״ז עַמּוּד א׳): ״הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא אֵין בּוֹ... אֶלָּא צַדִּיקִים יוֹשְׁבִין... וְנֶהֱנִין מִזִּיו הַשְּׁכִינָה״
as stated in Berachos (17a): "the World to Come contains no eating or drinking... but the righteous sit enjoying the radiance of the Shechinah";
וְשַׁבָּת ״מֵעֵין עוֹלָם הַבָּא״ (שָׁם נ״ז עַמּוּד ב׳), גַּם אָז מַשִּׂיגִין מֵעֵין קְדוּשָׁה זוֹ.
and Shabbat being a foretaste of the World to Come (ibid. 57b), on Shabbat one attains this holiness.
וְזֶהוּ מַה שֶּׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מְקַדְּשָׁם, שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִכְנָס בָּהֶם הַקְּדוּשָׁה בַּלֵּב גַּם בְּכָל שֵׁשֶׁת יְמֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה.
And this is Hashem sanctifying them, infusing holiness into the heart to illuminate all six weekdays.
וְהוּא ״מַתָּנָה טוֹבָה״ שֶׁנָּתַן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לְיִשְׂרָאֵל: שֶׁיְּהֵא בָּהֶם שׁוֹרֶשׁ קְדוּשָׁה קָבוּעַ וְקַיָּים בַּלֵּב מִצַּד הַשְׁפָּעַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
This being the precious gift granted unto Israel: an immutable root of holiness fixed in the heart by Hashem;
מֵאוֹר שְׁכִינָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ הַשּׁוֹכֵן אִתָּם בְּתוֹךְ טֻמְאֹתָם (וַיִּקְרָא ט״ז:ט״ז), גַּם בְּלֹא הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת אָדָם:
from the radiance of His Shechinah dwelling among them in the midst of their defilement (Vayikra 16:16), even without human striving!

אוֹת י׳ — אוֹצַר יִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם בְּבֵית גְּנָזָיו, שַׁבָּת כִּשְׁמָא דְּקֻדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא, וְ״קֻדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא לִבָּא בָּעֵי״ — Section 10: The Treasury of Fear of Heaven, Shabbat as the Divine Name, and God Desiring the Heart

The theme: Shabbat issuing from the treasury of fear of Heaven, perceiving the Divine Presence on Shabbat, and wisdom existing only when rooted in the heart. Hashem said: "I have a precious gift in My treasury". In Berachos (33b), the Sages declare: "The Holy One has nothing in His treasury save the storehouse of fear of Heaven (yir'at Shamayim), as it is said: The fear of Hashem is His treasure (Yeshayah 33:6)". Perforce, Shabbat is drawn from that very treasury! Fear of Heaven depends upon human free choice ("What does Hashem require of you, but to fear", Devarim 10:12); yet Hashem sanctifies Israel even within their free choice, empowering them to choose the good through the Sabbath holiness rooted in the heart, which leads to fear of Heaven. In the Zohar (II, 88b): "What is Shabbat? The Name of the Holy One, blessed is He". In the Future, the righteous will point with their finger: "Lo, this is our God; we have waited for Him" (Yeshayah 25:9; Ta'anit 31a); on Shabbat, Israel attains a foretaste of this direct awareness: "I have set Hashem always before me" (Tehillim 16:8), instilling awe, humility, dread, and bashfulness before Him (Nedarim 20a; Moreh Nevuchim; Rema, Orach Chaim 1:1). Awe resides in the heart: in Sanhedrin (106b) on Doeg and Ahithophel who possessed profound intellect yet lacked fear: "The Holy One desires the heart (Rachmana liba ba'i), for Hashem looks on the heart (I Shmuel 16:7)". Where the heart is absent, intellect is merely "a price in the hand of a fool to buy wisdom, seeing he has no heart" (Mishlei 17:16; Yoma 72b). Since the Holy One is the heart of Israel, one devoid of fear of Heaven lacks a heart, the Shechinah being absent from his interior!
וְאָמַר ״בְּבֵית גְּנָזַי״, וּבִבְרָכוֹת (ל״ג עַמּוּד ב׳) אָמְרוּ: ״דְּאֵין לוֹ לְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בְּבֵית גְּנָזָיו אֶלָּא אוֹצָר שֶׁל יִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם בִּלְבַד״
And Hashem said "in My treasury," and in Berachos (33b) the Sages taught: "the Holy One has nothing in His treasury save the storehouse of fear of Heaven alone";
וְעַל כָּרְחָךְ דְּגַם זֶה [שַׁבָּת] מֵאוֹתוֹ אוֹצָר, דְּזֶה: ״[מָה] ה׳ שֹׁאֵל מֵעִמָּךְ [כִּי אִם לְיִרְאָה]״ (דְּבָרִים י:יב) שֶׁהוּא הַתָּלוּי בִּבְחִירַת אָדָם
and perforce Shabbat derives from that very treasury, this being what Hashem requires: fear of Heaven, which depends upon human choice;
וְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מְקַדְּשָׁם גַּם בִּבְחִירָה זוֹ שֶׁיִּבְחֲרוּ בַּטּוֹב, עַל יְדֵי קְדֻשַּׁת הַשַּׁבָּת שֶׁנִּקְבַּע בַּלֵּב דִּמְבִיאַתּוּ לִידֵי יִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם.
Hashem sanctifying them within their free choice to choose the good, through the Sabbath holiness fixed in the heart that leads to awe.

כִּי עִיקַּר קְדֻשַּׁת שַׁבָּת הַנִּקְבָּע בַּלֵּב הוּא הַהַכָּרָה דְּ״צוּר לְבָבִי וְחֶלְקִי״ (תְּהִלִּים ע״ג:כ״ו), וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּזֹּוהַר (חֵלֶק ב׳ פ״ח עַמּוּד ב׳): ״מַאי שַׁבָּת? — שְׁמָא דְּקֻדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא״

For the essence of Sabbath holiness in the heart is the recognition of "the rock of my heart and my portion," the Zohar (II, 88b) declaring: "What is Shabbat? The Name of the Holy One, blessed is He";

וּכְמוֹ לֶעָתִיד כָּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד מַרְאֶה בְּאֶצְבָּעוֹ: ״[וְאָמַר בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא:] הִנֵּה אֱלֹהֵינוּ זֶה קִוִּינוּ לוֹ [וְיוֹשִׁיעֵנוּ]״ (יְשַׁעְיָה כ״ה:ט׳), כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּסוֹף תַּעֲנִית (ל״א עַמּוּד א׳)
and as in the Future each tzaddik will point with his finger: "Lo, this is our God; we have waited for Him, and He will save us" (Yeshayah 25:9; Ta'anit 31a);
כֵּן זוֹכִין מֵעֵין זֶה בְּשַׁבָּת לְהַכָּרַת הַנֹּכַח דְּ״שִׁוִּיתִי ה׳ לְנֶגְדִּי תָמִיד״ (תְּהִלִּים ט״ז:ח׳)
so on Shabbat one merits a foretaste of this direct presence: "I have set Hashem always before me" (Tehillim 16:8);
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה יַגִּיעַ אֵלָיו הַיִּרְאָה וְהַהַכְנָעָה וּפַחַד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וּבָשְׁתּוֹ מִמֶּנּוּ תָּמִיד (שֶׁהוּא הַיִּרְאָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּנְדָרִים כ׳ עַמּוּד א׳)
through which descend awe, submission, dread, and shame before Him (shame being awe, Nedarim 20a);
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּמוֹרֶה נְבוּכִים (חֵלֶק ג׳ פֶּרֶק נ״ב) הַמּוּבָא בְּהַגָּהַת רַמָ״א רֵישׁ שֻׁלְחָן עָרוּךְ אוֹרַח חַיִּים (סִימָן א׳ סְעִיף א׳).
as cited in Moreh Nevuchim (III, ch. 52) and quoted by the Rema (Orach Chaim 1:1).
וְהַיִּרְאָה הִיא בַּלֵּב, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּיוֹמָא (ע״ב סוֹף עַמּוּד ב׳) עַל פָּסוּק ״וְלֵב אָיִן״ (מִשְׁלֵי י״ז:ט״ז)
And awe resides in the heart: as expounded in Yoma (72b) on "seeing he has no heart" (Mishlei 17:16);
וּבְסַנְהֶדְרִין (ק״ו סוֹף עַמּוּד ב׳): ״רְבוּתָא לְמִיבְעֵי בָּעֵי וְכוּלֵיהּ? — אֶלָּא: קֻדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא לִבָּא בָּעֵי, דִּכְתִיב: ׳וַה׳ יִרְאֶה לַלֵּבָב׳ (שְׁמוּאֵל א ט״ז:ז׳)״
and in Sanhedrin (106b): "Did Doeg and Ahithophel ask great questions?... Rather: the Holy One desires the heart (Rachmana liba ba'i), for it is written: 'Hashem looks on the heart' (I Shmuel 16:7)";
וְהַיְינוּ דְּכַאֲשֶׁר ״לֵב אָיִן״ — חָכְמָתוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא: ״כִּמְחִיר בְּיַד כְּסִיל לִקְנוֹת [חָכְמָה וְלֶב אָיִן]״ (מִשְׁלֵי שָׁם)
meaning where the heart is absent, wisdom is merely "a price in the hand of a fool to buy wisdom, seeing he has no heart" (Mishlei 17:16);
כִּי עִיקַּר הַחָכְמָה כְּשֶׁהִיא קְנוּיָה בַּלֵּב
for authentic wisdom exists only when acquired in the heart;
וּמִי שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ יִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם קָרֵי לֵיהּ ״לֵב אָיִן״
and one lacking fear of Heaven is termed "one who has no heart";
דְּמֵאַחַר שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לִבָּן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל, אִם אֵין הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא שׁוֹכֵן בְּתוֹךְ לִבּוֹ — הֲרֵי ״לֵב אָיִן״:
for since the Holy One is the heart of Israel, if He dwells not within his heart, the heart is entirely absent!

אוֹת י״א — קְדֻשַּׁת הַלֵּב כְּבֵית קֹדֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁים, יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים, וְ״מָשְׁכֵנִי אַחֲרֶיךָ נָּרוּצָה״ בְּשַׁבָּת — Section 11: The Heart as the Holy of Holies, Yom Kippur, and "Draw Me, We Will Run After You" on Shabbat

The theme: The human heart mirroring the Holy of Holies entered by the High Priest on Yom Kippur, Jacob as the pure heart, and Shabbat drawing the soul into the weekdays. The sanctity of the heart in man is the sanctity of the Holy of Holies (Beit Kodesh HaKodashim) in the world, as stated repeatedly in the holy Zohar. In Berachos (30a), one praying must direct his heart toward the Holy of Holies. Into that chamber none may enter save the High Priest on Yom Kippur, when "from all your sins before Hashem you shall be clean" (Vayikra 16:30)—when all sins veiling the light are expiated. The High Priest was the most consecrated soul in Israel ("and Aaron was separated, that he should be sanctified as most holy", I Divrei HaYamim 23:13). "And there shall be no man in the tent of meeting when he goes in to make atonement in the holy place" (Vayikra 16:17)—the Sages expounding: even the angels whose faces are like human faces cannot enter, but Hashem alone in His glory, for there is the absolute union and cleaving of Israel unto their Father in Heaven! This is the spiritual rung of our father Jacob, who represents the heart and the body (liba v'gufa), whose heart was completely pure without any trace of "no heart" or worldly desire. Jacob embodied awe and chastity: "Surely the fear of God is not in this place; and they will slay me for my wife's sake" (Bereishis 20:11). Therefore in Jacob began the revelation of Sabbath holiness: "and he encamped before the city" (Bereishis 33:18)—establishing Sabbath boundaries (Bereishis Rabbah 79:6). On Shabbat, the worlds ascend and Hashem draws Israel unto Himself, like a laborer drawing in his breath when resting from his work. On this Scripture states: "Draw me, we will run after You" (Shir HaShirim 1:4)—"Draw me" on Shabbat, through which "we will run after You" throughout the secular workdays!
וּקְדֻשַּׁת הַלֵּב בָּאָדָם — הוּא קְדֻשַּׁת בֵּית קֹדֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁים בָּעוֹלָם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ כַּמָּה פְּעָמִים בַּזֹּוהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
And the holiness of the heart in man—is the sanctity of the Holy of Holies in the universe, as stated repeatedly in the Zohar;
וְכִידוּעַ שֶׁזֶּה רָמוּז בִּבְרָכוֹת (ל׳ עַמּוּד א׳): ״יְכַוֵּון אֶת לִבּוֹ כְּנֶגֶד בֵּית קֹדֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁים״
and as hinted in Berachos (30a): "he should direct his heart toward the Holy of Holies";
וּלְשָׁם אֵין נִכְנָס אֶלָּא כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים
and into that chamber none enters save the High Priest on Yom Kippur;
דְּאָז: ״[כִּי בַיּוֹם הַזֶּה יְכַפֵּר עֲלֵיכֶם לְטַהֵר אֶתְכֶם,] מִכֹּל חַטֹּאתֵיכֶם לִפְנֵי ה׳ תִּטְהָרוּ״ (וַיִּקְרָא ט״ז:ל׳)
when: "from all your sins before Hashem you shall be clean" (Vayikra 16:30);
כְּשֶׁהֵם ״לִפְנֵי ה׳״ הֲרֵי הֵם נִטְהָרִים מִכָּל חֵטְא, וְאֵין בְּיָדָם עָוֹן הַמַּאֲפִיל אוֹתוֹ אוֹר וּמַעֲלִים הַקְּדוּשָׁה.
standing "before Hashem" purified of all sin, no transgression veiling the light or concealing holiness.
וְהַכֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל הוּא הַנֶּפֶשׁ הַיּוֹתֵר מְקוּדָּשׁ שֶׁבְּיִשְׂרָאֵל, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ: ״וַיִּבָּדֵל אַהֲרֹן לְהַקְדִּישׁוֹ קֹדֶשׁ קָדָשִׁים״ (דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים א כ״ג:י״ג)
And the High Priest is the most consecrated soul in Israel: "and Aaron was separated, that he should be sanctified as most holy" (I Divrei HaYamim 23:13);
וְ״כָל אָדָם לֹא יִהְיֶה בְּאֹהֶל מוֹעֵד [בְּבֹאוֹ לְכַפֵּר בַּקֹּדֶשׁ עַד צֵאתוֹ]״ (וַיִּקְרָא ט״ז:י״ז)
and "there shall be no man in the tent of meeting when he goes in to make atonement in the holy place" (Vayikra 16:17);
וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה: ״אֲפִילּוּ אוֹתָם שֶׁדְּמוּת פְּנֵיהֶם פְּנֵי אָדָם״ (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה כ״א:י״ב; יְרוּשַׁלְמִי יוֹמָא פֶּרֶק ה׳ הֲלָכָה ב׳), דְּגַם מַלְאָכִים אֵין נִכְנָסִין לְשָׁם
the Sages expounding: "even those whose faces are like human faces" (angels) cannot enter there;
אֶלָּא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בִּכְבוֹדוֹ וּבְעַצְמוֹ, כִּי שָׁם הוּא הַיִּחוּד וְהַדְּבֵיקוּת הַגָּמוּר שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל לַאֲבִיהֶם שֶׁבַּשָּׁמַיִם.
but the Holy One in His glory alone, for there is the absolute union of Israel unto their Father in Heaven.
וְהוּא דַּרְגָּא דְּיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁהוּא ״לִבָּא וְגוּפָא״ כַּנּוֹדָע
And this is the rung of our father Jacob who is the Heart and the Body (liba v'gufa);
כִּי לְבָבוֹ הָיָה זַךְ לְגַמְרֵי, שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה בוֹ רוֹשֶׁם מִ״לֵּב אָיִן״ וְשׁוּם נְטִיָּה לְתַאֲווֹת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְעֵיל.
his heart being completely pure, without any trace of "no heart" or worldly lust as I wrote above.
וְזֶהוּ עִיקַּר הַיִּרְאָה: בְּהַגְדָּרָה מִתַּאֲווֹת, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ: ״[כִּי אָמַרְתִּי] רַק אֵין יִרְאַת אֱלֹהִים בַּמָּקוֹם הַזֶּה, [וַהֲרָגוּנִי] עַל דְּבַר אִשְׁתִּי״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית כ:יא)
And this is the core of awe: restraint from lusts: "Because I thought: Surely the fear of God is not in this place; and they will slay me for my wife's sake" (Bereishis 20:11);
וְשׁוֹרֶשׁ הַקְּדוּשָׁה, וְעַל כֵּן אֶצְלוֹ הָיָה הַתְחָלַת הִתְגַּלּוּת קְדֻשַּׁת הַשַּׁבָּת
and the root of holiness, wherefore in Jacob began the revelation of Sabbath holiness;
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה ע״ט:ו׳) עַל פָּסוּק ״וַיִּחַן אֶת פְּנֵי הָעִיר״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית ל״ג:י״ח): שֶׁקָּבַע תְּחוּמִין
as stated in Bereishis Rabbah (79:6) on "and he encamped before the city" (Bereishis 33:18): that he established Shabbat boundaries;
וְזֶהוּ הַתְחָלַת הַקְּדוּשָׁה שֶׁמִּצַּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁהוּא מֵאִיר לְזֶרַע יַעֲקֹב
this being the inception of holiness from Hashem radiating upon Jacob's seed;

שֶׁצוּרָתוֹ חֲקוּקָה בְּכִסֵּא הַכָּבוֹד (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה ס״ח:י״ב), שֶׁמִּשָּׁם מַחְצַב כָּל הַנְּפָשׁוֹת דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל מִצּוּרַת אָדָם שֶׁעַל הַכִּסֵּא (יְחֶזְקֵאל א:כו), דְּ״אַתֶּם — קְרוּיִם ׳אָדָם׳״ (יְבָמוֹת ס״א עַמּוּד א׳).
whose image is engraved on the Throne of Glory (Bereishis Rabbah 68:12), whence all Jewish souls are hewn from the Man upon the Throne (Yechezkel 1:26): "you are called Adam" (Yevamos 61a).
רַק לְפִי שֶׁלְּרִיחוּק הַהִשְׁתַּלְשְׁלוּת מֵעוֹלָם לְעוֹלָם עַד עוֹלָם הַגַּשְׁמִי וְהַגּוּפָנִי כְּבָר נִכְהָה הָאוֹר, וְכֹחוֹת הַגּוּפָנִים מַאֲפִילִים וּמַעֲכִירִים
Except that through the descent across worlds down into physical reality the light grew dim, bodily forces darkening and clouding the vision;
וְעַל כֵּן הוּא קְדֻשַּׁת יוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת שֶׁאָז הַעֲלָאַת הָעוֹלָמוֹת כַּנּוֹדָע, וְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מוֹשְׁכֵנוּ אֵלָיו
wherefore the holiness of Shabbat arrives when the worlds ascend, the Holy One drawing us unto Himself;
כִּידוּעַ מִמְּשִׁיכַת הַנְּשִׁימָה אֵלָיו הָעוֹשֶׂה בִּמְלָאכָה כְּשֶׁשּׁוֹבֵת מִמְּלַאכְתּוֹ
like the drawing of the breath of a laborer when resting from his physical work;
וְזֶהוּ הַמְשָׁכַת נִשְׁמַת חַיִּים שֶׁבָּאָדָם אֶל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּיוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת
this being the elevation of the breath of life within man unto the Blessed Name on Shabbat;
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: ״מָשְׁכֵנִי — אַחֲרֶיךָ נָּרוּצָה״ (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים א:ד):
concerning which it is said: "Draw me, we will run after You" (Shir HaShirim 1:4):
״מָשְׁכֵנִי״ — הוּא בְּיוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת;
"Draw me"—is on the day of Shabbat;
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה: ״אַחֲרֶיךָ נָּרוּצָה״ — גַּם בִּימוֹת הַחוֹל.
through which "we will run after You"—even throughout the secular weekdays!
וְזֶהוּ הַתְחָלַת קְדֻשַּׁת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בַּתּוֹלָדָה וְשָׁרְשָׁם מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם מַה שֶּׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מְקַדְּשָׁם, וְהוּא בִּפְנִימִיּוּת הַלֵּב:
And this is the inception of Israel's congenital holiness from Heaven wherewith Hashem sanctifies them, residing in the inward heart!

אוֹת י״ב — מִדַּת הַצְּפוֹנִי בַּיֵּצֶר הָרָע, שְׂעִיר עֲזָאזֵל, וְנִפְלַת עֻזָּא וַעֲזָאֵל לְהָרֵי חֹשֶׁךְ — Section 12: The Hidden Yetzer as the "Tzefoni", The Scapegoat, and the Fall of Uzza and Azael

The theme: The seventh name of the yetzer hara ("the Hidden One"), its expulsion into the wilderness like the scapegoat, and the fallen angels Uzza and Azael cast into the Mountains of Darkness. Inborn evil originates in the foreskin, which is an external superfluous tissue covering the organ of desire, destined to be excised through circumcision. The hypocritical asceticism of Shechem was willing to circumcise the body, but not for Heaven—merely to sate his desire for Dinah. Initially, holiness is hidden in the depths of the heart while evil is manifest on the body's exterior; but at the culmination, the reverse occurs! The seventh and final name of the yetzer hara is Tzefoni (the "Hidden One", Joel 2:20), because it hides (tzafun) within the human heart (Sukkah 52a). Once it becomes master of the house, it hides in secret, even permitting man to study Torah and perform mitzvos in order to nurse greater vitality for the unholy husks: "But unto the wicked God says: What have you to do to declare My statutes?" (Tehillim 50:16). Sukkah (52b) states: "for he has done great things" (Joel 2:20)—the yetzer attacks Israel more than the nations, and scholars more than all others! Hashem is destined to banish this Tzefoni into a barren and desolate land (Joel 2:20), like the scapegoat sent into the wilderness to Azazel. In Yoma (67b), the scapegoat atones for the rebellion of the fallen angels Uzza and Azael (Rashi ad loc.). In Zohar Balak (194a) on Balaam: "falling and having his eyes open" (Bamidbar 24:4)—referring to Uzza and Azael who fell into the Mountains of Darkness (harei choshech). Creation was structured so that darkness precedes light (reisha chashocha v'hadar nehora, Berachos 2b). When those angels protested the creation of man, Hashem cast them down into this world of darkness, proving that once exposed to the realm of physical concealment, they sank into defilement so deeply that they could never emerge!
וְהַתְחָלַת הָרָע שֶׁבַּתּוֹלָדָה וּמִן הַשָּׁמַיִם — הוּא בְּעוֹר הָעָרְלָה
And the inception of congenital evil from Heaven—is in the skin of the foreskin;
שֶׁהוּא [בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת חִיצוֹנִיּוּתוֹ לְבַד, וְאֵין לוֹ שׁוּם שַׁיָּיכוּת לִפְנִימִיּוּתוֹ, אֲפִילּוּ לִפְנִימִיּוּת הַגּוּף, שֶׁאֵינוֹ אֶלָּא עוֹר בַּגּוּף] מוֹתְרוֹת הַגּוּף
being [manifest merely on the external surface without connection to the inward essence, being merely outer skin] a bodily superfluity;
וְעוֹמֶדֶת לְהֵיחָתֵךְ בַּמִּילָה שֶׁהִיא בָּאָה לְהַגְדָּרַת תַּאֲוָה שֶׁבְּאוֹתוֹ אֵבֶר כַּנּוֹדָע.
destined to be severed in circumcision which arrives to fence the desire of that organ as is known.
וְיֵשׁ פָּרוּשׁ שִׁכְמִי שֶׁרוֹצֶה לִפְרוֹשׁ מִתַּאֲווֹת אֲבָל לֹא לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם, רַק כְּדֵי לְמַלֹּאות עַל יְדֵי זֶה תַּאֲוָתוֹ
And there is the asceticism of Shechem who seeks to withdraw from desire not for Heaven, but to sate his lust;
כִּשְׁכֶם שֶׁרָצָה בַּמִּילָה הַמַּגְדֶּרֶת תַּאֲוָה כְּדֵי לְמַלֹּאות תַּאֲוָתוֹ וְחֶשְׁקוֹ בְּדִינָה
like Shechem who submitted to circumcision to sate his desire for Dinah;
וְזֶהוּ מִצַּד הַתְחָלַת הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע בְּשׁוֹרֶשׁ הָרָע שֶׁמִּצַּד תְּחִלַּת הַבְּרִיאָה מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
this reflecting the inception of the yetzer in the root of evil created by Hashem;
נֶגֶד הַתְחָלַת הַקְּדוּשָׁה שֶׁמֵּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, וּבָזֶה הַקְּדוּשָׁה הִתְגַּלּוּתָהּ רַק בְּעֹומֶק הַלֵּב וְהָרָע בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת בְּפֹעַל בְּחִיצוֹנִיּוּת הַגּוּף.
opposite the inception of holiness from Hashem, where holiness is hidden in the heart's depths while evil is manifest on the body's exterior.
וְהַסּוֹף הוּא בְּהֵיפוּךְ:
And at the culmination it is the exact reverse:
דְּשֵׁם הַשְּׁבִיעִי מִשְּׁמוֹת הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע הוּא ״צְפוֹנִי״ (יוֹאֵל ב:כ), עַל שֵׁם שֶׁצָּפוּן וְעוֹמֵד בְּלִבּוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּסֻכָּה שָׁם (נ״ב עַמּוּד א׳)
For the seventh name of the yetzer hara is Tzefoni (the "Hidden One", Joel 2:20), because it stands hidden (tzafun) in the human heart (Sukkah 52a);
וְהַיְינוּ דְּאַחַר שֶׁנַּעֲשָׂה ״בַּעַל הַבַּיִת״ וְנִכְנַס לְמַעֲמַקֵּי הַלֵּב, אָז הוּא עוֹמֵד צָפוּן שָׁם שֶׁאֵינוֹ בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת
meaning once it becomes the "master of the house" and enters the inward heart, it hides in secret without overt manifestation;
וְכִידוּעַ עַל פָּסוּק: ״וְלָרָשָׁע אָמַר אֱלֹהִים: מַה לְּךָ לְסַפֵּר חֻקָּי [וַתִּשָּׂא בְרִיתִי עֲלֵי פִיךָ]״ (תְּהִלִּים נ:טז), כִּי בָּזֶה מוֹסִיף חַס וְשָׁלוֹם כֹּחַ בַּקְּלִיפָּה
as known on: "But unto the wicked God says: What have you to do to declare My statutes?" (Tehillim 50:16), for through this he adds power to the unholy husk;
וְעַל כֵּן אַחַר שֶׁנִּקְבַּע הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע בַּלֵּב, הוּא מַנִּיחוֹ אֵיזֶה פְּעָמִים לַעֲסוֹק בַּתּוֹרָה וּמִצְוֹת גַּם כֵּן שֶׁיְּהֵא לוֹ יְנִיקָה יוֹתֵר עַל יְדֵי זֶה כַּנּוֹדָע.
wherefore the yetzer permits him at times to engage in Torah and mitzvos so that the husks may suckle greater vitality.
וְעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ שָׁם (סֻכָּה נ״ב עַמּוּד ב׳): ״׳כִּי הִגְדִּיל לַעֲשׂוֹת׳ (יוֹאֵל ב:כ) — שֶׁמִּתְגָּרֶה בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל יוֹתֵר מֵאוּמּוֹת, וּבְתַלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים יוֹתֵר מִכּוּלָּם״.
And concerning this the Gemara expounds (Sukkah 52b): "'for he has done great things' (Joel 2:20)—attacking Israel more than the nations, and scholars more than all others".
וְזֶהוּ כֹּחַ ״הַצְּפוֹנִי״ הַזֶּה, שֶׁהוּא מַדְרֵיגָה הָאַחֲרוֹנָה שֶׁבְּכֹחוֹת הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע
And this is the power of the Tzefoni, the final stage among the faculties of the yetzer hara;
שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עָתִיד לַהֲדִיחוֹ: ״[וְאֶת הַצְּפוֹנִי אַרְחִיק מֵכֶם, וְהִדַּחְתִּיו] אֶל אֶרֶץ צִיָּה וּשְׁמָמָה״ (יוֹאֵל ב:כ), מְקוֹם שֶׁאֵין בְּנֵי אָדָם מְצוּיִם
which Hashem is destined to banish: "into a land barren and desolate" (Joel 2:20), where no human beings dwell;
דּוּגְמַת הַשָּׂעִיר הַנּוֹשֵׂא עֲווֹנוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶל אֶרֶץ גְּזֵרָה לַעֲזָאזֵל הַמִּדְבָּרָה (וַיִּקְרָא ט״ז:כ״א–כ״ב)
like the scapegoat bearing the iniquities of Israel unto a solitary land to Azazel into the wilderness (Vayikra 16:21–22);
וְאִיתָא בְּיוֹמָא (ס״ז סוֹף עַמּוּד ב׳): ״לְכַפֵּר עַל מַעֲשֵׂה עוּזָּא וַעֲזָאֵל״, עַיֵּין שָׁם בְּרַשִׁ״י
and in Yoma (67b): "to atone for the deeds of Uzza and Azael," see Rashi there;

וְיָדוּעַ מִזֹּוהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ פָּרָשַׁת בָּלָק (קצ״ד עַמּוּד ב׳) עַל פָּסוּק: ״אֲשֶׁר מַחֲזֵה [שַׁדַּי יֶחֱזֶה,] נֹפֵל וּגְלוּי עֵינָיִם״ (בַּמִּדְבָּר כ״ד:ד׳): דְּהֵם עֻזָּא וַעֲזָאֵל הַנִּזְכָּרִים שֶׁנִּקְרְאוּ כֵּן בִּנְפִילָתָם
and as known from Zohar Balak (194b) on "falling and having his eyes open" (Bamidbar 24:4): referring to Uzza and Azael named thus in their fall;
שֶׁנָּפְלוּ לְהָרֵי חֹשֶׁךְ הַנִּקְרָאִים ״הַרְרֵי קֶדֶם״, שֶׁהוּא הַחֲשׁוֹכָא שֶׁקָּדַם לִנְהוֹרָא
falling unto the Mountains of Darkness (harei choshech) called the Mountains of the East, which is the darkness preceding light;

הַיְינוּ בִּבְרִיָּתוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּרֵישׁ בְּרָכוֹת (ב׳ עַמּוּד ב׳): שֶׁכָּךְ הָיָה הָרָצוֹן יִתְבָּרַךְ בִּבְרִיאַת הָעוֹלָם שֶׁיְּהֵא חֹשֶׁךְ וְהֶעְלֵם הָאוֹר, וְאַחַר כָּךְ יַשִּׂיג הָאָדָם הָאוֹר.
matching the order of Creation: "first darkness and then light" (Berachos 2b), Hashem willing that darkness conceal the light so that man achieve the light through free choice.
וְאוֹתָם מַלְאָכִים קִטְרְגוּ עַל הָאָדָם, וְהִפִּילָם הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לְהַרְאוֹתָם:
And those angels prosecuted against the creation of man, wherefore Hashem cast them down to demonstrate unto them:
שֶׁכְּשֶׁהֵם יָבוֹאוּ לְהַאי עָלְמָא הַדּוֹמֶה לְלַיְלָה מְקוֹם הַחֹשֶׁךְ וְהֶעְלֵם הָאוֹר
that when they descend into this world which resembles night, the realm of darkness and concealment;
יֻשְׁקְעוּ בַּחֹשֶׁךְ יוֹתֵר, עַד שֶׁלֹּא יוּכְלוּ לָצֵאת כְּלָל:
they would sink into defilement so deeply that they could never emerge!

10.h: יִשְׂרָאֵל קְדוֹשִׁים — פֶּרֶק י׳, סְעִיפִים י״ג–י״ח

אוֹת י״ג — מַחֲזֵה שַׁדַּי בִּיסוֹד, יִחוּדָא עִילָּאָה וְיִחוּדָא תַּתָּאָה, וּקְרִיאַת שְׁמַע דְּיַעֲקֹב וּבָנָיו — Section 13: The Vision of the Holy Name in Yesod, Supernal and Lower Unification, and the Shema of Jacob and His Sons

The theme: The Holy Name in Sefirat Yesod, the world as concealment (he'elem), and the two tiers of divine unity in the Shema and Baruch Shem Kevod Malkhuto. The vision (machazeh) of the Holy Name Shaddai belongs unto Sefirat Yesod, which governs the holiness of the covenant (brit kodesh) within the seed of Israel. The Name Shaddai denotes: "He Who said unto the world: Enough! (she-amar l'olamo dai, Chagigah 12a)", for olam (world) shares the root of he'elem (concealment). The creation of the universe concealed His absolute Oneness—for prior to Creation He and His Name were One alone, and in ultimate truth "You are the same before the world was created, and You are the same since the world was created," the whole earth being full of His glory and there being none else besides Him. Israel perceives this light from within the darkness, declaring His Oneness twice daily. When Jacob’s sons proclaimed: "Hear, O Israel: Hashem our God, Hashem is One... just as there is no division in your heart, so is there no division in our hearts," Jacob answered: "Blessed be the Name of the glory of His Kingdom forever and ever" (Pesachim 56a). The proclamation of the Shema is Yichuda Ila'ah (Supernal Unification)—the primordial Oneness prior to Creation, which was Jacob's uninterrupted perception, wherefore he never died and possessed no spiritual dross. Jacob sought to reveal the final End (Ketz), the ultimate manifestation that all is holy; when the Shechinah departed, he feared dross existed in his offspring. His sons reassured him that in their inward hearts they likewise perceive absolute Oneness, but their perception must wrestle through the cosmic concealment of post-Creation reality (Yichuda Tata'ah, Lower Unification). On this Jacob responded: "Blessed be the Name of the glory of His Kingdom forever and ever," for an earthly kingdom requires a nation (ein melech b'lo am), mirroring the night wherein Israel remains "faithful believers, the children of faithful believers" (Shabbat 97a), cleaving unto Him in darkness: "though I sit in darkness, Hashem shall be a light unto me" (Michah 7:8)!

p: וְהֵם נִקְרָאִים ״מַחֲזֵה״ שֶׁל הַשֵּׁם הַקָּדוֹשׁ דִּסְפִירַת הַיְסוֹד [שַׁדַּ״י], כִּידוּעַ דְּאוֹתוֹ שֵׁם מוֹרֶה עַל קְדֻשַּׁת הַבְּרִית קֹדֶשׁ שֶׁבְּזֶרַע יִשְׂרָאֵל
And they are designated the "vision" (machazeh) of the Holy Divine Name of Sefirat Yesod [Shaddai], as is known that this Name denotes the holiness of the sacred covenant within the seed of Israel;
וְהוּא ״שֶׁאָמַר לְעוֹלָמוֹ: דַּי!״ (חֲגִיגָה י״ב עַמּוּד א׳), כִּי ״עוֹלָם״ — לְשׁוֹן ״הֶעְלֵם״
being the Name through which "He said unto His world: Enough!" (Chagigah 12a), for "world" (olam) shares the linguistic root of "concealment" (he'elem);
שֶׁזֶּה עִנְיַן בְּרִיאַת עוֹלָם: שֶׁהוּא הַמַּעֲלִים אַחְדוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ
this being the inner nature of the creation of the cosmos: acting as a veil concealing His Blessed Oneness;
שֶׁקּוֹדֶם שֶׁנִּבְרָא הָעוֹלָם הָיָה הוּא וּשְׁמוֹ אֶחָד (פִּרְקֵי דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר פֶּרֶק ג׳).
for prior to the creation of the universe, He and His Name were One alone (Pirkei d'Rabbi Eliezer ch. 3).
וּבֶאֱמֶת ״אַתָּה הוּא עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִבְרָא הָעוֹלָם, אַתָּה הוּא מִשֶּׁנִּבְרָא הָעוֹלָם״
And in absolute truth: "You are the same before the world was created, You are the same since the world was created";
דְּגַם עַתָּה הוּא אֶחָד מַמָּשׁ כְּמִקּוֹדֶם, דִּ״מְלֹא כָל הָאָרֶץ כְּבוֹדוֹ״ (יְשַׁעְיָה ו:ג), וְ״אֵין עוֹד מִלְּבַדּוֹ״ (דְּבָרִים ד:לה)
for even now He is in literal truth One exactly as before, "the whole earth being full of His glory" (Yeshayah 6:3), and "there is none else beside Him" (Devarim 4:35);
אֶלָּא שֶׁהָעוֹלָם וּמְלוֹאוֹ הַנִּרְאָה כִּבְרוּאִים נִפְרָדִים מַעֲלִים זֶה
save that the universe and its fullness, appearing as differentiated creations, veils this reality;
וְיִשְׂרָאֵל מַכִּירִים הָאוֹר מִתּוֹךְ הַחֹשֶׁךְ, וּמְיַחֲדִים שְׁמוֹ פַּעֲמַיִם בְּכָל יוֹם.
while Israel perceives the light from within the darkness, proclaiming the Oneness of His Name twice daily.
וּכְשֶׁאָמְרוּ לוֹ בָּנָיו לְיַעֲקֹב: ״שְׁמַע יִשְׂרָאֵל... כְּשֵׁם שֶׁאֵין בְּלִבְּךָ [אֶלָּא אֶחָד, כָּךְ אֵין בְּלִבֵּנוּ אֶלָּא אֶחָד]״
And when the sons of Jacob proclaimed unto him: "Hear, O Israel... just as there is in your heart only One, so is there in our heart only One";
אָמַר: ״בָּרוּךְ שֵׁם כְּבוֹד מַלְכוּתוֹ לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד״, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּפְסָחִים (נ״ו עַמּוּד א׳)
Jacob responded: "Blessed be the Name of the glory of His Kingdom forever and ever," as stated in Pesachim (56a);
דִּ״שְׁמַע וְכוּלֵיהּ״ הוּא יִחוּדָא עִילָּאָה, הַיְינוּ יִחוּד הַגָּמוּר דְּקּוֹדֶם שֶׁנִּבְרָא הָעוֹלָם
for "Hear, O Israel, etc." is Yichuda Ila'ah (Supernal Unification), the primordial Oneness prior to Creation;
וְזֶהוּ הָאוֹר שֶׁהִשִּׂיג יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, שֶׁזָּכָה דְּלֹא מֵת וְשֶׁאֵין בְּמִטָּתוֹ פְּסֹולֶת
this being the transcendent light perceived by our father Jacob, through which he never died and possessed no spiritual dross;
כִּי זָכָה לַיִּחוּד הַגָּמוּר דְּ״אֵין עוֹד מִלְּבַדּוֹ״ שֶׁאֵין שׁוּם פְּסוּל וּפְסֹולֶת כְּלָל.
having attained absolute union with "there is none else beside Him," wherein no defect or blemish can exist.
וְעַל כֵּן חָשַׁב לְגַלּוֹת הַקֵּץ, שֶׁהוּא גִּילּוּי הָאוֹר הַזֶּה: שֶׁאֵין בַּמְּצִיאוּת שׁוּם פְּסֹולֶת, כִּי כּוּלּוֹ קֹדֶשׁ לַה׳
Wherefore Jacob sought to reveal the final End (Ketz, Pesachim 56a), which is the revelation of this light: that no dross exists in ultimate reality, all being holy unto Hashem;
וּכְשֶׁרָאָה שֶׁנִּסְתַּלְּקָה שְׁכִינָה, נִתְיָירֵא: אוּלַי בֶּאֱמֶת יֵשׁ פְּסֹולֶת
and when he saw the Shechinah depart, he grew anxious: perhaps unholy dross truly lingered;
וְעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ: ״כְּשֵׁם שֶׁאֵין בְּלִבְּךָ וְכוּלֵיהּ״ — דְּהַיְינוּ בַּלֵּב גַּם אָנוּ מַכִּירִים הַיִּחוּד הַגָּמוּר כְּמוֹ בְּלִבְּךָ מַמָּשׁ
upon which his sons declared: "just as there is none in your heart, etc."—meaning within our inward hearts we likewise perceive absolute Oneness exactly like your heart;

רַק הַחִילּוּק: דְּאֶצְלָם הַהַכָּרָה מִתּוֹךְ הֶעְלֵם הַחֹשֶׁךְ דְּאַחַר שֶׁנִּבְרָא הָעוֹלָם, וְאֵינוֹ בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת גָּמוּר כְּמוֹ אֵצֶל יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁהָיָה חִיצוֹנִיּוּתוֹ מְזוּכָּךְ לְגַמְרֵי

the distinction being: with them this recognition must be forged through the dark concealment of post-Creation reality, not being outwardly manifest as with Jacob whose physical exterior was totally purified;
וְעַל כֵּן אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְגַלּוֹת עַדַיִין, וְעַל זֶה אָמַר: ״בָּרוּךְ שֵׁם כְּבוֹד מַלְכוּתוֹ לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד״
wherefore the End could not yet be revealed, upon which Jacob answered: "Blessed be the Name of the glory of His Kingdom forever and ever";
שֶׁהוּא יִחוּדָא תַּתָּאָה, שֶׁמִּצַּד מִדַּת מַלְכוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ הַמִּתְגַּלָּה בָּעוֹלָם.
this being Yichuda Tata'ah (Lower Unification), reflecting the attribute of His Kingdom manifest within the cosmos.
שֶׁעַל זֶה הָיָה בְּרִיאַת הָעוֹלָם, דְּ״אֵין מֶלֶךְ בְּלֹא עָם״ (פִּרְקֵי דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר פֶּרֶק ג׳)
For unto this purpose was the universe created, for "there is no king without a people" (Pirkei d'Rabbi Eliezer ch. 3);
וְזֶהוּ מִדַּת ״לַיְלָה״ כַּנּוֹדָע, דְּהַיְינוּ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה הֶעְלֵם וְחֹשֶׁךְ
this being the attribute of "night," meaning the presence of cosmic concealment and darkness;
וְעִם כָּל זֶה: ״[כִּי אֵשֵׁב בַּחֹשֶׁךְ] — ה׳ אוֹר לִי״ (מִיכָה ז:ח), מִצַּד: ״וֶאֱמוּנָתְךָ — בַּלֵּילוֹת״ (תְּהִלִּים צ״ב:ג׳)
and nevertheless: "though I sit in darkness, Hashem shall be a light unto me" (Michah 7:8), through: "and Your faithfulness in the nights" (Tehillim 92:3);
עַל יְדֵי תֹּקֶף הָאֱמוּנָה שֶׁיֵּשׁ לְזֶרַע יִשְׂרָאֵל, ״מַאֲמִינִים בְּנֵי מַאֲמִינִים״ (שַׁבָּת צ״ז עַמּוּד א׳)
through the fierce faith of the seed of Israel, "believers, the children of believers" (Shabbat 97a);
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין מַשִּׂיגִים אוֹר הַבָּהִיר בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת הַלֵּב בְּ״אוֹר פְּנֵי מֶלֶךְ חַיִּים״ (מִשְׁלֵי ט״ז:ט״ו)
and though they do not perceive the radiant light openly in the conscious heart as "in the light of the king's countenance is life" (Mishlei 16:15);
מִכָּל מָקוֹם הֵם מַאֲמִינִים הַיִּחוּד אֱמוּנָה שְׁלֵימָה בַּלֵּב שֶׁ״אֵין עוֹד מִלְּבַדּוֹ״, אַף שֶׁאֵינוֹ מוּרְגָּשׁ לָהֶם בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת גָּמוּר:
nevertheless they believe in His Oneness with absolute heart-faith that there is none else beside Him, even when not consciously felt in open manifestation!

אוֹת י״ד — צַדִּיק יְסוֹד עוֹלָם: שֶׁאָמַר לְעוֹלָמוֹ דַּי, הֶעְלֵם הַבְּרִיאָה בַּעֲשָׂרָה מַאֲמָרוֹת, וּמִדַּת הַבְּחִירָה — Section 14: The Righteous as the Foundation, Saying "Enough" to the Concealment, and The Ten Creative Utterances

The theme: Sefirat Yesod as the balance of cosmic concealment, cutting the foreskin to discover light, and why the world was created through Ten Utterances. "The righteous is the foundation of the world (tzaddik yesod olam, Mishlei 10:25)"—he is the foundation of the concealment (yesod ha-he'elem), for olam denotes he'elem (concealment). The spiritual labor of the Tzaddik is to attain divine perception even within concealment, accomplished through excising the foreskin that veils the holy covenant. The foreskin represents submersion in worldly desires which darken the divine light in the heart, answering to the primordial darkness of Creation (reisha chashocha). Creation was brought into existence specifically to act as a concealing veil, which is the root of evil inherent within physical existence. This is the Holy Name Shaddai in Yesod, which declared unto the world: "Enough (Dai)!"—meaning: this degree of concealment suffices! Had the concealment been deeper, the light could never have been recovered; had it been less, darkness would not have challenged man, eliminating free choice. God made man upright (Koheles 7:29) so that through his own effort he could tear the veil, cut the foreskin, and perceive the light out of the darkness. Divine wisdom calibrated the precise degree of concealment across both worlds to preserve free choice, as the Mishnah teaches: "By ten utterances was the world created... to give a good reward to the righteous and to punish the wicked" (Avos 5:1). These correspond to the ten categories of cosmic concealment. Were the darkness less intense, the reward of the righteous would be diminished because the light would be effortless; were the darkness more intense, the wicked could not be punished, being entirely coerced by impenetrable blindness. Free choice exists precisely because Creation was calibrated with exact contraction (tzimtzum), neither less nor more, reflecting the Name Shaddai which provides sufficient light for every soul to perceive according to its capacity!
וְ״צַדִּיק — יְסוֹד עוֹלָם״ (מִשְׁלֵי י:כה), זֶהוּ יְסוֹד הַהֶעְלֵם, דְּ״עוֹלָם״ — לְשׁוֹן ״הֶעְלֵם״
And "the righteous is the foundation of the world" (Mishlei 10:25)—he is the foundation of the concealment, for "world" (olam) shares the root of "concealment" (he'elem);
וְהַיְינוּ לְהַשִּׂיג גַּם בַּהֶעְלֵם, וְהוּא עַל יְדֵי הֲסָרַת הָעָרְלָה הַמְכַסָּה וּמַעֲלֶמֶת קְדֻשַּׁת בְּרִית
meaning to attain perception even within concealment, accomplished through removing the foreskin that veils the covenant;
שֶׁהוּא הַשִּׁיקּוּעַ בְּתַאֲווֹת הָעוֹלָם הַמַּשְׁכִּיחִים וּמַחְשִׁיכִים אוֹרוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁבַּלֵּב.
which is submersion in worldly desires that obscure the divine light in the heart.
וְזֶהוּ הַחֲשׁוֹכָא שֶׁבְּרֵישָׁא בַּבְּרִיאָה (בְּרָכוֹת ב׳ עַמּוּד ב׳)
And this is the primordial darkness at the inception of Creation (Berachos 2b);
דְּכְלַל הַבְּרִיאָה דְּעוֹלָם הָיָה לְכַוָּונָה זוֹ: שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לְדָבָר הַמַּעֲלִים
the entire creation of the cosmos having been intended to serve as a concealing veil;
וְזֶהוּ שׁוֹרֶשׁ הָרָע שֶׁבַּתּוֹלָדָה וּבַבְּרִיאָה כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל
this being the root of inborn evil in Creation as explained above;
הַיְינוּ מַה שֶּׁרָצָה הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה ״עוֹלָם״ שֶׁהוּא ״הֶעְלֵם״.
namely Hashem willing that there exist a "world" (olam) which is a "concealment" (he'elem).
וְזֶהוּ הַשֵּׁם הַקָּדוֹשׁ דִּיסוֹד [שַׁדַּ״י] שֶׁאָמַר לְעוֹלָמוֹ: ״דַּי!״
And this is the Holy Name of Yesod [Shaddai] which declared unto His world: "Enough!";
הַיְינוּ: דְּדַי בְּהֶעְלֵם כָּזֶה, דְּאִלּוּ הָיָה עוֹד מַעֲלִים יוֹתֵר — הָיָה הֶעְלֵם שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהִתְגַּלּוֹת.
meaning: this degree of concealment suffices, for had it been deeper, the light could never have been discovered.
וְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ ״עָשָׂה הָאֱלֹהִים אֶת הָאָדָם יָשָׁר״ (קֹהֶלֶת ז:כט): שֶׁיּוּכַל לְגַלּוֹת הַהֶעְלֵם, וְלִכְרוֹת הָעָרְלָה, וּלְהַכִּיר מִתּוֹךְ הַחֹשֶׁךְ — לָבוֹא עַל יְדֵי זֶה לִנְהוֹרָא
And Hashem "made man upright" (Koheles 7:29): that he be empowered to penetrate the concealment, excise the foreskin, and perceive the light out of darkness;
וְשִׁיעֲרָה חָכְמָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ מִדַּת הַהֶעְלֵם שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לִהְיוֹת כָּךְ כְּפִי הַמִּדָּה שֶׁקָּבַע בִּשְׁנֵי הָעוֹלָמוֹת שֶׁבָּזֶה יִהְיֶה מָקוֹם לַבְּחִירָה
His wisdom having calibrated the precise boundary of concealment across both worlds to preserve human free choice;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ: ״בַּעֲשָׂרָה מַאֲמָרוֹת נִבְרָא הָעוֹלָם... לִתֵּן שָׂכָר טוֹב לַצַּדִּיקִים... וּלְהִפָּרַע מִן הָרְשָׁעִים״ (אָבוֹת פֶּרֶק ה׳ מִשְׁנָה א׳)
matching the Mishnah: "By ten utterances was the world created... to give a good reward to the righteous and to punish the wicked" (Avos 5:1);
כִּי הֵם דֶּרֶךְ כְּלָל עֲשָׂרָה מִינֵי הֶעְלֵמוֹת, כִּי כָּךְ קָבַע הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מִדַּת הַהֶעְלֵם שֶׁיִּהְיֶה שָׂכָר טוֹב
these being ten general archetypes of concealment, calibrated so that the reward be great;
דִּבְפָחוֹת — לֹא הָיָה שָׂכָר כָּל כָּךְ, כִּי נָקֵל לְהַשִּׂיג הָאוֹר אִם אֵין הַחֹשֶׁךְ גָּדוֹל כָּל כָּךְ וְלֹא הָיָה הַבְּחִירָה
for had the concealment been less, the reward would be diminished, the light being easily attained and free choice vanishing;
וּבְיוֹתֵר מִזֶּה — לֹא הָיָה פּוּרְעָנוּת לָרְשָׁעִים, כִּי הָיוּ מוּכְרָחִים בְּמַעֲשֵׂיהֶם, שֶׁהָיָה כָּל כָּךְ חֹשֶׁךְ עַד שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהַשִּׂיג הָאוֹר כְּלָל.
and had the concealment been greater, the wicked could not be punished, being coerced by an overwhelming darkness where light could never be grasped.
וּמְצִיאוּת הַבְּחִירָה בְּכָל צַד הוּא כְּשֶׁהַבְּרִיאָה כְּפִי אוֹתָהּ הַמִּדָּה בְּצִמְצוּם דַּוְוקָא, לֹא פָחוֹת וְלֹא יוֹתֵר
The reality of free choice existing precisely when Creation is calibrated in exact contraction, neither less nor more;
שֶׁבָּזֶה יֵשׁ ״דַּי״ לְעִנְיַן הַמְכֻוָּון בִּבְרִיאַת הַבְּחִירָה וְשָׂכָר וָעוֹנֶשׁ לַצַּדִּיקִים וּרְשָׁעִים
wherein there is "enough" (Dai) to fulfill the divine intent of free will, reward, and punishment;
וְזֶהוּ קְדֻשַּׁת הַשֵּׁם הַנַּזְכָּר לְעֵיל [שַׁדַּ״י], שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ ״דַּי״ לְכָל בְּרִיָּה וּלְכָל אָדָם לְהַשִּׂיג כְּפִי מַה שֶּׁהוּא:
this being the sanctity of the Name Shaddai, containing sufficient light for every soul to perceive according to its measure!

10.h: אוֹת ט״ו — מַחֲזֵה שַׁדַּי וְעוֹר הָעָרְלָה, שָׂרָהּ שֶׁל מִצְרַיִם, וּבֵירוּר הַבְּרִית בְּיוֹסֵף וְאָסְנַת — Section 15: The Mirrored Vision, The Angel of Egypt, and Refining the Covenant in Joseph and Asenath

The theme: The vision of the divine reflected through a mirror (aspaklaria), Egypt as the epicenter of lust, and why Joseph married Asenath the daughter of Dinah. A "vision" (machazeh) denotes beholding an object not directly, but reflected through an indirect mirror (aspaklaria she-einah me'irah), Onkelos translating "mirrors" as machzayata (Shemos 38:8). In the spiritual realm, this indirect vision corresponds to the veil of the foreskin covering the holy covenant. In the angelic hierarchy, this realm of the foreskin was occupied by the fallen angels Uzza and Azael: Uzza was the celestial patron prince of Egypt (Yalkut Shimoni; Midrash Vayosha on Shemos 14:30). Egypt was "the nakedness of the land" (ervat ha-aretz, Bereishis 42:9), concerning whom it is written: "whose issue is like the issue of horses" (Yechezkel 23:20). Pesachim (113b) states that among the six traits of a horse, the first is that it loves licentiousness. Unto this very land Joseph—the root of Yesod and the holy covenant—was sold as a slave! This began the decree: "and they shall serve them, and they shall afflict them" (Bereishis 15:13), demonstrating that even when submerged in an alien land devoid of holiness, Israel would emerge with great wealth (bi-rekhush gadol), standing pure at Sinai where the Serpent's defilement was eradicated. Potiphar's wife sought to pull that defilement over Joseph ("to be with her in the world to come", Sotah 36b; Yalkut Shimoni §146), which is drawing forward the foreskin. Midrashically, she saw astrologically that she would produce offspring with him (Bereishis Rabbah 85:2), which materialized through her adopted daughter Asenath, the biological child of Dinah and Shechem (Pirkei d'Rabbi Eliezer ch. 38). Raising a child is akin to giving birth (Sanhedrin 19b). When a gentile cohabits with a Jewish woman, the child is legally kosher and Jewish ("your son", Kiddushin 68b), possessing no root in gentile foreskin; whereas a child born of a Jewish father and a gentile mother takes the status of the mother ("her son"), the holy seed turning into defiled seed!

p: וּ״מַחֲזֶה״ — הוּא מַרְאֶה שֶׁאֵין רוֹאִים גּוּף הַדָּבָר, רַק דֶּרֶךְ מַרְאָה וְאַסְפַּקְלַרְיָא שֶׁאֵינָהּ מְאִירָה
And a "vision" (machazeh)—is a sight wherein one perceives not the essence directly, but reflected through a dim mirror (aspaklaria she-einah me'irah);
וְכִדִּמְתַרְגְּמִינַן עַל ״מַרְאֹת [הַצֹּבְאֹת]״ (שְׁמוֹת ל״ח:ח׳): ״מֶחְזְיָתָא״
as Onkelos translates "the mirrors of the serving women" (Shemos 38:8): machzayata;
